messages.title: Time
paragraphs: “He who regards the day, regards it unto the Lord.” — PAUL (Romans 14:6)
Most men do not yet perceive the infinite values of time.
Indeed, there are those who abuse this divine concession. They believe that the wealth of benefits is owed to them by God.
It would be fair, however, to question them regarding the reason for such presumption.

Since Universal Creation constitutes a common heritage, it is reasonable that all should enjoy the possibilities of life; yet, in general, the creature does not meditate on the harmony of circumstances that align on Earth in favor of their spiritual improvement.
It is logical for every man to count on time, but what if that time lacks light, balance, health, and work?

Notwithstanding the appropriateness of the inquiry, it is important to consider that very rare are those who value the day, while everywhere multiply the ranks of those who seek to annihilate it in any way.
The old popular expression “to kill time” reflects common thoughtlessness in this regard.

In the darkest corners of the Earth, there are creatures exterminating sacred possibilities. Nevertheless, a day of peace, harmony, and enlightenment is very important for human cooperation in executing divine laws.

The immediate interests of the world proclaim that “time is money,” only to then restart all incomplete works in the wake of reincarnations… For this very reason, men build and undo, construct and destroy, learn frivolously, and recapitulate with difficulty in the acquisition of experience.
In almost every sector of earthly evolution, we see the abuse of opportunity complicating the paths of life; yet, for many centuries, the apostle has affirmed to us that time must belong to the Lord.

messages.title: Follow Me
paragraphs: “Jesus said to him: If I will that he remain until I come, what is that to you? Follow me.” — (JOHN 21:22)
In communities of Christian labor, we often observe companions who are deeply concerned with the task assigned to other fellow workers.
It is fair to consider, however, how the world would be elevated if every man took care of his own part in common duties with perfection and sincerity.
Has one of our friends been summoned to different obligations?
Let us comfort him with genuine understanding.

Sometimes, one of them appears changed to our eyes. There are coworkers who accuse him. Many consider him a bearer of dangerous temptations. Hasty comments and judgments are set in motion. Who, however, can penetrate the field of causes? Are we in the elevated condition of one who can analyze an event from every angle? Perhaps what seems like a fall or defection may constitute new determinations of Jesus regarding the redemption of the friend who now seems distant.
The Good Shepherd remains vigilant. He promised that of the sheep the Father entrusted to Him, none shall be lost.
It is fitting, therefore, that we attend with perfection to the duties assigned to us. Each one needs to know the obligations that belong to them.
In this standard of knowledge and attitude, there is always much noble work to be done.
If a brother seems astray to your mortal eyes, do your utmost to hear Jesus’ words to the fisherman of Capernaum: “What is that to you? Follow me.”

messages.title: Examine Yourself
paragraphs: “Do nothing through strife or vainglory, but in humility.” — PAUL (Philippians 2:3)
The service of Jesus is infinite. In its orbit, there is room for all creatures and for all healthy ideas in their substantial expression.
If, in the divine order, each tree produces according to its kind, in Christian labor, each disciple will contribute according to their evolutionary position.

The human experience is not a station of pleasure. Man remains here for the purpose of learning, and in this task, it is reasonable that he know how to value the opportunity to learn, facilitating the same opportunity for his fellow beings.
The apostle Paul understood this truth, affirming that we should do nothing through a spirit of strife and vainglory, but rather as an act of humility.

When you perform any action that goes beyond the framework of daily obligations, examine the motives that determined it. If it resulted from an unjust desire for supremacy, if it complied solely with unnecessary dispute, tend to your heart so that the path may be less ungrateful to you. But if you answered duty, even if you were interpreted as rigid and demanding, uncomprehending and unfaithful, receive the undue remarks and move forward.

Keep working in your ministry, remembering that, for serving others with humility, without strife and vainglory, Jesus was considered reckless and rebellious, a traitor to the law and an enemy of the people, receiving with the cross the glorious crown.

messages.title: Work
paragraphs: “And Jesus answered them: My Father works until now, and I work too.” — (JOHN 5:17)
In every corner, we observe complaining and dissatisfied creatures.
Almost all ask for help. Rare are those who love the effort assigned to them. The majority rebels against the kind of work they have.
Those who sweep the streets want to be merchants; farm workers would prefer life in the city.
The problem, however, is not the kind of task, but the understanding of the opportunity received.
Generally speaking, complaints in this regard are the offspring of unconscious laziness. It is the inborn desire to preserve what is useless and ruinous from falls in the dark past.
But Jesus came to pull us out of “death in error.” He brought us the blessing of work, which is the incessant movement of life.

So that we might know how to honor our effort, He referred to the Father, who never ceases to serve in His eternal work of love and wisdom, and to His own task, filled with imperishable dedication to Humanity.
When you feel weary, remember that Jesus is working. We began our humble labor yesterday, and since when has the Master been striving for us?

messages.title: Foundations
paragraphs: “Peter said to him: You shall never wash my feet. Jesus answered him: If I do not wash you, you have no part with me.” — (JOHN 13:8)
It is natural that we see, first of all, in the Master’s decision to wash the disciples’ feet, a sublime demonstration of sanctifying humility.

First, it is fair to examine the intellectual interpretation, advancing, however, to the deeper analysis of His divine acts. For through the permanent message of the Gospel, Christ continues washing the feet of all sincere followers of His doctrine of love and forgiveness.

Man usually lives indifferent to all his higher obligations, often applauding crime and thoughtlessness. However, upon contact with Jesus and His sublime teachings, he feels that he will step upon new foundations, while his fundamental appreciations of existence become very different.
Someone provides lightness to his spiritual feet so that he may walk differently on evolutionary paths.
Everything is renewed, and the creature understands that were it not for this wonderful intervention, he could not participate in the banquet of real life.

Then, like the apostle of Capernaum, he experiences new responsibilities on the path and, desiring to meet the divine expectation, begs Jesus to wash not only his feet, but also his hands and his head.

messages.title: Effort and Prayer
paragraphs: “And when he had sent the multitude away, he went up into a mountain apart to pray. And when evening was come, he was there alone.” — (MATTHEW 14:23)
From time to time, religious groups arise advocating total withdrawal from human struggles for the services of prayer.
In this regard, however, the Master is always the source of living teachings. Work and prayer are two hallmarks of His divine activity.

Jesus never secluded Himself at a distance from creatures in order to remain in absolute contemplation of the divine scenes that illuminated His heart, but He also cultivated prayer in its celestial height.
Once the multitude was dismissed and the daily effort concluded, He established the necessary pause to meditate apart, communing with the Father in solitary and sublime prayer.

If anyone remains on Earth, it is with the objective of reaching a higher point in evolutionary expressions through the work they were called to do. And through prayer, man receives from God the indispensable help for sanctifying the task.
Effort and prayer complement each other in the totality of spiritual activity.

A creature who only worked, without method and without rest, would end up in despair, in a horrible dryness of heart; one who only remained genuflecting would be in danger of succumbing to paralysis and idleness.
Prayer illuminates work, and action is like a book of light in a spiritualized life.
Attend to your duties, for that is why you remain in the world, but never forget that mountain located within your noblest feelings, so that you may pray “apart,” remembering the Lord.

messages.title: All Things New
paragraphs: “Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creature: old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new.” — PAUL (2 Corinthians 5:17)

It is very common to observe restless believers using the sacred resources of prayer to perpetuate unjustifiable situations simply because they involve certain immediate advantages for their selfish concerns.
Such a mental attitude constitutes a very serious decision.

Christ taught patience and tolerance, but He never instructed His disciples to make compromises with the errors that afflict the world. In the face of this decision, He went to the cross and bequeathed the ultimate testimony of non-violence, but also of non-compliance with the darkness in which the majority of creatures indulge.
Let the believer not be deceived concerning the path that belongs to him.

In Christ, everything must be renewed. The sinful past shall be dead, situations of doubt will have come to an end, the old concerns of the carnal man will give way to new life in spirit, where everything signifies healthy reconstruction for the eternal future.
It is a contradiction to use Jesus’ name to attempt the continuation of old mistakes.

When we notice the presence of a believer with fine words, but without an inner renewal, addressing the Master like a prisoner weighed down by chains, let us be certain that this brother may be at Christ’s door through sincerity of intentions; however, he has not yet managed to enter the sanctuary of His love.

messages.title: Jesus Came
paragraphs: “But emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, making himself in the likeness of men.” — PAUL (Philippians 2:7)

Many disciples speak of extreme difficulties in establishing good works within the services of evangelical fellowship, alleging the unfortunate state of ignorance in which an immense percentage of Earth’s creatures indulge. However, such complaints are not justified.

To carry out His divine mission of love, Jesus did not rely on the immediate collaboration of perfected and understanding Spirits; rather, He “emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, making himself in the likeness of men.”
We could not go to the Savior in His sublime position; nevertheless, the Master came to us, temporarily dimming His halo of light so as to benefit us without traces of sensationalism.
Jesus’ example, in this regard, represents an exceedingly profound lesson.
Let no one claim intellectual or sentimental achievements as a reason for discord with Earth’s brothers and sisters.

No man among those who have passed through this orb reached the heights of the Christ. Nevertheless, we see Him at the table of sinners, speaking fraternally to harlots, delivering His final testimony among thieves.

If your neighbor cannot rise to the spiritual plane on which you find yourself, you can go out to meet him for the good service of fraternity and enlightenment, without ostentation that might offend his inferiority.
Remember the demonstration of the Divine Master. To come to us, He emptied Himself, entering the world as a child of humble birth and departing from the glorious work as a crucified servant.

messages.title: Christian Meetings
paragraphs: “Then the same day at evening, being the first day of the week, when the doors were shut where the disciples were assembled for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in their midst, and said to them: Peace be with you.” — (JOHN 20:19)
Since the day of Christ’s glorious resurrection, earthly Humanity was considered worthy of relations with spirituality.

Deuteronomy had strictly forbidden communication with those who had departed through the gates of the grave, in view of the need to steer the human mind away from premature concerns. However, Jesus, just as He had softened the ancient law of inflexible justice with the forgiveness of a boundless love, eased the injunctions of Moses by coming to meet His longing disciples.

The doors being shut so that the tumultuous vibrations of unprovoked adversaries would not disturb the hearts of those longing for divine fellowship, behold, the dearly beloved Master appears, expanding everyone’s hopes in eternal life. From that unforgettable hour, the movement of exchange between the visible and invisible worlds was instituted. The Christian family, in its various departments, would never be without the sweet nourishment of its affectionate and intimate gatherings. From then on, the disciples would gather both in the upper rooms of Jerusalem and in the catacombs of Rome. And in modern times, the deepest essence of these assemblies remains the same, whether in Catholic churches, Protestant temples, or Spiritist centers.

The objective is one and the same: to seek the influence of the Higher Realms, with the difference that in Spiritist environments the soul can be nourished more abundantly in higher flights, by remaining removed from certain prejudices of dogmatism and organized priesthood.
.Emmanuel

messages.title: Mediumship
paragraphs: “And it shall come to pass in the last days, says the Lord, that I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your young men shall see visions, and your old men shall dream dreams.” — (ACTS 2:17)

On the day of Pentecost, Jerusalem was crowded with strangers. Sons of Mesopotamia, Phrygia, Libya, Egypt, Cretans, Arabs, Parthians, and Romans gathered in the vast square when the humble disciples of the Nazarene announced the Good News, addressing each group in the crowd in their own language.
A wave of surprise and joy swept over the general spirit.

There was no shortage of skeptics in that divine concert, attributing the observed revelation to madness and drunkenness. Simon Peter stepped forward and clarified that it was the light promised by the heavens to the darkness of the flesh.

From that day on, the radiance of Pentecost poured unceasingly over the world. Until then, the disciples had been fragile and hesitant, but from that hour forward, they broke free from environmental influences, healed the sick, lifted the spirits of the unfortunate, and spoke to the kings of the Earth in the name of the Lord.
The power of Jesus had been imparted to their limited energies.
The era of mediumship was established, the foundation of all Christianity’s accomplishments throughout the centuries.

Against its influx work, even today, the moral prejudices that ravage the paths of man; yet it is upon mediumship—that glorious light from the Heavens offered to creatures at Pentecost—that the spiritual edifices of all sincere communities of Christ’s Doctrine are built, and it is also mediumship which, expanded from the apostles to the circle of all people, reemerges in Christian Spiritism as the immortal soul of revived Christianity.

messages.title: Help from the Invisible
paragraphs: “When they were past the first and the second ward, they came unto the iron gate that leadeth unto the city; which opened to them of his own accord: and they went out, and passed on through one street; and forthwith the angel departed from him.” — (ACTS 12:10)

Men always anxiously await aid from the spiritual Realm. It matters not by what name this support is designated. In its essence it is invariably the same, although it is known among Spiritists as “the guides’ protection” and in Protestant circles as “manifestations of the Holy Spirit.”
The denominations are of secondary interest. What is essential is to consider that such collaboration constitutes a vital element in the activities of the sincere believer.
Nevertheless, the assistance received by Peter in prison represents a lesson for all.

Under very heavy chains, the fisherman of Capernaum sees the angel of the Lord draw near, who delivers him, goes through the first perils in prison by his side, and walks beside the messenger along a street; yet, the emissary departs, leaving him once again to his own freedom, so as not to devalue his initiatives.
This example is typical.

The aids from the invisible are undeniable and never fail in their multiform expressions at the opportune moment; but it is essential that the believer does not become dependent on this kind of cooperation, learning to walk alone, using independence and will in what is just and useful, convinced that one is in the world to learn, not being permitted to demand from the instructors the solution to problems necessary to one's condition as a student.

messages.title: All in God
paragraphs: “I can of mine own self do nothing.” — JESUS (John 5:30)
Meditation on the transcendent factors that govern the smallest phenomena of life constitutes an excellent exercise against personal vanity.
Man can do nothing without God.

We have all seen domineering personalities arise on the earthly stage, declaring themselves powerful without the support of the Most High; however, the only achievement they actually attain is an illusory expansion by the breath of the world, deflating at the first contacts with divine truths. When they appear, fearsome, these giants of wind scatter material ruins and afflictions of the spirit; yet, the very world that confers upon them a pedestal casts them into the abyss of common contempt; the same crowd that blows them up is tasked with putting them back in their proper place.

Sincere disciples do not ignore that all their possibilities come from the wise and loving Father, that the opportunities for edification on Earth, with the excellence of landscapes, daily resources, and the blessings of loved ones, came from God, who invites them, through the spirit of service, to holier ministries; they will act, therefore, always loving, taking advantage for the good and enlightening toward truth, rectifying paths and kindling new lights, because their hearts acknowledge that they can do nothing of themselves and will honor the Father, entering into holy cooperation in His works.

messages.title: The Christian and the World
paragraphs: “First the blade, then the ear, after that the full corn in the ear.” — JESUS (Mark 4:28)
Let no one think it easy to acquire a title referring to spiritual elevation. The Master wisely resorted to the living symbols of Nature, aiding our comprehension.
The blade is far from the ear, just as the ear remains distant from the ripe grains.

In this chapter, the soul’s strongest adversary in desiring to follow the Savior is the world itself. When the common man rests in the vulgarities and trivialities of earthly existence, no one examines his steps. His attitudes are of no interest to anyone. However, as soon as the tender blade of rectifying faith springs up in his heart, his life becomes an object of curiosity for the multitude. Thousands of eyes, which did not see him when he was straying in ignorance and indifference, now follow his slightest gestures with heightened vigilance. The poor aspirant to the title of disciple of the Lord is still nothing more than promising foliage, and already ears of celestial works are demanded of him; he still remains far from the first down of spiritual wings, and supreme flights over human miseries are already demanded of him.
Many apprentices become discouraged and return to the mire, where their companions may not see them.

The world forgets that these eager souls are still in their first hopes and, for that very reason, in harsher struggles to burst the cocoon of lower passions in their aspiration to ascend; within the old ignorance characteristic of it, the multitude only understands man in the animality in which it delights, or else, if the companion intends to rise, immediately demands of him positive credentials from Heaven, forgetting that no one can betray time or deceive the spirit of sequence in Nature. It remains for the Christian to cultivate his sublime purposes and listen to the Master: “First the blade, then the ear, after that the full corn in the ear.”

messages.title: The World's Esteem
paragraphs: “If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub, how much more shall they call them of his household?” — JESUS (Matthew 10:25)
Many disciples of the Gospel exist who are jealous of their preferences and viewpoints in the individual sphere.
False conceptions shadow their gaze.

They are almost always uneasy over public recognition of the virtues that adorn their character, harbor the secret purpose of obtaining the admiration of all, and feel wronged if the transitory authorities of the world do not grant them esteem.

They act forgetting that the Kingdom of God does not come with outward observation; they fail to realize that, for now, only prominent figures in financial or political vanguards set themselves up as holders of earthly prerogatives, almost absolute masters of personal tributes and glowing obituaries.
The children of the Divine Kingdom rarely stand out and, generally speaking, fill the world with benefits without man seeing them, after the manner of what occurs with the Father Himself.
If Jesus was called a sorcerer, crucified as a malefactor, and snatched from his loving mission to the shameful cross, what should his sincere apprentices not expect when truly devoted to his cause?

The disciple cannot be unaware that one's stay on Earth stems from the need for fruitful work and not from the enjoyment of ephemeral advantages that, in many cases, would annul one's capacity to serve. If human force tortured the Christ, it will not fail to torture him as well. It is illogical to vie for the esteem of a world that, later on, will be compelled to regenerate in order to attain redemption.

messages.title: The Symbolic Sword
paragraphs: “Think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword.” — JESUS (Matthew 10:34)

Countless readers of the Gospel are troubled by these statements of the Divine Master, because the concept of peace among men has for many centuries been viscerally corrupted. In common parlance, having peace means having attained external securities within which the body may vegetate carefree, surrounding oneself with servants, rotting in idleness, and absenting oneself from the movements of life.

Jesus could not endorse tranquility of this sort, and, in opposition to the false principle established in the world, brought with him the regenerating struggle, the symbolic sword of inner knowledge through divine revelation, so that man might begin the battle of self-improvement within himself. The Master came to establish the combat of redemption on Earth. From his very first teaching, the bloodless battlefront was formed, destined for the illumination of the human path. And He Himself was the first to inaugurate the testimony through supreme sacrifices.
For nearly twenty centuries the Earth has lived under these renewing impulses, and woe to those who sleep, oblivious to the sanctifying process!
To seek the false peace of idleness is to stray from the light, fleeing from life and precipitating death. Nevertheless, Jesus is also called the Prince of Peace.

Yes, in truth the Christ brought to the world the renewing sword of war against evil, constituting in himself the divine source of rest for hearts that unite with his love; these, in the most dangerous situations on Earth, find in Him unalterable serenity. It is because Jesus began the combat of salvation for Humanity, representing, at the same time, the mainstay of sublime peace for all good and sincere men.

messages.title: Not All
paragraphs: “And it came to pass about an eight days after these sayings, he took Peter and John and James, and went up into a mountain to pray.” — (LUKE 9:28)

Worthy of note is the Master's attitude, inviting only Simon and the sons of Zebedee to witness the sublime manifestation on the mount, when Moses and another divine emissary would be in direct contact with Jesus, before the eyes of the disciples.
Why did he not summon the other companions?

Would not Philip or Andrew have delighted in the sublime revelation? Was not Thomas an inquisitive companion, eager for spiritual equations? Nevertheless, the Master knew the reason for his decisions, and only He could suitably measure out the gifts of higher knowledge.
This fact should be remembered by all who wish to force the door of the Spiritual Realm.
To be sure, communication with this or that group of entities from the Beyond is possible, but not all are prepared, at one and the same time, to receive responsibilities or benefits.

One does not imprudently entrust an instrument of precious production, whose handling depends on prior competence, to the first man who comes along filled with good desires. Natural order is not betrayed with impunity. Not all apprentices and students will receive great revelations from the Beyond at a moment's notice. Each center of spiritualizing activity must be presided over by the finest sense of harmony, effort, and affinity. In this undertaking, in addition to good intentions, presenting a record of personal good works is indispensable. And in the world, everyone remains ready to want this or that, but very few creatures are willing to serve and educate themselves.

messages.title: To Give
paragraphs: “Give to every man that asketh of thee; and of him that taketh away thy goods ask them not again.” — JESUS (Luke 6:30)
The act of giving is among the most sublime in the operations of life; nevertheless, many men are careless and incomprehensible in its execution.
Some distribute alms heedlessly; others forget vigilance, delivering their work to evildoers.

Jesus is our Master in the slightest occurrences. And if we hear him recommending that we be ready to give “to anyone” who asks, we see him attending to all creatures along his path, not according to whims, but according to needs.

He granted beatitudes to the afflicted and warnings to the moneychangers. To be sure, the bad-faith merchants inwardly pleaded with him to maintain the status quo, but his response was eloquent. He gave joy at the wedding in Cana and rebukes in assemblies of the disciples. He provided each situation and each personality with what they needed; and when the ungrateful took from him the right to his very life in the eyes of Humanity, the Christ did not return to ask them to leave him to the work he had begun.

He gave all that was in accordance with the good. And he gave in abundance, with the notable highlight that, under the weight of the cross, he granted sublime understanding to general ignorance without complaint of any kind, because he knew that the act of giving comes from God, and nothing is more sacred than collaborating with the Father who is in Heaven.

messages.title: The Coming of the Kingdom
paragraphs: “The kingdom of God cometh not with observation.” — JESUS (Luke 17:20)

Religious groups in the world almost always remain preoccupied with the conversions of others. The most enthusiastic believers long to transform the conceptions of their friends. Because of this, everywhere we are confronted by brethren distressed over expanding proselytism in their study circles.
Such activity is not always useful, since on many occasions it can disturb noble projects underway.

Jesus states that the Kingdom of God does not come with outward observation. The concern to vainly display pomp and numbers in groups of faith is always ruinous. Transitory expressions of human power do not attest to the Kingdom of God. Divine fulfillment will begin from within creatures, constituting the glorious light of the inner temple. It does not appear to common appreciation, because most men walk semi-blind through the tunnel of the flesh, burying the errors of a guilty past.

The flesh is worthy and venerable, for it is a vessel of purification, receiving us for necessary redemption; yet, for redeemed Spirits it signifies “death” or “permanent transformation.” Carnal man, in view of the circumstances governing his effort, can see only what is “dead” or that which is “about to die.” The Kingdom of God, however, divine and immortal, naturally escapes human sight.

messages.title: Reincarnation
paragraphs: “Wherefore if thy hand or thy foot offend thee, cut them off, and cast them from thee: it is better for thee to enter into life halt or maimed, rather than having two hands or two feet to be cast into everlasting fire.” — JESUS (Matthew 18:8)
Only reincarnation clarifies the questions of being, suffering, and destiny. On many occasions, Jesus spoke to us of its beautiful and wise principles.
This passage from Matthew is supremely expressive. It is essential to consider that the Master was addressing a stagnant, nearly dead society.

In the concert of divine lessons he receives, the Christian, strictly speaking, truly knows only one kind of death: that which befalls the conscience guilty of straying from the Law; and the contemporaries of the Christ were, for the most part, creatures without edifying spiritual activity, hardened in soul and paralyzed in heart. The expression “it is better for thee to enter into life” represents a fundamental solution. Were not the listeners human persons? Yet the Lord was referring to continuous existence, to the everlasting life within which every Spirit will awaken to its glorious eternal destiny.

In the elevated symbolism of his words, Jesus presents to us the determining motive for painful rebirths, in which we observe the crippled, the blind, and the paralyzed from birth, who ask for such trials as periods of renewal and regeneration indispensable to future happiness.

As for the image of “everlasting fire” found in the gospel writings, it is a device well suited to the lesson, because until the creature is willing to live with the Christ, one will be impelled to do so through a thousand different means; if rebelliousness persists for an infinity of centuries, the purifying processes will likewise remain, like material fire, which will exist on Earth as long as its contribution endures in time as an indispensable utility for physical life.

messages.title: We Shall Always Find
paragraphs: “For every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth.” — JESUS (Luke 11:10)
When the believer experiences the need for something, he mechanically recalls the Master’s promise when He assured an adequate response to anyone who asks.
It is important, however, to know what we are seeking. Naturally, we will always receive, but it is essential to know the object of our request.
Jesus asserted: “He that seeketh findeth.”
Whoever seeks evil encounters evil likewise.
There is a perfect correspondence between our soul and the soul of things. We do not advance a hypothesis; we examine a law.

For those who look for thieves, listening to the false appeals of their own inner world, all men will be dishonest. So it is with those who have aspirations of belief, approaching religious groups with suspicion. They never catch sight of faith, because they analyze everything through the bad faith they harbor. They experiment and persist so much, wielding the lower purposes on which they feed, that they effectively find nothing beyond the disappointments they expected.
In order to find the good, it is necessary to seek it every day.

Undeniably, in a field of shocking struggles such as the Earthly Sphere, the hunt for evil is immediately crowned with success, due to the preponderance of evil among creatures. Fishing for good is not so easy; nevertheless, good will be found as a divine and eternal value.
Great vigilance is therefore indispensable when deciding to seek something, for the Master affirmed: “He that seeketh findeth”; and we will always find what we seek.

messages.title: Comfort
paragraphs: “If any man serve me, let him follow me.” — JESUS (John 12:26)
Frequently, religious organizations, and especially Spiritist ones nowadays, are filled with people anxious for comfort.

Indeed, the lofty Doctrine of the Spirits is the divine expression of the Promised Consoler. In its activities, new paths shine forth for human thought, full of profound consolations for the hardest days.
However, it is essential to consider that it is not fair for someone to want to be comforted without taking the necessary trouble...

Many ask for support from the messengers of the invisible Realm; but how can they receive it if they have gone so far as to abandon themselves to the whims of the impetuous gale blowing hard upon the slippery slopes along the way?

Spiritual comfort is not like worldly bread, which passes mechanically from hand to hand to satisfy bodily hunger, but rather like the Sun, which is the same for all, yet penetrates only where an enclosed stronghold has not been made for the shadows.

The disciples of Jesus may speak of their needs for comfort. That is natural. Yet, before that, they need to know whether they are serving the Master and following him. Christ never failed his promises. His divine kingdom is built upon immortal consolations; but, to reach it, it is necessary to follow in his footsteps, and no one is unaware of what Jesus' path was like upon the stones of this world.

messages.title: Successive Lives
paragraphs: “Marvel not that I said unto thee, Ye must be born again.” — JESUS (John 3:7)
Jesus’ word to Nicodemus was clear enough.
Diverting it to preposterous interpretations may be understandable in organized priesthood, attentive to the demands of human struggle, but never in spirits who love the legitimate truth.
Reincarnation is a universal law.
Without it, earthly existence would represent a whirlpool of disorder and injustice; in the light of its clarifications, we understand all the painful phenomena of the path.
Man has not yet realized the full extent of divine mercy in the processes of redemption and readjustment.
Among men, the criminal is condemned to cruel punishments, whether by the death penalty or prolonged suffering.

Providence, however, corrects while loving... It does not dispatch the accused to foul and damp prisons. It merely determines that the partners in nefarious dramas exchange their carnal garments and return to the stage of human activity, so as to redeem themselves before one another.

To Magnanimous Wisdom, the one who erred is not always a scoundrel, just as the victim is not always pure and sincere. God sees not only the malice that surfaces in a scandal; He knows the somber mechanism of all the circumstances that led to a crime.

The absolute tormentor, like the absolute victim, is unknown to man; the Father, however, identifies the needs of His children and periodically reunites them through ties of blood or within the web of edifying commitments, so that they may learn the law of love amid the difficulties and pains of destiny, blessed with temporary forgetfulness.

messages.title: Guides of the World
paragraphs: “Jesus answered and said unto him, Art thou a master of Israel, and knowest not these things?” — (JOHN 3:10)
It is very common in religious circles, notably in Spiritist ranks, for worldly guides to appear, demanding proof of the soul's existence.
A time will come when such inquiries will be considered childish, because, after all, these leaders of politics, education, and science are essentially asking whether they themselves exist.
Jesus' answer to Nicodemus, although referring to the problem of reincarnation, fits the subject perfectly, since contemporary leaders continue to inquire about the essential realities of life.
Let us ask God to help man not to keep trying to enter the house of progress through the roof.

The reckless physician, until he ascertains spiritual truth, will be confronted by painful experiences in the field of achievements pertaining to him. The merely theoretical teacher will often plunge into illusions. The makeshift administrator will remain exposed to tremendous errors until he adjusts to the responsibility that is his own.

For this reason, Jesus' reply applies accurately to the questions of modern instructors. Transformed into investigators, they address us, often with irony, demanding certainty about the existence of the Spirit; yet, they guide others and introduce themselves into the lives of our brothers and sisters in humanity. Considering this circumstance, and being such an essential issue for themselves, it is reasonable that they should not ask, for they ought to know.

messages.title: Like Lazarus
paragraphs: “And he that was dead came forth, bound hand and foot with graveclothes: and his face was bound about with a napkin. Jesus saith unto them, Loose him, and let him go.” — (JOHN 11:44)
Lazarus's return to active life represents a magnificent symbol for all the workers of the Earth.
Repentant criminals, sinners who turn toward the good, those who have “cracked” the crystal of conscience, understand the marvelous quality of the verb to start over.

Lazarus could not be happy merely for clothing himself once more in perishable flesh, but rather for the opportunity to restart the human experience with new values. And in the evolutionary toil, whenever the Spirit obtains from the Divine Master the opportunity to return to Earth, behold, he is unbound from heavy wrappings... released from anguish, remorse, fear... The sensation of the tomb of impressions in which he found himself was a heavy blindfold covering his face...
Jesus, filled with compassion, exclaimed to the world:
— “Loose him, and let him go.”
This gospel passage is marked by profound beauty.

Precious is the existence of a man, because Christ allowed him to be loosed from criminal ties with the past, letting him head once again to the sources of human life so as to rebuild and sanctify the links of his spiritual destiny, through the supreme gift of beginning again.

messages.title: Do Not Forget
paragraphs: “Because that by reason of him many of the Jews went away, and believed on Jesus.” — (JOHN 12:11)

The Gospel of John relates that many people, heading to Bethany, sought to draw near to the Master, not only to see him, but also to behold the figure of Lazarus, taken from the tomb. In this movement, many went and returned transformed, irritating the Pharisaic circles.
This recollection of the Apostle is precious. The situation, however, is identical in present times.
The soul turned toward Christ was almost always resurrected by his love, escaping the shadow of intellectual nightmares that work the death of sentiment...

Many people are dead, buried in the sepulchers of indifference, selfishness, denial. When a fellow being, like Lazarus, is fortunate enough to be touched by Christ, general curiosity arises around his attitudes. Everyone wishes to know his changes.

If you are, therefore, a beneficiary of Jesus; if the Lord has already raised you from the earthly dust to the knowledge of infinite life, remember that most of your friends have heard of the Master; yet, they are not yet prepared to understand him fully. You will be, like Lazarus, the point of direct observation for them all. They will only begin to receive the clarity of sincere belief through you, recognizing the power of Jesus by the transformation you demonstrate. If, then, you have already been called by the Lord of Life, it is in your hands to remain in the realms of death or to rise up for the edification of those around you.

messages.title: The Letters of Christ
paragraphs: “Forasmuch as ye are manifestly declared to be the epistle of Christ ministered by us, written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God; not in tables of stone, but in fleshy tables of the heart.” — PAUL (2 Corinthians 3:3)
It is remarkable that the Master did not bequeath to the world a compendium of principles written by his own hands.
Earth’s notable figures always mark their passage on the planet, addressing to posterity their message of wisdom and love, whether on stone tablets or in aged documents.

With Jesus, however, the process was not the same. The Master made a point, as it were, of writing his doctrine to humanity by engraving it on the hearts of sincere companions. His spiritual testament consists of teachings to the disciples, and they were not written down by himself.

Human resources would be insufficient to reveal the eternal wealth of his Message. Letters and arguments of a strictly human nature most often give rise to controversies. In view of this, Jesus engraved his teachings on the hearts that surrounded him, and to this day the learners who remain faithful to him are his divine letters addressed to Humanity. These living documents of Christ’s sanctifying love pulsate in all religions and in all climes. They are the vanguards who know higher life, experience the sublime contact of the Master, and become his message to humanity.

Many disputes may arise around the most celebrated and beautiful pages; yet, before the soul that has become a living letter of the Lord, when there are no higher vibrations of understanding, there will always be divine silence.

messages.title: Ambassadors of Christ
paragraphs: “Now then we are ambassadors for Christ.” — PAUL (2 Corinthians 5:20)
In the cataloging of social values, every honest working man holds a specific delegation.
If politicians and administrators bear the responsibilities of the State, laborers receive the natural duties of the workshops to which they lend their efforts.
Every person of good will is a messenger of the center of accomplishments where they serve the movement of life through ennobling activity.
The streets are full of emissaries from departments, factories, institutes, agencies of inspection, production, welfare, and education, whose combined interests bring about social harmony.
It is necessary, however, not to forget that the values of eternal life would not remain in the world without representatives.
Christ has permanent ambassadors in his sincere disciples.
It is important to consider that in this statement by Paul of Tarsus we see no allusion to a presumptuous priesthood.

All loyal collaborators of Jesus, in whatever station of life and in the farthest corners of the Earth, are known at the spiritual headquarters of divine service. It is with them, devoted cooperators often unknown to the world's beneficiaries, that the Master moves each day, spreading the applied Gospel among earthly creatures, until the final victory.

Understanding this truth, examine your own tendencies, acts, and thoughts. Notice whom you serve, because if you have already received the Good News of Redemption, it is time for you to become an ambassador of its light.

messages.title: To Act Accordingly
paragraphs: “They profess that they know God; but in works they deny him, being abominable, and disobedient, and unto every good work reprobate.” — PAUL (Titus 1:16)
Spiritism, in its aspect of revived Christianity, has a far higher role than that of a mere field for new technical observations of the world's unstable science.
Earth, up to now, concerning religious organizations, has been full of those who profess the existence of God, yet deny Him through individual works.
Direct intercourse between the two worlds, visible and invisible, aims at this sentimental readjustment, so that the divine light may manifest in the ordinary relations of men.
How can one reconcile the knowledge of God with contempt for one's fellows?

The ancient religious schools, by virtue of enlisting as worldly political groupings under the control of the priesthood, ended up stagnating the impulses of faith in outward forms that degrade the living forces of the spirit.

The consoling doctrine of survival and communication between the inhabitants of Earth and the Infinite, with deep and broad foundations in the Gospel, flourishes among creatures with the marks of a new revelation, so that man may be, in common activities, a real affirmation of the good that springs from living faith.

messages.title: Fruitful Earth
paragraphs: “For the earth which drinketh in the rain that cometh oft upon it, and bringeth forth herbs meet for them by whom it is dressed, receiveth blessing from God.” — PAUL (Hebrews 6:7)
The disciples of Christ will always find great lessons in contact with the book of Nature.

The convert of Damascus refers here to the fruitful earth that produces abundantly, soaking in the rain that falls unceasingly upon its surface, representing the favored vessel for receiving God’s blessings.

Let us carry this symbol to the realm of hearts. Only those Spirits who are attentive to the spiritual benefits raining down daily from Heaven are capable of producing the useful fruits of divine service, keeping the Lord’s blessings.

Not that the Father establishes unjustified prerogatives. His merciful protection extends to all without distinction, but not all receive it; that is, countless creatures close themselves off in selfishness and vanity, wrapping their hearts in dense shadows.

God gives at all times, but His children do not always promptly receive the paternal gifts. Only the hearts that open to the spiritual light, allowing themselves to be soaked by the divine dew, correspond to the ideal of the Heavenly Farmer.
The Most High is the Lord of the Universe, the supreme dispenser of blessings to all creatures. On the earthly planet, Jesus is the Sublime Cultivator. The human heart is the earth.

It is our duty, therefore, to understand that the soil is not tilled without being rectified or without being wounded, and that only treated earth will produce fruitful herbs, nourishing and benefiting in the House of God, thus fulfilling the grower's hope.

messages.title: The Paralytic
paragraphs: “And when they could not come nigh unto him for the press, they uncovered the roof where he was: and when they had broken it up, they let down the bed wherein the sick of the palsy lay.” — (MARK 2:4)
Many people profess their need for Christ, but frequently claim obstacles that prevent their sublime approach.
Some cannot find time for meditation; others experience certain anxieties that seem endless to them.

However, for us to feel in the Master’s vicinity, as genuinely interested in his immortal benefits, it is essential to expand our capacity, extend our own resources, and march to meet Him under the light of living faith.

The Gospel of Mark relates to us the curious decision of the paralytic who, locating the house where the Lord was, fully besieged by the crowd, far from missing the opportunity, relied on the help of friends, letting himself be lowered through an opening made in the roof, so as to benefit from contact with the Savior, fervently seizing the divine occasion.

Remember the paralytic of Capernaum, and should you encounter great difficulties in enjoying the presence of Christ due to your material hindrances, turn toward on High with the support of your spiritual friends, and let yourself fall at his divine feet, receiving renewed strength to restore your peace and good cheer.

messages.title: Christian glory
paragraphs: “For our boasting is this: the testimony of our conscience.” — PAUL (2 Corinthians 1:12)
Ever since the savage tribes that preceded the organization of human families, the Earth has been a grand stage used for the display of passing glories.
Competition has intensified the pursuit of transitory honorary titles.

For a long time, the world has known the bloody glories of homicidal struggle, the glories of avarice in the vaults of dead fortune, of pride in emblazoned and useless parchments, of vanity in the deceptive pleasures that precede the tomb; science crystallizes its own in isolated academies, and sectarian religions in external pomp and expressions of proselytism.

In a plane where so many easy glories prevail, the Christian’s glory is deeper and more difficult. The victory of the follower of Jesus is almost always on the reverse side of worldly triumphs. It is the hidden side. Few manage to see it with mortal eyes.
However, this glory is so great that the world neither provides it nor can take it away. It is the testimony of one's own conscience, transformed into a tabernacle of the living Christ.

In the divine instant of this glorification, the soul is dazzled before the perspectives of the Infinite. It is because something strange has happened within, in the mysterious crypt of the heart: the child has found his Father in the fullness of eternity.

messages.title: Education in the home
paragraphs: “You do what you have seen with your father.” — JESUS (John 8:38)

An education based on the full liberty of man's instincts is advocated in today's world, little by little forgetting the ancient teachings regarding character formation in the home; however, society, sooner or later, will be compelled to readjust its purposes.

Human parents must be the first mentors of the creature. From their loving mission stems the organization of the right environment. Corrupted means signify bad parents among those who, at the cost of long sacrifices, manage to maintain, amidst collective carelessness, the possible security against threatening disorder.

Domestic duty will never be a valve for unproductive pleasures, because it constitutes work and cooperation with God. The man or woman who wishes at the same time to be parents and enjoyers of earthly life are blind and will end their foolish efforts, spiritually speaking, in the common ditch of uselessness.

In vain will sociologists improvise to replace education in the home with abstruse substitutes that poison the soul. Only a spirit that has understood the fatherhood of God, above all else, manages to escape the law by which children will always imitate their parents, even when the latter are perverse.
Let us listen to the word of Christ and, if you have children on Earth, keep the Master's declaration as a warning.

messages.title: Self-zeal
paragraphs: “Look to yourselves, that we do not lose what we have worked for, but that we may receive a full reward.” — (2 John, 8)
Physical nature, despite the deficiency of its expressions in the face of the spiritual grandeur of life, provides a vast repository of lessons alluding to self-zeal.

So that the Spirit may receive the sacred opportunity to learn on Earth, it receives a body equivalent to a true sanctuary. The organs and senses are its powers; but such a tabernacle would not rise without maternal dedications and, when the creature takes charge of itself, it will spend a large percentage of time on the cleansing, preservation, and defense of the temple of flesh in which it manifests. It will need to care for the epidermis, the mouth, the eyes, the hands, the ears.
What will happen if any department of the body is forgotten? Excrescences and filth will bring poison to life.
If the physiological framework, which is temporary and mortal, demands all this, what does the Spirit with its eternal values not require of our dedication?
If you have already received some light, watch over yourself so as not to lose it. Intensify it within you.
Wash your thoughts in daily effort, at the fountains of Christ; correct your feelings, renewing your aspirations by placing them in the direction of the Highest. Do not crystallize yourself.
Move forward in the work of self-zeal, for there are 'intangible microbes' that can attack the soul and paralyze it for centuries.

messages.title: Thorns
paragraphs: “Do people pick grapes from thornbushes?” — JESUS (Luke 6:44)
The Christian is an active combatant.
Awakening in the Lord's field, one's vision is stunned by the breadth and complexity of the work. Difficulties, stumbles, tangles, weeds…
And the Gospel, with conceptual propriety, elucidates that one cannot harvest grapes from thornbushes.
However, did Jesus assume the paternity of such a statement so that we might cross our arms in false beatitude?
If the terrain remains absorbed by briars, the disciple has received countless tools from the Master of masters. It is essential, therefore, to face the service.
Christ faced, face to face, the sacrifice for all Humanity.
Will the existence of a few thornbushes be the cause of our insurmountable obstacles?
No. If harvesting is impossible today, let us attack the hard ground. Let us till the arid soil. Let us fertilize it with sweat and tears.
There will always be the fecundating rains of heaven or the generous springs of the earth, blessing our effort. Divine Providence resides everywhere.
Let us not forget the imperative of work and then, in place of the briars, we shall reap the smooth and sweet fruit of the grapevine.

messages.title: Fruits
paragraphs: “Therefore by their fruits you will know them.” — JESUS (Matthew 7:20)
The present world, in its elevated characteristics of intelligence, demands fruits to examine the seeds of principles.
The Christian, therefore, needs to learn from the good tree that receives the elements of Divine Providence through sap, and converts them into utilities for creatures.
The effort of self-analysis is advisable, in order to identify the quality of our own actions.
Many sonorous words simply provide the impression of that cursed fig tree.
It is essential that we know the fruits of our lives, so as to know if they benefit our brothers.

Earthly life represents a vastest opportunity, full of doors and horizons for the eternal light. In its circles, man can daily receive the sap from on High, transforming it into fruits of a divine nature.

indisputably, the present time calls for edifying teachings, but it will understand nothing without practical demonstrations, not least because, since antiquity, wisdom has considered that man's most difficult achievement in the carnal sphere is to live and die faithful to the supreme good.

messages.title: Waiting in Christ
paragraphs: “If in this life only we have hope in Christ, we are of all men the most pitiable.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians 15:19)
The examination of the verse provides the student with very clear explanations.

It is natural to trust in Christ and wait in Him, but what can we say of the anguish of the soul tormented in the circle of earthly cares, selfishly expecting Jesus to come and satisfy its immediate whims?
Would it be reasonable to count on the Lord solely in the transient expressions of fragmentary life?

It is essential to discover the greatness of the concept of 'life', without confusing it with 'a life'. To exist is not to travel from the zone of childhood, with stopovers through youth, maturity, and old age, to the port of death; it is to participate in Creation through feeling and reasoning, it is to be someone and something in the concert of the Universe.
As incarnate beings, few subjects are as confusing as those of death, mistakenly interpreted as the end of that which cannot disappear.
It is imperative, therefore, to wait in Christ with the real notion of eternity. The philosophy of immediatism on Earth turns men into children.

Do not cling to the age of the physical body, to transient circumstances and conditions. Inquire of your own conscience if you remain with Jesus. And await the future, loving and accomplishing through good, convinced that legitimate hope is not rest, but rather trust in incessant work.

messages.title: Firmness of faith
paragraphs: “But the ones on the rock are those who, when they hear, receive the word with joy; and these have no root, who believe for a while and in time of temptation fall away.” — JESUS (Luke 8:13)

The word 'rock' among us is wont to symbolize rigidity and hindrance; however, we should not forget that Jesus occasionally resorted to it to signify firmness. Peter was once called by the Master the 'living rock of faith'.
The Gospel of Luke speaks to us of those who are upon the rock, who will receive the word with joy, but who, due to the absence of root, fall, fatally, at the time of temptations.
Not a few are surprised by this promise of temptations, which, moreover, must be considered as indispensable experiences.

In the domestic organization, parents will excessively care for their children when they are little, but an excess of tenderness is inappropriate at the time when they need to demonstrate self-effort.
The head of service will teach new assistants with patience and then demand, with justice, expressions of their own work.

We thus recognize, by Luke's note, that in religious experiences it is not advisable for anyone to rest upon the spiritual firmness of others; while the imprudent one rests on strange bases, he will probably be calm, but if he does not possess roots of security within himself, he will stray in difficult times in order to seek foreign foundations.
Everything invites man to the work of his improvement and enlightenment.
Let us respect the firmness of faith wherever it exists, but let us not forget the building of our own for stable victory.

messages.title: Children and servants
paragraphs: “And a slave does not abide in the house forever, but a son abides forever.” — JESUS (John 8:35)
In His exemplification, Jesus taught us how to attain the title of sonship to God.
Active and incessant work, detachment from the inferior interests of the world, and perfect submission to divine designs constituted the fundamental traits of His lessons on Earth.

Many men, notable for their goodness, adamantine character, worthy priests, and sincere believers, may be dedicated servants of the Almighty. But Christ induced us to be something more. He invited us to be children, explaining that these remain 'forever in the house'.
And the servants? These often undergo modifications. They will not always remain by the Father's side.
But is the Earth not equally a dependency, albeit a humble one, of God's house? Here beats the essence of the lesson.

The Master alluded to servants as persons susceptible to various self-interests. Children, however, share interests in common with the Father. The former, serving God and themselves, because as servants they await remuneration, can suffer anxieties, afflictions, delirium, and harsh pains. Children, though, are always 'in the house', that is, they will remain in peace, superior to the hardest circumstances, recognizing above all else that they belong to God.

messages.title: Idols
paragraphs: “That you abstain from things offered to idols.” — (ACTS 15:29)
Religious environments have not yet perceived the full extent of the concept of idolatry.
When we refer to idols, everything seems to point exclusively to materialized images on stone altars. This, however, is the simplest face of the problem.
Men need to exterminate, first of all, other more dangerous idols that disturb their vision and feeling.
The soul often lingers in deceptive adoration.

The verse refers to 'things offered to idols', and man is surrounded by the things of life. By moving them, the creature enriches its evolutionary heritage. It is necessary, however, to differentiate those found consecrated to God from those sacrificed to idols.

The ambition to attain spiritual values, according to Jesus, is called virtue; the purpose of achieving transitory advantages in the carnal field, on the plane of unjust restlessness, is called foolishness.

The 'places of honor', which the Master recommended we avoid, likewise represent idols. Therefore, not consecrating the things of life and the soul to the cult of earthly immediatism is escaping a gross adorative position.

When you find yourself, then, preoccupied with failures and displeasures within your individual circle, do not forget that Christ, by accepting the cross, taught us the resource of eliminating the idolatry maintained in our path by ourselves.

messages.title: While it is day
paragraphs: “I must work the works of Him who sent Me while it is day.” — JESUS (John 9:4)

We know that the divine labor of the Master is incessant and takes place in a perennial and resplendent day of opportunities; however, to imprint in our understanding the real value of the passing on Earth, Jesus speaks to us of His convenience in seizing the opportunity of direct contact with creatures.

If such an attitude constitutes a reason for concern for the Master, what can we say of ourselves, in the carnal circles or in the spheres immediately adjacent to them, within the obligations that fall to us in the sacred accomplishment of eternal good?
Christ does not refer to the need to speak of the works of God, but rather to build them in due time.

We are not unaware that, since He is the Envoy of the Almighty in the world, the disciples of the Good News are, in their turn, the messengers of His love in the most secluded places of the earthly orb. Those whose hearts vibrate toward the Gospel are effectively emissaries of the Divine Lesson among companions of material life, wherever they may be, and blessed will be all those who take advantage of the generous day, accomplishing within themselves and around their steps the sanctified works of Him who sent them.

Never disdain, therefore, the position in which you find yourself. Seek to value it through all the means within your reach, so that your effort may be a source of blessings for others and for your own circle. Never forget to make the most of time in the acquisition of light, while it is day.

messages.title: Spiritual Gifts
paragraphs: “And as they came down from the mountain, Jesus charged them, saying, Tell the vision to no man, until the Son of man be risen again from the dead.” — (MATTHEW, 17.9)
If man needs great prudence in the acts of ordinary life, even greater vigilance is required of the creature in dealing with the Spiritual Sphere.
It is the Divine Master Himself who exemplifies this for us.

Having led James, Peter, and John to the marvelous revelations of Tabor, where He was transfigured before the eyes of His companions, alongside glorious emissaries of the higher Plane, He solicitously recommends: “Tell the vision to no man, until the Son of man be risen from the dead.”
The Master did not mandate falsehood; however, He advised keeping the truth for the opportune occasion.
Each situation demands a certain quota of knowledge.
Jesus knew that the premature narration of the sublime vision could awaken misunderstandings and sarcasm in vulgar and idle conversations.
Let us not forget that we are all marching toward God, though it should be noted that the paths are not the same for everyone.

If you keep a precious spiritual experience within yourself, undoubtedly you can use it every day, utilizing it in appropriate doses to help each of those who surround you in the particular position in which they find themselves; but do not cheapen what the higher Sphere has granted you, handing the gift over to criminal misunderstandings, because everything that is conquered from Heaven is an untransferable achievement.

messages.title: Origin of Temptations
paragraphs: “But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” — (JAMES, 1.14)

Generally, when great evils arise, those who participate in the fall impute the cause that determined their disaster to God. They remember, belatedly, that the Father is Almighty and allege that the temptation could only have come from the Divine Design.

Yes, God is Absolute Love, so much so that the fallen remain standing, relying on the eternal values of time, supported by His compassionate hands. Temptations, however, do not proceed from the Heavenly Paternity.
Would the human statesman perhaps be responsible for the disrespectful acts of those who violate the law he created?
The Apostle's references are profoundly touched by the light of Heaven. “Every man is tempted, when he is drawn away by his own lust.”

Let us examine both nouns "temptation" and "lust" particularly. The first externalizes the second, which constitutes the vicious and perverse fondo of primitive human nature. To be tempted is to listen to one's own malice, is to harbor the inferior suggestions of oneself, for even if evil comes from the exterior, it only materializes and perseveres if we attune ourselves to it in the intimacy of the heart.
Finally, let us highlight the verb "to draw away" (to be attracted). We will verify the extent of our inferiority by the nature of the things and situations that attract us.
James's observation is a sure roadmap for analyzing the origin of temptations.

Remember that each day has specific magnetic situations. Consider the essence of everything that has attracted you over the course of the hours, and you will eliminate your own evils, fulfilling the good that Jesus desires.

messages.title: What Is the Flesh?
paragraphs: “If we live in the Spirit, let us also walk in the Spirit.” — PAUL (Galatians, 5.25)
Almost always, when spirituality is spoken of, many people appear who complain about the demands of the flesh.

It is true that the apostles often spoke of the lusts of the flesh, of its criminal impulses and harmful desires. We ourselves frequently feel the need to use the symbol to make the lessons of the Gospel more accessible. The Master Himself figured that the spirit, as a divine element, is strong, but that the flesh, as a human expression, is weak.
However, what is the flesh?

Each spiritual personality has its fluidic body, and have you not yet perceived, perhaps, that the flesh is a composite of condensed fluids? Naturally, these fluids, upon reuniting, will obey the imperatives of terrestrial existence, in what you designate as the law of heredity; but this assembly is passive and does not determine by itself. We can picture it as a terrestrial house within which the Spirit is the director—a dwelling that will take on the good or bad characteristics of its possessor.
When we speak of sins of the flesh, we can translate the expression as faults due to the inferior condition of the spiritual man upon the planet.
Debasing desires, depressing impulses, ingratitude, bad faith, the trait of the traitor, were never of the flesh.
It is necessary for man to install within himself the understanding of his need for self-mastery, awakening his faculties as a disciplinologist and renewer of himself in Jesus Christ.

One of the greatest absurdities of some disciples is to attribute to the set of passive cells that serve man the paternity of the crimes and deviations of the Earth, when we know that everything proceeds from the spirit.

messages.title: Sadness
paragraphs: “For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.” — PAUL (2 Corinthians, 7.10)

As we observe in Paul's warning, there is "a sorrow according to God" and another "according to the Earth." The former solves problems pertaining to true life; the latter is a path to death, as a symbol of stagnation in the deviation of feelings.

Many people consider incessant lamentation and continued boredom to be virtues. We find the sad ones due to the absence of money adequate for excesses; we see the tortured ones who lament the impossibility of practicing evil; we hear those addicted to sickly complaining, incapable of the pleasure of serving without goads. This is the sadness of the world that binds the Spirit to the web of corrective and dangerous reincarnations.

Rare men are touched by "godly sorrow." Very few contemplate themselves, considering the extent of the flaws that pertain to them, on the march toward the restoration of life, in the present and in the future. Whoever advances along this redemptive path, if they weep, never reaches the plane of sickly sobbing and uselessness, because they know how to readjust themselves, making use of time, through blessed blows of effort for the new edifices of destiny.

messages.title: Men and Angels
paragraphs: “Whereas angels, which are greater in power and might, bring not railing accusation against them before the Lord.” — (2 Peter, 2.11)

It is regrettable to observe the large number of people who are always ready to utter blasphemous sentences against one another. Levity dominates their conversations, and pettiness corrupts their activities in the most diverse sectors of life.

Except for the sincere cultivators of religious light, almost all men remain at the threshold of harsh situations in which defamatory effort poisons their life. They harbor unjust antipathies toward brothers of professional activity, toward the neighbor who does not accept their ideas, toward companions who do not attune to their principles. And since the law is one of compensation and exchange, they will receive the same destructive vibrations from colleagues and neighbors.
Silent wars in this sense sometimes have a secular duration.

However, the boastful man is always surrounded by the beneficial action of enlightened and generous Spirits who, the more they are clothed with divine power, the more they pity human frailties, extending welcoming hands to them along the way and never pronouncing condemning judgments before the Lord.

Whenever you are compelled to analyze the efforts of others, remember Peter's word. Do not forget that angelic entities, living and sublime springs of strength and power, never utter accusatory sentences against you before God.

messages.title: Always Forward
paragraphs: “For of whom a man is overcome, of the same is he brought in bondage.” — (2 Peter, 2.19)
The incarnate Spirit, in order to achieve the high objectives of life, needs to recognize its condition as a learner, extracting profit from each experience without becoming enslaved.
Money or material necessity, illness and bodily health, are educational conditions of immense value for those who know how to seize the opportunity of elevation in its legitimate essence.
Unfortunately, however, generally speaking, the creature only recognizes such truths when it approaches transformation through the death of the terrestrial body.

Rare people pass from one situation to another with due dignity. Commonly, if a rich person is transferred to a place of scarcity, they indulge in such extreme lamentations that they end up defeated, as a miserable servant of mendicancy; if a poor person is led to a high financial position, not infrequently they transform into a foolish ruler, enslaving themselves to extravagance and tyranny.
Great care is imperative so that transitory positions do not paralyze the soul's flights.
Keep rectitude of conscience and throw yourself into edifying work; then, in your eyes, every situation will represent an opportunity to reach "higher" and "further on."

messages.title: Hegemony of Jesus
paragraphs: “Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am.” — (JOHN, 8.58)
It is impossible to locate Christ in History in the manner of any human personality.

The divine revelation of which He was an Exalted Emissary and the harmonious set of His examples and teachings speak louder than the unstable message of the highest philosophers who visited the world.

Before Abraham, or preceding the great figures of wisdom and love in world history, Christ was already the luminous center of human achievements. From His mercy departed the missionaries of light who, launched into the movement of terrestrial evolution, fulfilled, more or less well, the redemptive task incumbent upon them among creatures, preceding the eternal edifices of the Gospel.

The historical localization of Jesus recalls the personal presence of the Lord of the Vineyard. The Envoy of God, the Loving and Wise Tutor, came to open new paths and establish the saving struggle so that men might recognize the condition of eternity proper to them.

The philosophers and illustrious friends of Humanity spoke to creatures, revealing within themselves a refracted light, like that of the satellite illuminating earthly nights; the appeals of these worthy and enlightened ambassadors are beautiful and edifying, yet they never escape a mixture of shadows.
The coming of Christ, however, is different. In His Divine Presence we have the source of positive truth, the resplendent Sun.

messages.title: Little Suffices
paragraphs: “Judas saith unto him, Lord, how is it that thou wilt manifest thyself unto us, and not unto the world?” — (JOHN, 14.22)
One of the most surprising facts of Christianity is the position chosen by the Savior to announce eternal truths.

Jesus does not appear in sensational decrees, revolutionary trophies, or situations of dominion. He arrives in peace at the simple manger, exemplifies labor, converses with a few obscure men in a humble village, and with that alone prepares the transformation of all Humanity.
For the inferior world, however, Thaddaeus's question is still fully current.

Vulgar creatures only understand those who impose themselves upon others, even if, to do so, they are compelled to hear tyrannical sentences uttered from bloody tribunals; they only comprehend spectacles that wound the sight and the theatrical gestures of those who dominate for a day only to suffer tomorrow the same transformative process imposed on the transitory world toward which they head.

Jesus, however, spoke to the immortal soul. For this reason, His revelations never die. Furthermore, He proved that social or economic prominence is not necessary for the service of utility to God, demonstrating also that a city with its regimentations and lavish resources is not indispensable for this. Edifying and simple principles, a nameless village, and a few friends will suffice.
The bearer of good will knows that this was the material with which Christ initiated the remodeling of terrestrial life.

messages.title: The Untransferable Gold
paragraphs: “I counsel thee to buy of me gold tried in the fire, that thou mayest be rich.” — (REVELATION, 3:18)
Easy-cost acquisitions are always vulgar.

It is not difficult for ordinary man to pursue financial possibilities, entice petty interests, and invent a thousand resources to achieve inferior ends; however, those who adopt such a norm are unaware of the sacred character of the most humble patrimony that falls into their hands, abusing possession only to feel, afterwards, poorer than ever.
The divine recommendation is sufficiently clear.
For a man to become rich, he must acquire gold tried in the fire—a fortune that proceeds from the generous hands of the Almighty.

Only this spiritual wealth, acquired in situations of arduous labor, deep understanding, victory over oneself, and incessant effort, will confer upon the Spirit the position of legitimate ascendancy, permanent well-being, beyond the transformations imposed by the tomb, and will only carry out such a lofty conquest after completely surrendering to the Father for the greatness of the Divine Service.

The man mobilized by man may undoubtedly receive voluminous salaries. Let us agree, however, that these goods always transform or one day will be transferred to another by the provisional holder. However, when the worker spends his possibilities in the works of good, forgetting selfishness, disinterested in himself, placing the objectives of the Work of God above the caprices of personality, struggling, loving, suffering, and surrendering to Him, he undoubtedly acquires the eternal and untransferable gold.

messages.title: Terrestrial and Celestial Things
paragraphs: “If I have told you earthly things, and ye believe not, how shall ye believe, if I tell you of heavenly things?” — JESUS (John, 3.12)

In the interchange with the spiritual world, complaints are frequent from certain scholars regarding the absence of information from communicating entities concerning the particularities alluding to the activities in which they move.

Why are the disincarnate not more explicit about the new kind of life to which they have been called? What are their cities, their houses, their common relational processes like? Through what means are they organized hierarchically? Do they have governments along terrestrial lines?

Others inquire regarding the reasons why scientists liberated from the physical Plane do not return to old research and achievement centers, popularizing methods of healing for so-called incurable diseases or revealing new inventions that accelerate world progress.
These are the hasty arguments of human laziness.

If communicating spirits have dealt almost exclusively with the material existing around the earthly creatures themselves, in a methodical course of introduction to higher tasks, and have not yet been fully heard, what would happen if they forgot serious commitments, indulging in the pleasure of premature commentaries?
Man must understand that God grants the aids; however, each Spirit is obliged to carve its own glory.

The great task of the spiritual world, in its mechanism of relations with incarnate men, is not to bring sensational and extemporaneous knowledge, but to teach men to read the divine signs that terrestrial life contains within itself, illuminating their march toward superior spirituality.

messages.title: The Banquet of the Publicans
paragraphs: “And when the Pharisees saw it, they said unto his disciples, Why eateth your Master with publicans and sinners?” — (MATTHEW, 9:11)
In general, the Christian community, in its various sectors, has not yet perceived the full significance of the Master's banquet among publicans and sinners.

Not only the Last Supper with His most intimate disciples was clothed in singular importance. In that Jerusalem gathering, which took place at Passover, Jesus reveals to us the sublime character of His relations with the friends of His apostolate. It is an intimate and familial agape, solemnizing an affectionate farewell and a divine lesson at the same time.

However, it is necessary to remember that the Master attended this circle last of all, for He had already dined affectionately with the publicans and sinners. He shared the supper with the disciples on a day of high religious vibration, but He had shared the joy of those who lived far from the faith, gathering them generously and bestowing upon them the same blessings born of His love.

The banquet of the publicans has special significance in the history of Christianity. It demonstrates that the Lord embraces all who desire the excellence of His spiritual nourishment in the labors of His vineyard, and that not only on occasions of faith does He remain present among those who love Him; at any time and in any situation, He is ready to attend to the souls that seek Him.

The banquet of the sinners was offered before the supper with the disciples. And let us not forget that the divine table continues in sublime service. It remains for the guests to make use of the concession.

messages.title: Pretensions
paragraphs: “I have planted, Apollos watered; but God gave the increase.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 3:6)
The church of Corinth was full of claims from restless disciples.
Certain members of the institution placed greater value on Paul's efforts, while others conferred privileges of edification upon Apollos.
