The apostle to the Gentiles was divinely inspired when commenting on the subject in his letter.
Why individual pretensions in a work of which we are all beneficiaries of the same Lord?

Today, it is commendable to examine Paul's recommendation to the Corinthians, for it is no longer the beneficiaries of the Christian organization who rejoice at receiving the blessings of the Gospel through this or that worker of Christ, but rather the laborers of the cause who, at times, arrive at the field of service displaying themselves as prominent figures of this or that work of good.
The certainty that “every good gift comes from God” constitutes an excellent exercise for common labors.

It is interesting to observe how man is always ready to appropriate circumstances that elevate him easily in the opinion of others. Always inclined to stand out in the circles of good that do not yet substantially belong to him, he rarely assumes the paternity of the errors he commits. This is one of the singular contradictions of the creature.

Do not forget. The service belongs to everyone. Some plant, others fertilize. Live contentedly in the sector of work entrusted to your hands or your intelligence and serve without pretensions, because man prepares the earth and organizes the sowing by the mercy of Providence, but it is God who puts flowers on the branches and grants the fruits, according to merit.

messages.title: For Love
paragraphs: “He hath blinded their eyes, and hardened their heart; that they should not see with their eyes, nor understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them.” — (JOHN, 12:40)
The humblest plans of Nature reveal Divine Providence in a sovereign expression of care and love.
The lilies do not spin, the birds do not store provisions, and a mysterious force provides them with what is necessary.

Observation of animal life demonstrates the extremes of tenderness with which the Father watches over Creation from the beginning: here, a wing; there, an extra tooth; yonder, an unknown power of defense.
The grand revelation of love affirms itself in everything.

However, when the Father calls His children to cooperate in His works, behold, the ungrateful often stand out, converting the favors received not into noble and constructive duties, but into new demands; then, it becomes necessary for their hearts to harden more and more, because, outside of equilibrium, they will find suffering in the indispensable restoration of the external laws of that same divine love. When they see nothing beyond the material aspects of the transitory landscape, the purifying struggle unexpectedly ensues.
This is when Jesus arrives and operates the cure.
Only then does the ungrateful person return to the understanding of Divine Magnanimity.
Love equilibrates, pain restores. That is why we often hear: “I would never have believed in God if I had not suffered.”

messages.title: In Yourself
paragraphs: “Hast thou faith? have it to thyself before God.” — PAUL (Romans, 14:22)
In the mechanism of daily achievements, the creature cannot forget that expression of self-confidence which it must maintain within the sphere of obligations it has to fulfill before God.

Those who live in the certainty of divine promises are those who keep faith in the relative power entrusted to them and, increasing it through their own effort, proceed in definitive edifications, with a view toward eternity.

Those who, however, remain disheartened regarding their possibilities, waiting upon human promises, give the idea of fragments of cork, without a purpose of their own, at the mercy of the waters, without a route and without an anchorage.

Naturally, no one can live on Earth without trusting someone from their closest circle; but affection, the friendly bond, the warmth of elevated dedications cannot exclude self-confidence before the Creator.

In the sphere of each creature, God can do all things; however, He does not dispense with the cooperation, the will, and the trust of the child to accomplish His work. A father who mechanically made the happiness framework of his descendants would exterminate, in each one of them, their most brilliant faculties.

Why will you remain undecided, if the Lord has conferred upon you this or that righteous labor? Do it uprightly, because if God has confidence in you for something, you must trust in yourself before Him.

messages.title: To the Mountains
paragraphs: “Then let them which be in Judaea flee into the mountains.” — JESUS (MATTHEW, 24:16)

Referring to the painful moments that would mark planetary renewal, the Master advised those who were in Judea to seek the mountains. The warning is profound, because by the term “Judea” we must take the “spiritual region” of all those who, through intimate aspirations, approach the Master for supreme illumination.

And the present state of the Earth is one of the strongest pictures of this kind. In every corner, struggles and ruins are established. Deadly poisons are inoculated by unconscious politics into the popular masses. The lowland is filled with tremendous fogs. The holy places remain full of abominable darkness. Some men walk by the sinister glare of fires. The ground is fertilized with blood and tears for the sowing of the future.

The moment has arrived for those who remain in Judea to withdraw to the “mountains” of higher ideals. It is indispensable for the disciple of good to remain on spiritual heights, without abandoning the elevated cooperation that the Master exemplified on Earth; that he may consolidate his position there as a faithful collaborator, invincible in peace and hope, convinced that, after the passing of the men of disturbance, bearers of wreckage and tears, it is the children of labor who sow joy once again and rebuild the edifice of life.

messages.title: Worse for Them
paragraphs: “And he began to say unto them, This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears.” — (LUKE, 4:21)
Taking his place among the inhabitants of Nazareth, Jesus exclaimed, after reading some of Isaiah's promises: “This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears.”

Religious groups are sought after, almost always, by curious investigators who, at first glance, seem like itinerant wanderers; however, it must be recognized that there are always spiritual influences compelling their spirits to examination and consultation; they themselves would not know how to define this subtle and silent call that forces them to listen, at times, to great lectures, long talks, expositions, and elucidations that seemingly do not interest them.

In various circumstances, they claim to tolerate the subject in view of the code of politeness and mutual respect; however, it is not so. There is something stronger, beyond good manners, that compels them to listen. It is that the moment of spiritual revelation has sounded for them.

Many remain indifferent, ironic, recalcitrant, but the responsibility of knowledge already weighs on their shoulders and, if they could feel the truth more clearly, they would harbor the affectionate admonition of the Master in the depths of their souls: “Today this Scripture is fulfilled in your ears.”
Mercy has been granted. Jesus gave something of His infinite goodness. The divine word was fulfilled. If those concerned do not benefit from it, so much the worse for them.

messages.title: One Only Lord
paragraphs: “No servant can serve two masters.” — JESUS (LUKE, 16:13)

If Christians of all times have encountered painful situations of perplexity along the roads of the world, it is because, after the apostles and martyrs, the majority has cooperated in the dissemination of false sentiments regarding the Lord whom they ought to serve.
Since Christ's Kingdom is not yet of this world, one cannot satisfy Jesus and the world at the same time. Vice and duty do not ally themselves in daily marching.
What can be said of a man who intends to direct two centers of antagonistic activity in simultaneous effort?
Christ is the central line of our thoughts.

He is the sole Lord, after God, for the children of the Earth, with inalienable rights, for He is our light from the first evolutionary day and redeemed us for salvation with the sacrifices of His love.

We are His servants. We need to attend to His sublime interests with humility. And for this, it is necessary neither to flee from the world nor from the responsibilities that surround us, but rather to transform the part of service entrusted to our effort, in the circles of struggle, into a cell of Christ's work.

The disciple's primary task is, therefore, to understand the transitory character of carnal existence, to consecrate himself to the Master as the center of life, and to offer His divine benefits to his fellows.

messages.title: Legion of Evil
paragraphs: “And he asked him, What is thy name? And he answered, saying, My name is Legion: for we are many.” — (MARK, 5:9)
The Master bequeathed an unforgettable lesson to the disciples in this passage of the Gospels.
As the dispenser of good and peace, Jesus approaches the perverse Spirit who receives Him in despair.
Christ does not grow impatient and affectionately asks his name, to which the interpellated one replies: “My name is Legion, for we are many.”
The apprentices who followed Him did not know how to interpret the scene in all its symbolic expression. And to this day, people ask about the content of the occurrence with justifiable strangeness.
It is because the Lord wished to transmit an immortal teaching to His companions in the redemptive task.

Before the delinquent and disturbed Spirit, He was only one; the interlocutor, however, called himself “Legion,” representing an overwhelming majority, personifying the vast mass of inferior and criminal intentions. The Master revealed that, for an indeterminate time, good would be in a diminutive proportion compared to evil in sweeping avalanches.

If you find yourself, therefore, in the service of Christ on Earth, do not forget to persevere in the good through all the hours of life, convinced that evil makes itself felt all around, like a threatening legion, demanding profound serenity and great trust in Christ, with work and vigilance, until final victory.

messages.title: What Have We to Do with Christ?
paragraphs: “Let us alone; what have we to do with thee, thou Jesus of Nazareth? art thou come to destroy us? I know thee who thou art, the Holy One of God.” — (MARK, 1:24)
It is a great mistake to suppose that the Divine Master had finished His active service on Calvary.
Jesus continues walking in all directions of the world; His redemptive Gospel is triumphing, inch by inch, in the terrain of hearts.
A similar circumstance must be remembered because malevolent Spirits also try to repel the Lord daily.
The evangelist refers to perverse entities that possessed the human body. However, these infernal intelligences continue to dominate vast organisms of the world.

In the building of politics, erected to maintain the principles of divine order, they arise under the names of discord and tyranny; in commerce, formed to establish fraternity, they appear with the nicknames of ambition and selfishness; in religions and sciences, sacred organizations of universal progress, they rush forth under the denominations of pride, vanity, dogmatism, and sectarian intolerance.
Not only the body of the human creature suffers the obsession of perverse Spirits. Human groups and institutions suffer much more.
And when Jesus approaches through the Gospel, people and organizations hastily ask: “What have we to do with Christ? What do we have to do with spiritual life?”
It is necessary to remain vigilant in the face of such subtleties, because the adversary is also penetrating the circles of evangelical Spiritism, dressed in the brilliant robes of false science.

messages.title: Doctrinations
paragraphs: “Notwithstanding in this rejoice not, that the spirits are subject unto you; but rather rejoice, because your names are written in heaven.” — JESUS (LUKE, 10:20)
We frequently encounter new disciples of the Gospel exulting with contentment because disturbed spirits are subject to them.
They narrate with joy the results of thrilling sessions in which they successfully doctrinating entities that were often ignorant and perverse.

Many get lost in the tangle of these dazzlements and proceed to multiply the so-called “practical works,” thirsty to guide, through more direct contacts, the unconscious or unhappy friends of the Planes immediately adjacent to the carnal Sphere.
Jesus recommended the appropriate remedy for similar situations in which apprentices, almost always interested in teaching others, gradually forget to learn for their own benefit.

May sincere indoctrinators rejoice, not for subduing disincarnate creatures in despair, convinced that under such circumstances good is ministered, not strictly by them in their human guise, but by emissaries of Jesus, charitable and solicitous, who use them as channels for Divine Mercy; may this joy be born of the opportunity to serve the good, with a conscience attuned to the Divine Master, amidst the sweet certainties of faith solidly guarded in the heart.
The Master's word to His companions is very expressive and can amply benefit the restless disciples of today.

messages.title: In Dealings with the Invisible
paragraphs: “And he called them unto him, and said unto them in parables, How can Satan cast out Satan?” — (MARK, 3.23)

This passage from the Gospel is highly enlightening for contemporary companions who, in the tasks of Christian Spiritism, strive to help unhappy disembodied souls re-balance themselves on the redemptive path.
Let no one expect immediate success when seeking to support those who have lost themselves in disorientation.

It is impossible to dispense with the collaboration of time for the characters of human tragedies to be enlightened and, as we know, not even the apostles were able to immediately convince the disturbed entities regarding the realism of their dangerous situation. However, without sterilizing attitudes, the disciple can do much in the sector of these illuminating activities. Today, companions devoted to service still suffer persecution from the adversaries of the light, who attribute to them a gloomy pact with wicked powers. Religious sectarianism brands them as followers of Satan, imposing tortures and humiliations upon them.

However, the exact same reproaches and unwarranted recriminations were hurled at the Divine Master by the organized priesthood of his time. Attending to the sick and the obsessed, surrendered to destructive forces of the shadow, Jesus received the title of sorcerer, son of Beelzebub. This constitutes a significant reminder that, naturally, will instill much comfort in new disciples.

messages.title: A Challenge
paragraphs: “And now why tarriest thou?” — (ACTS, 22.16)

Relating to the crowd his unforgettable experience at the gates of Damascus, the Apostle to the Gentiles recounts that, faced with the perplexity that confronted him, Ananias asked him in fraternal warning: “And now why tarriest thou?”
The interrogation deserves to be meditated upon by all who have already received invitations, appeals, gifts, or assistance from the Spiritual Plane.
Innumerable beneficiaries of the Gospel bind themselves to obstacles of all kinds in the nebulous province of complaint.

If blessed by the light of faith, they lament not having known the truth in their youth or in the days of plenty; yet, in mature age or material difficulty, they sustain the exact same inferior tendencies that marked their attitudes in the circles of ignorance.
In words, they always manifest great goodwill; however, when called to active service, they immediately complain about the lack of money, health, time, or strength.
They are contradictory workers who, at a time of organic balance, demand rest and, at a time of bodily illness, claim nostalgia for service.
It is essential to combat these destructive expressions of personality.

In any position and at any time, we are surrounded by possibilities for service with the Savior. And, for all of us who have received divine gifts in a thousand different ways, the sublime challenge has been pronounced: “And now why tarriest thou?”

messages.title: Self-Care
paragraphs: “Take heed unto thyself, and unto the doctrine; continue in them: for in doing this thou shalt both save thyself, and them that hear thee.” — PAUL (1 Timothy, 4.16)
Everywhere there are platoons of the army of pessimists, with crossed arms, in dismay.
They do not understand work and trust, serenity and living faith, and they tend to adopt high-sounding phrases, condemning situations and creatures.
Sometimes these negative soldiers are people who have assumed the responsibility of guiding. Yet, despite the importance of their roles, they remain deluded.

Earthly difficulties are indeed enormous, and their obstacles demand great effort from noble souls in transit on the planet, but it is imperative that each disciple not lose self-care. It is indispensable to watch over the inner field, to value disciplines and accept them, as well as to examine the needs of the heart. This procedure leads the spirit to vaster horizons, effecting an immense breadth of comprehension within which we harbor, inwardly, holy respect for all evolutionary circles, thereby diluting the patrimony of constructive hope and renewing optimism.
Taking heed of oneself is working for one's own salvation and the redemption of others. This is the logical path for the acquisition of eternal values.

For the learner to confine themselves to theoretical excesses, shunning the edifices of service, is to rest on the banks of labor, placing themselves, little by little, on the ungrateful terrain of satanic criticism regarding what was not the object of their attention and experience.

messages.title: Property
paragraphs: “But when the young man heard that saying, he went away sorrowful: for he had great possessions.” — (MATTHEW, 19.22)

The instinct of property has provoked great revolutions, staining peoples with blood. In the most diverse regions of the planet breathe men restless with material possession, jealous of their temporary expressions and willing to die in their defense.
This demonstrates that man has not yet learned how to possess.

With this argument, we do not wish to induce the creature to forget the provident ant, adopting the careless cicada as a model. We merely invite whoever reads us to examine the precariousness of ephemeral possessions.
Every earthly conquest should be utilized by the soul as a force for elevation.

Man will gain a sanctifying impulse by understanding that he only truly possesses what is found within him, in the spiritual content of his life. Everything related to the exterior — such as creatures, landscapes, and transitory goods — belongs to God, who will grant them according to their merits.

This reality felt and lived constitutes a brilliant light on the path, teaching the disciple the sublime law of use, so that property does not represent a source of restlessness and sadness, as happened to the youth in the teachings of Jesus.

messages.title: Conversion
paragraphs: “And when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.” — JESUS (Luke, 22.32)
The conversion of man is not as easy as bearers of hasty convictions claim.
Many say “I believe,” but few can declare “I am transformed.”

The Master's words to Simon Peter are very symbolic. Jesus uttered them on the eve of Calvary, at the solemn hour of the final meeting with the disciples. He recommended that the fisherman of Capernaum confirm his brethren in the faith when he was converted.

It is worth noting that Peter was always His most active companion in the apostolate. The Master always preferred his humble home to exercise the divine ministry of love. For three successive years, Simon witnessed astonishing events. He saw lepers cleansed, the blind regain their sight, the mad recover their reason; he was dazzled by the vision of the Messiah transfigured on Tabor, witnessed Lazarus emerge from the darkness of the tomb, and yet, he was not yet converted.
The immense labors of Jerusalem, personal sacrifices, and enormous struggles with oneself would be necessary so that he could convert to the Gospel and bear witness to Christ before his brethren.

It is not because your soul marvels at spiritual revelations that you will be converted and transformed for Jesus. Simon Peter witnessed these revelations alongside the Messiah Himself and it took a great deal to attain these titles. Let us work, therefore, to convert ourselves. Only under these conditions shall we be qualified for testimony.

messages.title: Goads
paragraphs: “It is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.” — JESUS (Acts, 9.5)
The evolutionary path is always replete with goads. Otherwise, we would not discern the redemptive door.

God gives Himself to the children of all Creation, shares the treasures of His infinite love with everyone, and stimulates them to elevate themselves through a thousand different ways; however, there are numerous circles like Earth where creatures do not perceive these glorious realities and paralyze their march, sleeping in the bed of illusion.
Before such inertia, the messengers of Providence, who were entrusted with the task of illuminating those lingering in the shadow, promote resources so that awakening takes place.

Aware that God gives everything — life, paths, infinite goods, inspiring geniuses — and only asks creatures to turn to His paternal arms, these divine emissaries organize the goads out of love for their wards.

In this program, Jesus created the noblest incitements for the terrestrial Sphere. Wealth and poverty, ugliness and beauty, suffering and struggle are goads or opportunities instituted by Christ for the benefit of humanity.
Each existence and each person has their particular difficulty, symbolizing a blessed opportunity. Analyze your life, locate your goads, and do not turn against them.
If a spirit of the greatness of Paul of Tarsus could not kick against the goad, imagine what will be asked of our effort.

messages.title: Youth
paragraphs: “Flee also youthful lusts: but follow righteousness, faith, charity, peace, with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart.” — PAUL (II Timothy, 2.22)

Almost always, those who address youth attribute such powers to it that young people end up in frank disorientation, deceived and distracted. It is customary to expect the safeguarding of everything from them.
We agree with their vast possibilities, but we cannot forget that this phase of earthly existence is the one that presents the greatest number of needs in the chapter of guidance.

The young person will be able to do much and will do much if the spirit aged in experience does not forsake them in labor. They will not manage to erect anything new if they do not draw upon the efforts that preceded their activities. In everything, they will depend on their predecessors.

Youth can be compared to the hopeful departure of a boat for an important voyage. Childhood was the preparation, and old age will be the arrival at port. All phases require the lessons of experienced sailors, learning to organize and finish the voyage with desirable success.
It is essential to properly support the youthful mindset and that no one offer them perspectives of illusory domination.
The desires of the younger ones do not always constitute the index of security in the future.
Youth may do much, but let it follow, in all things, “righteousness, faith, charity, peace, with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart.”

messages.title: Science and Love
paragraphs: “Knowledge puffeth up, but charity edifieth.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 8.1)

Science may be full of power, but only love benefits. Science, in all epochs, has achieved numerous evolutionary expressions. We see it in the world, exhibiting accomplishments that seemed almost unattainable. Enormous machines cross the skies and the depths of the oceans. The word is transmitted wirelessly over long distances. The press disseminates worldwide reasoning. But for this very science, it matters little whether man uses its fruits for good or for evil. It understands neither selflessness nor holy purposes.

Love, however, approaches its labors and rectifies them, conferring upon it the consciousness of good. It teaches that each machine should serve as a divine utility on man's path to God, that the edifying word should only be transmitted as a gift from the Most High, and that the publication of elevated reasoning would only be just for the redemptive effort of creatures.

If science discovers explosives, love clarifies how to use them in opening roads to connect peoples; if the former crafts a book, the latter teaches how to record comforting truth. Science can materialize many useful works, but only love institutes the highest works. We do not doubt that the former, well interpreted, can endow man with a courageous heart; however, only the latter can give an illuminated heart.

The world remains in obscurity and suffering because science has been hired out by hatred, which annihilates and perverts, and it will only reach the port of safety when it fully surrenders to the love of Jesus Christ.

messages.title: Passes (Magnetic Healing / Spiritual Passes)
paragraphs: “And besought him greatly, saying, My little daughter lieth at the point of death: I pray thee, come and lay thy hands on her, that she may be healed; and she shall live.” — (MARK, 5.23)
Jesus laid His hands on the sick and transmitted to them the blessings of health. His loving power knew the smallest imbalances of Nature and the resources to restore the indispensable harmony.
No act of the Divine Master is devoid of significance. Recognizing this truth, the apostles began to lay their fraternal hands in the name of the Lord and became instruments of Divine Mercy.

Currently, in revived Christianity, we once again have the rescue movement of the invisible Plane through the imposition of hands. Passes, as transfusions of psychic forces in which precious spiritual energies flow from the messengers of Christ to the donors and beneficiaries, represent the continuation of the Master's effort to alleviate the sufferings of the world.
It would be audacity on the part of new disciples to expect results as sublime as those obtained by Jesus with the paralytic, the disturbed, and the dying.
The Master knows, while the rest of us are learning to know. It is necessary, however, not to despise His lesson, continuing in our turn the work of love through fraternal hands.
Wherever there is a sincere mental attitude of goodness, the providential service of Jesus can extend.
The exterior formula does not matter. It behooves us to recognize that good can and must be administered in His name.

messages.title: To Renounce
paragraphs: “And every one that hath forsaken houses, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my name's sake, shall receive an hundredfold, and shall inherit everlasting life.” — JESUS (Matthew, 19.29)

In this verse of Matthew's Gospel, the Divine Master induces us to the duty of renouncing the goods of the world to attain eternal life. There is a need, the Messiah proclaims, to abandon earthly father and mother, wife and brethren. However, it is necessary to clarify how to renounce.
Jesus explains that success will belong to those who proceed thus for the love of His name.
At first glance, the divine suggestion seems like nonsense.

How can we forget the sacred duties of existence if Christ came to us to sanctify them? Precipitated disciples failed to grasp the meaning of the text in older times. Numerous brethren of the ideal retreated to the shadow of the cloister, forgetting superior and unavoidable obligations.
It is easy, however, to recognize how Christ renounced.

To the companions who abandoned Him, He appears glorious in the resurrection. Despite the hesitations of His friends, He shares with them eternal joys in the upper room. To the ungrateful men who crucified Him, He offers a sublime itinerary of salvation through the Gospel and never neglected creatures for a single minute.
Let us observe, therefore, what renouncing for the love of Christ represents. It is losing the hopes of Earth while conquering those of Heaven.

If parents are incomprehensible, if the companion is ungrateful, if brothers seem cruel, it is necessary to renounce the joy of having them better or perfect, uniting ourselves even more to all of them in order to work on improvement with Jesus.

Do you perchance find no understanding at home? Are friends and brethren indifferent and rude? Remain by their side anyway, waiting for later the joy of finding those who perfectly attune with you. Only in this way will you renounce your own, doing them all possible good out of dedication to the Master, and only with such renunciation will you attain eternal life.

messages.title: Among Christians
paragraphs: “Yet it shall not be so among you.” — JESUS (Mark, 10.43)
Since the most remote eras, religious groups have labored to obtain celestial favors.

In ancient times, Providence was remembered only on painful and serious occasions. Believers offered sacrifices for domestic happiness when illness invaded their homes; multitudes built temples when public calamities arose.
God was understood solely through happy days. The purifying storm belonged to wicked spirits.

Christ, however, inaugurated a new era. Humility was His path, love and work His example, and martyrdom His palm of victory. He left the understanding that, among His disciples, the principle of faith is never that of easily conquering favors from Heaven, but rather that of active effort toward self-illumination and the execution of God's designs, through the calm or stormy hours of life.

The greatest lesson of the Master of Masters is that instead of formulating conventional vows and sacrifices, promises and mechanical actions, as if to escape our duties, our primary obligation is to surrender ourselves, humbly, to the wise imperatives of Providence, submitting to the just and merciful will of God, so that we may be perfected in His hands.

messages.title: Intuition
paragraphs: “For prophecy never came by the will of man, but holy men of God spoke as they were moved by the Holy Spirit.” — (2 Peter, 1.21)

All men partake in the powers of intuition within the divine tabernacle of conscience, and all can develop their possibilities in this sense, in the domain of spiritual elevation. The great phenomenal manifestations of mediumship are not fundamentally necessary to establish movements of exchange between the visible and invisible Planes.

All the notions that dignify human life came from the Higher Sphere. And these noble ideas were not produced by the will of any man, because strictly earthly reasoning always leans toward materiality in its ingrained selfishness.

Divine revelation, representing the best that Humanity possesses, is the cooperation of sublime Spirituality, brought to creatures by the collaborators of Jesus through the exemplification, acts, and words of righteous men who, through their own efforts, break the circle of vulgarities surrounding them, becoming instruments of necessary renewal.

The intuitive faculty is a universal institution. Through its resources, terrestrial man receives the vibrations of higher life in religious, philosophical, artistic, and scientific contributions, broadening sentimental and cultural achievements—a collaboration that occurs always, not by the creature's will, but by God's concession.

messages.title: Do This and You Will Live
paragraphs: “And He said to him, ‘You have answered rightly; do this and you will live.’” — (LUKE, 10.28)
The case of that doctor of the Law who questioned the Master about what he must do to inherit eternal life is of great interest to all who seek the blessing of Christ.

Luke's account is highly elucidating. Jesus is not surprised by the question, and knowing the high intellectual condition of the questioner, He inquires about his conception of the Law and makes him feel that the answer to the question was already within himself, inscribed upon the mental tablet of his knowledge.
“You have answered rightly,” says the Master. And He adds: “Do this and you will live.”
Such a statement stands out singularly because Christ was addressing a man in the full strength of vital action, yet declaring: “Do this and you will live.”

This is because living is not restricted to the movement of the body, nor to the display of certain conventional titles. Life extends to higher Spheres, to other fields of superior achievement with sublime Spirituality.

The same evangelical scene is daily repeated in many sectors. A large number of learners, fully integrated into the knowledge of their duty, keep asking the Divine Messengers for guidance on the best way to act on Earth; yet the answer is within themselves, in their hearts that fear responsibility, decision, and rugged service...

If you have already been bathed by the clarity of living faith, if you have been benefited by the principles of salvation, execute what you have learned from our Divine Master: “Do this and you will live.”

messages.title: Baptism
paragraphs: “And when they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.” — (ACTS, 19.5)
In various departments of Christian activity, at all times, controversies arise regarding the problems of baptism in the faith.

The priesthood created ceremonials and sacraments for this purpose. There are baptisms of newborns in the Roman Church; in other evangelical centers, there is the baptism of adults. However, the believer could duly analyze the matter, drawing better conclusions through the ascendancy of logic. Spiritual renewal does not occur solely by applying more or less water, or by the circumstance of the exterior solemnity taking place at this or that physical age of the candidate.
Certain material ceremonies in this sense were understandable in the bygone eras in which they were employed.
We know that primary education in child instruction requires the collaboration of figures so that the child's memory may cross the thresholds of knowledge.
The Gospel, however, in its hidden lights, sheds immense clarity on the question of baptism.

“And those who heard were baptized in the name of Jesus.” Therein lies the sublime truth. The blessed renewal of the soul belongs to those who heard the teachings of the Divine Master and put them into practice. Many receive news of the Gospel every day, but only those who hear will be transformed.

messages.title: Whom Do You Follow?
paragraphs: “But you have not so learned Christ.” — PAUL (Ephesians, 4.20)

Man, naturally, will encounter diverse suggestions along the way. Not only from the material Plane will he receive certain counsels tending to divert him from the noblest achievements. The invisible Sphere, immediate to the Circle of his thoughts, may likewise offer him certain perspectives that do not align with the lofty duties that existence entails in itself.
In considering this problem, sincere disciples understand the need to center themselves in Jesus Christ.
When this imperative is forgotten, the greatest disturbances can occur.

The learner who is less centered on the teachings of the Master believes he can serve two masters, and at times even admits it is possible to cater to all the ravings of the senses without harming the peace of his soul. To justify this, they rely on new doctrines, offspring of the scientific novelties of the century; they avail themselves of certain improvised philosophers who attribute too much value to instincts; but having reached this point, let them prepare for great failures, because the need for spiritual development remains alive and increasingly imperative. They may resort to the concepts of the world's supposed wise men, yet Jesus did not teach thus.

messages.title: Straighten the Paths
paragraphs: “Make straight the way of the Lord, as the prophet Isaiah said.” — JOHN THE BAPTIST (John, 1.23)
The exhortation of the Precursor remains in the air, calling men of good will to the regeneration of the common roads.

In all times, we observe creatures who apply for the faith, who yearn for the benefits of Christ. They cry out for His peace, for the divine presence, and sometimes, after transforming their best sentiments into unjust restlessness, they end up discouraged and defeated.

Where is Jesus, who did not come to meet their successive pleas? In what distant Sphere does the Lord remain, far from their bitternesses? They do not understand that, through the generous messengers of His love, Christ is found every day beside all sincere disciples. What they lack is dedication to their own well-being. They run in pursuit of the Divine Master, heedless of John's advice: “straighten the paths.”

For anyone to feel the sanctifying influence of Christ, it is necessary to rectify the road upon which they have been living. Many weep in the paths of crime, lament in the slippery slopes of systematic error, and invoke Heaven without detaching themselves from the overpowering passions of the material realm. Under such conditions, it is not fair for the soul to address the Savior—who accepted humiliation and the cross without any complaints.

If you want Jesus to come and sanctify your activities, straighten the paths of your existence, regenerate your impulses. Dispel the shadows that surround you, and you will feel Him by your side with His blessing.

messages.title: The Man of Macedonia
paragraphs: “And a vision appeared to Paul in the night. A man of Macedonia stood and pleaded with him, saying, ‘Come over to Macedonia and help us.’” — (ACTS, 16.9)
Beyond daily activities in relational life, men participate in a vast spiritual movement whose phases of exchange cannot always be recorded by ordinary memory.
Not only those who face the grave communicate through the process of psychic vibrations. Incarnated Spirits do the same under identical circumstances, as long as they are apt for such achievements.
Later on, the generality of terrestrial creatures will expand these possibilities, perceiving their admirable value.
This, by the way, is nothing new, for as we see, Paul of Tarsus, in Troas, receives the spiritual visit of a man of Macedonia who asks him for help.

The apostolic narrative is very clear. The friend of the Gentiles has a vision in which neither an angelic figure nor a divine messenger appears to him. It is a man of Macedonia whom the former doctor of Tarsus identifies by his clothing and words.

It is useful to recall such an occurrence so that sincere disciples may consolidate the certainty that the Gospel bears all essential and necessary teachings, without imposing the need to resort to difficult nomenclatures far from the simplicity with which the Master bequeathed us the charter of redemption, in which He asks us for loving attention and not complicated theories.

messages.title: Let Us Make the Most Of It
paragraphs: “And you are witnesses of these things.” — (LUKE, 24.48)
Jesus always made the most of the minimum to produce the maximum.
With three years of apostolate, He kindled lights for millennia.
Gathering a small assembly of twelve companions, He renewed the world.
With a sermon on the mount, He inspired millions of souls for eternal life.
He converts a widow's mite into an imperishable lesson of solidarity.
By correcting some disturbed Spirits, He transforms the judicial system of Earth, erecting “love one another” for human happiness.
From five loaves and two fish, He extracts food for thousands of hungry people.
From the action of a well-intentioned Zacchaeus, He traces an edifying program for the stewards of material fortune.
From the attitude of a proud Pharisee, He extracts the truth that confounds less sincere believers.
By healing some sick people, He institutes spiritual medicine for all centers on Earth.
He makes a mustard seed a marvelous symbol of the Kingdom of God.
From a lost drachma, He forms an unforgettable teaching on spiritual love.
From a crude cross, He engraves the greatest lesson of Divinity in History.

Of all this we are witnesses in our condition of beneficiaries. In view of our knowledge, it behooves us to listen to our own conscience. What are we doing with the trifles of our path? Are we making the most of our opportunities to do something good?

messages.title: Let Us Hope
paragraphs: “He will not break a bruised reed, and He will not quench a smoking flax, till He sends forth justice to victory.” — (MATTHEW, 12.20)
Avoid definitive sentences in the face of scenarios formed by evil.
From the mud of the swamp, the Supreme Lord draws fertility.
From the rough stone, He avails Himself of solidity.
From the dry sand, He extracts valuable utilities.
From the bitter substance, He extracts a salutary remedy.
Today's criminal can be a helpful companion tomorrow.
The evildoer, under certain circumstances, exhibits noble qualities, hitherto unknown, which life uses to engrave poems of love and light.
God is not the author of crushing. He is the Father of mercy.
He does not destroy the bruised reed, nor extinguish the smoking flax. His hands repair damages, His divine breath restores and renews always.
Do not despise, therefore, the flickering lights and imprecise virtues. Do not abandon the swampy land, nor forsake the grove suffocated by weeds. Work for good and help unceasingly.
If God, Absolute Lord of Eternity, waits with patience, why should we, imperfect servants of relative labor, not be able to wait?

messages.title: Not Believing
paragraphs: “But he who does not believe will be condemned.” — JESUS (Mark, 16.16)
Those who do not believe are those who remain behind. For them, all expressions of life are reduced to finite sensations, destined for the dark abyss of death.

Those who lift their hearts to the higher life are saved. Their days of work are steps on an infinite ladder of light. Through valiant effort and heavy struggle, they distance themselves from their peers and, despite recognizing their own imperfection, they classify the surrounding landscape and identify the evolutionary paths. Taken with good courage, they feel themselves engaged in the laborious task of ascending the mountain of love and wisdom.
However, those who do not believe limit their own horizons and see nothing except with eyes destined for the grave, asleep regarding reflection and discernment.
Jesus stated that they find themselves condemned. At first glance, such a declaration seems at odds with the Master's magnanimity.
Condemned to what and by whom?
God's justice is coupled with mercy, and the endless hell is a dogmatic image.

Nevertheless, it is imperative to recognize that those who do not believe in the greatness of their own destiny sentence themselves to the lowest Spheres of life. Through the habit of admitting only the visible, they will remain kissing the dust due to their voluntary incapacity to access the superior Planes, while others march toward the certainty of immortal life.
Belief is a friendly lamp whose brightness is sustained by the infinite sun of faith. The wind of negation and doubt can never extinguish it.
Disbelief, however, only knows life by the shadows that its movements project, and understands nothing beyond the night and the swamp to which it condemns itself by its own deliberation.

messages.title: Do Not Disturb
paragraphs: “Therefore what God has joined together, let not man separate.” — JESUS (Matthew, 19:6)

The divine word does not refer only to matters of the heart. Affectionate ties are characterized by sacred foundations, and conjugal or domestic commitments always serve higher designs. Man will not outwit the imperatives of the law by abusing material conveniences to flatter the senses. By breaking the order that governs his paths, he will disorganize his own existence. The balancing principles of life will always arise, correcting and restoring…
Jesus' warning, however, presents a much broader significance for us.
“Do not separate what God has joined” also corresponds to “do not disturb what God has harmonized.”

Let no one plead ignorance of the divine purpose. Duty, no matter how hard, always constitutes the Will of the Lord. And conscience, the vigilant sentinel of the Eternal—unless man is sleeping at the level of the brute—remains able to discern what constitutes “obligation” and what represents “escape.”

The Father created beings and brought them together. He likewise created situations and things, adjusting them for the common good. Whoever disarms divine works, let him prepare for recomposition. Whoever injures the Father chains his own “self” to the results of his unhappy action and, at times, spends centuries untying shackles…

In present-day Earth, an overwhelming percentage of men consists of millions in reparative service, after having separated what God joined, disturbing, with evil, what Providence had established for good.

Let us honor the organizations of the Just Judge that the notion of duty identifies for us in all spheres of the world. Sometimes, it is possible to disturb His works with smiles, but we will invariably be forced to repair them with sweat and tears.

messages.title: External Goods
paragraphs: “A man's life does not consist in the abundance of the things he possesses.” — JESUS (Luke, 12:15)
“A man's life does not consist in the abundance of the things he possesses.” The Master's word is full of opportunity for any circles of human activity, at all times.
A man may retain a vast portion of money. Yet, what will he do with it?
He may exercise extensive authority. However, how will he behave within it?
He may dispose of many properties. Nonetheless, in what way does he use provisional patrimonies?
He will have many lofty projects. How many has he built?
He may keep countless ideals of perfection. But is he attending to the noble principles of which he is a bearer?
He will have written thousands of pages. What is the substance of his work?
He will count many years of existence in the body. However, what has he done with time?
He may count on numerous friends. How does he conduct himself before the affections that surround him?

Our life does not consist of the numerical wealth of things and graces, nominal acquisitions, and exterior titles. Our peace and happiness depend on the use we make, where we find ourselves today, here and now, of the opportunities and gifts, situations and favors, received from the Most High.
Do not seek to light-heartedly hoard what you hold on loan. Mobilize, with judgment, the resources deposited in your hands.

The Lord will not identify you by the treasures you gathered, by the blessings you retained, by the years you lived in the physical body. He will recognize you by the use of your gifts, by the value of your achievements, and by the works you left around your own feet.

messages.title: Definitive Possessions
paragraphs: “I have come that they may have life, and that they may have it more abundantly.” — JESUS (John, 10:10)
If the creature's peace does not consist in the abundance of what it possesses on Earth, it depends on the abundance of definitive values that the soul possesses.
Because of this, the Divine Master came to us so that we may be bearers of overflowing life, replete with light, love, and eternity.
For our own sake, we should never forget the substantial gifts to be garnered within our own Spirit.
In the game of external forces, we will never find the necessary illumination.
Earthly spring is wonderful, but winter will come after it.
The youth of the body is a phase of intoxicating pleasures; however, old age will not delay.
The most intact and harmonious physical vessel will one day experience illness or death.
Every manifestation of existence on Earth is a process of permanent transformation.
It is imperative to build the inner castle from which we can raise feelings to the highest fields of life.

Jesus filled us with His sublime presence, not so that we may possess ephemeral facilities, but to be possessed by imperishable riches; not so that we may surround ourselves with external favors, but to concentrate within us definitive acquisitions.
Let us be bearers of immortal life.
Christ did not visit us as a giver of ordinary benefits. He came to connect the lamp of our heart to the power plant of God's Love, converting us into inextinguishable lights.

messages.title: In Prayer
paragraphs: “Lord, teach us to pray…” — (LUKE, 11:1)
Prayer, in the circles of Christianity, is characterized by infinite gradation in its manifestations, because there are believers of all shades in the various courses of faith.
Restless followers complain about the fulfillment of inconstant purposes.
The selfish demand the solution of inferior whims.
The ignorant of goodness even beg for evil to their neighbor.
The sad ask for solitude with idleness.
The desperate supplicate for death.

Countless beneficiaries of the Gospel implore this or that, alluding to the good progress of business that interests their physical life. In short, they seek escape. They yearn only for distance from difficulty, from work, from dignified struggle.
Jesus patiently supports all ranks of candidates for His service, for His illumination, extending benign hands to them, tolerating their uncalled-for complaints and unacceptable tears.
However, when He accepts someone into definitive discipleship, something happens in the inmost soul contemplated by the Lord.
Noisy requests cease.
Tumultuous desires calm down.
Prayer is converted into edifying work.
The disciple claims nothing. And the Master, answering his prayers, modifies his will every day, casting out inferior objectives from his thought.
The heart united with Jesus is a joyful and silent servant. The Master said to him: Arise and follow me. And he arose and followed.

messages.title: In Meditation
paragraphs: “And they departed in a boat to a deserted place by themselves.” — (MARK, 6:32)
Your hands remain exhausted from doing and undoing.
Your eyes, naturally, are full of the anguish gathered in environmental disturbances.
Your feet hurt in painful recapitulations.
Your feelings come and go through tumultuous impulses, influenced by a thousand different people.
Your heart is tormented.
It is natural. Our mind thirsts for peace, just as dry earth needs cold water.

Come to a place apart, in the country of yourself, in order to rest a little. Forget social borders, domestic controls, the misunderstandings of relatives, difficult matters, unsettling problems, inferior ideas.
Withdraw from the commonplace places to which you still cling.
Concentrate for a few minutes in the company of Christ, in the boat of your purest thoughts, over the sea of daily worries.
He will wash your mind tainted with afflictions.
He will balm your ulcers.
He will give you wholesome counsel.
It is enough that you be silent, and His voice will speak in sublime silence.
Offer Him a heart courageous in faith and fulfillment, and His divine arms will do the rest.

You will then return to the circles of struggle, reinvigorated, strong, and happy. Your heart with Him, in order to act successfully in the valley of service. He with you, to climb the mountain of light without weariness.

messages.title: In the Real Picture
paragraphs: “I have given them your word; and the world has hated them because they are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.” — JESUS (John, 17:14)
Apprentices of the Gospel, expecting human facilities, will always constitute assemblies of voluntary deception.
The Lord promised His companions nothing but continued effort against shadows until the final victory of good.
The Christian is not an ornamental flower for isolated churches. He is the “salt of the Earth,” the preserving force of divine principles in the sanctuary of the entire world.
Jesus' word in this regard suffers no doubt:
“If anyone desires to come after Me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow Me.
“Love your enemies.
“Pray for those who persecute you and slander you.
“Bless those who curse you.
“Lend, hoping for nothing in return.
“Judge not, that you be not judged.
“He who is greatest among you shall be your servant.
“Enter by the narrow gate.
“Indeed I send you out as lambs among wolves.
“In the world you will have tribulation.”

Through such clear statements, it is impossible to await an easy-life giver in Christ. No one should approach Him without the sincere desire to learn to improve themselves. If Christianity is sublime hope, celestial love, and restoring faith, it is also work, sacrifice, incessant perfection.
Proving His divine lessons, the Supreme Master lived serving and died on the cross.

messages.title: For Christ
paragraphs: “But if he has wronged you or owes anything, put that on my account.” — PAUL (Philemon, 1:18)
Sending Onesimus to Philemon, Paul, in his inspired and happy expressions, recommended that his friend charge to his debit whatever was owed to him by the bearer.
Let us adapt the exhortation to our own needs.
In each new day of struggle, we become greater debtors to Christ.

If everything goes difficultly for us, it is from Jesus that fair provisions reach us. If everything develops straightly, it is through His love that we use the gifts of life, and it is in His name that we distribute hopes and consolations.
We are committed to His inexhaustible mercy.
We are His, and in this circumstance lies our highest title.

Why, then, pessimism and despair when calumny or ingratitude attack us harshly, bringing us the possibility of a vaster ascension? If we are totally committed to the Master's infinite love, will it not be reasonable to understand at least some particularity of our immense debt, preparing ourselves to accept a tiny parcel of suffering, in memory of His name, alongside our brothers of the Earth, who are equally His wards?
We must reflect that when we speak of peace, happiness, and superior life, we act in the field of trust, promising on Christ's account, since only He has to give in abundance.

In view of this, if you feel that someone has become a debtor to your soul, do not surrender to useless worries, because Christ is also your creditor, and you must place the damages of the way onto His divine account, and move on.

messages.title: Spiritual Mastery
paragraphs: “I am not alone, because the Father is with Me.” — JESUS (John, 16:32)
In afflictive trials, the creature always demonstrates where the external forces that subjugate its soul are located.

In the great hours of testimony, in suffering or in death, the avaricious cry out for ephemeral possessions, the arbitrary demand the obedience they believe they are owed, the super-sentimentalists claim the object of their affections.

Jesus, however, in the supreme field of the last earthly hours, proves to be absolute master of Himself, teaching us sublime identification with the Father's purposes as the most advanced resource of self-mastery.
Naturally connected to the most diverse forces, on the day of Calvary He did not bind Himself to any of them.
He attended to human government loyally, but Pilate does not frighten Him.
He respected the law of Moses; however, Caiaphas does not impress Him.
He tenderly loved His disciples; yet affectionate reasons do not dominate His heart.
He cultivated with admirable devotion His work of instructing and helping, healing and consoling; nevertheless, the possibility of staying does not seduce His spirit.
Judas' act does not extract curses from Him.
The ingratitude of the beneficiaries does not provoke despair in Him.
The weeping of the women of Jerusalem does not weaken His firm courage.
The sarcasm of the crowd does not break His silence.
The cross does not alter His serenity.
Suspended on the wood, He begs for excuses for the people's ignorance.

His lesson of spiritual mastery is deep and imperishable. It reveals the need to be “ourselves” in the roughest trials of life, with a tranquil conscience elevated to Divine Justice and a faithful heart directed by the Divine Will.

messages.title: Mother's Words
paragraphs: “His mother said to the servants, 'Whatever He says to you, do it.'” — (JOHN, 2:5)

The Gospel is an illuminated roadmap of which Jesus is the divine center. In this Charter of Redemption, surrounding His celestial figure, there are words, memories, gifts, and indications much loved by those who were His legitimate collaborators in the world.
We receive there friendly recollections from Paul, John, Peter, and other companions of the Lord, which we cannot forget.
We likewise have, in the Sacred Document, reminiscences of Mary. Let us examine her precious words in Cana, full of wisdom and maternal love.

Generally, when children seek a mother's affectionate intervention, it is because they feel orphaned in spirit or in need of joy. For this very reason, in all places of the world, it is common to observe children arguing with parents and crying before maternal hearts.
Justly interpreted as a guardian angel of Christianity, sometimes it is with immense afflictions that we resort to Mary.
Indeed, the apostle John's verse does not refer to painful landscapes. The episode occurs at a wedding feast, but we can take advantage of its sublime symbolic expression.

We too are at the engagement feast of the Gospel with the Earth. Despite the nearly twenty centuries that have elapsed, the joy is still one of engagement, since the perfect union has not occurred until now… In this great concert of the renewing idea, we are humble servants. On many occasions, the wine of hope runs out. We feel exhausted, disillusioned… We implore maternal tenderness and lo, Mary answers us: Do whatever He tells you.
The advice is wise and profound and was placed at the beginning of the works of salvation.
Listening to such a warning from a Mother, let us meditate on whether we are truly doing everything the Master told us.

messages.title: Tears
paragraphs: “Come to Me, all you who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.” — JESUS (Matthew, 11:28)
No one like Christ spread so much joy and courage of spirit on Earth. Recognizing this, many disciples heap arguments against tears and abhor expressions of suffering.

Paradise would already be on Earth if no one had reasons to cry. Considering this, Jesus, who was the Master of trust and optimism, called to His heart all those who were weary and oppressed under the weight of earthly disillusions.
He did not curse the sad: He summoned them to consolation.

Many people believe tears are a symptom of spiritual weakness. However, Mary sobbed on Calvary; Peter lamented after the denial; Paul plunged into weeping at the gates of Damascus; the early Christians cried in the circuses of martyrdom… but none of them shed tears without hope. They wept and followed the Lord's path, suffered and proclaimed the Good News of Redemption, endured and died loyal in supreme trust.
The tiredness experienced for love of Christ is converted into strength, the chains brought to His magnanimous gaze are transformed into divine ties of salvation.

Tears are characterized by specific origins. When they are born of sincere and constructive pain, they are filters of redemption and life; however, if they proceed from despair, they are mortal poisons.

messages.title: Zeal for the Good
paragraphs: “And who is he that will harm you, if ye be followers of that which is good?” — (1 Peter, 3:13)
Fearing those who practice evil is proof that goodness has not yet conveniently rooted itself in our soul.
Peter's question is laden with enormous meaning.
If there is a solid purpose of good in your paths, if you are careful in its practice, who will mobilize such great power to annul the edifices of God?

The problem, however, lies in the need for understanding. We are still incapable of examining all aspects of a question, all the contours of a landscape. What today seems to us real happiness may tomorrow be a cruel disappointment. Our human desires modify themselves at the purifying jets of the evolutionary fountain. It is urgent, therefore, that we attune ourselves to the Divine Law, reflect its sacred principles, and submit ourselves to the Higher Designs, working incessantly for the good, wherever we may be.

Personal sensitivities, false needs, crystallized prejudices often operate the blindness of the spirit. From there proceed immense disasters for all those who keep the intention of doing good, but give ear to inferior personalism.
He who cultivates obedience to the Father in his heart knows how to find opportunities to build with his love.

Those who achieve legitimate understanding, therefore, cannot fear evil. They never lose themselves in the dryness of demand nor in the deviations of sentimentalism. For these souls, who have found within themselves the pleasure of serving without questioning, failures, trials, illnesses, and obstacles are simply new decisions of the Divine Forces regarding the task concerning them, destined to lead them to the greater life.

messages.title: Daily Bread
paragraphs: “Give us day by day our daily bread.” — JESUS (Luke, 11:3)
Have you ever thought about your daily bread?
By force of possessing it in abundance, man usually devalues it, in the manner of the unreflecting creature who only meditates on health upon the advent of illness.

If the majority of the children of Earth were up to fulfilling gratitude in its real aspects, daily bread alone would suffice so that earthly communities would not lack perfect notions of the existence of God. So magnanimous is celestial goodness that, by promoting resources for the maintenance of men, it escapes the admiration of creatures, so that they may better understand life, integrating themselves into the responsibilities concerning them, into the labor organizations to which they were called, with the purpose of realizing their own improvement.

The Most High leaves men with the belief that terrestrial bread is their conquest, so that they may conveniently perfect themselves in the gift of serving. In truth, however, the daily bread for all the meals of the world proceeds from Divine Providence.
Man will dig the soil, scatter the seeds, defend the service, and cooperate with Nature, but germination, growth, flowering, and fruiting belong to the All-Merciful.
In daily nourishment prevails a sublime teaching of collaboration between the Creator and the creature, which rare people are willing to observe.
Man exerts himself and the Lord grants him utilities. The servant works and the Most High blesses his sweat.
It is in this process of intimate cooperation and natural understanding that the Father hopes to harvest, one day, the sweet fruits of perfection in the Spirit of His children.

messages.title: Cooperation
paragraphs: “And he said, How can I, except some man should guide me?” — (ACTS, 8:31)
Ever since the coming of Jesus, the movement of renewing education for the good has been one of the most impressive in the bosom of Humanity.
Everywhere temples have risen, books bearing sacred principles have been disseminated.

One perceives throughout this activity the subtle and magnanimous action of the Master, who misses no occasion to attract God's creatures to Infinite Love. From this blessed picture of work, however, stands out the fraternal cooperation that Christ left us as an indispensable norm for the unfolding of the world's eternal illumination.

Let no one harbor the presumption of elevating oneself without the help of others, although one should not seek a parasitic condition for ascension. We refer to solidarity, helpful support, edifying assistance. Those who learn something always avail themselves of men who have gone before, and do not go further if they lack the interest of contemporaries, even if that interest is minimal.
The apostles needed Christ, who, in turn, made a point of tethering the teachings of which He was the divine emissary to the ancient laws.
Paul of Tarsus needed Ananias to understand his own situation.

Let us observe the verse above, extracted from the Acts of the Apostles. Philip was unconcerned when an angel of the Lord sent him to the road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza. The disciple complies and there finds a man reading the Law without understanding it. And both enter into a sanctified effort of cooperation.

No one remains abandoned. The messengers of Christ always succor on the most desert roads. It is necessary, however, that the soul accept its condition of need and not despise the act of learning with humility, for we must not forget, through the evangelical text, that the beggar of understanding was the chief steward of the queen of the Ethiopians, superintendent of all her treasures. Besides, he was riding in a chariot and Philip was on foot.

messages.title: Living Lesson
paragraphs: “This is a hard saying; who can hear it?” — (JOHN, 6:60)
Christianity is the supreme religion of truth and love, summoning hearts to the higher life.
In view of religion translating a rebinding, it is primordial to turn back to God, to return to the field of Divinity.
Jesus presented His platform of immortal principles. He blazed the trails. He deceived no one regarding difficulties and obstacles.
It is necessary, the Lord clarified, to deny our own vanity, repent of our errors, and convert ourselves to the good.
The evangelist noted the observation of many of the disciples: “This is a hard saying; who can hear it?”
Yes, effectively it is indispensable to break with the alliances of the fall and sign the pact of redemption. It is imperative to follow in the ways of Him who is the light of our life.
For this, brilliant words and intellectual artifices are not enough. The problem is of “who can hear” the Divine Message, understanding it with Christ and following in His footsteps.

messages.title: Conventional Opinions
paragraphs: “The people answered and said, Thou hast a devil: who seeketh to kill thee?” — (JOHN, 7:20)
Do not bind yourself excessively to the judgments of the crowd. Conventionalism and habit possess vigorous forces over it.
If you tolerate offenses with love, they call you a coward.
If you forgive disinterestly, they consider you a fool.
If you suffer with patience, they deny your worth.
If you spread good with self-abnegation, they accuse you of being crazy.
If you acquire characteristics of sublime and sanctifying love, they judge you sick.
If you disregard vulgar pleasures, they classify you as abnormal.
If you show yourself pious, they assert that you have aged and tired before your time.
If you adopt simplicity as a norm, they secretly ironize you.
If you respect order and hierarchy, they qualify you as a flatterer.
If you reverence the Law, they point to you as fearful.
If you are prudent and dignified, they call you a fanatic and disturbed.

However, this same crowd, through the voice of its leaders, teaches love for one's fellows, the cult of legality, and the religion of duty. In its circles, however, the excess of words does not permit, for now, the reign of understanding.
It is indispensable to endure its unconsciousness in order to profitably attend to our obligations before God.
Do not irritate yourself, nor become discouraged. Jesus Himself was the target, for no reason at all, of the sarcasms of public opinion.

messages.title: The Divine Door
paragraphs: “I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved.” — JESUS (John, 10:9)

In the paths of life, each companion bearing a slightly higher intellectual expression naturally converts into an imperious voice for our ears. And each person who walks ahead of us opens doors to our spirit.
The unconformed open roads to rebellion and indiscipline.
Rogues offer passage to captivity where they exercise domination.
Writers of futilities provide a passport to the province of lost time.
Slanderers direct whoever listens to them to poisoned sources.
The vicious break the beneficial barriers of fraternal respect, unveiling precipices where danger is incessant.
The lazy lead to war against constructive work.
The perverse wide-open the chasms of crime.
Even if you do not perceive it, various people open doors to you every day through the spoken or written word, action, or example.
Examine where you enter with the sacred deposit of trust. Often, you will lose a long time to retake the path that is proper to you.
Let us not forget that Jesus is the only door of true liberation.

Through many stations in the field of Humanity, we will likely receive profitable experiences, gathering them at the cost of terrible disillusions, but only in Christ, in the sacred climate of the application of His principles, is it possible to find the blessed passage of definitive salvation.

messages.title: The New Commandment
paragraphs: “A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you.” — JESUS (John, 13:34)
The unobservant reading of the text would induce the reader to feel in these words of the Master absolute identity with His teaching regarding the golden rule.
However, it is necessary to point out the difference. The “love thy neighbor as thyself” is diverse from the “that ye love one another as I have loved you.”
The first institutes a duty, in whose execution it is not reasonable that man should cogitate on another's understanding. The learner will love his neighbor as himself.
Jesus, however, enlarged the formula, creating the new commandment in the Christian community. The Master refers to this in the final meeting with dear friends, in the intimacy of hearts.
The recommendation “that ye love one another as I have loved you” ensures the regime of true solidarity among the disciples, guarantees fraternal trust and the certainty of reciprocal understanding.
In all common relations, the Christian will love his neighbor as himself, recognizing, however, that in the home of his faith he counts on brothers who effectively support one another.

This is the new commandment that established legitimate intimacy among those who surrendered to Christ, meaning that, in their environments of work, there is he who sacrifices and he who understands sacrifice, he who loves and feels loved, he who does good and knows how to give thanks.

In any circle of the Gospel where this characteristic does not mark the manifestations of companions among themselves, the arguments of the Good News may have reached inquiring brains, but have not yet penetrated the sanctuary of hearts.

messages.title: Intimate Purification
paragraphs: “Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.” — (JAMES, 4:8)
Each man has an exterior life, known and analyzed by those who surround him, and an intimate life of which only he himself can provide testimony.
The interior world is the source of all good or bad principles, and all exterior expressions keep their foundations there.
As a general rule, we are all bearers of serious intimate deficiencies needing rectification. But the work of purifying is not as simple as it seems.

It will be very man to confess the acceptance of religious truths, to operate verbal adherence to edifying ideologies... Another thing, however, is to realize the work of self-elevation, availing oneself of self-discipline, fraternal understanding, and the spirit of sacrifice.

The Apostle James understood perfectly the gravity of the subject and advised the disciples to cleanse their hands, that is, to rectify the activities of the exterior plane, to renew their actions before the gaze of all, appealing for the purification of feeling to be carried out equally within the sacred enclosure of conscience, known only by the learner in the unsearchable solitude of their thoughts. The valiant companion of Christ, however, did not forget to affirm that this is work for the double-minded, because such renewal will never be done solely at the cost of brilliant words.

messages.title: Let Us Make Our Light
paragraphs: “Let your light so shine before men.” — JESUS (Matthew, 5:16)
Before the glory of evolved worlds, of the sublime Spheres that populate the Universe, the narrow field in which we agitate on the Planetary Crust is a limited circle of action.
If the problem, however, were only one of space, we would have nothing to lament. The small and humble house, illuminated with Sun and joy, is a paradise of happiness.

The anguish of our Plane proceeds from shadow. Darkness invades the paths in all directions. Darkness born of ignorance, malice, and folly, enveloping peoples, institutions, and persons. Fogs that assault consciences, reasoning, and feelings.

In the midst of the great night, it is necessary that we light our light. Without this it is impossible to find the path of liberation. Without the bright irradiation of our own being, we cannot be seen with ease by the Divine Messengers, who help in the name of the Most High, nor will we effectively help anyone.
It is indispensable to organize the interior sanctuary and illuminate it, so that darkness does not dominate us.

It is possible to march, availing ourselves of others' lights. However, without a clarity that is our own, we will suffer the constant threat of falling. The owners of lit lamps may move away from us, summoned by the mountains of elevation we do not yet deserve.

Avail yourself, therefore, of the lights of the path, apply the wick of good will to the oil of service and humility, and light your torch for the journey. Thank him who illuminates you for an hour, for a few days, or for many years, but do not forget your lamp, if you do not wish to slip into the precipices of the long road!...

The fundamental problem of redemption, my friend, is not summarized in spoken or written words; it is very easy to pronounce beautiful speeches and give excellent information, while keeping blindness in one's own eyes.
Our basic need is for our own light, intimate clarification, self-education, and substantial conversion of the “self” to the Kingdom of God.

You may speak marvelously about life, argue brilliantly about faith, teach the values of belief, eat the bread of consolation, exalt peace, gather the flowers of good, enjoy the fruits of others' generosity, conquer the ephemeral crown of easy praise, and pile up diverse titles that adorn your personality in transit through the valleys of the world...
All this, in truth, can be done by the Spirit who lingers indefinitely in certain corners of the road. However, advancing without light is impossible.

messages.title: In Propaganda
paragraphs: “And they shall say to you, See here, or, see there: go not after them, nor follow them.” — JESUS (Luke, 17:23)
The Master's exhortations to the disciples are too precise to provoke any uncertainty or indecision.

When so many sectarian expressions requisition Christ for their intellectual excesses, it is fair that new learners, in the light of the Comforter, meditate on the elevated significance of this verse of Luke.
In genuinely Christian propaganda it is not enough to say where the Lord is. It is indispensable to show Him in one's own exemplification.
Many traverse temples and altars, searching for Jesus.
Changing religious belief can be a modification of path, but it can also be a continuation of disturbance. It becomes necessary to find Christ in the interior sanctuary.
Christianizing life is not imprinting new exterior features upon it. It is reforming it for the good within the private scope.

Those who affirm only in verbal form that the Master is here or there bear profound responsibilities. The preoccupation with proselytism is always dangerous for those who seduce themselves with the sonorous beauties of the word without edifying examples.

The sincere disciple knows that speaking is easy, but that it is difficult to reveal the Lord's purposes in one's own existence. It is imperative to do good before teaching it to others, because Jesus recommended that no one follow the criers who only said where the Son of God could be found.

messages.title: The Companion
paragraphs: “Shouldn't you also have had mercy on your fellow servant, just as I had mercy on you?” — JESUS (Matthew, 18.33)
Nowhere can a man act in isolation when dealing with the work of God, which is perfected everywhere.
The Father established cooperation as one of the noblest principles at the core of the laws that govern life.
In the most humble nook, you will find a companion in effort.
At home, he may be called “father” or “son”; along the way, he may be named “friend” or “comrade in ideals.”
Deep down, there is only one Father who is God and one great family composed of brothers.
If the Eternal has directed a less desirable companion to your environment, have compassion and teach always. Elevate those who surround you.
Sanctify the bonds that Jesus promoted for the good of your soul and of all those around you.
If the task presents obstacles, remember the countless times Christ has already applied mercy to your spirit. This mitigates the shadows of the heart.
Observe in each companion of struggle or of daily life a blessing and an opportunity to fulfill the divine program regarding your existence.
Are there difficulties and setbacks, misunderstandings and disagreements? Use the mercy that Jesus has already used with you, giving you a new occasion to sanctify and to learn.

messages.title: Straight Paths
paragraphs: “And He said to them: Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find.” — (JOHN, 21.6)
Life should constitute, on the part of all of us, a rigorous observance of the sacred interests of God.
Frequently, however, the creature seeks to override the divine designs.
Imbalance is then established, because no one will deceive the Divine Law. And man suffers, compulsorily, in the task of reparation.

Some companions despair in the good fight for their own perfection and plunge into a veritable hell of inner shadows. They complain about destiny, accuse the creating wisdom, gesticulate in the abysses of wickedness, forgetting the caprice and imprudence that made them fall.
Jesus, however, almost twenty centuries ago, exclaimed: “Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find.”

Figuratively, the human Spirit is a “fisherman” of evolutionary values in the regenerating school of Earth. Each person's position is the “boat.” Every new day, man rises with his “net” of interests. Are we casting our “net” to the “right side”? Are our thoughts and acts founded on true justice?

It is wise to consult the inner life in daily effort, because Christ, in this teaching, generally recommended to His disciples: “Dedicate your attention to the straight paths and you will find what is necessary.”

messages.title: What Seek Ye?
paragraphs: “And Jesus, turning and seeing them following Him, said to them: What seek ye?” — (JOHN, 1.38)

Life in itself is a divine set of experiences. Each isolated existence offers man the profit of new knowledge. The acquisition of religious values, however, is the most important of all, by virtue of constituting the movement of the definitive illumination of the soul toward God.
Men, nevertheless, extend to this divine department their vitiation of feelings in the inferior game of selfish interests.
The stone temples are full of unjustified promises and absurd vows.
Many devotees expect to find in Divine Providence a bribable force, laden with privileges and preferences. Others resort to the spiritual Plane with the purpose of solving petty problems.
