They forget that Christ taught and exemplified. The cross of Calvary is a living symbol.

Whoever desires freedom must obey the supreme designs. Without the understanding of Jesus in the intimate field, associated with the acts of each day, the soul will always be the prisoner of inferior concerns.
Let no one forget the truth that Christ is found at the threshold of all the religious temples of the world, asking with interest those who enter: “What seek ye?”

messages.title: Living by Faith
paragraphs: “But the just shall live by faith.” — PAUL (Romans, 1.17)
In his epistle to the Romans, Paul states that the just shall live by faith.
Not a few learners misinterpreted the statement. They supposed that living by faith would be strictly executing the exterior ceremonies of religious cults.

Frequenting temples, harmonizing with priests, respecting sectarian symbology would indicate the presence of the just man. But we do not always see the good ritualist allied with the good man. And, above all, it is necessary to be a creature of God in all circumstances of existence.
Paul of Tarsus meant that the just will always be faithful, will live invariably in true fidelity to the Father who is in Heaven.

Are the days smiling and tranquil? Let us have a good memory and not disdain moderation. Are they dark and sad? Let us trust in God, without whose permission the storm would not break. Has the abandonment of the world come? The Father never abandons us. Have illnesses, disappointments, ingratitude, and death arrived? They are all good friends, for they bring to us the opportunity to be just, to live by faith, according to the sacred dispositions of Christianity.

messages.title: The Rusted Treasure
paragraphs: “Your gold and your silver are rusted.” — (JAMES, 5.3)

The feelings of man, in his own passionate ideas, if directed toward the good, would always produce as a consequence the most substantial fruits for the work of God. In almost everywhere, however, they develop in reverse, preventing the realization of divine purposes regarding the redemption of creatures.

Generally speaking, we see love interpreted merely as a transitory emotion of the material senses, beneficence producing disturbance among dozens of people to attend to three or four sick individuals, faith organizing sectarian wars, the sacred zeal of existence creating fulminating egoism. Here, forgiveness speaks of difficulties in expressing itself; there, humility asks for the admiration of others.
All the feelings conferred upon us by God are sacred. They constitute the gold and silver of our inheritance, but as the apostle asserts, we let the gifts rust over the course of time.

It is necessary that we labor strenuously to eliminate the “rust” that has attacked the treasures of the spirit. For this, it is indispensable that we understand in the Gospel the history of perfect renunciation and unobstructed forgiveness, so that we may truly walk toward Christ.

messages.title: Be Calm
paragraphs: “And Jesus said: Make the men sit down.” — (JOHN, 6.10)
This passage from the Gospel of John is one of the most significant. It occurs when the crowd of nearly five thousand people has need of bread in the isolation of nature.
The disciples are worried.
Philip states that two hundred denarii will not be enough to meet the unforeseen difficulty.
Andrew leads to the Master a young boy who carried with him five barley loaves and two fish. Everyone discusses.

Jesus, however, receives the crumb without disbelieving its precious significance and commands everyone to sit down, asks for order, for harmony to be made. And He wondrously distributes the resource to all.
The greatness of the lesson is profound.

Men starving for peace claim the assistance of Christ. They speak of Him, implore His help, await His manifestations. Yet they fail to establish order within themselves to receive the celestial resources. They mix Jesus with their imprecations, their crazy anxieties, and their criminal desires. Naturally they despair, increasingly disoriented, because they do not want to listen to the invitation to calm, they do not sit down so that order may be established, persisting in maintaining their own imbalance.

messages.title: To Suffer
paragraphs: “Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer.” — (REVELATION, 2.10)
One of Christ's greatest concerns was to banish the phantoms of fear from the paths of the disciples.
The acquisition of faith does not constitute a common phenomenon along the paths of life. It translates full confidence.
After all, what does “to suffer” signify?
The suffering of many men is, in essence, very similar to that of the child who lost his toys.
Numerous creatures feel eminently suffering because the practice of evil is not possible for them; others revolt because God did not attend to their pernicious whims.

In order to lend due cooperation to the Gospel, it is right that we incorporate ourselves into the faithful caravan that set out on the road to meet Jesus, understanding that the loyal friend is one who does not seek to contend and is always ready for the execution of good tasks.
Participating in the spirit of evangelical service is sharing in the decisions of the Master, fulfilling the divine designs of the Father who is in Heaven.
Let us not fear, then, what we may come to suffer.
God is the magnanimous and just Father.
A father does not distribute sufferings. He gives corrections, and every correction perfects.

messages.title: Business
paragraphs: “And He said to them: Why did you seek Me? Did you not know that I must be about My Father's business?” — (LUKE, 2.49)
The man of the world is always concerned with business regarding his ephemeral interests.
Some spend their entire existence observing stock exchange quotations. Others absorb themselves in the study of markets.

Countries have internal and external business. In the services that concern them, wonderful activities of intelligence are utilized. However, despite their respectable appearance when legitimate, all these movements are precarious and transitory. The strongest stock exchanges will suffer crises; the commerce of the world is versatile and, at times, ungrateful.
Very rare are the men who consecrate themselves to their eternal interests. Frequently, they remember this too late, when the body is dying. Only then do they break the fatal forgetfulness.
Nonetheless, the human creature should understand the illumination of oneself as the best business on Earth, since such an operation represents the interest of Divine Providence regarding us.

God permitted transactions on the planet so that we might learn fraternity in the expressions of exchange; He allowed earthly business to proceed so as to teach us, through them, which is the greatest of all. That is why the Master speaks to us clearly, in Luke's notes: — “Did you not know that I must be about My Father's business?”

messages.title: Writers
paragraphs: “Beware of the scribes, which love to go in long clothing.” — JESUS (Mark, 12.38)
The literature of the world has always been full of “scribes who love to walk in long robes.”

Jesus referred not only to ambitious intellectuals, but also to eccentric writers who, under the pretext of novelty, poison spirits with their sickly conceptions, stemming from an excessive concern for originality.
It is necessary to flee from those who kill simple life. Intellectual toxicity tends to ruin numerous existences.

There are books whose useful function is to keep the torch of vigilance lit in the souls of characters solidified in the noblest ideals of life. Even now, when we are passing through disturbed and difficult times for man, the market of ideas presents itself full of deteriorated articles, calling for the intervention of “spiritual hygiene” posts.
Can you feed the body with rotted substances?
Your soul, likewise, cannot nourish itself with inferior ideals on the basis of irreligion, disrespect, disorder, indiscipline.
Observe the models of intellectual decadence and reflect sincerely on the peace you intimately desire. This will constitute a strong aid in favor of the extinction of the deviations of intelligence.

messages.title: To Be Content
paragraphs: “Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content.” — PAUL (Philippians, 4.11)
The vertigo of possession subjugates the majority of creatures on Earth.

Simple life, a condition of relative happiness that the planet can offer, has been forgotten by the generality of men. An overwhelming percentage of earthly supplications fails to advance beyond its narrow scope of origin. Strange and absurd things are asked of God.
Rare people are content with the material received for the solution of their needs; very rarely do they ask only for the “daily bread” as a symbol of indispensable acquisitions.

Incoherent man does not seek to know if he possesses the least for eternal life, because he is always anxious for more within transitory possibilities. Generally, he remains absorbed by perishable interests, insatiate, restless, under the agonizing torment of boundless ambition. In the mad rush toward immediacy, he forgets the opportunity that belongs to him, abandons the material granted to him for his own evolution, and hurls himself into adventures of unpredictable consequences in view of his infinite future.

If you already understand your responsibilities with Christ, examine the essence of your most intimate desires. Remember that Paul of Tarsus, the apostle called by Jesus for the dissemination of divine truth among men, was obliged to learn to be content with what he possessed, entering the path of harsh disciplines.
Are you, perhaps, waiting for someone to carry out such learning for you?

messages.title: The World and Evil
paragraphs: “I do not ask that You take them out of the world, but that You deliver them from evil.” — JESUS (John, 17:15)

In religious centers, there is always a large number of people preoccupied with the idea of death. Many companions believe neither in peace nor in love, except in Planes different from the Earth. The majority await imaginary and unjustifiable situations, unbefitting those who have never taken personal effort into account.
The yearning to die in order to be happy is an illness of the spirit.
Praying to the Father for the disciples, Jesus begged that they not be taken out of the world, but rather freed from evil.
Evil, therefore, is not essentially of the world, but of the creatures who inhabit it.
The Earth, in itself, has always been good. From its mud sprout lilies of delicate aroma, and its maternal nature is a repository of marvelous miracles that repeat themselves every day.

It is of no use for us to leave the planet when our evils have not been properly eradicated. In such circumstances, we resemble human bearers of so-called incurable diseases. We may change our residence; however, the change is almost nothing if our wounds accompany us. It is necessary, therefore, to beautify the world and improve it, by fighting the evil that is within us.

messages.title: Minimal Things
paragraphs: “If then you are not able to do the least things, why are you anxious for the rest?” — JESUS (Luke, 12:26)
Few people know the importance of the good execution of minimal things.
There are men who, with false superiority, mock humble tasks, as if they were not indispensable to the success of larger-scale works.
A wise person cannot forget that, one day, they needed to learn from the simple letters of the alphabet.
Furthermore, no work is perfect if the details have not been properly considered and understood.
In general, man is always fascinated by situations of great prominence, by dramatic and exciting destinies.
Standing out, however, requires much care. Thorns also stand out, and stones stand out on the common road.
It is advisable, therefore, to attend to the minimal things of the path that God has reserved for us, so that our action may become fixed with real profit to life.

The symphony will be disturbed if a note is missing, and the poem is obscure when a verse is omitted. Let us be zealous for tiny things. They are an integral and inalienable part of great achievements. Understanding the importance of this, the Master asks us in the Gospel of Luke: “If then you are not able to do the least things, why are you anxious for the rest?”

messages.title: Clouds
paragraphs: “And a voice came out of the cloud, saying, ‘This is my beloved Son, hear him!’” — (LUKE, 9:35)
Man's mind is almost always absorbed in the contemplation of the clouds that appear on his horizon. They are clouds of vexations, of frustrated projects, of shattered hopes.

At times, he despairs, poisoning the very sources of his life. Invariably, he would desire a blue sky in the distance, a bright sun during the day, and luminous stars to embellish his night. However, a cloud appears, and perplexity seizes him suddenly.
The Gospel tells us the beautiful story of a cloud.
The disciples found themselves dazzled by the vision of Jesus transfigured, having by his side Moses and Elijah, aureoled in intense light.

Behold, however, a great shadow appears. They no longer distinguish the marvelous scene. Nevertheless, from the mantle of thick mist, the powerful voice of divine revelation cries out: “This is my beloved Son, hear him!”
The word of Heaven manifested itself in the temporary shadow.
Earthly existence effectively imposes unsettling anxieties and bitter afflictions. It is advisable, however, that creatures maintain serenity and trust in difficult moments.
The sorrows and hardships of planetary struggle contain profound explanations, hidden lessons, and grandiose appeals. The wise and loving voice of God always speaks through them.

messages.title: Recapitulations
paragraphs: “For they loved the glory of men more than the glory of God.” — (JOHN, 12:43)
The centuries seem to relive their splendors and decadence.
The world provides the impression of a field where scenes constantly repeat themselves. Everything is unstable.

Force and right walk with alternatives of dominion. Enlightened multitudes return to new hallucinations. The human spirit, in its turn, considered in isolation, demonstrates that it recapitulates bad experiences after achieving good knowledge.

How can we explain the anomaly? The situation is surprising because, deep down, every man has a thirst for peace and a hunger for stability. It is important to recognize, however, that over the course of millennia, human creatures, in multiple existences, have loved earthly glory more than the glory of God.

Innumerable men presume themselves redeemed with the judicious meditation of twilight, but… what about the day that has already passed? In the merciful justice of His decisions, Jesus grants the hesitant worker a new opportunity. The day returns. Existence is recast. However, what does it profit the worker to avail himself solely of eternal goods in a twilight full of shadows?

Someone will ask him: what did you do with the bright morning, the blazing sun, the instruments that I gave you? Only at that point does he recognize the need to glorify himself in the Almighty. And men and peoples will continue to undo the false work to restart the effort once again.

messages.title: Eating and Drinking
paragraphs: “Then you will begin to say, ‘We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets.’” — JESUS (Luke, 13:26)
The verse from Luke noted here refers to the head of the household who closed the door to ungrateful children.

The scene reflects the situation of religious people of all shades who merely talked excessively, referring to the name of Jesus. On the day of meticulous analysis, when death opens the spiritual door once again, behold, they will say they “ate and drank” in the presence of the Master, whose teachings they knew and disseminated in the streets.

They only ate and drank. They selfishly availed themselves of the resources. They ate and believed with an intellectual faith. They drank and transmitted what they had learned from others. Assimilating the lesson into their own existence did not interest their inconstant minds.

They knew the Master, it is true, but they did not reveal Him in their hearts. Jesus also knew God; however, He did not limit Himself to affirming the reality of these relationships. He lived the love of the Father among men. Teaching the truth, He surrendered Himself to human redemption without thinking of reward. He understood creatures before they understood Him, granted us supreme favor with His coming, and gave Himself as a holocaust so that we might learn the science of good.
It is not enough to intellectually believe in Jesus. It is necessary to apply Him to ourselves.
Man must cultivate meditation within the circle of problems that concern him every day. Irrational animals also eat and drink. However, the children of nations are born on Earth for a higher life.

messages.title: Sowing
paragraphs: “But when it is sown, it grows up.” — JESUS (Mark, 4:32)

It is reasonable that all men seek to understand the substance of the acts they perform in their daily activities. Even if they are obeying certain regulations of the world that compel them to certain attitudes, it is imperative to examine the quality of their personal contribution within the mechanism of circumstances, because it is God's law that every sowing develops.
Good sows life, evil sows death. The former is the evolutionary movement on the ascending scale toward the Divinity; the latter is stagnation.

Many Spirits, body by body, remain on Earth with the same recapitulations for millennia. The harmful sowing conditioned them to the so-called “death in sin.” They cross the days, redeeming ghastly debts and falling again through the renewal of undesirable seed. Their existence constitutes a large vicious circle, because evil roots them to the burning and arid soil of ungrateful passions.
Only good can confer the award of supreme freedom, representing the sole key capable of opening the sacred doors of the Infinite to the anxious soul.
Let there be, therefore, sufficient care within us every day, because good or evil, having been sown, will grow alongside us, in accordance with the laws that govern life.

messages.title: Heresies
paragraphs: “For there must also be factions among you, that those who are approved may be recognized among you.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 11:19)
Let us receive heretics with sympathy, let materialists speak freely, let no one rise up against those who doubt, let unbelievers possess tribunals and voices.
This is just. Paul of Tarsus wrote this verse under deep inspiration.
Those who condemn the desperate of fate do not judge divine love with the necessary understanding. What can be said of the father who curses his son for having returned home sick and without hope?

Whoever cannot believe in God is sick. In this condition, the words of the desperate are sincere, for they proceed from empty souls, in cries for help, no matter how disguised those cries may seem under the brilliant cloak of the world's philosophical or scientific concepts. Even if the unfortunates of this order attack us, their useless efforts redound to the benefit of all, enabling the selection of legitimate values in the work initiated.

As for the supposed necessity of administering faith to deniers, let us forget the presumption of satisfying them, keeping with us the certainty that God has much to give them. Let us receive them as brothers and be convinced that the Father will do the rest.

messages.title: Vain Honors
paragraphs: “And in vain they worship me, teaching as doctrines the commandments of men.” — JESUS (Mark, 7:7)
The actuality of Christianity offers us profound lessons regarding the aforementioned statement.

No one doubts the Christian breath that animates Western civilization. It should be noted, however, that the Christian essence in its institutions was nothing more than a breath, without substantial renewals, because, soon after the divine ministry of the Master, men came and drafted ordinances and decrees under the presumption of honoring Christ, truly sowing separatism and destruction.

Recent centuries are full of notable figures of kings, religious figures, and politicians who claimed to be defenders of Christianity and apostles of its lights. All of them wrote or taught in the name of Jesus.

Princes issued famous commands, clerics published bulls and compendiums, and administrators organized celebrated laws. However, in vain did they seek to honor the Savior, teaching doctrines that are human caprices, because today's world is still a battlefield of ideas, just as in the time when Christ came to us personally, with the only difference that Pharisaism, the Temple, the Sanhedrin, the Praetorium, and Caesar's Court bear other names today. It is important to recognize, therefore, that over the effort of so many years, it is necessary to renew general understanding and serve the Lord, not according to men, but according to His own teachings.

messages.title: Preaching
paragraphs: “And He said to them, ‘Let us go into the next towns, that I may preach there also, because for this purpose I have come.’” — (MARK, 1:38)

In this verse from Mark, Jesus declares that He came into the world to preach. However, as the meaning of the concept has been erroneously interpreted, it is reasonable to remember that, with such an assertion, the Master included in the act of preaching all the sacrificial gestures of His life.
Generally, we see the mission of teaching heavily demoralized on Earth.

Official science has chairs, politics has tribunes, and religion speaks from pulpits. However, those who teach, with praiseworthy exceptions, are almost always characterized by two different ways of acting. They display certain attitudes when they preach, and adopt others during daily activity. Hence general perturbation results, because listeners feel at ease to change the “garment of character.”

Every dissertation molded in good is useful. Jesus came into the world for this, preached the truth everywhere, gave speeches of renewal, and commented on the necessity of love for the solution of our problems. However, He mixed words and living testimonies, from the first manifestation of His sublime apostolate until the cross. By preaching, therefore, the Master equally understood the sacrifices of life. Sending us divine teaching in this sense, the Gospel tells us that the Master wore a seamless tunic at the supreme hour of Calvary.

messages.title: Enter and Cooperate
paragraphs: “So he, trembling and astonished, said, ‘Lord, what do You want me to do?’ Then the Lord said to him, ‘Arise and go into the city, and you will be told what you must do.’” — (ACTS, 9:6)
This particular detail from the Acts of the Apostles is clothed in great beauty for those who desire an understanding of service with Christ.

If the Master had appeared to the passionate rabbi of Jerusalem in the splendor of divine and immortal light, if He had spoken direct and unforgettable words to his heart, why did He not finish the explanation, recommending instead that he enter Damascus in order to hear what it behooved him to know? It is because the law of cooperation among men is the great and generous principle through which Jesus closely follows all of Humanity through the channels of inspiration.

The Master teaches disciples and comforts them through themselves. The more the apprentice reaches His sphere of influence, the more qualified they will be to constitute themselves as His faithful and just instrument.
Paul of Tarsus contemplated the resurrected Christ in His imperishable greatness, but was forced to avail himself of Ananias to begin the redeeming task that befell him among men.

This lesson should be well used by companions who anxiously await the death of the body, begging for transfer to superior worlds merely because they have heard wonderful descriptions from divine messengers. Meditating on the teaching, they should ask themselves what they would do in the higher Spheres if they have not yet appropriated the educational values that Earth can offer them. It is more reasonable, therefore, that they rise from the past and penetrate the edifying struggle of each day on Earth, because, in the sincere work of fraternal cooperation, they will receive from Jesus the explanation regarding what it behooves them to do.

messages.title: Time of Trust
paragraphs: “And he said unto them, Where is your faith?” — (LUKE, 8.25)
The storm had established disturbance in the minds of the strongest disciples. Disoriented before the fury of the elements, they cried out to Jesus for help.
The Master attends to them, but then asks:
— “Where is your faith?”

The scene suggests far-reaching reflections. Jesus' interrogation clearly indicates the need to maintain trust when everything seems obscure and lost. In such circumstances arises the opportunity for faith, in its proper time.
If there is a time for work and rest, planting and harvesting, trust will likewise reveal itself at the appropriate hour.
No one exercises optimism when all situations combine for well-being. It is difficult to demonstrate friendship in happy moments.

The disciples should naturally await opportunities for greater struggle, in which they will need to apply the Lord's teachings more extensively and intensively. Without this, it would be impossible to measure values.
In the painful present, countless companions invoke Christ's direct cooperation. And help always comes, because heavenly mercy is infinite, but once the difficulty is overcome, expect the inquiry:
— Where is your faith?
And other obstacles will ensue, until the disciple learns to master himself, to educate himself, and to overcome, serenely, with the lessons received.

messages.title: The Golden Rule
paragraphs: “Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.” — JESUS (Matthew, 22.39)

incontestably, many centuries before the coming of Christ, the Golden Rule was already taught in the world, brought by ambassadors of His wisdom and mercy. It is important to clarify, however, that such a principle was transmitted with greater or lesser exemplification by its expositors.
The Greeks said: “Do not do to your neighbor what you do not wish to receive from him.”
The Persians affirmed: “Do as you wish to be done unto you.”
The Chinese declared: “What you do not desire for yourself, do not do to others.”
The Egyptians recommended: “Let pass him who did to others what he desired for himself.”
The Hebrews doctored: “What you do not want for yourself, do not desire for your neighbor.”
The Romans insisted: “The law engraved in human hearts is to love the members of society as oneself.”

In antiquity, all peoples received the golden law of Christ's magnanimity. Prophets, administrators, judges, and philosophers, however, acted as instruments more or less identified with the inspiration of the higher Planes of life. Their figures faded within the precincts of initiatory temples or became blurred on the screen of time in view of their fragmentary testimonies.

With the Master, however, the Golden Rule is the divine novelty, because Jesus taught and exemplified it, not with partial virtues, but in the plenitude of work, abnegation, and love, in the clarity of public squares, revealing Himself to the eyes of all Humanity.

messages.title: Glory to Good
paragraphs: “Glory, honour, and peace, to every man that worketh good.” — PAUL (Romans, 2.10)

Malice usually leads man to false appreciations of good, when it does not stem from the religious confession to which he dedicates himself, the work environment that is proper to him, or the family community in which he integrates.
Egoism makes him believe that complete good could only be born from his hands or those of his own. This is one of the most inferior characteristics of personality.

Good flows incessantly from God, and God is the Father of all men. And it is through the good man that the Most High works against the sectarianism that transformed His terrestrial children into stubborn combatants of sterile and bloody actions.
No matter how much the spontaneous lessons of Heaven summon creatures to recognize this truth, men continue in attitudes of offense, threat, and destruction toward one another.
The Father, however, will consecrate good, wherever good may be.
It is essential not to focus on individuals, but rather to observe and understand the good that the Supreme Lord sends us through them.

What does the external aspect of this or that man matter? What do his nationality, his name, his color matter? Let us note the message of which they are bearers. If they remain consecrated to evil, they are worthy of the good we can do them, but if they are good and sincere in the sector of service where they find themselves, they deserve the peace and honor of God.

messages.title: Consultations
paragraphs: “Now Moses in the law commanded us, that such should be stoned: but what sayest thou?” — (JOHN, 8.5)

Several times the spirit of bad faith surrounded the Master with questions, awaiting certain answers by which to ridicule Him. His word, however, was always firm, incontestable, full of divine flavor.
We refer to this fact to consider that such notes invite the disciple to always consult the wisdom, gesture, and example of the Master.
The teachings and acts of Jesus constitute spontaneous lessons for all questions of life.
Man usually spends great financial assets on the inquiries of intelligence. The opinion of legal professionals sometimes costs the price of agonizing sacrifice.
Jesus, however, provides decisive and profound opinions, free of charge. It is enough that the soul seeks prayer, balance, and quietude. The Master will speak to it in the Good News of Redemption.

Frequently, unexpected cases arise, problems of difficult solution. Man is not unaware of what customs and traditions command to be resolved in a certain way; however, it is essential that the apprentice of the Gospel asks, in the sanctuary of the heart:
— But You, Master, what do You say to me regarding this?
And the answer will not delay like divine light in the great silence.

messages.title: The Blind Man of Jericho
paragraphs: “Saying, What wilt thou that I shall do unto thee? And he said, Lord, that I may receive my sight.” — (LUKE, 18.41)
The blind man of Jericho is one of the great figures of evangelical teachings.
Luke's narrative informs us that the unfortunate man walked along the road, begging… Sensing the approach of the Master, he began to cry out, imploring mercy.

The common people grew angry in the face of such insistent pleas. They tried to stop him, recommending that he silence his requests. Jesus, however, hears his supplication, approaches him, and asks lovingly:
— “What wilt thou that I shall do unto thee?”
Before the magnanimous dispenser of divine goods, receiving such ample freedom, the sincere beggar answers only this:
— “Lord, that I may receive my sight!”
The purpose of this honest and humble blind man should be ours in all circumstances of life.

Immersed in the flesh or outside it, we are sometimes this beggar of Jericho, alms-seeking at the margins of the common road. Life calls us, work appeals to us, the light of knowledge blesses us, but we remain undecided, without the courage to march toward the elevated realization we must attain. And when the opportunity for our spiritual encounter with Christ arises, besides feeling that the world turns against us, inducing us to indifference, it is very rare for us to know how to ask sensibly.

For this very reason, the recollection of the poor man mentioned in Luke's verse is very valuable, since it is not necessary for us to appear before the Master with a voluminous baggage of requests. It is enough that we ask Him for the gift of seeing, with the exact understanding of the particulars of the evolutionary path. May the Lord, therefore, make us perceive all phenomena and situations, persons and things, with love and justice, and we will possess what is necessary for our immortal joy.

messages.title: Conversing
paragraphs: “Let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth, but that which is good to the use of edifying, that it may minister grace unto the hearers.” — PAUL (Ephesians, 4.29)
The taste for right conversation and edifying talks characterize relations of legitimate fraternal love.

Souls that understand one another, in this or that sector of common activity, cherish affectionate and wise conversations, like living caskets of God, exchanging among themselves the most precious values.
The word precedes all noble movements in life. It weaves the ideals of love, stimulates the divine part, unfolds civilization, organizes families and peoples.
Jesus bequeathed the Gospel to the world by conversing. And those who reach a higher plane of manifestation prize loving and clarifying speech.
Through the loss of the taste for conversing with someone, man can evaluate whether he is falling or if his friend is stalling in unexpected deviations.

However, besides those who remain in a position of superiority, there are those who disfigure the sacred gift of the verb, compelling it to the greatest baseness. They are lovers of ridicule, mockery, and false customs. The word, however, is a gift so holy that, even then, it reveals to correct listeners the quality of the spirit that insults and disfigures it, placing it immediately in the low place that belongs to it in the frameworks of life.
Conversing is a sublime possibility. Do not relax, therefore, this concession of the Most High, because by your conversation you will be known.

messages.title: Who Are You?
paragraphs: “There is one lawgiver, who is able to save and to destroy: who art thou that judgest another?” — (JAMES, 4.12)
There should exist, on man's part, great caution in issuing opinions regarding the wrongdoing of others.
An unconscious or frivolous opinion can generate disasters much greater than the error of others, converted into an object of examination.

Naturally, there are certain responsibilities that require careful and patient observations by those to whom they were conferred. An administrator needs to analyze the elements of human composition that integrate his machinery of services. A magistrate, paid by the people's savings, is obliged to examine the problems of social peace or health, deliberating with serenity and justice in defense of collective good. However, it is important to understand that men like these, understanding the extent and delicacy of their spiritual charges, suffer greatly when compelled to the service of regeneration of living parts, strayed or sickly, forwarded to their responsibility.
On the common road, however, there is a great excess of people addicted to precipitation and levity.

We believe it is useful for each disciple, when besieged by unwise considerations, to remember the exact role he is representing in the field of present life, questioning himself before answering the tempting inquiries: “Is this matter of my interest? Who am I? Am I, in fact, in a condition to judge anyone?”

messages.title: The Great Question
paragraphs: “And why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?” — JESUS (Luke, 6.46)
In lamentable indifference, many people wait for the death of the body in order to hear the sublime words of Christ.
However, the reason for such a purpose is not understood. The Master remains alive in His Gospel of Love and Light.

It is unnecessary to await solemn occasions to hear His sublime and clear teachings. Many apprentices approach holy work but desire direct revelations. They would have more faith, they assert nonchalantly, if they heard the Lord personally in His divine manifestations. They believe themselves deserving of celestial gifts and end up considering that the service of the Gospel is too great for human effort, and they set about waiting for unforeseen miracles, without perceiving that laziness subtly mixes with their vanity, neutralizing their strengths.

Such companions do not know how to hear the Divine Master in His immortal verb. They ignore that their service is the one to which they were called, no matter how humble the activities to which they adjust seem.
In the quality of a politician or a street sweeper, in a palace or a hut, the man of Earth can do what Jesus taught him.

This is why the Lord's timely question should be indelibly engraved in all temples, so that disciples, in pronouncing His name, never forget to sincerely attend to the recommendations of His sublime verb.

messages.title: Beware
paragraphs: “But these speak evil of those things which they know not: but what they know naturally, as brute beasts, in those things they corrupt themselves.” — (JUDE, 10)

In all places, we find people always disposed to ungracious and ungrateful commentary regarding what they do not know. Frivolous and inconstant souls, they do not master the movements of life, remaining subjugated by their own unconsciousness.

And these are precisely the ones who, in their instinctive manifestations, behave in what they know like irrational beings. Their particular action usually corrupts the most sacred matters, insults the most generous intentions, and ridicules the noblest deeds.
Beware of the attitudes of irresponsible murmurers.

Christ granted us the light of the Gospel so that our analysis might not be cold and obscure. Knowledge with Jesus is the transforming clarity of life, conferring upon us the gift of understanding the living message of each being and the significance of each thing on the infinite path.
Only those who judge their own ignorance, respecting the domain of circumstances they do not know, are capable of producing fruits of perfection with the gifts of God they already possess.
.Emmanuel

messages.title: Knowing and Doing
paragraphs: “If ye know these things, happy are ye if ye do them.” — JESUS (John, 13.17)
Between knowing and doing there is a singular difference.
Almost everyone knows, few do.
All religious sects, generally speaking, only teach what constitutes the good. All have servants, believers, and propagandists, but the apostles of each become scarcer every day.
There are always qualified voices to indicate the paths. It is the word of those who know.
Rare creatures bravely enter the path, often in silence, abandoned and misunderstood. It is the supreme effort of those who do.
Jesus understood the indecision of the children of Earth and, transmitting to them the word of truth and life, made the maximum exemplification through culminating sacrifices.
The existence of an elevated theory involves the necessity of experience and work. If edifying action were unnecessary, the humblest thesis of good would cease to exist as useless.

John noted the Master's lesson with wisdom. The verse demonstrates that only those who concretize the Lord's teachings can be blessed. Herein lies, in the field of Christian service, the difference between culture and practice, between knowing and doing.

messages.title: Accountable to oneself
paragraphs: “So then each of us shall give account of himself to God.” — PAUL (Romans, 14.12)

It is reasonable for man to dedicate himself to solving all the problems pertaining to the sphere that surrounds him in the world; however, it is necessary that he know the kind of account he will render to the Supreme Lord at the end of the obligations entrusted to him.
Most creatures are anxious about the destiny of others, while neglecting themselves. There are men who despair over the impossibility of improving their companions or certain institutions.

Yet, to whom do the world's patrimonial assets truly belong? The answer is clear, because the most powerful lords will detach themselves from planetary economy, handing it over to God's new laborers for the service of infinite evolution.

This argument, however, will raise certain questions from less discerning minds. If the required account refers to the personal circle, what does man have to do with the accounts of his family, his home, his workshop? It is incumbent upon us, then, to clarify that the companions of domestic intimacy, the possession of the home, the purposes of the group in which one works, belong to the Supreme Lord, but man, in the account proper to him, is obliged to reveal his line of conduct toward his family, the home in which he finds refuge, and the source of his common activities. Naturally, no one will answer for others; however, each Spirit, in detailing the effort incumbent upon him, will be compelled to clarify the quality of his action in the smallest departments of earthly realization, where he was called to live.

messages.title: Spiritual children
paragraphs: “For everyone who partakes only of milk is unskilled in the word of righteousness, for he is a babe.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 5.13)

When assessing the fellow strugglers who make up our daily work framework, it is useful to avoid shocks when flaws and weaknesses unexpectedly arise. Before issuing any judgment, it is advisable to know the caliber of the spiritual values under examination.

Let us never dispense with understanding toward those who stray from the straight path. The road traveled by the experienced man is full of children of this nature. God surrounds the steps of the wise with expressions of ignorance, so that the shadow may receive light and so that this same light may be glorified. In this substantially divine exchange, the ignorant learns and the wise grows.

Well-wishing disciples need a sincere attitude of observation and tolerance. It is natural that they rejoice in the rich and substantial food with which they are given to nourish the soul; however, let them not despise other brothers, whose spiritual organism still tolerates only the simple milk of early knowledge.
Every child is fragile and no one should condemn them for it.

If your mind can soar in higher flight, do not forget those who remained in the nest where you were born and where you spent a long time completing your plumage. Before your dazzled eyes, the infinite stretches out. They will be with you one day, and because full union is lagging, do not abandon them to chance, nor refuse them the milk they love and still need.

messages.title: Gifts
paragraphs: “Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above.” — (JAMES, 1.17)
Once man is certain that he possesses nothing good unless God grants it to him, life on Earth will take on new directions.
Wisdom has said since antiquity:
— Do your part and the Lord will help you.

Recognizing the high tenor of the exhortation, we are compelled to recognize that, even in the acquisition of professional titles, man is the child who strives for a few years so that the Father may grant him a certificate of competence through human teachers.
What occurs in the heritage of material achievements happens in the circle of the spirit's edifices.

Indisputably, every good gift and every perfect gift comes from God. However, to receive the benefit, it is necessary to “knock” on the door so that it may be opened to us, according to the evangelical recommendation.
Do you want the gift of healing? Begin by loving the sick, by taking an interest in solving their needs.
Do you want the gift of teaching? Make yourself a friend of those who minister knowledge in the name of the Lord, through works and edifying words.
Do you expect the gift of virtue? Discipline yourself.
Do you intend to speak correctly? Learn to be silent at the opportune moment.
Do you desire access to Christ's sacred circles? Approach Him, not only through elevated conversation, but also through attitudes of sacrifice, such as those of His life.
Excellent qualities are gifts that proceed from God; however, each one has its respective door and requires a different key.

messages.title: Peace
paragraphs: “Jesus said to them again, ‘Peace to you.’” — (JOHN, 20.21)
Many restless people, examining the exchange between the new disciples of the Gospel and the disincarnate, anxiously ask about the possibilities of spiritual collaboration alongside human activities.
Why do the emissaries of the invisible not provide sensational discoveries to the world?
Why do they not reveal the processes for curing diseases that defy Science?
How do they not prevent the painful clash between nations?

Such investigators, distanced from notions of justice, do not understand that it would be terrible to steal from man the elements of work, redemption, and elevation. They commonly become annoyed with the reiterated and affectionate recommendations of peace in messages from the Beyond, because they have not yet harmonized with Christ.

Let us observe the Master with the disciples when He returned to comfort them from the spiritual plane. We do not observe in His words any torturing message, He does not establish the least expression of sensationalism, He does not put forward concepts of supernatural revelation.
Jesus demonstrates survival to them and wishes them peace.

Is this insufficient for the sincere soul seeking integration with higher life? Does not the fact of recognizing the continuation of existence beyond death, in the certainty that there will be an examination of individual commitments, involve great responsibility?
Working and suffering constitute logical processes of perfection and ascent. And that we attend to these imperatives of the Law with ample peace is the loving and pure desire of Jesus Christ.
Let us strive to understand such truths, for there are numerous learners awaiting great signs, like lazy people who breathe in the shade, waiting for the will-o'-the-wisp of the least effort.

messages.title: The vine
paragraphs: “I am the true vine, and My Father is the vinedresser.” — JESUS (John, 15.1)
God is the Eternal Creator whose designs remain unfathomable to us. By His watchful love all beings are created, by His wisdom worlds move in the Boundless.
Small and obscure, the Earth cannot fathom divine greatness. The Father, however, envelops us all in the vibrations of His glorious goodness.
He is the soul of everything, the essence of the Universe.
We remain in the terrestrial field, of which He is the owner and supreme dispenser.
However, so that we may feel His presence in our limited understanding, Jesus was granted to us as His maximum personification.

It would be useful for man to observe on the Planet his immense school of labor; and all of us, before universal greatness, must recognize our condition as humble beings, in need of self-improvement and illumination.

Within our smallness, we would succumb to spiritual hunger, stalled in the shadow of ignorance, were it not for this vine of truth and love that the Supreme Lord granted us in Jesus Christ. From His divine sap proceed all our elevated achievements in the services of Earth. Nourished by this sublime source, it is incumbent upon us to recognize that without Christ the organizations of the world would be lost for lack of a foundation. In Him we find the living bread of souls and, from the beginning, His infinite love in the terrestrial globe is the divine foundation of all the truths of life.

messages.title: The branches of the vine
paragraphs: “I am the vine, you are the branches.” — JESUS (John, 15.5)
Jesus is the goodness and love of the beginning.

All generous notions of Humanity were born from His divine influence. With justice, He assured the disciples in this passage of the Gospel of John that His sublime Spirit represents the tree of life and His sincere followers the promising fronds, adding that, outside the trunk, the branches would dry up, walking toward the fire of purification.
Without Christ, without the essence of His greatness, all human works are destined to perish.
Science will be fragile and poor without the values of conscience; religious schools will be condemned as soon as they turn away from truth and goodness.
Infinite is Jesus' mercy in the movements of planetary life. At the center of every noble expression of existence beats His loving heart, replete with the sap of forgiveness and kindness.

Men are green branches of the glorious tree. When they betray their duties, they dry up because they turn away from the sap, rolling onto the floor of disillusionment, so that they may be purified in the fire of restorative sufferings, in order to be taken up again by Jesus, through His mercy, for renewal. It is reasonable, therefore, that we manifest our fidelity to the Divine Master, reflecting on the high number of times we dried up in the past, despite the immense love that sustains us throughout life.

messages.title: Gains
paragraphs: “And those things which you have provided—whose will they be?” — JESUS (Luke, 12.20)

In all human groupings, the preoccupation with gaining throbs. The spirit of profit reaches the simplest sectors. Boys, barely out of early childhood, show themselves interested in selfishly hoarding something. Today's world counts numerous mothers who abandon their homes to strangers for many hours of the day in order to experience the lucrative mine. In this sense, most creatures turn the evolutionary march into a restless race.
Behind the sepulcher, the point of arrival for all who left the cradle, truth awaits man and asks:
— What have you brought?
The unfortunate one will reply that he gathered material advantages, that he strived to secure a tranquil position for himself and his own.
Examined, however, the baggage is verified, almost always, to show victories as resounding defeats. They do not constitute values of the soul, nor do they bear the seal of eternal goods.

Having reached such an equation, the traveler looks back and feels cold. He binds himself, in an inexplicable way, to the results of everything he hoarded on Earth's Crust. The restless conscience fills with clouds and the voice of the Gospel sounds in his ears: Woe to you, because your gains were disastrous losses! “And those things which you have provided—whose will they be?”

messages.title: Money
paragraphs: “For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil, for which some have strayed from the faith in their greed, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.” — PAUL (1 Timothy, 6.10)
Paul does not tell us that money in itself is a scourge for Humanity.

Several times, we see the Master in contact with the subject, contributing to broadening our understanding. Receiving certain advice from the people who present Him with a certain coin of the era, bearing the effigy of the Roman emperor, He recommends that man give to Caesar what is to Caesar, exemplifying respect for constructive conventions. In one of His most beautiful parables, He uses the symbol of a lost drachma. In the movements of the Temple, He appreciates the widow's tiny mite.

Money does not signify evil. However, the apostle to the gentiles clarifies that the love of money is the root of all kinds of evils. Man cannot be condemned for his financial expressions, but rather for the misuse of such material resources, because it is through the obsession of possession that pride and idleness, two phantoms of human misfortune, install themselves in souls, compelling them to deviate from eternal light.

The money that comes into your hands through straight paths, which only your conscience can analyze in the divine clarity, is a friend who seeks your healthy guidance and humanitarian counsel. You will answer to God for the directives you give it, and woe to you if you materialize this beneficial force in the gloomy edifice of iniquity!

messages.title: Gaining
paragraphs: “For what will it profit a man if he gains the whole world, and loses his own soul?” — JESUS (Mark, 8.36)

Terrestrial creatures, in general, have not yet learned how to gain. However, the human spirit remains on the planet in search of something. It is indispensable to attain values of self-improvement for eternal life.

Jesus recommended to His charges that they seek, that they persist…… This signifies that man lingers on Earth to gain in ennobling struggle. All disturbance in this sense stems from the corrupted minds of straying souls.

Man is always determined to conquer the world, but never willing to conquer himself for a higher sphere. In this false concept, he subverts order in the opportunities of each day. If God grants him ample health, he usually uses it to acquire destructive disease; if he manages to amass financial possibilities, he tries to monopolize the interests of others.

The Divine Master did not recommend that the human soul move about stripped of goals and aspirations of gain; He merely pointed out that man needs to know what he seeks, what kind of profits he aims for, and what ends he proposes in his terrestrial activities.

If your desires rest on factitious acquisitions, regarding passing situations or patrimonies doomed to decay, renew your spiritual vision while there is time, because it is of no use to gain the world that does not belong to you and lose yourself indefinitely to immortal life.

messages.title: The beloved
paragraphs: “But, beloved, we are confident of better things concerning you.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 6.9)
People comment with bitterness on the apparent progress of the wicked.
The believer marvels at the good position of men who know no scruples, often highly placed in the financial sphere.
Many ask: “Where is the Lord who did not see their underhanded methods?”

The question, however, evidences more ignorance than sense. Where is the purpose of the wicked man's coined treasure? Even if he experienced unalterable health for a hundred years on Earth, he would be compelled to abandon the patrimony to restart learning.

Eternity confers reduced importance on external goods. Those who exclusively accumulate transitory advantages outside their souls, fully forgetting the inner sphere, are worthy of pity. They will leave everything, almost always, to the mercy of irresponsibility.

This does not happen, however, with the owners of spiritual wealth. Constituting the beloved of God, they feel identified with the Father wherever they are led. In difficulty and storm, they keep the joy of the divine heritage treasured in their hearts.

From the impious, it is reasonable to expect indifference, ambition, avarice, the preoccupation with unreflectingly hoarding; from the ignorant, it is natural to receive foolish questions. However, the apostle to the gentiles exclaims with reason: “But, beloved, we are confident of better things concerning you.”

messages.title: Practice of Good
paragraphs: “For this is the will of God, that by doing good you may put to silence the ignorance of foolish men.” — (1 Peter, 2.15)

As the spirit advances in knowledge, the more it understands the value of time and the opportunities that the greater life provides, recognizing, at last, the imprudence of spending precious resources in sterile and capricious discussions.
The apostle Peter recommends that we remember it is God's will that good be done, imposing silence on the ignorance and folly of men.
A dispute can last for many years, with serious disasters for the forces in litigation; however, a single expression of renunciation is enough for harmony to be established in a single day.
In the divine service, it is advisable not to dispute, except when clarification and energy translate charity. Along this path, the practice of good is the compass of teaching.
Before any dispute, it is convenient to give something of ourselves. This is useful and convincing.
The most humble good is a sacred seed.
Called to argue, Jesus sacrificed himself.
Because he transformed himself into divine light, he overcame the darkness of human ignorance for us.
He did not negotiate with us. Instead, he converted us.
He did not claim understanding. He understood our madness, located our blindness, and helped us even more.

messages.title: Ministries
paragraphs: “As each one has received a gift, minister it to one another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God.” — (1 Peter, 4.10)
Every creature receives from the Supreme Lord the gift of serving as an essentially divine ministry.
If man raises so many problems of difficult solution in his social struggles, it is because he has not yet grasped such high teaching.

The picture of earthly evolution presents a division between those you call 'magnates' and 'proletarians', because, in general, the dignity of honest work, no matter how humble, has not been understood in the world until now.
It is essential that there always be public cleaning professionals, clearers of unhealthy lands, factory managers, and press workers.

Men have not yet understood that the opportunity to cooperate in the works of the Earth transforms them into stewards of God's grace. However, the time will come when everyone will feel rich. The notion of 'capitalist' and 'worker' will be renewed. Both will understand themselves as efficient servants of the Most High.
The gardener will feel that his ministry is a brother to the task entrusted to the plant manager.
Each one will minister the goods received from the Father, in his own sphere of action, without the egoistic idea of earning to enrich on Earth, but of serving with profit to enrich in God.

messages.title: Kinship
paragraphs: “And he said to him: 'Get out of your country and from your kindred, and come to a land that I will show you.'” — (ACTS, 7.3)

In the circles of faith, various candidates for the position of disciples of Jesus complain about the systematic opposition of relatives regarding the principles they embraced for religious acquisitions.
Blood ties do not always unite essentially akin souls. Frequently, due to the impositions of consanguinity, great enemies are forced into daily embraces under the same roof.

It is reasonable to suggest a division between the concepts of 'family' and 'kinship'. The first would constitute the symbol of the eternal bonds of love, the second would signify the crucible of struggles, sometimes acerbic, in which we must dilute the imperfections of feelings, fusing them into the divine alloy of love for eternity. The family would not be the kinship, but the kinship would later convert into the holy expressions of the family.
We recall these concepts in order to awaken the vigilance of less-advised companions.

On the way to Jesus, it will be useful to abandon the sphere of gossip and misunderstandings of kinship and guide one's acts in the execution of the most sublime duty, without faltering in exemplification, because, in this way, the faithful apprentice will be exhorting them, without words, to participate in the rights of the greater family, which is that of Jesus Christ.

messages.title: Who are you?
paragraphs: “And the evil spirit answered and said, 'Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are you?'” — (ACTS, 19.15)
Any expression of commerce is based on purchasing power. To obtain, one must possess.

In the interchange of the two worlds, terrestrial and spiritual, the phenomenon obeys the same principle. In Caesar's commercial operations, coins or fiduciary expressions with effigies and identifications concerning them are required. In spiritual exchange operations, highly individualized values with the signs of Christ are required.
The money of Jesus is love. Without it, no one is allowed to venture into the sacred commerce of souls.
The verse named here constitutes a beneficial warning to all who, for the enlightenment of others, invoke the Master without living titles of His sacrificial school.
Especially with regard to relations with the invisible Plane, taking care to avoid random statements.
Do not venture into the movement without the purchasing power of the love of Jesus.
The Master is equally known to His unhappy adversaries. The sincere disciples of the Lord are observed by them as well. The enemies of light recognize their sublime value.

When you prepare yourselves, therefore, for this kind of work, do not forget your own identification, because you will probably be questioned by the representatives of evil, who will ask you who you are.

messages.title: The Greatest Treasure
paragraphs: “For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.” — JESUS (Luke, 12.34)

In the world, the temples of religious faith, once consecrated to the Divinity of the Father, are departments of the infinite house of God, where Jesus dispenses His goods to the hearts of the Earth, regardless of the school of belief to which they belong.
To these subdivisions of the eternal sanctuary come the wards of Christ, in their different degrees of comprehension. Each one instinctively reveals to the Lord where he places his treasure.

Often, for this very reason, in the various precincts of His house, Jesus receives, without response, the supplications of countless believers of childish, contradictory, or counterproductive mentality.
The selfish person speaks of his treasure, exalting precarious possessions; the miser refers to petty concerns; the hedonist demonstrates insatiable appetites; the fanatic repeats crazy requests.
Each one presents their wounded caprice as being the greatest pain.

Christ hears their requests and awaits the opportunity to make known to them the imperishable treasure. He listens in silence, because the tender grass needs time destined for the evolutionary process, and waits, confident, because He does not dispense with the collaboration of resolute and sincere disciples for the extension of the divine apostolate. At the appropriate moment, these arise under His sublime influx, and the landscape of the temples changes. They are not just believers who appear for prayer, they are determined workers who arrive for work. Full of courage, willing to die so that others may attain life, they exemplify renunciation and selflessness, reveal the Will of the Father in themselves and, with this, expand in the world the understanding of the greatest treasure, synthesized in the conquest of eternal light and universal love, which already enriches their magnified spirit.

messages.title: Asking
paragraphs: “And Jesus answered and said, 'You do not know what you ask.'” — (MATTHEW, 20.22)
Most believers go to houses of prayer with the purpose of asking for something.

Rare are those who appear there in the true attitude of children of God, interested in the sublime desires of the Lord regarding the improvement of knowledge, the renewal of intimate values, and the spiritual use of the opportunities received from On High.

Strictly speaking, men should recognize in the temples the sacred place of the Most High, where they should learn fraternity, love, and cooperation in His divine program. Almost all of them, however, prefer the act of insisting, of stubbornness, of imposing themselves on the paternal affection of God in order to bribe His Infinite Power. Ineveterate beggars, they abandon the straight path of their lives most of the time, due to supreme rebellion in relations with the Father.
They complain so much that the desired experience is granted to them. Disasters ensue. Pains arise. Then boredom appears, which is always the child of the incomprehension of our duties.

We provoke certain gifts along the way, we advance in requesting the inheritance that belongs to us, demanding premature concessions from the Father, in the manner of the prodigal son, but disenchantment constitutes the poison of imprudence and irresponsibility.
Boredom will always represent the bitter fruit of the precipitation of those who throw themselves into estates that do not belong to them.
Let us, therefore, be careful in asking, because, above all, we must request the understanding of Jesus' will regarding us.

messages.title: How do you ask?
paragraphs: “Until now you have asked nothing in My name. Ask, and you will receive, that your joy may be full.” — JESUS (John, 16.24)
In many corners, we find creatures disenchanted with prayer.

Did not Jesus promise the answer of Heaven to those who asked in His name? Many hearts remain discouraged because death has stolen a beloved friend, because unforeseen disasters have arisen on the common road.
However, let us repeat, the Divine Master taught that man should ask in His name.

For this very reason, the believing soul, convinced of its own fragility, should interrogate conscience about the content of its supplications to the Supreme Lord, in the mechanism of spiritual manifestations.

Will it be supplicating in the name of Christ or of the world's vanities? To complain, by virtue of the caprices that obscure the paths of the heart, is to throw the dust of earthly anxieties at the Divine Sun; but to ask, in the name of Jesus, is to accept His wise and loving will, is to surrender with all our heart so that we may be granted what is necessary.
Only in this act of perfect understanding of His sublime love will we find complete joy, infinite happiness.

Observe the substance of your prayers. How do you ask? In the name of the world or in the name of Christ? Those who reveal themselves discouraged with prayer confess the childishness of their requests.

messages.title: The Living of the Beyond
paragraphs: “And behold, two men were talking with Him, who were Moses and Elijah.” — (LUKE, 9.30)

Various religious schools, perhaps defending certain interests of the priesthood, ensure that the Gospel does not present bases for the movement of interchange between men and the discarnate Spirits who preceded them on the journey of the Beyond...
However, in this passage from Luke, we see the Master of Masters conferring with two entities coming from the invisible Sphere of which the tomb is the door of access.

In fact, under various circumstances, we find Christ in contact with troubled or perverse souls, alleviating the sufferings of unfortunate persecuted ones. However, the dogmatic mentality found there the manifestation of Satan, eternal and insatiable enemy.

Here, however, it is a sublime event on Tabor. We do not see any demonic demonstration, but rather two glorious Spirits in intimate conversation with the Savior. And we cannot place the phenomenon in an association of generalities, since the 'friends from the other world' who spoke with Jesus upon the mountain were duly identified. The fact was not registered declaring, for example, that it was the visit of an angel, but of Moses and his companion, clearly implying that the 'dead' return from their new life.

messages.title: Beyond the Tomb
paragraphs: “But if there is no resurrection of the dead, then Christ is not risen.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 15.13)
Eminent theologians, trying to harmonize temporal and spiritual interests, obscured the problem of death, imposing gloomy perspectives on the simple solution proper to it.

Many of them placed souls in specific zones of punishment or purgation, as if they were absolute masters of the elements indispensable to definitive analysis. Others declared that at the moment of the great transition, man plunges into an indefinable sleep until the final day consecrated to the Final Judgment.
Today, however, human intelligence recognizes that logic has evolved with all the possibilities of observation and reasoning.
Resurrection is infinite life. Life is work, joy, and creation in eternity.

How to qualify the presumption of those who designate neighbors and acquaintances to unlimited hell in time? How to believe that millions of creatures remain asleep, awaiting the decisive minute of judgment, when Jesus Himself affirms He is in incessant activity?
The theological arguments are respectable; however, we must not disregard the simplicity of human logic.

Commenting on the subject, within the doors of Christian effort, we are compelled to recognize that the deniers of the evolutionary process of the spiritual man, after the sepulcher, define themselves against the Gospel itself. The Master of Masters rose in edifying work. Who, then, will cross the portal of death to fall into incomprehensible idleness? We are souls, in function of perfection, and, beyond the tomb, we find the continuation of effort and life.

messages.title: Communications
paragraphs: “Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits, whether they are of God.” — (1 John, 4.1)
The new disciples of the Gospel, in their groups of interchange with the spiritual world, almost always manifest anxiety to establish clear and perfect communications with the Beyond.
If failures often appear in this regard, if the experimentations are devoid of success, it is because, in most cases, the inquirer obeys his own selfishness much more than the edifying imperative.

The purpose of exclusivity, in this sense, opens a wide door to deceit. Through it, wrongdoers with harmful instruments can penetrate the temple, since the apprentice closed his eyes to the horizon of eternal truths.

Beautiful and human is the dilation of the bonds of love that unite the incarnate man with the family members who preceded him on the journey Beyond the Tomb, but it is unacceptable that the student forces those who served as his father or brother to interfere in the particular situations concerning him.

There will always be someone who dispenses light in the assemblies of sincere men. The program of such assistance, however, cannot be substantially organized by creatures, who are often unaware of their own needs. Because of this, the apostle recommended that the disciple pay attention not to who speaks, but to the essence of the words, in order to ascertain if the visitor comes from God.

messages.title: Hidden Powers
paragraphs: “And wherever he entered, into villages, cities, or the country, they laid the sick in the marketplaces and begged that they might touch even the fringe of his garment. And as many as touched it were made well.” — (MARK, 6:56)

It is not uncommon to find eager scholars within spiritualist ranks striving, by any means, to acquire hidden powers that would grant them a position of prominence. Frequently, in such circumstances, they fill themselves with far-reaching assertions.

The yearning for self-improvement, the desire for balance, and the intention to maintain peace constitute noble purposes; however, it is advisable that the learner does not surrender to concerns of notoriety, treading the terrain of these thoughts with all possible caution.
Here, too, the Divine Master offers the finest exemplification.

No one on Earth has ever gathered such lofty expressions of unknown resources as Jesus. For the sick, it was enough to touch His garments to be cured of painful infirmities; His hands restored movement to the paralyzed and sight to the blind. Yet, on the day of Calvary, we see the Master wounded and outraged, without resorting to the powers that were His divine prerogative, for the sake of His own situation. Having fulfilled the law of sublime love in the service of the Father, He surrendered to His will when it came to His own personal interests. The Lord's lesson is quite significant.

It is understandable that the disciple studies and enriches themselves with spiritual energies, remembering, however, that before our own interests remain the well-being of others, and that this well-being, distributed along the path of life, is the voice that will speak for us to God and to men, today or tomorrow.

messages.title: To Bear Witness
paragraphs: “And it will turn out for you as an occasion for testimony.” — JESUS (Luke, 21:13)

Naturally, the Master does not take pleasure in seeing His disciples plunged into suffering. Considering, however, the extensive needs of the people of Earth, He understands the indispensable character of trials and obstacles.
Modern pedagogy is full of selective efforts, capacity contests, and intelligence tests.

The Gospel offers similar situations. The friend of Christ must not be a gloomy creature, waiting for sufferings; nevertheless, knowing their working position on a Plane like Earth, they must expect difficulties of every kind.
For the falsified pleasures of the world, the planet is full of misled guides.

How can one invoke the Savior for the continuation of fantasies? When called to Christ, it is so that we learn to execute work in favor of the greater Sphere, without forgetting that service begins within ourselves.
There are many men of cultural value who have established themselves as mentors to those who desire deceptive gifts on the physical plane.
In the Gospel, however, it is not so. When the Master invites someone to His work, it is not so that they may weep in discouragement or rest in idle satisfaction.
If the Lord has called you, do not forget that He already considers you worthy to bear witness.

messages.title: Transitoriness
paragraphs: “They will perish, but you remain; and they will all grow old like a garment.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 1:11)
Ecclesiastes tells us of human vanities and distress amid the whirlwind of Earth's misguided ambitions.

Since the earliest times of the human family, there are creatures confused by the false values of the world. However, it would take only a few minutes of meditation on the transitoriness of everything that throbs in the realm of forms to understand the sovereignty of the Spirit.

Consult the pomp of museums and the ruin of dead civilizations. To what end were so many monuments and triumphal arches raised? Everything functioned as clothing for thought. The idea evolved, the spirit was enriched, and the old coverings remain far behind.
Hands calloused in the construction of brilliant pillars learned from work the luminous secrets of life. Yet, how much bitterness was experienced by the fools who fought unto death to possess them?
Avail yourselves of every opportunity for service as sacred opportunities on the divine march toward God.
Scarcity is valuable because it brings discipline.
Abundance is precious because it multiplies the forms of good.

One and the other, however, will perish one day. In the carnal Sphere, glory and misery constitute frames of temporary presentation. Both pass away. Only Jesus and the Divine Law persevere for us as doors of life and redemption.

messages.title: Opportunity
paragraphs: “Jesus said to them, ‘My time has not yet come, but your time is always ready.’” — (JOHN, 7:6)
The bad worker is always complaining. When he does not attribute his failure to the tools in his hand, he laments the rain, cannot tolerate the heat, and curses the frost and the wind.
This is a blind person difficult to help, since they only see the rough side of situations.

The good worker, however, understands above all the deep meaning of the opportunity they have received. They value all the elements placed in their path, just as they respect the possibilities of others. They do not depend on the seasons. They plant the fruits of both cold and heat with equal enthusiasm. They are a friend of Nature, take advantage of its lessons, have good cheer, and find equal contentment in the harshness of sowing and the joy of harvest.

In this sense, the Master's lesson is clothed with marvelous significance. In the whirlwind of the world's misunderstandings, we should not await the Kingdom of Christ as an immediate achievement, but human opportunity is permanent for perfect collaboration in the Gospel, in order to build it.

The spiritually blind will continue to complain; however, those who have awakened to Jesus know that their season of redeeming work is ready, has not passed, nor is it yet to come. It is today, it is the blessed opportunity to serve, in the name of the Lord, here and now…

messages.title: Clean Hands
paragraphs: “And God worked extraordinary miracles by the hands of Paul.” — (ACTS, 19:11)
The Gospel does not tell us that Paul of Tarsus performed miracles, but rather that God worked extraordinary miracles through his hands.
The Father will always do the same, utilizing all children who present Him with clean hands.
Many Spirits, more conventional than truly religious, found in this news from Acts information about certain privileges that would have been granted to the Apostle.
Above all, however, it is necessary to know that such a concession is not exclusive. Most believers prefer to focus on the sanctified Paul without appreciating the militant worker.
How much did the cleansing of his hands cost the Apostle? Few inquire about this.

Let us remember that the friend of the Gentiles had been a famous rabbi in Jerusalem, had moved among elevated public duties, and had held dominating situations; nevertheless, for the Almighty to use his hands, he suffered all humiliations and made himself ready for all sacrifices for the good of his fellow men. He taught the Gospel amid mockery and scourging, afflictions and stoning. Despite writing luminous epistles, he never abandoned the humble loom until the old age of his body.

Consider the particulars of the subject and observe that God is always the same Father, that divine mercy has not changed, but it asks for clean hands for edificatory services alongside Humanity. Such a requirement is logical and necessary, for the work of the Most High must shine upon human paths.

messages.title: In Caesar's Household
paragraphs: “All the saints greet you, but especially those who are of Caesar's household.” — PAUL (Philippians, 4:22)
It is very common to hear ill-conceived observations from certain brethren in the faith regarding companions called to more difficult tasks amid the possibilities of money or power.

False piety is always ready to criticize the friend who, accepting a laborious public office, finds in it far more annoyances than notes of harmony. Distorted analysis maliciously views everything. If the brother is compelled to participate in major social representations, he is often stigmatized as a traitor to Christ.
It is necessary to expend much vigilance in these judgments.

In apostolic times, Christians of pure life were called 'saints.' Paul of Tarsus, humiliated and persecuted in Rome, had the opportunity to meet numerous souls in these conditions, and what is even more admirable—he fellowshipped with various disciples in such a position, connected with Caesar's palatial dwelling. From them he received attentions and favors, assistance and affection.
Writing to the Philippians, he makes special mention of these friends of Christ.
Do not judge your brother, therefore, by his apparent fortune or political privileges. Above all, remember that there were saints in Nero's household, and never forget such a grand lesson.

messages.title: Edifications
paragraphs: “You are the light of the world. A city set on a hill cannot be hidden.” — JESUS (Matthew, 5:14)
The Gospel is full of loving invitations for men to build themselves up in the example of the Lord.

Not always do the followers of Christ understand this great imperative of self-illumination in favor of harmony in the work to be accomplished. An overwhelming percentage of learners, first of all, remain attentive to the edification of others, belittling the opportunity to attain supreme goods for themselves.

Naturally, it is very difficult to find the opportunity amid the gratifications of human existence, since the blessed resource of illumination is often hidden in the obstacles, perplexities, and shadows of the path.

The Master was very clear in His exposition. So that the disciples may be the light of the world, they will symbolize cities built upon a mountain, where they are never hidden.
