In order for the worker of Jesus to function as an expression of clarity in life, it is indispensable that he elevate himself to the mountain of exemplification, despite the difficulties of the agonizing climb, presenting himself to all in the category of Christian construction.
Such a commitment is imperishable.

The ebb and flow of passions does not tear down edifications of this nature, stoning leaves them intact, and if someone tears them apart, their fragments constitute the continuation of light, in a sublime trail, everywhere, because it was thus that the early martyrs of Christianity sowed the faith.

messages.title: It Is Worth Reflecting
paragraphs: “So then, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath.” — (JAMES, 1:19)

Analyzing, reflecting, and pondering are modalities of the act of listening. It is indispensable that the creature always be disposed to identify the meaning of the voices, suggestions, and situations that surround it.
Without observation, it is impossible to execute the simplest task in the ministry of good. Only after listening with attention can man speak in an edifying way on the evolutionary road.
He who listens, learns. He who speaks, teaches. One keeps, the other scatters.
Only he who keeps in good experience scatters with success.
The apostle's advice is, therefore, of undying timeliness.
And it must be agreed that if man must be prompt in his observations and measured in his words, he must be slow to anger.

Certainly, the human path offers daily varied motives for energetic action; however, whenever possible, it is useful to postpone the expression of anger until the following day, since sometimes the occasion for a more sensible examination arises and the reason for anger disappears.

Let us keep in mind that every man is born to exercise a defined function. By always listening, he can be certain that he will serenely attain the ends for which he is destined, but by speaking, he may abandon the effort halfway, and by getting angry, he will probably accomplish nothing at all.

messages.title: Truths and Fantasies
paragraphs: “But because I tell the truth, you do not believe me.” — JESUS (John, 8:45)
The world always loudly distinguishes the expositors of fantasies.

It is common to observe, almost everywhere, the victory of verbose men who promise miracles and wonders. These deserve great credit from creatures. It is enough for them to cover up the illness, weakness, ignorance, or flaw of men to receive respect. The same does not happen to the cultivators of the truth, no matter how simple it may be. Through all times, for the latter, society has reserved the stake, poison, the cross, and implacable punishment.

Trying to escape the agonizing spiritual situation that is proper to him, man invented fortune-telling, yet imposing upon the diviners the golden disguise of dark and harsh realities. The most skillful charlatan in the manufacture of brilliant lies will be the master of the most numerous and enlightened clientele.
In the interchange with the invisible Sphere, it is urgent that new disciples guard against dangers of this sort.

The technique of praise, the disposition to appear better, the urge to walk ahead of others, the presumption of converting other people's consciences, are great fantasies. It is necessary not to believe in this. It is more reasonable to understand that the work of illumination is difficult, starting from the effort of regenerating ourselves. The friends of truth are not always accepted. They are generally considered fanatics or mystifiers, but… despite everything, for our happiness, it is necessary to attend to the truth while there is still time.

messages.title: To Each One
paragraphs: “Stand upright on your feet.” — PAUL (Acts, 14:10)

Generally speaking, when incarnated in the physical world, we only see the physically crippled, those who have lost bodily equilibrium, those who drag themselves painfully on the ground, enduring rugged defects. We do not possess sufficient vision to identify the sick in spirit, the lame in thought, the crushed in heart.

Where there were only the blind, the creature would end up losing the interest and memory of the visual apparatus; for the same reason, on the Crust of the Earth, where an overwhelming majority of people consist of paralyzed souls regarding virtue, rare are the men who know the disharmony of spiritual health that concerns them, conscious of their undeniable needs.

It is inferred, therefore, that the mission of the Gospel is much more beautiful and extensive than we can imagine. Jesus continues pouring out blessings every day. And the hidden prodigies, operated in the silence of His infinite love, are greater than those verified in Jerusalem and Galilee, since the blind and lepers who were cured, according to apostolic narratives, later fell ill again and died. The healing of our sick and paralyzed Spirits is more important, as it is effected with a view toward eternity.

It is indispensable that we do not lose ourselves in illusory conclusions. Let us sharpen our ears, keeping the apostle's word to the Gentiles. It is imperative that we rise, individually, upon our own feet, for there are many people waiting for angel wings that do not belong to them.

messages.title: Opinions
paragraphs: “Woe to you when all men speak well of you, for so did their fathers to the false prophets.” — JESUS (Luke, 6:26)

Undoubtedly, there are many people of estimable appearance to whom we can resort in appropriate moments, but let no one disregard the opinion of their own conscience, for the voice of God will usually enlighten us in that divine sanctuary.
It is utter madness to purpose counting on general approval for our efforts.

When Jesus uttered the sublime exhortation of this passage in Luke, He acted with absolute knowledge of creatures. The Master knew that in a plane of shocking contrasts like Earth, it will not be possible to please everyone simultaneously.
The man of truth will only be understood, in due time, by the Spirits who make themselves true.
The prudent person will not receive applause from the imprudent.

The Master, in His time, did not gather common sympathies. If He was loved by sincere and simple creatures, He suffered the merciless attack of conventionalists. To Mary of Magdala He was the Savior; to Caiaphas, however, He was the dangerous revolutionary. Time was the only force of general enlightenment.
If you find yourself in edifying service, if your conscience approves you, what do you care about frivolous or insincere opinions?
Fulfill your duty and walk.
Examine the material of the ignorant and slanderers as a profitable warning and remember that it is not possible to reconcile duty with levity, nor truth with falsehood.

messages.title: Human Ordinances
paragraphs: “Therefore submit yourselves to every ordinance of man for the Lord's sake.” — (1 Peter, 2:13)

Certain impulsive temperaments, upon approaching the lessons of Christ, presume the Gospel to be a treatise of principles that destroy the existing order in the world. There are those who picture the Master as a vigorous anarchist, inflamed by sublime rages. Jesus, however, will never be the patron of disorder.

The novelty that overflows from the Gospel does not advise the most humbled Spirit on Earth to adopt weapons against brothers, but rather to humble themselves even further, taking up the cross, following the example of the Savior.
It is clear that the Good News does not teach genuflection before insolent tyranny; however, it asks for respect for human ordinances, for the love of the Divine Master.

If the holder of authority demands more than is his due, he becomes a despot whom the Lord will correct, through circumstances that express His designs at the appropriate moment. This certainty is yet another factor of tranquility for the Christian servant who, under no circumstances, must break the rhythm of harmony.

Do not make yourself indifferent, therefore, to the ordinances of the machinery of work in which you find yourself. It is possible that, many times, they do not correspond to your desires, but remember that Jesus is the Supreme Orderer on Earth and would not place your personal effort where your contribution was unnecessary.

You have something sacred to do where you breathe today. With expressions of revolt, your activity will be negative. Remember this truth and submit to human ordinances for the love of the Divine Lord.

messages.title: Dry Trees
paragraphs: “For if they do these things in a green tree, what will be done in the dry?” — JESUS (Luke, 23:31)

Jesus is the eternal vine, full of divine sap, spreading abundant branches, comforting perfumes, and substantial fruits among men, and the world offered Him nothing save the cross of flagellation and infamously shameful death.
Since remote millennia He has been the Savior, the pure par excellence.
What should we not expect for our part, indebted creatures that we are, representing branches still dry on the tree of life?
In every experience, we need new processes in the service of repair and correction. We are wood without life of our own, which human passions have rendered useless in their destructive fury.
Countrymen strike the punitive rod on peach trees when their sickly branches do not produce. The effect is beneficial and rewarding.
The martyrdom of Christ surpassed the limits of our imagination. As the sublime trunk of life, He suffered because He wished to transmit His fertilizing sap to us.

Like dried wood, in the heat of evil, we suffer by necessity, in favor of ourselves. The world organized the tragedy of the cross for the Master out of a spirit of malice and ingratitude; but as for us, if we have crosses on the redeeming path, it is not because God is rigorous in the execution of His laws, but because He is a Loving Father of our souls, full of wisdom and compassion in His educational processes.

messages.title: Afflictions
paragraphs: “But rejoice to the extent that you partake of Christ's sufferings.” — (1 Peter, 4:13)

It is undeniable that in your earthly learning you will cross days of harsh winter, in which it will be essential to resort to provisions stored within, from the harvests of days of balance and abundance.
You will contemplate the world, in the disillusionment of much-beloved friends, like a temple in ruins, under the onslaught of a cruel storm.

Hopes have faded away in the distance, dreams remain trampled by the ungrateful. Affectionate ones have disappeared, some through indifference, others because they preferred integration into the framework of fleeting interests of the material Plane.

When such a day arises on your horizons, compelling you to restlessness and bitterness, surely you are not forbidden to weep. However, it is necessary not to forget the divine company of the Lord Jesus.

Do you suppose, perchance, that the Master of Masters inhabits a Sphere inaccessible to the thought of men? Do you judge, perhaps, that the Savior does not receive ingratitudes and taunts from human creatures daily? Before we knew the evil of others that afflicts us, He knew ours and suffered for our errors.
Let us not forget, therefore, that in afflictions, it is imperative to take His sublime company and press forward with His serenity and good cheer.

messages.title: Let Us Rise
paragraphs: “Arise, let us go from here.” — JESUS (John, 14:31)
Before retiring for the supreme prayers in the Garden, Jesus spoke to the disciples at length, explaining the deep meaning of His exemplification.
Connecting His sublime thoughts, He made the beautiful invitation inserted in the Gospel of John:
— “Arise, let us go from here.”
The appeal is highly significant.

At the touch of rising, the man of the world usually seeks the movement of easy victories, throwing himself into the struggle thirsty for supremacy or changing residence in the expectation of fleeting improvement.

With Jesus, however, the opposite occurred. He rose to be torn apart, shortly thereafter, by Judas's gesture. He distanced himself from the place where he was in order to reach, a little later, flagellation and death.
Naturally He departed for the glorious destiny of reunion with the Father, but we need to highlight the stages of the journey…

He rose and went out, in search of supreme glory. The stations of the march are eminently educational: — Gethsemane, the Prison, the Praetorium, the Via Dolorosa, Calvary, the Cross constitute very interesting observation points, especially nowadays, which presents countless Christians waiting for the possibility of the journey on the luxury cushions of least effort.

messages.title: Testimony
paragraphs: “Jesus answered him, — Are you speaking this of yourself, or did others tell you this concerning me?” — (JOHN, 18:34)
Christ's question to Pilate has a more extensive significance. We understand it when applied to our religious experiences.
When we look at the Master as the personality of the Savior, why do we affirm it? Are we acting like phonograph records, in the pure and simple repetition of heard words?

It is necessary to know the reason why we attribute loving and respectful titles to the Lord. It is not enough to retell enchanting lessons of others, but to substantially live the intimate experience in fidelity to the divine program.
When someone refers to a man by name, that man can inquire about the origins of the reference.
Jesus is not a legendary symbol; He is a Living Master.
The superficial concerns of the world arrive, educate the spirit, and pass on, but religious experience remains.
In this chapter, therefore, it is illogical to systematically resort to the patrimonies of others.
It is useful for every apprentice to testify of themselves, to illuminate the heart with the teachings of Christ, to observe His exalted influence in tranquil and stormy days.

Let us recognize, then, a praiseworthy attitude in the effort of the man who is inspired by the exemplification of the faithful disciples; however, let us not forget that it is counterproductive to rest on buildings that do not belong to us, forgetting the service that is properly ours.

messages.title: Jesus and Friends
paragraphs: “Greater love has no one than this, than to lay down one's life for his friends.” — JESUS (John, 15:13)
In the historical localization of Christ, we are impressed by the reality of His immense affection for Humanity.
For men, He did everything that was possible in renunciation and dedication.

His actions were celebrated in assemblies of fellowship and love. The first manifestation of His apostolate took place at the joyful feast of a home. He kept company with tax collectors, He thirsted for the perfect understanding of His disciples. He was a faithful friend to the needy who sought refuge in His immortal virtues. Through the evangelical lessons, one notes His effort to be understood in His infinite capacity to love. The Last Supper represents a complete landscape of integral affectivity. He washes the disciples' feet, He prays for the happiness of each one…
However, at the first clash with destructive forces, the Master experiences supreme abandonment. In vain do His eyes search for the multitude of affectionate ones, beneficiaries, and followers.
The lepers and the blind, healed by His hands, had disappeared.
Judas betrayed Him with a kiss.
Simon, who had enjoyed His domestic fellowship, denied Him three times.
John and James fell asleep in the Garden.
The others preferred to stall in hurried agreements with the unjust accusations. Even after the Resurrection, Thomas demanded signs from Him.

When you are at the “narrow gate,” expanding the conquests of eternal life, you will also go alone. Do not wait for your friends. They will not understand you; nonetheless, do not stop loving them. They are children. And every child fears and demands a lot.

messages.title: Why Do You Sleep?
paragraphs: “And He said to them, 'Why do you sleep? Rise and pray, lest you enter into temptation.'” — (LUKE, 22:46)
In the fundamental teachings of Jesus, it is imperative to avoid accommodating situations to the detriment of the activities of good.

The Gospel of Luke, in this passage, relates that the disciples “slept from sorrow,” while the Master prayed fervently in the Garden. One sees, therefore, that the Lord did not justify even the inactivity arising from shock in the face of great pains.

The apprentice will picture the world as the workplace of the Kingdom, where he will strive, industrious and vigilant, understanding that Christ continues in redeeming service for the total rescue of creatures.

Remembering the prayer in Gethsemane, we are obliged to remember that countless communities with Christian foundations remain sleeping in personal interactions, in petty interests, in fleeting vanities. They speak of Christ, they refer to His imperishable exemplification, as if they were sleepwalkers, unconscious of what they say and what they do, only to awaken at the moment of bodily death, in belated sobs.
Let us listen to the Savior's interrogation and seek edification and work, where there are no vacant places for what is useless and ruinous to conscience.

As for you, who are still in the flesh, do not sleep in spirit, disregarding the interests of the Redeemer. Rise and strive, because it is in the sleep of the soul that the most dangerous temptations are found, through nightmares or fantasies.

messages.title: Watching with Jesus
paragraphs: “Then He came to the disciples and found them sleeping, and said to Peter, 'What? Could you not watch with Me one hour?'” — (MATTHEW, 26:40)
Jesus came to Earth to awaken men to the greater life.

It is interesting to remember, however, that upon feeling the need for someone to accompany Him in the supreme testimony, He did not invite timid followers or beneficiaries of the day before, but rather disciples conscious of their own obligations. However, these very ones slept, intensifying the solitude of the Divine Envoy.

It is essential that we remember the evangelical text to consider that the Master continues in incessant effort and goes on summoning devoted cooperators for the necessary collaboration. Of course, He does not entrust tasks of fundamental importance to inexperienced or ignorant Spirits; but it is imperative to recognize the reduced number of those who do not sleep in the world, while Jesus awaits results of the commission entrusted to them.

Forgetting the mandate of which they are bearers, they become anxious about the execution of their own desires, holding in high regard the rapid days that the physical body offers them. They forget that life is eternity and that earthly existence is symbolically nothing more than “an hour.” In view of this, upon awakening to spiritual reality, the distracted workers weep under the whip of conscience and yearn to rediscover the peace of the Savior, but the words addressed to Peter echo in their ears: “Then, could you not watch with Me even for one hour?”
And indeed, if we still cannot remain with Christ for at least one hour, how can we pretend to divine union for eternity?

messages.title: Peter's Failure
paragraphs: “But Peter followed Him at a distance to the high priest's courtyard. And he went in and sat with the servants to see the end.” — (MATTHEW, 26:58)
Failure, like any success, has its positive causes.
Peter's denial has always been a subject of riveting interest in Christian communities.
Would the moral fall of the Master's generous friend fit into a plan of fatalism? Why would Simon refuse to cooperate with the Lord in such difficult minutes?
Useful, in this regard, is the examination of his lack of vigilance.
The loving fisherman's failure lies right there, in his inattention to the warnings he received.
A large number of modern disciples participate in the same denials, for continuing to be inattentive.

The Gospel informs us that, in that hour of supreme labors, Simon Peter followed the Master “at a distance,” stayed in the “courtyard of the high priest,” and “sat among the servants” of the latter, to “see the end.”

A careful reading of the text clarifies our understanding and we recognize that, even today, many friends of the Gospel continue to fall in their aspirations and hopes, because they follow Christ at a distance, fearful of losing immediate gratifications; when called to important testimony, they linger in the vicinity of the arena of redeeming struggles, among the servants of utilitarian conventions, setting examination binoculars in order to observe how the end of other people's services will be.
All apprentices under these conditions will naturally fail and weep bitterly.

messages.title: Opportunity for Good
paragraphs: “Jesus, however, said to him: Friend, why have you come? Then they came up and laid hands on Jesus and arrested Him.” — (MATTHEW, 26.50)
It is significant to observe the Master's optimism, lavishing opportunities for good right up to the end of His glorious mission of truth and love among men.

Christ was well aware of Judas's deviation; He had lovingly commented on the matter at the final, most intimate gathering with the disciples, and held no doubts regarding the torments that awaited Him. Yet, as he approached, the wayward co-worker kissed Him on the cheek, identifying Him to the executioners, and the Master, with sublime serenity, received the greeting affectionately and asked: “Friend, why have you come?”
His merciful heart offered the troubled disciple an opportunity for good right up to the final moment.

Although He saw Judas in the company of the guards who were going to arrest Him, He gave him the title of friend. He did not withdraw the trust of the first minute, did not curse him, did not give in to useless complaints, and did not commit him to posterity with accusations or less-than-worthy concepts.

In this gesture of unforgettable spiritual beauty, Jesus taught us that it is necessary to offer open doors to good until the very last hour of earthly experiences, even if, at the end of the final opportunity, nothing remains except the path to martyrdom or the cross of supreme testimonies.

messages.title: Field of Blood
paragraphs: “Therefore that field has been called the Field of Blood to this day.” — (MATTHEW, 27.8)
Disoriented, in view of the terrible consequences of his thoughtlessness, Judas sought out the priests and returned the thirty pieces of silver, throwing them at random into the Temple enclosure.

The leaders of Judaism concluded then that the money constituted the price of blood and, seeking to quickly rid themselves of possession of it, acquired a field meant for the burial of strangers, which has been called the Field of Blood ever since.

Deep is the symbolic expression of this memory, and in its light, we must recognize that the majority of men continue Judas's thoughtless action, unconsciously exchanging the Master for unfulfilled hopes, material advantages, and fleeting privileges. When they are able to examine the extent of the deceptions they embraced, they desperately seek out the accomplices of their illusions, trying to return whatever share they received in the criminal movements in which they compromised themselves in human struggle. However, with these bitter fruits, they only manage to acquire the field of blood of painful and harsh expiations, as a sepulcher for the corpses of their delinquent nightmares, estranged from the divine ideal of perfection in Jesus Christ.

Brother in humanity, you who have not yet been able to leave the millennial field of reincarnations, struggling to bury past crimes that do not conform to the Eternal Law, do not trade the Imperishable Christ for a handful of wretched ashes, because otherwise, you will remain confined to the dark region of the bleeding flesh.

messages.title: Magdalene
paragraphs: “Jesus said to her: Mary! — She turned and said to Him: Master!” — (JOHN, 20.16)
Of the most significant facts of the Gospel, Jesus's first appearance upon resurrection is one of those that invites substantial and careful meditation.
For what profound reasons would the Divine Master leave so many figures closer to His life to appear before Magdalene's eyes first?
We are naturally compelled to wonder why He did not appear first to the self-sacrificing and loving heart that had served as His mother, or to the beloved disciples…
However, Jesus's gesture is profoundly symbolic in its divine essence.

Among the figures of the Good News, no one did such violence to themselves to follow the Savior as the unforgettable obsessed woman of Magdala. Not even Paul of Tarsus would do as much later, because the apostle to the gentiles's conscience was passionate about the Law, but not about vices. Magdalene, however, had known the bitter depths of habits difficult to eradicate, had grown soft at the touch of perverse entities, and remained "dead" in the sensations that operate the paralysis of the soul. Yet, a single encounter with Christ was enough for her to abandon everything and follow in His footsteps, faithful to the end in acts of self-denial and in the firm resolve to take up the cross that befell her in the redemptive Calvary of her anguished existence.

It is understandable that many students investigate why the Master did not appear first to Peter or John, to His mother or His friends. However, it is equally reasonable to recognize that, with His unforgettable gesture, Jesus ratified the lesson that His doctrine will be, for all learners and followers, the golden code of lives transformed for the glory of good. And no one, like Mary of Magdala, had transformed hers in the light of the redemptive Gospel.

messages.title: Christian Joy
paragraphs: “But your sorrow will be turned into joy.” — JESUS (John, 16.20)

In the hours preceding the agony of the cross, the disciples could not disguise their pain and disappointment. They were sad. As human beings, they understood no victories other than those of the Earth. But Jesus, with vigorous serenity, exhorted them: “Most assuredly, I say to you that you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice; and you will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will be turned into joy.”

Through the centuries, the Gospel has been seen as a collection of painful news — a self-sacrificing and pure Savior led to the wood meant for the infamous, scattered disciples, countless persecutions, and martyrdoms and tears for all followers…

However, this heavy baggage of sufferings constitutes the foundations of a superior life, full of peace and joy. These pains represent God's help to the sterile soil of human hearts. They arrive as divine fertilizer to the feelings of earthly creatures, so that from despised swamps, lilies of hope may be born.

The restless savors of politics and science on the Planetary Crust prescribe rest and pleasure so that the spirit may weep later, for an indefinite time, cast into the dark recesses of a conscience wounded by criminal attitudes. Christ, however, demonstrating supreme wisdom, taught the natural order for acquiring eternal joys, showing that providing satisfied whims, without warning or measure, to the creatures of the world in their present evolutionary state is placing dangerous substances into infant hands. For this reason, He reserved labors and sacrifices for His beloved companions, so they would not get lost in illusion and would reach real life with a valuable heritage of stable buildings.
This is why Christian joy does not consist of the pleasures of unconsciousness, but of the sublime certainty that all pains are paths to immortal joys.

messages.title: When Saving Ourselves
paragraphs: “Save Yourself and come down from the cross.” — (MARK, 15.30)
This cry of irony from malicious men continues to resonate through the centuries.

The human creature could not understand the Savior's sacrifice. The Earth only knew conquerors who arrived brandishing weapons, covered in blood-stained glories, heroes of destruction and death on their way to altars and stone monuments.

That Messiah, however, departed from the usual standard. To conquer, He gave of Himself; in order to possess, He claimed nothing from men for Himself; with the purpose of enriching life, He surrendered Himself to death.
In view of this, scoffers were not lacking at the extreme moment, challenging the Divine Victor with a mordant expression.
In this testimony, the Master taught us that when we save ourselves, in the field of malice and ignorance, we will hear the cry of general malice under the exact same circumstances.

If we linger attached to the illusion of prominence, if we are workers exclusively interested in our temporary aggrandizement in the carnal Sphere while forgetting the needs of others, there are always many people who consider us privileged and victorious. If we ponder, however, our grave responsibilities in the world, they call us fools, and when they catch us in culminating experiences coated with sacred pain that carries us away to sublime Spheres, they pass by us displaying ironic gestures and, recalling the high principles espoused by our lives, disdainfully exclaim: — “Save Yourself and come down from the cross.”

messages.title: The Hidden Friend
paragraphs: “But their eyes were restrained, so that they did not know Him.” — (LUKE, 24.16)
The disciples, on the road to Emmaus, were bitterly discussing the terrible events of Calvary.
They remained under the storm of anguish. Doubt penetrated their souls, leading them to dejection and denial.
An unknown man, however, overtook them on the road. He had the appearance of a wretched pilgrim. Without identifying himself, he explained the truths of Scripture and exalted the cross and suffering.
Both companions, who had become entangled in the thicket of ungrateful contradictions, experienced a pleasant well-being upon hearing the comforting reasoning.
Only at the end of the journey, feeling strengthened in the warm atmosphere of the inn, did they realize that the unknown man was the Master.

There are still learners on the “symbolic road of Emmaus” every day. They reach the Gospel and balk at the sacrifices necessary for eternal spiritual illumination. They do not understand the divine atmosphere of the cross and seek distant “mental landscapes”… However, an unknown traveler always arrives, walking beside those who hesitate and flee. He takes the form of an uncomprehended wayfarer, an unexpected companion, a generous old man, a timid child. His voice is different from others, his explanations firmer, his appeals sweeter.

Whoever partakes, for a moment, in the banquet of the cross can never forget it. Many times, they will set out into the world, lingering on dark tracks; however, a minute will come when Jesus, in an unexpected way, seeks out these stray travelers and does not forsake them until He beholds them, secure and free, in the inn of trust.

messages.title: The Crown
paragraphs: “And they clothed Him with purple; and they twisted a crown of thorns, put it on His head.” — (MARK, 15.17)

It is almost unbelievable the degree of heedlessness of most Gospel disciples today, anxious for the crown of worldly triumphs. For a long time, the Churches of corrupted Christianity have delighted in grand spectacles through enormous displays of political strength. And it must be recognized that a large number of Christian Spiritist associations, still so recent in the world, tend toward the same inclinations.

Individually, proselytes yearn for well-being, a path without obstacles, honorable consideration from the world, the respect of all, and the faithful recognition—on the part of strangers—of the elevated principles they embraced in life. When this baggage of ease does not grace their edifying service, they feel persecuted, thwarted, and unhappy.
But… what about Christ? Would not the picture of the crown of thorns be enough to soothe our restlessness?

Naturally, the Master carried the Crown of Life with Him; however, He did not want to miss the opportunity to reveal that Earth's crown is still one of thorns, suffering, and incessant toil for those who wish to climb the mountain of Divine Resurrection. At the time the Lord inaugurated the Good News among men, the Romans crowned themselves with roses; but by leaving us this sublime lesson, Jesus gave us to understand that His faithful disciples should expect badges of another nature.

messages.title: Do You Love Me Enough?
paragraphs: “He said to him the third time: Simon, son of Jonah, do you love Me?” — (JOHN, 21.17)

To less-informed learners, it is strange that Jesus asked the apostle three times about the steadfastness of his love. Simon Peter himself, upon hearing the repeated question, grew sad, supposing the Master doubted his innermost feelings.

However, the teaching is deeper. At that moment, Jesus was entrusting him with the ministry of cooperation in redemptive services. The fisherman of Capernaum was going to contribute to the elevation of his wards in the world, was going to apostolize, reaching new values for eternal life.

The Lord's question is therefore very significant in this regard. Jesus does not ask the disciple for information regarding his personal reasoning, nor does He wish to ascertain the collaborator's knowledge concerning Him, nor does He demand a formal commitment. He only wants to know if Peter loves Him, letting it be understood that with love, all other difficulties are resolved. If the disciple possesses a sufficient supply of this divine essence, the hardest task turns into an apostolate of promising blessings.

It is imperative, therefore, to recognize that your intellectual achievements are worth a lot, and your inquiries are commendable, but in truth, you will only be an effective and efficient cooperator of Christ if you have love.

messages.title: Cloaks
paragraphs: “And he, throwing aside his cloak, rose and came to Jesus.” — (MARK, 10.50)
The Gospel of Mark presents an interesting account of the healing of Bartimaeus, the blind man of Jericho.
To receive the blessing of divine approach, he cast away his cloak, running to meet the Master and regaining sight for his dim and sad eyes.
Does a precious symbol not reside in this act?

Human beings display the most diverse cloaks in the world. There are mantles of kings and beggars. There are many friends of crime who show a preference for “saints' cloaks.” Rare are those who do not glue the mask of their own convenience to their faces. It is argued that human struggle remains full of varied demands, that it is essential to attend to the movements of the century; however, if someone sincerely desires to approach Jesus to receive lasting benefits, let them cast away the cloak of the transient world and present themselves to the Lord just as they are, without the ruinous worry of maintaining the pretended intangibility of ephemeral titles, whether those of material fortune or of an exaggerated notion of suffering. Maintaining false appearances before Christ or His messengers complicates the situation of anyone in need. Do not ask the Lord for anything with unreasonable demands or arguments. Strip off your worldly cloak and present yourself to Him, plain and simple.

messages.title: Promising
paragraphs: “Promising them liberty, while they themselves are slaves of corruption.” — (2 PETER, 2.19)
It is essential to distrust all promises of ease in the world.
Jesus, who could have opened the vastest horizons to the creature's astonished eyes, promised him the cross without which he could not distance himself from Earth to place himself in His presence.

Everywhere, there are careless disciples who accept the deception of unconscious adventurers. This is because they have not yet learned the living lesson of the proper work to which they were called to develop their individual activity.

Revolution makers and owners of absurd projects promise wonders. But if they are victims of ambition, servants of lower purposes, and slaves to terrible deceptions, how can they bring about for others the freedom or elevation from which they themselves remain distant?

Do not believe in saviors who do not demonstrate actions confirming their own salvation. You must know that you were created for glorious ascension, but that going down is the only thing that is easy. Climbing requires work, patience, and perseverance—essential conditions for finding love and wisdom.

If someone talks to you about the value of ease, do not believe it; it is possible that the adventurer is going down. But when they show you comforting perspectives through sweat and personal effort, accept the advice with joy. The one who understands the treasure hidden in obstacles and uses it to enrich life is climbing and is worthy of being followed.

messages.title: Interpretation of the Sacred Texts
paragraphs: “Knowing this first, that no prophecy of Scripture is of any private interpretation.” — (2 Peter, 1.20)
Jesus is the Way, the Truth, and the Life. His imperishable light shines upon the earthly millennia, like the Word from the beginning, penetrating the world for almost twenty centuries.

Bloody struggles, wars of extermination, social calamities have not modified a single iota of His words, which become more and more updated with the multiform evolution of the Earth. Tempests of blood and tears have done nothing more than heighten their greatness. Nevertheless, always late in taking advantage of precious opportunities, many times, in the course of renewed existences, we have despised the Way, indifferent to the patrimonies of Truth and Life.

The Lord, however, has never left us forsaken. Each day, He renews the titles of tolerance toward our debts; yet, it is in our own interest to raise the standard of the will, establish disciplines for personal use, and re-educate ourselves in contact with the Divine Master. He is the Generous Friend, but so often we forget His counsel that we are susceptible to reaching obscure zones of indefinite postponement of our inner enlightenment for eternal life.
With the purpose of valuing the opportunity for service, we have organized this humble interpretive work, without any pretension to exegesis.
We have merely concatenated a modest set of loose pages intended for common meditations.

Many friends will perhaps find our attitude strange, isolating verses and conferring upon them a color independent of the evangelical chapter to which they belong. In certain passages, we extract from them only tiny phrases, giving them a special physiognomy and, under certain circumstances, our valueless considerations seem to contradict the provisions of the chapter that inspires them.

We proceed this way, however, considering that, in a necklace of pearls, each one has a specific value and that, in the immense set of teachings of the Good News, each concept of Christ or His direct collaborators adapts to a certain situation of the Spirit along the roads of life. The Master's lesson, furthermore, does not constitute solely an imposition for the duties of worship. The Gospel is not reduced to a breviary for the kneeler. It is an indispensable guide for legislation and administration, for service and obedience. Christ does not establish dividing lines between the temple and the workshop. The whole Earth is His altar of prayer and His field of work at the same time. By praising Him in the churches and disparaging Him in the streets, we have shipwrecked a thousand times, through our own fault. All places, therefore, can be consecrated to the divine service.

Many disciples, in various Christian schools, have surrendered to theological inquiries, transforming the Lord's teachings into a dead relic of stone altars; nevertheless, Christ expects us all to convert His gospel of Love and Wisdom into a companion in prayer, a schoolbook in daily learning, an inspiring source of our most humble actions in common work, and a code of good manners in fraternal exchange.
Although I clarify our modest objectives, I notice beforehand ample perplexity in this or that group of believers.
What to do? We have immense distances to overcome on the Way, to acquire the Truth and the Life in their integral significance.
We understand the respect due to Christ, but, by the Master's own exemplification, we know that the labor of the faithful learner consists of worship and work, of prayer and personal effort.

For the rest, it consoles us to recognize that the Sacred Texts are the Father's gifts to all His children and, for this very reason, we report here to the wise words of Simon Peter: “Knowing this first, that no prophecy of Scripture is of any private interpretation.”
messages.note:
Pedro Leopoldo, September 2, 1948.
Emmanuel's Note — Some of these pages, already published in the Christian Spiritist press, have been revised and simplified by us for greater clarity of interpretation.

messages.title: Before the Lesson
paragraphs: “Consider what I say, and the Lord may give you understanding in all things.” — PAUL (2 Timothy, 2.7)
Before the exposition of the truth, do not shy away from meditation on the lights you receive.
He who glances at the sky without contemplating it does not see the stars; and he who listens to a symphony without opening the acoustics of his soul does not perceive its divine notes.
In vain will you listen to the inspired word of ardent preachers if you do not open your heart so that your feeling may plunge into the blessed clarity of that word.

Countless followers of the Gospel complain of an incapacity to retain the teachings of the Good News, affirming themselves inept in the face of new revelations, and this is because they do not spare greater attention to the lesson heard, lingering for a long time in the province of distraction and levity.
When the room remains dark, we are the ones who unbolt the window so that the sun may visit us.
Let us dedicate some effort to the grace of the lesson and the lesson will respond to us with its graces.
The apostle to the Gentiles is clear in his observation: “Consider what I say, and the Lord will give you understanding in all things.”
To consider means to examine, heed, reflect, and appreciate.
Let us, therefore, be convinced that, by paying attention to the notes of the Code of Eternal Life, the Lord, in retribution for our goodwill, will give us understanding in all things.

messages.title: Way of Doing
paragraphs: “Let this mind be in you which was also in Christ Jesus.” — PAUL (Philippians, 2.5)
Everyone does something in human life, but rare are those who do not return to the flesh to undo whatever they have done.
Even the idle creature, who spent time between uselessness and laziness, is constrained to return to the struggle in order to disintegrate the web of inertia they wove around themselves.
Only he builds, without the need for repair or correction, who is inspired by Jesus' standard to create good.
Doing something in Christ is always doing the best for everyone:
Without expectation of remuneration.
Without demands.
Without showing off.
Without displaying superiority.
Without tributes of recognition.
Without disturbances.
In all the steps of the Divine Master, we see Him in incessant action, in favor of the individual and the collectivity, without entangling Himself.
From the carpentry of Nazareth to the cross of Jerusalem, He goes about doing good, with no other pay than the joy of executing the Father's Will.
He exalts the widow's mite and praises Zacchaeus's fortune with the same serenity.
He talks lovingly with a few little children and multiplies bread for thousands of people without getting flustered.
He raises Lazarus from the tomb and walks to prison with His attention centered on the Heavenly Designs.

Do not forget to act for common happiness, in the infinite line of your days and hours. However, so that illusion does not impose upon you the gall of disenchantment or solitude, help everyone, indiscriminately, preserving, above all, the glory of being useful, “so that there may be in us the same sentiment that lives in Jesus Christ.”

messages.title: On the Great Pilgrimage
paragraphs: “By faith Abraham, when he was called, obeyed by going out to a place which he was to receive as an inheritance; and he went out, not knowing where he was going.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 11.8)
By faith, the learner of the Gospel is called, like Abraham, to the sublime inheritance destined for him. The conscription reaches everyone.
The great Hebrew patriarch went out not knowing where he was going… And we, in turn, must lift our hearts and set out likewise.
We are unaware of the contact stations on the enormous pilgrimage, but we are informed that our goal is Christ Jesus.

How many times will we be forced to step upon the briers of calumny? How many times will we travel the rugged path of misunderstanding? How many showers of tears will reach our spirit? How many clouds will be interposed between our thought and Heaven along vast stretches of the path?
The answer is insoluble. It matters, however, to march always, on the inner path of one's own redemption, without faltering.
Today is intensive sweat; tomorrow is responsibility; later is suffering, and subsequently is solitude… Even so, it is indispensable to proceed without discouragement.
When it is not possible to advance two steps a day, let us move forward at least a few millimeters…
The vanguard opens up into new horizons of understanding and goodness, spiritual enlightenment, and progress in virtue. Let us climb, without rest, up the steep mountain:
Conquering deserts…
Overcoming difficulties…
Piercing through fogs…
Eliminating obstacles…
Abraham obeyed without knowing where he was going, and he found the realization of his happiness.
Let us obey, in our turn, conscious of our destination and convinced that the Lord awaits us, beyond our cross, on the resplendent peaks of eternal resurrection.

messages.title: Each One
paragraphs: “There are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 12.4)
In all places and positions, each one can reveal divine qualities for the edification of all those who live with them.
Learning and teaching constitute tasks of every hour, so that we may collaborate in the aggrandizement of the common treasure of wisdom and love.
He who governs can more frequently express justice and magnanimity.
He who obeys possesses broader resources to demonstrate duty well fulfilled.
The rich man, more than others, can multiply work and divide blessings.
The poor man, more broadly, can amass the fortune of hope and dignity.
The strong man, more easily, can be generous at every moment.
The weak man, without major embarrassments, can show himself humble on any occasion.
The wise man, with dilated assets, can help everyone, renewing general thought for good.
The learner, with multiplied opportunities, can always distribute the wealth of goodwill.
The healthy person can commonly project charity in all directions.
The sick person, more securely, can mold the lessons of patience in the general mood.

Gifts differ, intelligence is characterized by diverse degrees, merit presents multiple values, capacity is the fruit of each one's effort, but the Divine Spirit that sustains creatures is substantially the same.
We are all capable of achieving much within the sphere of work in which we find ourselves.
Observe the position in which you find yourself and attend to the imperatives of the Infinite Good. Place the Divine Will above your desires, and the Divine Will will make good use of you.

messages.title: Can You Go?
paragraphs: “Come to me…” — JESUS (Matthew, 11.28)
The believer listens to the Master's appeal, noting blessed consolations. The lecturer repeats it to communicate vibrations of spiritual comfort to the listeners.

Everyone hears the words of Christ, which insist that the restless mind and tormented heart seek His refreshing lap… However, while it is easy to hear and repeat the Lord's “come to me,” how difficult it is to “go to Him”!

Here, the Master's words pour forth as a vitalizing balm, yet the ties of immediate convenience are too strong; beyond, the divine invitation is marked with promises of renewal for the redemptive journey, yet the prison of discouragement isolates the spirit through resistant bars; over there, the call from on High softens the pains of the disillusioned soul, but liberation from the impediments constituted by people and things, situations and individual interests, apparently unpostponable, is almost impracticable.
Jesus, our Savior, extends His loving and compassionate arms to us.
With Him, life will be enriched with imperishable values, and in the shadow of His celestial teachings we shall follow, through sanctifying work, toward the Universal Fatherland…
All believers register His consoling appeal, but rare are those who prove sufficiently valorous in faith to seek His company.
In short, it is very sweet to hear the “come to me”… However, to speak the truth, can you already go?

messages.title: Accept Correction
paragraphs: “Now no chastening seems to be for the present to be joyful, but grievous; nevertheless, afterward it yields the peaceable fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 12.11)
The earth, under the pressure of the plow, is torn and lacerated; however, shortly after, from its rectified furrows, delicious flowers and fruits sprout.

The tree, under a pruning regime, loses vast reserves of sap, becoming undernourished and disfigured; yet, in rapid weeks, it covers itself with new robustness, qualifying itself for beauty and abundance.
Humble water leaves the comfort of the spring, suffers the imperatives of movement, reaches the great river, and afterwards shares the greatness of the sea.
What occurs in the simple sphere of Nature happens in the complex realm of the soul.
Correction is always harsh, unpleasant, bitter; but in those who accept its light, it always results in blessed fruits of experience, knowledge, comprehension, and justice.
The earth, the tree, and the water endure it through constraint, but Man, the champion of intelligence on the Planet, is free to receive it and acclimate it within his own heart.
The problem of personal happiness, for this very reason, will never be solved by fleeing from the reparatory process.

Celestial correction manifests itself in all corners of the Earth. Rare, however, accept its blessing, because such a gift, most of the time, does not arrive wrapped in ermine, and when brought to the lips, it does not resemble a tasty confection. It appears coated with prickles or mixed with gall, by way of a healing and salutary remedy.
Do not lose, therefore, your precious opportunity for self-improvement.
Pain and obstacle, work and struggle are resources of sublimation that it behooves us to take advantage of.

messages.title: By Their Fruits
paragraphs: “You will know them by their fruits.” — JESUS (Matthew, 7.16)
Not by size.
Not by configuration.
Not by branches.
Not by the grandeur of the canopy.
Not by green shoots.
Not by dried-out tips.
Not by a shiny appearance.
Not by an unpleasant presentation.
Not by the age of the trunk.
Not by the fragility of the leaves.
Not by rustic or delicate bark.
Not by scented or odorless flowers.
Not by an attractive aroma.
Not by repulsive emissions.
No tree will be known or loved by its exterior appearances, but rather by its fruits, its utility, its production.
So too is our spirit in the midst of the journey…

No one truly dedicated to the truth will bear witness to us by what we seem, by the superficiality of our life, by the epidermis of our individual attitudes or expressions perceived or appreciated in passing, but rather by the substance of our collaboration in common progress, by the importance of our contribution to the general good.
— “You will know them by their fruits” — said the Master. — “We will be known by our actions” — we will repeat.

messages.title: Attentive Workers
paragraphs: “But he who looks into the perfect law of liberty and continues in it, and is not a forgetful hearer but a doer of the work, this one will be blessed in what he does.” — (JAMES, 1.25)

The disciple of the Good News, who truly communes with the Master, first of all understands the obligations incumbent upon him and renders sincere worship to the law of liberty, aware that he himself will reap in the world's furrows what he has sown. He knows that the judge will give account of the tribunal, that the administrator will answer for the stewardship, and that the servant will be held responsible for the work entrusted to him. And, respecting every laborer of progress and order, of light and good, in their proper place, he perseveres in taking advantage of the possibilities he received from Divine Providence, attentive to the lessons of truth and applied to the good works with which he feels charged by the Higher Powers of the Earth.

Characterized by such an attitude, Christ's collaborator, whether a statesman or a street sweeper, is integrated with his rightful duty, in the position of acting and serving, as naturally as he communes with oxygen in the act of breathing.

If he leads, he does not wait for others to remind him of the enterprises incumbent upon him. If he obeys, he does not complain of reiterated instructions regarding the attributes assigned to him in the regimental arrangement of works of any nature.
He does not demand that the government of his district send someone to fertilize his garden, nor does he wait for decrees to educate or improve himself.

Strengthening his own freedom to learn, self-improve, and help everyone through complete dedication to the noble duties that the world confers upon him, he becomes blessed in all his actions, which begin to produce substantial advantages in the prosperity and elevation of common life.
Such a follower of the Gospel passes from the category of the Master's learner to that of attentive workers, penetrating in glorious silence into the sublime reserves of the Celestial Apostolate.

messages.title: Let Us Be Content
paragraphs: “And having food and clothing, with these we shall be content.” — PAUL (1 Timothy, 6.8)
The monopolist of wheat will not be able to stock his table with anything other than a few slices of bread to satisfy the demands of his hunger.
The owner of the textile factory will spend no more than a few meters of cloth to make a suit intended for his own use.
No one should feed or dress themselves according to the standards of gluttony and vanity, but rather in conformity with the principles that govern life in its natural foundations.
Why do you await the banquet in order to offer a few crumbs to the passing hungry companion? Why do you demand a treasure of coins in reserve to be useful to the needy?
Charity does not depend on the purse. It is a fountain born in the heart.

The desire to possess something in the savings box for the relief of one's neighbor or oneself in days of storm and insecurity is always respectable, yet subordinating the practice of good to a stuffed safe is deplorable.
Open up the doors of your soul first of all and let your feeling shine for everyone, like a star whose rays illuminate, balm, nourish, and warm…
Rain, pouring down in drops, fertilizes the soil and sustains billions of lives.

Let us share the little we have, and the insignificance of goodwill, sustained by love, will in time convert into common prosperity. A few seeds, cared for with affection over the course of years, can dominate immense plots of land.

Let us be joyful and help all those who share our march because, according to the apostle's wise word, if we possess the grace of counting on bread and clothing for each day, we have the obligation to live and serve in peace and contentment.

messages.title: Certainly
paragraphs: “Surely I come quickly.” — (REVELATION, 22.20)
Almost always, while the human creature breathes in youthful flesh, the attitude that characterizes its heart toward life is that of a child who does not know the value of time.

Days and nights are short for immersion in joys and fantastical adventures. A thousand deceptions of ephemeral illusion obscure their gaze, and the hours vanish in a whirlwind of useless longings. Rare people escape such a loss.

Generally, however, when maturity appears and the soul already possesses a relative degree of education, man readjusts, in a hurry, his concept of the day. The week is reduced to what is incumbent upon him to do.

He understands that the same services, in the position where he finds himself, are repeated in certain months of the year, perfectly recapitulated, just as occurs with the seasons of cold and heat, flowering and fructification in Nature.
He stirs, he worries, he unfolds himself, in the eagerness to multiply his strengths to enrich the minutes or expand them, favoring his own energies.
And, commonly, at the end of the journey, the death of the body surprises him in the corners of expectation or entertainment, without it being given to him to recover the lost years.
Do not plunge yourself, therefore, into the human jungle, unconcerned with your qualification for spiritual light, before the eternal path.
In the penultimate verse of the New Testament, which is the Letter of Divine Love to Humanity, the Lord had His solemn promise recorded by the apostle: — “Surely, I come quickly.”
Avail yourself, therefore, of time and do not make yourself tardy in preparation.

messages.title: Absent
paragraphs: “But Thomas, one of the twelve, was not with them when Jesus came.” — (John, 20.24)
Thomas, discontented, demanding proofs because he had not witnessed Jesus' first visit after death, created a symbol for all apprentices unconcerned with their obligations.
What happened to the absent disciple is what happens to any worker distant from their proper duty.
Spiritual edification, with its blessings of light, is likewise an educational course.

The student enrolled in school, without attendance at the lessons, merely abuses the educational establishment that welcomed them, since the simple entry card does not solve the problem of achievement. Without mastering the alphabet, they will not reach syllabication. Without the possession of words, they will never reach the science of the phrase.
An identical process prevails in the refinement of the Spirit.

Far from the small duties toward the closest brothers, how can man qualify himself for the reception of divine grace? If he avoids contact with the humble obligations of each day, how can he dilate his feelings to adjust himself to eternal glories?
Thomas was not with his friends when the Master came. Afterward, he formulated complaints, creating the type of the suspicious and demanding apprentice.

In the spiritual works of perfection, the issue is analogous. The companion enrolls in the school of superior life, however, instead of dedicating himself to the service of daily lessons, he reveals himself merely as a candidate for immediate advantages.
In general, he is never found beside the other servants when Jesus comes; soon after, he complains and despairs.
Logic, however, never abandons the straight path.
Whoever desires the divine blessing, let them work to deserve it. The apprentice absent from class cannot claim benefits arising from the lesson.

messages.title: The Curtain of the “Self”
paragraphs: “For all seek their own, not the things which are of Christ Jesus.” — PAUL (Philippians, 2.21)
In truth, we study with Christ the divine science of connection with the Father, but we still find ourselves very distant from genuine communion with divine interests.
Behind the curtain of the “self,” we maintain lamentable blindness before life.

Let us impartially examine the attitudes that are peculiar to us in the very services of goodness, of which we are starting cooperators, and we will observe that, even there, in matters of virtue, our percentage of individual caprice is invariably enormous.
The ancient legend of Narcissus remains alive, in our smallest gestures, in greater or lesser proportion. In everything and everywhere, we fall in love with our own image.

In our most cherished beings, we habitually love ourselves, because if they demonstrate points of view different from ours, even when superior to the principles we espouse, we instinctively weaken the affection we consecrated to them.

In the works of goodness to which we devote ourselves, we esteem, above all, the methods and processes that emanate from our own way of being and understanding, because if the service evolves or perfects itself, reflecting the thought of other personalities above ours, we operate, almost without realizing it, the diminution of our interest in the initiated works.
We accept the collaboration of others, but we feel difficulty in offering the contest that is incumbent upon us.

If we find ourselves in a superior position, we joyfully donate a fortune to the needy brother who follows us in a subordinate condition, in order to contemplate with voluptuousness our noble qualities in the long-range recognition to which he feels constrained, but we rarely grant a willing smile to the wealthier or stronger companion, placed by Divine Designs before us.

In all steps of the human struggle, we find virtue surrounded by vices and dignifying knowledge almost suffocated by the thorns of ignorance, because, unfortunately, each of us, generally speaking, lives in search of “oneself.”

However, thanks to God's Goodness, suffering and death surprise us, in the experience of the body and beyond it, snatching us to the vast continents of meditation and humility, where we will learn, little by little, to seek what belongs to Jesus Christ, in favor of our true happiness, within the glory of living.

messages.title: Let Us Always Rejoice
paragraphs: “Rejoice always.” — PAUL (1 Thessalonians, 5.16)
The evangelical text does not exhort us to joy only on the days when we feel personally happy. It asserts with simplicity — “rejoice always.”
There is nothing in the world that cannot be transformed into a respectable motive for work, joy, and sanctification. And Nature itself, every day, displays expressive teachings in this regard.

After the tempest that uproots, mutilates trees, destroys nests, and muddies roads, the sowing reappears, the trunk puts forth new sprouts, the birds remake their suspended homes, and the path is crowned with sun.
Only man, hero of intelligence, keeps with him the grimace of pessimism, for an indefinite time, as if he were an angry and disillusioned genius, interested in destroying what does not belong to him.
The continued absence of hopes and joy in the soul signifies deficient evolution.
Everywhere, there are invitations to edification and improvement, challenging us to action in common aggrandizement.
No one is so unhappy that they cannot produce some thoughts of kindness, nor so poor that they cannot distribute some smiles and good words with their companions in the daily struggle.
Sadness at every moment is rust in the gears of the soul.
Incessant lamentation is idleness or destructive resistance.
It is necessary to awaken the heart and worthily attend to the part that is incumbent upon us in the evolutionary drama of life, without hatred, without complaint, without discouragement.
Experience is what it is. Our companions are what they are.
Each of us receives the share of struggle indispensable to the learning we must accomplish.
No one is disinherited of opportunities in favor of their improvement.
The great issue is to obey God, loving Him, and to serve one's neighbor willingly.

Whoever has solved such a problem within themselves knows that all creatures and situations on the path are living messages in which we can gather the blessings of love and wisdom, if we accept the lesson that the Lord offers us. In this sense, therefore, let us not forget that Paul, the fearless combatant of the Gospel, under storms of worries, found resource within himself to say to the brothers in struggle: — “Rejoice always.”

messages.title: Wait and Achieve
paragraphs: “And so, having patiently waited, he obtained the promise.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 6.15)
The hope of attaining divine peace, with unalterable happiness, vibrates in all creatures. The yearning of the patriarchs of Antiquity is analogous to that of modern men.
The home crowned with blessings.
Duty well fulfilled.
The edified conscience.
The superior ideal conveniently attended to.
Victorious work.
The happy harvest.
The soul's aspirations are always the same everywhere. However, waiting means persisting without fatigue, and achieving expresses triumphing definitively.
Between the objective and the goal, constant and prompt effort becomes imperative.
Hope is not inaction. And patience translates peaceful obstinacy in the work we propose to accomplish.
If you intend to materialize your purposes with Christ, keep the formula of patience as the only open door to victory.
Is there suffering in your tortured dreams? Incomprehension of many around your desires? Do ingratitude and pain visit your Spirit?
Do not weep wasting the minutes, nor curse the difficulty. Await the surprises of time, acting without precipitation.
If every night is new shadow, every day is new light.
Remember that not all waters are at the same level and not all trees are equal in size, growth, or species.
Recall the words of the apostle to the Gentiles. Waiting with patience, we will achieve the promise.
Do not forget that sure success does not belong to the one who storms it, but rather to the one who knows how to act, persevere, and wait for it.

messages.title: Before the Multitude
paragraphs: “And seeing the multitudes, He went up on a mountain…” — (Matthew, 5.1)
The procedure of cultured men toward the people will experience increasing elevation as the Gospel spreads in hearts.
Unfortunately, until now, the multitude has rarely encountered, on the part of great human personalities, the treatment it deserves.
Many ascend the mountain of authority and fortune, intelligence and power, but simply to humiliate it or forget it afterward.
Numerous priests enrich themselves with knowledge and seek to subjugate it to their liking.
Astute politicians exploit its passions for their own benefit.
Tyrants disguised as leaders poison its soul and hurl it to the precipice of destruction, after the manner of executioners of a flock who separate the livestock for the slaughterhouse.
Judges less prepared for the dignity of the functions they exercise confuse its reasoning.
Less scrupulous administrators regiment its numerical expressions for the creation of effects contrary to progress.
In all times, we see the work of legitimate missionaries of goodness prejudiced by ignorance that establishes disturbances and scarecrows for the popular mass.
However, for the community of Gospel apprentices, in any climate of faith, the standard of Jesus shines sovereign. Seeing the multitude, the Master goes up a mountain and begins to teach…
It is imperative to pledge our energies in the service of education. Let us help the people to think, grow, and refine themselves.
Helping everyone so that everyone may benefit and rise, as much as we desire improvement and prosperity for ourselves, constitutes for us real and indisputable happiness.
To the east and west, to the north and south of our individuality, thousands of creatures move about in a position inferior to ours.
Let us extend our arms, lengthen our heart, and radiate understanding, fraternity, and sympathy, helping them unconditionally.
When the Christian pronounces the sacred words “Our Father,” they are recognizing not only the Paternity of God, but also accepting all Humanity as their family.

messages.title: You Are the Light
paragraphs: “You are the light of the world.” — JESUS (Matthew, 5.14)
When Christ designated His disciples as the light of the world, He assigned them tremendous responsibility on Earth.
The mission of light is to clear paths, sweep away shadows, and save lives—a mission that invariably develops at the expense of the fuel that serves as its base.
The flame of the lamp consumes the oil of the wick. Electric illumination consumes the power of the plant.
And clarity, whether from the Sun or the candelabra, is always a message of security and discernment, comfort and joy, tranquilizing those around whom it shines.

If we comprehend, therefore, the lesson of Christ, interested in accompanying Him, our willingness to donate our strengths in the incessant activity of goodness is indispensable, so that the Good News may shine on the path of redemption for all.
A Christian without a spirit of sacrifice is a dead lamp in the sanctuary of the Gospel.
Let us seek the Lord, offering others the best of ourselves. Let us follow Him, helping indiscriminately.
Let us not dwell on conflicts or fruitless inquiries. “You are the light of the world” — the Master exhorted us —, and light does not argue, but rather clarifies and assists, helps and illuminates.

messages.title: Let Us Serve Goodness
paragraphs: “And the light shines in the darkness…” — (John, 1.5)
Do not grieve because you are seemingly alone in the service of goodness.
Jesus was alone before gathering companions for apostolic service. Alone, facing the vast world, like a laborer without working instruments before the immense jungle…
Nor did Christianity fail to emerge as a living temple of love, still building today on Earth for human happiness.
Jesus, however, despite knowing the strength of the truth He carried with Him, did not take advantage of His superiority to humiliate or wound.
Above all concerns, He invariably sought goodness through all situations and in all creatures.
He wasted no time on uncalled-for reproaches. He did not entrust Himself to useless polemics.
He instituted the saving reign of which He had made Himself a messenger, serving and loving, always helping and grounding each teaching with His own exemplification.
Let us continue, therefore, in our regenerative march forward, even when we feel alone.
Let us serve goodness above all; however, let us avoid discussions and agitations in which evil can expand.

Shadow flees the splendor of light. Let us not forget that thousands of kilometers of darkness in the bosom of the night cannot extinguish a few millimeters of the bright flame of a candle, yet a slight puff of wind is enough to extinguish it.

messages.title: Let Us Renew Ourselves Day by Day
paragraphs: “… Be transformed by the renewing of your mind, that you may prove what is that good and acceptable and perfect will of God.” — PAUL (Romans, 12.2)

It is no use transforming our personality outwardly in appearance. More titles, more financial resources, more possibilities of comfort, and greater social standing can be a simple aggravation of responsibility.
Let us renew ourselves inwardly.
It is necessary to advance in superior knowledge, even if the march costs us sweat and tears.
Accepting the problems of the world and overcoming them by the force of our work and serenity is the just formula for acquiring discernment.
Pain and sacrifice, affliction and bitterness are processes of sublimation that the Greater World offers us, so that our spiritual vision may be enhanced.
Material facilities usually stagnate our minds when we do not know how to overcome the fascinating dangers of earthly advantages.
Let us renew our soul, day by day, studying the lessons of the vanguard of progress and living our existence under the inspiration of incessant service.

Let us apply ourselves to the construction of a balanced life wherever we may be, but let us not forget that only through the execution of our duties, in the concretization of goodness, will we attain the understanding of life, and with it, the knowledge of the “perfect will of God” concerning us.

messages.title: A Little Leaven
paragraphs: “Do you not know that a little leaven leavens the whole lump?” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 5.6)
No one lives alone. Our soul is always a nucleus of influence for others.
Our actions have positive language. Our words act at a distance.
We are magnetically associated with one another. Actions and reactions characterize our march. It is necessary to know, therefore, what kind of forces we project onto those around us.
Our conduct is an open book.
How many of our insignificant gestures reach our neighbor, generating unexpected resolutions!
How many seemingly expressive phrases cast from our mouths establish great events!
Each day, we emit suggestions for good or for evil.
Leaders drag the led. Servants inspire administrators.
What path is our attitude indicating?
A little leaven leavens the whole lump. We do not have resources to analyze the extent of our influence, but we can examine its essential quality.
Beware, then, of the invisible nourishment you provide to the lives surrounding you.
Our destiny unfolds in currents of ebb and flow. The forces that exteriorize from our activity today will return to the center of our activity tomorrow.

messages.title: Following Christ's Example
paragraphs: “He well knew what was in man.” — (John, 2.25)
Yes, Jesus did not ignore what existed within man, but He never allowed Himself to be negatively impressed.
He knew that usury dwelt with Zacchaeus, yet He brought him from miserliness to benevolence.
He was not unaware that Magdalene was possessed by the genii of evil; nevertheless, He renewed her for pure love.
He recognized the intellectual vanity of Nicodemus, but gave him new conceptions of the greatness and excelsitude of life.
He identified the weakness of Simon Peter, yet little by little He installed in the disciple's heart the spiritual fortitude that would make him the pillar of nascent Christianity.
He sees the doubts of Thomas, without forsaking him.
He knows the shadow that dwells in Judas, without denying him the cultivation of affection.
Jesus was concerned, above all, with providing each soul with a broader vision of life and with endowing each Spirit with efficient resources for renewal toward the good.
Do not condemn your neighbor, therefore, because you observe inferiority and imperfection in them. Following Christ's example, help as much as you can.

The Divine Friend knows what exists within us... He is not unaware of our heavy and dark baggage from the past, amidst the difficulties of our present filled with hesitations and errors, but even so, He never ceases to lovingly extend His hands to us.

messages.title: Let Us Glorify
paragraphs: “Now to our God and Father be glory forever and ever.” — PAUL (Philippians, 4.20)
When the vessel was withdrawn from the pottery, it said without words:
— Blessed be the fire that provided me with solidity.
When the plow departed from the forge, it affirmed in silence:
— Blessed be the mallet that gave me form.
When the refined wood came to shine in the palace, it exclaimed, without a voice:
— Blessed be the blade that cruelly cut me, preparing my beauty.
When the silk shone, beautiful, in the temple, it asserted inwardly:
— Blessed be the ugly caterpillar that gave me life.
When the flower opened, velvety and sublime, it thanked in haste:
— Blessed be the dark earth that filled me with perfume.
When the sick person recovered health, they shouted, happy:
— Blessed be the pain that brought me the lesson of equilibrium.
Everything is beautiful, everything is great; everything is holy in the house of God.
Let us give thanks for the storm that renews, the struggle that perfects, the suffering that enlightens.
The dawn is a marvel of heaven that comes after the night on Earth.
May our Father be glorified forever in all our difficulties and shadows.

messages.title: Let Us Watch and Pray
paragraphs: “Watch and pray, lest you enter into temptation.” — JESUS (Matthew, 26.41)
The most terrible temptations stem from the dark depths of our own individuality, just as the most intense mud capable of staining a lake proceeds from its very bosom.
ഞങ്ങൾare reborn on Earth with the unbalanced forces of our past for the tasks of readjustment.
At the roots of our tendencies, we find the most vivid suggestions of inferiority.
In our intimate relations with our relatives, we are surprised by the strongest motives of discord and struggle.
Within ourselves we can exercise good cheer and patience, faith and humility.
In contact with our closest affections, we have copious material for learning to fix in our lives the values of goodwill and forgiveness, of pure fraternity and incessant good.

Do not propose, therefore, to cross the world without temptations. They are born with you, arise from yourself, and feed upon you when you do not combat them with dedication, like the farmer always willing to cooperate with the earth from which he needs to extract good seeds.

Walking from the cradle to the tomb under the hammer blows of temptation is natural. Facing obstacles, suffering trials, tolerating unprovoked antipathies, and crossing storms of tears are logical vicissitudes of human experience.

Nevertheless, let us remember the Master's teaching, watching and praying, so as not to succumb to temptations, since it is better to weep under the goads of resistance than to smile under the narcotics of falling.

messages.title: Let Us Strengthen Ourselves
paragraphs: “Be strengthened in the Lord.” — PAUL (Ephesians, 6.10)
There are many people who consider themselves strong...
In financial resources, which appear and flee.
In the possession of lands, which are transferred from owner to owner.
In physical beauty, which shines and passes.
In important relatives, who transform.
In the culture of intelligence, which often errs.
In popularity, which leads to disillusionment.
In political power, which time undoes.
In the oasis of exclusivist happiness, which the storm destroys.

Yes, there are many people who suppose they win today only to end up defeated tomorrow. However, only consciousness built upon faith, through duties well fulfilled in the face of Eternal Laws, manages to sustain itself, invulnerable, over self-mastery.
Only those who know how to sacrifice themselves for love find incorruptible security.
Let us strengthen ourselves, therefore, in the Lord and move forward with an uplifted soul in the execution of the task entrusted to us by the Divine Master.

messages.title: What Shall I Do?
paragraphs: “What shall I do?” — PAUL (Acts, 22.10)
Thousands of companions approach the Gospel for the inveterate cult of comfort.
— How shall I rule? — some ask.
— How shall I rest? — others inquire.
And pleas multiply, strange, reprehensible, incomprehensible...

There are those who ask for cheap comfort in the flesh, those who demand undue affections, those who sigh for unconfessable business, and those who demand resources to hinder the service of peace and good.
The apostle Paul's question, at the very moment he finds himself graced by the Divine Presence, is the standard for all apprentices and followers of the Good News.

The great worker of Revelation does not ask for a transfer from Earth to Heaven, nor does he descend into suggestions of favoritism for his personal circle. He does not beg for exemption from responsibility, nor does he flee from the duty of struggle. — What shall I do? — he said to Jesus, understanding the imperative of the effort required of him.
And the Master determines that the companion rise up for the sowing of light and love through self-sacrifice.
If you have been called to faith, do not resort to the Divine Counselor beseeching privileges and benefits that justify your permanence in spiritual stagnation.
