Let us seek with the Lord the service that His Infinite Goodness reserves for us, and we shall walk victoriously toward sublime renewal.

messages.title: Let Us Seek the Best
paragraphs: “Why do you look at the speck in your brother’s eye?” — JESUS (Matthew, 7.3)

The Master's question, even now, is clear and opportune. Often, the man who carries a speck in one of his eyes also carries bleeding feet. After a laborious journey in virtue, he reveals hands calloused from work and has a heart wounded by a thousand blows of ignorance and inexperience.
It is imperative to accustom our vision to the search for the best, so that we are not deceived by the malice inherent to us.
Commonly, out of the habit of seeking trifles, we lose the opportunity for great achievements.

Valuable and respectable collaborators are relegated to the sidelines by our thoughtlessness, in many circumstances simply because they bear slight defects or insignificant shadows of the past that ongoing service could heal or dissipate.
Knots in wood do not impede the artisan's work, and certain stony stretches of the field cannot frustrate the farmer's effort in producing noble seed.
Let us make use of the brother of goodwill in the planting of the good, forgetting the trivialities that surround his life.

What would become of us if Jesus did not excuse our daily errors and failings? And if we hope to achieve our own improvement, counting on the Lord's benevolence, why deny our neighbor trust in the future?

Let us consecrate ourselves to the task that the Lord has reserved for us in the building of goodness and light, and let us be convinced that, by acting thus, the speck that bothers our neighbor's eye, just as the beam that obscures our own gaze, will dissolve spontaneously, restoring happiness and balance to us through incessant renewal.

messages.title: Put Your Sword Back
paragraphs: “Put your sword back…” — JESUS (John, 18.11)
War has always been the terror of nations.

A hurricane of unconsciousness, it opens the door to all the monsters of iniquity through which it manifests. What civilization builds at the price of laborious centuries of sweat, it destroys with the fury of a few days.

Before it arise slaughter and devastation, which compel the people to cruelty and barbarism, through which appear bitter days of suffering and regeneration for the collectives that accepted its madness.
The same occurs within us when we wage war against our fellows...

Sustaining contention with our neighbor, a destructive tempest of feelings unhinges our heart. Superior ideals and sublime aspirations long cherished by our Spirit, constructions of the present for the future, and plantations of light and love in the terrain of our souls suffer collapse and disintegration, because imbalance and violence make us tremble and fall into the vibrations of absolute selfishness that we had relegated to the rear guard of evolution.
After this, we must often cross afflictive existences of expiation to correct the breaches that debase the boat of our destiny in brief moments of insanity...
In our Christian learning, let us remember the Lord's word:
— "Put your sword back..."
Nurturing war with others, we lose ourselves in outer darkness, forgetting the good fight we are called to maintain within ourselves.
Let us make peace with those around us, fighting against the shadows that still disturb our existence, so that the reign of light may be established within us.
With spear in hand, we will never conquer the good we desire. The Master's cross has the shape of a sword with the blade pointing downward.
Let us remember, therefore, that by sacrificing himself upon a symbolic sword, duly sheathed, Jesus conferred upon man the blessing of peace, with happiness and renewal.

messages.title: Let Us Keep Loyalty
paragraphs: “Moreover it is required in stewards that one be found faithful.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 4.2)
Let us live each day doing the best within our reach.
If you administer, be just in the distribution of work.
If you legislate, be faithful to the good of all.
If you spread the gifts of faith, do not neglect the souls around you.
If you teach, be clear in the lesson.
If you devote yourself to art, do not corrupt the divine inspiration.
If you heal, do not despise the sick person.
If you build, attend to safety.
If you plow the soil, do it with joy.
If you cooperate in public cleanliness, embrace hygiene as your priesthood.
If you have built a home, sublimate it for the blessings of love and light, even if it costs you affliction and sacrifice.
Do not be troubled by unexpected changes, nor impressed by the apparent victory of those who care for multiple interests, except those that concern them.
Remember the Vigilant Gaze of Divine Providence that observes our every step.

Remember that you live where you find yourself by the initiative of the Greater Power that supervises our destinies, and let us keep loyalty to the obligations that surround us. And, acting incessantly in the extension of good in the field of struggle that life entrusts to us, let us wait for new decisions of the Law regarding us, because the Law itself will elevate us in plane and sublimate our activities at the opportune moment.

messages.title: Go and Teach
paragraphs: “Go therefore and make disciples...” — JESUS (Matthew, 28.19)
Studying the Lord's recommendation to the disciples — go and teach —, it is fair not to forget that Jesus came and taught.
He came from the Heavenly Heights and taught the path of elevation to those who lay mired in earthly shadow.
Christ could have sent the lesson through faithful emissaries... He could have spoken brilliantly, clarifying how to do it...
He preferred, however, to teach securely and profitably, coming to men and living with them to show them how to live toward perfection.

To this end, above all, He made Himself humble and simple in the Manger, honored work and study in the home, and, in full public activity, was the providential brother of all, supporting each one according to their needs.
With indisputable accuracy, Jesus is called the Divine Master.
Not because He possessed a golden chair of academia...
Not because He was the owner of the best library in the world...
Not because He simply exalted correct and irreproachable speech...
Not because He ascended to the throne of cultural superiority, dictating obligations to listeners...

But rather because He raised His own heart to fraternal love and, while teaching, became a benefactor to all who gathered His sublime teachings. He spoke to us of the Eternal Father and revealed to us, through His sacrifice, the righteous way to seek Him.
If you propose, therefore, to cooperate with the Gospel, remember that it is not enough to speak, advise, and inform.
“Go and teach,” in Christ's word, means “go and exemplify so that others may learn how it must be done.”

messages.title: We possess what we give
paragraphs: “It is more blessed to give than to receive.” — PAUL (Acts, 20.35)
When someone refers to the evangelical passage that considers the act of giving a higher blessedness than the act of receiving, almost all apprentices of the Good News recall the word “money”.

Without a doubt, when referring to material goods, there is always more joy in helping than in being helped; nevertheless, it is imperative not to forget the spiritual goods which, radiated from ourselves, increase the level and intensity of joy around our steps.
He who gives reaps the happiness of seeing the multiplication of what he gave.
Offer kindness and you will encourage the planting of fraternity.
Extend the blessing of forgiveness and you will strengthen justice.
Administer goodness and you will have the growth of trust.
Give your good example and you will guarantee nobility of character.
The resources of Creation are distributed by the Creator with the Creatures, so that in permanent donation they multiply to Infinity.
You will be helped by Heaven, according to how you are helping on Earth.
We possess what we give.
Do not forget, therefore, that you are a steward of the life in which you find yourself.

Yield to your neighbor something more than the money you may have available. Give also your affectionate interest, your health, your joy, and your time, and, in truth, you will enter into the possession of the sublime gifts of love, balance, happiness, and peace, today and tomorrow, in this world and in eternal life.

messages.title: In our tasks
paragraphs: “… Mind not high things, but condescend to men of low estate.” — PAUL (Romans, 12:16)
“Mind not high things, but condescend to men of low estate” — recommends the apostle wisely.
Many learners of the Gospel aspire to great achievements from one day to the next...
The crown of holiness...
The power of healing...
The glory of superior knowledge...
Far-reaching edifices...
However, aspiring by itself is not enough for realization. Everything in the circles of Nature obeys the spirit of sequence.
The tree victorious at harvest time went through the condition of the fragile shrub.
The waterfall that moves powerful turbines is a collection of threads of water at its source.
Imposing is the project for building a noble house; nevertheless, the service of the pickaxe and the shovel, of brick and stone, is indispensable so that art and comfort may be expressed.
Let us embrace humble duties with devotion to our ideal of progress and triumph. No matter how arduous and simple our obligation may be, let us attend to it with love.

Paul's word is wise and just, because by firmly climbing the lower slopes of the mountain, we easily conquer its summit, and by willingly accepting tiny tasks, great tasks will spontaneously come to meet us.

messages.title: Go to now
paragraphs: “Go to now, ye that say… To-morrow…” — (JAMES, 4:13)
Now is the decisive moment to do good. Tomorrow, probably...
The friend will have disappeared.
The difficulty will be greater.
The illness will have become more serious.
The wound will possibly show itself extended further.
The problem may appear more complicated.
The opportunity to help will not repeat itself.
The good seed planted now is a guarantee of valuable production in the future.
The useful word, spoken without delay, will always be a light in the setting where you live.
If you wish to be excused for some fault, approach those you have wounded now and reveal your purpose of readjustment.
If you propose to assist a companion, help them without delay so that the blessing of your fraternal contribution may respond to your brother's needs with desirable efficiency.
Do not sleep on the possibility of doing your best.
Do not remain in inoperative expectation when you can contribute in favor of joy and peace.
The delayed gift tastes like gall.
“Go to now” — the Gospel tells us, in the apostolic word. Postponing the good we can accomplish is wasting time and stealing from the Lord.

messages.title: Hindrances
paragraphs: “Let us lay aside every weight… and let us run with patience the race that is set before us.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 12:1)
Wherever you journey on Earth, carrying the vessel of your faith to pour out in good works, you will always find hindrances in abundance, making your action difficult.
Today, it is failure in the initial attempts at progress.
Tomorrow, it is the companion who fails.
Afterwards, it is uncharitable persecution of your ideal.
You will grieve with the gall of many lips that deserve your appreciation.
You will suffer, from time to time, the incomprehension of others.
Periodically you will find a thousand obstacles in the vanguard, inducing you to inertia or negation.
The race that is set before us, however, must unfold along the route of incessant good...
What to do with the people and circumstances that compel us to delay and immobility?
The apostle to the Gentiles responds categorically: “Let us lay aside every weight.”

Setting difficulty aside, however, is not scorning the opinions of others when they are respectable, nor fleeing from ordinary struggle. It is respecting each individuality in its proper position, it is sharing the noblest angle of the good fight with our best collaboration for general improvement. And inwardly, in the intimacy of the heart, continuing with Jesus, today, tomorrow and always, acting and serving, learning and loving, until the divine light shines in our consciousness as much as we unconsciously already find ourselves within it.

messages.title: So is he
paragraphs: “So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.” — JESUS (Luke, 12:21)
You will keep countless titles of ownership over earthly utilities, but if you are not master of your own soul, all your patrimony will be nothing more than a simple introduction to madness.
You will multiply around your feet wonderful gardens of youthful joy; however, if you do not acquire superior knowledge for tomorrow's itinerary, your youth will be the noisy prelude to true old age.

You will cover your chest with honorary medals, increasing the series of admirers who applaud you, but if the light of a righteous conscience does not bathe your heart, you will resemble a chest of darkness, adorned on the outside and empty on the inside.

You will hoard riches and comforts for your earthly home, giving it a dominant profile and clothing it with artistic splendor; yet, if you do not possess within the intimacy of the home the harmony that sustains the happiness of living, your dwelling will be merely an adorned mausoleum.

You will pile up coins of gold and silver, in the shadow of which you will speak with authority and influence to the ears of your neighbor, nevertheless, if your assets do not expand in the form of relief and work, stimulus and education in favor of your fellow men, you will be merely a careless traveler heading toward dreadful disillusions.

You will grow horizontally, you will conquer power and fame, your physical presence on Earth will be revered, but if you do not bring with you the values of good, you will stand alongside the unhappy, on an unforeseen march toward the ruins of disenchantment.
So will be “everyone who lays up treasures for himself, without being rich toward God”.

messages.title: Let us seek the light
paragraphs: “All scripture given by inspiration of God is profitable… for instruction in righteousness.” — PAUL (II Timothy, 3:16)
Seek an idea for its own inherent value.

When common currency comes into your hands, you do not ask where it came from. You do not know if it comes from the house of a righteous or an unjust man, or if it was previously at the service of a saint or an evildoer.
Knowing its importance, you know how to keep it or use it with a practical sense, because you have learned to perceive in it the seal of authority that guides your human struggle.

Money is a representation of the purchasing power of the temporal government to which you submit, and therefore you do not argue about its origin, respecting it and using it to the extent of the possibilities with which it presents itself.
On the same basis, renewing and edificatory ideas arise.
Why demand that they be subscribed, in their exposition, by our relatives or particular friends, in order for them to produce the salutary effect we expect of them in us and around us?

Every comforting and instructive page is a gift from on High. It does not matter whether the thoughts embodied in it came through the Spirit of our earthly parents or our children in the flesh, our loved ones or our companions. The essential thing is the benefit it can offer us.

The money with which you buy today's bread may have passed yesterday through the hands of your greatest adversary, but it remains a blessing to guarantee your sustenance, due to the value with which it is endowed.

Thus also, the message from any origin that induces us to good or truth is always valuable and holy in its foundations, because by using it in our soul and our experience, we can acquire the eternal talents of wisdom and love, as it is a saving resource born of the infinite mercy of our Heavenly Father.
Let us seek the light wherever it may be found, and darkness will not overtake us.

messages.title: Let us understand one another
paragraphs: “And above all things have fervent charity among yourselves.” — PETER (1 Peter, 4:8)
There are no greater or lesser tasks. All are important in significance.

One man will be respected for the laws he institutes, another will be admired for the deeds he performs. But the legislator and the hero would not attain the prominence in which they stand without the humble labor of the farmer who sows the field and without the quiet effort of the street sweeper who contributes to the hygiene of the public road.
Do not isolate yourself, therefore, in the pride with which you presume yourself superior to others.
The community is an assembly of service, generating the wealth of experience. And we cannot forget that the harmony of this living machine depends on us.

When we can distribute the encouragement of our understanding and collaboration with everyone, respecting the importance of our own work and the excellence of the service of others, the face of the Earth will be renewed toward perfect happiness. For this, however, it is necessary that we devote ourselves to mutual assistance with ardent fraternal love...
Let us love our position in the social order, no matter how simple or rudimentary, lending our best forces to the good, progress, and education.
We will be understood to the extent of our understanding.
Let us look at our neighbor in the effort they expend, and the neighbor will identify us in the tasks to which we dedicate ourselves.
Let us extend our arms to the beings who surround us, and they will respond to us with the best they possess.
The most precious capital in life is goodwill. Let us put it into motion, and our existence will be enriched with blessings and joys, today and always, wherever we may be.

messages.title: Living in peace
paragraphs: “… Live in peace…” — PAUL (2 Corinthians, 13:11)
Keep yourself in peace. It is likely that others will wage war against you for no reason, attacking your way of living; however, you can advance along your route without warring against anyone.
For this, however — so that tranquility may bathe your thought —, it is necessary that compassion and kindness follow your every step.
Take upon yourself the commitment to avoid exasperation. Alongside serenity, you will be able to analyze every event and every person in the place and position that pertain to them.

Look affectionately upon those who seek you on the path... Everyone who appears, afflicted or desperate, wrathful or harsh, bears wounds or illusions. Prisoners of vanity or ignorance, they have not known how to tolerate the light of truth and cry out irritably... Anoint yourself with pity and penetrate the recesses of their being, and you will identify in all of them spiritual children who feel outraged or bruised.
Some accuse, others weep. Help them while you can. By pacifying their souls, you will harmonize your own life even further.
Let us learn to understand each mind in its problem.
Remember that Nature, ever divine in its foundations, respects the law of equilibrium and preserves it unceasingly.
Even when men show themselves deranged in open conflicts, the Earth remains ever firm and the Sun shines ever bright.
Living just anyhow belongs to everyone, but living at peace with oneself is the service of a few.

messages.title: Do not tire
paragraphs: “And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not.” — PAUL (Galatians, 6:9)

When the chisel began to strike the rough block of marble, the stone, in despair, cried out against its own destiny, but later, upon finding itself admired as one of the most beautiful artistic conceptions in the world, it praised the chisel that had carved it.

The caterpillar dragged itself along with extreme difficulty, and seeing flowers touched with beauty and perfume, it revolted against its misshapen body; yet one day, the viscous mass in which it had suffered turned into the wings of a graceful and agile butterfly, and then it praised the ugly body with which Nature had prepared its happy flight.

The red-hot iron placed on the anvil was startled and suffered, unreconciled; however, when it saw itself performing important functions in the machines of progress, it smiled gratefully at the fire that had purified and aggrandized it.

The seed cast into the dark grave wept, tormented, and asked why it was thus entrusted to extreme abandonment; nevertheless, upon seeing itself transformed into a shrub, it reached toward the Sun and became a respected and generous tree, blessing the earth that had isolated it in its bosom.
Do not tire of doing good.
He who does not understand your goodwill today will praise your devotion and effort tomorrow.
Never despair, and always help. Perseverance is the basis of victory.
Do not forget that you will reap later in your field of love and light, but you will only reach the divine harvest if you walk forward, amidst sweat and trust, without ever fainting.

messages.title: Richly
paragraphs: “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly…” — PAUL (Colossians, 3:16)
You say you trust in the power of Christ, but if the day appears in colors contrary to your expectation, you demonstrate a deplorable indigence of faith through your lack of resignation.

You affirm that you cultivate the love that the Master bequeathed to us, yet if a companion expresses points of view different from yours, you show enormous poverty of comprehension, abandoning yourself to displeasure and censure.

You declare that you accept the Gospel in its simplicity and purity, but if the Lord asks of you some sacrifice perfectly compatible with your possibilities, you exhibit an undeniable lack of cooperation, launching challenges and demanding redress.

You assert that you seek the Will of the Celestial Benefactor, but if your whims are not satisfied, you show a lamentable misery of patience and hope, casting your best thoughts into the mire of disenchantment.
Shall we light the fire, however, and remain in darkness?
Shall we bear witness to obedience while exalting rebellion?
Shall we teach serenity while inclining toward despair?
Shall we proclaim the glory of love while cultivating hatred?
The word of Christ does not invite us to march in weakness or lamentation, as if we were wards of ignorance.
According to Paul's enlightened concept, the Good News must radiate from our life, dwelling richly in our soul.

messages.title: Let us always help
paragraphs: “And who is my neighbour?” — (Luke, 10:29)
The neighbor to whom we must render immediate assistance is always the person who is closest to us.
In short, it is, by all means, the creature who draws near our steps. And as the Divine Law recommends that we love our neighbor as ourselves, let us prepare to help infinitely...
If we have a family member before us, let us assist them with our active cooperation.
If we are confronted by a hierarchical superior, let us practice respect and goodwill.
If a subordinate seeks us out, let us help them with attention and affection.
If an evildoer visits us, let us practice fraternity, attempting, without affectation, to open new paths for them toward the good.
If the sick person asks us for help, let us have compassion on their condition, whatever it may be.
If the good person avails themselves of our word, let us encourage them to become better.
If the bad person seeks our influence, let us support them without fanfare so that they may correct themselves.
If there is Christianity in our conscience, the systematic cultivation of understanding and kindness has the force of law in our destinies.
A Christian without activity in the good is an unhealthy-looking patient, weighing down the economy of the community.
In the Gospel, a neutral position means lesser effort.
Either with Jesus, up close, working intensively alongside Him; or with Jesus, from afar, delaying the advance of the light.
And we know that the Divine Master loved and supported, fought in favor of the light and resisted the shadow, unto the cross.
Before the neighbor, then, who draws near your heart each day, always remember that you are situated on Earth to learn and to assist.

messages.title: Real Humanity
paragraphs: “Behold the Man!” — PILATE (John, 19.5)
Presenting Christ to the crowd, Pilate was not designating an earthly victor...
Neither banquet nor purple.
Neither applause nor flowers.
Jesus found himself facing death.
A week of terrible flagellations was ending.
Betrayed, he had not rebelled.
Arrested, he had exercised patience.
Humiliated, he did not yield to retaliation.
Forgotten, he did not entrust himself to revolt.
Mocked, he had excused.
Scourged, he forgot the offense.
Wronged, he did not defend himself.
Sentenced to martyrdom, he knew how to forgive.
Crucified, he would return to the fellowship of the same disciples and beneficiaries who had abandoned him, to lift up their hope.
But, exhibiting him before the people, Pilate does not state: — Behold the condemned, behold the victim!
He says simply: — “Behold the Man!”
Seemingly defeated, the Master emerged in full spiritual grandeur, revealing the highest standard of human dignity.
Remembering, therefore, such a passage, let us remember that only in the moral lines of Christ will we attain Real Humanity.

messages.title: Do not reject trust
paragraphs: “Do not throw away your confidence, which has a great and abundant reward.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 10.35)
Do not throw away the confidence that nourishes your heart.
Often, the apparent progress of the wicked discourages the fervor of lukewarm souls.
Wandering virtue recoils before vice that seems victorious.
The fragile believer shrinks before the wrongdoer who stands out, aureoled with laurels.
However, if we accept Jesus as our Divine Master, we must receive the world as our school.
And the school reveals to us that the carnal journey is a simple stage of the Spirit in the immense field of life.
All centuries have had sovereign rulers.
Many erected themselves on pedestals of gold and power, at the price of the blood and tears of their contemporaries.
Many won battles of hatred. Others monopolized bread.
Some commanded political life. Others acquired popular fear.

However, they all passed... As an earthly prize for the laborious endeavors to which they dedicated themselves, they received only the sumptuous sepulcher in which they stand out in the cold house of death.
Do not reject faith because the educational passage through Earth imposes distressing pictures on your vision in the game of human conventions. Remember immortality — our divine heritage!
Wherever you go, lead your soul as a precious source of understanding and service!
Wherever you are, be generous, optimistic, and diligent in doing good!

The flesh is only your garment. Strive and improve yourself, work and accomplish with Christ, and wait, confident, for the future, in the certainty that today's life awaits you, ever righteous, tomorrow.

messages.title: Keep patience
paragraphs: “For you have need of endurance, so that when you have done the will of God you may receive what is promised.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 10.36)
You have probably been holding on to tortured hope for a long time.

You would wish that the world's response to your yearnings would arise immediately, sheltering your heart; however, what peace would you enjoy in the apparent triumph of your own dreams, without redeeming the debts that chain you to trouble and difficulty?
How can one rest before the demand of the creditor who requires payment from us? Will the delinquent rest before making just reparation for the fault committed?
You know that destiny will materialize your plans for happiness, that victory will finally crown your path of struggle, but you recognize yourself bound to the circle of certain obligations.
The home turned into a forge of anguish...
The institution you serve, where you suffer the intrusion of calumny or the blow of cruelty...
The relative to whom you owe respect and affection, from whom you reap contempt and ingratitude...
The web of obstacles... The conspiracy of shadows...
Gratuitous persecution, bodily illness, the imposition of the environment...
If trials imprison you within the constraining bars of duty to be fulfilled, have patience and satisfy the obligations to which you have bound yourself!...
Do not renounce renewing work! Remember that the Will of God expresses itself, each hour, in the circumstances that surround us! Let us pay our accounts with shadow, so that Light may favor us!
In truth, we will achieve the realization of our projects of happiness, but, before that, it is necessary to liquidate with patience the debts we have contracted before the Law.

messages.title: Let us rise
paragraphs: “I will arise and go to my father...” — (LUKE, 15.18)
When the prodigal son resolved to return to his father's arms, he inwardly resolved to rise.
To leave the dark pit of idleness for the field of regenerating action.
To rise from the cold ground of inertia to the warmth of reconstructive movement.
To elevate himself from the valley of indecision to the mountain of edifying service.
To flee the darkness and enter the light.
To leave the negative position and absorb himself in the restructuring of his own ideals.
He arose and set out toward the Father's Home.

How many of us, however, prodigal children of Life, after squandering the most valuable opportunities, clamor for the Lord's assistance, according to our less dignified desires, so that we may be satisfied? How many of us descend voluntarily into the abyss, and, once there, bogged down in the gloomy current of our passions, demand that the All-Merciful make Himself present at our side through His divine messengers, so that our caprices may be attended to?
If it is true, however, that we are engaged in our uplifting, let us stand up and remove ourselves from the rear guard we wish to abandon.
Improvement requires effort. Panorama of the peaks requires ascent.
If we aspire to the climate of the Higher Life, let us press forward, walking with the standards of Jesus.
— I will arise, said the young man in the parable.
— Let us arise, let us repeat.

messages.title: In the intimate sphere
paragraphs: “As each has received a gift, use it to serve one another, as good stewards of God's varied grace.” — PETER (1 Peter, 4.10)
Life is a divine machine of which all beings are important parts, and cooperation is the essential factor in producing harmony and good for all.
Nothing exists without meaning. No one is useless.
Each creature has received a certain talent from Divine Providence to serve in the world and to receive from the world the salary of elevation.
Old or young, with bodily health or without it, remember that it is necessary to set in motion the gift you received from the Lord, to advance toward the Great Light.
No one is so poor that they can give nothing of themselves. Even the paralytic, tied to the cot of illness, can provide others with patience and calm, in the form of peace and resignation.

Do not forget, therefore, the work that Heaven has conferred upon you and avoid the preoccupation of interfering in your neighbor's task under the pretext of helping. Whoever fulfills their own duty acts naturally for the benefit of general balance.
Often, believing we are doing the service that belongs to them more correctly than others, we are nothing more than agents of disharmony and disturbance.
Wherever we are, let us attend with diligence and nobility to the mission that life offers us.
Remember that the hours are the same for everyone and that time is our silent and inflexible judge.
Yesterday, today, and tomorrow are three phases of the single path.
Every day is an opportunity to sow and reap.

Let us thus observe our own task and remember the word of the Gospel: — “As each has received a gift, use it to serve one another, as good stewards of God's varied grace,” so that God's grace may enrich us with new graces.

messages.title: In the social field
paragraphs: “He answered them, ‘You give them something to eat.’” — (Mark, 6.37)
Facing the tired and hungry crowd, Jesus recommends to the apostles: — “You give them something to eat.”
The Master's observation is important, when he could actually have induced them to reprimand the crowd for the imprudence of an exhaustive journey to the mountain without the guarantee of provisions.

The Master wished, however, to engrave in the disciples' spirits their dedication to popular service. He taught that the cooperators of the Gospel, before the needy crowd, have only one duty — that of rendering disinterested and fraternal aid.

At that hour of unforgettable teaching, hunger was naturally of the body, overcome by fatigue, but, still and always, we see the crowd lacking support, dominated by hunger for light and harmony, whipped by the invisible scourges of discord and incomprehension. Jesus' collaborators are called, not to obscure it with pessimism, not to disturb it with indiscipline or immobilize it with discouragement, but rather to nourish it with enlightenment and peace, moral fortitude, and sublime hope.

If you find yourself before the people with the yearning to help them, if you propose to contribute to the regeneration of the social field, do not get lost in preachings of rebellion and despair. Maintain serenity and nourish your neighbor with your good example and your good word. Do not forget the Lord's recommendation: — “You give them something to eat.”

messages.title: Being afraid...
paragraphs: “So I was afraid, and went and hid your talent in the ground...” — (Matthew, 25.25)
In the parable of the talents, the negligent servant attributes fear as the cause of the failure in which he makes himself unhappy.
He had received reduced possibilities for gain. He had counted on only one talent and had feared fighting to valorize it.

As happened to the unwatchful servant of the evangelical narrative, there are many people who accuse themselves of being poor in resources to travel through the world as they would wish. And they retreat into idleness, alleging the fear of action.
Fear of working.
Fear of serving.
Fear of making friends.
Fear of disappointing.
Fear of suffering.
Fear of incomprehension.
Fear of joy.
Fear of pain.
And they reach the end of the body, like human mimosas, without the least effort to enrich existence.
In life, they cling to the fear of death. In death, they confess the fear of life.
And, under the pretext of being less favored by destiny, they gradually transform themselves into champions of uselessness and laziness.

If you have received, therefore, a harsher task in the world, do not be frightened before others and make it your path of progress and renewal. No matter how gloomy the road to which you were led by circumstances, enrich it with the light of your effort in doing good, because fear did not serve as an acceptable justification in the settlement of accounts between the servant and the Lord.

messages.title: What do you have?
paragraphs: “How many loaves do you have?” And they said, “Seven.” — (Mark, 8.5)
When Jesus, facing the hungry crowd, inquired about the disciples' possibilities to assist them, he was certainly seeking a basis in order to materialize the precise succor.
“How many loaves do you have?”
The question denounces the need for some contribution for the work of multiplication.
The evangelist Mark tells us that the companions presented him with seven small loaves, from which more than four thousand people were fed, with an appreciable quantity left over.
Would the Master have achieved so much if he could not count on any resource?
The image compels us to meditate regarding the imperative of our cooperation, so that the Celestial Benefactor may bless us with his gifts of abundant life.
Can Christ build the sanctuary of happiness in us and for us if he cannot count on the foundations of goodwill in our heart?
The most powerful power plant does not dispense with the humble outlet to illuminate a room.

Many await the miracle of the Lord's manifestation so that their hunger for peace and comfort may be satiated, but the Master's voice on the mountain continues to resound, unforgettable: — What do you have?
Infinite is the Goodness of God; nevertheless, something must emerge from our “self,” in our favor.
In any field of our accomplishments for the higher life, let us present to Jesus some reduced crumbs of our own effort and let us be convinced that the Lord will do the rest.

messages.title: Let us seek balance
paragraphs: “Whoever says he abides in him ought to walk in the same way in which he walked.” — JOHN (1 John, 2.6)
Although you must walk without fear, do not marry imprudence under the pretext of cultivating boldness.
If we devote ourselves to the Gospel, let us seek to act according to the standards of the Divine Master, which never leave room for rashness.
Jesus highlights the imperative of building the Kingdom of God, but he does not sacrifice the interests of others in hasty works.
He advises the sincerity of “yes, yes — no, no,” yet he does not trust himself to blunt rudeness.
He points out the moral ruins of dogmatic Pharisaism, yet he pays cult to the Law of Moses.
He raises Lazarus from the tomb, yet he does not harbor the pretension of stealing him definitively from bodily death.

Conscious of the power with which he is invested, he does not belittle the political authority that must govern the people's needs and teaches that we must give “to Caesar what is Caesar's and to God what is God's.”
Arrested and sentenced to torture, he does not lose himself in lip bravado, despite recognizing the devotion with which he is followed by angelic entities.
Let us attend to the Divine Model whom we must not forget, performing our task with loyalty and courage, but let us avoid unnecessary daring, which amounts to dangerous levity.
A fearful heart freezes work. A rash heart sets any service on fire, destroying it.
Let us seek, therefore, balance with Jesus and we will naturally flee from extremism, which is always the dark sign of disharmony or violence, disturbance or death.

messages.title: Always Forgive
paragraphs: “For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.” — JESUS (Matthew, 6.14)
No matter how serious the faults of your neighbor may seem to you, do not dwell on reproach. To condemn is to crystallize darkness, placing barriers in the way of the service of light.
Look in the victims of wickedness for some good by which you can uplift them, just as life operates the miracle of greening in apparently dead trees.
Above all, remember how difficult it is to judge the decisions of creatures in experiences that differ from ours!
How can we reflect, appropriating the conscience of another, and how can we feel reality using a heart that does not belong to us?
If the world today cries out in alarm around your steps, be silent and wait...
Just observation is impracticable when fog surrounds us. Tomorrow, when balance is restored, you will achieve enough clarity so that the shadow does not alter your understanding.
Furthermore, in matters of criticism, do not suppose yourself exempt from it.
Through harmful complacency with yourself, you do not perceive how many times you appear unsympathetic to your fellow men!
If there are those who love our praiseworthy qualities, there are those who highlight our scars and defects.
If there are those who help by exalting our luminous future, there are those who disturb us, constraining us to review a dark past.
Use kindness, therefore, and forgive incessantly. The Good News teaches us that Love covers a multitude of sins.

Whoever forgives, forgetting evil and fostering good, receives from the heavenly Father, in the sympathy and cooperation of one's neighbor, the warrant for self-liberation, qualifying oneself for sublime renewals.

messages.title: Let Us Live Calmly
paragraphs: “That you also aspire to lead a quiet life.” — PAUL (1 Thessalonians, 4.11)
Living quietly is not rotting in laziness.
There are people whose bodies remain lying down, wrapped against the cold of difficulty by the excellent blankets of economic ease, but who are mentally tortured by indefinable afflictions.
Living calmly, therefore, is not sleeping in stagnation.
Peace stems from the acquittal of our conscience before life, and work lies at the base of such balance.
If we desire health, it is necessary to strive for the harmony of the body.
If we expect a bountiful harvest, it is essential to plant with effort and defend the crops with perseverance and affection.
To guarantee the fortitude of our heart against the harassment of evil, it is imperative that we know how to live within the serenity of work faithful to the commitments assumed with order and good.
The progress of the wicked and the rest of the delinquents are stopping points at the door of the hell they created themselves.
Do not wish, therefore, to be at ease without effort, without struggle, without work, without problems...

However, according to the apostle's warning, let us live calmly, fulfilling with courage, good will, and a spirit of sacrifice the edifying obligations that the world imposes upon us each day in favor of ourselves.

messages.title: Let Us Attend to the Good
paragraphs: “Assuredly, I say to you, inasmuch as you did it to one of the least of these My brethren, you did it to Me.” — JESUS (Matthew, 25.40)
Not only through words, which can symbolize brilliant leaves on a sterile trunk.
Not only through the act of believing, which sometimes is nothing more than inoperative ecstasy.
Not only through titles, which on many occasions constitute possibilities of access to abuses.
Not only through statements of faith, because in many cases sonorous phrases are cries of an empty soul.
Let us not forget the "doing".
Connection with Christ, communion with the Divine Light, do not depend on the way one interprets the revelations of Heaven.
In all the circumstances of His apostolate of love, Jesus sought to draw the attention of creatures, not to the form of religious thought, but to human kindness.

The Good News did not promise the peace of the higher life to those who calloused their knees in incomprehensible penances, to those who speculated on the nature of God, who discussed the things of Heaven in advance, or who simply preached eternal truths, but it exalted the sublime position of all who disseminated love in the name of the All-Merciful.

Jesus did not compromise with those who fought in His name, with those who humiliated others under the guise of glorifying Him, or with those who offered Him spectacular worship in temples of gold and stone, but rather affirmed that the smallest gesture of kindness dispensed in His name will always be considered on High as an offering of love addressed to Himself.

messages.title: The Right Remedy
paragraphs: “But concerning brotherly love, you have no need that I should write to you, for you yourselves are taught by God to love one another.” — PAUL (1 Thessalonians, 4.9)
In its mission as the Consoler, Spiritism receives thousands of queries from anxious souls who implore help and solutions for various problems.
Here, it is a father who does not understand and entrusts himself to cruel systems of education.
There, it is a rebellious and ungrateful son who flees from the beauty of understanding.
Over there, it is a friend fascinated by the appearances of the world, who abandons commitments to the higher ideal.
Further on, it is a brother who refuses brotherly cooperation.
Elsewhere, it is the spouse who deserts the home.
Further ahead, it is the head of service, insensitive and blunt.
However, the remedy for the extinction of these old enigmas of human relations has been indicated for centuries in the teachings of the Good News.
Brotherly charity is the key to all doors for good understanding.
The disciple of the Gospel is someone who has been admitted to the presence of the Divine Master to serve.
The reward of such a worker, effectively, cannot be awaited in the immediacy of Earth.
How can one place the fruit on the green frond of the nascent little plant? How can one draw the masterpiece from the marble with the first blow of the chisel?
Whoever truly loves in the name of Jesus is sowing for the harvest in Eternity.
Let us not seek guidance from others for matters clearly solvable by our own effort. We know it is no use to despair or curse...
Each Spirit possesses its own roadmap. Let us know how to walk, therefore, on the path that life offers us, under the light of brotherly charity, today and always.

messages.title: In the Work of Salvation
paragraphs: “For God did not appoint us to wrath, but to obtain salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ.” — PAUL (1 Thessalonians, 5.9)
Why are we not understood?
For what reason does loneliness invade our existence?
For what reasons do difficulties surround us?
Why so much shadow and so much harshness around our steps?
And to each question, asked by us to ourselves, there commonly follow despair and non-acceptance, claiming, under the deadly rays of anger, the advantages of which we feel ourselves creditors.
We declare ourselves disappointed with our family, forsaken by our friends, misunderstood by our companions, and even persecuted by our brothers.
Mental intemperance brings to our innermost self the thorns of disenchantment and unapproachable organic imbalances, transforming our existence into a rosary of lazy and sickly complaints.
This, however, happens because we were not appointed by the Lord to the dark precipice of wrath, but rather to the work of salvation.
No one restores a service under the darkness of disorder.
No one helps by systematically wounding for the mere pleasure of tearing apart.
No one will bless the tasks of each day while cursing them at the same time.
No one can be simultaneously a friend and an executioner.
If you have news of the Gospel in the world of your soul, prepare yourself to help infinitely...
Earth is our school and our workshop. Humanity is our family.
Each day is the blessed opportunity to learn and help.
No matter how afflictive your situation may be, always support others, and you will be acting in the blessed service of salvation to which the Lord has called us.

messages.title: Timely Inquiry
paragraphs: “He said to them, ‘Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?’” — (ACTS, 19.2)
The apostolic question still vibrates in all directions, with the greatest timeliness, in the circles of Christianity.
Everywhere, there are people who are beginning to believe and who already believe, in the most varied situations.
Here, someone apparently accepts the Gospel to be agreeable in social relations.
There, an inquirer seeks the field of faith, trying to settle intellectual problems they consider important.
Further on, a sick person receives the help of charity and declares themselves a follower of the Good News, guided by impressions of physical relief.
Tomorrow, however, they resurface as unsatisfied and desperate as before.
In the ranks of Spiritism, such phenomena are frequent.

We find a large number of companions who claim to be people of faith because they have identified the survival of some discarnate relative, because they got rid of a headache, or because they obtained a solution for certain problems of material struggle; however, tomorrow they continue to doubt spiritual friends and respectable mediums, welcome new illnesses, or get lost through new labyrinths of human learning.

Paul's interrogation remains full of currency. What kind of spirit do we receive at the moment of believing in Jesus' guidance? That of fascination? Of indolence? Of useless research? Of systematic reproach to the experiences of others?
If we do not harbor the spirit of sanctification that improves and renews us for Christ, our faith represents a fragile lamp, susceptible to being extinguished at the first gust of wind.

messages.title: Following Jesus
paragraphs: “Now as they led Him away, they laid hold of a certain Simon, a Cyrenian, who was coming from the country, and on him they laid the cross that he might bear it after Jesus.” — (Luke, 23.26)
The crowd surrounding the Master on that supreme day was enormous.

There were the unrepentant jesters of the world, the champions of usury, the mockers, the ignorant, the weak spirits who recognized the superiority of Christ and feared to announce their own convictions, the wavering friends of the Gospel, the cowardly witnesses, the beneficiaries of the Divine Physician who hid themselves fearfully, afraid of sacrifices...
But a foreigner, urged by the people, accepted the timber, albeit reluctantly, and followed carrying it after Jesus.
The lesson, however, would be bequeathed to future centuries...
The world is still an enormous Jerusalem, congregating creatures of the most varied nuances, but if you approach the Gospel with sincerity and fervor, they will place the cross upon your heart.

From then on, you will be compelled to the greatest demonstrations of renunciation; few will observe your fatigue and anguish, and, notwithstanding your condition as a servant with the same problems as others, they will demand of you spectacles of humility and endurance, heroism and loyalty to the good.
Suffer and work, with your eyes turned to the Divine Light. From on High, the invisible torrents of heavenly sources will descend into your Spirit, and you will victoriously overcome.
For now, the cross is still the sign of faithful learners.

If you do not carry with you the marks of testimony through responsibility, work, sacrifice, or intimate improvement, it is possible that you deeply love the Master, but it is almost certain that you have not yet placed yourself beside Him on the redemptive journey.
Let us bless our cross, therefore, and follow Him fearlessly, seeking the victory of love and eternal resurrection.

messages.title: Renew Yourself Always
paragraphs: “Even though our outward man is perishing, yet the inward man is being renewed day by day.” — PAUL (2 Corinthians, 4.16)
Each day has its lesson. Each experience leaves its corresponding value. Each problem obeys a specific objective.
There are creatures who, tortured by counterproductive fears, proclaim the non-acceptance that possesses them in the face of illness or poverty, disillusionment or old age.

There is no lack, in the framework of daily struggle, of those who spectacularly flee from the duties that fall to them, seeking in the abandonment of the good fight and in gradual agreement with death the peace they cannot find.

Remember that civilizations have succeeded one another in the world for thousands of years, and that men, no matter how happy or powerful, were constrained to lose the vehicle of flesh to settle moral accounts with eternity.
Even if the trial seems invincible to you or the pain appears insurmountable, do not withdraw from the position of laborer in which Divine Providence has placed you.
Remember that tomorrow the day will return to your field of work. Remain firm in your sector of service, educating your thought in the acceptance of God's Will.
Illness may be a transitory and salutary summons from Celestial Justice.
The scarcity of earthly resources is always an educational obstacle.
Disappointment received with fervent courage is the Lord's work of selection for our benefit.
The senility of the physical body is the fixing of wisdom for eternal happiness.
Be optimistic and diligent in good, amidst trust and joy, because while the fleshly envelope slowly corrupts, the imperishable soul renews itself moment by moment for immortal life.

messages.title: Do Not Steal
paragraphs: “Let him who stole steal no longer, but rather let him labor, working with his hands what is good, that he may have something to give him who has need.” — PAUL (Ephesians, 4.28)
There are thefts of various natures, never cataloged in the codes of justice on Earth.
Thefts of time from those who work.
Assaults on the tranquility of one's neighbor.
Depredations of another's trust.
Invasions into the interests of others.
Misappropriations through thought.
Spoliations of joy and hope.

With the false keys of intrigue and calumny, cruelty and bad faith, there are merciless souls who subtly penetrate unsuspecting hearts, dilapidating them in their most valuable spiritual patrimonies...
For this reason, Paul's word is coated with sublime significance: — “Let him who stole steal no longer.”
If you have accepted the Gospel as a standard for the elevation of your life, seek, above all, to occupy your hands in edifying activities so that you may be truly useful to those who need it.
In laziness is located the management of evil. Whoever does something has something to share.
Seek your post of service, duly fulfill your daily obligations, and, attending to the duties the Lord has entrusted to you, you will cross the earthly path without stealing from anyone.

messages.title: Awake and Help
paragraphs: “Follow Me, and let the dead bury their own dead.” — JESUS (Matthew, 8.22)
Jesus did not recommend that the learner let “corpses take care of burying corpses,” but rather confer on the “dead the care of burying their own dead.”
There is, indeed, a great difference. A corpse is flesh without life, while a dead person is someone who absents themselves from life.

There are many people who wander in the shadows of death without dying. Deserters of evolution, they enclose themselves within the walls of their own minds, crystallized in selfishness or vanity, refusing to share common experience. They immerse themselves in sepulchers of gold, vice, bitterness, and illusion. If victimized by the temptation of wealth, they dwell in tombs of dollar signs; if defeated by pernicious habits, they incarcerate themselves in bars of shadow; if prostrated by discouragement, they sleep in the tears of moral bankruptcy; and if tormented by the lies with which they envelop themselves, they reside under the scarcely permeable tombstones of fatal delusions.

Learn to participate in the collective struggle. Step out of yourself each day and seek to feel the pain of your neighbor, the need of others, the anguish of your brother, and help as much as you can.
Do not galvanize yourself in the sphere of your own “self.” Awake and live with all, for all, and by all, because no one breathes solely for themselves.
In any part of the Universe, we are beneficiaries of the effort and sacrifice of millions of existences.
Let us yield a part of ourselves in favor of others, for the much that others do for us.

Let us remember, thus, the teaching of Christ. If you find a corpse, give it the blessing of burial in the list of your works of charity, but when dealing with the spiritual journey, always leave “the dead to bury their own dead”.

messages.title: Let Us Help Mental Life
paragraphs: “And a great multitude followed him from Galilee, and from Decapolis, and from Jerusalem, and from Judea, and from beyond Jordan.” — (Matthew, 4:25)
The crowd continues to follow Jesus in their eagerness to find Him, mobilizing all the resources within their reach. They come from everywhere, thirsty for comfort and revelation.
The interference of all those who interpose themselves between the crowd and the Lord is useless, because, from century to century, the search and hope intensify.

Let us not forget, therefore, that every collaboration we can render to the people, in our condition as learners, will always be blessed. No one needs to be a statesman or an administrator to help people elevate themselves.

Goodwill and cooperation represent the two master pillars in the edifice of human fraternity. And to contribute so that the community learns to think in the scope of good is to collaborate so that the attunement of the terrestrial mind with the Divine Mind is effected.
A precious program unfolds before us in this regard.
Alphabetization. Edifying reading. Educational lecture.
Contagious example in the practice of simple goodness.
Dissemination of comforting and instructive pages. Exercise in meditation.
May our primary task be the awakening of inner and personal values.
Let us help our companion produce whatever they can give of their best to common progress, in the plan, ideal, and activity in which they find themselves.
To guide thought, clarify it, and sublimate it is to guarantee the redemption of the world, unveiling new and rich horizons for ourselves.
Let us help the mental life of the crowd, and the people with us will find Jesus more easily, for the victory of Eternal Life.

messages.title: Beware of Dogs
paragraphs: “Beware of dogs.” — PAUL (Philippians, 3:2)
We are an immense caravan of beings, on the evolutionary road, moving under the gaze of the Divine Shepherd, in demand of higher Spheres.
Indeed, if we continue along the path, magnetized by the devotion of the Divine Conductor, we are undeniably also besieged by the dogs of ignorance, perversity, and bad faith.

Referring to dogs, Paul of Tarsus was not thinking of the friendly animal, a symbol of tenderness and fidelity after domestication. He was referring to wild, impulsive, and ferocious dogs. In the human flock, we will always find creatures who personify them. They are the systematic adversaries of the good.
They tear worthy reputations to pieces.
They cherish evil-speaking.
They practice cruelty.
They feel pleasure in the tyrannical imposition that is proper to them.
They undo the elevated and sanctifying conceptualization of life.
They disrupt the service of well-intentioned hearts.
They throw themselves, wildly, at the substance of constructive works, trying to consume or pervert them.
They vomit improprieties and slander.
They shout, frivolously, that evil remains victorious, that shadow has won, that misery has consolidated its dominion on Earth, disturbing the peace of hardworking and faithful servants.
And, when the microbe of hatred or anger excites their despair, woe to those who approach, generous and confident!

It is for this genre of brothers that Paul asks us to conjugate the verb to beware. For them, poor prisoners of misunderstanding and ignorance, only the educational process remains, in which we can cooperate with love, while recognizing, however, that this resource of domestication originates from God.

messages.title: Let Us Know How to Cooperate
paragraphs: “For without me you can do nothing.” — JESUS (John, 15:5)
The divine power of Christ, as the representative of God, remains latent in all creatures. All men have received sacred gifts from Him, even though many remain distant from the religious field.
We refer here, however, to cultivators of faith, who begin the laborious and long effort of discovering the sublime values that vibrate within themselves.

A large part sighs for spectacular demonstrations of Jesus in their paths, and countless companions believe that only those who are in the ministry of the word, at the altar, or on the platform of various religious confessions cooperate with the Lord. It is urgent, however, to rectify this interpretive error.
The Lord is with us in all positions of life. We could accomplish nothing without the influx of His sovereign will.
The Master tells us clearly: — “I am the vine, you are the branches.” How to produce anything without the essential sap?

Indeed, clever learners might object that, under this criterion, we will also find those who practice evil, grounded on the same bases. In response, we will only consider that such unfortunates graft infernal cacti onto the Divine Vine on their own account, paying a high price before the Government of the Universe.

We refer to the timid and vacillating, though well-intentioned companions, to conclude that, in all human tasks, we can feel the presence of the Lord, sanctifying the work entrusted to us. Therefore, we cannot forget the evangelical lesson that any effort in the good would be blessed, even if it were only that of administering a cup of pure water in His name.

The Master is not solely in the service of those who teach Divine Revelation through academic, instructive, or comforting speech. He accompanies those who manage the world's goods and those who obey the ordinances of the path, concurring in the building of a better future, in material and spiritual organizations. He remains beside those who turn the soil of the Planet, cooperating in the structuring of the Perfected Earth, just as He inspires the missionaries of intelligence in the evolution of human rights.

Let us know how to cooperate, thus, in the circles of service to which we were called for Christian participation. Do, as well as lies within your possibilities, the partial work entrusted to your hands.

For today, you may deceive yourself, supposing you are serving earthly authorities; nevertheless, the revealing minute will arrive when you will recognize that you remain at the service of the Lord. Unite yourself, therefore, with the Divine Artisan, in spirit and truth, because the fundamental problem of our peace is precisely that of knowing whether we live in Him as much as He lives in us.

messages.title: Take Refuge in Peace
paragraphs: “There were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.” — (Mark, 6:31)
The Master's invitation for the disciples to seek a place apart, in order to rest the mind and heart in prayer, is increasingly opportune.

All earthly roads are full of those who come and go, tormented by short-sighted interests, without finding time to receive spiritual nourishment. Countless people cross the path, hungry for gold, and return laden with disillusionments. Many others rush into adventures, thirsty for emotional novelty, and return with destructive boredom.
There have never been so many stone temples in the world, as now, for the manifestations of religiosity, and never has such a volume of disenchantment appeared in souls.
Labor legislation has been reducing the activity of hands as never before; however, at no time have worries arisen as agonizing as at present.
The machines of modern civilization have astoundingly limited human effort; yet afflictions culminate, presently, in wars of scientific devastation.

The technique of economic production has advanced in all sectors, selecting cotton and wheat to intensify harvests, but, to eyes contemplating the world landscape, never has such a scarcity of bread and clothing been verified among the incarnate.
Social theories of solidarity have been refined, and never has there been so much discord.

As happened in the times of Jesus' stay in the apostolate, the majority of men remain in the coming and going of the paths, between misguided searching and false finding, between frivolous youth and disillusioned old age, between despised health and profitless illness, between lost incarnation and despairing desencarnation.
Oh my friend, if you have effectively adopted learning with the Divine Master, withdraw to a place apart, and cultivate the interests of your soul.

It is possible that you will not find the outer garden that facilitates meditation, nor any piece of physical nature where you can rest from material fatigue, nevertheless, penetrate the sanctuary within yourself.

There are many feelings that have animated you for centuries, imitating, in your innermost self, the ebb and flow of the crowd. They pass hurriedly from your heart to your brain and return from the brain to your heart, always the same, incapable of access to spiritual light. They are the fantastical principles of peace and justice, of love and happiness that the fleshly plane has imposed on you. In certain circumstances of transitory experience, they can be useful; however, do not live exclusively beside them. They would exercise infernal captivity over you.
Take refuge in the temple apart, within your soul, because only there will you find the true notions of peace and justice, of real love and happiness, to which the Lord has destined you.

messages.title: The Heir of the Father
paragraphs: “Whom he appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 1:2)
Yield to respectable human powers what belongs to them by the logical right of life, but do not forget to give to the Lord what belongs to Him.
This conciliating formula of the Gospel still remains pulsating with interest for the well-being of the world.
It is not convenient to concentrate all our hopes and aspirations in mutable organizations of the carnal plane.

The inner man renews himself daily. Therefore, the science that answers his demands in passing minutes is not the same that served him in hours gone by, and that of the future will be very different from the one helping him in the present. The politics of the past gave way to the politics of modern struggles. The bloody triumph of the strongest in the time of unrestrained savagery was followed by militaristic autocracy. Force yielded to authority, authority to right. In the sector of religious activities, the evolutionary effort has been no less.
In view of such realities, why do you fall so vehemently in love with fallible creatures and transitory programs?

Today's men, no matter how venerable, are heirs of yesterday's men, engaged in the gigantic struggle for their own redemption. They may promise marvelous reigns of abundance and peace, freedom and harmony, however, they will not escape the work of correcting the errors they inherited, not only from those who preceded them in the field of collective commitments, but equally from their own past experiences in tenebrous deviations of sentiment.
Today's civilization is the successor to failed civilizations.
Nations that restore themselves take advantage of nations that fell apart.
Organizations emerging today keep the heritage of those that disappeared in the maelstrom of discord and tyranny.
Examining the unmistakable physiognomy of truth, how can you hypertrophy your feeling by defining yourself absolutely by terrestrial institutions that lack, above all, your own spiritual help?
How can a roofless house shelter you from the storm?
The blueprint of the skyscraper, intelligently traced on parchment, is not yet the construction that maintains legitimate security.

There are therefore no reasons that justify the torments of Christ's learners, anguished by the political anxieties of the passing hour; such a state of soul is simply the product of dangerous inadvertence, because we must all know that fallible men cannot build infallible works and that it is up to us, partisans of the Master, to hold the position of sincere workers, called to serve and cooperate in the patient and long, but definitive and eternal work of Him whom the Father “appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds”.

messages.title: In the Cult of Prayer
paragraphs: “And when they had prayed, the place was shaken where they were assembled together; and they were all filled with the Holy Ghost.” — (Acts, 4:31)
We all cast around us creative or destructive forces, agreeable or disagreeable to the personal circle in which we move.
The tree reaches us with the subtle matter of its own emanations.
The spider breathes in the center of its own webs. The bee may travel intensively, but it rests nowhere except in the compartments of its own hive.
Likewise, man lives within the bosom of the mental creations to which he gives origin.
Our thoughts are walls in which we enclose ourselves or wings with which we progress in ascension.
As you think, so you will live.
Our inner life is our place.
In order that we do not disturb the laws of the Universe, Nature only grants us the blessings of life in accordance with our conceptions.
Withdraw inward and you will see the limit of everything that surrounds you. Expand and you will find the infinity of everything that exists.
In order for us to elevate ourselves, with all the elements of our orbit, we know no other resource besides prayer, which asks for light, love, and truth.
Prayer, translating the ardent aspiration of spiritual climb through knowledge and virtue, is the force that illuminates the ideal and sanctifies work.

Acts narrates that, when the apostles had prayed, the place where they were gathered shook, and they were filled with the Holy Ghost: their yearning for fraternity was illuminated, their minds congregated in superior purposes were magnified, and sanctifying energy blessed their spirit.
Do not forget, therefore, that the cult of prayer is a decisive march. Prayer will renew you for the Lord's work, day by day, without you even perceiving it.

messages.title: Fraternity
paragraphs: “By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.” — JESUS (John, 13:35)
Since Constantine's victory, which opened the doors of political hegemony to the Christian world, we have tried various experiments on Earth to demonstrate our condition as disciples of Jesus.
We have organized famous councils, formulating daring conclusions concerning the nature of God and the Soul, the Universe and Life.
We have incited devastating wars that implanted misery and terror in those who could not believe according to the tuning fork of our faith.
We have disputed the sepulcher of the Divine Master, brandishing the deadly sword and kindling the devouring fire.
We have created commendations and religious offices, distributing poison and wielding the dagger.
We have lit bonfires and erected scaffolds, invented torments, and built prisons for all who disagreed with our points of view.
We have stimulated insurrections that operated the clash of brothers against brothers, in the name of the Lord who witnessed on the cross devotion to all Humanity.
We have built palaces and basilicas, famous for their sumptuousness and beauty, intending to reverence His memory, forgetting that He, in truth, did not possess a stone where to lay His head.
And, even today, we nourish separation and discord, erecting trenches of misunderstanding and animosity, one against the other, in the various sectors of interpretation.
However, Christ's word is infallible. We will not make ourselves holders of the Good News simply through external attitudes...

We do need the culture that refines intelligence, the justice that sustains order, the material progress that enriches work, and assemblies that favor study; yet all human movement, without the light of love, can lose itself in the shadows.
We will be admitted to the learning of the Gospel by cultivating the Kingdom of God that begins in the inner life.

Let us thus extend pure and simple fraternity, supporting one another... Fraternity that works and helps, understands and forgives, amidst the humility and service that ensure the victory of good. Let us attend to it wherever we are, recalling the word of the Lord who stated with clarity and certainty: — “By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.”

messages.title: The Prayer of the Righteous
paragraphs: “The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.” — (James, 5:16)
Considering the waves of desire in their vital force, every impulse and every yearning also constitute prayers that depart from Nature.
The worm that crawls with difficulty is fundamentally begging for resources of easier locomotion.
The she-wolf, caressing her little pup, in the core of her being remains imploring lessons of love that will modify her savage expression.
Primitive man, worshiping the thunder, in the recesses of his soul asks the Divinity for explanations in order to educate his impulses of faith.
All the world's needs, translated into the effort of living beings, count as supplications from creatures to the Creator and Father.
For this very reason, if the good man's desire is a prayer, the purpose of the evil or unbalanced man is also a petition.
Here, too, we have the law of specific density.
Throw a stone at your neighbor, and the projectile will be immediately pulled downward. Drop a few drops of perfume on your brother's forehead, and the aroma will spread into the atmosphere.
Release a snake, and it will look for a burrow. Release a swallow, and it will seek the heights.
Minerals, plants, animals, and human souls are habitually asking, and Divine Providence, through Nature, is always responding.
There are processes of prolonged solution and answers that take centuries to descend from the Heavens to the Earth.
But of all the prayers that rise on High, the apostle highlights that of the righteous man as being clothed with intense power.
This is because upright conscience, in adjustment to the Law, has already conquered numerous friendships and intercessions.
Whoever gathers friends hoards love. Whoever hoards love accumulates power.

Learn, thus, to act with justice and goodness, and your petitions will rise unhindered, supported by vehicles of sympathy and gratitude, because the righteous man, truly, wherever he is, is always a cooperator with God.

messages.title: Evil-Speaking
paragraphs: “Speak not evil one of another, brethren. He that speaketh evil of his brother, and judgeth his brother, speaketh evil of the law, and judgeth the law: but if thou judge the law, thou art not a doer of the law, but a judge.” — (James, 4:11)
Not all hours are adequate for the course of tenderness in the sphere of loyal conversations.
Explanatory speech sometimes calls for serene energy in unwavering affirmations; however, great care is indispensable regarding subsequent commentaries.
Evil-speaking waits for sincerity in order to muddy its waters and render fair efforts useless.

Evil does not deserve the crown of serious observations. Attributing great importance to it in verbal activities is to dilate its sphere of action. For this very reason, James's advice is clothed with sanctified wisdom.

When a problem of difficult solution arises between one learner and another, it is reasonable that they seek the Master's company, solving it in the clarity of His light, but that they never install themselves in the shadow, at a distance from one another, for malicious commentaries on the situation, aggravating the pain of open wounds.
“Speaking evil,” in its legitimate significance, is to render homage to inferior instincts and renounce the title of cooperator with God to become a critic of His works.
As we observe, evil-speaking is a subtle toxic that can lead the disciple to immense nonsense.
Whoever imbibes such poison is, above all, a servant of foolishness, but we likewise know that many of these fools are one step away from great inner misfortunes.

messages.title: Come!
paragraphs: “And let him that heareth say, Come. And let him that is athirst come.” — (Revelation, 22:17)
Earth is the great school of souls where students of all ages educate themselves.
If you have reached the level of great experiences, do not let the incessant extension of work disquiet you.
Do not see enemies in fellows of imperfect understanding. Many of them have not yet left spiritual kindergarten.
Always give good for evil, truth for a lie, and love for indifference...
The inexperience and ignorance of hearts starting out in the struggle frequently make a great fuss around the Spirit seeking itself.
Because of this, you will often suffer affliction and discouragement. Do not be disturbed, however.
If the illusions and toys of the majority no longer satisfy you, it is because maturity inclines you toward vaster horizons.
Remember that only Jesus is wise enough and strong enough to calm you. Hear His divine appeal, formulated in the final words of His Testament of Love: — “Come!”
No one can bar your access to the source of infinite light.
The Master is the Eternal Friend who breaks our shackles and opens renewing doors for us...
However, you must know how to want it. The Lord will never use violence against us.
Do you suffer? Are you fatigued? Do you stumble under the burdens of the world? Come! Jesus reserves His open arms for you.

Come and heed Him today still. It is true that you have always found occasions for service, that the Master has always been self-giving and merciful toward you, but do not forget that circumstances modify with the hours and that not all days are alike.

messages.title: Let Us Listen
paragraphs: “And straightway he called them.” — (Mark, 1:20)

In some circles of Christianity, this passage, alluding to the Lord's encounter with the disciples, is interpreted simply as a call from Christ to the religious ministry. However, we can impart a broader meaning to it. In every situation along the path, it is possible to register the celestial call.
In the family temple, where difficult problems arise…
Before the unknown companion who asks for cooperation…
Facing the adversary who expects understanding and tolerance…
At the feet of the sick person awaiting assistance and affection…
In the face of the ignorant person who claims help and teaching…
Beside the child who begs for kindness and understanding…
Wherever we go, Jesus, the Silent Master, calls us to the testimony of the lesson we have learned.
In the smallest experiences, at work or at play, at home or on the public road, behold, He invites us to the incessant exercise of good.
In this sense, the disciple of the Gospel finds in the world the sanctuary of their faith and in Humanity their own family.

Marking, therefore, the Christian norm as an inspiration for all daily labors, let us listen to the word of the Lord in every corner of the path, seeking to follow Him with invariable fidelity, today and always.

messages.title: No One Lives for Themselves
paragraphs: “For none of us lives to himself…” — PAUL (Romans, 14:7)
The tree you plant will produce not only for your hunger, but to relieve the needs of many.
The light you kindle will clear the path not only for your feet, but likewise for the travelers who follow by your side.
Just as the stream of water influences the earth through which it passes, your decisions inspire the decisions of others.
Thousands of eyes observe your steps, thousands of ears listen to your voice, and thousands of hearts receive your stimuli for good or for ill.
“None of us lives to himself…” — the Divine Message assures us.
Whether we wish it or not, it is of the Law that our existence belongs to the existences that surround us.
We live for our family members, our friends, our ideals…
Even the exclusivist usurer, who thinks he has no one, is living for another or for the utilities that he will restore to other higher or lower lives for which death will snatch his treasure.
Understanding such a reality, observe your own path.
Feeling, you think. Thinking, you accomplish.

And all that constitutes your works, through intentions, words, and acts, will represent the influence of your soul, assisting your liberation for the glory of light or aggravating your captivity for suffering in the shadows.
Watch, therefore, your intimate world and do the good you can, even today, because, according to the wise concept of the Apostle Paul, “none of us lives to himself”.

messages.title: Let Us Learn to Give Thanks
paragraphs: “In everything give thanks.” — PAUL (1 Thessalonians, 5:18)
Let us know how to thank for the gifts that the Lord grants us each day:
The breadth of life;
abundant air;
the grace of locomotion;
the faculty of reasoning;
the flash of the idea;
the joy of seeing;
the pleasure of hearing;
the treasure of the word;
the privilege of work;
the gift of learning;
the table that serves us;
the bread that nourishes us;
the cloth that dresses us;
