the unknown hands that intertwine in the effort to supply us with meals and shelter;
the anonymous benefactors who transmit to us the wealth of knowledge;
the conversation of the friend;
the warmth of home;
the sweet duty of family;
the contentment of building for the future; the renewal of one's own strength…
Many people are waiting for spectacular strokes of “worldly good luck” in order to express gratitude to Heaven.
The Christian, however, knows that the blessings of Divine Providence enrich the simplest corners of each hour within the space of our experiences.
Nothing is insignificant on the road we travel.
All the concessions of the Heavenly Father are precious in the field of our life.
Using, therefore, the patrimony that the Lord lends us, in incessant service to the good, let us learn to give thanks.

messages.title: Relatives
paragraphs: “But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.” — PAUL (1 Timothy, 5:8)
Causality is not found in the ties of kinship.
Subtle principles of the Law function in blood-related connections.
Impelled by the causes of the past to reunite in the present, it is indispensable to pay with joy the debts that bind us to certain hearts, so that we may settle our debts toward Humanity.
Useless is the flight from the creditors who breathe with us under the same roof, because time will await us implacable, compelling us to the liquidation of all commitments.

We have companions with sweet and edifying voices in salvationist propaganda who become true thunders of intolerance in the domestic atmosphere, accumulating unbalanced energies around their own tasks.

Without a doubt, the family team in the world is not always a garden of flowers. At times, it is a briar patch of worries and anguish, demanding sacrifice from us. Nevertheless, although we need firmness in our attitudes to temper the affection that is proper to us, we will never manage to heal the wounds of our private environment with the whip of violence or the plaster of neglect.
According to the Apostle's warning, if we fail in our care for our own family, we will be denying the faith.

Relatives are works of love that the Compassionate Father gave us to accomplish. Let us help them through cooperation and affection, attending to the designs of true brotherhood. Only by training patience and understanding, tolerance and kindness, on the narrow shore of the home, will we qualify ourselves to serve with victory on the high sea of great experiences.

messages.title: Children
paragraphs: “Take heed that ye despise not one of these little ones…” — JESUS (Matthew, 18:10)
When Jesus recommended that we not despise the little ones, He expected from us not only provisional measures alluding to bread and clothing.
It is not enough to feed tiny hungry mouths or to warm little frozen bodies. The moral shelter that ensures for the reborn Spirit the climate of work necessary for its sublimation is imperative.
Many parents guarantee the material comfort of their little children, but relegate their souls to lamentable abandonment.

Vagrancy in the street manufactures delinquents who end up situated in prison or the asylum, but spiritual relaxation in the domestic stronghold generates social demons of perversity and madness who on many occasions, sheltered by money or positions of prominence, cross wide tracts of the century, spreading misery and suffering, shadow and ruin, with deplorable impunity before earthly justice.
Do not despise, therefore, the child, handing them over to the impulses of animalized nature.
Remember that we are all in a process of education and re-education before the Divine Master.
The plate of food is important in the development of the creature; however, we cannot forget “that man shall not live by bread alone” लड़के.

Let us remember the spiritual nourishment of children through our attitudes and examples, warnings and corrections, in a timely manner, since morally abandoning the child in today's tasks will be to condemn them to self-contempt in the services for which they will take responsibility tomorrow.

messages.title: In the Absence of Love
paragraphs: “But he that hateth his brother is in darkness, and walketh in darkness, and knoweth not whither he goeth, because that darkness hath blinded his eyes.” — JOHN (1 John, 2:11)
If you do not know how to cultivate true brotherhood, you will be fatally attacked by pessimism, just as dry dust accumulates on dry soil.
Everything bothers the one who retreats into intransigence.
Companions who flee from the tasks of love are profoundly sad due to the gall of intolerance with which they feed themselves.
Invited to team effort, they assert that men breathe in moral bankruptcy.
Brought to the cult of faith, they suppose they recognize malice and disillusionment everywhere.
Called to charity, they consider their brothers in suffering to be probable enemies, withdrawing irritably.
Impelled to this or that manifestation of contentment, they recoil, disenchanted, believing they surprise malice and mud in the smallest expressions of festive beauty.
They walk in the world between bitterness and mistrust.
There is no affection that is enough for them. They vampirize creatures wherever they linger, crying, complaining, lamenting…
They have no certain course. They declare themselves expelled from society and family.

It is because, incapable of love for one's neighbor, they journey across the Earth under the heavy fog of selfishness that keeps us solely in the narrow circle of our needs, without any expression of respect for the needs of others.
They claim to be misunderstood because they do not wish to understand.
Absent from love, they dry up the machine of life, losing spiritual vision.
Impermeable to good, they make themselves representatives of evil.
If pessimism begins to approach your spirit, retreat into prayer and ask the Lord to multiply your strength in resistance before the assault of darkness.

Let us learn to live with everyone, tolerating so that we may be tolerated, helping so that we may be helped, and love will make us live, helpful and optimistic, in the luminous climate in which struggle and work are blessings of hope.

messages.title: In the Presence of Love
paragraphs: “He that loveth his brother abideth in the light, and there is none occasion of stumbling in him.” — JOHN (1 John, 2:10)

Whoever loves their neighbor knows, above all, how to understand. And whoever understands knows how to rid their eyes and ears of the poisonous mistletoe of scandal, in order to help instead of accusing or disserving.
It is necessary to bring the heart under the light of true brotherhood, to recognize that we are brothers to one another, children of one Father.

As long as we linger in the dark phase of exclusive attachment to ourselves, we imprison ourselves in selfishness and demand that others love us. In this unhappy step, we know how to love only ourselves, taking our fellow men as instruments of our satisfaction.
But if we truly love our companion on the path, the landscape of life changes, since the clarity of love will bathe our vision.
Love, therefore, and just as mud never offends the light, offense will no longer reach you.
You will know that misery is the fruit of ignorance and you will assist the victim of evil, finding in them your own brother in need of support and understanding.

You will learn to listen without revolt, even if crime seeks your ears, and you will cultivate help for the adversary, even when you see yourself torn apart, because forgiveness with absolute forgetfulness of the blows received will arise spontaneous in your spirit, just as tolerance appears natural in the spring that welcomes in its own bosom the stones hurled at it.
Love and you will understand.
Understand and you will serve more and more each day, because then you will remain under the glory of light, inaccessible to any incursion of darkness.

messages.title: Do Not Disturb Yourself
paragraphs: “Was then that which is good made death unto me? God forbid.” — PAUL (Romans, 7:10)

If we were to ask the grain of wheat what opinion it harbors about the mill, it would naturally answer that inside it finds the house of torture where it is afflicted and suffers; however, it is from there that it departs enhanced for the glory of bread in the subsistence of the world.

If we were to inquire of the wood regarding the saw, it would inform us that in it it identifies the tormentor of all moments, tearing its bowels apart; yet, under the sponsorship of the supposed executioner, it becomes delicate and useful to serve in increasingly noble activities.

If we consult the stone with allusion to the chisel, it will surely clarify that it discovered in it the detestable persecutor of its tranquility, wounding it mercilessly, day and night; however, it is from its blows that it rises to earthly treasures, perfected and brilliant.
Thus the soul. Thus the struggle.

Let us ask for man's opinion regarding the flesh, and he will perhaps utter a thousand improprieties. Let us listen to him about pain and we will record old verbal absurdities. Let us ask him to express himself with reference to difficulty, and he will pour out gall and weeping.

Nevertheless, it is imperative to recognize that from the disciplined body, purifying suffering, and suffocating obstacle, the Spirit always resurfaces more beautiful, more robust, and more enlightened for immortality.
Do not disturb yourself, therefore, before the struggle, and observe.
What seems like defeat to you is often victory. And what appears to be in favor of your death is a contribution to your aggrandizement in eternal life.

messages.title: In Ordinary Struggle
paragraphs: “For whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.” — PAUL (Galatians, 6:7)
It is not necessary to die in the flesh to know the law of compensations. Let us observe ordinary struggle.
The man who lives in indifference to the pain of others receives from his fellow men indifference to his own pain.
Let us withdraw from social intercourse and depressing solitude will be the world's response to us.
If we use severity toward others, we will be judged by others with rigor and harshness.
If we practice hostility and aversion in society or family, we will find antipathy and mistrust among relatives and neighbors.
If we insult our task with laziness, our task will relegate us to ineptitude.
A gesture of affection toward a stranger on the public road will earn us the fraternal assistance of the anonymous groups that surround us.
Tiny sowings of kindness generate blessed fountains of joy.
Well-lived work produces the treasure of competence.
Attitudes of understanding and gentleness establish solidarity and respect around us.
Optimism and hope, nobility of character, and pure intentions attract precious opportunities for service in our favor.
Every day is a time to sow. Every day is a time to reap.

It is not necessary to cross the shadow of the tomb to encounter justice face to face. In the principles of cause and effect, we find ourselves incessantly under its guidance, in every instant of our lives.

messages.title: In Common Effort
paragraphs: “A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump?” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 5:6)
Let us not forget that our thoughts, words, attitudes, and actions constitute mental molds for those who accompany us.
Each day, in our turn, we suffer the influence of others in the construction of our own destiny.

And, as we receive according to what we attract, and reap according to what we plant, it is imperative that we know how to provide the best of ourselves so that others may provide us with the best of themselves.
All your thoughts act on the minds that surround you.
All your words will generate impulses in those who listen to you.
All your written phrases will generate images in those who read you.
All your acts are living models, influencing those around you.
No matter how much you try to isolate yourself, you will always be a living piece in the machine of existence. The wheels that rest on the ground guarantee the comfort and safety of the carriage.
We are a team of workers, acting in perfect interdependence. From the quality of our effort is born the success or arises the failure of the whole.
Our life, in any sector of struggle, is a great molding workshop.
We will either enslave ourselves to the captivity of shadow or liberate ourselves for the glory of light, in accordance with the living molds that our guidelines and actions establish.
Let us remember righteousness and nobility in the most obscure gestures.
Let us remember the lesson of the Gospel: “A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump.”
Let us make our own path a blessed source of work and brotherhood, help and hope, so that our Laborious Today may convert itself for us into a Divine Tomorrow.

messages.title: Within the Struggle
paragraphs: “I do not ask that You take them out of the world, but that You deliver them from evil.” — JESUS (John, 17:15)
Do not ask for the removal of your pain. Pray for strength to endure it with serenity and heroism, so that you do not lose the advantages of the contact.
Do not request the disappearance of the stones in your path. Insist on receiving thoughts that help you make good use of them.
Do not demand the expulsion of the adversary. Ask for resources for your own self-elevation, so that you may transform their feelings.
Do not plead for the extinction of difficulties. Seek means to overcome them by assimilating their lessons.
Nothing exists without a reason. The Lord's Wisdom leaves no room for uselessness.
Suffering has its precious function in the plans of the soul, just as the storm has its important place in the economy of physical nature.
The tree, from birth, grows and produces, overcoming resistance. The creature's body develops amidst various kinds of dangers.
Let us accept our day of service, wherever and however the Wise Will of the Lord determines.
Presenting the disciples to the Heavenly Father, the Master said: — “I do not pray that You should take them out of the world, but that You should keep them from the evil one.”

The Earth has its mission and its greatness; let us free ourselves from the evil that operates within ourselves and we shall receive its sublime support, becoming alongside it living agents of the Blessed Kingdom of God.

messages.title: Let Us Learn from Jesus
paragraphs: “Bearing with one another, and forgiving one another, if anyone has a complaint against another; even as Christ forgave you, so you also must do.” — PAUL (Colossians, 3:13)
Any joint action is impossible without a basis in tolerance. Let us learn from Christ.
Man identifies within his own body the law of cooperation, without which he would not remain on Earth.

If the stomach did not endure the mouth's extravagances, if the hands did not obey the mind's impulses, if the feet did not tolerate the weight of the organic machine, physical harmony would be utterly impractical.
Complaining disfigures the dignity of work, delaying its execution.
It is indispensable to cultivate the renunciation of the small desires peculiar to us, in order to conquer the capacity for sacrifice that will structure our sublimation to higher levels.
In order for work to elevate us, we need to elevate it.
In order for the task to help us, it is imperative that we are willing to help it.
Let us remember that the supreme guide of Christian service teams is always Jesus. Within them, our opportunity to do something constitutes in itself a valuable prize.
Let us thus forget all evil, in order to build all the good within our reach.
And so that we may act according to these norms, it is imperative that we bear with one another as brothers, learning from the Lord, who has tolerated us infinitely.

messages.title: Before God
paragraphs: “Our Father…” — JESUS (Matthew, 6:9)
For Jesus, the existence of God offers no motive for strife and altercations.
He does not inquire about the nature of the Eternal One. He does not ask where He lives.
In Him, He does not see the obscure and impersonal cause of the Universe. He simply calls Him “Our Father.”
In moments of work and prayer, of joy and suffering, He addresses the Supreme Lord in the position of a loving and trusting son.
The Master standardizes for us the attitude that befits us before God.
Neither undue research. Nor hasty inquiry.
Neither unreasonable demand. Nor disrespectful definition.
When you pray, seek the secret chamber of conscience and entrust yourself to God, as our Heavenly Father.
Be sincere and faithful. In the condition of needy children, let us loyally surrender ourselves to Him.
Do not ask whether God is a generating focus of worlds or a force radiating lives.
We do not yet possess the intelligence capable of reflecting His greatness, but we bring the heart capable of feeling His love.
Let us therefore seek our Father, above all, and God, our Father, will listen to us.

messages.title: Do Not Doubt
paragraphs: “…He who doubts is like a wave of the sea driven and tossed by the wind.” — JAMES (James, 1:6)
In your acts of faith and hope, do not allow doubt to interpose itself like a shadow between your need and the power of the Lord.

The coagulating force of your thoughts in the achievements you undertake proceeds from yourself, from the depths of your soul, because only he who trusts manages to persevere in climbing the steps that will lead him to the height he wishes to reach.
Doubt, on the external plane, can aid experimentation in this or that sector of material progress, but hesitation in the intimate world is the solvent of our best energies.
He who doubts himself disturbs divine aid within himself. No one can help someone who does not help themselves.
Understanding the imperative of trust that must guide us forward, let us insist on the good, seeking it with all the possibilities within our reach.
Let us abandon haste and forget discouragement.
It does not matter whether our conquest comes triumphantly today or tomorrow. It is worth working and doing the best we can, here and now, because life takes care of bringing us what we seek.

Advancing without hesitation, loving, learning, and serving untiringly — this is the formula for walking successfully toward our victory. And in this tireless pilgrimage, let us not forget that doubt will always be the coldness of defeatism, inclining us toward negation and death.

messages.title: Let Us Follow Him
paragraphs: “He who follows Me shall not walk in darkness.” — JESUS (John, 8:12)
There are those who admire the glory of Christ. But pure and simple admiration can turn into inoperative ecstasy.
There are those who believe in the Lord's promises. However, belief by itself can generate fanaticism and discord.
There are those who defend the revelation of Jesus. However, defense considered in isolation can generate sectarianism and blindness.
There are those who trust in the Divine Master. Yet stagnant trust can be an inert force.
There are those who wait for the Eternal Benefactor. However, expectation without work can be useless anxiety.
There are those who praise the Savior. Exclusive praise, however, can coagulate unproductive adoration.
The word of the Celestial Envoy, however, is clear and incisive: — “He who follows Me shall not walk in darkness.”
If you have grown fond of the Gospel, do not place yourself outside of Christian service.
Let us seek the Lord, following in His footsteps.
Only thus shall we be with Christ, receiving His exalted light.

messages.title: Let Us Observe Ourselves
paragraphs: “He who says he abides in Him ought himself also to walk just as He walked.” — JOHN (1 John, 2:6)
There are those who claim to live with the goodness of Jesus and do not hesitate to lash out at their fellow men through evil-speaking and cruelty.
There are those who assert they understand the optimism of the Divine Master and do not hesitate to concentrate in the shadows of pessimism and despair.
There are those who proclaim the fraternity of Christ while encouraging separation and discord.
There are those who exalt the Lord's incessant work in extending the good while accommodating themselves in the hammock of laziness and comfort.
There are those who praise the simplicity of the Eternal Friend while complicating all the problems of the road.
There are those who glorify the patience of the Sublime Instructor while clinging to the boulder of aggressiveness and intolerance.
If we confess ourselves to be apprentices of the Gospel, let us observe our own footsteps.
Let us remember that the name of Jesus is pledged in our hands.
Understanding this, let us grow fond of the Divine Model.

When the apostle declares to us — “he who says he abides in Him ought himself also to walk just as He walked” —, he naturally means to say: “he who claims to be a follower of Jesus must certainly imitate His conduct, seeking to live in the exemplification in which the Master lived.”

messages.title: Between the Cradle and the Grave
paragraphs: “While we do not look at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen. For the things which are seen are temporary, but the things which are not seen are eternal.” — PAUL (2 Corinthians, 4:18)
The flower we see passes briefly, but the perfume that escapes it enriches the world's economy.
The monument that dazzles us will suffer the insults of time; however, the invisible ideal that inspired it shines eternally in the artist's soul.
The Acropolis of Athens, admired by millions of eyes, is gradually disappearing; however, the Greek culture that produced it is immortal in earthly glory.
The cross that the people imposed on Christ was an instrument of torture seen by all, but the Spirit of the Lord, whom no one sees, is a sun growing ever larger with the passage of the centuries.
Do not cling too much to the transitory flesh. Tomorrow, the body's childhood and youth will be the maturity and old age of the form.
The land you hold today will in the future inevitably be divided.
Ornaments of which you are presently proud will be dust and ashes.
The money that now serves you will later pass into hands different from yours.
Use what you see to treasure what you cannot yet see.
Between the cradle and the grave, man holds the usufruct of the earth for the purpose of self-perfection.
Do not cling, therefore, to the deceptive husk of beings and things.
Learning and struggling, working and serving with humility and patience in the construction of the good, you will accumulate within your soul the riches of eternal life.

messages.title: Let Us Seek Eternity
paragraphs: “…even though our outward man is perishing, yet the inward man is being renewed day by day.” — PAUL (2 Corinthians, 4:16)
Do not let yourself be cast down before the alterations of the physical equipment. Let us seek Eternity.
Ailments do not reach the soul when they are not tied to the remorses of conscience.
Old age does not overtake the Spirit when we seek to live according to the light of immortality.
Youth is not a state of the flesh. There are young people who walk through the world carrying hearts full of dreadful ruins.
Let us remember that the inner man is always renewing himself. Struggle enriches him with experience, pain refines his emotions, and sacrifice tempers his character.
The incarnated Spirit undergoes constant transformations on the outside in order to purify and aggrandize itself on the inside.

Remember that the stage on Earth is a simple spiritual journey. Just as the traveler uses sandals, wearing them out along the way, our soul appropriates forms, using them in its ascendant march toward the Great Light.

Unbar, therefore, the receiver of your heart to the sublime wave of the noblest ideals and most beautiful thoughts, and let us learn to live far from the termite of discouragement; and our Spirit, even amidst the most advanced trials of illness or senectude, will be like a radiant sun, externalizing itself in songs of work and joy, casting out shadow and bitterness wherever we may be.

messages.title: Christ and Us
paragraphs: “And the Lord said to him in a vision, ‘Ananias!’ And he said, ‘Here I am, Lord!’” — (ACTS, 9:10)
Men wait for Jesus, and Jesus likewise waits for men.
Let no one believe that the world is redeemed without redeemed souls.

The Master, to extend the sublimity of His saving program, asks for human arms to accomplish and intensify it. He began His apostolate by seeking the concurrence of Peter and Andrew, subsequently forming an assembly of twelve companions to tackle the service of planetary regeneration.

And from the very first day of the Good News, He invites, insists, and appeals to souls to become instruments of His Divine Will, making us realize that redemption proceeds from on High, but will not materialize among creatures without the active collaboration of well-meaning hearts.

Even when He appears personally, seeking someone for His labor of light, as happened in the conversion of Paul, the Master does not dispense with the cooperation of incarnate servants. After visiting the doctor of Tarsus directly, He seeks out Ananias, sending him to succor the new disciple.

Why did Jesus take the trouble to accompany the newly converted, assisting him in person? It is because, just as Humanity cannot enlighten and progress without Christ, Christ does not dispense with men in the work of uplifting and sublimating the world.
“Go and preach.”
“Behold, I send you forth.”
“Let your light so shine before men.”
“The harvest truly is great, but the laborers are few.”
Such statements by the Lord prove the importance He attributes to human contribution.
Let us love and work, always purifying and serving.
Wherever a follower of the Gospel is, there is found a messenger of the Celestial Friend for the incessant work of the good.
Christianity means Christ and us.

messages.title: Labeling
paragraphs: “Now if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he is not His.” — PAUL (Romans, 8:9)
Labeling does not bring peace. Let us seek the essence.
There are praises in memory of Christ on many banners that stimulate animosity among brothers.
There are symbols of Christ in numerous tribunals that, on many occasions, merely exalt injustice.
There are precious references to Christ in highly categorized voices of earthly culture who, in the name of the Gospel, seek to spread misery and ignorance.
There are oaths by Christ through conversations that constitute vast corridors toward darkness.
There are verbal invocations of Christ in purely commercial operations that are dark assaults on the harmony of conscience.
Let us meditate on the extent of our moral duties, in the circle of responsibilities we embrace with the Christian faith.

Jesus remains in images, posters, flags, medals, ornaments, songs, poems, narratives, speeches, sermons, studies, and disputes, but this is very little if we do not possess His living teaching in conscience and heart.
It is always easy to express enthusiasm and conviction, brilliant vows, and well-crafted phrases.
Let us, however, guard against the danger of mere labeling. With the apostle, let us not forget that if we do not possess the Spirit of Christ, we are still considerably distant from Him.

messages.title: Testimony
paragraphs: “For to this you were called, because Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example, that you should follow His steps.” — PETER (1 Peter, 2.21)
Many complain about the moral struggle in which they feel involved after accepting the Gospel.
Along different paths, they feel changed.
They no longer plunge into the dark currents of vanity.
They no longer take pleasure in pride.
They no longer sympathize with selfishness.
They no longer worship discord.
And therefore, with unbound souls, having lost old wrappers of illusion, they recognize that their sensitivity becomes sharpened, aggravating their afflictions in their earthly journey.

They feel exposed to a painful process of refinement and admit to suffering, more than others, anguished trials. But, in the spiritual sublimation to which they bear testimony, other children of Earth come into contact with the Good News, discovering the excellences of the Christian life and extending its divine light.

If we find ourselves, then, in extreme mismatches in our inner life, facing the problems raised by our faith, let us know how to courageously overcome the conflicts of the path, always choosing the sacrifice of ourselves in favor of the general good, since we were not brought into communion with Jesus simply for the act of believing, but to contribute to the extension of the Kingdom of God at the price of our own renewal.

Let no one retreat in the face of suffering. Let us learn to use it in building a more efficient life, in fruits of peace and light, service and fraternity, good cheer and joy, because, according to the Gospel, “to this we were called,” with the example of the Divine Master, who renounced for our benefit, leaving us the standard of spiritual height that it is incumbent upon us to attain.

messages.title: Before the Liberating Christ
paragraphs: “I am the door.” — JESUS (John, 10.7)
According to lexicons, the word “door” designates “an opening in a wall, at ground level or at the base of a floor, offering entrance and exit.”
However, symbolically, the world is full of deceptive doors. They provide entry without offering an exit.
Some of them are avidly contested by men who, eager to conquer ephemeral possessions, do not guard against the dangers they represent.
Many knock at the door of coined wealth and, after being welcomed, wake up imprisoned in the torments of usury.
Countless people force their way into the illusion of human power and awaken detained by the claws of suffering.
Very many cross the portal of earthly pleasures and find themselves, from one moment to the next, in the meshes of affliction and death.
Many breach the thresholds of public prominence, thirsty for popularity and influence, ending up walled up in the dungeon of despair.
Christ, however, is the door of Abundant Life.
With Him, we submit to the designs of the Heavenly Father and, in this direction, we accept existence as learning and service, in favor of our own growth toward Immortality.
See, then, to which door you resort in the daily struggle, because only through the teaching of Christ will you reach the path of true liberation.

messages.title: Before the Light of Truth
paragraphs: “You shall know the truth, and the truth shall set you free.” — JESUS (John, 8.32)
The Master's word is clear and secure.
We will not be liberated by “aspects of the truth” or by the “provisional truths” that we may hold within the circle of passionate assertions to which we incline.

Many, in politics, philosophy, science, and religion, become attached to certain angles of truth and transform their own lives into a trench of desperate struggle under the guise of defending it, when they are nothing more than prisoners of their “point of view.”
Many accept the truth, extend its lessons, advocate its cause, and proclaim its merits; however, the liberating truth is that which we know in the incessant activity of the Eternal Good.
Penetrating it is understanding the obligations that fall upon us.
Discernering it is renewing one's own understanding and converting existence into a field of responsibility toward the best.
There is only true freedom in submission to faithfully fulfilled duty.
To know the truth, therefore, is to perceive the meaning of life. And to perceive the meaning of life is to grow in constant service and refinement.
Observe, in this way, your position before the Light…
He who merely glimpses the blinding glory of reality talks a lot and acts less. He who, however, penetrates its indefinable greatness, acts more and talks less.

messages.title: Outstretched Hands
paragraphs: “Stretch out your hand. And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored as whole as the other.” — (Mark, 3.5)
In all houses of religious faith, there are believers with outstretched hands, begging for help… Afflicted souls reveal anxiety, weakness, hopelessness, and heart ailments.
Are we not all, incarnate and disincarnate, asking something of Divine Providence, similar to the man who had the withered hand?
Trapped in the labyrinth created by ourselves, here we are, claiming the help of the Divine Master… However, it is wise to ponder our attitude.
It is fair to ask, and no one can restrict any manifestations of humility, repentance, or intercession. But it is essential to examine the way of receiving.
Many people await the materialized response of Jesus.
This one expects money, that one counts on sudden social prominence, that other one demands the immediate transformation of circumstances on the earthly path…
Let us observe, however, the Master's help to the paralytic.
Jesus instructs him to stretch out his withered hand, and once stretched out, He does not bestow bags of gold or privilege tokens upon him. He heals it. He returns the opportunity for service to him.
The hand recovered at that moment remains as empty as before.

It is because Christ was restoring to him the blessed opportunity to work, conquering sacred accomplishments by himself; He was sending him back to the redemptive labors of the good, in which it was up to him to build and aggrandize himself.
The lesson is expressive for all temples of the Christian community.

When you stretch out your hands to the Lord, do not expect facilities, gold, prerogatives… Learn to receive His assistance, because Divine Love will restore your energies, but it will not provide you with any escape from the achievements of your own effort.

messages.title: Change
paragraphs: “But they did not receive Him, because His face was set like one journeying to Jerusalem.” — (Luke, 9.53)
Worthy of note is this passage from Luke. Observing that Jesus and the disciples were heading to Jerusalem, the Samaritans refused to receive them.
They identified them by their appearance. If they were travelers bound for other places, perhaps they would offer them lodging, comfort, joy…
Does not the same phenomenon occur to this day with the true followers of the Master?
Jerusalem, for us, symbolizes here the “testimony of faith.”
And it suffices for someone to resolutely head toward such a spiritual domain for ordinary, disoriented, and argumentative men to close the doors of their hearts to them.
The careless, who head in the direction of easy pleasures, find immediate welcome among the new Samaritans of the world.
Restless women, deceitful men, and well-groomed spiritual invalids possess, for now, on Earth, a shining assembly of companions.

However, when the apprentice of Jesus wakes up on the human road, realizing that it is essential to bear testimony to his trust in God through the denial of old caprices, most of the time he is constrained to walk on with no one.
It is because, usually on such occasions, man reveals himself changed.
He does not give the common impression of a creature disposed to please himself.
He is someone resolved to renounce his own defects and nullify them, through blows of immense effort, to embrace the redemptive cross that will identify him with the Divine Master…

For this reason, even within the doors of the home, almost always he will not be fully recognized, because his aspect has undergone a deep metamorphosis… He shows the sign of one who has taken the course of definitive inner renewal toward God, willing to consecrate himself to the eternal good and uplift his heart on the great path…

messages.title: Need for the Good
paragraphs: “And let us consider one another in order to stir up love and good works.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 10.24)
Many institutions of the Christian life, respectable for their programs and foundations, suffer incalculable damage due to the levity with which many companions observe one another.
Here, the disgraceful past of someone trying to recover with dignity today is discussed; there, small unhappy gestures are analyzed through the dark lenses of sarcasm and criticism…

Indiscriminate censure and disapproval, however, pour into the family of the ideal like corrosive rain on a plantation, annihilating nascent germs, destroying lush flowers, and poisoning fruits destined for the granaries of common progress.
It is never too much to repeat the need for forgiveness, kindness, and optimism in our ranks and activities.
Let us remember that, with our help, everything today can be better than yesterday, and everything tomorrow will be better than today.
Evil, under any circumstance, is disharmony before the Law, and all imbalance results in difficulty and suffering.
Let us examine one another, lighting the flame of fraternity so that fraternity may illuminate our destinies.

Without perseverance in the good, there is no path to happiness. For this very reason, the Apostle Paul recommended to us: — “and let us consider one another in order to stir up love and good works,” because only in this direction will we be serving the construction of the Kingdom of Love.

messages.title: Wealth for Heaven
paragraphs: “Lay up for yourselves treasures in Heaven…” — JESUS (Matthew, 6.20)
Whoever grieves unduly upon seeing the triumph and prosperity of many merciless and selfish men, deep down displays envy, revolt, ambition, and hopelessness.
It must not be so! After all, who can say that they retain the advantages of Earth with due merit?
If we observe men and women, devoid of any moral scruple, holding the transitory values of the world, let us instead feel sorry for them.
The word of Christ is clear and irrefutable. — “Lay up for yourselves treasures in Heaven” — the Lord told us.
This means “let us accumulate inner values to commune with eternal glory”!
Ephemeral will always be the gallery of carnal prominence.
Physical beauty, temporary power, passing property, and coined fortune may be simple attributes of the human mask, which tireless time transforms.
Let us amass goodness and culture, understanding and sympathy.
Without the treasure of personal education, our penetration into the Heavens is useless, since we would be orphans of attunement to respond to the appeals of the Higher Life.

Let us grow in virtue and incorporate true wisdom, because tomorrow we will be visited by the leveling hand of death and we will possess solely the noble or debased qualities that we have installed within ourselves.

messages.title: Reverence and Piety
paragraphs: “Let us serve God acceptably, with reverence and godly fear.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 12.28)
“Let us serve God cheerfully” — requests the apostle —, but he does not forget to emphasize the manner in which it behooves us to serve Him.
We could not spread sadness in the tasks of the good. All elements of Nature obey the Laws of the Lord, revealing joy.
The constellation shines within the night.
The Sun overflows with heat and light.
The Earth covers itself with flowers and greenery.
The fountain has a peculiar song.
The bird sings melodies of praise.
It would not be fair, then, to bring pessimism and bitterness to the service assigned to us by the Master.
The contentment of helping is one of the signs of our faith. However, it is necessary that our joy does not run wild into excesses.
Neither inappropriate noise nor improper concepts.
Neither less-than-worthy words nor laughter that might merely suggest sarcasm and contempt.
Let us serve cheerfully, with reverence and piety. Reverence toward the Lord and piety toward our neighbor.
You cannot personalize the All-Merciful to please Him, but you can serve Him daily in the person of your struggling brethren.
Let us thus steer the chariot of our work upon the tracks of respect and charity, and we will find in our favor the joy that never fades.

messages.title: Let Us Look at Our Hands
paragraphs: “…He showed them His hands…” — (John, 20.20)
Reappearing to the disciples after death, Jesus, upon identifying Himself, lets them see His wounded body, prominently showing them His hands…

The hands that had restored sight to the blind, raised the paralyzed, healed the sick, and blessed the elderly and children bore the marks of sacrifice. Pierced by the nails of the cross, they recalled His supreme renunciation.
The hands of the Divine Worker did not reap from the world merely calluses from intensive effort in the plow of the good. They received bloody and painful wounds…
The lesson reminds us of the activity of hands in every corner of the Globe.
The heart inspires. The brain thinks. The hands accomplish.
Everywhere, human life stirs through hands that command and obey.
Hands that direct, that build, that sow, that caress, that help, and that teach… And hands that kill, that wound, that stone, that beat, that set fire, that curse…
We all possess living antennas in our hands through which our spiritual life is exteriorized.

Reflect, then, on what you do each day. Do not forget that, beyond death, our hands exhibit the signs of our passage through Earth. Those of Christ, the Eternal Benefactor, revealed the scars obtained in the divine tillage of love. Yours, tomorrow, will likewise speak of you in the spiritual world, where, once earthly experience is interrupted, each creature gathers the blessings or lessons of life, according to their own works.

messages.title: Not Only
paragraphs: “Man shall not live by bread alone.” — JESUS (Matthew, 4.4)
Not only clothing to protect the body, but also the refuge of superior knowledge that strengthens the soul.
Not only the beauty of the facial mask, but equally the loveliness and nobility of feelings.
Not just the eugenics that improves muscles, but also the education that refines manners.
Not only surgery that eradicates the organic defect, but equally one's own effort that nullifies the inner defect.
Not only a comfortable home for physical life, but also the invisible house of edifying principles in which the Spirit becomes useful, esteemed, and respectable.
Not just honorable titles that illustrate transient personality, but equally proven virtues, in objective struggle, that enrich the eternal conscience.
Not only clarity for mortal eyes, but also divine light for imperishable understanding.
Not only a pleasant aspect, but equally living usefulness.
Not just flowers, but also fruits.
Not only continued teaching, but equally active demonstration.
Not only excellent theory, but also sanctifying practice.
Not just us, but equally others.
The Master said: — “Man shall not live by bread alone.”
Let us apply this sublime concept to the immense field of the world.
Good taste, harmony, and dignity in outer life constitute a duty, but let us not forget the purity, elevation, and sublime resources of inner life, with which we head toward Eternity.

messages.title: Christmas
paragraphs: “Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men.” — (Luke, 2.14)
The angelic legions, beside the Manger, announcing the Great Renewing Agent, did not present any word of violence.
Glory to God in the Divine Universe. Peace on Earth. Good will toward Men.
The Supreme Father, bequeathing the new era of security and tranquility to the world, did not declare the Celestial Ambassador invested with powers to wound or destroy.
No punishment for the greedy rich man.
No penalty for the desperate poor man.
No contempt for the weak.
No condemnation for sinners.
No hostility toward the proud Pharisee.
No anathema against the unconscious Gentile.
The Divine Treasure poured out, through the hands of Jesus, for the service of Good Will.
The justice of “an eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth” finally found Love willing to make a sublime renunciation even unto the cross.
Men and animals, astonished before the rising light in the stable, marked inexpressible joy... From that unforgettable moment on, the Earth would be renewed.
The torturer would be worthy of pity.
The enemy would be converted into a stray brother.
The criminal would pass to the condition of the sick.

In Rome, the people would gradually extinguish the slaughter in the circuses. In Sidon, slaves would no longer have their eyes gouged out by the cruelty of their masters. In Jerusalem, the sick would no longer be relegated to abandonment in the valleys of filth.
Jesus brought with Him the message of true fraternity and, revealing it, journeyed victoriously from the straw cradle to the bloody tree.
Brother, you who hear in Christmas the soft echoes of the miraculous song of the angels, remember that the Master came to us so that we may love one another.
Christmas! Good News! Good Will!…
Let us extend sympathy to all and begin to truly live with Jesus, under the splendors of a new day.
messages.note: This is the 17th lesson of the book “Antologia Mediúnica do Natal” (Mediumistic Anthology of Christmas), published by FEB in 1966.

messages.title: Feed
paragraphs: “Feed my sheep.” — JESUS (John, 21.17)
Significant is the appeal of the Divine Shepherd to the loving heart of Simon Peter to continue His apostolate.
Observing in Humanity His immense flock, Jesus does not recommend drastic measures in favor of compulsory discipline.
No shouts, no insults.
No chain, no gallows.
No whip, no rod.
No punishment, no imposition.
No abandonment of the unfortunate, no scourging of the strayed.
No lamentation, no despair.
“Peter, feed my sheep!” This is equivalent to saying: — Brother, sustain your companions who are more needy than yourself.
Do not be discouraged in the face of rebellion, nor condemn error, from which the beneficial lesson will arise later. Help your neighbor, instead of lashing them.
Educate always. Reveal yourself as a faithful worker.
Be demanding with yourself and support the sickly and fragile hearts that accompany your steps.
If you plant good, time will take care of germination, development, blossoming, and fruiting at the opportune moment.
Do not analyze by destroying. The inexperienced of today may be the mentor of tomorrow.
Nourish the “good part” of your brother and move forward. Life will turn evil into debris and the Lord will do the rest.

messages.title: Difference
paragraphs: “You believe that there is one God. You do well. Even the demons believe—and tremble!” — (JAMES, 2.19)
The apostle's warning is of essential importance in the spiritual admonition.
Expecting benefits from Heaven is an attitude common to all.
Adoring the Lord can be the work of the just and the unjust.
Admitting the existence of the Divine Government is a dominant trait of all creatures.
Accepting Supreme Power is proper to the good and the bad.
James was divinely inspired in this verse because his words define the difference between believing in God and doing His Sublime Will.
Intelligence is an attribute of all. Cognition stems from experience.
The living being always evolves, and whoever evolves learns and knows.
The differentiation between the genius of evil and the genius of good lies in the direction of knowledge.
The demon, as a symbol of wickedness, executes his own desires, often delusional and dark. The angel identifies with the designs of the Eternal and fulfills them wherever he is.
Remember, therefore, that the religious school to which you affiliate is not enough for the problem of personal happiness to reach the desired solution.
Adoring the Lord, hoping and believing in Him are characteristic attitudes of everyone.

The only sign that will reveal to you the noblest condition will be imprinted in the action you develop in life in order to execute His designs, because, in truth, it does not help perfection much to believe in the good that will come from the Lord, but rather the diligence in practicing good, today, here and now, in His name.

messages.title: Majority
paragraphs: “…The lesser is blessed by the greater.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 7.7)
In all activities of life, there are those who reach natural majority among their relatives, companions, or contemporaries.
There are those who become greater in physical experience, knowledge, virtue, or competence.
In general, however, whoever finds themselves elevated to any level of superiority tends to use the situation to forget their debt to the common spirit.
Often, whoever achieves financial majority becomes greedy, whoever finds scientific prominence becomes vain, and whoever finds themselves in the gallery of power embraces vain pride.
The Law of Life, however, does not recommend exclusivism and separatism.
According to divine principles, all legitimate progress turns into blessings for the entire community.
Nature itself offers sublime lessons in this sense.
The tree grows for fruiting. The spring grows for the benefit of the soil.
If you have grown in experience or elevation of any kind, remember the fraternal communion with all.
The Sun, with its rays of light, does not forsake the muddy cave and does not disdain the worm. Development is power.

Observe how you employ the advantages that have been added to your existence. The Highest Spirit of all who have ever manifested on Earth accepted supreme sacrifice in order to help everyone, unconditionally.
Do not forget that, according to the Divine Statute, the “lesser is blessed by the greater”.

messages.title: The Retribution
paragraphs: “Then Peter answered and said to Him, ‘See, we have left all and followed You. Therefore what shall we have?’” — (MATTHEW, 19.27)
The apostle's question expresses the attitude of many hearts in religious temples.
Man consecrates himself to a certain circle of faith and immediately cries out: — “What shall I receive?”
The answer, however, pours out silently through life itself.
What does the ripe grain receive after the harvest?
The crusher that helps it purify itself.
What prize is reserved for the white and noble flour?
The leaven that transforms it for general utility.
What privilege characterizes the bread after the oven?
The grace to serve.
Christians are not formed to be living ornaments of the world, but for the regenerating and sanctifying action of existence.

Formerly, the servants of human royalty received the spoils of the vanquished and, with them, surrounded themselves with gratifications of a physical nature, with which they shortened their own death.
In Christ, however, the picture is different. We conquer, in His company, to become brothers to all who share our experience, keeping the obligation to support them and be useful to them.

Simon Peter, who wished to know what his reward would be for adhering to the Good News, saw up close the necessity of his own renunciation. The more his faith kindled, the greater testimonies of love to Humanity were required of him. The more knowledge he acquired, the more extensive charity was compelled of him, unto extreme sacrifice.

If you have left, therefore, out of devotion to Jesus, the ties that bound you to the lower zones of life, remember that, to your happiness, you received from Heaven the honor of helping, the prerogative of understanding, and the glory of serving.
messages.note: This message was originally published in 1952 by LAKE and is the 40th of the 1st Part of the book “Cartas do Coração” (Letters from the Heart)

messages.title: Before the Sublime
paragraphs: “What God has cleansed you must not call common.” — (ACTS, 10.15)
There are expressions in the Gospel that, like flowers standing out on a divine branch, must be removed from the whole so that we may be dazzled by their peculiar brilliance and perfume.
The celestial voice, which addresses Simon Peter in Acts, encompasses horizons much vast than the individual problem of the apostle.
Ordinary man is surrounded by glories on Earth, yet he considers himself in a field of vulgarities, incapable of valuing the riches that surround him.

Blind before the superb spectacle of life that frames his development, he tramples upon the treasures of the world, without meditating on the patient effort of the centuries that Infinite Wisdom used in the improvement and selection of the values that surround him.
How many millennia must the formation of the rock have required?
How many ingredients harmonize in the elaboration of a single ray of sun?
How many obstacles were overcome for the flower to materialize?
How much effort did the domestication of trees and animals cost?
How many centuries must the Patience of Heaven have employed in the complex structuring of the organic machine in which the incarnate Spirit manifests?
Reason is gradual light before the sublime.

Do not forget, my brother, that the Lord has placed your earthly experience in a true paradise, where the tiny seed repays on the average of infinity by one, and where waters and flowers, soil and atmosphere invite you to produce in favor of the multiplication of Eternal Treasures.
Each day, praise the Lord who has graced you with valuable opportunities and divine gifts… Think, study, work, and serve.
Do not suppose common what God has purified and magnified.

messages.title: By Works
paragraphs: “And to esteem them very highly in love for their work's sake.” — PAUL (1 Thessalonians, 5.13)
This passage by Paul, in the First Epistle to the Thessalonians, is singularly expressive for our daily struggle.

We all experience the tendency to consecrate the greatest esteem only to those who read life by the primer of our points of view. Our devotion is always warm toward those who espouse our ways of seeing, our ingrained habits, and our social principles; however, our interpretations are not always the best, our customs the noblest, and our guidelines the most commendable.

From this comes the imperative to disintegrate the shell of our selfishness in order to dedicate our friendship and respect to companions, not by the affectionate servitude with which they bind themselves to our personal path, but by the fidelity with which they guide themselves in favor of the common good.
If we love someone solely for physical beauty, we will likely find the object of our affection tomorrow on the way to the trash heap.
If we esteem in a friend only brilliant oratory, it is possible he may be in afflictive muteness very soon.
If we consecrate ourselves to a certain creature only because they obey us blindly, we are likely provoking the fall of others into the same errors in which we have fallen so many times.
It is imperative to improve our way of seeing and feeling in order to advance toward superior life.

Let us seek creatures, above all, by the works with which they benefit the time and space in which we move, because one day we will understand that the best is rarely the one who agrees with us, but is always the one who agrees with the Lord, collaborating with Him in the improvement of life, inside and outside of us.

messages.title: In the Gifts of Christ
paragraphs: “But to each one of us grace was given according to the measure of Christ's gift.” — PAUL (Ephesians, 4.7)
The human soul, in these twenty centuries of Christianity, is a conscience enlightened by reason, in full battle for the conquest of illuminating values.
The field of struggle remains situated in our intimate life. Animality versus spirituality.
Millennia of crystallized shadows against the rising light.

And man, little by little, between the alternatives of life and death, rebirth in the body and return to spiritual activity, molds in himself the sublime qualities indispensable to ascension, which, deep down, constitute the virtues of Christ, progressive in each of us.
Hence the reason why divine grace occupies human existence or grows within it, to the extent that the gifts of Jesus—incipient, reduced, regular, or enormous—can express themselves in it.
Wherever you are, whatever you are, seek to acclimatize Christian qualities within yourself, with the watchful attention given to the cultivation of precious plants near the home.
Regarding the Earth, we are all susceptible to producing for good or for evil.

Let us offer the Divine Cultivator the vessel of the heart, remembering that if the “conscious soil” of our Spirit accepts the seeds of the Celestial Fruitgrower, every crumb of our good will will be converted into a miraculous channel for the exteriorization of good, with the permanent multiplication of the Lord's graces around us.
Observe your “good part” and remember that you can expand it to Infinity.
Do not attempt to destroy millennia of darkness from one moment to the next. Avail yourself of the effort of self-improvement each day.
Persist in learning from the Master of Love and Renunciation.
Let us not forget that Divine Grace will occupy our individual space to the extent of our real growth in the gifts of Christ.

messages.title: Worker Without Faith
paragraphs: “…And I will show you my faith by my works.” — (JAMES, 2.18)
Everywhere, we see the worker without faith, spreading restlessness and discouragement.
He devotes himself to a certain charity enterprise and abandons it at the outset, murmuring: — “What's the use? The world is no good.”
He commits to common duties and, without any sign of persistence, resigns from edifying obligations, alleging: — “I was not born for dishonorable servility.”
He approaches religious faith to enjoy its benefits, however, soon after, relegates it to oblivion, asserting: — “All this is lies and complication.”
If invited to a position of prominence, he repeats the old refrain: — “I don't deserve it! I am unworthy!…”
If brought to testimonies of humility, he affirms under manifest revolt: — “Who offends me like this?”
And he moves from situation to situation, between lamentation and indiscipline, with plenty of time to feel persecuted and disregarded.
Everywhere, he is the worker who does not finish the service he became responsible for, or the student who studies continuously without ever learning the lesson.
Do not concentrate on faith without works, which constitutes a dangerous intoxication of the soul; however, do not consecrate yourself to action without faith in Divine Power and in your own effort.

The servant who trusts in the Law of Life recognizes that all patrimonies and glories of the Universe belong to God. In view of this, he passes through the world under the light of enthusiasm and action in incessant good, completing the small and large tasks that fall to him, without falling in love with himself in vanity and without enslaving himself to the creations of which he has been a fortunate instrument.
Let us reveal our faith through our works in common happiness, and the Lord will confer upon our life the indefinable addition of love and wisdom, beauty and power.

messages.title: Destruction and Misery
paragraphs: “Destruction and misery are in their ways.” — PAUL (Romans, 3.16)

When the disciple distances himself from trust in the Master and shuns action along the lines of the example that His divine apostolado bequeathed to us, preferring the vast path of infidelity to his own conscience, he digs, without realizing it, wide abysses of destruction and misery wherever he passes.
If he crystallizes his mind in idleness, he eliminates good cheer in the hearts of the workers around him and strangles his own opportunities to serve.
If he descends to the ravine of denial, he destroys tender hopes in the feeling of those who approach the faith and weaves a vast web of shadows for himself.
If he transfers his soul to the dark residence of vice, he suffocates nascent virtues in his fellow journeyers and acquires heavy debts for the future.
If he harbors despair, he extinguishes the faint gleam of trust in the soul of his neighbor and weeps uselessly under the storm of destructive tears.
If he seeks refuge in the cold house of sadness, he asphyxiates optimism in those who accompany him and loses the wealth of time in fruitless lamentations.
The divine determination for the Gospel learner is to move forward, helping, understanding, and serving everyone.
To stall is to immobilize others and freeze oneself.
To revolt is to lash brothers and wound oneself.
To flee from good is to disorient fellow beings and annihilate oneself.

Wretched are those who do not follow the Master they found, because to know Jesus Christ in spirit and live far from Him is to spread destruction around our steps and preserve misery within ourselves.

messages.title: Something
paragraphs: “Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick.” — JESUS (Luke, 5.31)
Whoever knows how to read, let them not forget to support the one who has not yet learned.
Whoever possesses enlightened speech should help their companion, teaching them the science of correct and expressive phrasing.
Whoever enjoys organic balance should not despise the possibility of helping the sick.

Whoever has managed to kindle some light of faith in their own spirit should patiently support the unhappy person who has not yet opened themselves to the slightest notion of responsibility before the Lord, helping them to break away from the darkness.
Whoever has resources to work should not forget the brother less adjusted to service, leading him, whenever possible, to a dignified activity.
Whoever esteems the practice of charity should take pity on hardened souls, benefiting them with the vibrations of prayer.
Whoever is already treasuring humility should not distance themselves from the proud person, granting them, through example, the indispensable elements for readjustment.
Whoever is the holder of goodness should not refuse assistance to the wicked, since wickedness invariably results from revolt or ignorance.
Whoever is in the company of peace should help the desperate.
Whoever keeps joy should share the grace of contentment with the sad.
The Lord asserted that the well need no physician, but rather the sick.

Remember those who pass through the world amidst difficulties greater than yours. Life does not demand your total sacrifice in favor of others, but, for your own benefit, do not disdain doing something toward the extension of common happiness.

messages.title: Let Us Serve
paragraphs: “Serving with goodwill, as to the Lord, and not to men.” — PAUL (Ephesians, 6.7)

If you legislate, but do not apply the Law according to the designs of the Lord, who considers the needs of all, you walk among dangerous abysses dug by your own untamed creations, without reaping the benefits of your glorious mission in the collective order.

If you administer, but do not observe the interests of the Lord upon the road where you move in the position of steward of life, you suffer the threat of burying your heart in dark whims, without enjoying the blessings of the function you exercise in the public ministry.

If you judge your fellows and are not inspired by the Lord, who knows all the particularities and circumstances of the processes in transit through the courts, you live in the probability of falling spectacularly onto the very path taken by those you hastily judge, without extracting for your own benefit the wisdom that Justice preserves in your intelligence.

If you work in color or marble, in the word or in melody, without translating into your works the correction, love, and light of the Lord, you bear the tremendous responsibility of one who establishes delusive images for the consumption of the popular mind, losing in vain the glory that enriches your feelings.

If you were called to obedience in the structuring of utilities for the world, without the spirit of understanding with the Lord, who helped creatures by loving them even unto personal sacrifice, you live among the phantoms of indiscipline and discouragement, without fixing within yourself the divine clarity of the talent that rests in your hands.
Friend, the passage through Earth is a sublime learning.
Work is always the instructor of perfection. Let us serve without attaching ourselves.

In every place of the human valley, there are resources of action and betterment for those who wish to move forward. Let us serve everywhere with goodwill, as to the Lord and not to creatures, and the Lord will lead us to the heights of life.

messages.title: Educate
paragraphs: “Do you not know that you are the temple of God and that the Spirit of God dwells in you?” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 3.16)
In the tiny seed resides the germ of the beneficent trunk. In the heart of the earth are the melodies of the spring. In the block of stone are the masterpieces of statuary.
Meanwhile, the orchard demands active effort. The crystalline stream asks for aqueducts to transport itself uncontaminated. The sculpted jewel asks for the miracles of the chisel.
The spirit also brings with it the gene of Divinity.

God is in us, just as we are in God. But for the divine light to stand out from human darkness, it is necessary that the educational processes of life work upon us along the stony path of the millennia.
Only a heart ennobled in great understanding can pour forth sanctifying heroism.
Only a cultivated brain can produce enlightened forms of thought.
Only spiritual greatness manages to generate balanced speech, the sublime verb, and the balm-giving voice.
Let us interpret pain and labor as celestial artists of our purification.
Educate, and you will transform irrationality into intelligence, intelligence into humanity, and humanity into angelitude. Educate, and you will build paradise on Earth.
If we know that the Lord dwells in us, let us perfect our lives in order to manifest Him.

messages.title: Farmers
paragraphs: “The hardworking farmer must be the first to partake of the fruits.” — PAUL (2 Timothy, 2.6)
There are farmers of every kind. There are those who buy the field and exploit it through sweating tenant farmers, never touching the soil with their own hands.
We find in many places those who leave the hoe to rust, crossing their arms and blaming the rain or the sun for the failure of the sowing they do not watch over.
We are confronted by many who inspect their neighbors' planting without any attention to the work that concerns them.
We have several who talk nonsense concerning a thousand useless things, while destructive worms annihilate the fragile flowers.
We see numerous people accusing the earth of being incapable of any production, yet denying the glebe entrusted to them the blessing of a drop of water and the help of fertilizer.
We observe many who claim to be possessed by a headache, a cold, or a indisposition and lose the sublime opportunity to sow.
Nature, however, repays all of them with disillusionment, difficulty, denial, and disappointment.
But the farmer who truly works soon gathers the grace of the full barn. And so it is in the cultivation of the spirit.
No one will achieve an excellent result without striving, giving to the work of good the best of themselves.

Paul of Tarsus, writing in an era of masters and slaves, of superficiality and favoritism, does not tell us that the sower distinguished by Caesar or the wealthiest would be the rightful owner of the harvest, but asserted, with indisputable accuracy, that the farmer dedicated to his own duties will be the first to benefit from the advantages of the fruit.

messages.title: The Good Portion
paragraphs: “Mary has chosen the good portion, which will not be taken away from her.” — JESUS (Luke, 10.42)
Do not forget the “good portion” that resides in all creatures and in all things.
Fire destroys, but it carries within itself the purifying element.
Stone is blunt, but it consolidates security.
The gale lashes mercilessly, yet it helps renewal.
The torrent is filth, however, it usually carries the fertilizer indispensable to victorious sowing.
Likewise, there are creatures who, while revealing themselves as negative in certain sectors of human struggle, are extremely valuable in others.
Unilateral appreciation is always ruinous.
Complete imperfection, just as integral perfection, does not exist on the plane where we evolve.
The criminal, accused by everyone, tomorrow may be the nurse who hands you a cup of water.
The companion in whom you now discover a streak of darkness may later be the sublimated brother who invites you to good example.
The storm of the hour we live in is often the source of well-being for the hours we are going to live.
Let us seek the better side of situations, events, and people.

“Mary has chosen the good portion, which will not be taken away from her” — the Lord told us. Let us assimilate the essence of the divine lesson. Whoever seeks the “good portion” and dwells in it reaps in the field of life the spiritual treasure that will never be stolen from them.

messages.title: To Raise and Help
paragraphs: “And he gave her his hand and raised her up…” — (ACTS, 9.41)
Very significant is the lesson in Acts when Peter restores sister Dorcas to life.
The apostle is not content with pronouncing beautiful words to her ears, renewing her general strengths. He gives her his hand so that she may rise.

The teaching is highly symbolic. We observe many companions rising again to knowledge, joy, and virtue, bathed in the divine clarity of the Master, and who can lift thousands of creatures to the Higher Sphere.
For this, however, pure and simple preaching will not suffice.

The sermon is truly a sublime appeal which Christ Himself did not forgo, but we cannot forget that the Celestial Friend, if He taught on the mountain, likewise on the mountain multiplied the loaves for the hungry crowd, restoring their courage.
We, who found ourselves dead in ignorance, and who today, by the addition of Infinite Mercy, can already enjoy some blessings of light, need to extend relief service to others.
We will not discharge our salvationist task, however, simply by pronouncing a few admirable speeches.
It is imperative to use our hands in the works of good. The effort of the arms means personal activity.

Without the commitment of our energies to the construction of the Spiritual Kingdom with Christ on Earth, in vain shall we align excellent observations around the preciosities of the Good News or the needs of human redemption.

Finding our brother fallen on the road, let us do our utmost to awaken him with the resources of the transforming word, but let us not forget that to bring him back to constructive life, it will be indispensable, according to Peter's unforgettable lesson, to extend our hands to him fraternally.

messages.title: Let Us Keep Watch
paragraphs: “...but to those who are defiled and unbelieving nothing is pure.” — PAUL (Titus, 1.15)
Man always sees through inner vision. With the colors he uses inside, he judges external aspects.
By what he feels, he examines the feelings of others. In the conduct of others, he supposes he finds the means and ends of actions peculiar to himself.
Hence, the imperative of great vigilance so that our conscience is not contaminated by evil.
When shadow wanders in our mind, we glimpse nothing but shadows everywhere.
Alongside manifestations of the purest love, we imagine carnal hallucinations.
If we encounter a companion dressed with praiseworthy neatness, we think of vanity.
Before a friend called to a public career, we mentalize political tyranny.
If the neighbor knows how to save with perfect use of opportunity, we fixate on them with suspicion and usually weave long reflections around undue appropriations.
When we hear a friend in righteous defense, using the energy proper to them, we immediately relegate them to the category of the intractable.

When darkness spreads within the intimacy of our life, deplorable alterations afflict our thoughts. Virtues, under these circumstances, are never seen. Evils, however, always abound. The broadest gestures of blessing receive lamentable interpretations.
Let us keep watch every time we are visited by envy, jealousy, suspicion, or backbiting.

There are intricate cases in which silence is the blessed and effective remedy, because, undoubtedly, each Spirit observes the path or the traveler according to the clear or dark vision at their disposal.

messages.title: Let Us Extend the Good
paragraphs: “Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.” — PAUL (Romans, 12.21)
Notice that, right in the house of Nature, all elements, in the face of evil, offer the best they possess for the readjustment of harmony and the victory of good.
When the storm seems to have destroyed the entire landscape, the divine forces of life gather for the work of rebuilding.
The Sun sends light over the mud, healing the wounds of the ground.
The wind caresses the trees and dries their branches.
The song of the birds replaces the voice of thunder.
The plain receives the torrent without rebelling and converts it into precious fertilizer.
The air that bears the weight of the clouds and the shock of the destructive spark returns to lightness and softness.
The tree with broken or injured fronds regenerates in silence in order to produce new flowers and new fruits.
The earth, our common mother, periodically suffers the hail storm and the mud bath, yet this does not stop it from magnifying the good more and more.
Why should we, in turn, keep the gall and bitterness of evil within the intimacy of our heart? Let us learn to receive the visit of adversity, educating its energies for the benefit of life.
Ignorance is merely a great night that will yield to the sun of wisdom.
Use the treasure of your love in all directions, and let us extend the good everywhere.

The spring, when touched by mud, never admits defeat. It welcomes the debris into its own bosom and, continuing to flow, transforms them into blessings along the course of its waters, which continue running with gentleness and humility for the benefit of all.

messages.title: Enlightening Affirmation
paragraphs: “And you are not willing to come to Me that you may have life.” — JESUS (John, 5.40)
Those who seek the sublimation of individuality need to understand the supreme value of willpower in self-improvement.
The temples and schools of Christianity remain filled with learners who glimpse the divine powers of Jesus and recognize His magnanimity, yet walk at the mercy of cruel vacillations.
They believe and disbelieve, they help and unhelp, they organize and disturb, they enlighten themselves in faith and darken themselves in mistrust...
It is because they hope for the Lord's protection to enjoy immediate contentment in the body, but they do not want to go to Him to take hold of eternal life.

They ask for the miracle from Christ's hands, but do not accept His guidelines. They ask for His comforting presence, yet do not follow His steps. They intend to hear Him by the serene lake in lectures of hope and comfort, however, they refuse to share with Him the service of the road through sacrifice for the victory of good. They court Him in Jerusalem adorned with flowers, but flee from the testimonies of understanding and kindness before the deranged and ailing crowd. They beg Him for the blessings of resurrection, yet they hate the cross of thorns that regenerates and sanctifies.
They could go in the edifying vanguard, but they do not want to.
They cry out for divine light, yet they fear abandoning the shadows.
They sigh for the improvement of the conditions in which they agitate, yet they detest their own renewal.

We see, therefore, that it is easy to eat the bread multiplied by the infinite love of the Divine Master or to rejoice in His healing influence, but to attain the Abundant Life of which He made Himself the sublime ambassador, the faculty of power and the act of believing are not enough, but also the persevering will of one who has learned to work and serve, to perfect and to love.

messages.title: In the Regenerative Work
paragraphs: “Brothers, if someone is caught in a sin, you who live by the Spirit should restore him gently. But watch yourselves, or you also may be tempted.” — PAUL (Galatians 6:1)
If we try to guide a brother lost in the brush of error with the goads of anger, we do nothing more than arouse his wrath against ourselves.
If we strike him with blows, he will retaliate with just as many.
If we point out his flaws, he may highlight our less-than-happy gestures.
If we opine that he should suffer the same evil with which he wounded others, we merely increase the percentage of evil around us.
If we applaud his erroneous conduct, we approve of the crime.
If we remain indifferent, we sustain the disturbance.
But if we treat the error of our fellow being as one who considers removing an illness from a sick friend, we are, in reality, carrying out the regenerative work.
In difficult hours, when we see a companion plummet into inner shadows, let us not forget that, to help him, condemnation is as unadvisable as praise.
Just as it is not right to throw petroleum on flames with the purpose of extinguishing a bonfire, no one cures wounds by spraying perfume.
Let us be human, above all. Let us approach our unhappy companion with the values of understanding and fraternity.
No one will lose out by exercising the respect we owe to all creatures and all things.
Let us place ourselves in the position of the accused and reflect whether, in his conditions, we would have resisted the suggestions of evil.
Let us relate our advantages and the losses of our neighbor with impartiality and good intention.
Whenever we proceed in this manner, the picture changes in its smallest aspects.
Otherwise, it will always be easy to lash and condemn, only to fall, certainly, into the very same offenses when we, in our turn, are visited by temptation.

messages.title: If We Knew
paragraphs: “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing…” — JESUS (Luke 23:34)
If the murderer knew beforehand the tribute of pain that life would exact from him in the readjustment of his destiny, he would prefer not to have arms to deliver any blow.

If the slanderer could eliminate the crust of shadow that maddens his vision, observing the suffering that awaits him in the settlement of accounts with the truth, he would paralyze his vocal cords or immobilize his pen, so as not to entrust himself to unwarranted accusation.
If the deserter of good could manage to see the dangerous traps with which darkness will steal his joy of living, he would pause happily under the sanctifying shackles of the heaviest duties.
If the ungrateful person perceived the gall of bitterness that will later invade his heart, he would not perpetrate the crime of indifference.
If the selfish person contemplated the infernal solitude awaiting him, he would never depart from the indefatigable practice of fraternity and cooperation.
If the gluttonous person could see the imbalances toward which he directs his own body, hurrying his march to death, he would render invariable worship to frugality and harmony.
If we knew how terrible the result of our disrespect for the Divine Laws is, we would never stray from the straight path.
Therefore, forgive whoever wounds and slanders you…
Truly, those who yield to the disturbing suggestions of evil do not know what they are doing.

messages.title: Inoperative Faith
paragraphs: “In the same way, faith by itself, if it is not accompanied by action, is dead.” — (JAMES 2:17)

Inoperative faith is a problem deserving of the best attention at all times, so that the disciples of the Gospel may clearly understand that the noblest ideal, without work to materialize it for the benefit of all, will always be a superb, unproductive landscape.
What shall we say of a precious motor that no one uses? Of a spring that does not move to fertilize the field? Of a light that does not radiate?

We may trust with certainty in a given seed; however, if we do not plant it, what will our expectation result in, if not simple uselessness?
