We may sustain absolute hope in the works that a log of wood will provide us, but if we are not disposed to use the saw and the plane, surely the raw material will rest indefinitely on the way to disintegration.
Religious belief is the means. Apostleship is the end.
Celestial confidence illuminates intelligence so that beneficial action may extend, improvising everywhere blessings of peace and joy, aggrandizement and sublimation.

Whoever can receive a drop of spiritual revelation in the depth of their being, demonstrating the maturation necessary for superior life, should immediately seek the post of service that belongs to them, in favor of common progress.
Faith, in essence, is that mustard seed embryo of Jesus' teaching which, in full growth through elevation by incessant work, converts into the Divine Kingdom where the believer's soul comes to live.

Therefore, to keep religious ecstasy in the heart without any activity in the works of development of wisdom and love, consolidated in the service of charity and education, is to conserve a dead idol in the living soil of feeling, buried among the useless flowers of brilliant promises.

messages.title: Before the Goal
paragraphs: “To see if somehow I may attain to the resurrection.” — PAUL (Philippians 3:11)
We will reach the target we keep in our sights:
The miser dreams of coined treasures and reaches the strongbox.
The evildoer commonly spends a long time planning disturbing action and commits the crime.
The skilled politician yearns for authority and attains a high post in earthly dominion.
The unwary woman who concentrates her ideas on the waste of emotions enters the field of unsettling adventures.
And each goal we propose has its respective price.
The usurer, to amass money, almost always loses peace.
The delinquent, to carry out the fault he outlines, debases his name.
The opportunist, to secure a position of command, often disfigures character.
The foolish woman, to achieve fanciful pleasures, usually abdicates the right to be happy.
If such heavy taxes are demanded on Earth of those who pursue purely inferior results, what tributes will the Spirit pay who applies for glory in eternal life?
The Master on the cross is the answer for all who seek the sublimity of resurrection.
Contemplating this target, Paul knew how to seek it through misunderstandings, scourgings, afflictions, and stoning, constantly serving in the name of the Lord.
If you wish, in your turn, to reach the same destination, centralize your aspirations on the sanctifying goal and follow, with valiant effort, in the conquest of the eternal prize.

messages.title: On the Rugged Path
paragraphs: “Never will I leave you; never will I forsake you.” — PAUL (Hebrews 13:5)
The Lord's word does not refer solely to the sustenance of physical life in the stony climb of ascent. Much more than the bread of the body, we need the bread of the spirit.

If the cells of the physiological field suffer hunger and demand common soup, the needs and desires, impulses and emotions of the soul sometimes provoke immeasurable afflictions, demanding broader spiritual nourishment.
There are moments of profound exhaustion in our most intimate reserves. Energies seem depleted and hopes withdraw apathetically. Shadow installs itself within us as if thick night were enveloping us.

And just as happens to Nature under the night mantle, although we harbor fountains of understanding and flowers of goodwill across the vast extent of our inner country, everything remains veiled by the fog of our anxieties.

The All-Merciful, however, even then does not leave us completely relegated to the darkness of our indecisions and disappointments. Just as He makes dazzling stars shine on high, revealing the starry paths of the firmament to the traveler lost in the world, He kindles in the sky of our ideals new convictions and higher aspirations, so that our Spirit does not get lost on the journey to superior life.
“Never will I leave you; never will I forsake you” — promises Divine Goodness.
Neither solitude nor abandonment. Celestial Providence continues to watch…
Let us maintain, then, the comforting certainty that every storm is followed by a tranquil atmosphere and that there is no night without a dawn.

messages.title: For a Little While
paragraphs: “Choosing rather to be mistreated with the people of God than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a little while.” — PAUL (Hebrews 11:25)

In this passage, Paul refers to Moses' attitude, abstaining from enjoying for a little while the luxuries of Pharaoh's house in order to consecrate himself to the liberation of his captive companions, creating a sublime image to define the position of the incarnate Spirit on Earth.
“For a little while,” the administrator directs the people's interests.
“For a little while,” the servant obeys in subservience.
“For a little while,” the usurer retains money.
“For a little while,” the unhappy person suffers deprivations.
Ah! If man observed the brevity of the days at his disposal on Earth! If he saw the meagerness of the resources he can count on in the vessel of flesh in which he moves!…
Certainly, such perception, in the face of eternity, would give him a new concept of the blessed opportunity—precious and fleeting—granted to him in the world.
Everything favors or afflicts the earthly creature simply for a little while.
Many people, however, use this tiny fraction of hours to complicate themselves for many years.
It is essential to fix the brain and heart on the example of those who knew how to glorify their hurried pilgrimage on the common path.
Moses did not stop to enjoy, “for a little while,” in the Pharaonic climate, in order to leave us righteous legislation.
Jesus did not set out to dispute, not even “for a little while,” in the face of the cruelty of those who persecuted him, so as to teach us the divine secret of the Cross with Eternal Resurrection.
Paul did not dare to rest “for a little while,” after finding the Master at the gates of Damascus, so as to bequeath to us his example of work and living faith.

My friend, wherever you may be, remember that you remain there “for a little while.” Moderate yourself in joy and conform yourself in sadness, working unceasingly in the extension of good, because it is in the demonstration of the “little” that you will walk toward the “much” of happiness or suffering.

messages.title: Language
paragraphs: “Sound and blameless speech so that those who oppose you may be ashamed because they have nothing bad to say about us.” — PAUL (Titus 2:8)
Through language, man helps or hinders himself.
Even if our innermost being remains clouded by problems, it is not advisable that our word become turbid or unbalanced toward others.
Each person has their enigma, their need, and their pain, and it is not fair to increase a neighbor's afflictions with the burden of our anxieties.
The externalization of complaint discourages, the verb of harshness lashes, the observation of the backbiter confuses…
Through our poorly conducted manifestation toward the errors of others, we push truth away from us.
Through our less-than-ennobling verbal expression, we repel the blessing of love that would fill us with the joy of living.
Let us have the precise courage to eliminate, by ourselves, the rays of our uncontrolled feelings and desires.
The word is the channel of the “self.” Through the valve of the tongue, our passions explode or our virtues extend.
Every time we cast out the vocabulary that is proper to us, we emit forces that destroy or build, that undermine or restore, that wound or balm.

Language, in our view, consists of three essential elements: expression, manner, and voice. If we do not clarify the phrase, if we do not refine the manner, and if we do not educate the voice according to situations, we are liable to lose our best opportunities for improvement, understanding, and elevation.
Paul of Tarsus provides the proper recipe for the apprentices of the Gospel.

Neither language too sweet nor excessively bitter. Neither too mild, chasing away confidence, nor harsh or cutting, breaking sympathy, but rather “sound and blameless speech so that those who oppose you may be ashamed because they have nothing bad to say about us.”

messages.title: Let Us Have Faith
paragraphs: “…I am going there to prepare a place for you.” — JESUS (John 14:2)

The Master knew that, until the construction of the Divine Kingdom on Earth, all who accompanied him would live in a condition of misfits, working for the progress of all creatures, yet “without a place” adequate to the sublime ideals they treasure.
Indeed, the loyal Christian, everywhere, rarely receives the respect due to him:
Because he almost always stands out from the community—which is not yet fully Christianized—he suffers the uncharitable opinion of many.
If he practices humility, he is considered a coward.
If he adopts a simple life, he is accused of the crime of slackness.
If he seeks to be kind, he is categorized as a fool.
If he governs with dignity, he is judged proud.
If he obeys as is just, he is considered servile.
If he uses tolerance, he is seen as incompetent.
If he mobilizes energy, he is known as cruel.
If he works devotedly, he is interpreted as vain.
If he tries to improve himself, assuming responsibilities in the intensive effort of good works or comforting lectures, he is pointed out as a fake.
If he tries to help his neighbor, approaching the crowd with gestures of spontaneous kindness, he is often branded as individualistic and opportunistic, attentive to his own interests.

Despite such conflicts, however, let us continue acting and serving in the name of the Lord. Recognizing that the home of his followers is not built on the ground of the world, Jesus promised that he would prepare a place for them in higher life.
Let us continue, then, working with doubled fervor in the sowing of good, like servants provisionally distanced from their true home.
“My Father’s house has many rooms.” And Christ continues to serve ahead of us. Let us have faith.

messages.title: Only Thus
paragraphs: “This is to my Father’s glory, that you bear much fruit, showing yourselves to be my disciples.” — JESUS (John 15:8)
In our afflictions, the Father is invoked.
In joys, He is adored.
In the stormy night, He is always awaited with yearning.
On the festive day, He is solemnly revered.
Praised by grateful children and forgotten by the ungrateful, the Father always gives, spreading the blessings of His infinite goodness among good and bad, just and unjust.
He teaches the worm to crawl, the shrub to grow, and man to reason.

No one should doubt, however, regarding the Supreme Lord's expectation concerning us. From existence to existence, He helps us grow and serve Him so that, one day, we may integrate victoriously into His divine love and be able to glorify Him.
We will never reach such a condition, however, simply through the thousand ways of brilliant coloring in our feelings and reasonings.
Our superior ideals are indispensable, and deep down they resemble the most beautiful and fragrant flowers of the tree.
Our culture is undoubtedly indispensable and, in essence, constitutes the robustness of the respectable trunk.
Our elevated aspirations are precious and necessary, and represent the living and promising leaves.
All these requirements are imperatives of the harvest. The same occurs in the domains of the soul.
It is only possible to glorify the Father when we open ourselves to His decrees of universal love, producing for eternal good.

For this very reason, the Master was clear in His statement. May our activity within life produce much fruit of peace and wisdom, love and hope, faith and joy, justice and mercy, in dignified and constant personal work, because only thus will the Father be glorified by us and only in this condition will we be disciples of the Crucified and Risen Master.

messages.title: On the Cross
paragraphs: “He saved others; he cannot save himself!” — (Matthew 27:42)
Yes, he had redeemed many… He had extended love and truth, peace and light, raised the sick and resurrected the dead.
Meanwhile, for himself, the cross rose between thieves.
Indeed, for someone who had exalted himself so much, for someone who had reached the pinnacle, indirectly suggesting his own condition as Redeemer and King, the fall was enormous…
He was the Prince of Peace and found himself conquered by the war of inferior interests.
He was the Savior and did not save himself.
He was the Just One and suffered supreme injustice.
The Lord lay flagellated and vanquished.
To human consensus, it was extreme loss.
He had fallen, however, on the cross. Bleeding, but standing.
Tortured, but with open arms.
Relegated to suffering, but suspended from Earth.
Surrounded by hatred and sarcasm, but with his heart hoisted to Love.
He had fallen, vilified and forgotten, but the next day, he transformed his own pain into divine glory.
His head, matted with blood, hung on the timber, and he resurged in the sunlight at the breath of a garden.
Dark defeat converted into resplendent victory. The shameful wood covered itself with celestial brightness for the entire Earth.
The same occurs in the circle of our lives.
Do not stumble over easy triumph or the cheap halo of the crucifiers.

Whenever circumstances compel you to modify the course of your own life, prefer self-sacrifice, transforming your pain into help for many, because all those who receive the cross in favor of their fellow beings discover the path of eternal resurrection.

messages.title: Self-Liberation
paragraphs: “...For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out.” — PAUL (1 Timothy, 6:7)

If you wish to emancipate the soul from the dark shackles of the 'self', begin your course of self-liberation by learning to live 'as having nothing, and yet possessing all things', with everyone and without anyone.

If you arrived on Earth in the condition of a pilgrim in need of shelter and help, and if you know that you will leave it alone, resign yourself to living with yourself, serving everyone, for the sake of your spiritual growth toward immortality.
Remember that, by virtue of the laws that govern destinies, each creature is or will be in solitude, in their own way, acquiring the science of self-overcoming.
Dedicate yourself to good, not only for your own sake, but, above all, out of love for the good itself.
Truly great is he who knows his own smallness before infinite life.
Do not deliberately impose yourself, driving away sympathy; you will not dispense with the help of others in the execution of your task.

Never suppose that your pain is greater than your neighbor's, or that the situations that please you are the ones that should please those who follow you. What encourages you may frighten many, and the material of your joy may be a poison to your brother.

Above all, combat the tendency to personal offense with the same persistence used in the hygiene of the bed where you rest. Much recorded offense is a useless burden to the heart. Is harboring the sarcasm or insult of others not the same as cultivating foreign thorns in our house?
Clear your mind every morning and move forward, certain that we will settle our accounts with Him who lent us life and not with the men who squander it.
Let reality aid your vision, and you will find the divine happiness of the anonymous angel who blends into the glory of the common good.

Learn to be alone, to be freer in the performance of the duty that unites you to all, and, with your thoughts turned to the Heavenly Friend who embraced the narrow path of the cross, let us not forget Paul's warning when he tells us that, with regard to any material heritage, 'we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out'.

messages.title: Before the Lord
paragraphs: “Why do you not understand my speech? Because you are not able to listen to my word.” — JESUS (John, 8:43)
Christ's language has always seemed indecipherable and strange to many learners.
To do all possible good, even when evils are growing and numerous.
To lend without demanding return.
To forgive unceasingly.
To love one's adversaries.
To help slanderers and the wicked.
Many people listen to the Good News, but do not penetrate its teachings. This happens to many followers of the Gospel because they use their mental strength in other areas.
They believe vaguely in celestial help in times of bitterness, showing, however, absolute indifference to the study and application of divine laws.
The preoccupation with possession absorbs their existence.

They demand the gold of the soil, the bread of the barn, the usable linen, the balance of the flesh, the pleasure of the senses, and social consideration with such voluptuousness that they do not remember their position as mere usufructuaries of the world in which they find themselves, and they never reflect on the transience of all material patrimonies, whose sole function is to provide them with an adequate climate for work in charity and light, for the aggrandizement of the eternal Spirit.
They record Christ's calls, yet they furiously chain their attention to the appeals of primary life.
They perceive, but do not hear. They inform themselves, but do not understand.
In this field of contradictions, we always have respectable human personalities and, at times, admirable friends.
They preserve enormous potentials of goodness in their hearts; nevertheless, their minds live engaged in the game of perishable forms.
They are precious stations of useful service, with equipment, however, occupied in more or less useless activities.

Let us not forget, therefore, that it is always easy to register the Lord's language, but it is necessary to present Him with a heart emptied of Earth's residues, in order to receive His divine word in spirit and in truth.

messages.title: Fraternal Union
paragraphs: “Endeavoring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.” — PAUL (Ephesians, 4:3)
Before your eyes, a thousand paths open up each time you remember to fix your gaze on the distant vanguard.
There are millions of paths that run alongside yours. Do not forget your own road and advance fearlessly.
You might perhaps wish that all routes were subordinate to yours and refer to union as if the other travelers of life should gravitate around your steps...
Unite with others without demanding that others unite with you. Seek what is useful and beautiful, holy and sublime, and move forward...
The spring seeks the stream, the stream seeks the river, and the river connects to the sea.
Let us not forget that spiritual unity is the basic service of peace.
Do you observe the brother who devotes himself to children?
Do you notice the companion who set out to help the sick?
Do you identify the care of the one who became the friend of the old and the young?
Do you note the effort of the one who dedicated himself to the improvement of the soil or the education of animals?
Do you appreciate the service of the one who became a teacher in the extension of good?

Honor each of them with your gesture of understanding and serenity, convinced that only through the roots of understanding can the tree of fraternal union, which we all ambition to be robust and fruitful, sustain itself.
Do not assume that others are viewing life through your eyes.
Evolution is an infinite ladder. Each one encompasses the landscape according to the step on which they place themselves.
Approach each servant of the good, offering them the best you can, and they will respond with their best part.
War is always the poisonous fruit of violence.
Sterile contention is the result of imposition.

Fraternal union is the sublime dream of the human soul; however, it will not be achieved without us respecting one another, cultivating harmony in the face of the environment we were called to serve. We will only achieve such fulfillment by 'endeavoring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace'.

messages.title: Let Us Move Forward
paragraphs: “Brethren, I do not count myself to have apprehended; but one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind and reaching forward to those things which are ahead.” — PAUL (Philippians, 3:13-14)
On the Christian road, we are always confronted by a large number of brothers who have settled in the shadow of unproductivity, declaring themselves injured by spiritual disasters.
It is someone who weeps over the loss of a beloved relative, called to the transformation of the tomb.
It is the worker who found himself torn apart by the incomprehension of a friend.
It is the missionary who immobilized himself in the face of calumny.
It is someone who laments the desertion of a fellow warrior in the good fight.
It is the laborer of good who endlessly complains against the flight of a companion who did not perceive his affectionate dedication.
It is the idealist who waits for material fortune to begin the achievements that are incumbent upon him.
It is the cooperator who remains in expectation of a richly remunerated job to consecrate himself to good works.
It is the woman who wraps herself in the briar patch of complaints against uncomprehending family members.
It is the collaborator who is scandalized by the neighbor's defects, freezing the possibilities to serve.
It is someone who deplores a committed error, belittling the blessings of time in destructive remorse.
The past, however, if it holds the virtues of experience, is not always the best conductor of life into the future.
It is imperative to exhume the heart from all the numbing wrappings that sometimes shroud our soul.
Contrition, longing, hope, and scruple are sacred, but they must not represent an impediment to our Spirit's access to the Higher Sphere.

Paul of Tarsus, who knew terrible aspects of human combat within the intimacy of his own heart and who rose to the heights of the apostolate with Christ, offers us a safe itinerary for self-improvement.
‘Let us forget all the inferior expressions of yesterday and advance toward the illumined days that await us’ — this is the essence of his fraternal warning to the community of Philippi.
Let us centralize our energies in Jesus and walk forward.
No one progresses without renewing themselves.

messages.title: Open Tombs
paragraphs: “Their throat is an open tomb.” — PAUL (Romans, 3:13)

Referring to Spirits strayed from the light, Paul asserted that they have a throat like an open tomb, and in this image, we can frame many companions when they stray from the Royal Road of the Gospel onto the rugged tracks of delinquent personalism.

As soon as they settle into the dark empire of the 'self', forgetting the obligations that place us in the Divine Kingdom of Universality, their throat is transfigured into a truly uncovered tomb. They let out all the poisoned gall that overflows from their inner self, like a vessel of mud, and begin to tune in exclusively to the evils that still plague neighbors, friends, and companions.
They see only the defects, fragile points, and diseased areas of well-meaning people who share their journey.
They weave long commentaries in examining other people's ulcers instead of curing them.
They waste precious time in long and biting talks, blackening the intentions of others.
They overload their imagination with depressing pictures in the domains of suspicion and mental intemperance.
Above all, they complain about everything and everyone.

They project numbing emanations of bad faith, spreading discouragement and distrust against the prosperity of sanctification wherever they pass, scorching the flowers of hope and annihilating the unripe fruits of charity.
Such learners, deeply unfortunate due to the conduct they embrace, do indeed look like open tombs to us... They exhale ruins and toxins of death.

When you stray, therefore, into the slippery terrain of lamentations and accusations, which are almost always undue, reconsider your spiritual steps and remember that our throat must be consecrated to the good, for only thus will the Lord's sublime verb express itself through it.

messages.title: Serve and March
paragraphs: “Therefore strengthen the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 12:12)

If the production of healthy fruit in common agriculture is difficult, so that the body's bread is not lacking in the world's barns, the service of acquiring spiritual values, which mean the living and imperishable nourishment of the soul, is almost sacrificial.
The seed of good will is planted, but a thousand obstacles hinder its germination and growth.
It is the flood of futilities of inferior life.
The invasion of worms symbolized in annoyances of all kinds.
The mud of envy and spite.
The thunderstorms of incomprehension.
Thehails of malice.
The debris of calumny.
The heat of responsibility.
The cold of indifference.
The dryness of misunderstanding.
The weeds of ignorance.
The clouds of worries.
The dust of disenchantment.
All the ponderable forces of human experience seem to combine against the one who wishes to advance along the path of good.
Until we reach the divine inheritance to which we are destined, any descent is always easy...
Elevation, however, is the work of sweat, persistence, and sacrifice.
Do not recoil before the struggle if you can truly already interest your heart in the higher climates of life.
Although faced with all kinds of difficulties, move forward, offering to the service of perfection whatever you possess of noble, beautiful, and useful.
Remember Paul's advice and do not become immobilized. Move your tired hands to work and raise your feeble knees, certain that to obtain the best part of life one must serve and march unceasingly.

messages.title: In Preaching
paragraphs: “And I will very gladly spend and be spent for your souls; though the more abundantly I love you, the less I am loved.” — PAUL (2 Corinthians, 12:15)

There are numerous companions of salvationist preaching who gladly rise to gilded pulpits, discoursing preciously on the merits of kindness and faith, but, if invited to contribute to good works, they feel wounded in their wallets and quickly retreat under disparate allegations.
A thousand impediments prohibit them from practicing charity, and they walk away to different sectors where the good doctrine does not constitute a disturbance to their quiet lives.
Effectively, however, in the legitimate practice of the Gospel, it is not up to us only to spend what we have, but also to give of what we are.

It is not enough to pour out the treasury and solve issues related to the body's experience. It is imperative that we give ourselves, through the sweat of collaboration and spontaneous effort in solidarity, to substantially fulfill our primary obligations before Christ.
Whoever, in any way, does not commit themselves for the benefit of their companions only knows the lessons of the High in the circles of the word.
Many people wait for the love of others in order to love, when such an attitude only means delay in the sanctifying enterprises that are incumbent upon us.
Whoever helps and suffers out of devotion to the Good News gathers celestial supplies of strength to act in general progress.
Let us remember that Jesus not only yielded, for the benefit of all, all that He could retain for His own benefit, but He equally made the donation of Himself for the common elevation.

Preachers who neither spend nor spend themselves for the aggrandizement of the redeeming ideas of Christianity are orchids of the Gospel upon the problematic support of other people's possibilities; but he who teaches and exemplifies, learning to sacrifice himself for the upliftment of all, is the robust tree of the Eternal Good, manifesting the Lord in the rich soil of true fraternity.

messages.title: Let Us Earnestly Seek
paragraphs: “But earnestly desire the best gifts. And yet I show you a more excellent way.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 12:31)
The idea that no one should seek to learn and improve to be more useful to Divine Revelation is much more an attempt to consecrate oneself to idleness than an essay in incipient humility.

Life is an advanced course of improvement through effort and struggle, and if even stone must undergo refinement to reflect light, what can be said of ourselves, called from now on to exteriorize divine resources?

Let no one interrupt the blessed service of their education under the pretext of cooperating with Heaven, because progress is a train with tireless wheels that leaves behind those who rebel against the imperatives ahead.
It is indispensable to advance with the consequent improvement of all that surrounds us. And the Gospel does not endorse any attitude of disachieving expectation.
Paul's word is too significant. Addressing the Corinthians, the apostle to the Gentiles exhorts them to earnestly seek the best gifts.
It is imperative that we dispose ourselves to acquire the noblest qualities of intelligence and heart, sublimating the imperishable individuality.
Culture and sanctification, through work and fraternity, constitute a duty for all creatures.

Self-improvement is a common obligation. Let us zealously seek our own elevation, marking our presence, wherever we may be, with the blessings of service to all, and as soon as we are integrated into dignified effort, within personal and incessant action in the good, the High will unveil more illumined paths for our ascension.

messages.title: Elucidations
paragraphs: “For we do not preach ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord, and ourselves your bondservants for Jesus' sake.” — PAUL (2 Corinthians, 4:5)

We, the learners of the Good News, when in true communion with the Lord, cannot ignore the need to withdraw our individuality in order to project the Master's teachings to the multitude with the desired benefit.
In matters of Christian life, properly considered, the only justifiable passions are those of learning, helping, and serving, since we know that Christ is the Great Planner of our achievements.

If we remember that His supervision always acts in favor of whatever we can produce at our best, we will live attentive to the work that falls to us, convinced that His pronouncement remains invariable in the circumstances of life.

Our fundamental concern anywhere, therefore, must be the rendering of service in His Name, understanding that preaching ourselves, with the propaganda of particularisms peculiar to our personality, will be the simple interference of our 'self' in works of eternal life that refer to the Kingdom of God.

Writing to the Corinthians, Paul defines his position and that of the other apostles as being servants of the community for the love of Jesus. There is no clearer indication of the functions that befit us.
The leadership of the Divine Master is always more alive, and the general programming of services reserved for disciples of all conditions remains structured in His Gospel of Wisdom and Love.
Let us seek the bases of Christ so as not to act in vain.

Let us adjust ourselves to the consciousness of the Great Renewer, so as not to be tempted by our impulses of domination, because, in all climates and situations, the companion of the Good News is invited, called, and compelled to serve.

messages.title: Reborn Now
paragraphs: “Most assuredly, I say to you, unless one is born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.” — JESUS (John, 3:3)
Nature itself presents precious lessons in this particular regard.
The years follow one another with mathematical precision, but the days are always new.
Having, thus, three hundred and sixty-five opportunities for learning and restarting annually, how many opportunities for moral renewal will the creature find in the blessed period of an existence?
Keep from the past what is good and just, beautiful and noble, but do not keep the debris and shadows from the past, even when masked in charming garb.

Do for yourself, in the domains of your initiative through the application of real fraternity, the work that your negligence will fatally cast upon the shoulders of your spiritual benefactors and friends.
Each emerging hour can be a bearer of readjustment.
If possible, do not leave for later the bonds of love and peace that you can create now, to replace the heavy shackles of disaffection.

It is not easy to break old precepts of the world or unravel the heart in favor of those who hurt us. However, the best antidote against the toxins of aversion is our good will for the benefit of those who hate us or who still do not understand us.

While we linger in the defensive fortress, the adversary contemplates enriching his munitions, but if we descend to the public square, undaunted and serene, showing new dispositions in the struggle, the idea of agreement replaces, within us and around our steps, the dark fermentation of war.
Does someone hurt you? Restart the effort of good understanding.
Does someone not understand you? Persevere in demonstrating the noblest intents.
Let yourself revive each day in the crystalline and incessant current of the good.
Do not forget the Master's assertion: — 'Unless one is born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.'
Be reborn now in your purposes, deliberations, and attitudes, working to overcome the obstacles that surround you and achieving the anticipation of victory over yourself in time...
It is better to help even today than to be helped tomorrow.

messages.title: Apostles
paragraphs: “For I think that God has displayed us, the apostles, last, as men condemned to death; for we have been made a spectacle to the world, both to angels and to men.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 4:9)

The apostle is the educator par excellence. In him reside the improvisation of labor and self-sacrifice so that the disciples' minds may be transformed and enlightened, heading toward the higher sphere.
The legislator formulates decrees that determine balance and justice in the outer zone of the social field.
The administrator disposes of material and human resources, operating the machinery of terrestrial services.
The priest teaches the people the ways of faith, in primary manifestations.
The artist embellishes the path of intelligence, awakening the heart to the edifying messages that the world encloses in its content of spirituality.
The scientist surprises the realities of Divine Wisdom created for the evolution of the creature and reveals to them the visible or perceptible expression to popular knowledge.
The thinker questions, probing transient phenomena.
The physician succors the diseased flesh.
The warrior disciplines the multitude and establishes order.
The worker is the active minstrel of forms, perfecting the vessels destined for the preservation of life.
The apostles, however, are the conductors of the Spirit.

In all the great causes of Humanity, they are living institutions of revealing example, breathing in the world of causes and effects, offering in themselves the essence of what they teach, the truth they demonstrate, and the clarity they ignite around others.

They interfere in the elaboration of the thoughts of the wise and the ignorant, the rich and the poor, the great and the humble, renewing their way of believing and being, so that the world may be magnified and sanctified.
In them arises the equation of facts and ideas, of which they constitute pioneers or defenders, through the total donation of themselves for the benefit of all.
Therefore, they pass through Earth working and fighting, suffering and growing without rest, with numerous stages through the crosses of misunderstanding and pain.

Representing, in themselves, the spiritual leaven that ferments the mass of progress and refinement, they transit in the world, according to the definition of Paul of Tarsus, as if placed by Divine Providence in the last places of human experience, like those condemned to incessant suffering, for in them are condensed the positive demonstration of good for the world, the possibility of action for the Superior Spirits, and the source of imperishable benefits for all Humanity.

messages.title: Disciples
paragraphs: “And whoever does not bear his cross and come after me cannot be my disciple.” — JESUS (Luke, 14:27)

Christian circles of all shades remain full of students who classify themselves in the discipleship of Jesus, with unsurpassed verbal enthusiasm, as if the legitimate connection with the Master were circumscribed to a problem of words.
In reality, however, the Gospel leaves no doubts in this regard.
The life of every conscious creature is a set of duties toward oneself, toward the family of hearts that group around one's feelings, and toward all Humanity.
And it is not so easy to fulfill all these obligations with the full approval of the evangelical guidelines.

It is imperative to eliminate the rough edges of one's own temperament, guaranteeing the balance that is proper to us, contributing efficiently in favor of those who surround our path, giving each one what belongs to them, and serving the community of whose framework we are a part.
Without rectifying ourselves, we will not correct the route on which we march. Crooked trees do not project impeccable images.
If we seek sublimation with the Christ, let us listen to the divine teachings.
To be His disciples, it is necessary that we dispose ourselves firmly to carry the cross of our testimonies of assimilation of the good, following in His steps.
There are apprentices who carry with them the timber of saving trials, but do not follow the Lord because they confide in revolt through hardening and flight.
Others appear, following the Master in well-crafted phrases, but do not carry the cross that falls to them, abandoning it at the door of neighbors and companions.
Duty and renewal. Service and refinement.
Action and progress. Responsibility and spiritual growth.
Acceptance of the imperatives of good and obedience to the standards of the Lord. Only after such acquisitions will we attain true communion with the Divine Master.

messages.title: Words of Eternal Life
paragraphs: “You have the words of eternal life.” — SIMON PETER (John, 6:68)
Words surround you, in all phases of the struggle and in all angles of the path.
Respectable phrases that refer to your duties.
Friendly speech brought by dedications that reanimate and comfort you.
Opinions about matters that do not concern you.
Suggestions of varied origins.
Valuable lectures.
Empty speeches that your ears cast to the wind.
Spoken words… written words…

Among the articulated or silent verbal expressions, alongside which your mind develops, you will find, however, the words of eternal life. Keep your heart listening. They are born from the unfathomable love of Christ, like pure water from the immense bosom of the Earth.
Often you remain unaware and do not signal their warning, canticle, lesson, and beauty.
Watch in the world, isolated from yourself, so that you do not lose their flavor and clarity.
They exhort you to consider the greatness of God and to live in accordance with His Laws.
They refer to the Planet as our home and Humanity as our family.
They reveal in love the bond that unites us all.
They indicate in labor our route of evolution and perfection.
They open the divine horizons of life and teach us to lift our eyes to the highest and the furthest.

“Words, words, words…” Forget those that incite you to uselessness, take advantage of all that show you just obligations and teach you to magnify existence, but do not forget the phrases that awaken you to the light and to the good; they can penetrate our heart, through a friend, a letter, a page, or a book, but deep down, they always proceed from Jesus, the Divine Friend of Creatures.

Retain within you the words of eternal life, because they are the sanctifiers of the Spirit in every day's experience, and, above all, our secure mental support in the difficult hours of great renewals.

messages.title: Alms
paragraphs: “Give alms of such things as you have.” — JESUS (Luke, 11:41)
The Lord's word is always structured in luminous beauty that we cannot lose sight of.
In the chapter on alms, the Master's recommendation, within Luke's narrative, deserves special notes.
“Give alms of such things as you have.” Giving what we have is different from giving what we hold.

Charity is sublime in all aspects under which it reveals itself to us, and under no circumstances should we forget the admirable abnegation of those who distribute bread and clothing, medicine and succor for the body, learning solidarity and teaching it.
It is fair, however, to emphasize that fortune or authority are goods that we provisionally hold in the common march and that, in the substantial foundations of life, do not belong to us.
The owner of all power and all wealth in the Universe is God, our Creator and Father, who lends resources to men according to the merits or needs of each one.
Let us not forget, therefore, the donations of our intimate sphere and ask ourselves:
What do we have of our own to give?
What kind of emotion are we communicating to others?
What reactions do we provoke in our neighbor?
What do we distribute with our companions of daily struggle?
What is the stock of our feelings?
What kind of vibrations do we spread?

To diffuse goodness, no one needs to cultivate strident laughter or cheap smiles, but so as not to give stones of indifference to hearts hungry for the bread of fraternity, it is indispensable to garner in our Spirit the reserves of good comprehension, emitting the treasure of friendship and understanding that the Master entrusted to us in service to the good of all who surround us, near or far.
The charity that feeds the stomach is always small if it does not forget the offense, is not disposed to serve directly, or does not light a light for ignorance.

The warning of the Divine Instructor in Luke's notes means: — give alms of your intimate life, help by yourselves, spread joy and good cheer, opportunity for growth and elevation with your fellow men, be brothers dedicated to your neighbor, because, in truth, the love that radiates in blessings of happiness and work, peace and trust, is always the greatest gift of all.

messages.title: Never Faint
paragraphs: “…Always to pray and not to faint.” — (Luke, 18:1)
Do not allow external problems, including those of the body itself, to disable you for the service of your illumination.
As long as you find yourself on the plane of exercise, like the crust of the Earth, you will always be confronted by difficulty and pain.
The lesson given is a path to new lessons. Behind the resolved enigma, other enigmas appear.
The function of the school can be no other than to teach, exercise, and perfect. Fill yourself, therefore, with calm and good cheer in all situations.
You were placed among a thousand obstacles of a strange nature so that, overcoming inhibitions outside of yourself, you may learn to surpass your limitations.
Until the terrestrial community adapts to the new light, you will breathe surrounded by unsettling tears, thoughtless gestures, and dark feelings.
Dispose yourself to forgive and help always, so that you do not lose the glorious opportunity of spiritual growth.
Remember all the afflictions that surrounded the Christian spirit in the world since the coming of the Lord.
Where is the Sanhedrin that condemned the Celestial Friend to death?
Where are the vain and domineering Romans?
Where are the executioners of the newborn Good News?
Where are the warriors who made dark rivers of blood and sweat flow around the Gospel?
Where are the cunning princes who fought and negotiated in the name of the Crucified Restorer?
Where are the darkness of the Middle Ages?
Where are the politicians and inquisitors of all shades who struck in the name of the Exalted Benefactor?
Cast by time into the precipices of ash, they strengthened and consolidated the pedestal of light in which the figure of Christ shines, ever more glorious, in the government of the centuries.

Center yourself on the effort to help the common good, following with your cross toward the divine resurrection. In the constraining surprises of the march, remember that, above all, it matters to pray always, working, serving, learning, loving, and never fainting.

messages.title: Slowly, But Always
paragraphs: “Even though our outward man is perishing, yet the inward man is being renewed day by day.” — PAUL (2 Corinthians, 4:16)
Observe the spirit of sequence and gradation that prevails in the smallest sectors of Nature.
Nothing is accomplished by leaps, and in the rule of Divine Law, there is no privilege anywhere.
The ear of corn fills grain by grain.
The tree develops millimeter by millimeter.
The forest is born from insignificant seeds.
The building rises piece by piece.
The fabric begins in the threads.
The most famous pages were produced letter by letter.
The richest city is built span by span.
The greatest fortunes of gold and stones were extracted from the soil fragment by fragment.
The longest road is paved meter by meter.
The great river that empties into the sea is a set of liquid streams.
Do not abandon your great dream of knowing and doing in the superior domains of intelligence and feeling, but do not forget the tiny work, day by day.
Life is a renewing process everywhere, and, according to Paul's sublime word, even though the flesh corrupts, the imperishable individuality reforms incessantly.

So that we do not modify ourselves, however, in a direction opposite to the expectation of the High, it is indispensable that we know how to persevere with the effort of self-improvement, in constant vigilance, in the activity that helps and ennobles us.
If some divine ideal inhabits your spirit, do not forget the daily little service so that it materializes at the opportune moment.
Is there a favorable opportunity for fulfillment? Act with regularity, with your soul turned toward the goal.
Are there mishaps and struggles, thorns and rough stones on the path? Proceed anyway.
Time, the implacable dominator of civilizations and men, marches with only sixty minutes an hour, but never stops.
Let us keep the lesson and walk forward with the improvement of ourselves. Slowly, but always.

messages.title: Differences
paragraphs: “By this all will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.” — JESUS (John, 13:35)
In the various schools of Christianity, we see thousands of people who, in some way, connect with the Master and Lord.

There are hearts that dissolve in praises to the Great Physician, exalting His divine intercession in events where they recognized themselves favored, but they do not go beyond spectacular affirmations, as if they lived indefinitely immersed in marvelous visions.
They are simply beneficiaries and dreamers.

There are ardent temperaments that impress from the tribune through erudite and moving lectures, in which they relate the position of the Great Restorer in religion, philosophy, and history, yet they do not advance beyond precious speeches.
They are simply priests and preachers.

There are exquisite intelligences that pour out sublime pages of comforting belief, pulling tears of emotion from readers avid for revealing knowledge, yet they do not surpass the field of religious belles-lettres.
They are simply writers and intellectuals.
All guard specialized resources and merits.
There exists, however, in the works of the Good News, a different type of cooperator.
He praises the Lord with thoughts, words, and acts every day.
He distributes the treasure of goodness through comforting speech whenever possible.
He writes edifying concepts around the Gospel every time circumstances allow him.

He surpasses, however, all spoken or written preaching, acting incessantly in the sowing of the good, in works of self-sacrifice and pure love, in the molds of action that Christ bequeathed to us. He asks for no reward, asks for no results, and does not attune himself with evil. He blesses and helps always.
Such a companion is known as a true disciple of the Lord because he loves much.

messages.title: Sowers
paragraphs: “Behold, a sower went out to sow.” — JESUS (Matthew, 13:3)
Every teaching of the Divine Master is profound and sublime in its smallest expression.
When He prepares to tell the parable of the sower, He begins with a teaching of inestimable importance that is worth remembering.
He does not tell us that the sower should act through a contract with third parties, but rather that he himself went out to sow.

Transferring the image to the soil of the Spirit, where so many imperatives of renewal invite the workers of good will to the sanctifying tillage of elevation, we are led to recognize that the servant of the Gospel is compelled to go out of himself in order to benefit the hearts of others.
It is necessary to disintegrate the old prison of the “point of view” to devote ourselves to the service of our neighbor.

Learning the science of withdrawing ourselves from the dark chain of the “ego,” we will journey through the great continent called “general interest.” And in its infinite extension, we will find the “land of souls,” choked with thorns, scraped by poverty, coated with stones, or intoxicated with swamps, offering us the divine opportunity to act for the benefit of all.

It was along this route that the Divine Sower charted the ministry of light, initiating the celestial mission of help among humble animal keepers and continuing it through the friends of Nazareth and the doctors of Jerusalem, the wordy Pharisees and the simple fishermen, the just and the unjust, rich and poor, the sick in body and soul, old and young, women and children…

As we observe, the sower of Heaven absented himself from the greatness to which he is welcomed and came down to us, spreading the clarities of Revelation and increasing our vision and discernment. He humbled himself so that we might be exalted and blended with the shadow so that our light could shine, although it would have been easy for him to be replaced by millions of messengers if he so desired.
Let us move away, then, from our inhibitions and learn with Christ to “go out to sow”.

messages.title: Do Not Deceive Yourself
paragraphs: “Do you look at things according to the outward appearance? If anyone is confident in himself that he is Christ’s, let him think this again with himself, that just as he is Christ’s, even so we are Christ’s.” — PAUL (2 Corinthians, 10:7)
Do not deceive yourself concerning our common need for improvement.

Often, overestimating our values, we believe ourselves privileged in the art of elevation. And in such circumstances, we unthinkingly forget that others are doing much more for the good than we ourselves are.

The firefly ignites light flashes in the dark and supposes itself the prince of light, but finds the lit candle that outshines it. The candle struts atop a domestic piece of furniture and presumes itself on the absolute throne of clarity, however, along comes a day when the electric lamp shines on high, dimming its flame. The lamp, in turn, grows proud in the public square, but the Sun, each morning, shines in the firmament, clearing all the Earth and paling all planetary lights, large and small.

As long as the protective and educational shadow of the flesh endures, we are almost always victims of our illusions, but when the infinite glare of truth returns with the renewal of physical death, we verify, in the sun of spiritual life, that Divine Providence is glorious love for all Humanity.
Do not trade reality for appearances.
Let us respect each achievement in its time and each person in their due place.

We are all companions in evolution and perfection, still guarded between good and evil. Wherever we activate our “lower part,” the shadow of others will remain in our company. From the zone to which we project our “good part,” the light of our neighbor will come to meet us.
Each soul is always an enigma to another soul. Therefore, it is not lawful to build the walls of our tranquility upon the foundations of another's feelings.

Let us not delude ourselves. Let us rectify within ourselves whatever harms our intimate peace and extend fraternal arms and thoughts in all directions, certain that if we are bearers of virtues and defects, at times of judgment we will always receive according to our deeds. And, understanding that the Lord's Goodness shines for all creatures without distinction of persons, let us remember in our favor and in favor of others the significant words of Paul: — “If anyone is confident in himself that he is Christ’s, let him think this again with himself, that just as he is Christ’s, even so we are Christ’s.”

messages.title: Awake and Arise
paragraphs: “Awake, you who sleep, arise from the dead, and Christ will give you light.” — PAUL (Ephesians, 5:14)
There are thousands of our companions who sleep indefinitely while the glorious day of experience on Earth stretches out in vain for them.
They vaguely perceive the incessant production of Nature, but do not remember the obligation to do something for the benefit of collective progress.

Before the tree that covers itself with fruit or the bee that weaves the honeycomb, they do not remember the mundane duty to contribute to common prosperity. Generally speaking, they resemble preciously adorned corpses.
However, a day comes when they wake up and begin to praise the Lord in admirable ecstasy. This, however, is insufficient.

There are many brothers with open eyes, yet keeping their souls in the horizontal position of idleness. It is necessary that awakened hearts rise up to life, rise to work in the sowing and harvesting of the good, so that the Master may illuminate them.
Let us strive to alert our sleeping companions, but let us not forget the need to help them rise.
It is imperative that we know how to improvise the indispensable resources to help our loved ones or not, who need to rise up to the blessings of Jesus.

It is not enough to recommend. Whoever prescribes service and virtue to their neighbor without first preparing their understanding through the spirit of fraternity identifies with the demanding instructor who claims from the student complete knowledge about a certain valuable book without first teaching them how to read.

Paul said: — “Awake, you who sleep, arise from the dead, and Christ will give you light.” And we will repeat: — “Let us awake to superior life and arise in the execution of good works, and the Lord will help us so that we may help others.”

messages.title: Way of Feeling
paragraphs: “Be renewed in the spirit of your mind.” — PAUL (Ephesians, 4:23)

For many centuries, man has reasoned, obedient to almost unchanged rules, comparing external factors according to old observation processes; he rules physical life with great changes in the sector of fundamental organic operations and handles the word as one who uses elements indispensable to a certain construction of stone, earth, and lime.
In the circles of external nature, in itself, modifications in any aspect are minimal, with the exception of advanced progress in the techniques of science and industry.
In feeling, however, the changes are profound.

In truly educated peoples, no one takes pleasure in the enslavement of their fellows, no one plays with the life of their neighbor with impunity, and no one applauds systematic and deliberate cruelty as in the old days.
Through the heart, the ideal of humanity has been sublimating the mind in all climates of the Planet.
The home and the school, the temple and the hospital, welfare and charitable institutions are children of sensitivity and not of calculation.

A worker may demonstrate high characteristics of intelligence and skill, but if he lacks devotion to service, he will always be a conscious apparatus of repetition, just as the stomach has been a machine for digesting for millennia.
Only through inner renewal does the soul progress toward the path of perfected life.

Before Christ, thousands of men and women died on the cross; however, the Master's wood became an inextinguishable light due to the quality of feeling with which the crucified one delivered himself to sacrifice, influencing the way of feeling of nations and centuries.
To grow in goodness and understanding is to extend vision and sanctify objectives in common experience.
Jesus came to us to teach us, above all, that Love is the way to Abundant Life.

Do you live besieged by pain, affliction, shadow, or illness? Renew your way of feeling, according to the standards of the Gospel, and you will perceive the Divine Purpose of Life, acting everywhere, with justice and mercy, wisdom and understanding.

messages.title: Sowing and Building
paragraphs: “For we are God's fellow workers; you are God's field, you are God's building.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 3:9)

As Paul asserted his condition as a fellow worker of God and designated the Lord's field and building in the followers and beneficiaries of the Gospel around him, he traced the spiritual picture that will always exist on Earth in improvement, between those who know and those who are ignorant of divine truth.

If we have already received the lamp lit by the Good News for our journey, we are compulsorily considered collaborators in Jesus' ministry, and it is incumbent upon us to sow and build it in all creatures who share the road with us.
We know, therefore, in essence, what service the Revelation indicates to us as soon as we approach the Christian light.

If we already harbor the Master's blessing, it is up to us to restore the balance of the currents of life where we remain, helping those who fail to help themselves, seeing something for those who lie blind, and hearing something for the benefit of those who remain deaf, so that the work of the Divine Kingdom may grow, progress, and sanctify the whole Earth.

Service is of planting and edification, demanding personal effort and goodwill toward all, because, in accordance with the apostle's own symbolism, the vegetable requires time and affection to develop, and a solid house is not built in a day.
Everywhere, however, we see masons who complain about the weight of brick and sand, and cultivators who detest the demands of fertilizer and protection for the fragile plant.

The teaching of the Gospel, however, leaves no room for any doubt. If you already know the benefits of Jesus, you are his collaborator in the vineyard of the world and in the edification of the human Spirit for Eternity.
Advance in the task entrusted to you and do not fear. If faith represents our crown of light, work in favor of all is our daily blessing.

messages.title: Steadfastness and Constancy
paragraphs: “Therefore, my beloved brethren, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, knowing that your labor is not in vain.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 15:58)
Many people believe that embracing faith means committing oneself to unproductive ecstasy.

Under the pretext of guaranteeing the illumination of the soul, many hearts flee from struggle, locking themselves between the four walls of the domestic sanctuary, amidst vigils of adoration and deep thoughts about divine mysteries, forgetting that the whole of life is the Universal Creation of God.
Faith represents vision. Vision is knowledge and the capacity to help.
He who has penetrated the “spiritual land of truth” has found work as a greater grace.

The Lord and the disciples did not live merely in contemplation. They prayed, indeed, because no one can sustain themselves without the inner bath of silence, restoring their own strength in the superior currents of sublime energy that flow from the Heavenly Springs.

Prayer and reflection constitute the subtle lubricant in our machine of daily experiences. It is important to recognize, however, that the Master and the apprentices labored, served, and suffered in the active farming of good, and that the Gospel establishes incessant work for all who embrace its saving principles.
To accept Christianity is to renew oneself for the Heights, and only the climate of service can restructure the Spirit and sanctify its destiny.

Paul of Tarsus, invariably peremptory in his warnings and admonitions, writing to the Corinthians, emphasized the need for our steadfastness and constancy in tasks of elevation, so that we may abound in noble actions with the Lord.

Acting by helping, creating joy, concord, and hope, opening new horizons to superior knowledge, and improving life wherever we may be is the apostolate of all who have devoted themselves to the Good News.

Let us seek the living waters of prayer to soothe the heart, but let us not forget to set our feelings, reasoning, and arms in motion for the progress and perfection of ourselves, of everyone, and of everything, understanding that Jesus demands diligent laborers for the edification of his Kingdom throughout the Earth.

messages.title: Solitude
paragraphs: “But the governor said, ‘Why, what evil has he done?’ But they cried out all the more, saying, ‘Let him be crucified!’” — (Matthew, 27:23)
As you elevate yourself, up the mountain, in the performance of your duty, you experience the solitude of the peaks, and immeasurable sadness constrains your sensitive soul.

Where are those who smiled with you in the springtime park of early youth? Where do the hearts rest that sought your comfort in hours of fantasy? Where do those who shared your bread and dream in the smiling adventures of the beginning take shelter?
Certainly, they stayed... They stayed in the valley, fluttering in a narrow circle, like golden butterflies that shatter at the first touch of the slightest flame of light that opens up before them.
Around you, brightness, but also silence... Within you, the happiness of knowing, but equally the pain of not being understood...

Your voice cries out without an echo, and your yearning stretches out in vain. However, if you truly ascend, what ears could hear you from a great distance, and what heart hungering for the warmth of the valley would venture to understand your ideals of height at once?
You cry, you inquire, and you suffer... Yet, what kind of rebirth is not painful?
The bird, to liberate itself, destroys the cradle of the shell in which it formed, and the seed, to produce, suffers laceration in the unknown grave.
Solitude with service to one's fellows generates greatness. The rock that supports the plain tends to live in isolation, and the Sun that nourishes the entire world shines alone.

Do not tire of learning the science of elevation. Remember the Lord, who climbed Calvary with the cross on his wounded shoulders. No one followed him in his shameful death, except two malefactors, constrained to punishment in obedience to justice. Remember him and follow...
Do not tally the goods you have already spread. Trust in the Infinite Good that awaits you.
Do not wait for others on the march of sacrifice and aggrandizement.
And do not forget that, through the ministry of redemption he exercised for all creatures, the Divine Friend of Men not only lived, fought, and suffered alone, but was also persecuted and crucified.

messages.title: Take Advantage
paragraphs: “If someone says, ‘I love God,’ and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he who does not love his brother whom he has seen, how can he love God whom he has not seen?” — (1 John, 4:20)
Life is a process of growth of the soul toward the encounter with Divine Grandeur.
Take advantage of the struggles and difficulties of the path for the expansion of yourself, dilating your circle of relationships and action.
Let us learn in order to clarify.
Let us store up treasures in order to help.
Let us magnify ourselves in order to protect.
Let us educate ourselves in order to serve.
Through the act of doing and giving something, the soul extends ever further...
By keeping the blessing received only for oneself, the Spirit often merely adorns itself, but by spreading the wealth it carries, it grows constantly.
In the provision of service to one's fellows, one naturally incorporates oneself into the choir of joys one provokes.
In teaching the apprentice, one links oneself to the benefits of the lesson.
In the creation of good works, in labor, in virtue, or in art, one lives in the progress, sanctification, or beauty with which individual and collective experience broadens and perfects itself.
In the distribution of wholesome and elevated thoughts, one becomes a living fountain of grace and contentment for all.
In spontaneous contribution, within the ministry of good, one unites with common prosperity.
Give, therefore, of yourself, of your strengths and resources, acting without ceasing in the establishment of new values, helping others for the benefit of yourself.
The world is a vast path of evolution and improvement, where ignorance and weakness pass by your side.
Take advantage of the glorious opportunity for expansion that the physical sphere grants you and help those who pass by, without considering payment of any nature.
Our neighbor is our bridge of connection with God.

If you seek the Father, help your brother, supporting one another mutually, because, according to the enlightened word of the evangelist, “if someone says, ‘I love God,’ and hates his fellow man, he is a liar, for he who does not love the companion with whom he lives, how can he love God, whom he does not yet know?”

messages.title: Misunderstanding
paragraphs: “To the weak I became as weak, that I might win the weak. I have become all things to all men, that I might by all means save some.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 9:22)
Misunderstanding is undeniably like darkness before the light; however, if the vocation of clarity marks your inner self, continue fighting the shadows in the smallest corners of your path.
Do not forget, however, the law of help and observe its principles before taking action.
Descending to help is the divine art of those who have conscientiously attained the higher life.
Dazzling light produces blindness.
If the stars of wisdom and love populate your heart, do not humiliate those who pass under the fog of ignorance and malice.
Calibrate the manifestations of yourself so that your aid does not become destructive.

If the rain flooded the desert indefinitely under the pretext of quenching its thirst, and if the Sun burned the lake without measure under the excuse of removing its moist mud, we would never have a climate suitable for producing utilities for life.
Do not make yourself too superior before the inferior, nor excessively strong before the weak.
Schools do not graduate all learners in a mass, but rather a select few each year.
Every stewardship calls for a notion of responsibility, but it also demands a sense of proportion.
Maintain the constructive energy of respectable example, but do not forget that the science of teaching only triumphs fully in the guide who knows how to support, wait, and repeat.
Do not cry out, therefore, against misunderstanding using restlessness and disenchantment, vinegar and gall.
There is heavenly merit in one who descends into the swamp without becoming contaminated in the task of salvation and readjustment.
A dense mass of matter becomes coated with mud when thrown into a muddy well, yet a ray of light visits the depths of the abyss and departs from it unchanged.
What would become of us if Jesus had not dimmed his own brilliance, making himself like our weakness, so that we might witness his redemptive mission?

Let us learn from him to descend while helping, without detriment to ourselves. And in this sense, we cannot forget the expressive declaration of Paul of Tarsus when he affirms that, for the victory of good, he became weak to the weak, making himself all things to all men, in order by all means to succeed in lifting up some.

messages.title: Fraternal Encouragement
paragraphs: “And my God shall supply all your need according to his riches in glory by Christ Jesus.” — PAUL (Philippians, 4:19)
Do not consider yourself alone in the purifying struggle, because the Lord will supply all our needs.
Lift your eyes on High and, from time to time, contemplate the rear. If you find yourself in a position to serve, help and move forward.
Remember the brother who lingers without resources on the bed of indigence.
Think of the companion who hears the sobbing of little children without the means to dry their tears.
Pause to see the sick person whom circumstances have driven from home.
Stop for a moment, casting a look of sympathy toward the homeless child.
Meditate on the anguish of the mentally unbalanced, confused in the eclipse of reason.
Reflect on the crippled who are shackled in painful immobility.
Think of maternal hearts tortured by the scarcity of bread and harmony in the domestic sanctuary.
Interrupt your hurried pace from time to time to help the blind person groping in the shadows.
It is possible, then, that your own pain will disappear from your sight.
If you have arms to help and a mind capable of reflecting on the good of your fellows, you are truly superior to a king who possessed a world of precious coins without the courage to help anyone.
When you manage to overcome your afflictions to create joy for others, the happiness of others will seek you out wherever you are in order to improvise your fortune.
May illness and sadness never impede your journey.
It is preferable that death surprises us in service rather than waiting for it in a luxury armchair.
Kindle, my brother, a new flame of encouragement in the center of your soul, and press onward... Be the angel of fraternity to those who follow you dominated by affliction, ignorance, and suffering.
When you plant the joy of living in the hearts that surround you, soon the flowers and fruits of your sowing will enrich your path.

messages.title: When There Is Light
paragraphs: “For the love of Christ compels us.” — PAUL (2 Corinthians, 5:14)
When Jesus finds a sanctuary in the heart of a man, his entire march is modified.
There is no longer room within him for unproductive adoration, for belief without works, for inoperative faith.
Something indefinable in earthly language disturbs his spirit.
The common mass categorizes him as maladjusted, however, the apprentice of the Gospel, reaching this condition, knows that the Divine Worker occupies the depths of his being, as it were.
All his conceptualization of existence is renewed.
What was pleasure yesterday is a broken idol today.
What represented a goal to be attained is a wrong itinerary that he leaves behind in abandonment.
He becomes a creature easy to content, but very difficult to please.
The Master's voice, persuasive and sweet, exhorts him to serve without rest.
His soul becomes a marvelous estuary where afflictions come to seek refuge, and therefore he suffers the constant pressure of others' pains.
Physical life itself appears to him as a tree upon which the Master suffers. His body is the living cross upon which the Lord tosses in crucifixion.
The only refuge where he rests is persevering work in the general good.
Dissatisfied, yet resigned; firm in faith, notwithstanding anguished; serving everyone, yet alone within himself, he follows down the road, impelled by hidden and indescribable goads...
This is the type of apprentice whom the love of Christ compels, in Paul's happy expression.
Celestial light scourges him from within until he abandons the lower zones definitively.
To the world, he will be maladjusted and mad. To Jesus, he is the vessel of blessings.
The flower is a lovely promise wherever it may be found. The ripe fruit, however, is food for Today.
Happy are those who spread hope, but blessed are the followers of Christ who sweat and suffer, day by day, so that their brothers may find comfort and nourishment in the Lord!

messages.title: Administration
paragraphs: “Give an account of your stewardship.” — JESUS (Luke, 16:2)

In essence, every man is a servant through the work he performs in the work of the Supreme Father, and, simultaneously, he is an administrator, since every human creature holds enormous possibilities in the plane where he labors.

A steward of the world is not only the one who turns gray-haired at the head of collective interests, in public or private enterprises, fighting a thousand petty disputes in order to fulfill the mission to which he is dedicated.
Every intelligence on Earth will give an account of the resources entrusted to it.
Fortune and authority are not the only values of which we must give an account today and tomorrow.
The body is a sacred temple.
Physical health is a treasure.
The opportunity to work is a blessing.
The possibility to serve is a divine favor.
The chance to learn is a liberating door.
Time is an inestimable patrimony.
The home is a gift from Heaven.
The friend is a benefactor.
Beneficial experience is a great conquest.
The occasion to live in harmony with the Lord, with one's fellows, and with Nature is a common glory for all.
The hour to help those less favored in resources or understanding is valuable.
The soil to sow, ignorance to be instructed, and pain to be consoled are appeals that Heaven sends without words to the entire world.
What do you do, therefore, with the precious talents that rest in your heart, in your hands, and on your path?
Watch over your own task in the good before the Eternal, for the moment will arrive when Divine Power will ask you: — “Give an account of your stewardship.”

messages.title: Spiritual Leaven
paragraphs: “Do you not know that a little leaven leavens the whole lump?” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 5:6)
Leaven is a substance that excites other substances, and our life is always a spiritual leaven with which we influence the lives of others.
No one lives alone. We carry within us thousands of expressions of other people's thoughts, and thousands of other people inevitably guard our mental action.
The rays of our influence intertwine with the emissions of all who know us directly or indirectly, and they weigh in the scale of the world for good or for ill.
Our words determine words in those who hear us, and whenever we are not sincere, it is likely that the interlocutor will be equally disloyal.

Our manners and customs generate manners and customs of the same nature around our steps, especially in those who find themselves in a position inferior to ours in the circles of experience and knowledge.

Our attitudes and acts create attitudes and acts of the same tenor in all who surround us, since what we do reaches the domain of others' observation, interfering in the center of elaboration of our fellows' mental forces.
The only process, therefore, of reforming by building is to accept the suggestions of good and practice them intensively through our actions.
At the origins of our determinations, however, resides the idea. The mind, as a result, is the seat of our personal action wherever we may be.
Thought is spiritual fermentation. First, it establishes attitudes, second, it generates habits, and then it governs expressions and words through which individuality influences life and the world.
Once a man's thought is regenerated, the path that leads him to the Lord is revealed to him straight and clean.

messages.title: Lord's Prayer
paragraphs: “Our Father…” — JESUS (Matthew, 6:9)
The grandeur of the Lord's Prayer will never be properly understood by us who receive its divine lessons. Every word within it possesses the radiance of sublime light.
From the beginning, the Divine Master establishes its foundations in God, teaching that the Supreme Giver of Life must constitute, for all of us, the beginning and the purpose of our tasks.
It is necessary to begin and continue in God, associating our impulses with the divine plan, so that our work is not lost in ruinous or useless movement.
The Universal Spirit of the Father shall preside over our most humble efforts, in the action of thinking and speaking, teaching and doing.
Then, with a simple possessive pronoun, the Master exalts the community. After God, Humanity shall be the fundamental theme of our lives.
Shall we understand the needs and afflictions, the evils and struggles of all those who surround us, or will we remain segregated in primitivist selfishness?
All the triumphs and failures that illuminate and obscure the Earth belong to us, in some way.
The sobs of one hemisphere resonate in the other.
The pain of our neighbor is a warning for our own home.

The error of a brother, examined at its foundations, is likewise ours, because we are imperfect components of a less perfect society, generating dangerous causes; and therefore, the tragedies and flaws of others affect us from within.
When we understand such a reality, the “empire of the self” begins to incorporate itself as a blessed cell into the sanctifying life.
Without love for God and Humanity, we are not sufficiently secure in prayer.
Our Father… — said Jesus to begin.
Father of the Universe… Our world…

Without associating ourselves with the Father's purposes in the tiny task we were permitted to execute, our prayer will often be a simple repetition of “I want,” invariably full of desires, but almost always empty of common sense and love.

messages.title: Divine Grafting
paragraphs: “And they also, if they do not continue in unbelief, will be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again.” — PAUL (Romans, 11:23)
Every creature is truly a spiritual plant, the object of meticulous care on the part of the Divine Sower.
Each man, as occurs with plants, presents distinct periods in existence. Sowing, germination, fertilization, development, usefulness, flowering, fructification, harvest…
On the eve of the fruit, the orchardist watches over the improvement of the tree with even greater affection. It is imperative that there be abundance and usefulness.
In the spiritual struggle, under identical circumstances, the Lord adopts the same rules toward us.
Upon reaching knowledge, reason, and experience, the Celestial Orchardist grants us precious resources of spiritual grafting, aiming at our sublimation for eternal life.

With each new day of your human experience, you receive valuable assistance so that the results of your present incarnation enrich you with divine light through the happiness you transmit to others. You are, however, a “conscious tree,” with the independence to accept or reject the renewing elements, with the freedom to register the blessing or despise it.
Observe attentively how many times the Sublime Sower calls you to the self-aggrandizement of your own being.

The grafting from on High seeks us out in a thousand ways. Today, it is in the edifying conversation of a companion. Tomorrow, it will be in a friendly book. Later, it will come through a seemingly insignificant gift along the path.

If you therefore keep the purpose of elevation, take advantage of Heaven's contribution, illuminating and sanctifying the inner temple. But if disbelief isolates your mind for the time being, winding your forces on the spool of selfishness, the graft of sublimation will seek you in vain, because you do not yet produce, in the recesses of the Spirit, the sap that favors Abundant Life.

messages.title: Let Us Follow Peace
paragraphs: “Seek peace and pursue it.” — PETER (1 Peter, 3:11)
There are many people who seek peace; rare are those, however, who try to follow it.

There are companions who desire tranquility by all means and sigh for it, placing it in various positions in life; yet, they expel it from themselves as soon as the Lord grants them the requested gifts.
