This one asks for material fortune, believing it to be the bearer of the coveted peace; however, with the appearance of abundant money, he tortures himself with a thousand problems, for he does not know how to distribute, help, administer, and spend with simplicity.

Another begs for the blessing of marriage, but when Heaven grants it, he does not know how to be a brother to the companion the Father has entrusted to him, losing himself through exasperations of every kind.

Another still demands special titles of confidence in expressive public utility tasks, but upon seeing himself honored with popularity and the expectations of many, he repulses the blessings of work and retreats in terror.
Peace is not bodily indolence. It is the health and joy of the spirit.

If it is true that every creature seeks it in their own way, it is imperative to recognize, nevertheless, that legitimate peace results from the balance between our desires and the Lord's purposes, in the position in which we find ourselves.
Once we receive the work that Celestial Trust permits us to perform, it is essential that we know how to use the opportunity in favor of our elevation and improvement.
Peter said — “Seek peace and pursue it.”

Yet, there is no real tranquility without Christ within us, regardless of any situation in which we may be placed, and the formula for our soul's integration with Jesus is invariable: — “Deny yourselves, take up your cross, and follow me.” Without this adaptation of our human learner effort to the renewing impulse of the Divine Master, instead of peace, we shall always have renewed war within the heart.

messages.title: Fattened Hearts
paragraphs: “You have fattened your hearts as in a day of slaughter.” — (JAMES, 5:5)
For the prosperity and improvement of the world, the Sun works, which is the supreme expression of Vital Divinity in the earthly firmament.
The worm collaborates in the intimacy of the soil, preparing a suitable nest for the seeds.
The breeze contributes by exchanging the pollen of flowers.
Water labors incessantly, sustaining physical life and purifying it.
The tree serves by flowering, bearing fruit, and regenerating the atmosphere.
The animal cooperates, assisting human achievements, sweating and dying so that there may be normal life in the domain of higher intelligence.
An infallible law of work governs the Universe.
Movement and order, in the constancy of their benefits, constitute its essential characteristics. There are, however, millions of people who feel exempt from the glory of serving.

For such creatures, in whose brains reason sleeps blunt and empty, work means banishment and humiliation, hell and suffering. They pursue sinful facilities with the same instinct of novelty as a fly seeking debris. Having achieved the inferior solution they sought, they circumscribe their hours and possibilities to an unbridled attachment to themselves, imitating a pool of stagnant water that easily poisons itself.

Deep down, they are “fattened hearts,” according to the apostle's apt expression. They weave dense webs of hatred and selfishness, indifference and vanity, pride and indolence around themselves, and gravitate downward. Descending, descending through the heavy vibrations they embrace, they roll slowly into the bosom of lower lives, where it is natural for them to find the demands of many who take advantage of them, much like the common man who uses fat animals for slaughter.

messages.title: The Living Lamp
paragraphs: “Nor do they light a lamp and put it under a basket, but on a lampstand, and it gives light to all who are in the house.” — JESUS (Matthew, 5:15)
Many learners interpreted these words of the Master as a call to systematic preaching, and went wild with vehement speeches everywhere.
Others assumed that the Lord imposed upon them the obligation to violate their neighbors through compulsory propaganda of their belief, according to their particular point of view.
Indeed, the edifying sermon and fraternal help are indispensable in spreading the divine benefits of faith.
Without the word, the distribution of knowledge is almost impossible.
Without brotherly support, fraternity will not materialize in the world.
Jesus' assertion, however, goes further. Let us heed the symbol of the lamp.
The brightness of the lamp consumes force or fuel. Without the sacrifice of energy or oil, there is no light.
For us, here, the material of maintenance is our opportunity, our resource, our life. Our existence is the living lamp.
It is a lamentable error to expend our forces without profit for anyone, under the measure of our selfishness, our vanity, or our personal limitation.
Let us place our possibilities at the disposal of our fellow men. No one should hoard the advantages of earthly experience solely for themselves.
Each Spirit temporarily incarnated in the human circle enjoys immense prerogatives regarding the diffusion of good, if they persevere in the observance of Universal Love.

Preach, therefore, the revelations from on High, making them more beautiful and brilliant on your lips; urge relatives and friends to accept the imperishable truths, but do not forget that the living lamp of spiritual illumination is the perfect image of yourself.

Transform your energies into redeeming kindness and understanding for everyone, spending for this purpose the oil of your goodwill, in renunciation and sacrifice, and your life in Christ will truly begin to shine.

messages.title: He Who Serves, Progresses
paragraphs: “For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve.” — JESUS (Mark, 10:45)
Nature, everywhere, is a divine laboratory that elects the spirit of service as the normal process of evolution.
Attentive eyes observe cooperation and assistance in the humblest manifestations of the lower kingdoms.
The pit serves the seed. The seed will enrich man.
The wind helps the flowers by exchanging their principles of life. The flowers will produce blessed fruits.
Rivers entrust themselves to the sea. The sea makes the fertilizing cloud.
To maintain human life at its current stage, thousands of animals die on Earth from hour to hour, giving flesh and blood for the benefit of humans.
It can be inferred from such a struggle that service is the price of the liberating or sanctifying journey.

The person who gets used to being invariably served in all situations does not know how to act alone in any situation. The creature who serves for the pleasure of being useful always progresses and finds a thousand resources within themselves to solve all problems. The former crystallizes; the latter develops.

Whoever complains excessively about others, because they do not appreciate moving themselves to satisfy common needs, ends up enslaving themselves to servants, ruining their day when they cannot find someone to set their table. Whoever learns to serve, however, knows how to reduce all the embarrassments of the path, discovering new tracks.

A Gospel learner who does not improvise the joy of helping others remains very far from true discipleship, since the faithful companion of the Good News is informed that Jesus came to serve, and watches over the benefit of all until the end of the struggle.
If there is more joy in giving than in receiving, there is more happiness in serving than in being served.
He who serves, progresses…

messages.title: Let Us Move Beyond
paragraphs: “Therefore, leaving the discussion of the elementary principles of Christ, let us go on to perfection, not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 6:1)
Accepting the power of Jesus, holding the certainty of one's own resurrection beyond death, and comforting oneself before the benefits of belief constitute a rudimentary phase in Gospel learning.
Practicing the lessons received, adapting our daily personal experiences to them, represents the living and sanctifying course.
The student who never leaves alphabet exercises never enters the luminous mental domain of the great masters.

It is not enough to place our soul at the portico of the temple and reverently bend our knees there; it is imperative to return to the ordinary paths and materialize within ourselves the principles of redeeming faith, sublimating common life.

What can be said of the worker who only visits the door of his workshop, praising its greatness, without, however, dedicating himself to the work it demands? What can be said of an admirably equipped ship that lived indefinitely on the shore without sailing?

There are thousands of believers of the Good News in this lamentable position of stagnation. They are almost always correct people in all the rudiments of Christ's doctrine. They believe, adore, and comfort themselves irreproachably; yet, they do not march forward to become wiser and nobler. They do not know how to act, struggle, or suffer when left alone from a human point of view.

Guarding against such evils, Paul stated with profound accuracy: — “Leaving the rudiments of Jesus' doctrine, let us press on to perfection, refraining from repeating many repentances, for then we will be nothing more than authors of dead works.”

Let us thus avoid the position of the student who studies… and never harmonizes with the lesson, remembering also that while repentance is useful from time to time, repenting at every hour is a sign of stubbornness and addiction.

messages.title: In Instrumentality
paragraphs: “How will it be known what is played on the flute or on the harp?” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 14:7)

Every companion of Christian service should consider themselves an instrument in the hands of the Divine Master, so that the sublime harmony of the Gospel becomes irreproachable for the complete victory of good.
Yet, while the unlimited wisdom of the Celestial Sender remains sovereign and perfect, earthly receivers sin through lamentable deficiencies.
This one has faith, but does not know how to tolerate the shortcomings of his neighbor.
That one Christianly supports the weaknesses of his neighbor, yet possesses no energy even to govern his own impulses.
Still another is kind and trusting, but avoids study and meditation, fostering ignorance.
Another is imaginative and enthusiastic, yet subtly escapes the effort of physical labor.
One is an excellent counselor, yet does not sanctify his own actions.
Another retains brilliant speech in doctrinal preaching, yet is a passionate cultivator of lesser anecdotes with which he disfigures the respect for the revelation he bears.
This one esteems bodily chastity, but goes wild acquiring easy money.
Another further along has managed to detach himself from possessions of gold and land, house and mill, but cultivates a true fire in the flesh.
Our imperfection as followers of the Good News is indisputable. For this very reason, we hold the title of learners.
The Planet is not a finished paradise, and we, in turn, are very far from angelic status.
Yet, whether obeying or administering, teaching or fighting, it is essential to tune our instrument of service to the Master's pitch if we do not wish to harm His works.
Let us avoid insecure, indistinct, or disturbing execution, offering our full goodwill to the task that falls to us, and the Divine Kingdom will manifest itself more rapidly wherever we may be.

messages.title: Hindrances
paragraphs: “Let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which so easily ensnares us, and let us run with endurance the race that is set before us.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 12:1)
The great apostle to the Gentiles depicts Christian work as a race of the soul in the broad stadium of life.

Paul, naturally resorting to this image, was thinking of the Greek games of his time, and without referring to the enthusiasm and beneficial emulation that should preside over such an effort, let us recall solely the initial act of the competitors.
Each participant in the contest stripped off their outer garments to dispute the match in clothing as light as possible.
Thus, also, in acquiring eternal life, it is imperative that we divest ourselves of the suffocating attire of the Spirit.
It is necessary for the heart to become light, shedding every useless burden.
In the brightness of the Good News, the disciple finds himself before the Master, invested with sanctifying obligations toward all creatures.
Inhibitions against the victorious race tend to appear every day.
We encounter them frequently in the most insignificant steps of the path. Every hour an unexpected hindrance arises.
It is the cold and uncomprehending relative.
The dryness of the hearts around us.
The companion who deserted.
The woman who disappeared, pursuing inferior objectives.
The friend who deluded himself on the islands of rest, deciding to delay the journey.
The co-worker whom death took away.
Unjustified hatred.
Indifference to the appeals of good.
The persecution of evil.
The torment of discord.
The Good News, however, offers the Christian the conquest of divine glory.
If we wish to reach the goal, let us set aside every hindrance and run with perseverance in the test of love and light that is set before us.

messages.title: Are You Sick?
paragraphs: “And the prayer of faith will save the sick, and the Lord will raise him up.” — (JAMES, 5:15)
All human creatures fall ill, yet rare are those who consider real healing.
If you find yourself sick, do not believe that medicinal action, through the mouth or pores, can fully restore you.
The pill helps, the injection improves, however, never forget that true evils proceed from the heart.
The mind is a creative source.
Life gradually shapes around your footsteps what you desire.
What is the use of external medication if you remain sad, downcast, or unsubmissive?

At other times, you ask for the help of human doctors or spiritual benefactors, but as soon as the first improvements appear, you abandon the remedy or wholesome advice and return to the same abuses that led you to illness.
How can health be regenerated if you waste long hours in positions of anger or discouragement?

Rare indignation, when just and constructive in the general interest, is always a good thing when we know how to orient it in services of elevation; however, daily indignation regarding everything, everyone, and ourselves is a pernicious habit with unpredictable consequences.
Discouragement, in turn, is an anesthetic climate that numbs and destroys.
And what can be said of backbiting or uselessness, with which you spend valuable and long time in fruitless conversation, extinguishing your forces?

What miraculous genius will grant you organic equilibrium if you do not know how to be silent or excuse, if you neither help nor understand, if you do not humble yourself for superior designs, nor seek harmony with men?
No matter how much the helpers of Earth and the Spiritual Plane rush to your favor, you devour your own energies, an imprudent victim of indirect suicide.
If you are sick, my friend, above any medication, learn to pray and understand, to help and prepare your heart for the Great Change.

Detach yourself from transitory goods lent to you by Divine Power, according to the Law of Use, and remember that you will, now or later, be led back to the Greater Life, where we always encounter our own conscience.
Flee from brutality. Enrich your factors of personal sympathy through the practice of fraternal love.
Seek intimacy with wisdom through study and meditation.
Do not stain your path.
Serve always. Work in the expansion of good.
Keep loyalty to the superior ideal that illuminates your heart and remain convinced that if you cultivate the prayer of living faith, in all your steps, here or beyond, the Lord will raise you up.
messages.note: This message was originally published in 1950 by LAKE and is the 27th lesson of Part 1 of the book “Nosso livro” (Our Book).

messages.title: Have You Received the Light?
paragraphs: “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?” — (ACTS, 19:2)
The Catholic receives the sacrament of baptism and gains a seal for personal identification in the statistics of the Church to which they belong.
The reformer of evangelical letters enters the same ritual and acquires a number in the religious register of the temple they join.
The Spiritist joins this or that entity consecrated to our Consoling Doctrine and verbally participates in the renewing work.
All these learners of the Christian school are comforted and rejoice.

Some share the contentment of the Eucharistic table which revives their hope in Heaven; others sing together, exalting Divine Goodness, gathering abundant material for encouragement on the sanctifying journey; others still gather around ardent prayer, receiving luminous and revealing messages from celestial emissaries, which consolidate their conviction in immortality.

All these positions, however, are of profit, consolation, and advantage. It is imperative to recognize, nevertheless, that if the seed is aided by fertilization, water, and sun, it is compelled to work within itself in order to produce.
Meditate, therefore, on the sublimity of the apostolic inquiry: — “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?”
Avail yourself of the revelation with which faith benefits and sanctifies your path, spreading goodness.
Your life can become a fountain of blessings for others and for your soul if you truly apply yourself to the Master of Love.
Remember that it is not you who waits for the Divine Light. It is the Divine Light, the force of Heaven by your side, that remains waiting for you.

messages.title: Coming to Oneself
paragraphs: “But when he came to himself…” — (LUKE, 15:17)
This short excerpt from the parable of the prodigal son awakens valuable considerations concerning life.

Judas dreamed of the political dominion of the Gospel, interested in the compulsory transformation of creatures; however, when he came to himself, it was too late, because the Divine Friend had been handed over to cruel judges.
Other characters of the Good News, however, came to themselves in time to accomplish saving rectification.

Mary of Magdala had placed her intimate life in the hands of perverse geniuses; nevertheless, coming to herself under the influence of Christ, she observes the lost time and conquers the highest spiritual dignity through humility and renunciation.

Peter, intimidated by threats of persecution and suffering, denies the Divine Master; however, coming to himself when faced with the compassionate gaze of Jesus, he weeps bitterly and advances, resolute, toward his rehabilitation in the apostolate.

Paul entrusts himself to a delirious passion against Christianity and furiously pursues all manifestations of the nascent Gospel; however, coming to himself before the sublime call of the Lord, he repents of his errors and becomes one of the most brilliant collaborators of the Christian triumph.

There is a great mass of believers of all shades, in the most diverse lines of faith, yet perturbation and doubt reign among them, because they live immersed in purely verbalistic interpretations of celestial revelation, in fantasist pleasures, in the falsehoods of the carnal hour, or magnetically bound to the shell of life to which they unwarily cling. For them, joy is satisfied immediate interest and peace is the fleeting sensation of well-being of the fleshly body, without any pain, so that they may eat and drink without hindrance.
Come, however, to yourself, under the blessing of Jesus, and transferring yourself then from inertia to incessant work for your redemption, you will observe, surprised, how different life is.

messages.title: On Our March
paragraphs: “Jesus asked him: — ‘What do you want me to do for you?’ ” — (MARK, 10:51)
Each learner in their lesson.
Each worker in the task entrusted to them.
Each vessel in its utility.
Each fighter with the necessary test.
Thus, each of us has an individual testimony on the path of life.
Sometimes, we fail in the commitments we have assumed and incur infinite debts.
In the restorative service, however, we cry out for the Lord's mercy, begging Him for compassion and help.
The question addressed by the Master to the blind man of Jericho is, nevertheless, quite expressive: “What do you want me to do for you?”
The inquiry makes it perceptible that the delicate position of the interested party adjusted to the imperatives of the Law.

Nothing happens contrary to the Divine Designs. Bartimaeus, the blind man, knew how to respond, requesting vision. However, how many people beg access to the presence of the Savior and, when questioned by Him, respond to their own detriment?

Let us remember that, at times, we lose the earthly home in order to learn the way to the heavenly home; on many occasions, we are abandoned by the most agreeable human ties, so that we may return to divine bonds; there are times when the wounds of the body are called to heal the sores of the soul, and situations in which paralysis teaches the preciousness of movement.

It is natural that we ask for the Master's help in our difficulties and sorrows; meanwhile, let us not forget to work for good, in the most afflictive passages of rectification and ascension, convinced that we find ourselves invariably in the most just and profitable opportunity for work that we deserve, and that perhaps we may not know, right away, how to choose a better one.

messages.title: Manfully
paragraphs: “Be watchful, stand firm in the faith, act like men, be strong.” — PAUL (1 CORINTHIANS, 16:13)
Be watchful in the common struggle.
Remain firm in the faith before the storm.
Act manfully in all difficult trials.
Be strong in pain, to keep its lesson of light.
Paul's advice to the Corinthians still clothes itself, even today, with surprising timeliness.
To conquer the substantial values of redemption, it is imperative to preserve the fortitude of soul of one who trusts in the Lord and in oneself.

A shower of uncalled-for tears is of no avail in the face of a committed fault. To repent of any evil gesture is a duty, but to weep over it indefinitely is to steal time from the service of rectification.
Certainly, deliberate evil is a crime; however, unthought-of error is valuable teaching whenever man inclines toward the designs of the Lord.
Without moral resistance, in the whirlpool of purifying conflicts, the noblest heart shatters. It is not up to us, therefore, to rest in the service of elevation.
It is natural that we may stumble many times. It is understandable that we frequently wound ourselves on the thorns of the path.
Lamentable, however, will be our situation every time we demand a soft bed of undue consolations, interrupting the march toward the Heights.

The Christian is not an apprentice of false rest. As a disciple of a Master who served without partiality until the cross, it is incumbent upon him to work in the sowing and reaping of the Infinite Good, watching, helping, and acting manfully.

messages.title: Problems of Love
paragraphs: “…that your love may abound more and more in full knowledge and all discernment.” — PAUL (PHILIPPIANS, 1:9)
Love is the divine force of the Universe.
It is imperative, however, to be very vigilant so that we do not divert it from its righteous application.

When a man devotes himself absolutely to his perishable coffers, this energy in his heart is called “avarice”; when he torments himself exclusively in defense of what he possesses, considering himself the center of life in the place where he finds himself, this same force turns within him into “egoism”; when he only sees reasons to praise what he represents, what he feels, and what he does, with manifest disrespect for the values of others, the feeling that predominates in his orbit is called “envy.”

Paul, writing to the loving Philippian community, formulates an indication of lofty reach. He assures that “love must grow more and more in knowledge and discernment, so that the learner may approve the things that are excellent.”
Let us instruct ourselves, therefore, to know.
Let us educate ourselves to discern.
Intellectual culture and moral refinement are imperatives of life, enabling us to manifest love within the empire of sublimation that brings us closer to God.

Let us heed the apostolic counsel and grow in spiritual values for eternity, because, many times, our love is simply wanting, and solely with “wanting” it is possible to thoughtlessly disfigure the most beautiful pictures of life.
messages.note:
[1] In the book “Follow Me”, this lesson, from this point on, was reproduced with the addition of the following three paragraphs:
“Hatred is commonly yesterday's poisoned love.”
“Jealousy is love dressed in tearing thorns.”
“Arrogance is a deranged love for oneself.”

messages.title: Demonstrations of Heaven
paragraphs: “They said to him then: What sign do you do, that we may see and believe you?” — (JOHN, 6:30)
In all times, when someone on Earth refers to the things of Heaven, a veritable multitude of inquirers steps forward asking for objective demonstrations of the announced truths.
Thus it is that modern mediums are constantly besieged by the demands of those who set out in search of spiritual life.
This one is clairvoyant and must give proof of what he identifies.
That one writes under supernormal conditions and is constrained to provide testimony of the sources of his inspiration.
That other one materializes the disembodied and, therefore, is summoned to public test.
However, many people forget that all the Lord's creatures exteriorize the signs that pertain to them.
The mineral is recognized by its utility.
The tree is selected by its fruits.
The firmament spreads messages of light.
Water gives news of its incessant work.
Air scatters information, without words, of its power in the maintenance of life.
And among men, the same imperatives prevail. Each brother of struggle is examined by his characteristics.
The foolish gives himself to be known by his childishness.
The understanding one reveals signs of prudence.
The best one demonstrates the virtues peculiar to him.
Thus, the learner of the Gospel, when requesting revelations from Heaven for the earthly journey, must not forget the need to reveal himself firmly disposed to walk toward Heaven.
There was a day when the vulgar crowd addressed the Savior Himself who benefited them, asking: — “What sign do you do, that we may see and believe you?”

Imagine, then, that if such an interrogation was directed to the Lord of Life, what inquiry will not be made from on high of us, every time we beg for signs from Heaven in order to fulfill our simple duty?

messages.title: Intimate Altar
paragraphs: “We have an altar.” — PAUL (HEBREWS, 13:10)

Until now, we have built altars everywhere, revering the Master and Lord. Of gold, of marble, of wood, of clay, inlaid with perfumes, precious items, and flowers, we have erected sanctuaries and summoned the contribution of art for the touches of artificial lighting and exterior beauty.
Once the monument of faith is materialized, we kneel in an attitude of prayer and seek divine inspiration.

Indeed, all movement in this direction is respectable, even when we commit the common error of forgetting the hungry of the road in favor of the pomp of worship, because love and gratitude to Celestial Power, even when poorly guided, deserve veneration.
However, it is imperative to grow toward the greater life.
The Master Himself warned us, by the Samaritan woman, that times would come when the Father would be worshiped in spirit and truth. And Paul adds that we have an altar.
The ultimate purpose of temples of stone is to awaken our conscience.
The awakened Christian, however, walks officiating as a priest of himself, glorifying love before hatred, peace before discord, serenity in the face of perturbation, good in sight of evil…
Let us not forget, therefore, the intimate altar that it behooves us to consecrate to Divine Power and Celestial Goodness.

To appear before the altars of stone with a soul closed to the light and inspiration of the Master is the same as casting an impermeable chest of darkness into full solar clarity. If luminous waves continue to be luminous waves, shadows do not alter likewise.

Let us present, therefore, to the Lord our offerings and sacrifices in blessed quotas of love for our neighbor, worshiping Him through the altar of the heart, and let us press on in the work we are called to accomplish.

messages.title: Helmet of Hope
paragraphs: “And for a helmet the hope of salvation.” — PAUL (1 THESSALONIANS, 5:8)

The helmet is the defense of the head where life situates the seat of the manifestation of thought, and Paul could not remember a symbol more appropriate to the attire of the Christian brain than the helmet of the hope of salvation.

If feeling is often subject to the attacks of violent anger, reasoning on many occasions suffers the siege of discouragement before the struggle for the victory of good, which cannot wane at any time.
Anesthetic rays are unleashed upon the spirit of learners by all forces contrary to the saving Gospel.
The demand of everyone and the indifference of many seek to crystallize the disciple's energy, scattering his noble impulses or neutralizing his ideals of renewal.
However, it is imperative to always await the development of the latent principles of good, even when transitory evil extends roots in all directions.

It is necessary to await the strengthening of the weak, like the farmer who does not lose confidence in tender shoots; to await the joy and courage of the sad, with the same expectation of the florist who counts on revelations of perfume and beauty in the garden full of bare branches.

It is imperative to recognize, nevertheless, that the Christian's serenity never represents an inoperative attitude, as it continuously acts and improves people, things, and situations in all the particularities of the path.

For this very reason, perhaps, the apostle does not refer to a protective cap. A hat almost always indicates a walk, rest, leisure, when it does not define a convention in exterior attire, according to established fashion. A helmet, however, is the garb of struggle, effort, defensiveness.

And the disciple of Jesus is an effective combatant against evil, who does not have much time to dwell on himself, nor can he demand too much rest when he knows that the Master Himself remains in active and edifying labor. Let us safeguard, therefore, our thought with the helmet of faithful hope and press on toward the supreme victory of good.

messages.title: See and Follow
paragraphs: “One thing I know, that whereas I was blind, now I see.” — (JOHN, 9:25)

Although the renewing work of the Gospel, in the circles of consolation and preaching, unfolds before the masses, sowing miracles of comfort in the soul of the people, the subtle and almost unknown service of making use of the Good News is always individual and non-transferable.

Learners of the Christian life, in the ordinary activity of the path, enjoy the concept of normality, but if they do not enjoy observable advantages in the immediacy of human experience—such as those of consolation, encouragement, or material prosperity—in order to imprint the living teaching of Jesus in their own lives, they pass into the category of strange people, often even before their own fellow ministers.
Having reached such a position, and if he knows how to take advantage of the sublime opportunity through submission and diligence, the disciple experiences a complete transposition of plane.
He modifies the table of values surrounding him.
He knows where eternal foundations are hidden.
He descries new spheres of struggle through an inner vision that others do not understand.
He discovers different motives for elevation through personal sacrifice and identifies higher sources of incentive for his own effort.
In view of this, he frequently provokes heated discussions regarding the attitude he adopts before Jesus.
Because he sees with greater clarity the instructions revealed by the Master, he is taken for a fanatic or a retrograde, an idiot or a madman.

If, however, you effectively seek redemption with the Lord, proceed secure of yourself; observe, without affliction and without discouragement, the contentions that the genuine action of Jesus within you receives from uncomprehending and stationary hearts, repeat the words of the blind man who attained sight, and press forward.

messages.title: Beyond Others
paragraphs: “Do not even the tax collectors do the same?” — JESUS (MATTHEW, 5:46)

To work impeccably during regular hours, to care for domestic duties, to satisfy legal demands, and to practice correctness of conduct, doing enough in the sphere of unavoidable obligations, are tasks peculiar to believers and non-believers on the daily path.
Jesus, however, expects something more from the disciple.
Do you respond to the imperatives of daily work by creating courage, joy, and encouragement around you?
Do you know how to improvise good where other people proved fruitless?
Do you successfully make use of the material that someone else discarded as useless?
Do you wait with patience where others despaired?
In the position of a believer, do you maintain the spirit of service where the non-believer has frozen the spirit of action?
Do you share the joy of your friends without envy and jealousy, and do you partake in the suffering of your adversaries without false superiority and without fanfare?
What do you give of yourself in the ministry of charity?
Ensuring the continuation of the species, revealing general utility, and adapting to the movements of life are characteristics of unreasoning animals themselves.
The ordinary man, for many millennia now, has been eating and drinking, sleeping and acting without fundamental differences in the collective order.

From twenty centuries to this part, however, blessed light shines on Earth with the teachings of Christ, inviting us to scale the summits of higher spirituality. Not everyone perceives it yet, notwithstanding its encompassing everyone. But for those who rejoice in its extraordinary blessings, the challenge of the Master arises, inquiring about what extraordinary thing we are doing.

messages.title: The Word of the Cross
paragraphs: “For the message of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 1.18)
The message of the cross has been painful in all times.
From Calvary, a voice descended to the world, at first unpleasant and incomprehensible.
In the Master's martyrology lay all the arguments of superficially absolute negation.
The complete abandonment of loved ones.
The agonizing thirst.
Irremediable capitulation.
Spontaneous forgiveness that expressed full humiliation.
Sarcasm and ridicule among thieves.
Defeat without defense.
Infamous death.
Yet Christ uses apparent failure to teach the path of the Eternal Resurrection, demonstrating that the "self" will never direct itself toward God without self-improvement and self-sublimation.

Even today, the language of the cross is foolishness to those who remain endlessly in the circle of reincarnations of low spiritual content; such creatures seek only to ally themselves with death, exterminating the most beautiful blossoms of feeling. They dominate many, incapable of self-mastery, hoarding treasures that imprudence undoes and weaving dark threads of obsessing passions in which they succumb time and again, like a spider trapped in its own webs.

Let us repeat the message of the cross to the brother who drowns in the flesh, and he will classify us as fools, but all of us, who have been saved from greater falls by the warnings of renewing faith, are informed that in supreme testimonies, the disciple follows the Master, just as the Master ascended to the Father, in the hidden glory of crucifixion.

messages.title: Breastplate of Charity
paragraphs: “Let us be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and charity.” — PAUL (1 Thessalonians, 5.8)
Paul was infinitely wise when he advised the breastplate of charity to the workers of the light.
In favor of the desirable success in the mission of love to which we propose ourselves, in the company of Christ, it is first of all indispensable to preserve the heart.

And if we do not harbor the fountain of feeling in the vibrations of ardent love, served by an elevated understanding in the circles of sanctifying experience in which we struggle in the earthly arena, it is very difficult to succeed in the task entrusted to us by the Lord.
Permanent irritation in the face of ignorance delays the advantages of beneficial teaching.
Excessive indignation before weakness exterminates the fragile germs of virtue.
Frequent anger in the field of struggle can multiply our enemies without any profit to the work to which we are devoted.
Too much severity before people still strangers to the benefits of discipline is accompanied by counterproductive effects due to a lack of education in the environment in which it manifests.

Understanding, thus, that the Christian finds themselves in a true state of struggle, in which, at times, we are confronted by suggestions of intemperate irritation, inopportune indignation, unjustified anger, or destructive severity, the apostle to the Gentiles prescribed to us the breastplate of charity as a defensive sentinel of the central organs of the expression of life.
It is indispensable to arm the heart with infinite fraternal understanding to attend to the ministry in which we are engaged.
The conviction and enthusiasm of faith are enough to begin honorably, but to continue the service, and finish it successfully, no one can dispense with patient, benign, and invincible charity.

messages.title: Persist and Go On
paragraphs: “Therefore, lift up the hands that hang down, and the feeble knees.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 12.12)

The inattentive farmer almost always listens to the suggestions of fatigue. He interrupts his work because of the storm, and the flood steals his started work and annihilates his fledgling courage. He rests because of the calluses the hoe gave him, and worms take it upon themselves to nullify his labor.
He lifts his hands at the beginning, but does not know how to "lift them up again" in the continuation of the task, and loses the harvest.

The traveler, in turn, when unvigilant, does not know how to properly reach the end of the journey. He complains about the heat and falls asleep in the shadow of illusory shelters, where unexpected perils surprise him. At other times, he emphasizes the importance of his bloodied feet and lies down by the wayside, transforming himself into an ordinary beggar.
He uses healthy knees, yet is unwilling to mobilize them when disjointed and wounded, losing the joy of reaching the goal at the scheduled time.
Thus it happens with us on the spiritual journey.
The struggle is the means. Improvement is the end.
Disillusionment bitters. Difficulty complicates.
Ingratitude hurts. Malice wounds.

However, if we abandon the field of the heart because we do not know how to lift our hands again in persistent effort, the worms of discouragement will proliferate precipitately at the center of our dearest hopes; and if we do not wish to march with disjointed knees, it is possible we may be held back by the shadow of false refuges for consecutive centuries.

messages.title: With Jesus and For Jesus
paragraphs: In the introduction to The Spirits' Book [Prolegomena], we gather from Allan Kardec this expressive statement:

“Communications between the spiritual world and the corporeal world are in the natural order of things and do not constitute a supernatural fact, so much so that traces of such communications are found among all peoples and in all epochs. Today they have become generalized and patent to all.”
In item VIII of the concluding pages of the same book, the Codifier asserts with certainty:

“Jesus came to show men the path of true good. Why, having sent Him to remind them of His law which was forgotten, would God not send the Spirits today, in order to remind men of it once more, and with greater precision, when they forget it to sacrifice everything to pride and greed?”

And we know that, in between, the great book that laid the foundations of Spiritism deals, among valuable subjects, with the laws of adoration, work, society, progress, equality, liberty, justice, love, charity, and moral perfection, as well as hopes and consolations.

We refer to such statements to recall that the spiritist phenomenon has always been present in the world, in all evolutionary stages of Humanity, and that Allan Kardec, from the beginning of the ministry to which he dedicated himself, imprinted on his work the religious character from which it could not be absent, even emphasizing that Spiritism is strong because it rests upon the very foundations of Religion: God, the soul, and future punishments and rewards.

We fully accept the scientific and philosophical bases upon which Spiritism rests, which afford us the acquisition of “reasoned faith capable of facing reason face to face”; however, upon such foundations, we see it, still and always, in its condition of restored Christianity, perfecting souls and renewing life on Earth for the victory of Infinite Good, under the aegis of Christ, our Divine Master and Lord.

The apostle of the Codification was not unaware of the high mandate regarding the principles he was compiling, and for this very reason, from the very first hour, he concerned himself with the moral imperatives with which the New Revelation is clothed, having emphasized that the consequences of Spiritism are summarized in improving man and, consequently, making him less unhappy through the practice of the purest evangelical morality.

We know that the retort does not sublimate character and that philosophical discussion has nothing to do with charity and justice. With all our respect, therefore, for the philosophy that inquires and the science that clarifies, we will always recognize in Spiritism the Gospel of the Lord, revived and active, to install with Jesus the Cosmic Religion of Universal Love and Divine Wisdom upon Earth.
Disembodied spirits by the millions and in all degrees of intelligence swarm the world, requesting, just as the incarnate do, the assistance of education.

We cannot, therefore, accompany those who make of our Redemptive Doctrine a mere debating tribune or a simple hunt for demonstrations of survival, merely for the realization of literary tournaments or for long parlor chats and drawing-room anecdotes, without any spiritual consequence for the path proper to them.
Let us thus study the lessons of the Divine Master and learn them in daily practice.

Death will reunite us all for the understanding of true life… And, knowing that justice will define us according to our works, let us embrace the Kardecian Codification, pressing forward, with Jesus and for Jesus.

messages.title: To Work
paragraphs: “How is it then, brethren? Whenever you come together, each of you has a psalm, has a teaching, has a tongue, has a revelation, has an interpretation. Let all things be done for edification.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 14.26)
The church of Corinth was struggling with some rather severe difficulties when Paul wrote the observation transcribed here.

The content of the letter addressed various spiritual problems of the companions of the Peloponnesus, but we can isolate the verse and apply it to certain situations of the new Christian groups formed within the environment of Spiritism in the revival of the Gospel.
We almost always notice an intense preoccupation among workers regarding novelties in phenomenology and revelation.
Some groups tend to paralyze their activities when they do not have trained mediums. Why?
No medium will definitively solve the fundamental problem of the companions' illumination.
Our spiritual task would be absurd if it were circumscribed to the mechanical attendance of many at any given center, simply to mark the effort of a very few.

Let the disciples convince themselves that work and achievement belong to all and that it is imperative for each one to move within the edifying service that pertains to them. No one should allege an absence of novelties when massive concessions from the higher Sphere await the firm decision of the willing learner to understand life and elevate themselves.

When you gather, remember the doctrine and the revelation, the power to speak and to interpret which you already possess, and put your hands to the work of good and light in indispensable self-improvement.

messages.title: Think a Little
paragraphs: “The works that I do in my Father’s name, they bear witness of me.” — JESUS (John, 10.25)

It is common for ordinary man to be preoccupied with family traditions and earthly institutions to which he nominally clings, exalting himself in the conventional titles that identify his personality.

However, in true life, no creature is known by such processes. Each Spirit carries within itself the living history of its own deeds, and only the works performed reveal the value or demerit of each one.

With this statement, we do not wish to assert that the word is devoid of its undeniable advantages; nevertheless, it is necessary to understand that the spoken word is also a profound potential received from Infinite Goodness as a divine resource, making it indispensable to know what we are accomplishing with this gift of the Eternal Lord.
Jesus' statement in this regard is clothed in imperishable beauty.
What would we say of a Savior who established rules for Humanity without sharing its difficulties and impediments?

Christ began His divine mission among country men, lived among irritated doctors and rebellious sinners, united with the sick and afflicted, ate the hard bread of humble fishermen, and ended His holy task between two thieves.
What more do you desire? If you await an easy life and prominent situations in the world, remember the Master and think a little.

messages.title: The Plow
paragraphs: “And Jesus said to him, ‘No one, having put his hand to the plow, and looking back, is fit for the Kingdom of God.’” — (LUKE, 9.62)
Here, we see Jesus use one of the most beautiful symbols in the edification of the Divine Kingdom.
Indeed, had He wished, the Master could have created other images. He could have referred to world laws, social duties, or prophetic texts, but He prefers to ground His teaching on simpler bases.

The plow is a tool of all times. It is heavy, demands collaborative effort between man and machine, provokes sweat and care, and above all, wounds the earth so that it may produce. It builds the cradle for the seeds, and in its passage, the ground yields so that rain, sun, and fertilizers can be properly utilized.

It is necessary, therefore, that the sincere disciple take lessons from the Divine Cultivator, embracing the plow of responsibility in the edifying struggle, without ever removing their hands from it, so as to avoid grave damage to the "earth of oneself."

Let us meditate on lost opportunities, on the rains of mercy that fell upon us and passed without any benefit to our spirit, on the sun of love that has been vivifying us for many millennia, on the precious fertilizers we have refused because we preferred idleness and indifference.
Let us examine all this and reflect upon Jesus' symbol.
A plow promises service, discipline, affliction, and fatigue; however, one must not forget that after it come the sowing and the harvest, bread on the plate, and well-stocked barns.

messages.title: Before Serving
paragraphs: “Just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve.” — JESUS (Matthew, 20.28)
In the company of the spirit of service, we will always be well guarded. The entire Creation reaffirms this truth with absolute clarity.
From the lower realms to the highest spheres, all things serve in their own time.
The law of work, with the division and specialization of tasks, predominates in the humblest elements across the various sectors of Nature.
This tree will cure illnesses; that other one will produce fruit. There are stones that contribute to the construction of a home; others exist paving the paths.

The Father provided the human child with the planetary home, where each object is in its proper place, awaiting only dignified effort and the word of command to teach the creature the art of service. If gunpowder meant for the release of energy was given to him and gunpowder continues to be used as an instrument of death against fellow beings, this falls upon the user of the earthly dwelling, because the Supreme Lord in everything suggests the practice of good, aiming at the elevation and enrichment of all values of the Universal Patrimony.
Let us not forget that Jesus passed among us working. Let us examine the nature of His sacrificial cooperation and learn from the Master the happiness of serving holily.
You can begin today. A hoe or a cooking pot constitutes an excellent starting point.
If you find yourself ill, with hands disabled for direct collaboration, you can still begin nonetheless, serving in the moral edification of your brethren.

messages.title: Wages
paragraphs: “And be content with your wages.” — JOHN THE BAPTIST (Luke, 3.14)
John the Baptist’s response to the soldiers who begged him for clarification is a model of conciseness and common sense.
Many people get lost through inextricable labyrinths due to a deficient understanding regarding the problems of remuneration in ordinary life.

There are workers who claim wages due to ministers, without considering the grave responsibilities that not infrequently turn the administrators of the world into victims of restlessness and insomnia, when not martyrs of representations and banquets.
There are educated men who sell the peace of their homes in exchange for extended earnings.

Countless people follow, from youth to bodily old age, anxious and unbelieving, sick and afflicted, because they cannot conform to the monthly salaries that the circumstances of the human path assign to them within the Inscrutable Designs.
It is not through excess of remuneration that a creature will integrate into the divine ranks.
If a man remains conscious of his duties, the higher paid he is, the more unsettled he will be.

Popular philosophy has long clarified that for the great ship, the great storm will arise. For each servant to be content with their own salary is proof of elevated understanding before the justice of the Almighty.
Before analyzing earthly pay, therefore, get used to valuing the concessions of Heaven.

messages.title: Avail Yourselves of the Light
paragraphs: “Walk while you have the light, lest darkness overtake you.” — JESUS (John, 12.35)

The contemplative man will find divine thoughts by analyzing the past and the future. He will see himself placed between two eternities—that of the days gone by and that which beckons from the future.
Examining the treasures of the present, he will discover his precious opportunities.

In the future, he foresees the blessed light of immortality, while in the past lie the darkness of ignorance, of committed errors, of poorly lived experiences. The overwhelming majority of human personalities possesses no other landscape regarding their near or remote past than this, constituted of ruin and disenchantment, compelling them to revalue the resources at hand.

Human life, therefore, despite being transitory, is the flame that places you in contact with the service you need for righteous ascent. In this blessed occasion, it is possible to redeem, correct, learn, gain, conquer, reunite, reconcile, and enrich oneself in the Lord.
Reflect upon the Master’s observation and you will grasp its luminous meaning. Walk while you have the light, He said.
Make the most of the gift of time received in edifying work.
Move away from the inferior condition, acquiring a higher understanding.

Without the characteristics of improvement and self-mastery in the act of marching, you will be dominated by darkness—that is, you will nullify your holy opportunity, returning to less worthy impulses and going back, following the death of the body, to the very place of shadows from which you emerged to conquer new steps on the sublime mountain of life.

messages.title: The Seed
paragraphs: “And when you sow, you do not sow that body that shall be, but bare grain, it may chance of wheat, or of some other grain.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 15:37)
In the works of Nature, the seed assumes, to our eyes, the sacred role of priestess of the Creator and of Life.
Glorious heir to divine power, it cooperates in the evolution of the world and transmits a silent and sublime lesson, touched with infinite values, to the creature.
It wisely exemplifies the need for starting points, the fair requirements of work, proper places, and appropriate times.

There are restless and insatiated men who have not yet managed to understand it. They demand great works overnight, impose tyrannical measures through the force of regulations or weapons, or attempt to betray the deep laws of Nature; they accelerate the processes of ambition, establish transitory dominion, flaunt false achievements, puff themselves up, and fall, without any sanctifying edification for themselves or for others.
They did not know how to learn from the tiny seed that gives them wheat for their daily bread and guarantees their life in all regions of planetary struggle.
Knowing how to begin constitutes a very important service.

In the redeeming effort, it is essential not to lose sight of small possibilities: a gesture, a talk, an hour, a phrase can represent glorious seeds for immortal edifications. It is imperative, therefore, never to despise them.

messages.title: Anxieties
paragraphs: “Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.” — (1 Peter, 5:7)
Anxieties breed many crimes and never build anything useful on Earth.
Invariably, the hasty man counts on all the probabilities against himself.
Opposing anxious restlessness, Nature’s lessons of patience speak across all sectors of the human path.
If man were born to go about anxious, it would mean he came into the world not in the category of a worker on a sanctifying task, but as a despairing soul without remission.

If the creature were to reflect more sensibly, it would recognize the content of service that the moments of each day can offer and would know how to watch over, with heightened value, its own assets.

Undoubtedly, landscapes will change incessantly, compelling us to face unpleasant surprises resulting from our inadequate attitude in joy or pain; nevertheless, our obligation to proceed daily in the direction of good represents an imperative of the law.
Anxiety will try to violate generous hearts because earthly roads unfold many dark angles and difficult-to-solve problems; however, let us not forget Peter's recipe.
Cast your worries upon your hopes in Our Heavenly Father, because Divine Love cares for the well-being of all of us.

It is right to desire firmly the victory of light, to seek peace with perseverance, to discipline oneself for union with the Higher Planes, and to insist on attuning with the highest Spheres. Do not forget, however, that anxiety always precedes the act of falling.

messages.title: Men of Faith
paragraphs: “Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock.” — JESUS (Matthew, 7:24)

The great preachers of the Gospel have always been interpreted as maximum expressions of Christianity in the gallery of venerable types of faith; however, this only happened when the instruments of truth effectively did not forget the vigilance indispensable to righteous testimony.

It is interesting to note that the Master highlights, among all disciples, the one who hears his teachings and puts them into practice. From this, we conclude that men of faith are not merely the talkative and enthusiastic ones, but those who are equally bearers of attention and goodwill before the lessons of Jesus, examining their spiritual content for application in daily effort.

It comforts us to note that all creatures in service within the evangelical field will move toward the inner wonders of faith. However, we must highlight, at all times, the high value of moderate men who, registering the teachings and warnings of the Good News, carefully look after the solution of all problems of the day or the occasion, without allowing their individual edifications to take place far from the essential Christian bases.

In all services, the contribution of the word is sacred and indispensable, but no learner should forget the sublime value of silence, at the right time, in the superior work of self-perfection, so that reflection may make itself heard within one's own soul, guiding its destinies.

messages.title: Fraternal Feelings
paragraphs: “But as touching brotherly love ye need not that I write unto you: for ye yourselves are taught of God to love one another.” — PAUL (1 Thessalonians, 4:9)
A strong contradiction that disrupts human contribution in the divine building of Christianity is the sectarian impulse that torments enormous ranks of its followers.
More reflection, more attentiveness to the teaching of Jesus, and these unjustified battles would be forever erased.

Even today, with the manifestations of the Spiritual Plane in the renewal of the world, groups and personalities constantly emerge, asking for formulas from Beyond so they can integrate into the field of pure fraternity.
What, however, are enlightened companions waiting for to be effectively brothers to one another?

Many people forget that legitimate solidarity is scarce in environments where the spirit of service is reduced and criticism abounds. Notable institutions are led to disturbance and extermination in view of the absence of mutual aid in the terrain of understanding, work, and goodwill.
Lack of assistance? No.
Every honest and generous work reverberates in the highest Planes, conquering selfless cooperators.

When disharmony invades the institutes of good, let human agents accuse themselves for their defection in assumed commitments or for indifference to the act of serving. And let no one ask Heaven for specific recipes of fraternity, because the sacred and immutable formula remains with us in "love one another."

messages.title: Let Us Give Thanks
paragraphs: “In everything give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.” — PAUL (1 Thessalonians, 5:18)
The stone secures.
The thorn warns.
The gall remedies.
The fire remelts.
The trash fertilizes.
The storm purifies the atmosphere.
Suffering redeems.
Illness warns.
Sacrifice enriches life.
Death always renews.
Let us learn, thus, to praise the Lord for the blessings He bestows upon us.
Good is the heat that modifies, good is the cold that preserves.
The joy that stimulates is sister to the pain that perfects.
Let us pray to Heavenly Providence for sufficient light so that our eyes may identify the granary of grace in which we find ourselves.
It is inner blindness that makes us stumble over obstacles where only divine favor exists.
And, above all, when uttering a noble desire, let us prepare ourselves to gather the lessons we must embrace in order to fulfill it according to the higher purposes that govern our destinies.
Let us not be startled by difficulties or painful unforeseen events.
Succor from Above does not always appear in the form of celestial manna.

Commonly, it appears in the guise of a less desirable resource. Let us remember, however, that a man in danger of drowning in deep waters covering the abyss is sometimes saved only at the price of harsh blows.
Let us give thanks, then, for all the experiences of the evolutionary path in the sanctifying search for the Divine Will in Jesus Christ, Our Lord.

messages.title: Resist Temptation
paragraphs: “Blessed is the man that endureth temptation.” — (JAMES, 1:12)

As long as our spiritual boat navigates the waters of inferiority, we cannot expect exemption from harsh internal conflicts. Especially in the carnal sphere, whenever we undertake the soul's improvement using the world's labors and obstacles, we must expect a multiplication of the difficulties that lie right on the path of illuminating knowledge.
Against our yearning for clarity, we have millennia of shadow. Opposing our most humble aspiration to grow in goodness are the centuries in which we delighted in evil.
This is why, intertwined with blessings from on High, temptations of all shades abound on the disciples' path.

Sometimes, the learner believes himself prepared to defeat the dragons of animality that prowl his doors; however, when he least expects it, degrading suggestions watch for him again, compelling him to a hard-fought battle.

Clear, therefore, is that not even the grave exempts us from friction with darkness, whose roots spread throughout our very spiritual organization. Only the death of imperfection within us will free us from them.
May there be constructive tolerance around the human journey, because malicious insinuations will surround us everywhere while we linger in the partial realization of good.
We will only achieve liberation when we reach full light.

Understanding the transcendence of the matter, the apostle proclaims blessed the one “that endureth temptation.” Any reference to absolute triumph is impossible for now, because we still live very far from the angelic condition; however, we will be blessed if we endure this kind of struggle well, controlling the impulses of less refined feeling and perfecting it, little by little, at the cost of our own effort, so that we do not surrender defenceless to the lower suggestions that seek to turn us into living instruments of evil.

messages.title: Us and Caesar
paragraphs: “And Jesus answering said unto them, Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's.” — (MARK, 12:17)
In every place in the world, man will always find, according to his own merits, the figure of Caesar, symbolized in state government.
Bad men, undoubtedly, will produce bad statesmen.
Idle and indifferent collectivities will receive disorganized administrations.
In any case, Caesar's influence will surround the creature, demanding the execution of material commitments. It is imperative to give him what belongs to him.
The Gospel learner must not invoke religious principles or individual idealism to exempt himself from these obligations.

If there are errors in the laws, let us remember the extent of our debts to Divine Providence and collaborate with human governance, offering our contribution in work and goodwill, conscious that inattention or revolt does not solve our problems.

It is preferable for the disciple to sacrifice himself and suffer rather than linger in delay before the respectable laws that govern him transiently on the physical plane, whether due to indiscipline before established principles or unhealthy enthusiasm that tempts him to advance too far ahead of his time.
Are there iniquitous decrees?
Recall whether you have already cooperated with those who govern your material landscape.

Live in harmony with your superiors and do not forget that the best position is one of balance. If you intend to live righteously, do not give Caesar the vinegar of bitter criticism. Help him with your efficient work, in the healthy desire to get things right, convinced that he and we are children of the same God.

messages.title: Cross and Discipline
paragraphs: “And they compel one Simon a Cyrenian, who passed by, coming out of the country, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to bear his cross.” — (MARK, 15:21)
Many scholars of Christianity combat the memories of the cross, alleging that the reminiscences of Calvary constitute an undue culture of suffering.

They assert that the Master's memory during the hours of crucifixion among common evildoers is negative. We, however, are among those who prefer to view all of Christ's days as glorious journeys and all His minutes as divine portions of His sacred ministry in the face of human soul needs.
Each hour of His presence among creatures is clothed with particular beauty, and the moment of the shameful tree is replete with symbolic majesty.
Various disciples weave extensive commentaries around the Lord's cross and tend to examine with theoretical details the imaginary woods they carry with them.
However, only he who has reached the power of denying himself in order to follow in the footsteps of the Divine Master will have taken up the cross of redemption that pertains to him.

Many people confuse discipline with spiritual enlightenment. Only after having agreed to the gentle yoke of Jesus Christ can we raise upon our shoulders the cross that will endow us with spiritual wings for eternal life.

Against the arguments, almost always idle, of those who have not yet understood the sublimity of the cross, let us look at the example of the Cyrenian at the culminating moments of the Savior. Christ's cross was the most beautiful in the world, yet the man who helps Him does not do so of his own free will, but rather answering an irresistible request. And even today, most men accept the obligations inherent to their own duty because they are constrained to do so.

messages.title: Sacred Right
paragraphs: “For unto you it is given in the behalf of Christ, not only to believe on him, but also to suffer for his sake.” — PAUL (Philippians, 1:29)
Personally cooperating with human administrators in a direct sense has always been the ambition of servants in this or that earthly organization.

An invariable act of trust, the sharing of responsibility between the superior who knows how to command and administer justice and the subordinate who knows how to serve, establishes the basis of harmony for daily action—an achievement that all institutions strive to reach.
Many disciples of Christianity seem to ignore that, in relation to Jesus, reciprocity is the same, elevated to the highest degree in the terrain of fidelity and understanding.
More understanding of the divine program means a greater expression of individual testimony in the Master's services.
Expanded competence—increased duties.
More light—more vision.

Many men, naturally usable in certain intellectual characteristics but still mentally ill, would wish to accept the Savior and believe in Him, but they cannot immediately achieve such inner edification. In view of the ignorance they do not remove and the whims they cherish, they lack integration into the right to feel the truths of Jesus, which they will only achieve when they readjust themselves, as is indispensable.

However, the disciple admitted to the benefits of belief was considered worthy of living spiritually with the Master. Between him and the Lord, there is already a sharing of trust and responsibility. Yet, while the joys of Bethlehem and the glories of Capernaum persist, the work of faith unfolds wonderfully, but upon the arrival of the division of the cross's anguish, many learners flee fearing suffering, revealing themselves unworthy of the choice. Those who act this way are categorized as fools, for to subtract oneself from collaboration with Christ is to belittle a sacred right.

messages.title: Primordial Observation
paragraphs: “And Jesus answered him, The first of all the commandments is, Hear, O Israel; The Lord our God is one Lord.” — (MARK, 12:29)
Replying to the scribe who questioned Him regarding the first of all commandments, Jesus places an initial article before the Decalogue of original observation that deserves highlighting.

Before all of Moses' programs, the prophets' revelations, and His own redeeming blessings in the Gospel, the Master places an energetic declaration of principles, calling all spirits to the plane of substantial unity. Grounding the saving service that He Himself brought from the higher Spheres, Christ proclaims to Humanity that there is only one All-Powerful Lord—the Father of Infinite Mercy.

He knew beforehand that many men would not accept the truth, that numerous souls would seek to escape fair obligations, and that delay, bad will, indifference, and laziness would arise around the Good News; nevertheless, He sustained divine unity so that all learners would become convinced that they could poison their own freedom, create fictitious gods, raise discords, temporarily betray the Law, stall on the roads, and rehearse war and destruction, yet they could never deceive the plan of eternal truths, to which all will adjust one day in the perfect understanding that “the Lord our God is one Lord.”

messages.title: There is a great difference
paragraphs: “Then Peter said, Silver and gold have I none; but such as I have give I thee.” — (ACTS, 3.6)

It is right to recommend great caution to those who are interested in the advantages of human politics, referring to Jesus and attempting to explain, through the Gospel, certain absurdities in matters of social theories.
Almost always, human law addresses the governed with this formula: — “What you have belongs to me.”
Christianity, however, through the inspired mouth of Peter, asserts to the ears of one's neighbor: — “What I have, that I give to you.”
Have you meditated on the greatness of the world when men are resolved to give of what they possess for the building of universal evolution?
In the services of common charity, in public benevolent institutions, the creature rarely yields to a fellow being that which constitutes their intrinsic property.
For the real service of eternal good, will anyone rely upon the perishable possessions of Earth in an absolute character?

The generous person will distribute money and utilities to the needy along their path; however, they will not fix within themselves the light and joy born of these gifts if they did not perform them with the feeling of love, which, deep down, is their imperishable and legitimate wealth.
Each individuality brings with it the noble qualities it has already conquered and with which it can advance ever further in the field of spiritual acquisitions of a superior order.

Do not forget Peter’s loving word and give of yourself in the effort of salvation, for whoever waits for gold or silver in order to contribute to good works is truly still far from the possibility of helping themselves.

messages.title: Piety
paragraphs: “But godliness with contentment is great gain.” — PAUL (1 Timothy, 6.6)
Much is spoken of piety on Earth; however, when we note references to such a virtue, we hardly discern between compassion and humiliation.
— I help, but this man is an addict.
— I will attend to her, however, this woman is ignorant and evil.
— I feel sorry, yet this brother is ungrateful and cruel.
— I sympathize, nevertheless, this is a worthless person.
Such statements are repeated at every step by lips that call themselves Christian.
Really, in a general way, on Earth we only find this compassion of soft voice and thorny hands.
It pours honey and venom.
It heals wounds and tears them open.
It extends its arms and collects debts of recognition.
It helps and beats.
It supports and discourages.
It offers good words and launches hostile challenges.
It quenches the hunger of the travelers of experience with breads stuffed with gall.
True piety, however, is the legitimate child of love.
It wastes no time in identifying evil. It is excessively interested in the good to neglect it in exchange for trifles, and it knows that the minute is precious in the economy of life.

The Gospel does not speak to us of this deceitful piety, full of illusions and demands. Whoever reveals enough energy to embrace the Christian life finds resources to help joyfully. They do not get caught in the webs of destructive criticism and know how to sow the good, fortify its germs, cultivate its sprouts, and await its fruiting.
Paul tells us that “godliness with contentment is great gain” for the soul, and truly, we know of no other that can bring prosperity to the heart.

messages.title: Prayer
paragraphs: “Continue in prayer, and watch in the same with thanksgiving.” — PAUL (Colossians, 4.2)
Many believers would like to wield prayer as one wields a broom or a hammer.

They demand immediate results because they are unaware of any preparatory effort. Others persevere in prayer while remaining anxious and frightened. They wear themselves out and consume valuable energies in unjustified afflictions. They see only wickedness and darkness and never deign to examine the tender shoot of the divine seed or the near or remote possibility of good. They imprison themselves in the “bad side” and sometimes lose an entire existence without any purpose of transferring to the “good side.”

What probability of success is reserved for the needy person who makes a request amidst shouting, with obvious symptoms of imbalance? The wise dispenser will, at first, postpone the solution, prudently waiting for serenity to return to the petitioner.
Paul’s word is clear in this regard.

It is essential to persist in prayer, watching in this work with thanksgiving. And it must be recognized that praising is not merely pronouncing brilliant vows. It is also rejoicing in the midst of the battle for the victory of the good, thanking the Lord for the reasons of sacrifice and suffering, and seeking the advantages that adversity and work have brought to our spirit.

Let us ask Jesus for the gift of peace and joy, but let us not forget to glorify His sublime designs whenever His merciful and just will clashes with our lower purposes. And let us be convinced that untimely prayer, made up of desperate thoughts and uncalled-for demands, is destined for the renewing ground, much like the unproductive flower that the wind carries away.

messages.title: Three imperatives
paragraphs: “And I say unto you, Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.” — JESUS (Luke, 11.9)
Ask, seek, knock…
These three imperatives of Jesus' recommendation were not enunciated without a special meaning.

In the tangle of struggles and debts of earthly experience, it is imperative that man learns to ask for paths of liberation from the old chain of suffocating conventions, sterile prejudices, empty devotions, and crystallized habits.
It is necessary to desire with strength and decision the exit from the dark thicket in which the majority of creatures have lost sight of eternal interests.
Soon after, it is imperative to seek.

The search consists of selective effort. The field lies full of lower solicitations, some of them embroidered with brilliant suggestions. It is essential to locate dignified and sanctifying action. Many pursue dangerous mirages, much like moths that fall in love with the clarity of a fire. They arrive from afar, approach the flames, and consume the blessing of the body.

It is imperative to learn to seek the legitimate good. Once the edifying roadmap is established, the moment has come to knock on the door of construction; without the hammer of methodical effort and without the chisel of good will, it is very difficult to transform the resources of carnal life into luminous works of divine art, with a view to spiritual happiness and eternal love.
It will not suffice, therefore, to pray without direction, to seek without examination, and to act without a high objective.

Let us ask the Lord for our liberation from primitivistic animality, let us seek sublime spirituality, and let us work for our placement within it, in order to become faithful instruments of the Divine Will.
Ask, seek, knock!…
This trilogy of Jesus is clothed with special significance for the learners of the Gospel in all times.

messages.title: The good is tireless
paragraphs: “But ye, brethren, be not weary in well doing.” — PAUL (2 Thessalonians, 3.13)
It is very common to find people who declare themselves tired of practicing good. Let us be convinced, however, that such claims do not stem from a pure source.
Only those who aim at certain advantages for particularistic interests, in the zone of immediacy, acquire the boredom bordering on desperation when they cannot satisfy egotistical purposes.
Much prudence is indispensable when this or that circumstance leads us to reflect on the evils that assault us after the good we believe we have sown or nourished.

The sincere learner is not unaware that Jesus exercises His ministry of love without exhaustion since the beginning of planetary organization. Regarding our personal cases, the Master has often felt the thorn of our ingratitude, identifying our retreat from the labors of our own illumination; yet, even while verifying our voluntary and criminal deviations, the patience of the Christ who corrects us while loving, and tolerates while building, has never been exhausted, opening merciful arms to us for renewing activity.
If He has supported and waited for us through so many centuries, why can we not experience with a firm spirit some small disappointments for a few days?

Paul’s observation to the Thessalonians, therefore, is very fair. If we grow weary in the practice of good, such a disaster will truly express that it has not yet been possible for us to emerge from the evil within ourselves.

messages.title: Personal magnetism
paragraphs: “And the whole multitude sought to touch him: for there went virtue out of him, and healed them all.” — (LUKE, 6.19)
At present, we observe a whole pleiad of eminent spiritualists spreading concepts related to personal magnetism with such strangeness, as if we were facing a true novelty of the 19th century.

Such a service of investigation and dissemination of the occult powers of man represents a valuable contribution to the educational work of the present and the future; however, it must be remembered that the edification is not new.

Jesus, during His passage through the Planet, was the individualized sublimation of personal magnetism in its substantially divine expression. Creatures disputed the charm of His presence, multitudes followed in His steps, touched by singular admiration. Almost everyone sought to touch His garment. From Him emanated irradiations of love that neutralized stubborn illnesses. The Master spontaneously produced the climate of peace that reached all who enjoyed His company.

If you seek, therefore, an easier path for the full emergence of your psychic potentialities, it is reasonable that you take advantage of the experience that earthly guides offer you in this sense, but do not forget the examples and living demonstrations of Jesus.
If you intend to attract, it is essential to know how to love. If you desire legitimate influence on Earth, sanctify yourself through the influence of Heaven.

messages.title: Make to yourselves friends
paragraphs: “And I say unto you, Make to yourselves friends of the mammon of unrighteousness.” — JESUS (Luke, 16.9)

If man could, starting from human experience, pierce the deep past, he would more quickly reach the conclusion that all the possibilities that bless him in knowledge and health come from Divine Goodness, and that most of the material resources at the disposal of his whims stem from injustice.

It is not for us to particularize, but rather to deduce that the conceptions of human law originated from divine influence, because, as for ourselves, we are compelled to recognize our slow individual evolution from ferocious egoism to universalist love, from iniquity to real justice.
