It suffices to recall, in this sense, that almost all earthly States arose, centuries ago, upon cruel conquests. With exceptions, men have been wasteful servants who, at the moment of reckoning, do not prove themselves equal to their stewardship.
This is why Jesus bequeathed to us the parable of the unfaithful employee, inviting us to sincere fraternity so that, through it, we may find the path of rehabilitation.
The Master advised us to make friends, that is, to expand the circle of sympathies in which we feel ourselves ever more intensively supported by the spirit of cooperation and by intercessory values.

If our spiritual past is dark and painful, let us seek to simplify it by acquiring true devotions that help us through the rough climb of redemption. If we do not have certain connections with the riches of injustice today, we had them yesterday, and it is imperative to use the time for our individual readjustment before Divine Justice.

messages.title: Everlasting habitations
paragraphs: “And I say unto you, Make to yourselves friends of the mammon of unrighteousness; that, when ye fail, they may receive you into everlasting habitations.” — JESUS (Luke, 16.9)

A man oblivious to spiritual obligations will judge he finds in this passage an intelligent thief buying the favor of venal lawyers in order to reinstate himself in the honorable titles of human convention. However, when Jesus speaks of friends, He refers to sincere and devoted brothers, and when He mentions the riches of injustice, He includes the total past of the creature, with all the painful lessons that characterize it. Likewise, when He reports on everlasting habitations, He does not locate them in celestial palaces.
The Master situated the sacred tabernacle in the heart of man.
More than anyone, the Savior identified our imperfections and, showing immense piety in the face of the deficiencies that mark our spirit, uttered the divine words that serve for our study.

Knowing our deviations, He stated, in summary, that we must take advantage of the transient goods within our reach, mobilizing them in legitimate fraternity so that, forgetting the crimes and hatreds of another time, we may become self-sacrificing brothers to one another.

Let us thus value our stay in the services of Earth, as incarnate or disincarnate beings, favoring by all resources at our disposal our own improvement and the elevation of our fellows, acting in the direction of light and loving always, because, within these norms of sublime solidarity, we can count on the dedication of faithful friends who, as disciples more dedicated and ennobled than we, will effectively help us, welcoming us into their hearts, turned into tabernacles of the Lord, helping us not only to obtain new opportunities for readjustment and sanctification, but also endorsing before Jesus our promises and aspirations in the face of superior life.

messages.title: Thy faith
paragraphs: “And he said unto her, Be of good cheer, daughter: thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace.” — (LUKE, 8.48)
It is important to note that the Divine Master, after dispensing a benefit, always refers to the prodigy of faith, the sublime patrimony of those who seek Him.

Several times we hear Him in the expressive affirmation: — “Thy faith hath made thee whole.” Sick in body and soul, after relief or cure, they hear the generous phrase. It is because the will and confidence of man are powerful factors in the development and illumination of life.
The navigator without direction who trusts in nothing will only reach some port by virtue of the play of forces upon which he balances himself, completely unaware, however, of what may happen to him.

The sick person, unbelieving in the action of all remedies, is the first to work against their own safety. The man who shows himself disheartened in all things should not await the useful cooperation of anything.

Empty souls vainly claim the share of happiness that the world owes them. The negations in which they wander transform them, before life, into zones of damping, like electrical insulators. A vitalizing current passes, but they remain insensitive.

In the undertakings and needs of your path, do not isolate yourself in negative positions. Jesus can do all things, your true friends will do the utmost for you; however, neither the Master nor your companions will fully accomplish the happiness you aspire to without the contribution of your faith, because you too are a child of the same God, with the same possibilities of elevation.

messages.title: New Athenians
paragraphs: “And when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked: and others said, We will hear thee again of this matter.” — (ACTS, 17.32)
Paul’s contact with the Athenians at the Areopagus presents an interesting lesson for new disciples.

While the apostle commented on his impressions of the famous city, perhaps sharpening the vanity of those present through references to the sanctuaries and the subtle play of reasoning, he was attentively listened to. It is possible that the assembly would have acclaimed him with fervor if his word had stopped at the philosophical framework of the early expositions. Athens would have then revered him as a wise man, presenting him to the world in the special mold of its unforgettable names.

Paul, however, refers to the resurrection of the dead, hinting at the glorious continuation of life beyond earthly trifles. From that instant on, the listeners felt less at ease and went so far as to mock his loving and sincere word, leaving him almost alone.

The teaching fits the present day perfectly. Numerous workers of Christ in the various sectors of modern culture are attentively listened to and respected as authorities in the subjects they specialized in; however, upon declaring their belief in life beyond the body, affirming the law of responsibility beyond the grave, they immediately receive the scoffing laughter of the admirers of moments before, who leave them alone, giving them the impression of a true desert.

messages.title: The door
paragraphs: “Then Jesus said to them again: Truly I say to you, I am the door of the sheep.” — (JOHN, 10:7)
It is not enough to attain the qualities of the sheep, regarding meekness and tenderness, to reach the Divine Kingdom.
It is necessary for the sheep to recognize the door of redemption, with indispensable discernment, and to keep its course, disregarding the appeals of the lower order emerging from the waysides.
Hence we conclude that sanity, to be victorious, does not dispense with caution in the orientation to follow.

The loss of the flock does not always result from the attack of wild beasts, but rather because imprudent sheep cross natural barriers, deaf to the shepherd's voice, or blind to the right exits, in search of the pastures that belong to them. How many are unexpectedly struck by the terrible wolf because, fascinated by the greenery of neighboring pastures, they stray from their own road, breaking obstacles to satisfy destructive impulses?
Thus it happens with men in the course of experience.

How many noble spirits have lost precious opportunities through their own imprudence? Masters of admirable patrimonies, they sometimes reveal themselves as arbitrary and capricious. In most situations, they copy the virtuous and useful sheep who, after conquering various ennobling titles, forgets the door to be reached and breaks the beneficial and necessary disciplines to surrender to the devouring wolf.

messages.title: Listen to them
paragraphs: “Abraham said to him: They have Moses and the prophets; let them listen to them.” — (LUKE, 16.29)
Abraham's response to the rich man in the parable is still a daily teaching on the common path.
Countless people approach the sources of spiritual revelation, however, they fail to achieve liberation from selfish ties so that they may see and hear, as suits their essential interests.

Precisely a century ago, a more intense exchange was established between the two Planes, in the great movement of reviving Christianity; yet, there are learners who contemplate the sky, anguished simply because they never received a direct message from a father or a son in human experience. Some go so far as to stray from the path alleging such motives. For these, the phenomenon and revelation in evangelical Spiritism are a simple set of untruths, because they obtained nothing from “dead relatives” in consecutive years of observation.
This, however, is nothing more than nonsense.
Who can guarantee the perpetuity of the fragile links of earthly connections?
The animal impulse has limits.
Let no one justify their own blindness with the dissatisfaction of personal caprice.

The world has been full of messages and emissaries for millennia. The great problem, however, does not lie in requesting the truth to serve each creature's exclusivist circle, but in each man's determination to walk with his own value toward eternal realities.
messages.note: [1] This lesson was psychographed in 1950, a century after the first manifestations that gave rise to modern Spiritism; see retrospective Spiritism.

messages.title: In family
paragraphs: “First learn to show piety to your own family and to repay your parents, for this is pleasing and acceptable before God.” — PAUL (1 Timothy, 5.4)

The struggle in the family is a fundamental problem of man's redemption on Earth. How shall we be benefactors of a hundred or a thousand people, if we have not yet learned to serve five or ten creatures? This is a logical inquiry that extends to all sincere disciples of Christianity.
A good preacher and a bad servant are two titles that do not match.

The apostle advises the exercise of piety within domestic activities, however, he does not allude to piety that weeps without courage before distressing enigmas, but to the one that knows the neuralgic areas of the house and strives to eliminate them, awaiting the divine decision in due time.
We know numerous brothers who feel alone, spiritually, among those who joined their personal circle through blood ties, thus surrendering to lamentable discouragement.

It is imperative, however, to examine the transitoriness of bodily connections, considering that there are no casual unions in the earthly home. Salvific or regenerative trials predominate there for now. Therefore, let no one despise this sacred field of service no matter how overwhelmed they feel by incomprehension. It would be a grave mistake to forget its infinite possibilities for illuminating work.
It is impossible to help the world when we cannot yet be useful even to a small house — the one in which the Father's Will has placed us on a precarious basis.
Before great personal projection in collective work, let the disciple learn to cooperate in favor of family members today, convinced that such an effort represents an essential achievement.

messages.title: This is what you were called for
paragraphs: “Not repaying evil for evil, or reviling for reviling; but contrariwise, blessing: knowing that for this you were called.” — (1 Peter, 3.9)
The ranks of those who complain have always been numerous in all tasks of good.
In the evangelical apostolate, we likewise observe this general rule.

Many learners, in obedience to a pernicious habit, prefer the path of friction or scandalous dissensions. However, a little more reasoning would awaken the community of disciples to a greater understanding.

Would Jesus invite us to sterile conflicts, merely to repeat the pictures of individual caprice or tyrannizing force? If it were so, the ministry of the Kingdom would be entrusted to the stubborn, the arguers, the giants of physical energy.
It is nonsense for the servant of the Good News to indulge in lamentations that have no reason to be.

Bitterness, persecutions, slander, brutality, misunderstanding? These are old figurations that torment souls on Earth. To contribute to their extinction is why the Lord called us to His ranks. Do not feed them by giving them excessive appreciation.
The Christian is a living point of resistance to evil wherever he may be. Think about this and try to understand the meaning of the verb to endure.
Do not forget the obligation to serve with Jesus. This is what you were called for.

messages.title: Always help
paragraphs: “Then Paul answered: What do you mean by weeping and breaking my heart?” — (ACTS, 21.13)
One of the most dramatic passages in the Acts of the Apostles is the one in which Paul of Tarsus prepares himself, facing the testimonies that awaited him in Jerusalem.

In the fighter's heroic soul, no shadow of hesitation hovers. His spirit, as always, is ready. But the companions weep and lament; and from the sensitive and courageous heart of the Gospel battler flows the painful inquiry.
Despite the serene energy that dominated his vigorous constitution, Paul missed friends as courageous as himself.

The companions who followed him were sincerely disposed to sacrifice, however, they did not know how to manifest the feelings of a faithful soul. For weeping or lamentation never help in moments of difficult testimony. Whoever cries beside a friend in a dangerous position disorganizes their resistance.

Jesus wept in the Garden when alone, but in Jerusalem, under the weight of the cross, He asked the generous women who supported Him to cease their distressing tears. At the dawn of the Resurrection, He asks Magdalene to clarify the reason for her weeping by the sepulcher.
The lesson is significant for every learner.

If a loved one remains longer under the necessary storm, do not give in to useless despairs. Complaining does not solve problems. Instead of hurting them with sobs, approach them and extend your hands.

messages.title: Have you thought about this?
paragraphs: “Knowing that I must shortly put off this my tabernacle, even as our Lord Jesus Christ has shown me.” — (2 Peter, 1.14)

If great voices of Christianity have often referred to supposed crimes of the flesh, it is necessary to mention the weaknesses of the "self", the inferiorities of the spirit itself, without concentrating false accusations on the body as if it represented the role of an implacable executioner, separated from the soul, which would then be its prisoner and victim.
We notice that Peter called the organism his tabernacle.
The human body is a set of agglutinated cells or terrestrial fluids that gather under planetary laws, offering the Spirit the holy opportunity to learn, value, reform, and magnify life.

Often man, like an idle or perverse worker, imputes the bad qualities with which he is afflicted to the useful instrument. The body is a concession of Divine Mercy so that the soul may prepare itself before the glorious future.
Far from undue accusations of the flesh, let us reflect on the millennia spent in the formation of this sacred tabernacle in the evolutionary field.
Have you ever thought that you are an immortal Spirit, having on Earth, for a time, valuable powers granted by God to your needs for work?
Such powers form your body.

What do you do with your feet, your hands, your eyes, your brain? Do you know that these powers were entrusted to you to honor the Lord by illuminating yourself? Meditate on these questions and sanctify your body, finding in it the divine temple.

messages.title: Conciliation
paragraphs: “Agree with your adversary quickly, while you are with him in the way; lest at any time the adversary deliver you to the judge, and the judge deliver you to the officer, and you be cast into prison.” — JESUS (Matthew, 5.25)
Many ennobled souls, after receiving the exhortation of this passage, suffer inwardly upon encountering the hardness of yesterday's adversary, inaccessible to any conciliation.
The Master's warning, however, is fundamentally comforting for individual conscience.
The Lord's word asserts — "agree", which is equivalent to saying "do your part".
Correct as much as possible regarding past errors, move in the direction of revealing persevering goodwill. Insist on kindness and understanding.

If the adversary is ignorant, reflect on the time when you also ignored primary obligations and observe if you did not act with worse characteristics; if he is perverse, categorize him as a sick and demented person on the way to recovery.

Do the good you can while walking the same paths, because if the enemy is so implacable that he seeks to deliver you to the judge anyway, you will then equally have proofs and testimonies to present. A legitimate trial includes all pieces and only Spirits frankly impenetrable to good will suffer the rigor of extreme justice.
Work, therefore, as much as possible in the chapter of harmonization, but if the adversary disdains your good desires, conciliate with your own conscience and wait confidently.

messages.title: Dunghill
paragraphs: “It is neither fit for the land, nor yet for the dunghill; but men cast it out. He that has ears to hear, let him hear.” — JESUS (Luke, 14.35)
According to our deduction, Jesus gave significance to the dunghill.
Earth and garbage, in this passage, take on essential value. With the former, we will carry out sowing; with the latter, it is possible to make fertilization where necessary.

A large portion of learners, imitating the attitude of the ancient Pharisees, flee from the first encounter with the "stercoral zones" of their neighbor; however, this happens because they do not know their profitable expressions.
The Gospel is full of lessons in this sector of illuminating knowledge.

If Joseph of Galilee or Mary of Nazareth symbolize lands of abundant virtues, the same does not happen to the apostles who, at every step, need to resort to the fountain of tears that flow from the dunghill of remorse and weaknesses, properly human, in order to fertilize the impoverished soil of their hearts. How much fertilizer of this nature did Magdalene and Paul need, for example, until they reached the glorious position in which they stood out?

Let us transform our miseries into lessons. Let us identify the dunghill that our own ignorance piled up around ourselves, convert it into fertilizer for our "intimate land", and we will have provided a reasonable solution to the problem of our great evils.

messages.title: Sin and sinner
paragraphs: “Beloved, follow not that which is evil, but that which is good. He that does good is of God: but he that does evil has not seen God.” — (3 John, 11)

Human society should not divide itself as a field separating the good and the bad, but rather live as a great family integrating spirits who are beginning to understand the Father and those who have not yet managed to sense Him.

Of course, the words "wickedness" and "perversity" will still appear for vast years in the terrestrial dictionary, defining certain inferior mental attitudes; nevertheless, it must be agreed that the question of evil is gaining new interpretations in human intelligence.
The evangelist presents a fair concept. John does not tell us that the perverse is exiled from our Father, nor that he remains absent from Creation. He only states that he "has not seen God".

This does not mean we should cross our arms before the poisonous weeds and pestilential zones of the path; however, it obliges us to remember that a farmer does not remove briars and debris from the soil to turn it into precipices.

Many people believe that the "fallen man" is someone who must be annihilated. Jesus, however, did not adopt this guideline. Addressing the sinner lovingly, He knew He was first of all confronted by an unhappy sick person, from whom the characteristics of eternity could not be subtracted.
Fight against crime, but support the creature entangled in its dark meshes.
The Master indicated constant combat against evil, however, He awaits legitimate fraternity among men as the sublime mark of the Celestial Kingdom.

messages.title: Common condition
paragraphs: “And straightway the father of the child cried out, and said with tears, Lord, I believe; help you my unbelief.” — (MARK, 9.24)
That man from the crowd, approaching Jesus with his sick son, constitutes a representative expression of the common spirit of terrestrial humanity.
Religious circles excessively comment on faith in God, yet in moments of storm, devotees who remain firm in trust are scarce.

The masses reveal themselves very attentive to external cult rituals, participating in buildings alluding to belief, yet facing the difficulties of scandal, almost everyone slips down the precipice of mutual accusations.

If a missionary fails, a stampede occurs. The community of believers casts its eyes on fallible men, blind to purposes or indifferent to institutions. In such a movement of spiritual insecurity, without paradox, human creatures believe and disbelieve, trusting today and fainting tomorrow.
We are also confronted by the regime of uncertainty of infantile spirits who barely begin to conceive notions of responsibility.

Happy, then, are those who, like the needy father, approach Christ, confessing the precariousness of their intimate position. Thus, while affirming belief with their mouth, they will ask at the same time for help for their lack of faith, attesting with tears to their own wretchedness.

messages.title: Nothing Is Lacking
paragraphs: “And if I send them away fasting to their own houses, they will faint on the way; for some of them come from afar.” — JESUS (Mark, 8:3)
Jesus' concern for the needy crowd remains alive across time.
How many religious schools pulsate within the bosom of nations, under the influx of the Divine Master's providential love?

There may be perverse and desperate men who persist in malice and denial, but no community can be seen without the succor of faith. Savages themselves receive assistance posts from the Lord, naturally in accordance with the rusticity of their primitivist interpretations. Heavenly nourishment is never lacking to creatures. If some spirits declare themselves disbelievers in the Paternity of God, it is because they find themselves incapacitated or ill due to the interior ruins to which they have surrendered.
Jesus shows an invariable concern in nourishing the spirit of His wards through a thousand different ways, from the indigenous hut to the cathedrals of large metropolises.

In these posts of sublime succor, man learns, through gradual effort, to nourish himself spiritually, until he brings the church into his own home, transporting it from the domestic sanctuary to the enclosure of his own heart.
Few people meditate on the infinite mercy that serves, in the world, the edifying table of religious ideas.

The Master bends down for the good of all men. Full of abnegation and love, He knows how to nourish, with specific resources, the ignorant and the wise, the inquirer and the believer, the rebellious and the unhappy. More than anyone, Jesus understands that otherwise creatures would fall, exhausted, into the immense precipices that border the evolutionary path.

messages.title: Separation
paragraphs: “Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away.” — JESUS (John, 16:7)
Such a statement by the Master resonates in our innermost fibers.
No one knew how to love as much as He did; yet, He was the first to recognize the convenience of departure in favor of His companions.
What would have happened if Jesus had insisted on staying?
Probably earthly crowds would have accentuated their selfish tendencies, consolidating them.

Because the Divine Friend had sought Lazarus in the tomb, no one else would resign themselves to separation by death. Because some lepers had been cleansed, no one would accept, in the future, the beneficial cooperation of physical illnesses. The logical result would be general disturbance in the evolutionary mechanism.

The Master needed to absent Himself so that everyone's effort would become visible in the divine plan of the world's work. Otherwise, it would mean perpetuating the indolence of some and the selfishness of others.
In different aspects, the great hour of the evangelical family is repeated daily in our kindred groups.
How often widowhood, orphanhood, the suffering of distance, perplexity, and pain will arise for the elevated convenience of the common good?
Remember this passage from the Gospel when separation makes you cry, because if the death of the body is renewal for those who leave, it is also new life for those who stay.

messages.title: The Thorn
paragraphs: “And lest I should be exalted above measure through the abundance of the revelations, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me.” — PAUL (2 Corinthians, 12:7)

It is an extremely dangerous attitude for a man to praise himself, presuming to be unaware that he is on a plane of arduous service, within which it is incumbent upon him to issue difficult testimonies daily. It is a mental position that is not only threatening but also false, because an unexpected moment comes when the thorn of the heart appears.

The prudent disciple will nurture confidence without boasting, proving to be courageous without being meddlesome. He recognizes the extent of his debts to the Master and finds no glory in himself, realizing that all glory belongs to Him alone, the Lord.

Not a few men of the world, vigilanteless and restless, after receiving the incense of the crowd, come to nurse the bitternesses of solitude; many of them take delight in the galleries of fame, as if they had been converted into eternal idols, only to cry later, alone, with their unknown thorn in the recesses of their being.

Why assume the position of an infallible master when we are nothing more than simple apprentices? Would it not be more righteous to serve the Lord, in youth or in old age, in abundance or in scarcity, in administration or in subalternity, with a spirit of moderation, observing our vulnerable points in the insufficiency and imperfection of what we have been until now?

Let us remember that Paul of Tarsus was with Jesus personally; he was appointed to divine service in Antioch by the very voices of Heaven; he fought, worked, and suffered for the Gospel of the Kingdom and, writing to the Corinthians, already aged and tired, still referred to the thorn that was given to him so that he would not be exalted in the sublime work of revelations.

messages.title: Law of Return
paragraphs: “And shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of damnation.” — JESUS (John, 5:29)
In few passages of the Gospel does the reincarnationist law remain as clear as here, where the Master's teaching refers to the resurrection of condemnation.
How would theologians interested in the existence of a burning and imperishable hell understand these words?

Creatures dedicated to good will find the source of life by bathing in the waters of bodily death. Their future achievements follow a righteous ascent, in direct correspondence with the persevering effort they developed toward sanctifying spirituality; however, those who take pleasure in evil cancel their own possibilities of resurrection in the light.
They must repeat the expiatory course.
It is the return to the lesson or the remedy. No different alternative arises for them.
The law of return, therefore, is broadly contained in this synthesis of Jesus.
Resurrection is resurgence. And the meaning of renewal does not harmonize with the theory of eternal punishments.
In summary and definitive sentences there is no saving resource. Through the Master's reference, however, we observe that Divine Providence is much richer and more magnanimous than it seems.
There will be a resurrection for everyone, with the sole difference that the good will have it in new life and the evil in a new condemnation, resulting from their own reprehensible creation.

messages.title: It Is Because They Do Not Know
paragraphs: “And these things will they do unto you, because they have not known the Father, nor me.” — JESUS (John, 16:3)
Painful perplexities not infrequently assail disciples, inspiring questions.
Why is there disharmony surrounding fraternal endeavor?

The journey of good encounters dark barriers. An attempt is made to establish light, but darkness penetrates the roads. Simple projects for charity are formulated which bad faith tries to disturb at the first impulse of realization.

Almost always, the destructive demonstration comes from men marked by prominent positions, indicated by the circumstances to exercise the function of guides of general thought. These are the ones who, on most occasions, set themselves up as expositors of unreasonable impositions and demands.
The sincere apprentice of Jesus, however, should not waste time with unjustified questions and anxieties.
The Divine Master clarified this great problem in advance.

Ignorance is the common source of imbalance. And if this or that group of creatures seeks to prevent the manifestations of good, it is because they are unaware, for the time being, of the blessings of Heaven.
Nothing more than this. It is necessary, therefore, to forget the shadows that still dominate most earthly sectors, with each disciple living in the light that pulsates in the service of the Lord.

messages.title: In the Breaking of Bread
paragraphs: “And they told what things were done in the way, and how he was known of them in breaking of bread.” — (LUKE, 24:35)
Very important is the episode in which the Master is recognized by the disciples who were heading to Emmaus in despair.
Jesus had followed them like a hidden friend, fixing truth in their hearts with verbal, affectionate, and sweet formulas.

Much of the journey was crossed in the company of that loving and wise man, whom both interpreted as a generous and sympathetic stranger, and only in the breaking of bread do they recognize the much-loved Master.
The two apprentices failed to identify Him either by words or by the affectionate gesture; yet as soon as materialized bread appeared, they dissipated all doubts and believed.
Is this not the same thing that has been happening in the world for millennia?

Compact crowds of candidates for faith turn away from divine service because they do not achieve, after a certain expectation, the advantages they awaited in the immediacy of human struggle. Without financial guarantee, without satisfied whims, they do not commune in the renewing, respectable, and faithful belief.
It is necessary to combat such myopia of the soul.
Praise be to the Lord for all the lessons and testimonies He grants us, but you will remain very far from truth if you seek Him only in the division of fragmentary and perishable goods.

messages.title: Necessary Seasons
paragraphs: “Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out, when the times of refreshing shall come from the presence of the Lord.” — Peter (ACTS, 3:19)

Restless believers almost always assume that the work of redemption proceeds through some conventional measures and that merely with a certain external activity they already possess the highest titles alongside the Divine Messengers.

Most Roman Catholics expect exemption from difficulties through exterior ceremonies; many Protestants believe in full identification with heaven merely by reciting a few hymns, while an enormous percentage of Spiritists believe themselves in the intimacy of supreme revelations simply for having attended a few sessions.
All this constitutes valuable preparation, but it is not everything.
There is an illuminating effort toward the interior, without which no man will enter the sanctuary of Divine Truth.

Peter's word to the popular mass contains the synthesis of the vast program of essential transformation to which every creature must submit for the happiness of union with Christ. There are indispensable seasons for this achievement, since no one will immediately reach the eternal clarity of the culmination.

First of all, it is imperative that the culprit repents, recognizing the extent and volume of their own faults, and that they convert in order to reach the time of refreshing through the presence of the Lord within themselves. Once there, they will qualify for the construction of the Divine Kingdom within themselves.
If you truly understand the mission of the Gospel, you will identify the season in which you find yourself and will be informed regarding the services you must carry out to move on to the next.

messages.title: Where Are They?
paragraphs: “Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.” — JESUS (Matthew, 11:29)
Jesus addressed the crowd of the afflicted and disheartened, proclaiming the divine purpose of relieving them.
— “Come unto me! — cried the Master — take my yoke upon you, and learn of me, for I am meek and lowly in heart!”
His loving appeal vibrates in the world through all the centuries of Christianity.
Compact is the mob of the desperate and oppressed on Earth, despite the loving invitation.

This is because the Master in the “Come unto me!” naturally expects restless and sad souls to seek Him for the acquisition of divine teaching. But not all the afflicted intend to renounce the object of their despairs, and not all the sad ones want to flee the shadow to encounter the light.
Most of the disheartened even try to satisfy criminal whims with the protection of Jesus, uttering strange prayers.
However, when sufferers sincerely turn to Christ, they will hear Him, in the silence of the inner sanctuary, calling upon their spirits to disregard the reprehensible disputes of the lower field.
Where are the afflicted of Earth who intend to trade the captivity of their own passions for the gentle yoke of Jesus Christ?
For them were spoken the holy words “Come unto me!”, reserving for them in the Gospel powerful light for indispensable renewal.

messages.title: The World and Belief
paragraphs: “Let Christ the King of Israel descend now from the cross, that we may see and believe.” — (MARK, 15:32)
Because men qualified for the true understanding of pure belief in its essential values are very rare, we find those who insulted Christ to confirm Him.

Miracle-seeking mentality has always swum on the surface of the senses, without reaching the zone of the eternal Spirit, and if it fails to achieve the less worthy ends to which it is directed, it descends into biting challenges.

And, in the Master's case, the observations do not come solely from the populace. Mark asserts that the chief priests along with the scribes shared in the insulting movements, as if to say that intellectualism does not translate spiritual elevation.
The demonstrators remained deaf to the Good News of the Kingdom, blind to the contemplation of the benefits received, insensitive to the touch of love that Jesus had addressed to hearts.
They wanted only a spectacle. Let Christ descend from the Cross by a magic trick, and all problems of inferior belief would be solved.
The divine interlocutor, however, gave them no other answer besides silence, making them understand the magnitude of His gesture, which was inaccessible to the childish purpose of the inquirers.
If you are a sincere disciple of the Gospel, do not forget that even today the situation is not very different.

Work prudently in the service of faith. Unite with the Lord, give as much as you can in His name, and continue serving in the extension of good, convinced that the vast inferior world will only maliciously ask you for distractions and signs.

messages.title: In All Things
paragraphs: “But in all things approving ourselves as the ministers of God, in much patience, in afflictions, in necessities, in distresses.” — PAUL (2 Corinthians, 6:4)

Most disciples of the Gospel do not seriously face the religious background of life, except in the activities of external worship. In the conception of many, it is enough to attend the assemblies of faith assiduously and all the enigmas of the soul will be deciphered in the chapter of relations with God.
However, Christ's teachings call for individual renewal and refinement under all circumstances.

What can be said of a man, seemingly contrite in the public acts of the religious confession to which he belongs and immersed in swearing within his domestic sanctuary? Not a few declare themselves believers alongside the crowd, proving indolent in work, desperate in pain, incontinent in joy, unfaithful in ease, and blasphemous in the heart's distresses.

Why would Jesus fight for the formation of followers only to be praised by them for a few hours a week in genuflection? To attribute such a purpose to the Master would be to lower His sublime principles.

It is imperative that apprentices become recommendable in all things, revealing the excellence of the ideas that nourish them, both at home and in churches, both in common services and on public roads.

Certainly, no one needs to live exclusively with clasped hands or a fixed gaze on the firmament; however, let us not forget that kindness, goodwill, cooperation, and politeness are divine aspects of living prayer in Christ's apostolate.

messages.title: The Great Future
paragraphs: “My kingdom is not of this world.” — JESUS (John 18:36)
Since the dawn of Christianity, we have observed apprentices who deliberately withdraw from the world, claiming that the Kingdom of the Lord does not belong to Earth.
They kneel for indefinite periods in houses of worship, believing that holiness is achieved through flight.

Many cross their arms in front of the services of regeneration and, when questioned, express outrage at the shocking scenes that earthly experience offers them, referring to Christ before Pilate when the Master asserted that His kingdom had not yet been established in the circles of human struggle.

However, it is fair to ponder that Christ did not disown the planet. His word did not pledge the absolute negation of celestial happiness for Earth, but merely defined the landscape as it then existed, without forgetting the hope in the future.
The Master clarified: — “My kingdom is not of this world.”

Such a statement reveals His trust. Jesus, therefore, cannot endorse the false attitude of disheartened workers simply because the shadow has grown denser around transitory problems or because human wounds sometimes become more painful. Such occurrences often obey pure visual illusion.
Divine activity never ceases, and it is precisely within the framework of beneficial struggle that the disciple will carve out their own victory.
It is not up to us to desert through a contemplative attitude, but rather to advance confidently toward the great future.

messages.title: Spiritual Nourishment
paragraphs: “It is good that the heart be established by grace, not with foods which have not profited those who have been occupied with them.” — PAUL (Hebrews 13:9)
There are vices in the nourishment of the soul just as there are in the feeding of the body.
Many people swap pure water for exciting drinks, much like those who prefer to deal with pernicious illusion when dealing with spiritual problems.
The food of the heart, to be effective in eternal life, must be based on the simple realities of the evolutionary path.

It is imperative that we are fortified with illuminative values, without yielding to the dazzles of fantasy that originate from the outside. And it is precisely on the religious road that such an effort demands broader refinement.

Believers, in general, are always thirsty for situations that cater to their harmful caprices, much as the gourmet yearns for exotic dishes; however, just as table pleasures are of no use in essential activities, the exciting sensations of the phenomenal zone become useless to the spirit when it does not possess sufficient inner resources to understand the purposes. Countless apprentices keep their religious experience as a purely intellectual matter. It is imperative, however, to recognize that the nourishment of the soul, in order to firmly take root, calls for a heart sincerely interested in divine truths. When a person places themselves in this intimate position, they truly fortify themselves for sublimation, because they recognize so much dignified working material around their own steps that any transitory sensation for them comes to be located on the lowest rungs of the path.

messages.title: Necessary Renewal
paragraphs: “Do not quench the Spirit.” — PAUL (1 Thessalonians 5:19)

When the Apostle to the Gentiles wrote this exhortation, he did not mean that the Spirit can be destroyed, but sought to renew the mental attitude of those who continually stifle their higher tendencies.

Not infrequently, we observe creatures acting against their own conscience so as not to be categorized among the spiritual. However, incarnated entities remain within laborious learning in order to rise from the world as glorious Spirits. This is the greatest purpose of the human school.

Men, however, linger far from the great truth. Usually, they prefer strict conventionalism and, only with difficulty, open their understanding to the realities of the soul. Customs, effectively, are powerful and determining elements in evolution, yet only when inspired by principles of a higher order.
It is necessary, therefore, not to asphyxiate the germs of edifying life that are born every day in the heart under the influx of the Merciful Father.

There are brothers of ours who return from Earth through the same door of ignorance and indifference through which they entered. That is why, in the balance of daily activities, disciples should ask themselves: — “What did I do today? Did I emphasize the traits of the inferior creature I was until yesterday, or did I develop the elevated qualities of the spirit that I wish to retain tomorrow?”

messages.title: Conflict
paragraphs: “I find then a law, that, when I would do good, evil is present with me.” — PAUL (Romans 7:21)
Sincere disciples of the Gospel, after the manner of Paul of Tarsus, encounter great conflict within their own nature.

Almost always they are confronted by enormous difficulties in their testimonies. At the exact moment when they are supposed to reveal the presence of the Divine Companion in their hearts, a word or a hasty attitude betrays them before their own conscience, indicating the persistence of old weaknesses.
Most experience sensations of shame and pain.

Some attribute their falls to the influence of malevolent Spirits and generally look for the enemy on the outer plane, when they should heal within themselves the undesirable cause of attunement with evil.

It is unquestionable that we still find ourselves in a region very distant from one where we can live exempt from adverse vibrations; however, it is necessary to verify Paul's observation within ourselves.

As long as a person remains in the ice of indifference or the restlessness of stubbornness, they are not called to pure analysis; however, as soon as they awaken to renewal, their inner field turns into a battle zone.

Against the flickering aspiration of the good on the passing day, the heavy baggage of shadows accumulated in our souls since past centuries arises. Therefore, great serenity and endurance on our part are essential so that the progress achieved is not lost.
The Lord grants us the clarity of Today to forget the darkness of Yesterday, preparing us for Tomorrow along the path of imperishable light.

messages.title: Enemies
paragraphs: “Love your enemies.” — JESUS (Luke 6:35)
The statement of the Divine Master deserves meditation everywhere. Naturally, the recommendation regarding the love of enemies calls for special analysis.

The crowd, in general, does not translate the verb to love except through affectionate activities. For a person to demonstrate affective capacity in the eyes of the vulgar, they must deploy an immense capital of words and tender attitudes, when we know that love can shine in the heart of creatures without any superficial exteriorization. Because the Father grants us laborious and harsh experiences, on Earth or in other worlds, we cannot attribute any denial of love to Him.
In the terrain referred to by the Divine Friend, it is fair that we pause for legitimate reflections.

Where there is struggle there is antagonism, revealing the existence of circumstances with which it would not be lawful to agree when dealing with the common good. When the Lord advised us to love our enemies, He did not demand applause for those who deliberately steal or destroy, nor did He command us to multiply the wings of perversity or bad faith. He truly recommended helping the most cruel; however, not with undue approval, but with the sincere and fraternal disposition to help them rise back to the divine path through patience, restorative resource, or healing work. Above all, the Master was concerned with protecting us against the poison of hatred, preventing us from falling into inferior, useless, or disastrous disputes.

Love, therefore, those who show themselves contrary to your heart, supporting them fraternally with all the possibilities of help within your reach, convinced that such a measure will save you from the calamitous duel of evil against evil.

messages.title: Let Us Look at This
paragraphs: “For Christ sent me not to baptize, but to preach the gospel: not with wisdom of words, lest the cross of Christ should be made of none effect.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians 1:17)
Generally, when incarnated, we feel a vain pleasure in attracting the greatest number of people to our way of believing.
We are invariably good preachers and eminently subtle in creating reasoning that crushes the viewpoints of those who cannot understand us in the immediacy of struggle.

At the first small triumph achieved, we become industrious in consulting holy books, not to acquire vaster enlightenment, but with the objective of researching the human letters of the divine scriptures, seeking to highlight the vulnerable statements of our opponents.

If Roman Catholics, we insist on our friends' observance of Mass and materialized sacraments; if adherents of reformed churches, we demand general compliance with external worship; and if Spiritualists, we seek to multiply sessions of exchange with the invisible Plane.

Such an effort is nonetheless commendable in some of its characteristics; however, it is imperative to remember that the Gospel apprentice, when sincerely seeking to understand Christ, feels viscerally renewed in their intimate conduct.

When Jesus penetrates a person's heart, He turns them into a living testimony of the good and commands them to evangelize their brothers and sisters with their own life; and when a person reaches Jesus, they do not stop purely and simply at the station of brilliant words, but live according to the Master, exemplifying the work and love that illuminate life, so that the glory of the cross may not be made in vain.

messages.title: Offerings
paragraphs: “For this he did once, when he offered up himself.” — PAUL (Hebrews 7:27)

Human beings always fare well in a bountiful house under a blue sky. However, as soon as difficulties arise, there they are, looking for someone to replace them in places of annoyance and pain. Often, they pay a high price for flight and indefinitely postpone the beneficial experience to which they were invited by the Lord's hand.
Because of this, religious people of all times establish complicated problems with the offerings of faith.
In primitive rites there was no hesitation regarding the sacrifice of youths and children.
With the passage of time, humanity moved on to the slaughter of sheep, bulls, and goats in sanctuaries.
For many centuries the plan of offering precious items and riches destined for worship services endured.
Through all these demonstrations, however, humanity seeks nothing less than to court the exclusive sympathy of God, as if the Father were inclined to earthly particularisms.

Most of those who offer material gifts do not act this way before the houses of faith out of love for the divine work, but with the deliberate purpose of buying heaven's favor, exempting themselves from the work of self-improvement.

In this sense, however, Christ provided a precious response to His wards in the world. Far from pleading any prerogatives, He sent no substitutes to Calvary or animals for sacrifice in the temples, but embraced the heavy cross Himself, immolating Himself in favor of humanity and implying that all disciples will be compelled to offer their own testimony on the altar of their own lives.

messages.title: Pages
paragraphs: “But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, and easy to be entreated, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy.” — (JAMES 3:17)

Every written page has a soul, and the believer needs to listen to its nature. Sincere examination will immediately clarify to which sphere it belongs within the circle of destructive activity in the world or at the center of edification efforts for spiritual life.

First, the reader who loves truth and goodness will analyze its lines to judge the purity of its content, understanding that if its expressions were born from superior sources, they will find therein the unequivocal signs of peace, moderation, fraternal affability, loving understanding, and good fruits after all.

However, if the page reflects the subtle poisons of human partiality, such a message of thought does not originate from the nobler spheres of life. Even if it originates from the action of supposedly superior disincarnated Spirits, the leaf that does not bring benefit in harmony and fraternal construction is merely a reflection of inferior conditions.

Examine, therefore, the pages of your daily contact with the thoughts of others, and keep company with those that wish you elevation. You do not need the ones that seem the most brilliant, but the ones that make you better.

messages.title: Let Us Remember
paragraphs: “Remember my bonds.” — PAUL (Colossians 4:18)
In habitual childishness and thoughtlessness, believers remember only the luminous halo of sanctified Spirits on Earth.
Many suppose they will easily find them beyond the tomb to receive their precious reminders. They expect nothing less than Heaven through brilliant repose in cosmic immensity...

How many will remember Paul solely in his glorification? However, in this remark to the Colossians, the great apostle exhorts his friends to remember his imprisonments, as if to say that disciples must not crystallize their thought in the anticipation of celestial ease, but rather reflect seriously on the righteous labor to possess the divine kingdom.
The conquest of sublimated spirituality also has its paths. It is indispensable to walk them.
Before fixing the resplendent crown of the faithful apostles, let us meditate on the thorns that wounded their brows.
Paul managed to reach the heights; however, how many blows of the whip, stonings, and ironies did he endure, adapting to the teachings of Christ as he climbed the mountain!...

— Do not look only at the manifest superiority of those to whom you consecrate admiration and respect. Do not forget to imitate them by attaching yourself to the sacrificial services to which they devoted themselves to achieve divine ends.

messages.title: Fraternal Love
paragraphs: “Let brotherly love continue.” — PAUL (Hebrews 13:1)

Family affections, blood ties, and natural sympathies can be very holy manifestations of the soul when the individual elevates them on the altar of superior feeling; nevertheless, it is reasonable that the spirit does not fall under the weight of its own inclinations.
Balance is the ideal position.
Through excessive care, countless parents harm their children.
Through excessive worries, many spouses descend into the caves of despair, confronted by the insatiable monsters of jealousy that annihilate their happiness.
Because of lack of vigilance, beautiful friendships end in an abyss of shadow.
The evangelical appeal, for this very reason, is coated with immense importance.
Pure fraternity is the most sublime of relational systems among souls.
A person who feels like a child of God and a sincere brother to all creatures is not a victim of the phantoms of spite, envy, ambition, or distrust.
Those who love one another fraternally rejoice in the joy of their companions; they feel happy with the fortune that visits their peers.
Violent affections, commonly known on Earth, pass by like volcanic fires and are useless.

In the web of reincarnations, affective titles constantly change. This is because fraternal love, sublime and pure, representing the supreme goal of the effort of understanding, is the imperishable light that will survive on the eternal path.

messages.title: Retaliations
paragraphs: “Actually, then, it is already a complete failure for you that you have lawsuits against one another. Why not rather accept injustice? Why not rather be defrauded?” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 6.7)
Lawsuits do not always remain in the courts of justice, in the scandalous terrain of public trials.

They express themselves on a much larger scale in the center of homes and institutions. There they move about, through mental disorder and whispered conversations, in the invisible sludge of hatred that suffocates hearts and neutralizes energies. If they persist, however, it is because members of the family or association feed them with the oil of repressed animosity.
Countless learners become victims of similar disturbances because they entrench themselves in false regenerative principles.
Generally speaking, a large part prefers the aggressive attitude, sword in hand, fencing warmly in the illusory supposition of operating the repair of one's neighbor.

Ready to protest, accuse, and criticize amid great noise, they usually clarify that they serve the truth. For what reason, however, do they not exemplify their own faith, enduring injustice and harm heroically, in the silence of a faithful soul, before opting for any retaliation?

How many homes would be happy, how many institutions would convert into permanent springs of light, if the believers of the Gospel learned to be silent in order to speak, at the right time, with profit?
We do not refer here to ordinary men, but rather to the disciples of Jesus.

How much the world will profit when the follower of Christ feels blessed to be a mere instrument of good in the Divine Hands, forgetting the old purpose of being an arbitrary guide of the Heavenly Service?

messages.title: Do Not Tyrannize
paragraphs: “And with many such parables He was speaking the word to them, as they were able to hear it.” — (MARK, 4.33)
In the diffusion of evangelical teachings, from time to time we encounter rigorous and demanding preachers.

Such an anomaly is not verified only in the general framework of service. In the private sphere, not infrequently, severe and fervent friends emerge who desperately demand the attunement of loved ones with the religious principles they have embraced.
Bitter discussions arise, touching on venomous sourness.
Beautiful affective expressions are shaken at their foundations by undue offenses.
However, if the disciple truly remains possessed by the purpose of union with the Master, such an attitude is easy to correct.
The Lord only taught those who listened to Him, “as they were able to understand.”

To the apostles He imparted instructions of high symbolic value, while to the crowd He transmitted fundamental truths through simple stories. His conversation differed according to the spiritual needs of those who surrounded Him. He never violated anyone's natural position.
If you are in the Lord's service, consider the imperatives of illumination, because the world needs Christian servants, not doctrinal tyrants.

messages.title: Make Preparations
paragraphs: “And he will show you a large upper room, furnished; make preparations there.” — JESUS (Luke, 22.12)
That furnished upper room, referred to by Jesus, is a perfect symbol of the internal chamber of the soul.

Faced with nature, which offers valuable lessons on all planes of activity, let us observe that man waits each day, always renewing the provisions of the home. Here, debris is swept away; there, walls are adorned. The furniture, almost always the same, goes through daily cleaning processes.
The conscientious man will recognize that the majority of actions, in physical experience, end in incessant preparation for the life that will be faced beyond the death of the body.
If this happens with the material facet of earthly life, what shall we say of the strictly spiritual effort for the eternal path?

Certainly, numerous creatures will cross the day like irrational beings, in almost mechanical movements. They rise from bed, feed the perishable body, absorb their attention with trifles, and sleep again each night.

The sincere learner, however, knows that he has reached the symbolic upper room of the heart. Although he cannot change his ideas daily, as happens with the furniture of a residence, he gives them new shine at every moment, sublimating impulses, renewing conceptions, elevating desires, and continually improving the commendable qualities he already possesses.
The simply earthly man remains in expectation of organic death; the spiritual man awaits the Divine Master to consolidate his own redemption.
Do not abandon, therefore, the upper room of faith and, within it, make preparations in constant ascension.

messages.title: Workers
paragraphs: “Be diligent to present yourself approved to God as a worker who does not need to be ashamed.” — PAUL (2 Timothy, 2.15)
Since immemorial times, creatures have idealized a thousand ways of presenting themselves to God and His messengers.

Many people worry throughout their entire existence about how to tailor garments for the celestial concert, while countless believers carefully note down earthly sorrows with the purpose of stringing them into an immense rosary of complaints before the Lord, seeking prominence in the future world.

The majority of devotees wish to begin the journey beyond death with titles of saints; however, there is no more accurate way to reflect upon our position with truth than that in which we fit into the condition of laborers.
The world is a department of the Divine House.
Chairs and hoes do not constitute elements of humiliating division, but rather hierarchical steps for different cooperators.
The edifying path unfolds for all.
Here, graves are opened in productive soil; there, books are handled for the furrow of intelligence, but the spirit is the living foundation of manifested service.
Workers are classified into different positions; however, the field is one.

At the center of realities, therefore, let no one worry about honorary titles, not least because work is complex in all sectors of dignifying action, and the result is always the fruit of well-lived cooperation. This is why we judge with Paul that the greatest victory for the disciple will be to present himself one day to the Lord as an approved worker.

messages.title: Following the Truth
paragraphs: “Instead, speaking the truth in love, we are to grow up in all aspects into Him who is the head, even Christ.” — PAUL (Ephesians, 4.15)
Because truth equally partakes of relative condition, countless thinkers embark upon absolute negativism, converting materialism into a zone of extreme intellectual disturbance.
How are we to interpret the truth if it seems so elusive to ordinary methods of appreciation?

Flaunting superiority, the officious scientist asserts that reality goes no further than organized forms, much like the fanatic who only admits divine revelation within the circle of the dogmas he embraces.
Paul, however, offers a profitable indication to those who desire to penetrate the domain of higher knowledge.
It is necessary to follow the truth in charity, without the purpose of imprisoning it in the cage of limited definition.

Let us convert the noble teachings received into love. Truth added to charity presents spiritual progress as the resultant of effort. Without heeding such an imperative, we will be surprised by vigorous obstacles on the path of sublimation. We need to grow in everything that experience offers us of usefulness and beauty for eternity with Christ, but we will not achieve this fulfillment without transforming, on a daily basis, the small portion of truth we possess into love for our neighbors.
Understanding asks for reality, just as reality asks for understanding.
Let us be true, therefore, but let us be good.

messages.title: It Is Not Only That
paragraphs: “But now you also, put them all aside: anger, wrath, malice, slander, and abusive speech from your mouth.” — PAUL (Colossians, 3.8)
In religious activity, many people believe in the reform of personality as long as the disciple of faith detaches himself from certain material goods.

A man who distributes a large quantity of clothing and food among the needy is considered renewed in the Lord; however, this constitutes a modality of true transformation, without representing the whole of the characteristics that pertain to it.
There are creatures who strip themselves of money in favor of beneficence, but do not yield in the terrain of personal opinion, in the sublime effort of renunciation.
Enormous ranks of learners proclaim themselves willing to practice good; however, they demand that beneficence services be carried out according to their whims and not according to Jesus.
Ermanywhere, fervent promises of fidelity to Christ are heard; yet, no one will achieve such an accomplishment without observing the full set of necessary obligations.

A small miscalculation can betray the balance of an entire building. That is why when someone strips themselves of some material patrimony for the benefit of others, they must not forget to also dismantle, around their own steps, the old coverings of rancor, unhealthy whim, hasty judgment, or criminal levity, within which we strap a heavy mask to our face in order to appear what we are not.

messages.title: Reapers
paragraphs: “Then He said to His disciples, 'The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few.'” — (MATTHEW, 9.37)
The teaching here does not refer to the spiritual harvest of great periods of renewal in time, but rather to the harvest of consolations that the Gospel encompasses in itself.

At that hour, a mob of disheartened and wandering hearts remained around the Master which, according to Matthew's narrative, resembled a flock without a shepherd. They were downcast faces and supplicant eyes in painful dejection.
It was then that Jesus raised the symbol of the truly great harvest, flanked, however, by rare reapers.

The reason is that the Gospel remains in the world as a blessed celestial harvest destined to enrich the human spirit, yet the percentage of creatures willing to do the reaping work is very reduced. The majority await processed wheat or ready bread for their own nourishment. Very few are those who face storms, the rigor of labor, and the dangerous surprises that the effort of harvesting demands from the devoted and faithful worker.
Because of this, the crowd of the desperate and disillusioned continues passing through the world, in a growing file, across the centuries.

The self-denying workers of Christ remain burdened by virtue of so many hungry people who surround the harvest without the precise courage to seek for themselves the food of eternal life. And this picture will persist on Earth until good consumers learn to be good reapers as well.

messages.title: Believing in Vain
paragraphs: “by which also you are saved, if you hold fast the word which I preached to you, unless you believed in vain.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 15.2)

Just as many flowers do not reach fruition in the proper season, there are countless souls in the services of belief who do not achieve self-illumination over long periods of earthly struggle, because they believed in vain along the tracks of life.
Paul of Tarsus was very explicit when he asserted to the Corinthians that they would be saved if they retained the Gospel.
The revelation of Jesus is an extensive field where there is room for all men, referring as we do to diverse services.

Many arrive at the work, yet do not go beyond the letter, cooperating in purely intellectual organizations; some improvise theological systems, others contribute to statistics, and still others concern themselves with the historical location of the Lord.

It is imperative to recognize that every worthy task is clothed in usefulness in due time, in conformity with the feelings of the collaborator; however, as regards the eternal life that Christianity unfolds before our gaze, it is essential that we retain the Master's teaching within us, with a view to its necessary application.

Each learner must be a living page of the book that Jesus is writing with the evolutionary material of the Earth. The disciple will engrave the Gospel in his own existence or else prepare himself to restart learning, since without fixing the light of the lesson within himself, he will have believed in vain.

messages.title: Thoughts
paragraphs: “Finally, brethren, whatever is true, whatever is honorable, whatever is right, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is of good repute, if there is any excellence and if anything worthy of praise, dwell on these things.” — PAUL (Philippians, 4.8)

All human works constitute the resultant of the creatures' thoughts. Evil and good, the ugly and the beautiful lived, first of all, in the mental source that produced them, in the incessant movements of life.

The Gospel embodies the generous roadmap for man's mind to renew itself along the paths of higher spirituality, proclaiming the necessity of such a transformation toward the highest Planes. It will not be solely with the intellectual refinements of Philosophy that the disciple will begin his efforts toward a fulfillment of this tenor. Renewing thoughts is not as easy as it seems at first glance. It demands much capacity for renunciation and profound self-mastery, qualities that man cannot achieve without labor and sacrifice of the heart. This is why many servants modify verbal expressions, thinking they have recast their thoughts. However, at the moment of recapitulating, through the repetition of circumstances, the redeeming experiences, they once again find analogous disturbances, because obstacles and shadows remain in the mind like hidden phantoms.

To think is to create. The reality of this creation may not exteriorize itself suddenly in the field of transient effects, but the object formed by mental power lives within the intimate world, demanding special care for the effort of continuity or extinction.

Paul's advice to the Philippians presents sublime content. The disciples who can comprehend its profound essence, seeking to see the true, honorable, right, pure, and lovely side of all things, cultivating it each day, will have found the divine equation.
.Emmanuel

messages.title: It Is the Same
paragraphs: “For the Father Himself loves you.” — JESUS (John, 16.27)
Let no one despise the values of trust.
Let no servant flee from the benefit of cooperation.
Whoever can give something useful today will possibly need some essential collaboration tomorrow.
However, because one enriches oneself with fraternity and faith, let one not forget the need for infinite development in the good.
Sincere workers of the Gospel must work against pernicious favoritism.

The divine husbandry has no privileged ones. In its numerous sections, there are workers who are more devoted and more faithful; however, these must not be categorized as fetishes, but rather respected and imitated as symbols of loyalty and service.
Creating human idols is worse than erecting statues destined for adoration. Marble is impassive, but our companion is our neighbor, whose condition no longer should anyone abuse.
Let every man pay the tribute of his own effort to life.
The Supreme Lord expects only this from us, in order to convert us into direct collaborators.
Christ Himself affirmed that the same Father who distinguishes Him loves humanity equally.
The God who inspires the physician is the one who supports the sick person.
It does not matter that Asians and Europeans designate Him under different names. Invariably, it is the same Father.

Let us preserve, then, the light of consolation, the blessing of fraternal assistance, trust in our Elders, and the certainty of their protection; however, let us not forget the natural duty to press onward to the High, utilizing our own feet.

messages.title: No One Leaves
paragraphs: “Simon Peter answered him: Lord, to whom shall we go? you have the words of eternal life.” — (JOHN, 6.68)

As the Master revealed new characteristics of His doctrine of love, the followers, then numerous, penetrated vaster circles in the domain of responsibility. Many of them, because of this, fearful of the duty that would fall to them, discreetly withdrew from the welcoming upper room of Capernaum.
Christ, however, aware of the obligations of a divine order, far from violating the principles of freedom, gathered the small remaining assembly and asked the disciples:
— Do you also want to leave?
It was under these circumstances that Peter gave the wise response, forever engraved in the Christian edifice.

Indeed, whoever begins the service of superior spirituality with Jesus will never feel identical emotions at a distance from Him. The sublime experience can sometimes be interrupted, but never annihilated. Compelled on various occasions by imperatives of the physical zone, the companion of the Gospel will suffer spiritual accidents, submitting to a brief standstill; however, he will not permanently lose the way.
Whoever truly partakes in the banquet of Christian revelation will at no time forget the loving Master who addressed the invitation to them.
For this reason, Simon Peter asked very appropriately:
— Lord, to whom shall we go?

It is because the world remains full of philosophers, scientists, and reformers of every kind, undoubtedly respectable for the advanced human conceptions they preach; in most situations, however, they are mere expositors of transient words, with reflections in ephemeral experiences. Christ, nevertheless, is the Savior of souls and the Master of hearts, and with Him, we find the pathways of eternal life.

messages.title: In What Way?
paragraphs: “What do you want? shall I come to you with a rod, or in love and a spirit of gentleness?” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 4.21)

Sometimes the apostle to the Gentiles, inflamed with sublime inspirations, brought direct interrogations to his companions—almost cruel if considered solely in a literal sense, but bearers of admirable reality when viewed through the imperishable light.
In all Christian homes, irradiations of love and peace vibrate. Jesus never left faithful followers forgotten, no matter how separated they walk in the field of interpretations.
Selfless emissaries of heavenly devotion spread sanctifying help in all epochs of Humanity. History is a demonstration of this incontestable truth.
No century has lacked legitimate missionaries of goodness.
Promises and revelations of the Lord reach the ports of knowledge through a thousand ways.

The learners who have entered the evangelical ranks, therefore, cannot plead ignorance of purpose in order to hide their own faults. Each one, in their proper place, has already received the program of service they are to execute each day. If they flee from work and escape the testimony, they owe such an anomaly to their own paralytic will.
This is why a moment may arise when the idle and begging disciple will hear the Master, without intermediaries, exclaiming in the same way:
— “What do you want? shall I come to you with a rod, or in love and a spirit of gentleness?”

messages.title: Let Us Not Stumble
paragraphs: “Jesus answered: Are there not twelve hours in the day? If anyone walks in the day, he does not stumble, because he sees the light of this world.” — (JOHN, 11.9)
The content of the Master's question has vast significance for the disciples of today. “Are there not twelve hours in the day?”
Consciously, each one should inquire of themselves how they are applying such a great capital of time.
People speak with emphasis on the problem of the unemployed in modern times. However, any crisis in this sense does not result from a lack of work, but rather from the absence of individual goodwill.

A thorough investigation in this regard would reveal the reality. Many people remain without activity out of rebellion against the kind of service offered to them or out of non-acceptance regarding salaries.
Imbalance ensues immediately.
The idleness of the workers provokes the vigilance of the stewards, and the transient laws of the world reflect animosity and distrust.

If arms come to a standstill, workshops fall asleep. The same occurs in the spheres of spiritual action. How many learners abandon their posts, alleging anguish of time? How many do not transfer themselves to the zone of laziness, because this or that happened, completely out of tune with the superior principles they embrace?

And, for trifles, a large number of vigorous servants seek the shadow-filled rear. But he who retains auditory acuity still listens with profit to the word of the Lord: — “Are there not twelve hours in the day? If anyone walks in the day, he does not stumble.”

messages.title: The Opposites
paragraphs: “What then shall we say to these things? If God is for us, who can be against us?” — PAUL (Romans, 8.31)
Paul's interrogation still represents a precious theme for the evangelical community of our days.
Before our effort unfolds an immense field, where the Master awaits our resolute collaboration.
Often, however, a large number of companions prefer to abandon construction to dispute with evildoers along the way.

Adverse elements surround us everywhere. Unexpected obstacles draw before our afflicted eyes, old friends leave us alone, and situations that were favorable until yesterday are metamorphosed into cruel hostilities.
Enormous ranks of workers flee from danger, fearing the storm and forgetting the testimony.
However, we were not placed in the work in order to surrender to panic, nor did the Master send us to work with the objective of confusing us through experiences in the outer circles.

We were called to build. Naturally, we must count on the thousand eventualities of each day, capable of springing from opposing forces, making our building difficult; our day of struggle will be besieged by perturbation and fatigue. This is inevitable in a world that expects everything from the genuine Christian.

By reason of such an imperative, amidst threats and misunderstandings of the path, it behooves us to inquire, good-humoredly, in the manner of the apostle to the Gentiles: — “If God is for us, who can be against us?”

messages.title: Against Folly
paragraphs: “Are you so foolish? Having begun in the Spirit, are you now being made complete by the flesh?” — PAUL (Galatians, 3.3)

One of the greatest disasters in the path of disciples is the false understanding with which they begin their effort in the superior region, marching in reverse toward the circles of inferiority. They thus give the idea of men who set out in search of gold, contenting themselves afterward with the mud of the puddle.
Such failures become common across the various sectors of religious thought.

We observe sick individuals who turn to elevated spirituality, nurturing noble impulses and taken with precious intentions; once healing is achieved, however, they ponder the best way to apply the advantages gained toward acquiring easy money. Some, after being helped by friends from the sublimated spheres in transcendent questions of eternal life, intend to attribute to those same benefactors the function of human police officers in the search for less worthy objectives.

Numerous learners persist in the works of goodness; however, less favorable hours appear and they surrender, inert, to discouragement, demanding a reward for the meager terrestrial years in which they tried to serve in the field of the Divine Master, completely unconcerned with the multi-millennial periods in which we have been served by the Lord.
Such spiritual anomalies that considerably disturb the effort of disciples proceed from the poisonous filters composed of the anxieties of reward.
Let us work, therefore, against the expectation of retribution, so that we may continue the task begun, in the company of humility, the bearer of imperishable light.

messages.title: Heaven with Heaven
paragraphs: “But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust destroys and where thieves do not break in and steal.” — JESUS (Matthew, 6.20)

In all Christian ranks, individuals ambitious for reward mingle and presume to find, in this statement of Jesus, a positive resource of vengeance against all those who, through work and devotion, received greater possibilities on Earth.
What seems to them trust in God is disguised hatred toward their fellow men.
Because they cannot monopolize financial resources before their eyes, they launch thoughts of criticism and rebellion, awaiting paradise for the desired retaliation.
However, it is not by surrendering the body to the laboratory of nature that the human personality will automatically find the planes of Resplendent Beauty.

Certainly, imperishable sanctuaries shine in the sublimated Spheres, but it is imperative to consider that, in the regions immediate to human activity, we still find an immense copy of moths and thieves, in the evolutionary lines that extend beyond the sepulcher.

When the Master recommended that we lay up treasures in heaven, He was advising us to expand the values of goodness in the peace of the heart. The man who acquires faith and knowledge, virtue and illumination, in the divine recesses of conscience, possesses the celestial itinerary. Whoever applies the redeeming principles they embrace ends up conquering this precious chart; and whoever works daily in the practice of good lives piling up riches on the Heights of Life.
Let no one be deceived in this sense. Beyond Earth, blessings of the Lord shine in the Celestial Paradigms; nevertheless, it is necessary to possess light to perceive them.
It is of the Law that the Divine identify with what is Divine, because no one will contemplate heaven if they harbor hell in their heart.

messages.title: The Selfish Son
paragraphs: “So he answered and said to his father: Lo, these many years I have been serving you; I never transgressed your commandment at any time; and yet you never gave me a young goat, that I might make merry with my friends.” — (LUKE, 15.29)
The parable does not present only the prodigal son. With sharper attention, we will find the selfish son.

The veiled teaching of the Master demonstrates two extremes of filial ingratitude. One resides in squandering; the other, in avarice. These are the two extremities that close the circle of human incomprehension.

Generally speaking, believers have only seen the son who abandoned the paternal home in order to live in the dissipation of scandal, making himself deserving of all punishments; and rare learners have managed to fix their thoughts on the condemnable conduct of the brother who remained under the family roof, no less subject to reprimand.
Observing paternal generosity, the inferior sentiments that animate him come to the surface, and there he is in a demonstration of stinginess.
