He is bothered by the vibration of love reigning in the domestic environment; he alleges, like an authentic sluggard, his years of family service; he invokes, in the position of a vain believer, his supposed observance of the Divine Law, and disrespects the parent, incapable of sharing his righteous contentment.

This type of selfish man is very common in the cadres of life. Before the well-being and joy of others, he rebels and suffers through the dryness that annihilates him and the jealousy that poisons him.

Reading the parable with attention, we do not know which of the sons is more unfortunate, the prodigal or the selfish one, but we dare to believe in the immense unhappiness of the second, because the first already possessed the blessing of remorse in his favor.

messages.title: Internal Government
paragraphs: “But I discipline my body and bring it into subjection, lest, when I have preached to others, I myself should become disqualified.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 9.27)
Indeed, the body is a miniature of the Universe. It is imperative, therefore, to know how to govern it.

As a representation in terrestrial material of the spiritual personality, it is reasonable that each one be attentive to their dispositions. It is not that the passive substance has acquired power superior to that of the human will, yet it is imperative to recognize that inferior tendencies seek to subtract our power of dominion.
It is indispensable that every man be up to date with the governance of himself.

The inner life, in some way, resembles the life of a State. The Spirit assumes self-leadership, aided by various ministries, such as those of reflection, knowledge, comprehension, respect, and order. Diverse and simultaneous ideas constitute good or bad appeals of the intimate parliament. There exist, in the depths of each mind, vast potentials of progress and sublimation, demanding work.

The supreme governor, which is the Spirit, within the cellular cosmos, drafts beneficent laws, but does not always mobilize the auditing organs of its own will. And the inferior zones continue in ancient disorders, unconcerned with the renewing decrees that they neither oppose nor execute. When such an anomaly is verified, man becomes a living enigma, if he does not turn into a blind man or a scoundrel.
Whoever expects a healthy life without self-discipline is not far from ruinous or total imbalance.
It is necessary to install the government of ourselves in any position of life. The fundamental problem is one of a strong will toward ourselves, and of goodwill toward our brethren.

messages.title: The Possession of the Kingdom
paragraphs: “Strengthening the souls of the disciples, exhorting them to continue in the faith, and saying, 'We must through many tribulations enter the kingdom of God.'” — (ACTS, 14.22)
The Gospel deceives no one in its teachings.

It is common for believers to try to bribe divine forces. However, it will not be at the price of many masses, many hymns, or many psychic sessions that man will effect the sublime acquisition of excelsior spirituality.
Naturally, every edifying practice should be used as an element of assistance; however, the illuminative effort falls to each human individuality.
The Good News does not distribute indulgences at the world's price, and the creature finds countless paths for ascension.

Temples and instructors multiply, and each offers parcels of help or assistance in the service of guidance; however, entry into and possession of the eternal inheritance will be verified through righteous testimonies.
This is not accidental. It is a logical and necessary measure.
Rare statues are not improvised without chisel blows, just as wheat is not harvested without a plowed field.

Not a few learners tend to interpret certain warnings of the Gospel as an excess of exhortation to suffering; however, what seems to them an obsession with pain is an imperative of the soul's education for the imperishable life.
No man will find the infinite estuary of divine energies without the concurso of the Earth's tribulations.

A personality without struggle on the Planetary Crust is a narrow soul. Only work and sacrifice, difficulty and obstacle, as elements of progress and self-superation, can give man true news of his greatness.

messages.title: Whom Do You Obey?
paragraphs: “And having been perfected, He became the author of eternal salvation to all who obey Him.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 5.9)
Every creature obeys someone or something.
No one remains without a goal.
Rebellion itself is submitted to the corrective forces of life.

Man obeys at all times. However, if he has not yet been able to define his own submission by virtue of a constructive virtue, it is because he frequently attends, first of all, to the low impulses of nature, resisting the service of self-elevation.
Almost always, he transforms the obedience that saves him into slavery that condemns him.

The Lord established the gradations of the path, instituted the law of personal effort in acquiring the supreme values of life, and determined that man should accept His designs to be truly free; but the creature preferred to attend to its condition of inferiority and organized captivity. The disciple needs to examine attentively the field in which he develops his own task.
Whom do you obey? Do you perhaps attend, first of all, to human vanities or other people's opinions before observing the counsel of the Divine Master?
It is just to reflect always upon this, because only when we heed, in everything, the living teachings of Jesus can we break the slavery of the world in favor of eternal liberation.

messages.title: The Great Struggle
paragraphs: “For we do not wrestle against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this age, against spiritual hosts of wickedness in the heavenly places.” — PAUL (Ephesians, 6:12)
According to our reiterated statements, the great struggle does not lie in combat with blood and flesh, strictly speaking, but rather with our inferior spiritual dispositions.
Paul of Tarsus acted divinely inspired when he wrote his recommendation to the companions in Ephesus.
The silent and incessant conflict between sincere disciples and the forces of shadow is linked to our own nature, for we openly connived with evil in a not-so-remote past.
We have been declared participants in delinquent actions in the heavenly places.
And, even today, among the condensed fluids of the flesh or in the Spheres close to them, we act in the service of self-restoration in full paradise.
The Earth is likewise a sublime step of Heaven.
When someone refers to fallen angels, human listeners immediately keep the impression of a superb and mysterious palace, from which wise and luminous creatures are expelled.
Does the same not happen when an educated man indulges in murder, in front of a university or a temple?
Usually, the earthly observer relates the crime, without, however, stopping to examine the sacred and venerable place where it was consummated.
The great struggle, to which the Apostle refers, continues without rest.

Human cities and buildings are heavenly zones. Neither they nor the organic cells that serve us constitute the powerful enemies, but rather the “spiritual hosts of wickedness,” with which we attune through the inferior points that we desperately keep with us, vast regimentations of beings and dark thoughts that obscure human vision, and that operate subtly, so as not to lose yesterday's active companions.

messages.title: Who Do You Say That I Am?
paragraphs: “He said to them, ‘But who do you say that I am?’” — (LUKE, 9:20)

In the discussions properly belonging to the world, there will always be writers and scientists willing to examine the Master along the lines of their purely intellectual impressions, under the qualms of human presumption.

These friends, however, have not had contact with the soul of the Gospel, have not surpassed academic circles, nor do they risk conventional titles in a dispassionate excursion through divine revelation; naturally, therefore, they will continue to be deceived by vanity, prejudice, or fear peculiar to their transitory way of being, until their experience is renewed on the roads of imperishable life.
However, in the intimacy of sincere and faithful disciples, Jesus' question takes on singular importance.
Each of us must have our own opinions regarding the wisdom and mercy with which we have been graced.

Vain lectures about Christ suit only spirits distraught on the path of life. To the rest of us, however, falls the testimony of intimacy with the Lord, because we are direct beneficiaries of His infinite goodness. Let us meditate and renew aspirations in His Gospel of Love, understanding the impropriety of mutual interrogations regarding the Master, because the sublime interrogation comes from Him to each of us and we all need to know Him, so as to mark Him in our daily tasks.

messages.title: Spiritual Manifestations
paragraphs: “But the manifestation of the Spirit is given to each one for the profit of all.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 12:7)
With the revival of pure Christianity in the groups of Spiritism with Jesus, an identical concern arises to those that tortured the disciples of apostolic times regarding mediumship.
The majority of workers in evangelization worry about the immediate development of incipient faculties.
In certain centers of service, achievements superior to the possibilities at their disposal are demanded; in others, they dream of far-reaching phenomena.
The problem, however, is not reduced to external acquisitions.
Let man enrich his own intimate illumination, intensify spiritual power through knowledge and love, and he will enter into the possession of eternal treasures naturally.
Many apprentices would like to be great seers or admirable revealers, lulled by the perspective of superiority, but they do not even dare to meditate on the sweat of sublime conquest.

They lean toward the proceeds, but do not consider the effort. In this sense, it is interesting to remember that Simon Peter, whose spirit felt so well with the glorious Master on Tabor, could not endure the anguities of the flogged Friend on Calvary.

It is fair that disciples aim for spiritual aggrandizement; nonetheless, whoever possesses a humble faculty should not despise it because a closer brother holds more expressive qualities. Let each one work with the material entrusted to them, convinced that the Supreme Lord does not attend to the problem of spiritual manifestations according to human whim, but rather according to general utility.

messages.title: To Give Thanks
paragraphs: “And be thankful.” — PAUL (Colossians, 3:15)
It is curious to see that the multitude of disciples is always interested in receiving graces; however, it is rare to find someone with the disposition to minister them.
Spiritual resources, however, in their common movement, should obey the same system applied to provisions of a material order.

In the chapter of soul blessings, one should not receive and spend senselessly, but resort to the criterion of prudence and righteousness, so that possibilities are not absorbed by disorder and injustice.
This is why, in his instructions to the Christians of Colossae, the apostle recommends that we be thankful.

Among sincere disciples, the old habit of expressing recognition in bombastic and laudatory phrases is not justified. In the community of workers faithful to Jesus, giving thanks means applying the gifts received profitably, both to one's neighbor and to oneself.
For loving parents, the children's best thanksgiving consists of the elevated understanding of work and life to which they bear witness.

Expressing gratitude to Christ, the apostles were loyal to Him until the final sacrifice; Paul of Tarsus receives the Master's appeal and, in a sign of joy and love, serves the Divine Cause through nameless sufferings for over thirty successive years.

Giving thanks will not be merely a problem of brilliant words; it is feeling the greatness of gestures, the light of benefits, the generosity of trust, and responding spontaneously by extending the treasures of life to others.

messages.title: The Devil
paragraphs: “Jesus answered them, ‘Did I not choose you, the twelve, and one of you is a devil?’” — (JOHN, 6:70)
When theology refers to the devil, the believer immediately imagines the absolute lord of evil, dominating in an endless hell.
In the disciple's conception, the cursed region is located in a distant sphere, within stormy darkness...

Yes, purgatorial zones are countless and gloomy, terrible and painful; however, according to Jesus' own statement, the devil shared in the apostolic services, remained alongside the disciples, and one of them constituted a representation of the infernal genius himself. This is enough for us to learn that the term “devil” did not indicate, in the Master's concept, a giant of perversity, powerful and eternal, in space and time. It designates man himself when chained to the turpitudes of inferior feeling.
From this we conclude that each human creature presents a certain percentage of demonic expression in the lower part of the personality.
Satan will then symbolize the force contrary to good.

When man discovers it within the vast world of himself, he understands evil, combats it, avoids the intimate hell, and develops the divine qualities that elevate him to superior spirituality. Vast multitudes plunge into secular despairs because they have not yet managed to identify such a truth.

And, commenting on this passage of John, we are compelled to ponder: — “If among the twelve apostles there was one who had turned into a devil, despite the divine mission of the circle destined for the transformation of the world, how many will there be in each group of ordinary men on Earth?”

messages.title: False Discourses
paragraphs: “But be doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves with false discourses.” — (JAMES, 1:22)
It is never too much to comment on the importance and sacred character of the word.

The Gospel itself asserts that in the beginning was the Word, and whoever carefully examines the current position of the world will recognize that all difficult situations originate from misapplied verbalist power.

False discourses have deceived individuals, families, and nations. Some believed in vain promises, others in fallacious theories, and still others in perspectives of freedom without obligations. And races, groups, and creatures, identifying the illusion, clash with one another, seeking the paternity of faults.
Much blood and many tears have the creation of the human verb cost. It is impossible, for now, to compute this painful price or determine how much time will be necessary for the precise ransom.
In the whirlwind of struggles, however, the friend of Christ can make use of the evangelical treasure for the benefit of his individual sphere.

Fulfilling the Master's word within us is the divine program. Without the execution of this plan of salvation, the remaining services under our responsibility will constitute sublimated theology, brilliant reasoning, magnificent literature, much admiration and respect from the world's inferior field, but never the necessary realization.
This is why it is always dangerous to linger on the way, listening to whoever flees the reality of our duties.

messages.title: Cure of Hatred
paragraphs: “Therefore ‘If your enemy is hungry, feed him; If he is thirsty, give him a drink; For in so doing you will heap coals of fire on his head.’” — PAUL (Romans, 12:20)
Man, generally, when decided upon the service of good, finds rows of gratuitous adversaries wherever he goes, much like light which is invariably besieged by the antagonism of shadows.

Sometimes, however, whether due to mistakes of the past or misunderstandings of the present, he is confronted by stronger enemies who become a constant threat to his tranquility. Counting on an enemy of this sort is suffering a painful inner illness when the creature has not yet grown fond of living experiences in the Gospel.

Almost always, the well-meaning apprentice develops the maximum of his own strengths in favor of reconciliation; however, the broadest effort seems in vain. Impenetrability characterizes the other's heart, and the best gestures of love go unnoticed by him.

Against this situation, however, the Divine Book offers a salutary recipe. It is not advisable to aggravate friction, develop discussions, and much less for the well-intentioned creature to dissolve into flattering gestures. Wait for the opportunity to manifest good.

From the minute the offended party forgets the dissension and returns to love, Jesus' service is re-established; however, the offender's vision is slower and, on many occasions, he only understands the new light when it turns into an advantage for his personal circle.

A sincere disciple of Christ easily frees himself from inferior ties, but yesterday's antagonist may persist for a long time in the hardening of his heart. This is why giving him all the good at the opportune moment is heaping renewing fire upon his head, curing his hatred full of infernal expressions.

messages.title: Understanding
paragraphs: “Be transformed by the renewing of your mind.” — PAUL (Romans, 12:2)
When we report on the problem of spiritual transformation, the community of Gospel disciples agrees with us regarding such a necessity, but not all demonstrate perfect understanding of the subject.
Deep down, all yearn for modification, yet the majority aspires to nothing more than a change in conventional classification.

Those less favored by money seek to climb the domain of material possibilities, holders of humble tasks plead for grand positions and, in a disconcerting crescendo, almost all aim for the undue transformation of the opportunities to which they adjust, plunging into unsettling disorder. The indispensable renewal is not that of a floating exterior plane. The devoted Christian will transform himself not by external signs, but by understanding, endowing his own mind with new light in new conceptions.
Just as any earthly work asks for the sincere application of the apprentices dedicated to it, the service of mental improvement demands constancy of effort in good and knowledge.
Here too, it is forced to recognize that discipline will enter with decisive factors.
Do not crystallize yourself, then, in false notions that have already harmed your yesterday.

Observe the structure of your reasonings now, before the circumstances surrounding you. Ask yourself how much you have gained in the Gospel to rightly analyze this or that event on your path. Do this and the Lord's Goodness will assist you in the enlightening answer to yourself.

messages.title: At Dawn
paragraphs: “Now on the first day of the week Mary Magdalene went to the tomb early, while it was still dark, and saw that the stone had been taken away from the tomb.” — (JOHN, 20:1)
We must not forget the circumstance in which Mary of Magdala receives the first message of the Master's resurrection.
Amidst the disturbances and discouragements of the small community, the great convert wastes no time in sterile lamentations nor seeks the sleep of oblivion.

The companions had broken the standard of trust. Between the remorse of their own defection and the bitterness over the Savior's sacrifice, whose sublime lesson they still could not grasp, they confused themselves in negative attitudes. Contradictory and anguished thoughts whipped their hearts.

Magdalene, however, breaks the veil of painful emotions that blocks her steps. It is imperative not to succumb under burdens, transforming them, above all, into a basic element in spiritual construction, and Mary resolves not to cower before pain. Because Christ was immolated on the cross, it would not be lawful to condemn His beloved memory to oblivion or indifference.

Vigilant, attentive to herself, before any satisfaction to old conventionalisms, she goes to meet the great obstacle constituted by the tomb, very early, preceding the awakening of her own friends, and finds the radiant answer of Eternal Life.
Reminiscing about this symbolic event, let us remember our ancient falls for having forgotten the “first day of the week,” exchanging, on all occasions, the “earlier” for the “later”.

messages.title: Eyes
paragraphs: “Having eyes full of adultery.” — (2 PETER, 2:14)
“Eyes full of adultery” constitute a rebellious disease in our evolutionary struggles.
Rare men use their eyes as blessed lamps and few employ them as living instruments of sanctifying work in the necessary vigil.
Most creatures try to use them, in front of any landscapes, to identify what they possess of worst.

Ordinary men habitually rest their eyes on a given situation only to fixate on the most appreciable angles to the inferior interests that concern them. If they cross a field, they do not note its meritorious function in the frameworks of collective life, but rather the possibility of personal and immediate profits it can offer them. If they see the affectionate sister of the human journey who follows not far from them, they almost always premeditate the organization of less worthy ties. If they find companions in places where they attend to inferior objectives, they do not recognize them as possible bearers of elevated ideas, but as competitors for their less fortunate purposes.
Let us listen to Simon Peter's cry of alarm, forgetting the habit of analyzing with evil.
Optimistic eyes will know how to extract sublime motives of teaching from the most diverse situations on the path they pursue.

No one should invoke the need for vigilance to justify manifestations of malice. The Christianized and prudent man knows how to contemplate his own problems; however, he never sees evil where evil does not yet exist.

messages.title: Intercession
paragraphs: “Brothers, pray for us.” — PAUL (1 Thessalonians, 5:25)
Many creatures smile ironically when spoken to about intercessory prayers.

Mankind has grown so accustomed to theatrical automatism that it finds a certain difficulty in understanding the deepest manifestations of spirituality. Intercessory prayer, however, continues to spread benefits with its unaltered values. It is not fair to believe that this prayer is flattering incense pouring out in the presence of an earthly monarch in order to obtain certain favors.

The supplication of intercession is one of the most beautiful acts of fraternity and constitutes the emission of beneficial and illuminating forces which, starting from the sincere spirit, go to the targeted goal by blessed contribution of comfort and energy. This does not happen, however, under the guise of a favor, but as a consequence of just laws. Man finds it hard to believe in the influence of the invisible waves of thought; nevertheless, the space that surrounds him is full of sounds that his material ears do not register; he only admits tangible help, yet, in physical nature itself, one sees venerable trees that protect and preserve herbs and shrubs, receiving the blessings of life without ever touching their roots and trunks.
Do not forget the blessings of intercession. Jesus prayed for His disciples and followers in supreme hours.

messages.title: The Tongue
paragraphs: “The tongue is also a fire.” — (JAMES, 3:6)
The sloth of creatures justifies James's bitter considerations in his epistle to the companions.
The beginning of all hecatombs on the Planet is located, almost always, in the misuse of the tongue.
It is placed among the members like the rudder of a powerful boat, as the great apostle of Jerusalem reminds us.
Within its potential remain sacred resources of creating, just as the small-proportioned rudder was installed to steer.

The tongue holds the divine spark of the word, but man, generally speaking, tends to divert it from its edifying function, placing it in the swamp of subordinate thoughts and, for this very reason, we see it at the forefront of almost all the aberrations of suffering humanity, crystallized in petty purposes, lacking humility and love.
War is born from the language of criminal, unsatisfied interests. Great social tragedies originate, on many occasions, from the conversation of inferior sentiments.
Rarely has man's tongue consoled and edified his brothers; let us recognize, however, that its disposition is always active to excite, dispute, depress, defile, accuse, and wound ruthlessly.

The sincere disciple finds in James's notes a brilliant thesis for all his experiences. And when the night of each day arrives, it is fair that he ask himself: — “Have I used my tongue today the way Jesus used His?”

messages.title: Law of Use
paragraphs: “And when they were filled, he said unto his disciples, Gather up the fragments that remain, that nothing be lost.” — (JOHN, 6:12)
Once the law of use is observed, misery will flee from the human path.
Against waste and avarice, everyone's work is imperative, because once balance is identified, the service of economic justice will be complete, provided goodwill dwells with all.

The evangelical passage that describes the work of feeding the crowd points out significant words of the Lord regarding the leftover bread, transmitting a teaching of profound importance to the disciples.
Generally, the sincere apprentice, in the first dazzle of revealing faith, wishes to give himself over to benevolent activities without a basis in real harmony.
Here we have, unquestionably, a laudable impulse, but even in the distribution of material goods, it is essential to avoid lack of control and excess.
The Father does not abolish winter because some of His children complain of the cold, but balances the situation by giving them blankets.
Charity calls for enthusiasm, yet it also demands generous discernment that does not incline the heart to dryness.

In the great assembly of the needy on the mount, certainly there would be no lack of lazy and wasteful people, ready to waste the remaining portion of bread without just necessity. Jesus, however, before the thoughtless could manifest themselves, clearly recommended: — “Gather up the fragments that remain, that nothing be lost.” This means that in all things, man must recognize that use is comprehensible in the Law, rejecting abuse, which is a mortal poison in the fountains of life.

messages.title: What Do You Awaken?
paragraphs: “Insomuch that they brought out the sick into the streets, and laid them on beds and couches, that at the least the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them.” — (ACTS, 5:15)
The conqueror of bloody glories spreads terror and ruin wherever he passes.
The crafty politician sows mistrust and doubt.
The biased judge awakens destructive fear.
The rebellious one spreads clouds of subtle poison.
The backbiter injects malignant dispositions into listeners, provoking rambling speech.
The slanderer extends threads of darkness on the path he treads.
The lazy person puts to sleep the energies of those he meets, inoculating them with numbing fluids.
The liar leaves disturbance and insecurity around his own steps.
The joker, with his simple presence, inspires and encourages hilarious stories.
All of us, through thoughts, words, and acts, create a private atmosphere that identifies us in the eyes of others.
The shadow of Simon Peter, who had accepted Christ and dedicated himself to Him, was sought after by sufferers and the sick who found in it hope and relief, comfort and joy.

Examine the subjects and attitudes that your presence awakens in others. With attention, you will discover the quality of your shadow and, if you are interested in acquiring illuminating values with Jesus, it will be easy to discover your own deficiencies and correct them.

messages.title: How to Bear Witness
paragraphs: “But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is coming upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.” — (ACTS, 1:8)
Indeed, Jesus is the Savior of the World, but He will not free the Earth from the empire of evil without the contribution of those who seek His saving resources.
The Divine Master, therefore, needs helpers with the duties of agents and witnesses everywhere.
The improvement of souls is impractical without education, and education requires legions of cooperators.
However, to fulfill the task of representatives of the Lord in the sublime work of elevation, external title alone, with a view to religious school, is not enough.
It is indispensable to obtain blessings from on High through the execution of our duties, no matter how difficult and painful.
Until now, we know to satiety on Earth the power to dominate, govern, refuse, and wound, easily accessible in the field of life.

Rare creatures, however, make themselves deserving of Jesus for the celestial power of obeying by teaching, of loving by building for good, of hoping by working, of helping selflessly. Without receiving such resources that identify us with the Divine Worker, and without the possibilities of reflecting Him to our neighbor in spirit and truth through our constant effort of personal application of the Gospel, we can personify excellent preachers, brilliant writers, or notable sympathizers of Christian doctrine, but not His witnesses.

messages.title: Spiritism in Faith
paragraphs: “And these signs shall follow them that believe; In my name shall they cast out devils; they shall speak with new tongues.” — JESUS (Mark, 16:17)
The manifestations of spiritual life remain in all the foundations of Divine Revelation, in the most varied circles of faith.
Spiritism in itself, therefore, ceases to be a novelty of modern times to figure at the root of all religious schools.
Moses establishes contact with the spiritual Plane at Sinai.
Jesus is seen by the disciples on Tabor, flanked by illustrious dead.
The apostolic college relates to the Spirit of the Master after His death and consolidates redemptive Christianity in the world.
The martyrs of the circuses leave battered flesh, contemplating sublime visions.
Muhammad begins his religious task by hearing an invisible messenger.
Francis of Assisi perceives emissaries of Heaven who exhort him to the renewal of the Church.
Luther registers the presence of beings from another world.
Teresa of Ávila receives the visit of disembodied friends and even inspects purgatorial regions through the mediumistic phenomenon of projection.

Signs of the kingdom of Spirits shall follow those who believe, affirms Christ. In all institutions of faith, there are those who enjoy, who take advantage, who calculate, who criticize, who inspect… These are still candidates for definitive and renewing illumination. Those who believe, however, and accept the determinations of service that flow from on High, will be followed by the revealing notes of immortality wherever they may be. In the name of the Lord, emitting sanctifying vibrations, they will cast out darkness and wickedness, and will be easily known among startled men, because they will always speak in the new language of sacrifice and peace, renunciation and love.

messages.title: Treatment of Obsessions
paragraphs: “There came also a multitude out of the cities round about unto Jerusalem, bringing sick folks, and them which were vexed with unclean spirits: and they were healed every one.” — (ACTS, 5:16)
The Christian church of the first centuries did not stagnate the redemptive ideas of Christ in silverware and splendors of external worship. It was alive, full of appeals and answers.
Like it, evangelical Spiritism today opens its benevolent doors to those who suffer and seek a saving path.

It is curious to note that the enormous work of Spiritists nowadays in aiding complex and painful obsessions was familiar to the apostles. They doctored perturbed spirits, renewing by example and teaching not only the suffering disembodied, but also the sick mediums who suffered their influences.

From the earliest hours of doctrinal work, the soul of Christianity has known that invisible, less balanced beings wander about the world, producing psychic sores in those who receive their action, and it is not unaware of the demands of the conversion and elevation work it must perform; religious dogma, however, prevented its efficient service for many centuries.
In full contemporaneity, however, the primitive scenes of the Good News resurface.
Ignorant and unfortunate spiritual entities acquire new light and a new roadmap in the houses of love that Christian Spiritism establishes, overcoming prejudices and major mishaps.

The treatment of obsessions, therefore, is not eccentric work in our circles of renewed faith. It constitutes simply the continuation of the effort of salvation for the wayward of all shades, begun in the luminous hands of Jesus.

messages.title: In the Revelation of Life
paragraphs: “And with great power gave the apostles witness of the resurrection of the Lord Jesus: and great grace was upon them all.” — (ACTS, 4:33)

The direct companions of the Divine Master did not establish the services of the Christian community on crystallized, immovable principles. They cultivated order, hierarchy, and discipline, but they also supported the people's spirit, distributing the goods of spiritual revelation according to the receptive capacity of each candidate for the new faith.
To deny, presently, the legitimacy of the Spiritist effort in the name of Christian faith is a testimony of ignorance or levity.

The disciples of the Lord knew the importance of certainty in survival for triumph in moral life. They themselves saw themselves radically transformed after the resurrection of the Heavenly Friend, upon recognizing that love and justice govern being beyond the tomb. For this very reason, they attracted new companions, transmitting to them the conviction that the Master continued alive and active beyond the sepulchre.

Because of this, the apostolic ministry was not divided solely into discussing the intellectual problems of belief and adorative praises. Christ's continuers provided, “with great power, witness of the resurrection of the Lord Jesus” and, given the love with which they devoted themselves to the salvationist work, “great grace was upon them all.”
Evangelical Spiritism comes to set in motion the divine service that encompasses in itself not only comforting belief, but also the indisputable knowledge of immortality.

Dogmatic schools will continue lining up articles of inoperative faith, freezing ideas in affirmative absurdities, but Christian Spiritism comes to restore, in its redemptive activities, the teaching of individual resurrection consecrated by the Divine Master, who Himself returned from the shadows of death to exalt the continuity of life.

messages.title: Let Us Keep Mental Health
paragraphs: “Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth.” — PAUL (Colossians, 3:2)
Primitive Christianity was not unaware of the need for a sound and illuminated mind of superior aspirations in the life of those who embrace substantial renewal in the Gospel.
The work of notable thinkers today finds roots further back.
Those who deal with mediumistic phenomena now know that the death of the flesh does not impose celestial delights.
Man finds himself beyond the tomb with the virtues and defects, ideals and vices to which he consecrated himself in the body.
The criminal attaches himself to the circle of his own crimes, when he does not chain himself to partners in the committed fault.
The miser is bound to superfluous goods that he abusively hoarded.
The vain person remains linked to transitory titles.
The alcoholic roams around possibilities of satisfying the thirst that dominates his centers of force.
Whoever falls in love with the capricious organizations of the “self” spends long days undoing the webs of illusion in which his personality is segregated.
The program precedes the service. The project outlines the achievement.
Thought is radiating energy. Let us spread it on Earth and we will naturally bind ourselves to the ground. Let us elevate it on High and we will conquer sublime spirituality.
Our Spirit will reside where we project our thoughts, living foundations of good and evil. For this very reason, Paul wisely said: — “Set your mind on things above.”

messages.title: Inner Combat
paragraphs: “Having the same conflict which ye saw in me, and now hear to be in me.” — PAUL (Philippians, 1:30)

In the prime of youth, Paul fought against common circumstances in order to consolidate a position to impose himself on the race's future. He strove to surpass the intelligence of many of his contemporary youths, leaving colleagues and companions behind. He argued with doctors of the Law and defeated them. He surrendered to conquering an enviable material situation and achieved it. He fought to stand out in the highest court of Jerusalem and overcame old leaders of the chosen people. He decided to persecute those he interpreted as enemies of the established order and multiplied adversaries everywhere. He wounded, tormented, complicated situations of respectable people, sentenced innocent persons to unspeakable worries, waged war on sinners and saints, the just and the unjust…
Yet, a moment arose when the Lord summoned his spirit to another kind of battle — combat with oneself.
When this hour arrived, Paul of Tarsus fell silent and listened…
His sword broke in his hands forever.
He had no arms to attack, but rather to help and serve.
He walked, modified, in the opposite direction. Instead of humiliating others, he bowed his own neck.
He suffered and perfected himself in silence, with the same willingness to work that characterized him in the times of blindness.
He was stoned, whipped, imprisoned, often misunderstood, but always proceeded toward Divine Renewal.

If you do not yet combat within yourself, a day will come when you will be called to a similar service. Pray and watch, prepare yourself, and attune your heart to humility and patience. Remember, my brother, that not even Paul, graced by the personal visit of Jesus, managed to escape.

messages.title: Let us understand by serving
paragraphs: “For we ourselves were also sometimes foolish.” — PAUL (Titus, 3:3)
The hammer truly collaborates in the splendors of statuary, but it cannot strike the stone indiscriminately.
Bitter medicine brings about the cure of the sick body, yet it demands skill in dosage.
Neither more nor less. In the sowing of truth, likewise, it is essential that we do not dissolve into thoughtless movement.
On Earth, we do not breathe in a home of angels.
We are millions of creatures, in the labyrinth of clamorous debts of the past, sighing for the desired equation.
Whoever teaches with sincerity has naturally learned the lessons, crossing hard obstacles.
Of course, excessive tolerance results in the absence of fair defense, however, it is undeniable that to educate others, we need an immense store of patience and understanding.
Paul, incisive and energetic, was not unaware of such a reality.
Writing to Titus, he recalls his own misunderstandings of another era to justify the serenity that should characterize our action in the service of the Redeeming Gospel.
We will never achieve our goals by torturing sores, pointing out scars, commenting on defects, or throwing thorns in the face of others.
Comprehension and respect must precede our task anywhere.
Let us remember ourselves, in our passage through the lowest circles, and extend fraternal arms to the brothers who struggle in the shadows.

If you find yourself interested in Christ's service, remember that He did not function as an accusing prosecutor, but rather on the tribune of sacrifice up to the cross, in the condition of lawyer for the whole world.

messages.title: Trials by fire
paragraphs: “And the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 3:13)

The mechanized industry of modern times refers a lot to trials by fire to prove the resistance of its works and, pondering this fact, let us remember that the Gospel, likewise, has referred to these trials for almost twenty centuries, with respect to spiritual acquisitions.

Writing to the Corinthians, Paul imagines human workers building upon the only foundation, which is Jesus Christ, each one organizing their own achievements in accordance with their evolutionary resources.
Each disciple, however, must build his own peculiar work, convinced that times of struggle will discover him to the eyes of all, so that a right judgment may be made regarding his quality.

The improvement of the world, in its material aspect, can provide an image of the importance of these major assessments. The Earth remains full of fortunes, positions, values, and intelligences that cannot withstand the trials by fire; as soon as purifying movements approach, they descend precipitously down the steps of misery, ruin, and decay. In the service of Christ, it is also fair that the learner awaits the moment of verification of their own possibilities. Character, love, faith, patience, hope represent conquests for eternal life, performed by the creature with the holy help of the Master, but all disciples must count on the necessary experiences that, at the opportune moment, will prove their spiritual qualities.

messages.title: Believe and follow
paragraphs: “As thou hast sent me into the world, even so have I also sent them into the world.” — JESUS (John, 17:18)

If you have embraced, my friend, the Spiritist-Christian task, in the name of sublimated faith, thirsty for superior life, remember that the Master sent your renewed heart to the vast field of the world to serve Him.
You will not only teach the good way. You will act according to the elevated principles you proclaim.
You will dictate noble guidelines for others, yet you will march within them in your turn.
You will proclaim the need for good cheer, but following the road ahead, sowing joys and blessings, even when misunderstood by all.
You will not be content with distributing coins and immediate benefits. You will always give something of yourself to those in need.
You will not only forgive. You will understand the offender, helping them to rise again.
You will not criticize. You will find unexpected resources to be useful.
You will not rail. You will make use of time to materialize the good thoughts that guide you.
You will not dispute uselessly. You will find the way of service to your fellow men anywhere.
You will not simply live in wordy combat against evil. You will retain the good, sowing it with everyone.
You will not condemn. You will discover the light of love to make it shine in your heart, even unto sacrifice.
Pray and watch.
Love and hope.
Serve and renounce.
If you are not willing to take advantage of the Divine Master's lesson, shaping your own life to His teachings, your faith will have been in vain.

messages.title: False allegations
paragraphs: “What have I to do with thee, Jesus, thou Son of God most high? I beseech thee, torment me not.” — (LUKE, 8:28)
The case of the troubled Spirit who felt the approach of Jesus, receiving His presence with furious questions, presents many aspects worthy of study.
The circumstance of begging the Divine Master not to torment him requires much attention on the part of sincere disciples.

Who could suppose Christ capable of inflicting torments on anyone? And, in this case, it is an ignorant and perverse entity who, in his intimate derangements, was already suffering much by himself. The Master's proximity, however, brought him enough clarity to contemplate the martyrdom of his own conscience, bogged down in a swamp of crimes and dark defections. The light punished his inner darkness and revealed his painful and pitiable nakedness.

The picture is very significant for those who flee from the religious truths of life, categorizing its content as a bitter elixir of anguish and suffering. These indifferent and mocking spirits usually affirm that the services of faith flood the path with tears, clouding the heart.
Such statements, however, denounce them. In greater or lesser scale, they are companions of the unhappy brother who accused Jesus of being a minister of torments.

messages.title: The march
paragraphs: “Nevertheless I must walk today, and tomorrow, and the day following.” — JESUS (Luke, 13:33)

It is important to always move forward, in search of definitive spiritual edification. It is essential to walk, overcoming obstacles and shadows, transforming all pains and difficulties into steps of ascension.

Tracing His program, Jesus referred to the march toward Jerusalem, where the final glorification through martyrdom awaited Him. We can apply the teaching, however, to our incessant experiences on the itinerary of the Jerusalem of our redeeming testimonies.
It is imperative, however, to clarify the characteristic of this journey for the acquisition of eternal goods.
Many believe that walking is invading situations of prominence in the world, conquering positions of transitory distinction or bringing the vastest financial expressions to one's personal circle.
However, it is not that. In this particular, the so-called "men of routine" perhaps hold greater probabilities in their favor.
The dominant personality, in ephemeral situations, has its march fraught with dangers, complex responsibilities, and atrocious threats. The sensation of height increases the sensation of falling.
It is necessary to walk always, but the journey belongs to the eternal Spirit, in the field of inner conquests.
Often, certain creatures who presume themselves to be at the highest points of the journey, to Divine Wisdom find themselves merely paralyzed in the contemplation of will-o'-the-wisps.
Let no one be deceived at the stations of false repose.

It is important to work, to know oneself, to illuminate oneself, and to attend to Christ daily. To fix such a lesson within us, we have been born on Earth, sharing its struggles, spending its bodies, and in it we shall be born again.

messages.title: Deep sea
paragraphs: “Now when he had left speaking, he said unto Simon, Launch out into the deep, and let down your nets for a draught.” — (LUKE, 5:4)
This verse leads us to meditate on the companions of struggle who feel abandoned in human experience.
A disturbing sensation of solitude cuts through their hearts.
They cry from longing, from pain, renewing their own bitternesses.
They believe destiny has reserved for them the cup of infinite bitterness.
They remember, with remorse, the days of childhood, of youth, of hopes withered in the conflicts of the world.
Inwardly, they experience, at every moment, the vague stampede of reminiscences that dilates their impressions of emptiness.
However, these bitter hours belong to all mortal creatures.

If someone has not lived them in a certain region of the path, let them wait for their opportunity, since, generally, almost every Spirit departs from the flesh when the cold signs of winter multiply around.

When your time of difficulty arises, therefore, convince yourself that the days of service in the "deep sea" have arrived for your soul, the time to seek true values without the incentive of certain illusions of material experience. If you find yourself alone, if you feel abandoned, remember that beyond the tomb, there are companions who assist you and wait for you affectionately.

The Father never leaves His children forsaken, so if you presently see yourself without domestic ties, without certain friends on the transitory landscape of the Planet, it is because Jesus has sent you to the open sea of experience, in order to prove your conquests in supreme lessons.

messages.title: Inconstant
paragraphs: “For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.” — (JAMES, 1:6)

Unquestionably there is a scientific and philosophical doubt in the world which, lodged in loyal hearts, constitutes a precious stimulus to the possession of great and elevated convictions; however, James refers here to the inconstancy of man who, seeking to receive divine benefits in the sphere of particularistic advantages, usually pursues varied situations in the field of intellectual research without any purpose of trusting in the substantial values of life.
Whoever worries about crossing several doors in simultaneous movement ends up crossing no door at all.
Fickleness harms creatures in all paths, especially in work positions, bodily illnesses, and affectionate relationships.
For someone to judge correctly regarding a certain experience, they need to enumerate how many years they spent within it, living its characteristics.
We need, above all, to sincerely trust in the Wisdom and Goodness of the Most High, understanding that it is indispensable to persevere with someone or with some cause that helps and edifies us.
The inconstant remain figured in the wave of the sea, absorbed by the wind and thrown from one side to another.

When you serve or when you await the blessings of the High, do not let yourself be led by sickly restlessness. The Father has innumerable instruments to administer good and is always the same Paternal Lord through all of them. The gift will arrive, but it depends on you, on your way of proceeding in the constructive struggle, persisting or not in trust, without which Divine Power finds natural obstacles to express itself in your path.

messages.title: Not of all
paragraphs: “And that we may be delivered from unreasonable and wicked men: for all men have not faith.” — PAUL (2 Thessalonians, 3:2)

Addressing the brethren of Thessalonica, the apostle of the gentiles begged for their assistance in favor of the evangelical labors, so that the Lord's service might be free from wicked and unreasonable men, justifying his appeal with the declaration that faith is not for all.

Through Paul's words, one perceives his certainty that perverse creatures would approach the nuclei of Christianizing work, that their malice could cause them harm, and that it was necessary to mobilize spiritual resources against such influence.

The great convert, in a few words, recorded a warning of infinite value, because, indeed, the religious label will characterize the outer garment of entire communities, but faith will be the patrimony only of those who work without measuring sacrifices to install it in the sanctuary of their own inner world. The label of Christianity will be displayed by anyone, however, Christian faith will reveal itself pure, unconditional, and sublime in rare hearts. Many people wish to master it as if it were a mere bill of exchange, while countless learners of the Gospel invoke it precipitously, like a wandering butterfly. They forget, however, that if the material needs of the body demand daily personal effort, the essential needs of the spirit will never be solved by inoperative expectation.

Admitting the truth, seeking it, and believing in it are attitudes for all; nevertheless, retaining living faith constitutes the divine achievement of those who worked, strived, and suffered to acquire it.

messages.title: Prodigal sons
paragraphs: “And when he came to himself, he said, How many hired servants of my father's have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger!” — Jesus (LUKE, 15:17)
Examining the figure of the prodigal son, everyone idealizes a rich man dissipating material possibilities in the feasts of the world.
The picture, however, must be broadened, encompassing different modalities.
Prodigal sons do not breathe only where money is abundant. They accommodate themselves in all fields of human activity, slipping from various positions.

Great scientists of the Earth are spendthrifts of intelligence, distilling intellectual poisons unworthy of the concessions granted to them. Precious artists sometimes uselessly spend imagination and sensitivity through petty adventures, falling eventually into the recesses of relaxation and crime.

Everywhere, we see the dissipators of goods, knowledge, time, health, and opportunities. They are the ones who, contemplating simple and humble hearts marching toward God, possessed of true confidence, experience the enormous anguish of uselessness and, distant from inner peace, exclaim disheartened:
— “How many tiny workers keep the bread of tranquility, while the hunger for peace tortures my spirit!”
The world remains full of prodigal sons and, hour by hour, thousands of voices utter afflictive exclamations equal to this one.

messages.title: On the roads
paragraphs: “And these are they by the wayside, where the word is sown; but when they have heard, Satan cometh immediately, and taketh away the word that was sown in their hearts.” — JESUS (Mark, 4:15)
Jesus is our permanent way to Divine Love.
Beside Him follow, hopefully, all Spirits of good will, sincere adherents to the sanctifying itinerary.
From this blessed and eternal path proceed the seeds of Celestial Light for ordinary men. Much observation by creatures is imperative so that the treasure does not pass them by unnoticed.
The sanctifying seed will always come amidst the most varied circumstances.
As occurs with the generous wind that spontaneously spreads the principles of life among plants, invisible goodness distributes the opportunity of access to the path of love to all hearts.
Almost always the divine spark appears in the ordinary events of each day, in a book, in an insignificant detail of work, in the helpful observation of a friend.

If the terrain of your heart lives occupied by weeds and if you have already received the celestial principle, cultivate it with devotion, sheltering it in the furrows of your soul. Human speech may fail, but the Word of the Lord is imperishable. Accept it and fulfill it, because if you shirk the imperative of eternal life, sooner or later the angel of anguish will visit your spirit, pointing out new directions to you.

messages.title: Immediate Works
paragraphs: “Shepherd God’s flock that is among you, exercising oversight, not out of compulsion, but voluntarily, according to God; not for shameful gain, but eagerly.” — (1 Peter, 5:2)

Naturally, in the pauta of just possibilities, no one should deny support or assistance to companions who signal from afar with reasonable requests; however, it is our obligation to heed Peter's teaching regarding our immediate works.

There are creatures who gladly surrender to the voluptuousness of anxiety over catastrophic events, planned by the diseased minds of others and which will probably never come to pass. They waste long periods prescribing courses of action or uttering useless laments.
Other people's farming and future occurrences, to be examined, always demand great qualities of consideration.

Furthermore, it is essential to recognize that the difficult problem, beside us or at a distance from us, has the purpose of enriching our own experience, enabling us to solve the most intricate enigmas of the path.
This is why Simon Peter's note is profound and timely, for all times and situations.

Let us attend to the imperatives of the divine service located in our individual landscape, not through constraint, but through spontaneous good will, fleeing more and more from our particularistic interests and with a firm and ready mind to serve the good as much as possible.

Sometimes, it is reasonable for a person to worry about the world situation, the regeneration of communities, the positions and responsibilities of others, but it is not fair for us to forget that “flock of God which is among us”.

messages.title: Crushing of Evil
paragraphs: “And the God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet.” — PAUL (Romans, 16:20)
In every part of the Planet, one can recognize the relentless struggle between good and evil.

The great conflict manifests itself in the most diverse forms, and, in the whirlwind of its movements, many sensitive souls invariably maintain the attitude of invoking tutelary geniuses so that they may come to the arena to combat the enemies that stun them, prostrating them once and for all.

Asking for help or resorting to the law of cooperation represent praiseworthy acts of the Spirit that identifies its own weakness; however, insisting that someone else replace us in the effort that only we are meant to expend demonstrates a false position, capable of accentuating our needs.

Satan, representing the power of evil in human life, will be crushed by God; however, Paul of Tarsus defines with great clarity the place of divine victory. The supreme triumph will take place under the feet of man.

When the creature, through their own dedication to illuminating work, surrenders to the Father without reservations, carrying out His holy will, forgetting the old animal selfishness, and grasping the greatness of their position as an eternal spirit, they will achieve sublime victory.

The All-Paternal Lord has already given Himself to His earthly children, but rare children have given themselves to Him. It is therefore essential not to forget that evil will not be eliminated at random, but rather beneath the feet of each one of us.

messages.title: And the Ends?
paragraphs: “But not all things build up.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 10:23)
There have always been indefinable men who, if they did no harm to anyone, likewise benefited no one.
Examined through this same prism, the things of the path need sensible interpretation so that they are not lost in uselessness.

It is lawful for man to dedicate himself to literature or honest worldly business, and no one can contest the praiseworthy character of those who consciously choose their individual line of action in useful service. However, it is fair to know the ends of the writer or the purposes of the merchant. What will it profit the former to produce long works, full of verbal embellishments and theoretical raptures, if his words remain devoid of constructive thought for the eternal plane of the soul? What will it profit the merchant to have immense fortune, won through industriousness and calculation, when it lives stagnant in safes, awaiting the follies of descendants? In both situations, one could not say that such men contemplated illicit achievements; nevertheless, they wasted precious time, forgetting that the smallest things carry an edifying purpose.
The worker conscious of their responsibilities does not stray from the straight paths.

There is much affliction and bitterness in the workshops of earthly improvement because their servants care, above all, about material gains, forgetting the ends for which they are destined. While this happens, projects and experiments intensify, but just and necessary edification is always lacking.

messages.title: The Vineyard
paragraphs: “And he said to them, ‘You go into the vineyard too, and whatever is right I will give you.’ So they went.” — (MATTHEW, 20:4)
No one can think of an Earth full of beauty and possibilities, yet drifting aimlessly in universal immensity.
The Planet is not an ungoverned boat.

Human communities tend to fall into disorder, but the laws that preside over the destinies of the Earthly Home express themselves with absolute harmony. This realization helps us understand that the Earth is Jesus's vineyard. There, we see Him working since the dawn of the centuries, and there we witness the transformation of creatures who, from experience to experience, integrate into His divine love.

The beautiful parable of the servants involves deep concepts. In essence, it designates the place of human services and refers to the volume of obligations that the apprentices received from the Divine Master.

For now, men harbor the illusion that the globe can be a stage for racial or political hegemonies, but they will realize their resounding mistake in time, because all children of reason, embodied on the Earth's Crust, carry with them the task of contributing to a higher standard of living in the corner where they transiently act.
Wherever you are, remember that you are in the Vineyard of Christ.
Do you live besieged by difficulty and misfortune?
Work for the general good, even so, because the Lord has granted each coworker the appropriate and just material.

messages.title: Conventions
paragraphs: “And he said to them, ‘The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.’” — (MARK, 2:27)

The Sabbath, in this evangelical passage, symbolizes the conventions organized for human service. There are creatures who sacrifice all possibilities of spiritual elevation for them. Like certain public service officials who indefinitely postpone certain measures of collective interest due to the absence of a tiny stamp, there are people who, for trifles, abandon great opportunities for union with the higher Sphere.

No one is unaware of the useful side of conventions. If they were totally useless, the Father would not allow their existence in the play of circumstances. They are tables for classifying everyone's efforts, boards that designate the appropriate time for this or that task; however, turning them into an impregnable precept or an insurmountable obstacle constitutes grave harm to common tranquility.
Most people attend to them before their own obedience to God; however, the Almighty arranged all the organizations of life to help the evolution and improvement of His children.

The Planet itself was built for the sake of man. If the Creator went to such an extreme of solicitude in favor of creatures, why should we fail to satisfy His divine designs by clinging to the lower concerns of earthly activity?

Conventions define, catalog, specify, and enumerate, but they must not tyrannize existence. Remember that they were arranged along the path to serve you. Respect them in a fair and constructive fashion; however, do not turn them into a prison.

messages.title: With Charity
paragraphs: “Let all that you do be done in love.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 16:14)

There are still many people who do not understand any charity other than the one that dresses in humble attire on Saturdays or Sundays to share some bread with the underprivileged of fortune, that waits for public calamities to manifest itself, or that launches touching appeals on press posters.
We cannot dispute the praiseworthy intentions of this or that group of people; however, we must recognize that the sublime gift is of sublime extension.
Paul indicates that charity, expressing Christian love, must encompass all manifestations of our life.

Extending a hand and distributing comfort is beginning the execution of the excelsior virtue. All the powers of the spirit, however, must adjust to the divine precept, because there is charity in speaking and listening, preventing and favoring, forgetting and remembering. The time will come when the mouth, ears, and feet will be allies of fraternal hands in the services of supreme good.

Each person, like each thing, needs the contribution of goodness in a particular way. Men who lead or who obey demand its holy assistance so that they may be enlightened in the department of the House of God where they find themselves. Without sublimated love, there will always be obscurity, generating complications.

Perform your smallest tasks with charity from now on. If you do not find spiritual retribution in the domain of understanding in an immediate sense, know that the Father accompanies all His children devotedly.
Are there stones and briers? Fix your gaze on Jesus and pass through.

messages.title: Corpses
paragraphs: “Wherever the corpse is, there the vultures will gather.” — (MATTHEW, 24:28)
Presenting the image of the corpse and the vultures, the Master referred to the need of penitent men who require resources to combat the extinction of the shadows in which they plunge.
A swamp is not eliminated by throwing flowers at it.
Bodies rotting in the field attract ravens that devour them.
This figure, of high symbolic significance, is one of the Lord's strongest appeals, calling upon the servants of the Gospel to engage in the movements of sanctifying work.

In various circles of newborn Christianity, there are those who complain, disheartened, of the action of visible and invisible persecutors, obsessors, and vile executioners. Some apprentices declare themselves tied to their influence and confess themselves incapable of attending to Jesus's designs.
It would be wise, however, to ponder deeply before making statements of this sort, which merely accuse their own authors.
It is essential to always remember that pitiless birds will gather around abandoned corpses.
Ravens nest in other regions when the field where they remained is cleaned.
A man who claims to be invariably unhappy gives the impression of breathing inside a sepulcher; however, when he seeks to renew his own path, the dark birds of negative sadness move further away.

Fight against corpses of any nature that shelter within your inner world. Let the divine sun of spirituality penetrate you, for as long as you are a coffin of dead things, you will be closely followed by the vultures of destruction.

messages.title: Let Us Also Work
paragraphs: “And saying, ‘Men, why are you doing these things? We also are men of the same nature as you.’” — (ACTS, 14:15)
The cry of Paul and Barnabas still resonates among faithful learners.
The Christian family has often desired to perpetuate the illusion of the inhabitants of Lystra.

The missionaries of Revelation have no privileges before the spirit of personal witness in service. The achievements that we might point to as grace or special prerogative express nothing more than their own profound effort to learn and apply with Jesus.

Christ did not found with His doctrine a system of gods and devotees separated from each other; He created a vigorous organism of spiritual transformation for the supreme good, destined for all hearts thirsty for light, love, and truth.

In the Gospel, we see Magdalene dragging painful mistakes, Paul pursuing saving ideals, Peter denying the Divine Friend, Mark struggling with his own hesitations; yet, even there, we contemplate the daughter of Magdala, renewed on the redemptive path, the great persecutor converted into a herald of the Good News, the fragile disciple led to spiritual glory, and the wavering companion transformed into an evangelist of all Humanity.
Christianity is a blessed source of the soul's restoration to God.

The trouble with many learners stems from the idolatry they indulge in around the valiant exponents of living faith, whom they accept in sacrifice as the true formula of elevation; they imagine them on fantasy thrones and grovel at their feet, feeling confused, unfit, and miserable, forgetting that the Father grants all children the energies necessary for victory.

Naturally, we all owe love and respect to the great figures of the Christian path; however, for this very reason, we cannot forget that Paul and Peter, like so many others, emerged from human weaknesses into heavenly gifts, and that the Terrestrial Planet is a school of illumination, power, and triumph, whenever we seek to understand its grand mission.

messages.title: Deserted Place
paragraphs: “And he said to them, ‘Come away by yourselves to a deserted place and rest a while.’” — (MARK, 6:31)
Jesus's exhortation to His companions is of singular importance for the disciples of the Gospel in all times.
It becomes indispensable to learn the path of the “private place” where the Master awaits His disciples for constructive rest in His love.
In the precious symbol, we have the intimate sanctuary of the heart thirsting for divine light.

In no way did the Lord refer solely to the solitude of places that favor meditation, where we always find living suggestions of human nature. He referred to the silent chamber located within ourselves.

Furthermore, we cannot forget that the Spirit thirsting for divine union, from the moment it immerses in the currents of higher idealism, begins to feel out of place, in deep isolation in the world, even though serving it daily according to the unfailing designs of the High.
In the secret temple of the soul, Christ waits for us to reinvigorate our exhausted forces.
Men began the search for the “deserted place” by retreating to monasteries or wild landscapes; however, the Savior's teaching is not fixed on the external world.

Prepare yourself to serve the Divine Kingdom, in the city or in the country, in any season, and do not seek rest thoughtlessly, convinced that often the immobility of the body is the torture of the soul. Above all, seek to discover within yourself the “private place” where you will rest in the company of the Master.

messages.title: The Operant Christ
paragraphs: “For he who worked effectively through Peter for his apostleship to the circumcised worked also effectively through me for the Gentiles.” — PAUL (Galatians, 2:8)
Human vanity has always maintained the pretense of keeping Christ within the circles of religious sectarianism, but Jesus continues to operate wherever the principle of good thrives.

Within all lines of terrestrial evolution, among sanctuaries and academies, move restless newcomers, false believers, and unhappy fanatics who ignite the fire of opinion and sustain it. Among them, however, arise men of living faith, who become the sacred vehicles of the operant Christ.
Simon Peter centralized all the works of the nascent Gospel, readjusting the aspirations of the chosen people.
Paul of Tarsus was a powerful magnet for the renewal of gentility.
Through both, the same Master expressed Himself with a single objective—the improvement of man for the Divine Kingdom.
It is time to recognize the light of these eternal truths.
Jesus remains at work, and His infinite goodness reveals itself in all sectors where love is raised to the rank of supreme ideal.

Let no one cling to the domain of unjust complaints, viewing sincere and devoted disciples as holders of divine privileges. Every apprentice should strive to create in their heart the atmosphere propitious to the manifestations of the Lord and His emissaries. Work, study, serve, and help always, in search of the higher Spheres, and you will feel the operant Christ by your side in your daily relationships.

messages.title: Until the End
paragraphs: “But he who endures to the end shall be saved.” — JESUS (Matthew, 24:13)
Here we do not see Jesus referring to an end that symbolizes termination, but rather to the purpose, the target, the objective.
The Gospel will be preached to the peoples so that creatures may understand and attain the higher ends of life.
This is why only those incarnate Spirits who know how to persevere manage to break the cocoon of their animality.
When the Master praised persistence, He highlighted the arduous task of those who seek the excellences of the spiritual path.
It is necessary to erase the false notions of the Divinity's gratuitous favors.
No one will escape, with impunity, the percentage of effort that is due from them in the work of their own self-improvement.

The gates of Heaven remain open. They have never been closed. However, for man to elevate himself up there, he needs wings of love and wisdom. For this, the Supreme Lord grants an extensive supply of mercy material to all creatures, conferring, nonetheless, upon each one the duty to carve them; such a task, however, demands enormous effort. To conclude it, the contribution of days and existences is recruited. Many people become discouraged and prefer to stall, for centuries on end, in the labyrinths of inferiority; however, good workers know how to persevere until they reach the divine purposes of the earthly path, continuing on a sublime trajectory toward perfection.

messages.title: It Would Be Useless
paragraphs: “He answered them: I told you already, and you did not listen; why do you want to hear it again?” — (JOHN, 9:27)

It is very common for many religious people to be preoccupied with forcibly transforming their friends, calling them to their particularist convictions. Almost always, they engage in long and tedious discussions, in continuous word games, without any wholesome or edifying achievement.
The heart sincerely renewed in faith, however, never proceeds this way.

It is essential to dilute the itch for superiority that infests the feelings of a large part of learners, as soon as they let themselves be led to new ports of knowledge in the gradual revelations of divine wisdom, because discussers with bad inclinations take it upon themselves to intercept their march.
The reply of the man born blind to the shrewd and inquiring Jews is an active standard for sincere disciples.

Naturally, the follower of Jesus will not deny an explanation about the Master, but if he has already explained the matter, if he has already tried to benefit his closest brother with the values that bring him happiness, without reaching the other's understanding, why argue? If a man has heard the truth and has not understood it, he provides evident signs of spiritual paralysis. It will be useless for him, therefore, to listen to immediate repetitions, because no one will cheat time, and the wise man who defied the ignorant would lower himself to the title of a fool.
Do not waste your hours, then, through minute and repeated elucidations for someone who cannot understand them, before the sun and rain, the fire and water of experience befall them on the path.
You have a thousand resources to work in favor of your friend, without provoking them regarding your way of being and your faith.

messages.title: Private Account
paragraphs: “If you had known, even you, especially in this your day, the things that belong to your peace!” — JESUS (Luke, 19:42)
Jesus' exclamation near Jerusalem applies much more to the heart of man — the living temple of the Lord — than to the material city, destined for ruin and disaggregation in the sectors of experience.
Let us imagine what the world would be like if each creature knew what belongs to their intimate peace.
Due to the almost general inattention to this imperative of life, men engage in painful friction, assuming rugged debts.
Let us pay attention to the Master's assertion — “even you, especially in this your day.”

These words invite us to think about the opportunity for service that we currently have and to reflect on the centuries we have lost; they compel us to ponder the opportunity for work, always open to diligent spirits.
The incarnate man has a glorious time that is provisionally his, which was provided to him by the Most High for his own renewal.

It is necessary for each one to know what touches their individual tranquility. Let every man keep a dignified attitude of understanding his own duties, and the phantoms of restlessness will be cast away. Let each person take care of what refers to their private account, and two-thirds of the world's social problems will naturally appear resolved.
Notice the tiny demands of your circle and attend to them, in favor of yourself.
You will not walk among the stars before treading the humble paths that belong to you.

messages.title: Invitation to Good
paragraphs: “But when you are invited, go.” — JESUS (Luke, 14:10)
In all eras, goodness constitutes the divine source capable of providing us with immortal values.
The thoughtful man will have observed that the entire period of childhood is a set of appeals to the sublime source.
The sacred invitation is repeated, year after year. It comes through loving human parents, school mentors, wholesome reading, religious sentiment, common friends.
However, rare intelligences reach youth with their attention fixed on the elevated call. Almost everyone hears the requests of the lower nature, forgetting precious duties.
The appeals, however, continue…
Here, it is a friendly book, revealing the truth in silence; there, it is a generous companion who insists in favor of the luminous realities of life…

Rebellion, however, even in the full maturity of man, tends to laugh unconsciously, passing nevertheless, on a compulsory march, toward the natural disillusions that impose more balanced thoughts upon it.
In the Gospel of Jesus, the invitation to good is clothed in eternal clarity. By heeding it, we will be able to go forth to meet Our Father without hesitation.
If the Christian bugle has already reached your ears, accept its blasts without faltering.
Do not wait for the goad of necessity.
Amidst the storm, the view of the port is increasingly difficult.
Most of our brothers on Earth walk toward God under the ultimatum of sorrows, but do not wait for the whip of shadows when you can follow calmly along the bright roads of love.

messages.title: In Preparation
paragraphs: “For this is the covenant that I will make... Says the Lord: I will put my laws in their mind and write them on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 8:10)
In all languages,
In all cultures,
Exalting its greatness,
Highlighting its sublimity,
Sowing its poetry,
Commenting on its truth,
Interpreting its lessons,
Imposing ourselves upon reason,
Refining the heart,
And reforming intelligence,
Renewing laws,
Perfecting customs,
And clearing paths…
But the moment will come
When the Good News
Must be imprinted within ourselves,
In the recesses of the mind,
In the nooks of the chest,
Through words and actions,
Through principles and ideals,
Through aspirations and hopes,
Through gestures and thoughts.
Because, truly,
If Heaven allows us to spread
Its Divine Message in the world,
One day it will demand that we become
Living translations of the Gospel on Earth.

messages.title: In the Future
paragraphs: “None of them shall teach his neighbor, and none his brother, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’ for all shall know Me, from the least of them to the greatest of them.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 8:11)
When man engraves the luminous paragraphs of the Divine Law upon his own soul, companion will not reprimand companion, brother will not denounce another brother.
Prisons will close their doors, courts will remain silent.
Cannons will be converted into plows, men of arms will return to the sowing of the soil.
Hatred will be expelled from the world, bayonets will rest.
Machines will not vomit flames for fire and death, but will peacefully tend to planetary progress.
Justice will be surpassed by love.
The children of faith will not only be just, but good, profoundly good.
Prayer will consist of joy and praise, and houses of prayer will be dedicated to the sublime work of supreme fraternity.

The preaching of the Law will live in the acts and thoughts of all, because the Lamb of God will have transformed the heart of every man into a tabernacle of eternal light, in which His Divine Reign will shine forever.

messages.title: Always Alive
paragraphs: “He is not the God of the dead, but the God of the living. You are therefore greatly mistaken.” — JESUS (Mark, 12:27)

Considering the conventions established in our dealings with incarnate friends, from time to time we refer to spiritual life using the word “death” in this or that sentence of usual conversation. However, it is imperative to understand it not as cessation, but as a transforming activity of life.
Spiritually speaking, we only know one fearful kind of death — that of the conscience blackened by evil, tortured by remorse, or paralyzed on the precipices that border the road of folly and crime.
The time has come for us to recognize that we are all alive in the Eternal Creation.

Due to the delay of such knowledge among men, great errors occur.
