Because of this, the Roman Catholic Church created, in its theology, an artificial heaven and hell; various communities of Protestant evangelical organizations cling to the letter, believing that the body, the material garment of the Spirit, will one day rise from the tombs, violating the principles of Nature; and countless spiritualists view us as laboratory phantoms or fluttering, vague, and airy forms, wandering indefinitely.
Whoever passes through the tomb continues working, and here, just as there, disorder exists only for the disorderly. On the Earth's Crust or beyond its circles, we invariably remain alive.

Do not forget, therefore, that disembodied beings are neither magicians nor fortune-tellers. They are brothers who continue in the struggle for self-improvement. We encounter death solely on the paths of evil, where shadows impede the glorious vision of life.
Let us keep the lesson of the Gospel and never forget that Our Father is the God of the immortal living.

messages.title: Good Manners
paragraphs: “And take your seat at the lowest place.” — JESUS (Luke, 14:10)
The Master, in this passage, provides an unforgettable teaching on good manners.

Certainly, the sentence reveals highly symbolic content regarding the paternal banquet of Divine Goodness; however, it is fitting to shift the concept in order to apply it equally to the mechanism of ordinary life.

The Savior's recommendation lends itself to all situations in which we find ourselves called upon to examine something new alongside our fellow men. Anyone who enters a house or participates in a meeting for the first time, making a point of showing that they know everything or that they are superior to the environment they are in, becomes intolerable to those around them.

Even if it is a group misled in its purposes or intentions, it is not reasonable that the enlightened man, entering it for the first time, should become an austere and demanding indoctrinator, since for the task of rectifying or leading souls back, it is essential that the worker faithful to goodness initiate the effort by meeting hearts through the bonds of legitimate fraternity. Only thus will he manage to effectively shed imperfection, eliminating a fraction of shadow each day through constant service.
We know that Jesus was the great reformer of the world; however, correcting and loving, He asserted that He had come to the path of men to fulfill the Law.

Do not assault the places of prominence wherever you pass. And when you stop with our brothers anywhere, do not dazzle them with the display of how much you have already conquered in the domains of love and wisdom. If you find yourself determined to cooperate for the good of others, humble yourself in some way so that your neighbor can understand you. By imposing norms or exhibiting power, you will achieve nothing stronger than establishing greater disturbances.

messages.title: Cures
paragraphs: “And heal the sick there, and say to them, ‘The kingdom of God has come near to you.’” — JESUS (Luke, 10:8)

Indeed, Jesus healed many the sick and recommended them, in a special way, to His disciples. However, the Heavenly Physician did not forget to claim for the Divine Kingdom all those who are restored from human deficiencies.
We are not only interested in the regeneration of the vehicle through which we express ourselves, but above all, in the spiritual corrective.

May the ordinary man be freed from illness, but it is imperative that he understand the value of health. There is, however, as much difficulty in understanding the hidden lesson of bodily illness as there is in assimilating the appeal to sanctifying work addressed to us by organic balance.
Would the Lord permit the constitution of cellular harmony only for a vicious will to strike and break it to the detriment of the spirit?
The sick person may yearn for the readjustment of vital energies, however, it behooves him to know the prudence and value of the elements placed at his disposal in the edifying experience of Earth.

There are sick creatures who lament being confined to bed and weep in affliction, not because they wish to renew their conceptions regarding the sacred foundations of life, but because they feel unable to prolong their own follies.

It is always useful to heal the sick when there is permission of a higher order for this, yet, in the face of such a concession from the Most High, it is reasonable that the person interested in the blessing reconsider the issues concerning them, understanding that a new day has dawned for their spirit on the redemptive path.

messages.title: When You Pray
paragraphs: “And whenever you stand praying, forgive.” — JESUS (Mark, 11:25)

The sincere attitude of the soul in prayer does not obey ordinary mechanical movements. In the operations of ordinary struggle, the creature invariably attends to the automatisms of material experience, which changes in an imperceptible way within the circles of time; however, when the soul turns to the divine sanctuaries of the higher Plane through prayer, the conscience places itself in contact with the eternal and creative sense of infinite life.

Let each learner examine the sensations they experience when placing themselves in the position of petitioning the Heights, understanding that it is indispensable for them to maintain internal peace before the creatures and circumstantial pictures of the path.
The mind that prays remains in motion within the invisible Sphere.

Incarnate intelligences, even when they do not know one another according to the standards of material conventions, communicate through the tenuous threads of desire manifested in prayer. In such moments, which we should consecrate exclusively to the highest zone of our individuality, we dispatch messages, appeals, intentions, projects, and anxieties that seek an appropriate objective.

Worthy of pity is everyone who uses the opportunity to widen the current of evil, consciously or unconsciously. It is for this reason that Jesus, understanding the scarcity of men and women free from guilt, launched this expressive program of love for the benefit of each disciple of the Gospel: — “And whenever you stand praying, forgive.”

messages.title: We, However
paragraphs: “We then that are strong ought to bear the infirmities of the weak, and not to please ourselves.” — PAUL (Romans, 15:1)
With what objective does man acquire the just notion of trust in God? To evade the struggle and live awaiting Heaven? Such an attitude would not be comprehensible.
The disciple attains the light of knowledge in order to apply it to his own path. Jesus granted him a trace of Heaven so that he might develop and extend it across the earth upon which he treads.
To receive the Master's sacred help and withdraw from His workshop of redemption is to bear witness to extreme ignorance.
To give oneself to Christ is to work for the establishment of His kingdom.

Terrestrial temples, through a lack of understanding of the truth, remain filled with paralyzed souls who have deserted service out of a yearning for bliss. This can be understood in creatures who have not yet acquired the necessary sense of reality, but you, who are already strong in knowledge, must not rest in indifference before the sacred imperatives of the light kindled, through the infinite goodness of Christ, within your inner world. It is imperative that each one take up their working instruments, in the task that falls to them, acting for the victory of good within the circle of people and activities surrounding them.
Many sick spirits, amidst false worries and the idleness of the world, may plead ignorance. You, however, are neither weak nor poor in the Lord's mercy.

messages.title: The Problem of Pleasing
paragraphs: “For if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ.” — PAUL (Galatians, 1:10)

The sincere disciples of the Gospel must be very concerned with their own duties and with the isolated and tranquil approval of conscience in the labors they are called to execute each day, learning to dispense with the unreasonable opinions of the world.

The multitude will know how to bestow affection and admiration only upon those who satisfy its demands and whims; in the conflicts that mark its march, the faithful apprentice of Jesus will be a different worker whom, in its instinctive impulses, it will not be able to understand.

The messenger of the Good News who shows restlessness regarding the world's opinions of him will reveal much inexperience and lack of vigilance; when he finds himself in material prosperity, in which the Master confers upon him a more rigorous stewardship, many neighbors will ask him, maliciously, the cause of the successive successes that surround him, and when he enters the field of poverty and difficulty, people will attribute his difficult experiences to supposed defections from the sublime ideas he espouses.

It is indispensable to work for men as one who knows that the integral work belongs to Jesus Christ. The world will understand the effort of the sincere servant, but on another occasion, when evolutionary ascension permits him to do so.

On many occasions, popular opinions are equivalent to the shouting of children's assemblies, which do not tolerate the most highly inspired educators along the lines of order and elevation, work and achievement.
May the sincere worker of Christ, therefore, know how to operate without concern for the erroneous judgments of creatures. Jesus knows him and this is enough.

messages.title: Let Us Understand
paragraphs: “Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offerings for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 10:8)
The ancient world did not understand its relations with the Most High except through sumptuous offerings and heavy burnt offerings.
Certain primitive peoples reached exquisite religious extravagance, bringing human blood to the altars.
Such unfortunate manifestations are attenuating in the crucible of the centuries; nonetheless, even today lamentable urges of eccentricity are verified in vows of this nature.

Christianity operated a complete renewal in the understanding of divine truths; nevertheless, even within its ranks, absurd promises still tend to arise that merely favor the intrusion of ignorance and vice.

The highest conception of God that we can harbor in the sanctuary of the spirit is the one that Jesus presented to us, revealing Him to us as a loving and just Father, awaiting our testimonies of understanding and love.

Upon the very Crust of the Earth, any conscientious and upright head of a family does not desire his children in a constant motion of useless offerings with the purpose of cooling his affectionate vigilance. If such initiatives do not please human progenitors, who are capricious and fallible, how can we attribute such a flaw to the All-Merciful under the presumption of conquering celestial meritoriousness?
It is indispensable to work against this criminal deception.

Real happiness is only possible in the Christian home of the world when its members fulfill the obligations that fall to them, even at the price of heroic decisions. With our Heavenly Father, the program is no different, because the Supreme Lord does not ask us for sacrifices and tears, but rather serene courage to accept His sublime will and put it into practice.

messages.title: Old Argument
paragraphs: “And as he thus spake for himself, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad.” — (ACTS, 26:24)
It is very common for the scientificist circles of the century to hurl the false accusation of madness upon the disciples of the Gospel.
The argument is very old on the part of all those who intend to flee from the truth, complaisant with their own errors.
There are workers who lose valuable time lamenting that the multitude classifies them as unbalanced. This does not constitute a reason for sterile contentions.
Many times, the Master Himself was interpreted as demented, and the apostles received no other definition.

In one of his last defenses, we see the valiant friend of the Gentiles before the Provincial Court of Caesarea, proclaiming the immortal truths of Christ Jesus. The assembly is touched with immense astonishment. That frank and noble word stuns the listeners. It is then that Porcius Festus, in his capacity as head of the guests, decides to break the vibration of astonishment that dominates the environment. Before doing so, however, the shrewd Roman considered that it would be necessary to justify himself on solid grounds. How could he accuse the great convert of Damascus, however, if he, Festus, knew his upright character, sincere humility, sublime patience, and ardent spirit of sacrifice? He then remembers the "much learning," and Paul is called mad because of the divine science to which he bore witness.

Remember, then, the self-sacrificing fighter and do not dispense appreciation to the false considerations of those who provoke you to abandon the truth. Evil is incompatible with good, and whether by "little learning" or by "much," once you enlist among the apprentices of Jesus, the inferior world will not fail you with sarcasm and persecution.

messages.title: Preserve Thyself
paragraphs: “Go, and sin no more.” — JESUS (John, 8:11)
The valuable seed that you do not help may be lost.
The tender tree that you do not protect remains exposed to destruction.
The spring that you do not shelter may dry up.
The water that you do not distribute forms swamps.
The unutilized fruit rots.
The good earth that you do not defend is suffocated by useless weeds.
The hoe that you do not use gathers rust.
The flowers that you do not cultivate do not always repeat themselves.
The friend that you do not keep flees from your path.
The medication that you do not respect in its dosage and opportune moment does not benefit your organic field.
So it is also with Divine Grace.

If you do not guard the favor of the Most High, respecting it within yourself, if you do not use the elevated knowledge you receive for the benefit of your own happiness, if you do not prize the contribution that comes to you from above, the dedication of the spiritual messengers will be of no avail to you. In vain will they improvise miracles of love and patience in solving your problems, because without the adherence of your will to the regenerative program, all saving measures will prove useless.
“Go, and sin no more.” Jesus' teaching is sufficient and expressive.
The Divine Physician provides the cure, but if we do not preserve it within ourselves, no one can foresee the extent and consequences of the new imbalances that our lack of vigilance will invite.

messages.title: Help Thyself
paragraphs: “Preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every sickness.” — (MATTHEW, 9:35)
Cure your cataract and conjunctivitis, but correct the spiritual vision of your eyes.
Defend yourself against deafness; however, rectify your way of registering the various voices and requests that seek you out.
Treat arrhythmia and dyspnea, yet do not surrender your heart to devastating impulsiveness.
Combat neurasthenia and exhaustion, but take care to readjust your emotions and tendencies.
Pursue gastralgia, but educate your appetites at the table.
Improve the condition of your blood, however, do not overload it with the residues of inferior pleasures.
Wage war on hepatitis, yet rid your liver of the excesses in which you take delight.
Remove the dangers of uremia, however, do not suffocate your kidneys with the poisons of glittering cups.
Displace rheumatism from your limbs, while repairing what you do with your feet, arms, and hands.
Sanate the cerebral errors that threaten you, yet learn to keep your mind in superior idealism and noble acts.

Dedicate yourself to your own healing, but do not forget the preaching of the Divine Kingdom "to your organs." They are living and educable. Without your thought purifying itself and without your will commanding the ship of the organism toward the good, the intervention of human remedies will be nothing more than a measure on its way to uselessness.

messages.title: Subtle Dangers
paragraphs: “Neither be ye idolaters.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 10:7)
Paul's recommendation to the Corinthians should be remembered and applied at any time in the services of religious ascension in the world.
It is indispensable to avoid idolatry in all circumstances. Its manifestations have always represented serious dangers to spiritual life.
Ancient beliefs remain full of exterior cults and dead idols.
The Comforter, sent to the world in the venerable Spiritist mission, will watch against this poisonous process of soul paralysis.

Here and there, urges of adoration arise that it is imperative to combat. No longer images from human circles, nor physical instruments supposedly sanctified for conventional ceremonies, but friendly entities and earthly mediums whom foreign unconsciousness inadvertently enthrones upon the fragile altar of fanciful honors. It is necessary to recognize that here we have a subtle danger through which countless workers have slipped into the precipice of uselessness.

Inopportune homages tend to pervert dedicated and inexperienced mediums, besides creating a certain atmosphere of incomprehension that prevents the spontaneous exteriorization of true friends of the good on the spiritual Plane.
Let no one forget the condition of relative perfection of the disincarnate messengers who communicate and the framework of immediate needs in the life of human mediums.

Let us combat the false idols that threaten Christian Spiritism. May each disciple utilize the ample resources of the law of cooperation, throw themselves into their own effort with sincere devotion to the task, and let us all remember that in the apostolate of the Divine Master, love and fidelity to God constituted the central theme.

messages.title: In Chains
paragraphs: “For which I am an ambassador in bonds: that therein I may speak boldly, as I ought to speak.” — PAUL (Ephesians, 6:20)
We observe in this passage the apostle to the Gentiles making a statement that seems contradictory at first sight.
Paul claims the condition of an emissary in chains and, simultaneously, declares that this occurs so that he may serve the Gospel as freely as it behoove him.

The great worker was addressing his companions in Ephesus, referring to his distressing situation as a prisoner of the Roman authorities; nevertheless, precisely because of this, in view of the difficult testimony, he brought a freer spirit to the service he was called upon to perform.
The picture is significant for those who desire economic-financial independence or excessive freedom in the world in order to exemplify the evangelical teachings.

There are many people who declare they are awaiting days of material abundance and earthly facilities in order to attend to Christian idealism. This, however, is a contradiction. The service of Jesus is intended for every place.

Paul, amidst chains, felt freer in preaching the truth. Naturally, not all disciples will be traversing these culminating mounts of testimony. All of them, however, without distinction, bring with them the holy shackles of daily obligations in the home, in common work, in the routine of the hours, in the center of society and family.
Let no one, therefore, try to break the chains in which they find themselves under the false supposition that they will qualify for a better post in the workshops of Christ.
Only duty well fulfilled grants us access to legitimate freedom.

messages.title: Reason for the Appeals
paragraphs: “Therefore came I unto you without gainsaying, as soon as I was sent for: I ask therefore for what intent ye have sent for me?” — PETER (Acts, 10:29)
Peter's question to the centurion Cornelius is a trait of great significance in the apostolic acts.

The Roman official was known for his traditions of a charitable and upright man; he invoked the presence of Jesus' disciple attending to elevated reasons of a moral order, following the generous advice of an emissary from Heaven, and yet, upon reaching his domestic circle, the former fisherman of Caperhasum sensibly asks:
— “For what intent ye have sent for me?”
Simon needed to know the purposes of such a demand, just as the vigilant servant needs to know where he treads and for what purpose he is called to the fields of others.
This expressive picture suggests many considerations to new apprentices of the Gospel.
Many people, upon hearing references to this or that elevated Spirit, tend to invoke their presence in doctrinal meetings.
The resolution, however, is untimely and unreasonable. Why claim company that we do not deserve?
It cannot be affirmed that the impulse is affiliated with levity, but we need to stress the importance of the purposes at stake.

Imagine yourselves calling Simon Peter to a certain prayer circle and picturing the venerable apostle's acquiescence to the appeal. Naturally, you would be forced to expose to the great celestial emissary the motives of the requisition. And, guiding our mental attitudes with common sense, let us inquire of ourselves whether we possess sufficient elevation to see, hear, and understand his glorious spirit. Who among us will answer in the affirmative? Would we thus have the sufficient audacity to invoke the sublime Cephas solely to hear him speak?

messages.title: Invisible Things
paragraphs: “For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead.” — PAUL (Romans, 1:20)
The spectacle of Universal Creation is the strongest of all manifestations against negativist materialism, child of ignorance or folly.
It is the created things that speak most justly of the invisible nature.
Where is there an activity that unfolds without a basis?
Every intelligent form was born of an intelligent disposition.

Man knows only the causes of his transitory realizations, while ignoring the complex motives of each corner of his path. The exterior landscape that affects his senses is a tiny part of the trove of divine creations that sustain his habitat, conditioned to his possibilities of utilization. The human eye will not see beyond the limit of its capacity to endure. The creature will coexist with the beings it needs in the work of elevation and will receive an environment adequate to its imperatives of perfection and progress, but let no one summarize the vital expression of the Sphere in which he breathes into what mortal fingers are capable of touching.
Visible objects in the field of ephemeral forms constitute a brief and transitory result of invisible forces on the eternal Plane.
Fulfill the duties that fall to you, and you will receive the rights that await you. Do correctly what the present day asks of you, and you will not need to repeat the experience tomorrow.

messages.title: Successes and Failures
paragraphs: “I know how to be brought low, and I know how to abound.” — PAUL (Philippians, 4.12)

In every social community, there are numerous people excessively concerned with particularist successes, affirming themselves anxious for the opportunity of prominence. These are precisely the ones who least anchor themselves in positions of distinction when invited to the highest posts in the world, disastrously spoiling the opportunities for elevation that life confers upon them.
Almost always, it is those who have learned to endure poverty who know how to manage material resources more appropriately.
For this reason, a treasure amassed for someone who has not worked for its possession is often the cause of crime, separatism, and disturbance.

Working and honest parents will instill in their children the mentality of self-effort and affectionate cooperation, whereas selfish and careless parents will foster uselessness and laziness in their descendants.

Paul of Tarsus, in his lesson to the church in Philippi, refers to the precious imperative of the path regarding balance, demonstrating the disciple's need concerning the valuation of poverty and fortune, of scarcity and abundance.

Success and failure are two cups holding diverse elements which, nevertheless, adapt to the same sublime purposes. Human ignorance, however, finds in the first the liquor of intoxication and in the second identifies gall for despair. Therein lies the profound error, because the wise person will extract from joy and pain, from abundance or scarcity, the divine content.

messages.title: Before Jesus
paragraphs: “And whatever you do, do it heartily, as to the Lord and not to men.” — PAUL (Colossians, 3.23)

The understanding of Christ’s service among human creatures will later attain the precise amplitude for the glorification of Him who follows us closely from the first day, enlightening our path with the divine light.

If every educated person were to inquire of themselves concerning the essential foundation of their activities on Earth, they would always find in the inner sanctuary vast horizons for inferences of infinite value.
For whom has the century worked? To whom has it offered the fruit of each day's labors?

We do not wish to belittle the respectable position of homelands, organizations, family, and personality; however, we cannot ignore their expression of relativity in time. In the course of the years, borders change, laws evolve, the domestic group renews itself, and man rises to ever higher destinies.

Everything that represents the creature's effort was the realization of itself within the framework of Christ's permanent works. What we have accomplished across the centuries constitutes benefit or offense to ourselves in the work that belongs to the Lord and not to us others. Legislators and governed pass away in time with their own baggage, and Jesus remains in order to judge the advantage or disadvantage of each one's collaboration in the divine service of evolution and improvement.
Administration and obedience, the responsibilities of charting and following, are merely subdivisions of the stewardship conferred by the Lord upon His wards.
Dignified work is the holy opportunity. Within the circles of service, the attitude assumed by man will honor or dishonor his eternal personality before Jesus Christ.

messages.title: To Contribute
paragraphs: “So let each one give as he purposes in his heart, not grudgingly or of necessity; for God loves a cheerful giver.” — PAUL (2 Corinthians, 9.7)
When Paul's statement that God loves a cheerful giver was disseminated, many people only remembered material alms.
The praise, however, is not restricted to generous hands that scatter the offerings of kindness among the needy and suffering.
Naturally, all gestures of love come into account in divine recognition, but we must consider that the verb to contribute, in the present lesson, appears in all its grandiose sublimity.

Cooperation in good is a pressing issue of every place and every day. Any human being is capable of providing it. It is not only the beggar who awaits it, but also the cradle from which experience is renewed, the family in which we refine the conquests of virtue, the neighbor—our brother in humanity—and the workplace, which marks our individual utilization in the effort of each day.

Upon the arrival of the moment of diurnal repose, each heart can question itself regarding the quality of its collaboration in service, in conversations, in affectionate relationships, in this or that concern of common life.

Let us guard against sorrows and sterilizing shadows. Ill will, complaints, dissatisfaction, levity do not integrate the framework of the works that the Lord expects from our activities in the world. Let us mobilize our resources with optimism and not forget that the Father loves the child who contributes with joy.

messages.title: Let Us Follow Until Then
paragraphs: “If you abide in me, and my words abide in you, you will ask what you desire, and it shall be done for you.” — JESUS (John, 15.7)
In the Lord's Prayer, Jesus teaches His co-workers the need for the full observance of the Father's designs.
The Master knew that human will is still very frail and that countless struggles surround the creature until it learns to establish union with the Divine.
Despite this, the lesson of prayer has always been interpreted by most believers as a resource for easily obtaining celestial support.

Many ask for specific favors and mechanically recite verbal formulas. Certainly, they cannot receive immediate satisfaction for their own whims, because in the state of downfall or ignorance, the spirit needs, above all, to learn to submit to the divine designs regarding itself.

We will, however, reach the era of prayers fully answered. We will attain such an achievement when we are spiritually in Christ. Then, whatever we wish will be done for us, because we will have penetrated the true sense of each thing and the purpose of each circumstance. We will be empowered to desire and to ask in Jesus, and life will present itself to us in its true characteristics of infinity, eternity, renewal, and beauty.

As incarnate or disincarnate beings, we are still walking toward the Master so that we may experience the glorious union with His love. Until then, let us work and watch to understand the divine will.

messages.title: Logic of Providence
paragraphs: “After you were illuminated, you endured a great struggle with sufferings.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 10.32)
Cultivators of sincere faith are usually pointed out in the world as great sufferers.
There are even those who claim to deliberately stay away from religious circles, fearing the contagion of spiritual hardships.

The impious, the ignorant, and the futile display themselves spectacularly in common life through bizarre traits of external fantasy; however, when they approach celestial truths, before gaining access to the permanent joys of superior spirituality, they traverse great tunnels of sadness, dejection, and taciturnity. The phenomenon, nonetheless, is natural, since there will always be pondering after folly and remorse after debauchery.
The problem, however, encompasses a broader circle of clarifications.
The mercy that manifests in the justice of God transcends human comprehension.

The Father grants ignorant and straying children the right to harsher experiences only after they have been illuminated. Only after learning to see with the eternal Spirit does life offer them different values. From then on, the indispensable strength for triumph in the great struggle of afflictions will be born in their hearts.

The frivolous and opportunists, despite appearances, are usually fragile souls, like dry branches that break at the first blow of the gale. Noble Spirits, who endure the storms of the earthly path, know this. Only spiritual light guarantees success in trials.
No one entrusts the responsibility of a boat full of worries and dangers to mere children.

messages.title: Man with Jesus
paragraphs: “Rejoice in the Lord always. Again I will say, rejoice!” — PAUL (Philippians, 4.4)
From inertia to service...
From ignorance to wisdom...
From instinct to reason...
From might to right...
From selfishness to fraternity...
From tyranny to compassion...
From violence to understanding...
From hatred to love...
From false possession to the search for imperishable goods...
From bloody conquest to edifying renunciation...
From extortion to justice...
From harshness to pity...
From empty words to the creative verb...
From monstrosity to beauty...
From vice to virtue...
From imbalance to harmony...
From affliction to contentment...
From the swamp to the mountain...
From mud to glory...
Man, my brother, let us rejoice in the midst of redemptive struggle!
What peaks of angelitude can we reach if we truly consecrate ourselves to the Divine Friend who descended and humbled Himself for us?

messages.title: Jesus for Man
paragraphs: “And being found in appearance as a man, He humbled Himself and became obedient to the point of death, even the death of the cross.” — PAUL (Philippians, 2.7,8)
The Master descended to serve, from splendor to darkness...
From eternal dawn to full night...
From the stars to the manger...
From infinity to limitation...
From glory to the carpentry shop...
From greatness to self-abnegation...
From the divinity of angels to the misery of men...
From the company of sublime geniuses to the companionship of sinners...
From ruler of the world to servant of all...
From magnanimous creditor to slave...
From benefactor to persecuted...
From savior to forsaken...
From emissary of love to victim of hatred...
From redeemer of the centuries to prisoner of shadows...
From celestial shepherd to oppressed sheep...
From powerful throne to the cross of martyrdom...
From the sanctifying verb to anguished silence...
From advocate of creatures to defendant without defense...
From the arms of friends to the touch of thieves...
From donor of eternal life to sentenced in the valley of death...
He humbled Himself and made Himself obscure so that man might rise and shine forever!
Oh! Lord, what did You not do for us, so that we might learn the path of the Glorious Resurrection in the Kingdom?
messages.note: This is the 1st lesson of the book “Antologia Mediúnica do Natal” (Mediumistic Anthology of Christmas), published by FEB in 1966.

messages.title: The Lord Always Gives
paragraphs: “If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him!” — JESUS (Luke, 11.13)
An earthly father, despite the blind affection with which he often surrounds the heart, always knows how to surround his child with beneficial gifts.
For what reason would the Heavenly Father, full of wisdom and love, remain deaf and motionless before our supplications?
The paternal devotion of the Supreme Lord surrounds us everywhere. It is important, however, not to warp our understanding.
Let us remember that Divine Providence operates invariably for the infinite good.
It frees the suffocating atmosphere with the resources of the storm.
It defends the flower with thorns.
It protects useful vegetation with unpleasant fertilizers.
It sustains the greenery of the valleys with the hardness of rocks.

Likewise, in the circles of planetary struggles, events that seem disastrous to our private activity represent props to our balance and success, whereas phenomena interpreted as calamities in the collective order constitute enormous public benefits.

Implore, therefore, the Lord for the blessing of Divine Light for your heart and intelligence, so that you do not get lost in the labyrinth of problems; however, do not forget that, on most occasions, Heaven's initial help comes to our common path through anguish and disillusionment. Wait, however, confident in the passing of time. Time is our silent explainer and will reveal to your heart the infinite goodness of the Father who restores the health of our soul through the thorn of disillusionment or the bitter elixir of suffering.

messages.title: Better to Suffer in Good
paragraphs: “For it is better, if it is the will of God, to suffer for doing good than for doing evil.” — PETER (1 Peter, 3.17)
To amass financial resources that he will be compelled to abandon precipitately, man often acquires deplorable illnesses that corrode his energy centers, bringing undesired death.
By purchasing fleeting sensations for the flesh body, he commonly receives dangerous ailments that accompany him until the final days of the vehicle in which he moves on Earth.
By becoming angry over insignificant lessons along the path, he poisons vital organs, creating fatal imbalances in physical life.

By stuffing his stomach on certain occasions, he establishes the vitiation of important devices of physiological instrumentality, renouncing the perfection of the carnal vessel for the simple pleasure of gluttony.
Why fear the mishaps of the clear path of love and wisdom, if the dark trail of hatred and ignorance remains replete with avenging and disturbing forces?

How can we fear the fatigue and exhaustion, the complications and misunderstandings, the conflicts and displeasures arising from the blessed struggle for the supreme victory of good, if the fight for the provisional triumph of evil leads combatants to afflictive tributes of suffering?
Let us spend our best possibilities in the service of Christ, committing our lives to Him.

The criminal weapon that breaks and the repugnant measure accomplished always provoke curses and shadow, but for the servant torn in duty and for the lamp that goes out in illuminative service, a different destiny is reserved.

messages.title: Let Us Have Peace
paragraphs: “Be at peace among yourselves.” — PAUL (1 Thessalonians, 5.13)

If it is not possible to breathe in a climate of perfect peace among creatures, given the ignorance and belligerence that predominate on the human road, it is reasonable for the learner to seek interior serenity in the face of the conflicts that seek to envelop them at every instant.
Each incarnate mind constitutes an extensive center of spiritual government, subordinated now to just limitations, served by various powers translated into senses and perceptions.
When all individual centers of power are dominated within themselves with ample movement toward legitimate good, then war will be banished from the Planet.
For this, however, it is necessary that our brothers in humanity, older in experience and knowledge, learn to have peace with themselves.

Educating vision, hearing, taste, and impulses represents the primordial basis of edifying pacifism. Generally, we hear, see, and feel according to our inclinations and not according to essential reality. We register certain information far from the good intention in which it was initially cast, and instead, according to our internal disturbances. We note situations and landscapes with the light or darkness that absorb our intelligence. We feel with the reflection or chaos that we install in our own understanding.
This is why, as much as possible, we should establish serenity around our steps before the conflicts of the sphere in which we find ourselves.
Without calm, it is impossible to observe and work for the good.
Without peace within us, we will never reach the circles of true peace.

messages.title: Good Will
paragraphs: “See then that ye walk circumspectly.” — PAUL (Ephesians, 5:15)
Good will discovers work.
Work operates renewal.
Renewal finds the good.
The good reveals the spirit of service.
The spirit of service attains understanding.
Understanding gains humility.
Humility conquers love.
Love generates renunciation.
Renunciation reaches the light.
Light accomplishes self-improvement.
Self-improvement sanctifies man.
Sanctified man converts the world to God.
Walking prudently, through simple good will the creature will reach the Divine Kingdom of Light.

messages.title: Ill Will
paragraphs: “And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness.” — PAUL (Ephesians, 5:11)
Ill will generates shadow.
Shadow favors stagnation.
Stagnation preserves evil.
Evil enthrones idleness.
Idleness creates discord.
Discord awakens pride.
Pride wakes up vanity.
Vanity stirs inferior passion.
Inferior passion provokes indiscipline.
Indiscipline maintains hardness of heart.
Hardness of heart imposes spiritual blindness.
Spiritual blindness leads from the abyss.
Given over to the unfruitful works of incomprehension, through simple ill will man can tumble indefinitely into the precipice of darkness.

messages.title: Need to Awaken
paragraphs: “Awake thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead, and Christ shall give thee light.” — PAUL (Ephesians, 5:14)

A great number of newcomers or not to the circles of Christianity accuse strong difficulties in understanding and applying the teachings of Jesus. Some find obscurities in the texts, others persist in literary petty squabbles. They become uneasy, protest and reject the divine bread because of the human wrapping it needed to preserve itself on Earth.
These friends, however, do not realize that this happens because they remain sleeping, victims of paralysis of the superior faculties.

On most occasions, the divine invitations pass by them, suggestive and sanctifying; nevertheless, the distracted companions interpret them as sacred scenes, worthy of praise, but quickly relegated to oblivion. The heart does not adhere, dozing numbly, incapable of analyzing and understanding.

The creature needs to ask itself what it is doing, what it desires, what purposes it serves, and what goals it is destined for. It becomes essential to examine oneself, emerge from animality, and rise to master one's own path.

Great masses, supposedly religious, are led through the circumstances of each day like rows of unconscious sleepwalkers. People speak of God, faith, and spirituality as if they were breathing in the strange atmosphere of a dark nightmare. Shaken by the incessant current of the river of life, they roll in the whirlpool of events, blinded, dormant, and semi-dead until they awaken and rise through personal effort, so that Christ may enlighten them.

messages.title: Today
paragraphs: “But exhort one another daily, while it is called To day; lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 3:13)
The counsel of reciprocal, daily exhortation indicated by the apostle requires much reflection so that shelter is not established for certain doubts.
Let us emphasize that Paul places singular importance on the time called Today, highlighting the need to value the resources in movement through our possibilities on the passing day.

Many believe that to counsel their brethren they need to speak constantly, turning into inveterate arguers. It is important to recognize, however, that a warning, when it consists only of words, leaves an invariable void after its passing.
As occurs in the plane of physical organizations, no spiritual edifice will rise without foundations.
The “exhort one another” represents an appeal more important than the simple call to verbal duels.

Invitations and counsels transpire, with greater force, from the example of each one. Everyone who lives in the real practice of the noble principles to which they devoted themselves in the world, who zealously fulfills the duties contracted and demonstrates goodness sincerely, is exhorting their brothers in humanity to the path of elevation. It is to this kind of daily testimony that the convert of Damascus calls us. Only through this constant exercise of self-improvement will man free himself from fatal deceptions.
Do not harden yourself, therefore, on the road the Lord has led you to tread, for your ransom, improvement, and sanctification. Remember the importance of the time called Today.

messages.title: Praise
paragraphs: “But he said, Yea rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it.” — (LUKE, 11:28)

Jesus had addressed the crowd with the enormous power of His love, winning their general attention. Scarcely had He finished His loving and wise observations when a woman stood up in the midst of the mob and, magnetized by His expression of sublime spirituality, spoke out in a loud voice about the beatitudes that should belong to Mary for having contributed to the coming of the Savior to the face of the Earth. But promptly, in the perfect understanding of the unfortunate consequences that could arise from the thoughtless attitude, the Master replies that, first of all, blessed are those who hear God's revelation and practice His teachings, observing His principles.

The passage constitutes a living clarification so that the campaign against personal praise—the poison of the holiest works, capable of suffocating their purposes and hopes—might not be dampened among sincere disciples.

If you admire some companion who qualifies in your eyes as a faithful worker of the good, do not disturb them with words, which the world has often abused by constructing superficial phrases in the dangerous feast of flattery. Help them, with good will and understanding, in the execution of the ministry that falls to them, without forgetting that, above all beatitudes, shine the divine gifts of those who hear the Lord's Word and put it into practice.

messages.title: Shake Off the Dust
paragraphs: “And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when ye depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.” — JESUS (Matthew, 10:14)

The disciples themselves materialized Jesus' teaching by shaking the dust off their sandals when retiring from this or that place of rebellion or impenitence. However, if the symbol that transpires from the Master's lesson were intended merely as a mechanical gesture, we would have in it nothing more than a set of empty words.
The teaching, however, is deeper. It recommends the extinction of unhealthy leaven.

Shaking the dust from one's feet means not keeping any resentment or any debris at the foundations of life, in the face of ignorance and perversity that manifest on the path of our common experiences.

Natural is the desire to entrust the seeds of truth and goodness to others; however, if we are received by the hostility of the environment we address, it is not reasonable that we maintain ourselves in long observations and notes which, instead of leading our task to timely success, establish shadows and difficulties around us.

If someone did not receive your good will, nor perceived your good intention, why waste time on accusatory sentences? Such an attitude does not solve spiritual problems. Do you not know that the denier and the indifferent will be equally called by the death of the body to our homeland of origin? Commend them to Jesus with love and proceed in a straight line, seeking your sacred objectives. There is much to do in the spiritual edification of the world and of yourself. Shake off, then, bad impressions and march joyfully.

messages.title: Contemplate Further
paragraphs: “For with the same measure that ye mete withal it shall be measured to you again.” — JESUS (Luke, 6:38)
To the Eskimo, heaven is a continent of ice sustained by seals.
To the forest savage, there is no other paradise besides abundant hunting.
To the sectarian religious man, the glory of the beyond belongs exclusively to him and those who are fond of him.
To the wise man, this world and the celestial circles surrounding it are tiny departments of the Universe.

Transfer your observation to your field of daily experience and do not forget that external situations will be portrayed in your interior plane, according to the material of reflection you welcome into your conscience.
If you persist in anger, all the forces around you will seem angry to you.
If you prefer sadness, you will note despondency at every stretch of the road.
If you doubt yourself, no one will trust your effort.
If you have grown accustomed to disturbances and frictions, you will hardly know how to live in peace with yourself.

You will breathe in the superior or inferior, tortured or tranquil zone in which you place your own mind. And within the organization in which you delight, you will live with the geniuses you invoke. If you dwell in repose, you can acquire it in all tones and shades, and if you fix yourself on work, you will find a thousand different resources to serve.

Around your steps, the landscape that shelters you will always be, in your appreciation, what you think of it, because with the same measure you apply to Nature, the living work of God, Nature will likewise measure you.

messages.title: Let Us Learn Soon
paragraphs: “As ye have therefore received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk ye in him.” — PAUL (Colossians, 2:6)

Among those who refer to Jesus Christ we can identify two major currents distinct from each other: those who know Him through information and those who have received His benefits. The former gathered news of the Master from books or others' exhortations, yet they walk toward the condition of the latter, who have already received His blessings. To these latter, more properly, the Gospel should be spoken.

How do we find the Lord in our passing through the world? Sometimes, His divine presence manifests in a difficult solution to a human problem, in the restoration of bodily health, in the return of a loved one, in the spontaneous renewal of the common road so that new light may dawn in reasoning.
There are many people informed about Jesus and countless people who have already absorbed His saving charity.
It is essential, however, that the beneficiaries of Christ, as much as they experience joy in the gift, feel equal pleasure in work and in the testimony of faith.
It will not suffice to stuff ourselves with blessings. It is necessary that we collaborate, in our turn, in the service of the Gospel, attending to its sanctifying program.

Many tedious recapitulations and much useless activity may be peculiar to merely informed spirits; however, we, who have already received infinitely from the Lord's Mercy, let us learn, as soon as possible, personal adaptation to His sublime designs.

messages.title: Bad Conversations
paragraphs: “Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 15:33)

Less worthy conversation always leaves the trace of inferiority wherever it has passed. The atmosphere of distrust immediately replaces the climate of serenity. The poison of unhealthy investigations spreads rapidly. After unworthy conversation, there is always less sincerity and a lower expression of fraternal strength. In its ignominious cradle, the phantoms of calumny are born, slipping among holily intended creatures, attempting the destruction of honest homes; inferior preoccupations arise, peering from afar, blackening respectable attitudes; criminal curiosity emerges, showing up where it is not called, uttering unbridled opinions, inducing those who hear it to lying and dementia.

Bad conversation corrupts the most dignified thoughts. Profitable talks suffer its relentless persecution everywhere, and it becomes imperative for man to keep on guard against its insistent and destructive siege.
When the heart has surrendered to Jesus, it is very easy to control subjects and eliminate debasing words.

Always examine the verbal suggestions that surround you on your daily path. Have they brought you denunciations, bad news, frivolities, unhealthy reports of other people's lives? Observe how you act. On all occasions, there is a resource to rectify lovingly, since you can renew all this material in Jesus Christ.

messages.title: Murmurings
paragraphs: “Do all things without murmurings and disputings.” — PAUL (Philippians, 2:14)

A dispute has never been seen that was not preceded by inferior murmurings. It is an old habit of levity to seek ingratitude, moral misery, pride, vanity, and all the scourges that ruin souls in this world in order to organize the talks of the shadow, where goodness, love, and truth are focused upon with malice.
When someone begins to find easy motives for many complaints, it is fair to perform a rigorous self-examination, in order to verify whether they are suffering from the terrible disease of murmurings.
Those who fulfill their duties along the guidelines of righteous activities certainly cannot cultivate opportunities for complaints.

It is essential for the disciple to keep on guard against these accumulators of destructive energies, because, generally speaking, their pernicious influence invades almost all places of struggle on the Planet.

It is easy to identify them. For them, everything is wrong, nothing works, one should not expect anything better in anything. Their speech is permanent irritation, their observations are unjust and discouraging.

Let us fight, as much as lies in our power, against these humiliating mental attitudes. Confident in God, let us expand all our hopes, certain that, as old Proverbs assert, the optimistic heart is a medicine of peace and joy.

messages.title: The witnesses
paragraphs: “Therefore, since we are surrounded by such a great cloud of witnesses, let us throw off everything that hinders.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 12:1)
This concept by Paul of Tarsus deserves special consideration from the learners of the Gospel.

Each human existence is always a valuable day of struggle — a generous step toward infinite ascension — and, in whatever position they remain, the creature will be surrounded by an enormous legion of witnesses. We are not referring solely to those who are an integral part of the domestic circle, but, above all, to the friends and benefactors of each person, who observe them from the different angles of life, from the highlands of the higher Spirituality.

In every part of the Earth, the disciple breathes surrounded by a great cloud of spiritual witnesses, who record their steps and note their attitudes, because no one reaches terrestrial experience haphazardly, without solid reasons based on love or justice.

Before reincarnation, generous Spirits endorsed the pleas of the repentant soul, judges functioned in the processes concerning them, friends interfered in assistance services, contributing to the organization of the particularities of the redeeming struggle… These brothers and educators become permanent witnesses of the ward while the new task lasts, speaking to them without words in the recesses of conscience. Children and parents, husbands and wives, siblings and blood relatives of the world are protagonists of the evolutionary drama. The observers, in general, remain on the other side of life.
Therefore, do all the good possible to your fellow combatants today, and do not forget those who accompany you in spirit, full of concern and love.

messages.title: Answering
paragraphs: “Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how you ought to answer each one.” — PAUL (Colossians, 4:6)
The act of profitably answering heterogeneous intelligences requires superior qualities that man must strive to acquire.

Not all arguments can be addressed, indiscriminately, to the collectivity of companions who struggle among themselves in evolutionary and redeeming tasks. It is necessary to reply correctly to each one. To the one who labors in the field, we should not retort by mentioning spectacles of the city; to the one who comments on the harsh difficulties of the individualistic path, we shall not reply with high-level scientific information.

First, it is imperative not to displease the listener, seasoning the verbal attitude with a legitimate understanding of life's problems, making it our duty to help those who have strayed from simplicity and usefulness to readjust.

Every answer in an important matter is a remedy. It is essential to know how to dose it with a view to its effects. Each creature will tolerate, with benefit, a certain dynamization. The very solutions of truth and love should not be administered without this criterion. Applied in inadequate portions, truth can destroy just as much as love tends to ruin...

Even if you are questioned by the greatest evildoer in the world, you must maintain a pleasant and dignified attitude to inform or clarify. Knowing how to answer is a virtue within the framework of celestial wisdom. For your own sake, do not forget the best way to attend to everyone.

messages.title: According to the flesh
paragraphs: “For if you live according to the flesh, you will die.” — PAUL (Romans, 8:13)

For those who live according to the flesh—that is, in conformity with lower impulses—the earthly season of struggle is nothing more than a series of empty events. At all moments, limitation will be an incessant phantom to them.
With a brain crushed by negative notions, they will encounter death at every step.
For the conscience that has had the misfortune of espousing such dark conceptions, human existence will be nothing more than an unhappy comedy.
In suffering, it identifies a house suited to despair.
In work destined for spiritual purification, it feels the climate of revolt.
It cannot count on the blessing of love, because, given its own appreciation, affective ties are mere accidents in the mechanism of temporary desires.
Pain, the benefactor and preserver of the world, is intolerable to it; discipline constitutes an agonizing prison; and service to others represents heavy humiliation.
It never forgives, knows not how to renounce, finds it painful to yield in favor of someone, and, when it helps, demands the subservience of a slave from the beneficiary.
Wretched is the man who lives, breathes, and acts according to the flesh! The conflicts of possession torment his heart for an indefinite time, with the same heat as savage life.

Woe to him, however, for the renewing hour will always sound! And if he fled the atmosphere of immortality, if he suffocated the best aspirations of his own soul, if he escaped the salutary exercise of suffering, if he made a point of increasing appetites and pleasures through absolute integration with the 'lower side of life,' what can he expect from the end of the body except the sepulcher, shadow, and impossibility within the cruel night?

messages.title: The "but" and the disciples
paragraphs: “I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.” — PAUL (Philippians, 4:13)
The diligent disciple asserts:
— Of myself, I possess nothing good, but Jesus will supply me with resources according to my needs.
— I do not have perfect knowledge of the path, but Jesus will lead me.
The lazy learner declares:
— I do not disbelieve in Jesus' goodness, but I have no strength for Christian work.
— I know the path remains in Jesus, but the world does not allow me to follow it.
The first climbs the mountain of decision. He identifies his own weaknesses, however, he trusts in the Divine Friend and resolves to live His lessons.
The second esteems rest in the deep valley of lower experience. He recognizes the graces the Master has conferred upon him, yet prefers to shirk them.
The first fixed his mind on the divine light and moves forward.
The second stopped his thought on his own limitations.

The 'but' is the conjunction that, in verbalistic processes, habitually defines our intimate position before the Gospel. Placed before the Holy Name, it expresses our firmness and confidence, faith and courage; however, located after it, it places us in indecision and idleness, impermeability and indifference.
Just three letters betray our course.
— Thus my principles recommend, but Jesus asks for something else.
— Thus Jesus advises, but I cannot do it.

Through a small and simple word, we make either our profession of faith or our confession of inefficiency. Let us remember that Paul of Tarsus, despite being stoned and persecuted, managed to victoriously state to the Philippians: — 'I can do all things through Him who strengthens me.'

messages.title: The "no" and the struggle
paragraphs: “But let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes,’ and your ‘No,’ ‘No.’” — JESUS (Matthew, 5:37)
Love, according to the lessons of the Gospel, but do not allow your love to become a shackle, preventing your march toward higher life.
Help all who need your cooperation, however, do not let your support create disturbances and vices along the path of others.
Respond with joy to whoever asks you for a favor, yet do not yield to levity and folly.
Open doors of access to well-being for those around you, but do not forget the education of your companions for true happiness.
Cultivate delicacy and cordiality, nevertheless, be loyal and sincere in your attitudes.
The 'yes' can be very pleasant in all situations, however, the 'no,' in certain sectors of human struggle, is more constructive.
Satisfying all the requests of the path is losing time and, at times, one's own life.
Just as the 'yes' must be pronounced without flattering incense, the 'no' must be said without harshness.
Often, it is necessary to thwart in order that legitimate help is not lost; yet we must recognize that a salutary refusal never disturbs. What lacerates is the blunt tone in which it is cast.
Manners, on most occasions, speak louder than words.

‘Let your speech be: yes, yes; no, no,’ recommends the Gospel. To agree or refuse, however, no one needs to be made of honey or gall. It will suffice to remember that Jesus is Master and Lord not only by what He does, but also by what He refrains from doing.

messages.title: In Paradise
paragraphs: “And Jesus said to him, ‘Assuredly, I say to you, today you will be with Me in Paradise.’” — (LUKE, 23:43)
At first glance, it seems that Jesus inclined toward the so-called good thief through particular sympathy.
But it is not so. The Master, in this lesson of Calvary, renewed the definition of paradise.
In another passage, He Himself asserted that the Divine Kingdom does not come with outward appearances. It begins, develops, and consolidates in eternal splendors within the depths of the heart.

In that hour of supreme sacrifice, the good thief surrendered unconditionally to Jesus Christ. The reader of the Gospel is not informed regarding the strenuous labors and new responsibilities that would weigh on his shoulders to cement union with the Savior, yet he is convinced that from that moment on the former evildoer would enter Heaven.
The symbol is beautiful and profound and gives an idea of the infinite extension of Divine Mercy.

We may present ourselves with a voluminous baggage of debts from a dark past before the truth; but from the instant we surrender to the Lord's designs, sincerely accepting the duty of our own regeneration, we advance to a different spiritual region where every yoke is easy and every burden is light. Having reached this height, the indebted Spirit will not remain in a false beatific attitude, recognizing, above all, that with Jesus, suffering is rectification and crosses are immortal clarity.
This is why the good thief, in that very hour, entered the heights of paradise.

messages.title: In spirit
paragraphs: “But if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the flesh, you will live.” — PAUL (Romans, 8:13)
Whoever lives according to the sublime laws of the spirit breathes in a Sphere different from the material field where they still rest their feet.
Advanced understanding marks their intimate position.
They use the day like a diligent learner who cherishes their stay on Earth as valuable time for learning that must not be belittled.
They find in work the blessed gift of elevation and refinement.
In the ignorance of others, they discover precious possibilities for service.
In the difficulties and afflictions of the road, they gather resources for their own illumination and aggrandizement.
They watch obstacles pass by like watching clouds float by.
They love responsibility, but are not attached to possession.
They lead with devotion, yet flee from domination.
They support without unhealthy inclinations.
They serve without enslaving themselves.

They remain attentive to the obligations of sowing, however, they are not anxious for the harvest, because they know that the field and the plant, the sun and the rain, the water and the wind belong to the Eternal Giver.
Beneficiaries of divine goods, wherever they may be, they carry within themselves, in conscience and heart, their own treasures.
Blessed is the man who journeys through life in spirit! For him, afflictive death is nothing more than the dawn of a new day, a sublime transformation, and a joyful awakening!

messages.title: According to love
paragraphs: “Yet if your brother is grieved because of your food, you are no longer walking in love. Do not destroy with your food the one for whom Christ died.” — PAUL (Romans, 14:15)
Dogmatic prejudices make victims in all times, and the heirs of Christianity were not lacking in this concert of incomprehension.
Even today, sectarian processes, although less rigorous in their manifestations, continue to wound hearts and disregard feelings.

In another era, disciples coming from Judaism provoked violent friction due to traditions regarding unclean food; now, we do not have the problem of meats sacrificed in the Temple; however, new religious formalisms have replaced the old motives of polemics and discord.

There are priests who only feel like missionaries when celebrating their proper offices, and believers who do not understand meditation and spiritualizing service except during Sunday hours, with prayer in an exclusive bodily posture.
The disciple who has already managed to overcome such barriers must cooperate in silence to extend the benefits of his victory.

It would be absurd to cross the obstacle and continue deliberately in purely conventionalist demonstrations, but it would also be a lack of charity to hurl reproaches at poor brothers who are still in agonizing mental conflicts trying to find themselves within the august idea of God.

When you notice a friend imprisoned by these illusions, remember that the Master equally went to the cross because of him. Place kindness ahead of analysis, and your observation will be constructive and sanctifying. Every time there is understanding in the pitcher of your soul, you will find infinite resources to help, love, and serve.

messages.title: Lifting up holy hands
paragraphs: “I desire therefore that the men pray everywhere, lifting up holy hands, without wrath and doubting.” — PAUL (1 Timothy, 2:8)
In this excerpt from Paul's first epistle to Timothy, we receive a precious recommendation for service.

Some learners might wish to glimpse in the text only an exhortation to attitudes of praise; however, the convert of Damascus clarifies that we must lift up holy hands everywhere, without wrath or doubting.

Paul was not referring to the act of folded hands that the creature always prefers to perform in certain religious circles where, due to the respectable artificiality of the situation, visible irritations or disputes are unjustified. The apostle mentions the honest and edifying action of man who collaborates with Divine Providence and refers to daily work, which takes place in the most secluded regions of the Globe.

Reading his advice, it is reasonable to recall that man, in his individualistic effort, invariably raises his hands in daily toil. If he administers, he remains pointing out paths; if he participates in intellectual labors, he wields the pen; if he operates in the field, he will guide the agricultural instrument. Paul adds, however, that these hands must be sanctified, implying that many people move their arms in earthly work, yet emphasizing the convenience of judging the purpose and content of the expended action.
If you wish to apply reasoning to yourself, observe, first of all, whether your accomplishment is proceeding without destructive anger and without useless demands.

messages.title: And the adulterer?
paragraphs: “And having set her in the midst, they said to Him: Master, this woman was caught in adultery, in the very act.” — (JOHN, 8:4)
The case of the sinner presented by the crowd to Jesus involves very significant considerations regarding man's impulse to see evil in others without seeing it in himself.
Among the reflections the narrative suggests, we identify that of the erroneous concept of unilateral adultery.

If the unhappy woman was found in the very act, where had the adulterer taken refuge, who was not brought to trial by popular care? Was she the only one responsible? If there was a sore in the collective organism requiring intervention to be extirpated, in what den was the one hiding who helped cause it?

The Master's attitude at that hour was characterized by infinite wisdom and unsurpassable love. Jesus could not center the weight of guilt on the wretched woman and, letting the general error be perceived, asked those who were without sin.
The great and spontaneous silence that then ensued constituted a response more eloquent than any verbal declaration.
Beside the adulterous woman also stood the perverted men, who withdrew ashamed.

Man and woman appear in the world with specific tasks that integrate, however, into an essentially single work within the plan of universal evolution. In the chapter of lower experiences, one does not fall without the other, because both were granted an equal opportunity to sanctify themselves.

If women who stray from their lofty mission continue under a sad spotlight on the social path, it is because adulterers remain absent from the hour of judgment, just as they were at the moment of Jesus' famous suggestion.

messages.title: Try and Act
paragraphs: “And make straight paths for your feet, so that what is lame may not be entirely dislocated, but rather healed.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 12:13)
The well-intentioned person will intensely reflect upon better paths, feeding superior ideals and leaning toward goodness and justice.
Let us agree, however, that good intention will pass without greater benefit if it does not connect with the sphere of immediate realities in righteous action.
It is necessary to meditate on the good; nevertheless, it is imperative to execute it.

Divine Providence surrounds the path of creatures with the material of eternal edification, enabling them to build the “straight paths” to which Paul of Tarsus refers. Such an achievement on the part of the disciple is indispensable, because, around their paths, follow those who limp. The prisoners of ignorance and bad faith drag themselves, as best they can, along the margins of the service of higher order, and, from time to time, approach the faithful servants of Christ, proposing measures and business that suit their inferior mentality. Only those who build straight roads escape their subtle assaults, defending themselves and also offering them new bases so that they do not stray entirely from the Divine Designs.

Always apply your good intentions in the plane of practical realities, so that your good works are enlightened by love and so that your love does not become an orphan of good works. Do this for yourself, who are in need of elevation, and for those who still seek you limping.

messages.title: Ponder Always
paragraphs: “And the things that you have heard from me among many witnesses, commit these to faithful men who will be able to teach others also.” — PAUL (2 Timothy, 2:2)

The disciples of the Gospel, in Christian Spiritism, often show unrestrained enthusiasm, anxious to spread the renewed, contagious, and ardent faith. However, such mental movement requires great care, not only because astonishment and admiration do not mean interior elevation, but also because it is indispensable to know the quality of the spiritual terrain to which the power of knowledge is to be transmitted.

Of course, we are not referring here to the act of general sowing of the revealing truth, nor to the manifestation of fraternal kindness, which translate our natural obligations in the action of good. Let us rather understand the need for each brother to govern the patrimony of spiritual gifts received from the superior plane, so as not to relegate celestial values to the contempt of wickedness and ignorance.
Let us distribute the light of love with our fellow journeyers; nevertheless, let us defend our inner sanctuary against the onslaughts of darkness.

Let us remember that the Master Himself reserved different lessons for the popular masses and for the small community of apprentices; He was not accompanied by all the disciples in the transfiguration of Tabor; at the Last Supper, He waits for Judas to be absent before commenting on the anguish that would follow.

It is necessary for us to pay attention to these attitudes of Christ, understanding that not everything is destined for everyone. The ennobled spirits who communicate in the carnal Sphere always adopt the selective criterion, seeking able and faithful creatures, qualified to teach others. If they, who can already identify problems with enlightened vision, act with prudence in this sense, how should the disciple who only has bodily eyes watch? Let us work for the benefit of all, let us extend fraternal ties, understanding, however, that each creature has its step on the infinite scale of life.

messages.title: Corrections
paragraphs: “If you endure chastening, God deals with you as with sons; for what son is there whom a father does not chasten?” — PAUL (Hebrews, 12:7)
Blessed is the Spirit who understands the correction of the Lord and accepts it without resisting. Rare, however, are the creatures who manage to understand it and endure it.

Sometimes, the generous reprimand from the High — a symbol of watchful love — reaches the field of man, translating a sacred and silent warning, but, on most occasions, the incarnated mind repels the saving goad, plunges into the night of rebellion, eliminates precious possibilities, and qualifies as unbearable misfortune the renewing influence destined to clear its dark and sad path.

Many people, in the face of the regenerative phenomenon, resort to a spectacular escape from the difficult situation and surrender, unarmed, to slow suicide, abandoning themselves to total indifference toward their own destiny.

Whoever proceeds in this way cannot be treated as a son, because they have isolated themselves, distanced themselves from Divine Providence, and erected compact walls of shadow between their own heart and the Fatherly Blessings.
Those who understand the corrections of the All-Merciful readjust themselves in a circle of new and promising life.

Once the inner storm is overcome, they revalue the opportunities to learn, serve, and build, and, grounded in the bitter experiences of yesterday, they apply the graces of the superior life with a view to tomorrow.
Do not forget that evil cannot offer rectifications to anyone. When the correction of the Lord reaches your path, accept it humbly, convinced that it constitutes a true message from Heaven.

messages.title: Beatitudes
paragraphs: “Blessed are you when men hate you, and when they exclude you, and revile you, and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of Man's sake.” — JESUS (Luke, 6:22)
The problem of the beatitudes requires serious reflections before being interpreted as a settled matter behind the scenes of knowledge.

Jesus confers the credential of blessedness upon the followers who share His afflictions and labors; however, it behooves us to point out that the Master categorizes sacrifices and sufferings as educational and redemptive blessings. Thus arises the imperative of knowing how to accept them.
This or that man will be blessed for having built the good in material poverty, for finding joy in simplicity and peace, for knowing how to keep a long and divine hope in their heart.
But… what about sincere adherence to the sacred obligations of the title?

The Master, in the supervision that marks His teachings, refers to the eternal beatitudes; however, rare are those who approach them with the perfect understanding of one nearing an immense treasure. The majority of the less favored in the Terrestrial Plane, if visited by pain, prefer lamentation and despair; if invited to the test of renunciation, they slip into unreasonable demands and, almost always, instead of working peacefully, launch themselves into unworthy adventures of those who get lost in boundless ambition.
Jesus offered many beatitudes. Rare, however, desire them. This is why there are many poor and many afflicted who may be greatly needy in the world, but who are not yet blessed in Heaven.

messages.title: The Divine Worker
paragraphs: “His winnowing fan is in His hand, and He will thoroughly purge His threshing floor, and gather the wheat into His barn; but the chaff He will burn with unquenchable fire.” — JOHN THE BAPTIST (Luke, 3:17)
Apostles and followers of Christ, since the primitive organizations of the evangelical movement, designated Him through various names.

Jesus was called the Master, the Shepherd, the Messiah, the Savior, the Prince of Peace; all these titles are just and venerable; however, we cannot forget, alongside these sublime evocations, that unexpected presentation by the Baptist. The Precursor designates Him as an attentive worker who has the shovel in His hands, who will clean the hard and uncultivated ground, who will gather the wheat at the appropriate time, and who will purify the debris with the flame of justice and love that never goes out.

It is interesting to note that John does not present the Lord wielding laws, full of ordinances and parchments, nor does he refer to Him, according to the old Jewish traditions, who awaited the Divine Messenger in a chariot of magnificent glories. He refers to the self-sacrificing and optimistic worker. The rustic shovel does not rest beside Him, but remains vigilant in His hands, and in His spirit reigns the hope of cleaning the earth entrusted to His saving guidelines.

All you who live engaged in earthly services for a better era, keep burning in your hearts devotion to the cause of the Gospel of Christ. Let us not be curtailed by difficulties or ingratitudes. Let us unfold our activities under the precious stimulus of faith, because with us goes ahead, blessing our humble cooperation, that divine worker who will clean the threshing floor of the world.

messages.title: That Is Your Concern
paragraphs: “Saying, ‘I have sinned by betraying innocent blood.’ And they said, ‘What is that to us? You see to it!’” — (MATTHEW, 27:4)
The word of human wickedness is always cruel to those who hear its criminal insinuations.
Judas's case demonstrates the irresponsibility and perversity of those who cooperate in the execution of great crimes.
The improvident spirit, if it considers malicious advice, soon realizes the solitude in which it finds itself within the circles of disastrous consequences.

Whoever acts correctly will find, in the happy results of their initiatives, floods of companions wishing to share their victories; however, very rarely will they feel the presence of someone sharing their afflictions in the days of temporary defeat.
Such a reality induces the creature to the most insistent precaution.
Judas's bitter experience repeats itself with the majority of men every day, albeit in other sectors.

There are those who hear delusive insinuations of malice or indiscipline concerning interior tranquility, family matters, and common work. Sometimes man breathes in peace, carrying out the tasks required of him; however, he is reached by the counsel of envy or despair and gets disturbed by false perspectives, inadvertently entering dark and ungrateful labyrinths. When he recognizes the error of brain or heart, he turns anxiously to the counselors of the previous day, but the inferior world, echoing the observation to Judas, exclaims mockingly: — “What is that to us? You see to it!”

messages.title: God Does Not Forsake
paragraphs: “And I gave her time to repent of her sexual immorality, and she did not repent.” — (REVELATION, 2:21)
If the Apocalypse is full of deep symbols, this does not prevent us from examining its expressions, compatible with our understanding, extracting lessons capable of expanding our spiritual progress.
The mentioned verse provides an idea of the long-suffering of the Almighty in considering the flaws and defections of transgressive children.

Many people insist on the rigidity and irrevocability of determinations of divine origin, however, we must recognize that hearts inclined to such an interpretation still cannot analyze the sublime essence of love that erases dark debts and makes a new day dawn on the horizons of the soul.
