If among earthly judges there are fraternal provisions, such as freedom on probation, would the celestial tribunal be constituted by harsher and more inflexible intelligences?

The Father's House is much more generous than any figure of magnanimity presented so far in the world by religious thought. In its abundant barns, there are loans and moratoria, concessions of time and resources that the most vigorous human imagination will never calculate.

The Almighty provides gifts to all, and, presently, it is advisable for earthly man to meditate on the resources granted to him by Heaven for repentance, seeking to renew himself in the paths of good.

The prisoners of the conception of implacable justice ignore the powerful aids of the Almighty, which manifest themselves through a thousand different ways; however, those who seek their own enlightenment through universal love know that God always gives and that it is necessary to learn to receive.

messages.title: The Gospel and Woman
paragraphs: “So husbands ought to love their own wives as their own bodies; he who loves his wife loves himself.” — PAUL (Ephesians, 5:28)

Often, the apostle to the Gentiles has been accused of excessive severity toward the feminine element. In some passages of the letters he addressed to the churches, Paul proposed austere measures that, in a way, shocked countless apprentices. Few disciples noticed, in the energy of his words, the mobilization of Christ's resources to strengthen the defense of women and the patrimonies of elevation concerning them.

With Jesus, legitimate feminism began. Not the one that fills the hands of its proponents with colored banners of the world's political ideologies, but the one that traces superior and sanctifying guidelines in their hearts.

In the most rigorous environments regarding religious faith, such as Judaism before the Master, woman was no more than merchandise condemned to captivity. Eminent figures, such as David and Solomon, could not escape the abuses of their time in this regard.

The Gospel, however, inaugurates a new era for feminine hopes. In it we see the consecration of the Holy Mother, the sublime conversion of Magdalene, the dedication of Lazarus's sisters, the self-sacrificing spirit of the ladies of Jerusalem who accompanied the Lord until the final moment. Since Jesus, we observe a growing respect on Earth for the feminine mission. Paul of Tarsus was the consolidator of this regenerative movement. Despite the harsh energy marking his words, he sought to lift woman from her degraded condition, entrusting her to man as a mother, sister, wife, or daughter, associated with his destinies and, as a creature of God, equal to him.

messages.title: Sex
paragraphs: “I know and am convinced by the Lord Jesus that there is nothing unclean of itself; but to him who considers anything to be unclean, to him it is unclean.” — PAUL (Romans, 14:14)
When Paul of Tarsus wrote this observation to the Romans, he referred to food, which at the time represented an object of arid discussions between Gentiles and Jews.
In passing days, the act of eating no longer awakens dangerous polemics, however, we can take the verse and project it onto other sectors of false opinion.

Let us look at sex, for example. No department of terrestrial activity suffers greater slanders. Fundamentally blind in spirit, man, generally speaking, still fails to discover therein one of the most sublime motives of his existence. Some of the most beautiful achievements in the planetary struggle, such as the approach of souls in fatherhood and motherhood, the creation and reproduction of forms, the extension of life, and precious stimuli to work and regeneration, were provided to creatures by the Lord through sexual emotions; nevertheless, men disparage the “holy place,” populating its altars with the phantoms of debauchery.
Sex made the home and created the name of mother; however, human selfishness gave it in return absurd experimentations of animality, organizing cruel trials for itself.
The Father offered the sanctuary to His children, but incomprehension constituted their offering. This is why painful and distressing romances spread across all the continents of Earth.

Even so, plunged into deplorable deviations, man asks for sex education, demanding its programs. Yes, such programs can be useful; however, only when the holy notion of the divinity of the creative power is spread, because, as long as there is filth in the heart of whoever analyzes or teaches, the methods will be nothing more than equally filthy things.

messages.title: This Is the Message
paragraphs: “For this is the message that you heard from the beginning, that we should love one another.” — (1 JOHN, 3:11)

All over the world we feel enormous restlessness for new messages from Heaven. Dynamic forces of thought insist on receiving modern expressions of old truths, rehearsing different mental creations. We notice, however, that art seeks new experimentations and populates itself with negative images, that politics invents ideologies and unprecedented processes of governing and dilutes the course of destructive war, that science seeks to take higher flights and institutes theories dissolving concord and well-being.
Large religious factions perform heroic work in demonstrating the eternity of life, begging for spectacular signs of the invisible realm for ordinary man.

Let us agree that there will always be benefit in the elevated aspirations of the human spirit when it sincerely seeks vibrations of a divine nature; however, we need to recognize that while there are countless substantial, edifying, and enlightened messages on Earth, the greatest and most precious of all, since the beginning of planetary organization, is that of fraternal solidarity in “love one another.”
This is the primordial recommendation. Feeling it, each disciple can examine, in the circles of daily struggle, the index of understanding they already possess concerning Divine Designs.
Even if this or that brother has not yet understood it, begin the execution of the paternal counsel within yourself.
Love always. Do all good. Begin by cherishing those who do not understand you, convinced that they will make you better all the faster.

messages.title: Precisely for This Reason
paragraphs: “I have not written to you because you do not know the truth, but because you know it.” — (1 John, 2:21)
The increasingly intensive exchange between the so-called “living” and “dead” constitutes a great event for evangelical organizations in general.
It is not merely an achievement for the Spiritist school; it belongs to the communities of all Christianity.
For now, we note protests of organized dogmatism here and there; however, the revival of the truth demands it.
Every acquisition has its price, and any renewal encounters spontaneous obstacles.
The day will come when the various subdivisions of evangelism will comprehend the divine purpose of the new covenant.
The movement of spiritual exchange between the two spheres is increasingly expanded. The devotion of the disembodied attracts the attention of the embodied.
The Lord permitted a worldwide Pentecost for the readjustment of eternal reality.

It is worth noting, however, that the moving and invigorating voices from Beyond commonly repeat old formulas of Revelation and recall the past of terrestrial Wisdom, in order to extract a more respectable conceptualization regarding life.
It is at this point that we recall the words of John, sincerely asking: do the “dead” communicate with the “living” because men are ignorant of the truth?
Not at all. If those who depart speak once more to those who remain, it is because the latter know the way of redemption with Jesus, but they are neither heartened nor decided to tread it.

messages.title: Keep the Pattern
paragraphs: “Hold fast the pattern of sound words.” — PAUL (2 Timothy, 1:13)

Distribute the resources that Providence has directed to your industrious hands; however, do not forget that the comforting word to the afflicted represents the direct service of your heart in the sowing of good.
The bread of the body is an alms for which you will always receive just reward, but the friendly smile is a blessing for eternity.
Send messengers to fraternal succor; nevertheless, do not fail, at least once in a while, to visit the sick brother and listen to him in person.
The dispatch of aid is a kindness that will win you sympathy, yet direct intervention in supporting the needy will grant you spiritual preparation ahead of your own struggles.

Ascend the tribune and teach the redeeming path to your fellow beings; however, interrupt the lectures from time to time in order to heed the lament of a companion in human experience, even when it is a child of despair or ignorance, so that you do not lose your sense of proportion on your march.

Cultivate the flowers in the private garden of your dearest affections, because, without the experimental flowerbed, it is very difficult to tend the noble and intensive crops, but do not systematically flee from the human forest, out of fear of the worms and monsters that populate it, since it is imperative that you prepare to advance within it later.
In the circles of life, do not forget the need for teaching engraved within yourself.

Just as you cannot take individual nourishment through a substitute, nor can you learn a lesson by keeping its characters in someone else's memory, you will not manage to appear before the Supreme Forces of Wisdom and Love with achievements and victories that have not been lived and conquered by yourself. Therefore, “keep” with you “the pattern of sound words.”

messages.title: Avoid Contending
paragraphs: “And a servant of the Lord must not quarrel.” — PAUL (2 Timothy, 2:24)
Flee from those who seek strife in the service of the Lord.

They are not looking for divine light for the heart. They merely dispute praise and prominence in the realm of transient considerations. Analyzing the sacred letters, they do not attract the resources necessary for their own enlightenment, but rather the means to make themselves prominent in inferior personalism. They combat fellow beings who do not adopt their particular primer, they lash out against services that do not maintain their direct control, they collaborate only from the apex to the base, they see no advantages except in tasks they themselves undertake. They cherish long discussions regarding the placement of a comma and waste immense days discovering the apparent contradictions of writers dedicated to the ideal of Jesus. They never have time for the services of Christian humility, being so interested in personal prominence. They always find great strangeness in conjugating the verbs to help, to forgive, and to serve. They invariably fixate on the imperfect zone of humanity and bring scourges in their hands out of the bad taste of whipping. They contend about all the particularities of the evangelical edifice, and when prospects of constructive agreement arise, they create new motives for disturbance.
Those who incorporate themselves into the Saving Gospel out of a spirit of contention are among the greatest and most subtle adversaries of the Kingdom of God.
The disciple's vigilance is indispensable so that they do not get lost in the delirium of harsh and useless words.

We are not called to quarrel, but rather to serve and learn with the Master; nor were we called to the enthronement of the “self,” but rather to fulfill the higher designs in the construction of the Divine Kingdom within us.

messages.title: With Ardent Love
paragraphs: “And above all things have fervent love for one another.” — PETER (1 Peter, 4:8)
It is not enough to proclaim virtue in favor of the establishment of the Divine Kingdom among creatures.
An excessively debated problem — a more delayed solution...
Let us individually heed the apostolic warning and fill ourselves with fervent love for one another.
Speaking well, teaching accurately, and believing sincerely are primary phases of service. It is imperative to work, do, and feel with Christ.
Fraternity simply advised to others builds brilliant facades that experience can consume in a minute. We urgently need to reach the substance, the essence...

Let us be understanding toward the ignorant, vigilant toward those led astray in wickedness and darkness, patient toward the sickly, serene toward the irritable, and, above all, manifest goodness toward all those whom the Master has entrusted to us for daily teachings.

Prompt reasoning, able to act with agility on Earth, can constitute a patrimony of value; however, if it lacks the heart to feel the problems, guide them, and solve them for the common good, it is easily susceptible of turning into a calculating machine.
Let us not dwell on theoretical piety. Let us seek fraternal, spontaneous, ardent, and pure love.
Celestial charity not only spreads benefits; it also radiates divine light.

messages.title: In Christian Service
paragraphs: “For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that each one may receive the things done in the body, according to what he has done, whether good or bad.” — PAUL (2 Corinthians, 5:10)
There is no lack of those who see in Spiritism a mere field of phenomenal experimentation, without any moral significance for creatures.
Many learners of the Consoling Doctrine, thus, limit themselves to laboratory investigations or confine themselves to philosophical discussions.
It is imperative to recognize, however, that there are as many categories of disembodied men as there are of embodied ones.
Disputatious, frivolous, rebellious, and fickle entities transit everywhere. Furthermore, unknowns and problems arise for the inhabitants of both Planes.

In view of such reasons, the proponents of the world's effective progress, distanced from physical life, strive for Spiritism with Jesus, converting our exchange into a factor of sanctifying spirituality.
We believe that one should not attack another circle of life when we are not interested in improving the personality within the one where we breathe.
It is not worth researching resources that do not dignify us.

This is why for us, who suppose we have brought our hearts awake to the responsibility of living, Spiritism does not express a simple conviction of immortality: it is a climate of service and edification.

It is useless to keep the certainty of the soul's survival beyond death without terrestrial preparation in the direction of spiritual life. And in this effort of qualification, we have no wiser or more loving guide than Christ.
Only in the light of His sublime lessons is it possible to readjust the path, renew the mind, and purify the heart.
Not everything that is admirable is divine.
Not everything that is great is respectable.
Not everything that is beautiful is holy.
Not everything that is pleasant is useful.
The problem is not merely one of knowing. It is one of self-reform for the expansion of good.

Let us, therefore, become attached to the felt and lived Gospel, understanding the imperative of our inner enlightenment, because, according to the opportune and wise word of the Apostle, “we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that each one may receive, according to what he has done in the body, whether good or bad.”

messages.title: Let the Reader Understand
paragraphs: “Whoever reads, let him understand.” — JESUS (Matthew, 24:15)

Just as creatures, in general, have converted the sacred productions of the Earth into objects of perversion of the senses, an analogous movement takes place in the world regarding the fruits of thought.
Frequently, the holiest readings are taken as emotional seasoning, destined for renewed sensations that match pernicious recreation or indifference to the most rightful obligations.
Very rarely do readers seek the reality of life. The Gospel itself has been a vast field of undignified observations for the imprudent and frivolous.
How many eyes pass over it, hurried and restless, noting deficiencies in the letter or cataloging possible errors, in order to spread sensationalism and disturbance?
They eagerly line up apparent contradictions and proceed to squander, with enormous contempt for the labor of others, the tender and bountiful plants of renewing faith.
Jesus' recommendation, however, is infinitely expressive.

It is reasonable that the reading of ignorant and animalized man represents a set of ignominious jests, but the spirit of religiosity needs to penetrate serious reading with a real attitude of elevation.

The problem for the disciple of the Gospel is not to read to achieve emotional novelties or to know Scripture to transform it into an arena of intellectual fencing, but to read to serve God, fulfilling His Divine Will.

messages.title: Watch How You Live
paragraphs: “And calling ten of his servants, he delivered to them ten minas, and said to them, ‘Do business till I come.’” — JESUS (Luke, 19:13)

With the precise maturity of reasoning, man will understand that his entire existence is a great set of spiritual businesses and that life, in itself, is nothing more than a permanent religious act, directed toward the divine duties that bind us to God.
For now, the world merely demands testimonies of faith from persons designated as holders of an essentially religious mandate.

Roman Catholics surround priests with demands, subverting their apostolate. Protestants, for the most part, attribute the most complete obligations of worship to evangelical ministers. Spiritists demand supreme demonstrations of charity and purity from doctrinal speakers and mediums, as if the light and truth of the New Revelation could constitute the exclusive patrimony of a few fallible brains.
It is urgent to consider, however, that Christian testimony in the transitory field of human struggle is the duty of all men, without distinction.
Each creature has been called by Providence to a specific sector of spiritual work on Earth.
The merchant is in the business of supply and fraternity.
The administrator remains in the business of guidance, distribution, and responsibility.
The servant was brought to the business of obedience and edification.
Terrestrial mothers and fathers were called to the business of renunciation, exemplification, and devotion.
The carpenter is manufacturing columns for the living temple of the home.
The scientist lives by providing equations of progress that improve the well-being of the world.
The cook works to feed the worker and the sage.

All men live within the Work of God, availing themselves of it to attain divine greatness one day. As usufructuaries of patrimonies that belong to the Father, they find themselves in the field of present opportunities, trading with the values of the Lord.
In reason of this truth, my friend, watch what you do and do not forget to subordinate your desires to God in the businesses entrusted to you in the world for a time.

messages.title: The Necessary Thing
paragraphs: “But one thing is needed.” — JESUS (Luke, 10:42)
You will have many businesses, near or far, but you will not be able to strip them of their character as a lesson, because death will unveil realities to you of which you do not even faintly dream...

You will administer various interests, however, you will not be able to control all angles of the service, since malice and indifference insinuate themselves into all tasks, impairing the scope of action of all missionaries of elevation.
You will amass an enormous fortune, yet you will ignore for many years to what region of life money will lead you.
You will improvise pompous speeches, however, you are unaware of the consequences of your words.
You will organize great movement around your steps, nevertheless, if you do not build something within them for legitimate good, you will tire in vain.
You will experience many sorrows, but if you do not remain vigilant in taking advantage of the struggle, your hardships will be in vain.
You will exalt the right with indignant and ardent speech, however, you are likely doing nothing more than stimulating the indiscipline and idleness of many.
“One thing is needed,” asserted the Master in His lesson to Martha, a dedicated and active cooperator.

Jesus wished to say that, above all, it is incumbent upon us to keep within ourselves an adequate attitude toward the designs of the Almighty, advancing according to the roadmap traced for us by the Divine Law. Once this “necessary thing” is accomplished, every event, every person, and every thing will adjust themselves, before our eyes, in their proper place. Without this spiritual position of attunement with the Celestial Instructor, it is very difficult for anyone to act profitably.

messages.title: In Silence
paragraphs: “Not with eyeservice, as men-pleasers, but as bondservants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart.” — PAUL (Ephesians, 6:6)
If you know, attend to the ignorant without dazzling them with your light.
If you have, help the needy without molesting them with your possession.
If you love, do not wound the beloved object with demands.
If you intend to heal, do not humiliate the sick person.
If you want to improve others, do not curse anyone.
If you teach charity, do not wear yourself in thorns, so that your touch does not lacerate those who suffer.
Be careful in the task entrusted to you by the Lord.
It is very easy to serve in plain sight. Everyone wants to do so, seeking the appreciation of men.
Difficult, however, is serving in secret, without the illusory cloak of vanity.
This is why, at all times, almost all the work of creatures is dispersive and deceptive. In general, care is taken to obtain human gratifications and honors at any cost.
You, however, my friend, learn that the sincere servant of Christ speaks little and builds increasingly with the Lord, in the divine silence of the spirit...
Go and serve. Do not let the fantasies that confuse the eyes of the flesh trouble you, nor consecrate yourself to the noises of the mouth.
Do good in silence.
Flee from personal references and let us learn to fulfill the will of God from the heart.

messages.title: With Love
paragraphs: “But above all these things put on love, which is the bond of perfection.” — PAUL (Colossians, 3:14)
Every disciple of the Gospel will need courage to tackle the services of self-redemption.
No one can dispense with the armor of faith in order to march fearlessly through storms.
The path of redemption and elevation remains full of thorns.

Work will consist of struggles, sufferings, sacrifices, sweat, and testimonies. All preparation is necessary in the chapter of endurance; however, above all this, it is indispensable that our soul be clothed with charity, which is sublime love.

Nobility of character, trust, benevolence, faith, science, penetration, gifts, and possibilities are precious threads, but love is the divine loom that will interweave them, weaving the tunic of spiritual perfection.
Discipline and education, school and culture, effort and work are flowers and fruits on the tree of life, yet love is the eternal root.
But how shall we love in daily service?
Let us renew ourselves in the spirit of the Lord and understand our fellow beings.
Let us help in silence, understanding each one's situation, tempering goodness with energy, and fraternity with justice.
Let us heed the suggestion of love at every step along the evolutionary path. Whoever loves, understands; and whoever understands, works for a better world.

messages.title: Multitudes
paragraphs: “I have compassion on the multitude.” — JESUS (Mark, 8:2)
Spiritually educated individuals have always been greatly indebted to the multitude.
Few men, however, understand this imperative of spiritual laws.

In general, the steward of earthly possibilities, merely instructed in worldly culture, avoids the common masses instead of helping them. He exploits their passions, maintains their ignorance, and often steals their opportunity for progress. He draws up laws so that they pay the heaviest taxes, creating wars of extermination in which they must contribute the highest tributes of blood. Organized priesthood almost always imposes shadows upon them, while philosophy and science offer them mocking smiles.
In all times and political situations, the people count on few friends and legions of adversaries.
Above all human possibilities, however, the multitude has the Divine Friend.

Jesus continues to work. He who walked the planet among fishermen and proletarians, the crippled and the blind, tired old men and afflicted mothers, turns to the suffering mob and feeds their hope, just like at the moment of the multiplication of the loaves.
Remember, my friend, that you are an integral part of the earthly multitude.
The Lord observes what you do. Do not steal the bread of life; strive to multiply it.

messages.title: To the Disciples
paragraphs: “But we preach Christ crucified, to the Jews a stumbling block and to the Greeks foolishness.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 1:23)
Modern life, with its brilliant realities, teaches the religious communities of Christianity that to preach is to reveal the greatness of Jesus' principles in one's daily actions.
The man who enters the strange territory of speeches, without deeds corresponding to the elevation of the word, exposes himself more and more to ridicule and denial.

For many centuries, the movement of utilitarian philosophies has prevailed. And even now, there is no shortage of guides who contemplate the construction of egotistical palaces based on personal magnetism, nor of psychologists who publicly teach the subtle exploitation of the masses.

It is within this dark picture of Earth's intellectual development that the apprentices of Christ are exponents of the edifying philosophy of renunciation and goodness, revealing in their isolated works the divine experience of Him who preferred crucifixion to a pact with evil.

New disciples, therefore, are emerging beyond the organized priesthood. Brothers to the suffering, the simple, and the needy, Christian Spiritists encounter terrible obstacles in the intoxicated culture of the century and in the utilitarian spirit of comfortable ideas.

Nearly two thousand years ago, Paul of Tarsus alluded to the scandal that the attitude of the disciples spread among the Jews and the false impression of madness it awakened in the minds of the Greeks.

Present times are the very ones Jesus declared had arrived on the planet; and the Jews and Greeks, updated today into dishonest businesspeople and vain intellectuals, continue in the same position as at the beginning. Among them emerges the continuer of the Master, transmitting His teachings with the verb sanctified by testimonial actions.
Difficulties, sarcasms, and conflicts arise... The faithful apprentice, however, is not frightened.

The commercialism of avarice will remain with scandal, and poisoned instruction will linger with the imbalances inherent to it. He, however, will move forward, loving, exemplifying, and educating with the immortal Liberator.

messages.title: Marks
paragraphs: “From now on let no one trouble me, for I bear in my body the marks of the Lord Jesus.” — PAUL (Galatians, 6:17)
All human achievements bear their own mark.

Houses, books, articles, medicines—everything displays a sign of identification to attentive eyes. If a similar measure is useful in the law of using transitory objects, the same principle cannot be subtracted from the cataloging of everything related to eternal life.
Jesus likewise possesses His own signs. The imagery used by Paul of Tarsus in his exhortations to the Galatians can be extended.
The marks of Christ are not only those of the cross, but also those of His activity in ordinary experience.
In every situation, man can reveal a manifestation of the Divine Master.

Jesus provided educational standards in all the particularities of His passage through the world. The Gospel presents Him in the most diverse settings: beside work, simplicity, sin, poverty, joy, pain, glorification, and martyrdom. His attitude in every position of life marked a new trait of conduct for the apprentices.
Every day, therefore, the disciple can find resources to highlight their most common actions with the records of Jesus.

When each day ends, review the small experiences you shared along the ordinary road. Observe the signs with which you marked your acts, remembering that the mark of Christ is, fundamentally, that of self-sacrifice for the good of all.

messages.title: The Light Always Follows
paragraphs: “And their words seemed to them like idle tales, and they did not believe them.” — (LUKE, 24:11)
The perplexity that arose on the day of the Lord's Resurrection is still the same in passing times, whenever the divine nature, invisible to the common eye of men, manifests its glorious messages.
The devoted women who went on a pilgrimage of love to the Master's tomb have always found successors. However, Peters willing to rise up to investigate the truth are very rare.
In all times, transmitters of news from beyond the tomb have journeyed on Earth just as they do today.
Distorted religious schools, however, have only on rare occasions accepted the valuable assistance offered to them.

In past times, almost all instruments of spiritual revelation were categorized as witches and burned in the public square, and even today they are considered demented, visionary, and sorcerers. This is because the majority of companions on the human journey live clinging to the inferior interests of a few moments, and the words of immortalist truth have always seemed to them sheer nonsense. Handed over to the ephemeral, they do not believe in the expansion of life within infinity and eternity, but the light of the Resurrection always continues, inspiring its still-misunderstood missionaries.

messages.title: Lift Up Your Eyes
paragraphs: “Behold, I say to you, lift up your eyes and look at the fields, for they are already white for harvest!” — JESUS (John, 4:35)
The world is full of labors connected to the stomach.
Earthly existence remains overflowing with emotions related to sex.
No one disputes the sacred foundation of both; however, we cannot stall in one expression or the other.
We must lift our eyes and survey higher zones. We need to contemplate the harvest of new values, tending to our own granary.
Life is not summarized by nutrition phenomena, nor simply by the continuity of the species.
Laborious service of spiritual illumination requires man. Valuable knowledge calls him to higher spheres.

Eternal truths proclaim that happiness is not a myth, that life does not constitute merely the short period of carnal manifestations on Earth, that peace is the treasure of the children of God, and that divine greatness is the marvelous destination of creatures; however, to receive such high gifts it is indispensable to raise our eyes, elevate our understanding, and sanctify our reasoning.
It is imperative to raise the sublime lamp of faith above the shadows.

Most beloved brother, who remains under the divine tree of life, do not focus solely on the fruits of missed opportunity that you left to rot in abandonment... Do not imprison yourself in the inferior field, contemplating sorrows, failures, disappointments!... Look up!... Notice the immortal fronds, swaying to the breath of Divine Providence! Give yourself to the labors of the harvest and observe that, although the roots still linger attached to the soil, the verdant branches, full of substantial fruits, advance into Infinity toward the Heavens.

messages.title: What Do We Do with the Master?
paragraphs: “What then shall I do with Jesus who is called Christ?” — PILATE (Matthew, 27:22)
In the circles of Christianity, Pilate's question is of singular importance.
What do men do with the Divine Master in the field of daily lessons?
The idle try to turn Him into an oracle that satisfies their aspirations of least effort.
The vain seek to transform Him into an exhibition gallery through which they can make a permanent display of inferior personalism.
The foolish improperly call upon Him to approve the madness to which they surrender, far from dignified work.
Large ranks follow in His footsteps, like the crowd that accompanied Him on the mountain, interested only in the multiplication of loaves for the stomach.
Others approach Him, seeking to torment Him, like the shrewd Pharisees, begging for “signs from heaven.”
Numerous people visit Him, imitating Jairus's gesture, begging for blessings, believing and disbelieving at the same time.
Various apprentices listen to His teachings like Judas, examining the best way to establish their own domination.
Several hearts observe Him with sympathy, but at the first opportunity, like Zebedee's wife, they inquire about the distribution of heavenly places.
Many others accompany Him along the road, like countless admirers of Galilee who esteemed His benefits and consolations while detesting His crystalline truths.
Some imitate the beneficiaries of Judea, raising folded hands at the moment of advantages, and fleeing in terror from sacrifice and testimony.
The vast majority proceed in Pilate's fashion, solemnly inquiring what to do with Jesus and ending up crucifying Him with carefree disregard for duty and responsibility.
Few imitate Simon Peter who, following the illumination at Pentecost, follows Him unconditionally unto death.
Rare are those who copy Paul of Tarsus, who rises on the path of error, setting out on the road to redemption through obstacles and stonings, until the end of the struggle.
It is not enough to make Christ Jesus the benefactor who heals and protects. It is indispensable to transform Him into a permanent standard of life, as the daily example and model.

messages.title: Have You Heard?
paragraphs: “These things I have spoken to you, that you should not be made to stumble.” — JESUS (John, 16:1)
Before returning to the Resplendent Spheres, the Divine Master did not leave us helpless regarding warnings for the work to be done.
When the spirit matured in the comprehension of the redemptive work surrenders to the field of evangelical service, it cannot dispense with the Lord's prior information.
It is indispensable to hear them so as not to stumble within the framework of common obligations.

The Master's word clarified that as long as the domination of ignorance in the world endured, the legitimate cultivators of the principles of spiritual renewal brought by Him would not be viewed with sympathy. They would be pursued relentlessly by the forces of shadow. They would appear before condemnation tribunals to face false accusations from those still incapable of greater understanding. They would endure taunts from family members strangers to interior illumination. They would suffer expulsion from temples organized by the pragmatics of literalist sects. They would hear gratuitous libels from intelligences dedicated to mocking divine truths. They would live like peaceful sheep among famished wolves. They would sustain incessant war against evil. They would fall into clumsy traps. They would contemplate the growth of weeds alongside wheat. They would identify the ephemeral progress of the wicked. They would carry the marks of the cross with them. They would experience the misunderstanding of many. They would feel loneliness in grave hours. They would see calumny, stoning, and ingratitude close up...
The Divine Master, therefore, did not leave His companions and continuers unadvised.

He offered no apprentice on Earth a crown of roses without thorns. He promised them edifying struggle, educational work, rectifying situations, opportunities for illumination through the greatness of sacrifice that produces elevation and the spirit of service that establishes light and peace.

It is important, therefore, for all those who have matured their reasoning in earthly struggle, to vividly remember Christ's warnings in the sector of evangelical edification, so they do not stumble in the difficult tests of the individual plane.

messages.title: Troubled and Perplexed
paragraphs: “We are hard-pressed on every side, yet not crushed; we are perplexed, but not in despair.” — PAUL (2 Corinthians, 4:8)
Since the earliest days of the Gospel, Jesus' loyal followers have known tribulations and perplexities because they remain in the faith.

When they gathered in Jerusalem, remembering the Master in the services of the Divine Kingdom, they experienced stoning, torture, exile, and the confiscation of property; when they instituted apostolic works in Rome, teaching truth and fraternal love, they were entrusted to the lions of the circus, bloody spectacles, and martyrdom stakes.
Since then, they have experienced painful surprises in all parts of the world.

The medieval age, enveloped in shadows, attempted to ignore Christ's mission and lit bonfires for them, leading them besides to unexpected and unknown torments through the political and religious tribunals of the Inquisition.

And even today, while they pray trustfully, exemplifying evangelical love, they witness the progress of the wicked and suffer the domination of the vain of all stripes. While the bad and indifferent triumph in earthly comforts, they are relegated to difficulties and stumbles, facing the simplest situations.
Despite the undeniable evolution of law in the world, they are still called to account for the good they do and watched strictly because of the comforting truth they teach.

But all faithful disciples know, with Paul of Tarsus, that "in everything they will be troubled and perplexed," yet they will never surrender to anguish and discouragement. They know that the Divine Master was the Great Troubled One and learned from Him that from perplexity, affliction, martyrdom, and death, the soul transfers to the Eternal Resurrection.

messages.title: Before the Multitude
paragraphs: “And others mocking said, ‘They are full of new wine.’ ” — (ACTS, 2:13)
The lesson gathered by Jesus' disciples at Pentecost is still a living symbol for all Gospel apprentices before the multitude.
The revelation of eternal life continues in all directions.

That “sound as of a rushing mighty wind” and those “cloven tongues of fire” referred to in the apostolic description descend to this day upon the continuers of Christ among the children of all nations.
The expressions of Pentecost expand in all countries, despite the antagonistic vibrations of darkness.
However, for thousands of listeners and observers, there function only a few rare apostles entrusted with preserving the divine light.

Indeed, innumerable are those who, consciously or unconsciously, receive the benefits of celestial revelation; however, there are not a few mockers of all times, disposed to irreverence and irony before the truth.

To these, the loyal followers of the Master are intoxicated and mad. They do not understand the humility that consecrates itself to good, the fraternity that gives without unreasonable demands, and the faith that always trusts despite storms.

It is indispensable not to be surprised by the harassment of these poor unconscious ones if you are effectively disposed to serve the Lord of Life. They will surround your work, accusing you of being drunk; they will criticize your attitudes, calling you a coward; they will listen to your words of love while keeping irony in their mouths. To them, your selflessness will be degradation, your renunciation will signify incapacity, and your faith will be interpreted as madness.
Do not hesitate, however, in the spirit of service. You remain, like the first apostles, in the great public squares where men and women, ignorant and wise, old and children crowd together...
Perfect your reception qualities wherever you may be, because the Lord has called you as an interpreter of His Voice, even if the wicked mock you.

messages.title: In the Same Dishes
paragraphs: “And He answered and said, ‘He who dipped his hand with Me in the dish will betray Me.’ ” — (MATTHEW, 26:23)
Every occurrence in Jesus' mission is imbued with deep symbolic expression.

An attack by strangers could hardly provoke the painful Calvary. The judges of the Sanhedrin personally were not qualified to handle the sinister matter, nor could the Master's gratuitous accusers carry out the infamous trial by themselves.
Someone had to falter and betray themselves. Ingratitude is not a plant from a contrary field.
The most formidable transgressor in all good works is always the wayward friend, the frivolous companion, and the indifferent brother.

Despite the respect we owe to the redeemed Judas, it is worth remembering the lesson in favor of vigilance service—not only for disciples in apprenticeship so they do not fail, but also for disciples under trial so they may exemplify with the Lord, understanding, acting, and forgiving.

In the lines of Christian work, it is not too much to expect great struggles and great tests, considering, however, that the greatest anguishes will not come from adversary circles, but precisely from the most intimate sphere, when restlessness and revolt, levity and imprudence penetrate the hearts of those we love most.

Generally speaking, calumny and error, defection and gall do not come from our declared opponents, but rather from those who feed with us in the same dishes of life. Let every disciple keep themselves fully informed regarding such truth, so that we may know how to imitate the Lord in the great days.

messages.title: World peace and Christ's peace
paragraphs: “Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you.” — JESUS (John, 14.27)
It is essential not to confuse the world's peace with Christ's peace.
The calm of the lower plane may be nothing more than stagnation.
The serenity of the highest spheres means divine work, on the way to Immortal Light.
The world manages to provide many agreements and arrangements in this field, but only the Lord can grant true peace to the spirit.

In the circles of the flesh, the peace of nations usually represents the provisional silence of bayonets; that of unconscious the wealthy is unproductive and incapable laziness; that of those who rebel, within the framework of necessary struggles, is the manifestation of sickly despair; that of systematic idlers is the flight from work; that of the arbitrary is the satisfaction of their own whims; that of the vain is the applause of ignorance; that of the vengeful is the destruction of adversaries; that of the wicked is the victory of cruelty; that of shrewd businessmen is inferior exploitation; that of those who cling to low-grade sensations is the vitiation of the senses; that of gluttons is the opulent repast of the stomach, even though there is spiritual hunger in the heart.

There are many impious, slanderous, criminal, and indifferent people who enjoy the peace of the world. They feel triumphant, fortunate, and dominant in the century. Moneyed ignorance, well-dressed vanity, and intelligent laziness will always say that they are doing very well.

Do not forget, however, that the world's peace can often be the sickly sleep of the soul. Seek, therefore, that peace of the Lord, peace that surpasses understanding, born and cultivated within the spirit, in the field of conscience and in the sanctuary of the heart.

messages.title: How do you cooperate?
paragraphs: “Now we have received, not the spirit of the world, but the spirit which is of God.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 2.12)

Reading Paul's statement, we recognize that, at all times, the sincere disciple of the Gospel is confronted by the great conflict between the suggestions of the lower region and the inspirations of the higher spheres of life.

The “spirit of the world” is the collection of all our sinful actions, over centuries of incessant experiences; the “spirit which is of God” is the constant appeal of the Forces of Good, which renew our opportunity to progress each day, in order to discover the eternal glory to which Infinite Goodness has destined us.
God is the Father of Creation. Everything, fundamentally, belongs to Him.
Every field of work belongs to the Lord, every service rendered will be delivered to the Lord, but not all actions that take place in ordinary activity come from the Lord.

Divine creation and human collaboration coexist in earthly workshops, whatever they may be. And cooperators arise who use stewardship to exercise cruel domination, who take advantage of intelligence to intensify the ignorance of others, or who value the helpful hoe, not to cultivate the field, but to use it in crime.
The scientist, in the comfort of the laboratory, and the rude sailor, under the storm, are working for the Lord; however, for the happiness of each one, it is important to know how they are working.

Let us remember that there is divine service within us and outside of us. For the sake of our own redemption, it is fair to inquire whether we are cooperating with the inferior spirit that dominated us until yesterday or whether we have already grown fond of the renewing spirit of the Eternal Father.

messages.title: Tares
paragraphs: “Let both grow together until the harvest: and in the time of harvest I will say to the reapers, Gather ye together first the tares, and bind them in bundles to burn them.” — JESUS (Matthew, 13.30)
When Jesus recommended the simultaneous growth of the tares and the wheat, He meant nothing less than to demonstrate sublime celestial tolerance within the framework of life's experiences.

The Master never subtracted man's opportunities for growth and sanctification, and in this sense, evil itself, originating from less-than-worthy passions, is patiently examined by His infinite love, without being destroyed right away.

It is important to consider, therefore, that the tares do not grow due to laxity on the part of the Divine Plowman, but rather because the optimism of the Celestial Sower never loses hope in the final victory of good.

Christ's field is a region of incessant and intense activity. Astonishing tasks mobilize heroic phalanges; however, despite the dedication and vigilance of the workers, tares appear, threatening the service.
Jesus, however, commands the application of defensive processes based on enlightenment and mercy. Time and the Lord's blessing act slowly, and lower purposes are transubstantiated.

Ordinary man does not yet possess adequate vision to identify the renewing work. Many thorny or sterile plants are modified in their essential nature by the loving filters of the Administrator of the Harvest, who uses new affections, different situations, unexpected stimuli, or tender responsibilities that speak to the heart; however, if the harvest season arrives, after a time of expectation and observation, the elimination of the tares in bundles then becomes necessary.
The harvest is not the same for all the seeds of the Earth. Each species has its day, its season.

This is why, when the right time appears, each man and each collectivity is required to extinguish the tares, when Jesus' transforming processes have been received in vain. At that moment, we see the individual or the people agitating through various afflictions and cataclysms, crying out in alarm and for help, as if they were in the shadows of an inexorable shipwreck. However, it is merely the destruction of our ruinous or useless acquisitions. And, seeing that the tares are bound in bundles, a sorrow never comes alone.

messages.title: Let us work in Christ
paragraphs: “And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him.” — PAUL (Colossians, 3.17)
Waiting for results, after admittedly elevated expressions and actions, can cause enormous damage on our journey toward the Supreme Light.
While we await external manifestations of gratitude or improvement, we are susceptible to paralyzing our own obligations, diverting ourselves into the dark terrain of backbiting or hasty judgment.
As much as possible, let us distribute good, surrendering our activities to Christ, the divine donor of earthly benefits.

It is dangerous to establish standards of recognition for other people's hearts, even when they are precious jewels from our spiritual casket. In our anxious expectation to behold the sum of our noble gestures, we may appear selfish, ungrateful, and slanderous.
Let us copy the sensible orchardist. Let us prepare the earth, helping it and fertilizing it. Next, let us cast valuable seeds and seedlings into the soil.

The most important service will fall to the Lord of Life. He will take care of the favorable circumstances in space and time, developing our sowing, or He will annul our service through natural processes, postponing the fulfillment of our desires for reasons we do not know.
The balanced orchardist works with titles of sincere trust in Heaven, completely unaware of whether he will reap flowers or fruits from his works within the framework of human immediatism.
He relies, however, on Divine Providence and works constantly for the benefit of all.
Thus, let us fulfill our task, no matter how high or how humble, working invariably in the name of Jesus. By His side, may the glory of love and the pleasure of service be ours.

messages.title: Hereby we know
paragraphs: “Hereby know we the spirit of truth, and the spirit of error.” — (1 John, 4.6)
When we know how to maintain our connection with Divine peace, despite all human disturbances, forgiving as many times as necessary the companion who hurts us;
forgetting evil in order to build good;
sincerely supporting those who annoy us;
cooperating spiritually, through action and prayer, for the benefit of those who persecute and slander us;
forgetting our private desires to serve for the good of all;
keeping faith in the Supreme Power as an inextinguishable light in the heart;
persevering in constructive goodness, even though a thousand strokes of wickedness besiege us;
denying ourselves so that the divine blessing shines around our footsteps;
carrying our difficulties as celestial gifts;
receiving adversaries as instructors;
blessing the struggles that perfect our soul before the Greater Sphere;
converting earthly experience into granaries of joy for Eternity;
discerning opportunities to serve everywhere;
understanding and helping always, without the concern of being understood and helped;
loving our fellow men as we have been loved by the Lord, without expectation of reward; then we will know the spirit of truth within us, illuminating our path toward divine redemption.

messages.title: Open the door
paragraphs: “And when he had said this, he breathed on them, and saith unto them, Receive ye the Holy Ghost.” — (JOHN, 20.22)
Deeply expressive are Jesus' words to the disciples in the first manifestations after Calvary.
Appearing at the companions' meeting, He spreads over them His spirit of love and life, exclaiming: “Receive the Holy Ghost.”

Why didn't the Lord's blessings automatically bind themselves to the learners? Why didn't Jesus purely and simply transmit His divine power to His successors? He, who had distributed gifts of health and blessings of peace, recommended that the disciples receive the divine spiritual gifts. Why not impose such an obligation?
It is because the Master would not violate the sanctuary of each child of God, not even out of love.
Each spirit keeps its own treasure and will open its sacred doors to communion with the Eternal Father.

The Creator offers the seed the sun and the rain, the climate and the field, defense and fertilizer, the care of the farmers and the blessing of the seasons, but the seed must germinate by itself, rising toward the sunlight.

Man likewise receives the Sun of Providence and the rain of gifts, the facilities of cooperation and the field of opportunity, the defense of love and the fertilizer of suffering, the affection of Jesus' messengers and the blessing of diverse experiences; however, we are constrained to break through the lower envelopes by ourselves, rising toward the Divine Light.

The Master's inspirations and designs remain around our soul, suggesting useful modifications, inducing us to the legitimate understanding of life, illuminating us through the higher consciousness; however, it is up to us whether or not to open the internal door to them.

Let us therefore cease the war of our lower creations from the past and surrender ourselves, each day, to the new realizations of God instituted in our favor, persevering in receiving along the path the gifts of constant renewal, in Christ, for eternal life.

messages.title: Essential charity
paragraphs: “And this is love, that we walk after his commandments. This is the commandment, That, as ye have heard from the beginning, ye should walk in it.” — JOHN (2 John, 6)
In all places and situations of life, charity will always be the divine source of the Lord's blessings.

Whoever gives bread to the hungry and water to the thirsty, medicine to the sick and light to the ignorant, is collaborating in the edification of the Divine Kingdom, in any sector of existence or religious faith to which they have been called.
The compassionate and fraternal voice that enlightens the spirit is sister to the hands that feed the body.

Assistance, medication, and teaching constitute holy modalities of generous charity that execute the programs of good. They are different garments of a single virtue. They conjugate and complete each other in a noble and worthy whole.

No one can assist another efficiently unless they have sought their own edification; no one will medicate profitably unless they have acquired the spirit of goodwill toward those in need, and no one will teach securely unless they possess acts of love toward their neighbor in their favor, regarding fraternal understanding and assistance.

Because of this, the smallest manifestations of charity, born of the sincere disposition to serve with Jesus, are sacred and indisputable activities. Everywhere, they will always be sublime lights of fraternity, disseminating joy, hope, gratitude, comfort, and blessed intercessions.

Before, however, the charity that manifests outwardly in the varied sectors of life, let us practice essential charity, without which we cannot effect our own edification and redemption. This refers to the charity of thinking, speaking, and acting according to the teachings of the Divine Master in the Gospel. It is the charity of truly living in Him so that He may live in us. Without this, we can carry out great external services, achieve valuable intercessions in our favor, and spread remarkable works of stone, but within ourselves, in moments of supreme testimony in faith, we will be empty and desolate, like beggars of light.

messages.title: Sublime recommendation
paragraphs: “Howbeit Jesus suffered him not, but saith unto him, Go home to thy friends, and tell them how great things the Lord hath done for thee, and hath had compassion on thee.” — (MARK, 5.19)
Eminently expressive is Jesus' word to the demoniac who had recovered his balance at the touch of His divine love.
That sick man who, after healing, felt tormented by incomprehension, begged the Lord to allow him to stay by His side to enjoy His sublime company.
Jesus, however, does not allow it and recommends that he seek out his own people to announce the benefits received.
How many disciples copy the attitude of this sick man who had himself accompanied by a legion of wicked spirits!

With eyes open to the truth and heart touched by new light, at the first difficulty on the path they intend to flee the world, hungry for rest by the side of the Nazarene, forgetting that the Master works unceasingly.
The problem of Christ's apprentice is not to conquer celestial holidays, but to attend to the active services to which he has been called, in any place, situation, age, and time.

If you have received the light of the Lord, my friend, go serve the Master among your own people, those bound to your walk. If you have no direct family, you have an indirect one. If you have no relatives, you have neighbors and companions. Announce the Savior's benefits by displaying your own healing. Whoever demonstrates their own renewal in Christ qualifies to cooperate in the spiritual renewal of others. As for your own well-being, you will be called to it at the opportune moment.

messages.title: Science and temperance
paragraphs: “And to knowledge temperance; and to temperance patience; and to patience godliness.” — (2 Peter, 1.6)
Whoever knows needs to be sober. It is worthless to know in order to destroy.

Many people, upon first contacting the source of knowledge, assume contradictory attitudes. Imposing ideas, striking out here and there, such expositors of knowledge achieve nothing more than disturbance.
This is why science, in its various expressions, lends a strong hand to ruinous or useless conflicts in politics, philosophy, and religion.
Almost all the imbalances in the world originate from intemperance in those who have learned something.

Let us not forget. All science, from the humblest to the highest corner of the Earth, demands ponderation. The sanitation worker needs temperance so that his broom does not become a stumbling block, just as the statesman needs sobriety in enacting laws so as not to disturb the spirit of the multitude. And let us not forget that temperance, to achieve the desired success, cannot dispense with patience, just as patience, to demonstrate itself well, cannot flee from piety, which is always understanding and fraternal assistance.

If you know something in life, do not rush to teach like a tyrant, disparaging the achievements of others. Examine the characteristic situations of each one and try, first of all, to understand your struggling brother.

Knowing is not everything. It is necessary to do. And to do well, no man will dispense with the calm and serenity indispensable to success, nor will he disdain cooperation, which is the beloved companion of love.

messages.title: The flight
paragraphs: “And pray ye that your flight be not in the winter, neither on the sabbath day.” — JESUS (Matthew, 24.20)

Remaining in the lowest circles of nature establishes a second way of being for the soul, in which vice becomes obsessive and imperative. For someone to withdraw from such swamps of the spirit, it is imperative that they flee.
Rarely, however, will the victim manage to break free without self-discipline.
Often, it is necessary to do violence to one's own heart. Only thus will they demand new planes.
It is fair, therefore, to resort to the Master's imagery when He referred to the Planet in general, highlighting the needs of the individual.
It is advisable for every apprentice to make a profitable flight from the muddy region of life, before the “winter” arrives or the final resources of time received for human service run out.

Every man possesses, along with existence, a series of seasons and a list of days, structured on a precious calculation of probabilities. It is reasonable for the worker to take advantage of the spring of youth, the summer of physical strength, and the autumn of reflection for the great journey from the interior to the superior; however, the majority wait for the winter of old age or irremediable suffering on Earth, when the opportunity for work has ended.

The possibilities for a given experience lie exhausted. It is not the end of life, but the end of a precious concession. And, naturally, the careless servant who left for Saturday the work he should have performed on Monday will be forced to repeat the task, God knows when!

messages.title: The Blackboard
paragraphs: “And these things have I told you, that when the time shall come, ye may remember that I told you of them.” — JESUS (John, 16:4)
Jesus was referring to His own trials; however, we can likewise apply these divine concepts to ourselves, both disembodied and incarnated.
Each disciple will have their hour of revelation regarding individual progress.
Primary schools do not dispense with the customary blackboard, intended for the student's isolated demonstrations.
Before the conscientious teacher, the apprentice will show how much they have progressed, without the resources of affectionate plagiarism among companions.
Upon the dark surface, the clear chalk will faithfully define the student's firm or insecure position.

And is this not precisely what repeats itself in the vast school of the world? Man, in everyday struggles, can indefinitely rely on good friends. The Father permits such contacts so that the opportunities to learn become unrestricted; however, "that hour" eventually arrives when the individual must take the white and pure chalk of spiritual achievements, placing themselves beside the blackboard of edifying trials.

Some learners fail because they know neither how to multiply blessings nor how to divide them. They ignore how to subtract light from darkness, they sum up conflicts, and they form equations of hatred and vengeance. They forget that Jesus highlighted love, as the supreme glory, in all situations of the evangelical apostolate, and that, even on the cross, after receiving the factors of injury, persecution, irony, and contempt, He added them up on the tablet of His heart, extracting the divine equation of serenity, understanding, and forgiveness.

Oh! You who go to the blackboard of earthly activities, abandon the dark chalk of despair! Write in characters of light what you have learned from the Divine Master! Reveal your true worth! Remember that benevolent and wise instructors inspire your hands! Bless the blackboard that asks you for the chalk of sweat and tears, for beside it you may conquer the higher course!…

messages.title: Arm Yourselves
paragraphs: “Wherefore take unto you the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand.” — PAUL (Ephesians, 6:13)
The movement of faith does not provide consolations alone. To seek its sublime sources merely for comfort would be to act like children who see nothing in them but sweets.

It is indispensable to take the armor of God in the houses consecrated to divine labor. It is illogical for an adult child to approach the fatherly presence with the exclusive concern of receiving affection. The youthful mind needs to accept the constructive education offered to it, clothing itself in beneficial powers through the incessant action of good, so that the parents feel rewarded in their heroic dedication.

The thirst for tenderness throbs in all beings, yet one must not forget the work that hardens common energies, the responsibility that defines the right position, and the personal effort that ennobles the path.
In all temples of elevated religious thought, the Father is offering armor to His children.

Believers, in a praiseworthy impulse, may naturally surrender to the best affectionate expansions, but they should not forget that the Lord offers them spiritual instruments for the strength they need within the redemptive struggle; only in possession of such armor can the soul resist in the evil days of earthly experience, sustaining its own serenity in painful moments and keeping itself within the breastplate of God's firmness.

messages.title: Not Only
paragraphs: “And this I pray, that your love may abound yet more and more in knowledge and in all judgment.” — PAUL (Philippians, 1:9)
Charity is invariably sublime in its smallest manifestations; nevertheless, countless people often try to limit it, concealing its divine spirit.
Many learners believe that practicing it is merely offering material gifts to those in need of bread and shelter.
Charity, however, represents much more than that for the true disciples of the Gospel. In his letter to the Philippians, Paul offers a valuable assertion regarding the subject.
It is indispensable that the charity of the faithful Christian abounds in elevated knowledge.

A certain benefactor may distribute much bread, but if he deliberately remains in the shadows of ignorance, sectarianism, or self-worship, is he not failing in the duty of charitable assistance to himself?
Spreading good is not merely transmitting facilities of a material nature. Many machines, in modern times, distribute energy and power automatically.

Essential charity is to intensify good in all respectable forms, without forgetting the imperative of self-sublimation so that others may renew themselves for higher life, understanding that it is indispensable to conjugate, at the same rhythm, the verbs "to give and to know."

Many believers prefer only to give, and others simply circumscribe themselves to knowing; the activities of all benefactors of this kind are useful, but incomplete. Both classes can suffer from poisonous presumption.
Kindness and knowledge, bread and light, succor and illumination, feeling and conscience are divine arches that integrate the perfect circles of charity.
Not only to receive and give, but also to teach and learn.

messages.title: For This
paragraphs: “For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps.” — PETER (1 Peter, 2:21)

A high percentage of believers consider themselves immune to all suffering because, in the concept of a large part of those who accept the Christian faith, surrendering to religious formulas is to exempt oneself from struggle, running as a candidate for imperturbable beatitude.
In the estimation of many people, those who pray should not know pain.
Divine succor would resemble the protection of an earthly monarch, a donor of favors in exchange for received flattery.
The situation of Jesus' disciple is, however, very different. Christ's titles are not those of inactivity, with exemption from responsibility and effort.
All those called to evangelical work cannot forget the needs of service.
The Master naturally needs companions who trust in Him, but He will not dispense with those who prove to be faithful collaborators in His work.
Would it be fair for the debtor to stand indefinitely before the creditor's generosity, trusting always, without the slightest sign of settling the acquired debt?
Not only do men live under the law of exchange. Divine Forces base the movement of good on the same principle.

The Celestial Master truly teaches everyone the sublime lessons of life; however, it is not reasonable that every century marks the same lazy and restless students in the school benches of human experience.
It is indispensable that groups of good workers head to the zones of service, prepared for the tests of the teachings received.
Simon Peter synthesizes the work of Christians in a masterful way.
You are called for this — asserts the apostle. The simple statement indicates that loyal disciples were summoned to suffer for the good.

messages.title: Complaints
paragraphs: “Grudge not one against another, brethren, lest ye be condemned.” — (JAMES, 5:9)

Complaining has never resolved problems of an evolutionary order; nevertheless, if Gospel learners were to sum up the minutes wasted in this false system of venting, they would be astonished at the volume of time lost.
Indeed, many valuable workers do not refer to suffering and service with a spirit of repulsion toward the task entrusted to them.
Friendship and trust always authorize confidences; even in this particular, however, it is worth disciplining conversation.
The lamenting word disfigures many noble pictures along the path, besides nullifying large quotas of energy fruitlessly.

The disciple of the Gospel should, before any bitter allusion, tranquilize the internal world and ask themselves: "Why complain? Is not the sphere of struggle the field of learning? Is it not the shadow that asks for light, the pain that claims relief? Is it not evil that requests the contest of good?"
Complaining is an imperceptible vice that distracts well-intentioned people from the execution of rightful duty.
There are tiny and miraculous obligations which, carried out, would benefit entire groups; yet, a single moment of complaint is enough for them to be irremediably forgotten.

If someone or some event offers you the opportunity for fraternal assistance, do the good you can without noticing others' gratitude, and however hard the common service may seem, learn to cooperate with Christ in the solution of difficulties.

Complaining does not serve Christian fulfillment anywhere, and it complicates all problems. Remember that if you give it your tongue, it will lead you to idleness, and if you give it your ears, it will direct you to perturbation.

messages.title: Fortitude
paragraphs: “Knowing that tribulation worketh patience [fortitude].” — PAUL (Romans, 5:3)
Do you want fortitude? Do not avoid the storm.

Many people intend to strengthen themselves at the price of supplications to avoid harsh service. Once the precious opportunity to bear witness to faith arrives, believers generally enter the wide paths of escape, believing themselves to be safe. However, sooner or later, the painful occasion arises in which they go bankrupt within themselves.
They then consider themselves persecuted and abandoned. Such impressions, however, are born from the absence of internal preparation.
The improvident forget that the storm possesses certain regenerating and educational functions that must not be underestimated.
Tribulation is the storm of souls. No one should forget its benefits.

When truth shines on the path of creatures, it will be seen that obstacles and sufferings do not represent a scarecrow for men, but rather precious pictures of sublime lessons that sincere learners can never forget.
What would a child be without experience? What will a spirit be without necessity?
Afflictions, difficulties, and struggles are forces that compel the expansion of power, the widening of the path.

It is necessary that man, despite the seemingly destructive gusts of destiny, stand upright, undauntedly, marching firmly to meet the sacred objectives of life. New light will then bless his intimate sphere, leading him, from Earth, to the glorious resurrection in the spiritual Plane.
Let us listen to Paul's words and live them!
Woe to those who lie down during the storm! The debris projected from the mountain by the currents of the downpour could suffocate them, dragging them to the bottom of the abyss.

messages.title: Standard
paragraphs: “For he was a good man, and full of the Holy Ghost and of faith: and much people was added unto the Lord.” — (ACTS, 11:24)
Achieving the title of priest, in obedience to mere worldly precepts, does not represent an essentially difficult effort. The illustration of intelligence in conventional ordination will suffice.
Being a theologian or exegete does not involve major obstacles. Only cultural intellect with careful study of numbers and letters is required.
Preaching doctrine presents no significant hurdles. One asks merely for the emphasis linked to correct verbal expression.
Receiving messages from the Beyond and transmitting them to others can be the copy of the world's postal service.
Counseling those who suffer and providing external elements of illumination are services peculiar to any man who sensibly uses the word.
Soundings and research, inquiries and analyses are old labors of human curiosity.

Uniting souls to the Lord, however, is an activity for which the apostle is indispensable. Barnabas, the great cooperator of the Master in Jerusalem, presents the fundamental lines of the right standard.
Let us see the application of the teaching to our Christian task.

Everyone can transmit spiritual messages, lecture to brothers, and investigate phenomenology, but to magnetize hearts in Jesus Christ it is indispensable that we be faithful servants of good, bringing our brains full of superior inspiration and our hearts inflamed with living faith.
Barnabas enlightened many companions "because he was a good man, full of the Holy Ghost and of faith."
Let us never forget such a lesson from Acts. It is a standard we cannot forget.

messages.title: Heirs
paragraphs: “And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ.” — PAUL (Romans, 8:17)
Incomprehensibly, many religious schools, through their speakers, relegate man to the sphere of absolute wretchedness.
Pulpits, rostrums, public squares, books, and newspapers are full of tremendous accusations. The children of Earth are categorized as defendants of the ultimate penalty.

No one disputes that man, as a student growing in Universal Wisdom, has erred at all times; no one ignores that crime still obsesses, many times, the thoughts of earthly creatures; however, it is indispensable to re-establish essential truth. If many souls remain fallen, God daily renews their opportunity to rise again.
Furthermore, the Gospel is the roadmap of divine optimism.
Paul, in his epistle to the Romans, justly grants men the title of heirs of the Father and co-heirs of Jesus.

Why would Heaven's patience toward us be prolonged if we, the incarnate and disincarnate workers of Earth, were nothing more than wretched and useless beings? Would it be fair to renew the opportunity for improvement to irremediably cursed creatures?
It is necessary to strengthen the sublime faith we raise on High, without forgetting that the High deposits sanctified faith in us.
May Humanity not underestimate hope.

We are not ghosts of eternal punishments, but heirs of Celestial Glory, despite our ancient imperfections. The imperative of happiness, however, demands that we educate ourselves properly, qualifying ourselves for the undying possession of the divine inheritance.
Let us forget the waste of energy, the whims of spiritual childhood, and grow up to be, with the Father, the guardians of ourselves.

messages.title: Friendship and Understanding
paragraphs: “I have fed you with milk, and not with meat: for hitherto ye were not able to bear it, neither yet now are ye able.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 3:2)

Many companions of struggle demand enlightened cooperators for tasks concerning them, valuable friends who understand their purposes and value their works, forgetting that affections, like plants, require proper cultivation.
Understanding is not improvised. It is a work of time, collaboration, harmony.

Christ Himself first sowed the divine ideal in the hearts of His followers before gathering their understanding. He suffered their denials, tolerated their weaknesses, and excused their demands to finally form the apostolic college.

In this regard, Paul of Tarsus provides us with a judicious lesson, declaring to the Corinthians that he had fed them with milk. Such a small statement overflows with vastest wisdom. The generous apostle, a giant in knowledge and living faith, had edified the companions of his evangelical mission in Corinth not with the complex nourishment of difficult theses, but with the simple teachings of truth and pure demonstrations of love in Christ Jesus. He had not conquered their trust and esteem by displaying culture or imposing principles, but rather by praying and serving, working and loving.
There is a science of cultivating friendship and building understanding. As happens to wheat in the spiritual field of love, it is not possible to reap without sowing.

Examine daily, therefore, your affective husbandry. Observe whether you are demanding premature flowers or anticipated fruits. Do not forget attention, fertilizer, the watering can. Place yourself in the position of a plant in someone else's garden, and realizing the care you demand, do not disdain to pay your debts of love toward others.
Imitate the prudent and devoted farmer if you wish to achieve a harvest of great and precise results.

messages.title: Today, Wherever We May Be
paragraphs: “For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.” — PAUL (Romans, 6:23)
For those who remain in the flesh, death means the end of the dense body; for those who live in the spiritual Sphere, it represents the restart of experience.
In any case, however, the termination full of pain or the recapitulation full of difficulties constitute the wages of error.
How often have we returned to the carnal Circles in expiatory obligations, feeling once more the suffocation within physiological vehicles to return to true life?

Many learners esteem long repetitions, yet from what we have learned, we are compelled to consider that one day well-lived with the Lord is worth more than a hundred years of rebellion in our inferior creations.

Unfortunately, however, so many coarse ties we have invented for our souls that our living, on most occasions, in the condition of incarnated or disincarnated beings, is still captivity to millennial passions.

The Lord granted us Eternal Life, but we have not known how to live it, transforming it into sickly experimentation. From this proceeds our landscape of shadow upon disincarnating on Earth or returning to its thresholds.
Complicated trial is the consequence of error, perturbation is the fruit of forgetting duty.

Let us renew ourselves, therefore, on this Day, wherever we may be. Let us forget the curved lines of our indecisions and make of our effort a straight line toward the good in accordance with the Lord's Will.
Tiny dots form gigantic figures. Minute things build grandiose edifices.
Let us withdraw from the dark regions of death in the practice of evil, so that we may become worthy of eternal life, which is the free gift of God.

messages.title: Bitterness
paragraphs: “See to it that no one falls short of the grace of God and that no bitter root grows up to cause trouble and defile many.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 12:15)
To serve the Lord well, it is not reasonable that we march along the path of honorable work in the manner of tearful and discontented laborers.
Grief, very often, reflects distrust and disloyalty.
The industrious and confident heart never loses optimism, placing itself, before anything else, before the Infinite and Eternity.
Are there difficulties and problems?
Let us proceed in service and the Divine Master will offer us the solution.
Are there shadows?
Let us remember that there are no eternal clouds, because the Center of Creation is Imperishable Light.
Are there falls?
Let us be convinced that getting back up will not be delayed.

The worker's duty is to continue the task entrusted to them, just as the obligation of the faithful servant is to march in the execution of the program of the One who granted them the blessing of edifying service.

Let us keep in mind that, in favor of the general success of our effort, the incessant combat against the roots of bitterness in the heart is imperative. If they sprout freely, they will be poisonous bushes, harming the movement of collective interests of elevation and peace.
Let us maintain reflection and prudence, but destroy unjustified bitterness, so that we may not disturb the Master's work and so that our loved ones may not deprive themselves of the grace of God.

messages.title: The Sound
paragraphs: “Again, if the trumpet does not sound a clear call, who will get ready for battle?” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 14:8)
Let no one judge that great cataclysms are necessary for the modification of the creature's Plans to take place.
Man can move to another Sphere without cosmic fanfare, and the upper and lower zones represent degrees of life, on the scale of the Infinite.
Elevation and fall, before one's own conscience, constitute an impulse upwards or downwards, in the unlimited field of manifestations of the imperishable spirit.
