Every modification for the better demands struggle, just as any ascension requires effort. The preparation of each one for spiritual ascension is imperative.
It is natural, therefore, that the vanguard be spokespersons to all those who accompany the work of improvement, gathered in a crowd.
This is why, personifying the living trumpet of Christ in the disciple of the Gospel, we must expect sure warnings from him.
In almost all places, we observe instruments of uncertain sounds that give news of the work to be done, but do not reveal right paths.
In most nuclei of resurgent Christianity, we encounter workers highly endowed with spiritual light, who doubt themselves, valuable companions whose faith only vibrates in discontinuous flashes.
It is necessary to understand, however, that the uncertain sound does not meet the exact itinerary. It serves to awaken, but does not provide guidance.

The apprentices of the Good News constitute the instrumentality of the Lord. We know that, collectively, they all remain engaged in serving Him, however, let no one forget the need to tune the trumpet of feelings and thoughts to the diapason of the Divine Master, so that individual interference does not become a dissonant note in the sublime concert of redemptive service.

messages.title: The Lord Will Show
paragraphs: “I will show him how much he must suffer for my name.” — JESUS (Acts, 9:16)
The dialogue between the Master and Ananias, regarding the help that Paul needed, is coated with special significance for all apprentices of the Gospel.

Noteworthy is Jesus' observation, recommending that the apostle to the gentiles enter Damascus, where He would reveal to him what was fitting for him to do, and very important is the determination to Ananias to attend to the famous executioner brought to the faith.

The call from Heaven to cooperativism overflows with a lesson. Persecutor and persecuted meet on the altar of fraternity and useful work. The old man of Damascus provides help to the ex-rabbi. Paul, in return, lavishes enormous joy upon his heart.
It should be noted, however, that Jesus took upon Himself the task of revealing to the newly converted how much it was up to him to struggle and suffer for the love of the Divine Kingdom.
Similar spiritual operations are repeated, every day, in earthly activities.

Under the inspiration of Christ, daily there are movements of approximation among those who run for good understanding before eternal life. Some bring the comforting and friendly hand of fraternal assistance, others the sacred joy of sublime hope. New agreements are established. New guidelines are drawn.
It is imperative to recognize, however, that the Lord will show each worker the content of service and testimony that it is up to them to provide in the ministry of His Infinite Love.

messages.title: Constructive Obedience
paragraphs: “As a prisoner for the Lord, then, I urge you to live a life worthy of the calling you have received.” — PAUL (Ephesians, 4:1)
When reading the Gospel, it is necessary to fix thought on the divine lessons, so that we may absorb their content of wisdom.
In the verse under our attention, we perceive in Paul of Tarsus the example of supreme humility before the designs of Providence.
Writing to the Ephesians, the apostle declares himself a prisoner of the Lord.
That wise and vigorous man, who had surrendered to Jesus unconditionally at the gates of Damascus, reveals to the Christian community the sublime quality of his faith.
He does not claim to be a prisoner of the Romans, nor does he comment on the situation resulting from Jewish intrigue.
He does not name his tormentors, nor does he refer to the sentinels who closely accompany him.
He does not examine services rendered.
He does not list lamentations.

Understanding that he remains in the service of Christ and conscious of the sacred duties incumbent upon him, he considers himself a prisoner of the Celestial Order and quietly continues his own mission.
A simple phrase demonstrates his elevated conception of obedience. Noting his noble attitude, it would be wise to remember our need to give primacy to the will of Jesus in our experiences.

When disciples who feel themselves administrators of the Lord, workers of the Lord, and cooperators of the Lord predominate in the frameworks of earthly evolution, the Earth will reach an expressive position within the spheres.
Imitating Paul's example, let us be faithful servants of Christ everywhere. Only thus shall we leave the cave of primitive impulsiveness, setting out on the path to a better world.

messages.title: Your Gift
paragraphs: “Do not neglect your gift, which was given you.” — PAUL (1 Timothy, 4:14)
In all sectors of the reorganization of Christian faith, within the frameworks of contemporary Spiritism, there are always companions dominated by harmful anxieties.
The problem of mediumship, principally, is one of the most discussed, often forgetting the essential imperative of service.
Psychic acquisitions do not constitute mechanical achievements.
It is indispensable to apply nobly the blessings already received, so that we may request new concessions.

Everywhere, there is an unquenchable anxiety to collect gifts from Heaven, without any sincere disposition to spread them for the benefit of all, in the name of the Divine Giver. However, the field of earthly struggles and experiences is the vast work of Christ, within which a certain particularity of service is imposed upon each worker.
Daily, there will be a more abundant distribution of spiritual light in favor of those who use the light already granted to them for the aggrandizement and peace of the community.
It is not reasonable, however, to confer new instruments upon idle hands that leave hoes to rust.
Remember, then, my friend, that you can be the Master's intermediary anywhere.
It is enough that you understand the fundamental obligation in the work of good, and attend to the Will of the Lord, acting incessantly in the realization of Celestial Designs.

Do not afflict yourself, therefore, if you have not yet received the credential for direct interchange with the invisible Plane, from a phenomenal point of view. If you sigh for frank communication with disincarnate Spirits, remember that you too are an immortal Spirit, temporarily on Earth, with the duty to apply the sublime gift of serving that is within yourself.

messages.title: Freedom
paragraphs: “You, my brothers and sisters, were called to be free. But do not use your freedom to indulge the flesh; rather, serve one another humbly in love.” — PAUL (Galatians, 5:13)

In all times, freedom has been used by the rulers of the Earth. In various sectors of human evolution, the stewards of the world take advantage of it for the exercise of tyranny, while servants use it in explosions of revolt and discontent.
Almost all the inhabitants of the Planet intend the exoneration of any and all responsibility, to plunge into slavery to all sorts of misdeeds.

No one, however, should resort to the Gospel to debase this sublime principle. The word of the apostle to the gentiles is quite expressive. The greatest value of the relative independence we enjoy lies in the possibility of serving one another, glorifying the good.
Man will always enjoy conditional freedom and, within it, can alter the course of his own existence through the good or bad use of such a faculty in common relations.
It is necessary to recognize, however, that very few decide upon the dignifying application of this superior virtue.

On almost all occasions, the persecuted person, given the opportunity to excuse, schemes violent reprisals; the slandered person, given the chance of divine forgiveness, resorts to vengeance; the misunderstood person, at the opportune moment to reveal fraternity and benevolence, demands reparations.

Where are those who take advantage of suffering to intensify learning with Jesus Christ? Where are those who feel sufficiently free to convert thorns into blessings? Yet the Father grants relative freedom to all children, observing their conduct.

Very rare are the creatures who know how to elevate the sense of independence into expressions of spiritual flight into the Infinite. Most men fall disastrously at the first new concession from Heaven, sometimes transforming velvet links into bronze shackles.

messages.title: Salvation Service
paragraphs: “And everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.” — (ACTS, 2:21)
The most recalcitrant Spirits in crime will be saved from the clutches of evil if they truly invoke the support of the Lord.
And it is necessary to observe that an instant always arrives in individual experience when we are constrained to resort to what we possess most precious in the realm of belief.

Materialists themselves do not escape this imperative of human struggle; as occurs with others, in tearing contingencies they request the help of money, provisional science, conventional positions, which, by the way, in good theory, help but do not save.
It becomes indispensable to resort to Jesus for the solution of our fundamental questions.
Let us invoke His compassion and adequate resource will not fail us. However, it will not suffice merely to learn to ask. Let us also study the art of receiving.

Sometimes, superficial differences arise between request and supply. The saving work of Heaven will come to meet us, but on a great many occasions it will not obey the expectation of our imperfect vision. In many cases, Divine Providence visits us in the form of illness, scarcity, and contrition...

Earthly myopia, however, generally interprets the word "salvation" only as "immediate advantage" and, for that reason, a slight disappointment or a useful disillusionment provokes torrents of unproductive lamentations. Despite everything, however, Christ never ceases to succor and relieve, and His sublime effort of redemption assumes varied aspects as diverse as the needs of each one.

messages.title: Do Not Confuse
paragraphs: “As Scripture says, ‘Anyone who believes in him will never be put to shame.’” — PAUL (Romans, 10:11)
In all circles of Christianity there are diverse forms regarding individual belief.

There are Roman Catholics who restrict the object of trust to the priest; evangelical reformers who limit themselves to verbal formulas; and spiritists who concentrate all expressions of faith in the mediumistic organization. The harvest of disillusionments is, therefore, natural.
Everywhere, there are priests who do not satisfy, verbalist formulas that do not meet needs, and mediums who do not solve all necessities.

Furthermore, we must consider that any blind belief, distant from Christ, can result in serious disturbance... Almost always, devotees ask for nothing more than egoistic satisfaction in common worship, in the rudimentary feeling of religiosity, and hence the disasters of the heart.
The sincere disciple, under all circumstances, understands the probability of failure in human collaboration and, therefore, places the teaching of Jesus above everything.

The Master did not come into the world to operate the exaltation of individual egoism, but rather to trace a definitive itinerary for creatures, instituting edifying work and revealing the sublime objectives of life.
Always remember that your existence is a journey toward God.
In what object do you centralize your belief, my friend?
Remember that it is necessary to believe sincerely in Jesus and follow Him, so that we may not be put to shame.

messages.title: Love One Another
paragraphs: “Dear children, let us not love with words or speech but with actions and in truth.” — JOHN (1 John, 3:18)
As a norm of pure and sincere fraternity, the Divine Word recommends: “Love one another.”
It does not determine selections.
It does not exalt conveniences.
It does not impose conditionals.
It does not disfavor the unhappy.
It does not belittle the weak.
It makes no privileges.
It does not ask for the removal of the wicked.
It does not disregard the children of other people's homes.
It does not highlight consanguineous relatives.
It does not undervalue adversaries.
And the apostle adds — “Let us not love with words, but through works, with all the fervor of the heart.”
The Universe is our home. Humanity is our family.
Let us approach the worst, to help. Let us approach the best, to learn.
To love one another, serving each other, not with words, but from the heart, constitutes for all of us the glorious path of ascension.

messages.title: Conscience
paragraphs: “They must keep hold of the deep truths of the faith with a clear conscience.” — PAUL (1 Timothy, 3:9)
Curiosity or suffering offer doors to faith, but do not represent the divine vessel destined for its maintenance.
Everywhere, we observe people who, following great calamities of fortune, rush hurriedly to temples or new oracles, manifesting hope in the remedy of words.
The phenomenon, however, is very often merely verbal. What vibrates in their hearts is unsatisfied caprice or wounded by the lashes of cruel experiences...
Clearly, such a resource can constitute a path for the edification of trust, without being, however, the ideal provision.
Paul of Tarsus, in his recommendations to Timothy, clarifies the problem with a firm stroke.
It is imperative to keep faith and belief in pure feelings. Without this, man will oscillate in unquietness due to the insecurity of his intimate world.
Obscure or stained conscience invariably leans toward painful rectifications, in whose service new debts may be born when the creature is characterized by a fragile and sickly will.
Apprentices of the Gospel must remember the Pauline counsel, which is coated with profound importance for all schools of Christianity.
The divine mystery of living faith is a problem of crystal-clear conscience. Let us work, therefore, to present to the Father the rectitude and purity of our thoughts.

messages.title: Vigilance
paragraphs: “Watch therefore, for you do not know what hour your Lord is coming.” — JESUS (Matthew, 24.42)
Let no one claim the title of Jesus' apprentice to exempt themselves from active service in the struggle of good against evil, of light against shadow.
The call for vigilance came from the very lips of the Divine Master.

How is it possible to preserve any precious heritage without watching over it attentively? The person of upright conscience, in all eras, will be obliged to participate in the effort of preservation, expansion, and defense of the good.

It is an undeniable truth that we are all marching toward universal fraternity, toward the concrete realization of Christian teachings; however, until we reach the time when the Gospel will be materialized on Earth, it will not be fair to hand over to evil, disorder, or disturbance the portion of service that falls to us.
To protect oneself from storms and harsh weather, man built a home and dressed himself suitably.

A similar law of preservation governs every sphere of work in the world. Communities demand institutions that guarantee them well-being and dignified labor, without the afflictions of captivity. Nations require "houses" of noble principles, where they may take refuge against the storms of ignorance or aggressiveness, despair or decay.
And in the service of the Christian construction of the future world, it is essential to watch over the field that belongs to us.

The apostleship is Jesus'; the work belongs to Him. He will come, at the opportune moment, to all departments of service, guiding the particularities of the ministry of purification and sublimation of life; however, let no one forget that the Lord does not dispense with the collaboration of sentinels.

messages.title: Spiritual House
paragraphs: “You also, as living stones, are being built up a spiritual house.” — PETER (1 Peter, 2.5)
Each person is a spiritual house that must be, through the resident's deliberation and effort, in continuous modification for the better.

Using the symbol, we recall that there are houses abandoned, heading toward ruin, and others that reveal themselves smothered by intertwined ivy or transformed into redoubts of treacherous and venomous beings of the shadow; from time to time, slackly maintained buildings appear, whose tenants never summon the courage to remove the despicable trash, and one observes fanciful dwellings that display a superb facade with unmistakable internal disarray, just as those that are encumbered by heavy mortgages, and it is fair to add that completely free residences, in constant renewal for the better, are rare.

The apprentice of the Gospel must, therefore, reflect upon the words of Simon Peter, because the lesson of Jesus should not be taken merely as a lulling caress, but rather as building and rebuilding material for the integral reform of the intimate house.
Very often, it is imperative that the foundations of our interior sanctuary be shaken and renewed.
Christ is not merely a philosophical or religious figure in the highlands of universal thought. He is also the restorer of the spiritual house of men.

The Christian without internal reform possesses only the blueprints for the work. The sincere disciple, however, is the devoted worker who reaches the light of the Lord, not for Jesus' benefit, but above all, in favor of himself.

messages.title: Furnishing and Belongings
paragraphs: “In that day, he who is on the housetop, and his goods are in the house, let him not come down to take them away.” — JESUS (Luke, 17.31)
The Master's word leaves no room for hesitation.
Naturally, every apprentice lives within their own proper organization. Each one remains at home, that is, in the individual creation or in the field of testimony to which the Lord has led them.

Generally, however, they are never alone. Whether small or extensive, there is always an entourage of affections accompanying them. Very often, nevertheless, the companion, the father, and the son are unable to move beyond the lower zones of understanding, when the disciple, through the noble efforts expended, balances triumphantly on the highest level of comprehension.
Having reached such a situation, many diligent workers experience major difficulties.

They do not know how to separate decorative items from essential vessels, frivolities from righteous duties, and they suffer painful shocks in their hearts. It is indispensable that they guard against this common danger.

Let the sacred obligation be fulfilled, let the program of the Divine Will be attended to first of all, let fraternity and tolerance be exemplified by lighting the lamp of one's own effort, but let not the divine service of ascension be harmed out of fear of personal sensitivities and purely exterior conventions.

A home does not live simply by reason of the furnishings that populate it transiently, but rather by the spiritual foundations that built its bases. A person will not be superior because they satisfy passing opinions, but rather because they know how to fulfill, in all things, the designs of God.

messages.title: Parents
paragraphs: “And you, fathers, do not provoke your children to wrath, but bring them up in the training and admonition of the Lord.” — PAUL (Ephesians, 6.4)
Assuming commitments in fatherhood and motherhood constitutes an aggrandizement of the spirit, whenever man and woman comprehend their divine character.
Unfortunately, the Planet still presents an enormous percentage of ill-advised creatures regarding these sublime attributes.

A large number of men and women seek poisoned pleasures in this regard. Those who, however, pursue ruinous fantasy still live far from true notions of humanity and must be placed outside any appreciation.
It is urgent to recognize, moreover, that the Gospel does not speak to the embryos of spirituality, but to the minds and hearts already susceptible to receiving its assistance.

The parents of the world, admitted to the assemblies of Jesus, need to understand the complexity and greatness of the work that assists them. It is natural that they interest themselves in the world and ordinary events; however, it is imperative not to lose sight of the fact that the home is the essential world, where divine designs must be attended to regarding the most important services conferred upon them. Children are the precious works that the Lord entrusts to their hands, asking them for loving and efficient cooperation.
Receiving charges of this nature is attaining noble titles of trust. Therefore, raising little children and perfecting them is not such an easy service.

The majority of human parents live astray in various ways, whether in excesses of tenderness or in an excess of demands, but in the light of the Gospel, all will walk toward the new era, understanding that if deep endowments of love are necessary to be a father or mother, the divine gift of balance must shine at the forefront of these qualities.

messages.title: Children
paragraphs: “Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right.” — PAUL (Ephesians, 6.1)
If right is a field of elevation open to all spirits, duty is a zone of service peculiar to all beings of Creation.
Not only human parents are surrounded by obligations, but equally the children, who need to watch over themselves with singular attention.

Almost always youth suffers from a strange forgetfulness. It esteems creating whimsical paths, disdaining the sacred experiences of those who preceded it in the unfolding of earthly achievements, only to return later, in discouragement, to the starting point, when suffering or the maturity of years restores its comprehension.
Children are marked by divine duties alongside those to whom they were entrusted by the Supreme Lord on the human path.
It is indispensable to show obedience to progenitors within the spirit of Christ, because such an attitude is just.

If parents often withdraw from the clarity of spiritual progress, choosing to park in inferior zones, not even under circumstances of this order would it be reasonable to consign them to their own misfortune. It is clear that children must not descend into the whirlpool of folly or crime to cater to their poisonous whims, but they will always find the appropriate resource to repay the benefactors for the priceless gifts they owe them.
Let us not forget that the careless, idle, or perverse child is tomorrow's unconscious father and the inferior person who will not enjoy domestic happiness.

messages.title: Conjugal Life
paragraphs: “Nevertheless let each one of you in particular so love his own wife as himself, and let the wife see that she respects her husband.” — PAUL (Ephesians, 5.33)

The tragedies of conjugal life usually populate the common path. To explain the imbalance, incompatibility of temperaments, the disenchantments of intimate life, or excessive domestic afflictions are invoked.
The husband disputes new company or harmful entertainment, while in many cases, the female mind opens to the empire of temptations, entering a false path.
Such a situation, however, will always be strange in homes formed upon the schools of faith, within the circles of Christianity.
Spouses with Christ welcome, above all else, the sweet exhortations of fraternity.

It is possible that dreams often dissolve at the touch of saving trials within affective nests built on the tree of fantasy. Many men and women demand, for a vast time, celestial flowers over earthly thorns, complaining of attitudes and guidelines from others that they are, for the time being, incapable of adopting, and marriage turns into a detestable institution for them.

The Christian, however, cannot ignore the transitoriness of human experiences. With Jesus, it is impossible to destroy the divine foundations of real friendship. Let one seek the useful and holy side of the task, and let hope be the lit lamp on the path…

Does your wife maintain herself at a level inferior to your expectation? Remember that she is the mother of your little children and the servant of your needs. Is your husband ignorant and cruel? Do not forget that he is the companion God has granted you...

messages.title: Let Us Illuminate the Sanctuary
paragraphs: “For you are the temple of the living God.” — PAUL (2 Corinthians, 6.16)
Individual effort establishes the necessary differentiation among creatures, but the distribution of divine opportunities is always the same for everyone.
Indiscriminately, all people receive identical possibilities for mental growth and elevation to the superior field of life.

We are all, therefore, according to Paul's sentence, sanctuaries of the living God. Despite this, countless people declare themselves far from eternal light, disinherited of faith. While they have health and the treasure of human possibilities, they make light and ironic jokes. When earthly lights go out, however, unable to move in the field of fantasy, they revolt against Divinity and plunge into an abyss of despair. They are unvigilant companions who occupied the sanctuary of the spirit with inadequate material. Absorbed by the short-sighted concerns of the lower sphere, they transformed hopes into criminal ambitions, expressions of confidence into blind fanaticism, aspirations of the High into interests of the lowest zone.

In vain does the delicate and pure word of the Lord make itself heard within the internal sanctuary when the creature, obsessed by the illusions of the physical Plane, loses the faculty to listen. Between their ears and the sublime warning rise thick borders of crystallized egoism and vicious affliction. And, little by little, the child of God incarnated on Earth, from rich in human ideals and transient achievements, passes to the condition of a beggar of light and peace in old age and death…

The Lord continues teaching and loving, guiding and directing, but because deafness persists, the renewing bombs of suffering arrive in due time, inviting the stray and obscure mind to discover its own values, reintegrating it into the sanctuary of itself for a sublime reenactment with Divinity.

messages.title: It Is Sanctification
paragraphs: “Sanctify them by Your truth.” — JESUS (John, 17.17)
We cannot forget that, addressing the Father in the final moments of his apostleship, Jesus prayed that He would sanctify the disciples who would remain on the carnal Plane.

It is significant to observe that the Master did not ask for perks and facilities for his continuers. He did not recommend that the Supreme Lord place his friends in enchanted palaces of pleasure, nor isolate them in particularist privileges. Instead, he begged the Father to sanctify them in the human condition.

It is understandable, therefore, that sincere disciples receive from Providence a greater share of purifying elements in beneficial labors and testimonies. On Earth, duty and responsibility almost always seem to crush them; nevertheless, the word of the Gospel is quite clear in the realm of eternal conquests.
We do not refer to banal peripheral rewards. We highlight spiritual aggrandizement, divine illumination, and redemptive perfection, still inaccessible to ordinary understanding.
Indeed, the Lord announced sacrifices and sufferings to his followers, emphasizing, however, that he would not leave them orphans.
They would be summoned to humiliating interrogations; nevertheless, Sublime Inspiration would not fail them.
They would walk troubled, but not distressed; persecuted, but never forsaken.
They would receive blows and disappointments, but hope and comfort would not be denied them.
They would endure human incomprehension, yet higher designs would act in their favor.
They would suffer flagellations in the world; however, their pains would stock the granaries of grace and consolation for the afflicted.
Very often, they would take the last places among earthly creatures, to be among the first in cooperation with the Divine Worker.
They would be detained in prisons, but would have the presence of angels amid songs of glorification.
They would carry scars as celestial signs.
They would tolerate sarcasms in honorable service to the Truth.
Persecuted and tortured, they would represent the throbbing letters of Christ to Humanity.
Suffering and humiliated servants in the carnal field, they would march marked by imperishable light.
They would scale calvaries of pain, bearing crosses, yet finding resurrection, crowned with glory.

Effectively, therefore, the collaborators of the Gospel are, generally speaking, anonymous and despised in the conventional spheres of Earth; nevertheless, for them, the Master repeats in all times the sublime words: “You are My friends if you do whatever I command you.”

messages.title: Utilization
paragraphs: “Meditate on these things; give yourself entirely to them, that your progress may be evident to all.” — PAUL (1 Timothy, 4.15)
Generally, the first impulse of those entering the faith is the concern to compulsively transform others.

Such a purpose sometimes borders on imprudence, on obsession. The new believer flagellates all who listen to their warm arguments, scourging customs, condemning others' ideas, and violating situations, forgetting that the soul's experience is laborious and long and that there are many spheres of service in our Father's house.
Accepting the good doctrine, memorizing its verbal formulas, and spreading its precepts are important tasks, but utilizing it is essential.

Many companions proclaim valuable teachings; however, deep down, they are always inclined to harsh conflicts at the slightest pinprick on the path of belief. They do not tolerate small domestic annoyances and maintain a true game of masks in all positions.
Paul's word, nevertheless, is very clear…

The fundamental issue is utilization. Undeniable that doctrinal culture represents an indispensable conquest for the safe ministry of the good; however, it is imperative to recognize that if the believer's heart aspires to self-sanctification on the way to the superior zones of life, it is indispensable that they occupy themselves with the sacred things of the spirit, not out of vanity, but so that their rightful utilization may be evident to all.

messages.title: The Helmet
paragraphs: “And take the helmet of salvation.” — PAUL (Ephesians, 6.17)
If safeguarding important members of the body is just, with much more propriety is it imperative to defend the head in moments of struggle.
Moreover, it is reasonable to consider that arms and legs are not always required to expend greater energy.
The head, however, does not rest. The seat of thought is a nursery of incessant work. It is necessary to safeguard it, to defend it.
In military movements, the soldier preserves it through special resources.
In the daily struggle maintained by the disciple of Jesus, we equally cannot forget the apostle's advice to the Gentiles.

It is indispensable that every apprentice of the Gospel take the helmet of salvation, symbolized in the mental covering of solid ideas and Christian attitudes, structured upon conceptions of the good, confidence, and sincere optimism.
Let us weave our spiritual helmet with the threads of unshakable courage, pure faith, and the spirit of service. Possessing it, we will face any moral combat of large proportions.
Let no disciple of the Good News forget their condition as a fighter.

Forces contrary to the good, my friend, will target your intimate world through all flanks. Defend your interior dwelling. Examine the defensive coating you have been using regarding desires and beliefs, purposes and ideas, so that the projectiles of wickedness do not reach you from within.

messages.title: The shield
paragraphs: “Take up the shield of faith, with which you can extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one.” — PAUL (Ephesians, 6:16)
No one decides to enter into battle without the necessary equipment. We are not referring here to bloody clashes.

Let us take economic achievements as an example. Who would guarantee success in production without articulating the basic elements essential to industry? Agriculture requires field instruments, and factories ask for adequate machinery.
In everyone's battle, the preparation of feelings is also indispensable. Intense work in sowing, care, personal effort, and discipline are required.
Paul of Tarsus, who so deeply knew the assaults of evil and endured its permanent onslaughts both within and outside himself, recommended that we use the shield of faith above all defensive elements.

Only trust in the Greater Power, in Victorious Justice, and in Divine Wisdom can nullify the invisible arrows inflamed with the poison that intoxicates hearts. Every sincere worker of Christ moves forward in a long and hard-fought struggle on Earth. Blows from the shadow and stiletto thrusts of misunderstanding surround them everywhere. And if goodness comforts and hope softens, it is essential not to forget that only faith represents a shield strong enough to keep the heart immune from darkness.

messages.title: Tribulations
paragraphs: “We also glory in tribulations.” — PAUL (Romans, 5:3)
Commenting on the favors received from the Higher Plane, Paul of Tarsus very rightly did not forget to add his joy in tribulations.
Christianity is full of sublime teachings for all times.

Many learners do not remember the apostle to the Gentiles except for his divine encounter with the Messiah at the gates of Damascus, fixing his transformation under the renewing breath of Jesus; and many companions approach his heart visualizing him with the crown of a redeemed spirit and a glorified worker in the house of the Heavenly Father.
The words of Christ's great laborer, however, leave no room for doubt as to the price redemption cost him.

Many times, he reports on the lacerations of the path, highlighting the educational and restorative stations between the first glimmer of faith and the supreme testimony. After the comforting blessing that reforms his life, there he is among whips, despair, and stoning. Between the grace of Jesus that went out to meet him and the effort he had to make to re-encounter Him, heavy years of arduous service and continuous renunciation are indispensable.
Let us look at ourselves before the evangelical light.

Not everyone is reborn on Earth with defined tasks in authority, social eminence, or world government, but we can assert that all disciples, in any situation or circumstance, can have strength, position, and self-control.

Let us remember that tribulation produces fortitude and patience, and truly, no one finds the treasure of experience in the swamp of idleness. It is necessary to wake up with the day, following its brilliant course of service in the opportunities for work it unveils for us.
Earthly existence is a passage to eternal light. And to continue with Christ is to follow in His footsteps, avoiding the insidious deviation.

In examining Paul's considerations, therefore, let us not forget that if Jesus came to us, it is up to us to march fearlessly to meet Him, understanding that for this, the great preparation service must begin in the wonderful and unknown “land of ourselves”.

messages.title: Spiritual letters
paragraphs: “After this epistle has been read among you, see that it is also read in the church of the Laodiceans, and that you likewise read the epistle from Laodicea.” — PAUL (Colossians, 4:16)
Heaven's mail has never been interrupted.
Ever since human intelligence placed itself in a condition to receive the vibration of the higher planes, the Father has not ceased to send His appeals through all resources.

Because of this, edifying inspiration has never failed creatures. And nowadays, with the intensification of exchange between visible and invisible circles, in view of evangelical Spiritism which restores Christianity in the world in its essential purity, spiritual letters are more direct, more tangible.
A large part of students, however, following the old current of indifferentism, upon noticing this or that edifying page, eagerly seek the names of those to whom they are addressed.

If there are wise counsels, they must be for others; if friendly warnings or severe appeals arise, they must likewise be for others. And a compact assembly of companions displays a singular anxiety to receive particularist messages with individual notes. To prevent such extremes, Paul recommended that epistles dedicated to a specific church be read and commented upon in different sanctuaries for the necessary fusion and expansion of elevated knowledge.

Today's spiritual letters should observe an identical process. We are compelled to recognize that we are all individually bearers of an inner temple. Let us know how to extinguish selfish solicitations and seek in each message from the Higher Plane the consolation, remedy, counsel, or warning that we lack.
When we know how to understand the small experiences of each day with the light of the Gospel, we will conclude that all epistles of good proceed from God for the general community of His children.

messages.title: In the midst of wolves
paragraphs: “Go! I am sending you out like lambs among wolves.” — JESUS (Luke, 10:3)
Naturally, Jesus, in pronouncing such a recommendation, was referring to strong lambs who managed to breathe on a plane superior to voracious wolves.
Would it be reasonable to send fragile sheep to violent beasts? It would be the same as aiding a carnage.
The Master undoubtedly desired the qualities of tenderness and magnanimity in His followers, but He would not endorse their hesitations and weaknesses.

Moreover, for service of such magnitude, unfolding into true spiritual battles, He needed faithful, kind, prudent, but valiant cooperators. He sent the disciples into the center of harsh conflict, not with the gesture of someone sending sheep to the slaughterhouse, but rather to the field of service where they could sow new and sublimated spiritual gifts among hungry wolves through exemplification in incessant goodness.

However, there are companions, even today, who believe themselves to be collaborators of Christ simply because they lift their hands in suppliant attitude toward the skies. They forget that Jesus stated peremptorily: “Go! I am sending you!…”
In such a determination, we clearly see that there are works to be carried out, meritorious actions to be instituted.
The world is the field where the worker will find their share of collaboration.

It is truly necessary to go to the wolves. It would be dangerous to wait for them. Many laborers, however, complain against the cross and martyrdom, forgetting that the Lord and His courageous successors found resurrection and eternity in them through constructive resistance against evil.
If the timbers and lions were to return, they should find the worker engaged in the effort that behooves them and never in an attitude of inertia, far from the ministry entrusted to them.

The appeal of Christ still resonates now… It is imperative to walk toward the wolves, not in the condition of beast against beast, but in the position of ambassador-lambs; not as emissaries of death, but as givers of eternal life.

messages.title: Demonstrations
paragraphs: “The Pharisees came and began to question Jesus, testing Him by asking for a sign from heaven.” — (MARK, 8:11)
In Christian Spiritism, from time to time, learners of the Gospel appear who are extremely interested in meeting certain requisites in the chapter of psychic phenomenology.
They demand tangible, unquestionable signs from Heaven.
Most of the time, however, this movement is nothing more than a simple repetition of the gesture of the ancient Pharisees.
A large number of mediums and other companions do not guard against the fact that requests for celestial demonstrations are formulated almost invariably in obedience to inferior purposes.

There are logical inferences on the subject that it matters not to disregard. If a Spirit remains incarnate on Earth, how can they provide signs from Jupiter? If requests of this nature, addressed to Christ Himself, were placed in the realm of temptations, with what argument could new disciples impose them on their friends from the invisible?
Instead of this, faithful learners should be prepared for Jesus' demonstrative work on Earth.

It is obvious that a Christian cannot project a magic screen upon wandering clouds, but they can reveal how the ministry of fraternity is exercised in the world. They cannot unfold the total landscape where disembodied creatures move in other vibrational fields, yet they are qualified to provide intensive collaboration in enlightening the men of the present and the future.
Whoever demands signs from Heaven is perhaps ignorant or acting in bad faith; however, the follower of the Good News who seeks to satisfy the foolish person is distracted or insane.

If exotic demonstrations are requested of you, reply resolutely that you were not appointed to produce wonders, and clarify to your brother that you remain determined to learn the science of Abundant Life from the Master, in order to offer Earth your sign of love and light, unshakeable in faith, so as not to succumb to temptations.

messages.title: Who follows
paragraphs: “When Jesus spoke again to the people, He said, ‘I am the light of the world. Whoever follows Me will never walk in darkness, but will have the light of life.’” — (JOHN, 8:12)
There are believers who do not shy away from the impositions of external worship. They demand genuflection and thunderous crowds from moment to moment.
Others prefer frivolous commentary about the general activities of religious faith, entrusting themselves to useless quarrels or cheapening divine resources.

The crowd of followers of this type usually declares that external attitudes and sickly discussions represent a sacrosanct duty for them; yet, as soon as unexpected blows of suffering or experience arise on the ordinary road, they plunge into gloomy despair, retreating into hopeless abysses.
In those gray hours, learners feel abandoned and oppressed, showing internal insufficiency. Many become lax in their obligations, claiming to be unprotected by Jesus or forgotten by Heaven.
This happens, however, because they have not listened to the divine revelation as it needs to be made.

The Master did not promise clarity to the path of those who only speak and believe. However, He signed a real commitment of continuous assistance to the disciples who follow Him. In this regard, it is important to consider that Jesus does not refer to lamps of a physical nature, whose irradiations hurt organic eyes. He assured the gift of the light of life. Whoever effectively prepares to accompany Him will not find time to spend with detailed examinations of thick, dark clouds, because they will feel the eternal clarity within themselves.
When you make the customary balance of your faith, therefore, observe with impartial honesty whether you are merely speaking about Christ or if you seek to follow in His footsteps on the common path.

messages.title: In our hearts
paragraphs: “Open your hearts to us.” — PAUL (2 Corinthians, 7:2)
Believers and workers of the Gospel use various means to establish its advantages, but rare are those who open the doors of life to it.

The words of Paul, Peter, Matthew, or John are commonly used in long and stubborn verbal duels through useless disputes, incapable of producing any noble action. Others receive evangelical warnings and lights in the manner of ambitious merchants, seeking to convert them into great economic sources. Still others seek divine admonitions, asserting egolatric principles in laborious and unfruitful polemics.
In the immense conflict of interpretations, however, Paul of Tarsus's request in his second epistle to the Corinthians should be respected.
The apostle to the Gentiles begs that he and his ministry companions be received into hearts.
The Christian community will emerge very differently if the disciples heed this request.
When the learner of the Good News receives the visit of Jesus and the divine emissaries on the internal plane, then discord and sectarianism will have disappeared from the sublime continent of faith.
Because of this, my friend, even if most of your brothers in ideal keep their intimate door closed, do your best not to postpone your own tranquility.

Record the lesson of the Gospel in the sanctuary of your being. Do not neglect it by relegating it to the external world, at the mercy of backbiting, perturbation, and misunderstanding. Harbor it within yourself, preserving your own happiness. Adorn yourself with the brilliance that stems from its greatness, and Heaven will communicate with Earth through your heart.

messages.title: Divine members
paragraphs: “Now you are the body of Christ, and members individually.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 12:27)
It is inadmissible for someone to hand over their spirit to the direction of Christ and their bodily garment to the adversaries of Divine Light.

Many misguided believers carry out stations of pleasure in the realms of crime and unconsciously exclaim: — “Today, my body attends to the fatalties of the world, but tomorrow I will be in church with Jesus.”
Others, after entrusting their youth to the guardianship of vice, wait for decrepitude in order to examine grand spiritual problems.
There are likewise those who flagellate the flesh through misplaced mortifications, supposing they are cooperating in the refinement of the soul by employing merely a few epidermal phenomena.

All learners of this class are unaware that life in Christ is a fair balance, embodying His feelings and designs in all lines of earthly service. Paul of Tarsus asserts that we are the members of the Master, “individually.”
Wherever we are, let us attend to the imperative of our tasks, convinced that our hands replace those of the Celestial Worker, albeit in a precarious condition.
The Lord acts in us, for our benefit.

It is indisputable that Jesus can do all things, but to do everything, He does not dispense with the collaboration of the human being who seeks His determinations. The faithful cooperators of the Gospel are the working body in His redemptive work.
May there be, therefore, a legitimate understanding between the servant and the legitimate guide.

Jesus demands instruments and companions. Whoever can satisfy this sublime imperative should remember that they must appear before Him demonstrating harmony of views and objectives, first and foremost.

messages.title: Scales
paragraphs: “Immediately something like scales fell from Saul’s eyes, and he could see again.” — (ACTS, 9:18)
Ananias's visit to Paul of Tarsus in the distressing situation of Damascus suggests elevated considerations.

What have we been in the shadows of the past if not creatures covered in heavy scales from all points of view? Not only have our eyes been covered with such excrescences. All the possibilities entrusted to us have been eclipsed by our negligence through the centuries. Hands, feet, tongue, ears, all the powers of the creature have remained for millennia under the poisonous coating of laziness, selfishness, pride, idolatry, and foolishness.

The help granted to Paul of Tarsus, however, offers profound teaching. Before receiving it, the former persecutor surrenders unconditionally to Christ; he enters the city in obedience to divine recommendation, defeated and alone, revealing extreme renunciation where he had once been applauded as a triumphant victor. Welcomed in a simple inn, abandoned by all companions, he trusted in Jesus and received His sublime cooperation.

It is important to note, however, that the Lord, using the instrumentality of Ananias, cures only his eyes, restoring the gift of sight to him. Paul feels scales fall from his visual organs and, from then on, offering himself to the work of Christ, enters the path of sacrifice in order to remove by himself the remaining scales that obscured the other zones of his being.
How much did Paul struggle and suffer in order to purify his feet, hands, mind, and heart? This is a question worthy of being meditated upon at all times.

Do not forget, therefore, that in daily struggle you may find the Ananiases of fraternity in the Master's name; they will approach your needs with compassion, but do not forget that the Lord only allows them to give you back your eyes so that, seeing clearly, you may rectify your life by yourself.

messages.title: They do not understand
paragraphs: “Wanting to be teachers of the law, and understanding neither what they say nor the things which they confidently affirm.” — PAUL (1 Timothy, 1:7)
Multitudes arise everywhere who abuse the word.
Destructive discussions are fanned in the sphere of science, politics, philosophy, and religion. However, such imbalances manifest not only in these sectors of intellectual activity.

Ordinary society in almost the entire world is a battlefield in this regard, in view of the condemnable influence of those who impose themselves as doctors of unwarranted information. Pretencious authorities on unrequested opinions spread general perturbation, delay edifying achievements, destroy a large part of the seeds of good, poison sources of generosity and faith, and above all, altering the currents of progress, convert domestic sanctuaries into trenches of “cordial” hostility.
These are the unconscious poisoners who spread disharmony, not understanding what they affirm.
Whoever says something, however, is sowing something in the soil of life, and whoever determines this or that is consolidating that sowing.

Many noble Spirits are cultivators of the trees of truth, goodness, and light; nevertheless, the sowers of the darnel of ignorance, the thistles of slander, and the thorns of backbiting also move about everywhere. Perturbation and stagnation operate through them. They abuse the verb, but they pay double price for their levity, because although they wish to be teachers of the law and however much they try to confuse its paragraphs, and even if they prolong their own foolishness for a long time, the closer they come to the results of their actions, within the circle of which that same law imposes upon them the realities of eternal life through disillusionment, suffering, and death.

messages.title: Debt of Love
paragraphs: “Render therefore to all their dues: tribute to whom tribute is due; custom to whom custom; fear to whom fear; honour to whom honour.” — PAUL (Romans, 13:7)
We all keep a general debt of love toward one another, but this love and this obligation subdivide into countless manifestations.
To each being, each thing, landscape, circumstance, and situation, we owe some expression of love in a different way.
The creature who is unaware of such an imperative has not yet found the true notion of spiritual balance.
Valuable enlightening opportunities are relegated by unwatchful souls to obscurity and disturbance.
What a prodigious Eden the Earth would be if each person granted their neighbor what is due by justice!

The ordinary person, however, revolving around their own “self,” in a climate of fierce selfishness, closes their eyes to the needs of others. They forget that they breathe the world's oxygen, that they feed upon the world and receive from it the material indispensable for improvement and redemption. To any demand from the external field, they become annoyed and irritated, believing themselves to be the creditor of all.
Many know how to receive, rare are those who know how to give.
Why should anyone evade the petitions of the patch of land that welcomes our spirit? Why deny respect to who governs, or attention to who is in need?
Redeem the bonds of love that bind you to all beings and things along the way.
The greater a person's understanding, the higher their debt to Humanity; the wiser, the richer to satisfy the imperatives of cooperation in universal progress.

Do not delude yourself. You always owe something to your fellow traveler in the struggle, as well as to the road you tread so carelessly. And when you redeem your obligations, you will walk upon the Earth receiving the love and reward of all.

messages.title: He Will Rise Again
paragraphs: “Jesus said to her, ‘Your brother will rise again.’” — (JOHN, 11:23)
For many centuries, the religious schools of Christianity clothed the phenomenon of death in depressing scenery.
Priests assuming hieratic attitudes, ministers commenting on the scourges of hell, black catafalques, and mourning cloths.
What could all this create but instinctive dread and mandatory constraint?

No one denies the suffering of separation. No spirit will bypass the planting of longing in the inner garden. Christ Himself was moved near Lazarus's tomb. However, the emotion of the Celestial Friend was built upon hope, awakening living faith in the companions who heard Him. His promise to Martha's fraternal affection is quite significant. “Your brother will rise again” — affirmed the Master.
Moments later, Lazarus was restored to earthly experience, surprising the observers of the unexpected event.

A gesture that transformed into a vigorous symbol, we know today that the Lord lifts us up everywhere, in the varied spheres of life. There is victorious and sublime resurrection in the carnal zones and in the different circles that dilate to infinity.
The most shadowed Spirit in the tomb of evil and the hardest heart are snatched from psychic darkness into the light of eternal life.
The Lord was not moved solely by Lazarus. Divine Friend, His affectionate hand extends to us all.
Let us place death back in its place as a renewing process and fill yourselves with confidence in the future, multiplying the sowings of affection and sanctifying services.
When you temporarily lose the direct company of a loved one, remember the words of Christ; that small family of Bethany is a miniature of the immense family of Humanity.

messages.title: Cares
paragraphs: “Therefore do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about its own things.” — JESUS (Matthew, 6:34)
The lazy of all times have never missed the opportunity to falsely interpret evangelical statements.
Jesus's recommendation regarding worry is one of those that most lent themselves to the arguments of idle debaters.
After Christ referred to the lilies of the field, not a few recognized themselves in the condition of flowers, when they are still nothing more than thorny plants.

Decidedly, the lily neither spins nor weaves, according to the Lord's teaching, but it fulfills the will of God. It does not solicit the admiration of others, it blooms in the garden or uncultivated land, it gives its perfume to the passing wind, it adorns joy or comforts sadness, it is useful to sickness and health, it does not revolt when its own brilliance fades or when selfish hands separate it from the cradle where it was born.
Would the inert man accept the standard of the lily in relation to existence in the community?

Jesus recommended that the soul not harbor any harmful anxiety regarding food, clothing, or accessory matters of the material field; He asserted that the day, constituting the resultant of general laws of the Universe, would take care of itself.

For the faithful disciple, clothing oneself and eating are verbs of easy conjugation and the day represents a sublime opportunity for collaboration in the work of good. But to base oneself on these simple realities to affirm that man should march without care for himself would be to belittle Christ's effort, converting His saving platform into a campaign of irresponsibility.

Man cannot nurture the pretense of rectifying the world or his fellows from one day to the next, tormenting himself in uncalled-for afflictions, but he must take care of himself, improving, educating, and enlightening himself ever more.
Indeed, the bird sings happily, but builds its own house. The flower adorns itself peacefully; however, it obeys the designs of the Eternal.
Man must live confidently, always attentive, nevertheless, to aggrandize himself in wisdom and love for the divine work of perfection.

messages.title: Saddening
paragraphs: “Now I rejoice, not that you were made sorry, but that your sorrow led to repentance. For you were made sorry in a godly manner.” — PAUL (2 Corinthians, 7:9)

How often do families, groups, or communities agitate so that the storm does not reach their common environment? How often does a creature gaze at the sky in supplication, so that pain does not visit their path or adversity flees to pursue other routes? Yet reality always arrives, inevitable and inflexible.
In the whirlwind of shadows of saddening, man not infrequently feels defeated and abandoned.
However, what seems like misfortune or defeat may represent the saving provisions of the All-Compassionate.
On many occasions, when earthly creatures weep, their friends of the Higher Sphere rejoice, much like fruit growers who rest peacefully after the field is well pruned.

Tears in the homes of the flesh frequently express the joys of celestial homes. The divine guides, however, do not rejoice because their wards are holders of sufferings, but precisely because such a situation indicates renewing possibilities in the work of improvement.
Every field must know the time of necessary reaping or cleaning.

When you are saddened in the face of faults you thoughtlessly committed, it is reasonable that you suffer the passage of heavy, dark clouds you accumulated over your heart; however, when trial and struggle surprise your home or spirit in circumstances beyond your will, then has arrived the hour of godly sorrow, which elevates you spiritually and, for that very reason, provokes the joy of the angels watching over you.

messages.title: Why Do You Disdain?
paragraphs: “Test all things; hold fast what is good.” — PAUL (1 Thessalonians, 5:21)
The Christian must not lose good cheer no matter how unsettling the perplexities of the path may appear. Not only regarding pain, but also concerning customs, events, changes, disturbances...

There are companions excessively preoccupied with the extent of others' errors, without guarding against their own faults. They point out suspicious houses, flee from social movement, malign facts, or condemn people before any serious examination of situations. And in this emotional complex that distances them from reality, they prolong misunderstandings with pretentious attitudes of improvised saviors, who merely accentuate the sterility of fanaticism.
Far from rendering real benefits, they constitute a neutralizing material to the renewing movement.
The Gospel of Christ, however, did not institute cubicles of isolation; rather, it seeks to establish sources of Abundant Life everywhere.
To examine impartially is to seek clarification.

Why hasty condemnation or destructive criticism? When Paul directed the celebrated recommendation to the Thessalonians, he was not referring only to books and Earth's sciences. He was referring to everything, including the very impulses of popular opinion, alluding to the maximum and minimum phenomena of the vulgar path.
In all occurrences of peoples and personalities, in all human facts and achievements, the faithful apprentice of the Good News must analyze everything and retain the good.

Why distance yourself from work and common struggle? Why discourage those cooperating in the purifying labor with your thoughtless disdain? If you feel united to Christ, remember that the Lord abandons no one, not even the seemingly poisonous beings of the ground.

messages.title: Tranquility
paragraphs: “These things I have spoken to you, that in me you may have peace.” — JESUS (John, 16:33)
Christ's word is always grounded in the spirit of service, so that disciples do not deceive themselves in the chapter of tranquility.

In general, apprentices of the Gospel await peace where reigning calm means nothing more than sometimes criminal stagnation. In the majority's concept, security resides in financial guarantees, prestigious relations in the world, astronomical salaries. This, however, is secondary. Nighttime storms tend to cleanse the day's atmosphere, the agonies of death renew the false vision of earthly experience.
It is better to stay up to date with the struggle than to keep oneself in provisional rest and find it tomorrow with the painful surprise of one confronted by ghosts.
Earth is a school of incessant work. Obstacles and sufferings are the creature's guides.
It is indispensable, therefore, to renew the conception of peace in man's mind, to adjust him to the mission he was called to fulfill in the divine work, in favor of himself.

To preserve peace in Christ is not to hold the peace of the world. It is to find the eternal treasure of blessings in the obligations of each day. It is not fleeing from service; it is accepting it where, how, and when determined by the will of Him who continues in redeeming action alongside us throughout the Earth.

Many men are wont to seek the tranquility of corpses, but the faithful disciple knows they have duties to fulfill at all instants of existence. Reaching such a zone of comprehension, they know the secret of peace in Jesus, with the maximum of struggles on Earth. For them, battles, friction, work, and testimonies continue on the Planet; nonetheless, no external situation modifies their interior serenity, because they have attained the luminous path of fundamental tranquility.

messages.title: The Vessel
paragraphs: “That each of you should know how to possess his own vessel in sanctification and honor.” — PAUL (1 Thessalonians, 4:4)
Paul of Tarsus's recommendation to the Thessalonians remains fully current.

The creature's vessel is the body entrusted to them. The ordinary man, in his false vision of the evolutionary path, inadvertently seeks to saturate it with disease, mud, and shadows, and everywhere, funesome consequences of such deviations are observed.
Here, abuses of diet appear; beyond, unmentionable excesses emerge. Numerous existences stumble into the tomb like precious vehicles run over or crushed by improvidence.
However, resources of Divine Goodness are not lacking so that the patrimony remains intact in the hands of the beneficiary, which is our immortal soul.
Hygiene, temperance, preventive medicine, and discipline should never be forgotten.

The Compassionate Father does not disregard the children's needs, but rather the children themselves belittle the values that Infinite Wisdom lends them out of love. Some overload the sacred vessel with toxic and staggering drinks, others transform it into a machine of carnivorous gluttony, when they do not shatter it in the clashes of criminal pleasure.

In obeying the imperatives of balance in the Divine Law resides the magnificent test for all children of intelligence and reason. Rare are those who emerge from it entirely victorious. Most expect miracles to absolve themselves of assumed commitments, forgetting that the problem of redemption and readjustment is up to each individual.

The best earthly father will not manage to preserve his children's vessels except by transmitting to them the guidelines of righteous conduct. Outside of the lesson of word and example, therefore, it is imperative to recognize that each creature must know how to possess their own vessel in sanctification and honor before God.

messages.title: Salutary Remedy
paragraphs: “Confess your trespasses to one another, and pray for one another, that you may be healed.” — (JAMES, 5:16)

Disease is always a formidable ghost in the human field, as if the flesh were touched by a curse; however, we can affirm that the number of essentially organic illnesses, without psychic interference, is positively minuscule.

Most maladies proceed from the soul, from the depths of being. Not referring to the immense torrent of expiatory trials that invades countless existences in their physiological expressions, we refer solely to ailments that arise unexpectedly with roots in the heart.
How many illnesses pompously christened by medical science are nothing more than vibrational states of an unbalanced mind?
Any internal disharmony will naturally attack the organism in its vulnerable zone. One will experience the effects in the liver, another in the kidneys, and yet another in the blood itself.
In theory, all morbid manifestations boil down to imbalance, an imbalance whose cause rests in the mental world.

The great apostle of nascent Christianity was a wise physician when he advised reciprocal approach and mutual assistance as salutary remedies. The offender who reveals their own faults before the offended casts out psychic debris, relieving the internal plane; when we pray for one another, our minds unite in the circle of spiritual intercession, and, although there is no immediate registration in our common consciousness, silent conversations take place through the “wireless” of thought.

Cure will never arrive without the necessary intimate readjustment, and whoever desires positive improvements on the path of elevation should apply James's counsel; in it, we possess a salutary remedy so that we may be healed as incarnate or desencarnate patients.

messages.title: Transformation
paragraphs: “Behold, I tell you a mystery: We shall not all sleep, but we shall all be transformed.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 15:51)
The apostle to the Gentiles refers to one of the most beautiful realities of spiritual life.

Regarding the problems of death, Christian schools, worked by theological reflections of all times, erected diverse theories defining the creature's situation after carnal detachment. It is fair that such a situation be as diversified as possible. No one penetrates the circle of earthly life in an absolutely uniform process, just as there are no desencarnation phenomena with full analogy. Each soul has its “entrance” and “exit” door according to its own conquests.
People speak too much of purgatorial zones, outer darkness, regions of psychic sleep.
All of this effectively exists in a grandiose and sublime plane that, for now, transcends limited human understanding.
All who drink from the pure fountains of truth with Christ should always keep optimism and confidence.

“We shall not all sleep” — says Paul. This means that not all creatures will wander blindly in the mental regions of semi-unconsciousness, not all will be snatched to purgatorial Spheres, and even if such occurrences were to happen, let us listen once more to the devoted friend of the Gospel when he assures us — “but we shall all be transformed.”
Paul does not promise endless suffering nor unending rest. He promises transformation. No one departs at the call of Eternal Life except to transform themselves.
Death of the body is spiritual growth. The tomb in one Sphere is a cradle in another.
And, since the function of life is to renew for perfection, let us transform ourselves for the good, starting today.

messages.title: To Shine
paragraphs: “Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father in heaven.” — JESUS (Matthew, 5:16)
Many apprentices assume that shining means acquiring a prominent position in intelligence services within the field of faith.
Indeed, to exclude spiritual culture in its various angles from the luminous position to which we should all aspire would be utter foolishness.
Learning evermore to better know and serve is the destiny of whoever faithfully consecrates themselves to the Divine Master.

It is urgent to understand, however, in the immediacy of human experience, that if the Savior recommended that disciples shine before men, He did not forget to add that this clarity should shine in such a way that they see our good works, giving thanks to the Father in the form of joy at our presence.
Let no one delude themselves with the will-o'-the-wisps of artificial intellectualism.

Let us teach the path of redemption, let us trace saving programs wherever we are; let the light of the Gospel shine in our speech or in our written phrase, but let us remain convinced that if these clarions do not unveil our good works, we will invariably be received in others' ears and understanding amidst expectation and distrust, because only in fused thought, word, and action in the teaching of Christ Jesus will there be constructive glorification around us to Our Father who is in Heaven.

messages.title: You, However
paragraphs: “You, however, must teach what is appropriate to sound doctrine.” — PAUL (Titus 2:1)
As long as you are not experiencing a temporary inhibition of speech, you will be pressured to speak in all situations.
You will be called upon to speak by those who wish to be good and those who are deliberately evil, the blind of the shadowy roads and the travelers of tortuous paths.
Disturbed hearts will attempt to extract disturbing expressions from you.
Slanderers will induce you to slander.
Liars will lead you to lie.
Frivolous people will try to lead you into frivolity.
Ironists will seek to locate your soul on the false terrain of sarcasm.

It is understandable that they act this way, for they are ignorant, distracted from spiritual illumination. Unfortunate blind people without knowing it, they go from fall to fall, from disaster to disaster, creating their own misfortune.

You, however, who know what they do not know, who cultivate spiritual values in your mind that they do not yet cultivate, take care to use the spoken word as befits the Spirit of Christ who governs our destinies. It is very easy to speak to those who question us in a way that satisfies them, and it is not difficult to reply to them as suits our particular interests and conveniences: however, addressing others with loving prudence and educational tolerance, as befits the Master's sound doctrine, is a complex and ennobling task that requires the science of good in the heart and evangelical understanding in reasoning.

Let the ignorant and the blind of soul speak disorderly, for they neither know nor see… You, however, be cautious in your verbal creations, like someone who does not forget the natural accounts to be settled in the coming day.

messages.title: Children of the Light
paragraphs: “Live as children of the light.” — PAUL (Ephesians 5:8)
Every creature always gives news of its own spiritual origin.
Actions, words, and thoughts constitute living information of the mental zone from which we proceed.
The children of restlessness usually smother those who listen to them in dark mantles of affliction.
The offspring of sadness spread the fog of discouragement.
The cultivators of irritation strike down the spirit of gentleness with the lightning bolts of anger.
The bearers of petty interests shadow the road they travel upon, establishing a dark climate in the minds of others.
Hardened hearts generate clouds of mistrust wherever they pass.
Those who are fond of slander and backbiting distribute poisonous portions of darkness with which great evils and great crimes are improvised.
Christians, however, are children of the light. And the mission of light is uniform and unmistakable.
It benefits everyone without distinction.
It makes no demands in order to give.
It drives away shadows without fanfare.
It spreads growing joy and revelation.
It sows renewed hopes.
It enlightens, teaches, supports, and radiates.

messages.title: Christians
paragraphs: “For I tell you that unless your righteousness surpasses that of the Pharisees and the teachers of the law, you will certainly not enter the kingdom of heaven.” — JESUS (Matthew 5:20)
The scribes and Pharisees were neither criminals nor enemies of humanity.
They fulfilled public and private duties.
They respected established laws.
They revered Divine Revelation.
They attended to the precepts of faith.
They fasted.
They paid taxes.
They did not exploit the people.
Naturally, at home, they must have been excellent stewards of family comfort.
However, to the Celestial Emissary, their righteousness left much to be desired.

They worshipped the Eternal Father, but did not hesitate to humiliate the unfortunate brother. They repeated verbal formulas in the cult of prayer, yet they did not pray with their hearts exposed. They were correct in their outward position, yet they did not know how to step down from the pedestal of false pride upon which they erected themselves, to help their neighbor and excuse him even to the point of self-sacrifice. They reasoned perfectly within the framework of their personal interests, yet they were incapable of feeling true brotherhood, capable of leading their neighbors to the lap of the Supreme Lord.
This is why Jesus traces a new standard of life for His disciples.

The Christian did not arise on Earth to circumscribe themselves to the small cottage of personality; they appeared, with the Master of the Cross, to transform lives and perfect them with their very existence which, under the inspiration of the Divine Mentor, will always be a hymn of service to their fellow men, exalting glorious and endless love toward the Kingdom of Heaven which begins, invariably, within ourselves.

messages.title: The Unquenchable Light
paragraphs: “Love never fails.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians 13:8)
You remain in the field of human experience, in full transforming activity.
All the situations in which you take pride are usually just necessary but unstable angles of your struggle.
Material fortune, if you do not base it on edifying and continuous work, is insecure patrimony.
The human family, without bonds of true spiritual affinity, is a gathering of souls in an experiment of brotherhood, from which you will depart one day with extreme disillusionments.
Directive eminence, when not solidified on robust foundations of justice and wisdom, of work and consecration to the good, is the antechamber of disenchantment.
Social position is always a transitory game.
The emotions of the physical sphere, for the most part, extinguish themselves like the flame of a candle.
The youth of the dense body is a passing blossoming.
Fame and popularity are usually processes of incessant torture.
Deceptive tranquility is an introduction to moral torments.
Unbalanced celebration is the eve of laborious repair.
Abuse of any nature compels hurried readjustment.
Everything around your steps in outer life is obscure and problematic.
Love, however, is the unquenchable light. Charity never ends.
The good you practice somewhere is your advocate everywhere.
Through love that elevates us, the world improves. Love, therefore, in Christ, and you will attain eternal glory.

messages.title: The Brother
paragraphs: “Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians 13:4)
Whoever gives to show off is vain.
Whoever gives to twist the thoughts of others, bending them to their own peculiar points of view, is a tyrant.
Whoever gives to rid themselves of the sufferer is dismissive.
Whoever gives to display ephemeral titles is foolish.
Whoever gives to receive with advantages is ambitious.
Whoever gives to humiliate is a companion of evil works.
Whoever gives to probe the extent of evil is distrustful.
Whoever gives to confront the position of others is arrogant.
Whoever gives to place their name in the gallery of benefactors and saints is envious.
Whoever gives to entrap their neighbor and exploit them is a potential delinquent.

In all these situations, in most cases, the one who gives reveals themselves to be somewhat better than the one who does not give, whose mind is crystallized in indifference or dryness; however, for the one who gives, radiating silent love without purposes of reward and without mixture of inferior personalism, the Higher Plan reserves the title of Brother.

messages.title: Above Us
paragraphs: “For it is written: 'I will destroy the wisdom of the wise; the intelligence of the intelligent I will frustrate.'” — PAUL (1 Corinthians 1:19)
Dozens of centuries have passed over the Planet, renewing the structure of all human concepts.
The science of war has multiplied States, however, all administrative cabinets that trace its dark paths succumb, over time, through the claws of the monsters they themselves created.

Religious science has established many venerable temples, yet whenever these sanctuaries entrust themselves to unregulated material comfort, upon the pedestal of dogma and despotism, they fall, little by little, poisoned by the virus of separatism and persecution that they decree for others.

Philosophical science erects systems upon systems, however, when it seeks to install itself in absolute negativism before the Divinity of the Lord, it suffers humiliations and setbacks, within which it achieves ends entirely contrary to those it set out to accomplish.

Throughout History, we see yesterday's conquerors cast into the dust of the Earth, scientists who sow vanity and reap the fruits of death, philosophers praised by the heedless crowd who plant audacious theories of race and economy, leading the people to hunger, ignorance, and destruction.

Seek, therefore, faith and act in accordance with the law of love that it reveals to your heart, because above us, infinite is the Power of the Lord, and a day will come when all falsehood and all vanity will be confounded.

messages.title: Just As
paragraphs: “As the Father has sent me, I am sending you.” — JESUS (John 20:21)
Every sincere Christian knows how the Supreme Lord sent the Divine Ambassador to Earth.
He had Him born in a simple manger.
He gave Him constructive work in childhood.
He conferred heavy duties upon Him in preparation, with prayer and fasting in the desert.
He inspired a frugal and simple life for Him.
He did not allow Him to linger in artificial joys.
He led Him to active service for the good of all.
He inclined His heart toward the sick and needy.
He sent Him to the circle of habitual sinners.
He induced Him to banquet with people considered of ill repute, so that His love might not be a luxury jewel but rather the blessed climate for the salvation of many.
He had Him teach the good and practice it among the paralytics and blind, lepers and madmen, so as to benefit them.

And, at the end of His sublime mission, He gave Him death on the cross, among thieves, abandoned by friends, under persecution and scorn, so that creatures might learn the process of personal sacrifice as a guarantee of happiness, on the way to the resurrection of the inner man to eternal life.

It was thus that the Supreme Father sent the Divine Son to Earth, and in this pattern, we can understand what Jesus wished to say when He asserted that He would dispatch messengers to the world under the same norms.
Thus, therefore, the Christian who aspires to move among earthly facilities has certainly not yet awakened to the truth.

messages.title: Answers from on High
paragraphs: “Which of you fathers, if your son asks for a fish, will give him a snake instead?” — JESUS (Luke 11:11)

In the circles of faith, we find various exhausted and disillusioned hearts. They refer to prayer the way hopeless patients refer to the efficacy of medicine, claiming that they receive no answers from on High.
However, deeper meditation would grant them a higher notion of the Divine Designs, understanding at last that the Lord never offers stones to the child who asks for bread.
It is not always possible to immediately comprehend the celestial answer on our path of struggle; however, it is never too much to reflect in order to perceive with wisdom.
On many occasions, bitter contrariateness is a beneficial warning, and illness is a resource of salvation.
