Not infrequently, the flowers of Christ's compassion visit the creature in the form of thorns, and in many circumstances of earthly experience, the blessings of celestial medicine temporarily transform into sanctifying wounds.

In many phases of the struggle, the Lord decrees the curtailment of time for the servant's circle so that he does not fill his days with the repetition of grave offenses, and not rarely, He gives ugliness to the physical body so that his soul may be enlightened and progress.
If earthly fatherhood, imperfect and deficient, watches over its children, what can be said of the Fatherhood of God, who sustains the Universe at the price of inexhaustible love?
The All-Compassionate never throws stones at the supplicant hands that beg Him for help.

If you linger, therefore, in the bosom of provisional inhibitions, remain convinced that all impediments and pains were granted to you as answers from on High to your requests for help, support, and lesson, with a view to eternal life.

messages.title: Our Brothers
paragraphs: “And he has given us this command: Anyone who loves God must also love their brother.” — JOHN (1 John 4:21)

Indeed, we love God in all reasons for joy along our evolutionary march. The Gospel, however, is full of recommendations in the sense that we must also love our brothers amidst the stones and shadows of the rugged climb.

Certainly, the word of the Good News does not refer to the beloved and happy companions who have already solved the questions of mental harmony with us, but rather to those who breathe in our atmosphere, demanding fraternal and secure help.
They are: our sick brothers who demand medicine;
the unfortunate ones who ask for comfort;
the weak who await defense;
the ignorant who yearn for clarification;
the maladjusted who need understanding;
the criminals distanced from help and light;
the insubordinate who challenge our tolerance;
the unbalanced who induce us to watchfulness for the good;
the demolishers who offer us the opportunity to rebuild;
the revolutionaries who help us recognize the benefits of order;
those who wound us, helping us polish our own imperfections;
those who persecute and slander us, providing us the opportunity to endure with Christ in the practice of the Gospel.

The enlightened and kind brother, in himself, already represents a living work of the Father, through whom we know and admire Him; the ignorant or unhappy brother, however, is a work that Heaven invites us to support and embellish toward perfection, in the name of the All-Merciful.
If you love God in the brother who understands and helps you, do not forget to honor and cherish Him in the brother who cannot yet love you.

messages.title: They Seem to Be, But Are Not
paragraphs: “Anyone who does not have the Spirit of Christ does not belong to him.” — PAUL (Romans 8:9)
The ruler will resort to the Divine Testament to reconcile the interests of the people.
The legislator will incorporate thoughts of the Gospel into the laws they establish.
The judge will use the Master's suggestions to illuminate the sentences they write.
The administrator will combine sacred verses to base opinions in service processes.
The writer will master sublime images of Revelation to awaken enthusiasm and hope in thousands of readers.
The poet will use passages of the Lord to color the verses of their inspiration.
The painter will refer to apostolic scenes and create imperishable masterpieces by adjusting canvas, paint, and brush.
The sculptor will fix in marble the memory of the eternal lessons of the Divine Messenger.
The revolutionary will repeat expressions of the Celestial Guide to justify claims of all kinds.
Even the beggar will speak in the name of the Savior, begging for alms.
Let no one be deceived, however, by outer appearances.

If the ruler, the legislator, the judge, the administrator, the writer, the poet, the painter, the sculptor, the revolutionary, and the beggar do not reveal striking and living traits of the Master in their individuality, demonstrating that they possess His spirit, truly, they do not yet belong to Him. They seem to be, but are not.

messages.title: While it is Today
paragraphs: “While it is said: Today, if you will hear His voice, do not harden your hearts.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 3:15)
Emphasizing the opportunity for spiritual regeneration in physical life will never be a tedious argument in circles of religious education.
The dense body somehow represents the mold used by divine compassion in our favor, across a large number of reencarnations, to readjust our habits and refine them.

The flesh, in many respects, is living clay of sublime ceramics, where the Celestial Potter often guides us, through the heat of struggle, to the same mold in order to perfect the subtle vehicle of manifestation of the eternal Spirit; however, almost always, we spoil the opportunity, heading toward uselessness or ruin.
Within this subject, however, Paul's word is valuable and timely.
As long as you can listen to or perceive the word Today, with hearing or reflection, in the physiological field, make use of time to register divine suggestions and make them concrete in your walk.

For the brutalized man, death does not bring great differences. Ignorance spends the day in impulsiveness and the night in unconsciousness, until time and individual effort wear away the shadows, clearing the path.
Here, however, we refer to the moderately enlightened creature.

All small bad habits, seemingly inexpressive, must be very well eradicated by those who, already on Earth, possess some knowledge of spiritual life, because one of the greatest torments for the disembodied soul, instructed in some way about the paths that unfold beyond death, is to feel, within the circles of sublimated matter, flowers and darkness, light and mud within itself.

messages.title: Efficient Aid
paragraphs: “And opening his mouth he taught them.” — (MATTHEW, 5:2)
The man who distances himself from the crowd rarely assumes a dignified position at its front.
In general, whoever receives authority thinks of entrenching themselves in a superior zone.
Whoever achieves high financial wealth usually forgets those who were companions from the beginning and draws humiliating dividing lines so that the needy do not annoy them.
Whoever refines their intelligence almost always abuses popular passions that are easily exploitable.
And the mass, in most regions of the world, continues relegated to itself.
Inferior politics turns it into a toy for common maneuvering.
Unfair commerce looks to it for a vein of exorbitant profits.
Vain intellectualism involves it in the expansions of the pedantry peculiar to it.
From epoch to epoch, the crowd is always the object of scorn or contempt for the spiritual needs that characterize its movements and attitudes.
Extremely rare are the men who help it climb the illuminating mount. Very few mobilize resources in social support.

Jesus, however, outlined the desirable program, instituting efficient aid. Observing that the common people approached Him, He began to teach them the straight path, making us realize that the educational work of the crowd challenges the religious and scientists of all times.
Whoever honors themselves, therefore, in serving Jesus, should imitate His example. Help your closest brother to dignify life, to build themselves up through healthy work, and to feel better.

messages.title: Tomorrow
paragraphs: “You do not know what will happen tomorrow.” — (JAMES, 4:14)
The lazy person says: “tomorrow I will do it.”
The weak person exclaims: “tomorrow, I will have strength.”
The delinquent asserts: “tomorrow, I will regenerate myself.”
It is imperative to recognize, however, that the creature, by postponing personal effort, has not yet truly attained the real notion of time.
Whoever does not make the most of the blessing of the day lives far from the glory of the century.
A soul without the courage to advance a hundred steps will not walk twenty thousand.

The farmer who misses the hour for sowing cannot foresee the consequences of procrastinating the service to which they are devoted, because, between one hour and another, impediments and struggles of indefinable duration may arise.
Many people await death to enter a good life; however, the law is clear regarding the destination of each one of us.
We will always achieve the results to which we propose ourselves.

If all birds have wings, not all adjust to the same task, nor do they soar at the same level. The swallow flies toward the spring climate, but the crow, generally, devotes itself, in any weather, to the debris on the ground.
That which man seeks now, he will surprise tomorrow, before his eyes and around his heart.

Take care, therefore, to do, without delay, what must be done for the benefit of your own happiness, because Tomorrow will be very pleasant and beneficial only to the one who works in the good, who grows in the higher ideal, and who valorously perfects themselves in the blessed hours of Today.

messages.title: In the Physical Field
paragraphs: “It is sown a natural body, it is raised a spiritual body.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 15:44)
Let no one despise the animal expression of human life under the pretext of preserving themselves in holiness.
The immersion of the mind into terrestrial fluids is an opportunity for sublimation that the industrious and awakened spirit transforms into the structuring of eternal values.

Common sowing is a perfect symbol. The germ cast into the dark pit suffers the action of the Earth's debris, faces the mud, the cold, the resistance of the ground, but soon turns into greenery and utility in the foliage, into perfume and color in the flowers, and into nourishment and wealth in the fruits.
Let us understand, therefore, that the seed did not stall. It broke all obstacles and, above all, obeyed the influence of the light that guided it upward, toward the Sun.
The pit of the body is also precious for spiritual farming when we submit to the law that induces us Onward.
Every creature provisionally shackled to matter can make the most of time in creating divine spirituality.

The apostle, however, is very clear when he uses the term “it is sown.” Whoever plants nothing, whoever does not work toward the elevation of their own life, coagulates mental activity and rolls in time like a pebble that advances almost unaltered, struck by unexpected blows of nature.
Whoever cultivates thorns will naturally reap brambles. But the forewarned heart that sows good and light in the soil of itself may happily await the harvest of spiritual glory.

messages.title: Foods
paragraphs: “Foods for the stomach and the stomach for foods, but God will destroy both it and them.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 6:13)
The food of the body and the soul, regarding bread and emotion, represents a means for evolution and not the end of evolution in itself.
There are creatures, however, who make the plate and the simplistic continuation of the species the sole reasons for being throughout life. They work to eat and procreate without thinking.
When spoken to about the spirit or eternity, they yawn unconcernedly, when they do not anxiously change the subject.

Indeed, the satisfaction of physiological senses is to the soul what soil and fertilizer constitute for the seed. However, if the seed persists in remaining in the pit to enjoy the delights of the fertilizer, contradicting the Divine Law, its precious collaboration will never be utilized.
Valuable and indispensable to physical experience is the stomach.
Venerable and sublime are the creative faculties.
It is urgent, nonetheless, to understand the needs of the imperishable spirit.
Enlightenment through study, mental growth through work, and illumination through sanctifying virtue are imperatives for the future stage of men.

Whoever spends time dedicating all the forces of the soul to the fantasies of the body, forgetting that the body must remain at the service of the soul, will soon stumble into perturbation, uselessness, or shadow.

For the community of applied and prudent learners, however, the eloquent warning of Paul shines in the Gospel: “foods are for the stomach and the stomach for foods; but God will destroy both it and them.”

messages.title: The Divine Bread
paragraphs: “Moses did not give you the bread from Heaven; but My Father gives you the true bread from Heaven.” — JESUS (John, 6:32)
Every religious regimentation on Earth has no greater scope than to prepare souls in the face of the grandeur of spiritual life.
Temples of stone ruin.
Dogmatic principles disappear.
External cults modify.
Revelations expand.
Priests pass.

All services of living faith represent, in some way, that bread which Moses dispensed to the Hebrews, undoubtedly a valuable food, but which sustained the body for only a day, and whose primary purpose is to maintain the sublime opportunity of the soul in search of the true bread of Heaven.
Evangelical Spiritism, in these present days, is a blessed granary of this bread. In its lines of work, there is more certainty and hope, more understanding and joy.

May each companion be convinced, however, that personal effort in the divine bread for the renewal, purification, and aggrandizement of the soul must be a dominant cult in the learner, or we will continue in the same mental and emotional obscurities of yesterday.
Observations of a phenomenic order are destined for oblivion.
Doctrinal statements rise for the good.
Horizons of knowledge expand to infinity.
Processes of communication with the invisible always progress.
Mediums succeed one another.

If you seek happiness itself, apply yourself with all your energy to making the most of the divine bread that descends from Heaven to your heart through the word of spiritual benefactors, and learn to ascend, with your mind inflamed by love and light, to the inexhaustible granaries of celestial bread.

messages.title: The Master's Platform
paragraphs: “He will save His people from their sins.” — (MATTHEW, 1:21)

Indeed, two thousand years ago, people believed that Jesus would be a revolutionary commander, like so many others, devoted to political demands at the cost of the death, sweat, and tears of many people.
Even today, we see compact groups of undisciplined men who, administering or obeying, report to Christ, interpreting Him as if He were a patron of individual rebellions, thirsty for civil war.
However, no program in that sense transpires from the Gospel.
That Jesus is the Divine Governor of the Planet we cannot doubt. What He will do with the redeemed world we do not yet know, because the plans of the General are forbidden to the humblest soldier.

The Good News, however, is very clear regarding the first platform of the Master of Masters. He presented no titles of reformer of political habits, vitiated by the bad inclinations of governors and governed of all times.

He announced to us the celestial revelation that He would come to save us from our own sins, to free us from the chain of our own errors, keeping us away from the selfishness and pride that still legislate for our world of consciousness.
We find ourselves, to this day, in a simple beginning phase of evangelical apostolate—Christ freeing man from the sores of himself, so that the cleansed man may manage to purify the world.
The individual kingdom that can accept the liberating service of the Savior will find new life.

messages.title: The Truth
paragraphs: “I am the way and the truth.” — JESUS (John, 14:6)
For now, no one will dare, in good logic, to display pure truth on Earth before the vision of collective forces.
The profound diversity of minds, with the heterogeneity of characters and temperaments, aspirations and purposes, prevents the exposition of full reality to the spirit of the common masses.

Each religious school, for this reason, maintains different courses of gradual revelation in the world. Immaculate clarity would not be assimilable by all immediately at the present stage of human evolution.
We must wait for the passing of hours. In the circles of time, the seed, with man's effort, provides the granary; and coal, with the help of nature, turns into a diamond.

Because of this, we see stagnant truths in dogmatic churches, provisional truths in sciences, progressive truths in philosophies, convenient truths in political struggles, and debatable truths in all corners of civilized life.
Such an imperative, however, for the Christian mentality, only applies regarding the masses.
Before each disciple, in the individual kingdom, Jesus is the sublime and revealing truth.

Everyone who discovers His blessed light absorbs His transformative celestial rays… And begins to observe experience through other prisms, chooses higher standards of struggle, unveils sanctifying goals, and identifies with broader horizons. The kingdom of one's own heart begins to gravitate around the new vital, glorious, and eternal center. And as each disciple of the Lord rids themselves of the attractions of falsehood, they penetrate more intensively into the orbit of the Truth, which is Pure Light.

messages.title: The Way
paragraphs: “I am the way…” — JESUS (John, 14:6)
There are still many people on Earth believing that Christianity is a panacea like so many others for the salvation of souls.
For this caste of believers, human life is a process of enjoying what is possible in the fleshly body, reserving the light of faith for occasions of irremediable suffering.
Is there decay in the flesh? One seeks the comfort of temples.
Did the death of loved ones come? One listens to one preaching or another that helps the descent of momentary tears.
Are there disasters? Knees are bent for a few minutes, and celestial intervention is awaited.
Prayer is used in exceptional moments like a miraculous ointment, only advisable for the skin on occasions of severe injury.
Most students of the Gospel seem to forget that the Lord revealed Himself to us as being the way… A road without use is not understood.
Embracing Christianity is advancing toward a better life.

Accepting the tutelage of Jesus and marching in His company is learning constantly and serving daily, with incessant renewal for infinite good, because constructive work, in all moments of life, is the soul's sublime journey toward knowledge and virtue, experience and elevation.

Areas without roads to intensify their service and transport are regions of paralytic economy. Christians who do not take advantage of the Lord's way to achieve legitimate spiritual prosperity are creatures voluntarily condemned to stagnation.

messages.title: Edification of the Kingdom
paragraphs: “The Kingdom of God is in the midst of you.” — JESUS (Luke, 17:21)
Neither in excessive joy that deafens.
Nor in excessive sadness that depresses.
Nor in unconditional tenderness that harms.
Nor in indiscriminate severity that destroys.
Nor in affective blindness that never corrects.
Nor in rigor that parches.
Nor in affirmative absurdity that is dogma.
Nor in negative absurdity that is vanity.
Nor in works without faith that are reduced to stone and dust.
Nor in faith without works that is the soul's stagnation.
Nor in movement without an ideal of elevation that is empty weariness.
Nor in an ideal of elevation without movement that is brilliant idleness.
Neither a head excessively turned toward the firmament with complete disregard for valuable work on Earth.
Nor feet definitively nailed to the floor of the Planet with the full forgetfulness of Heaven's appeals.
Neither demands at every instant.
Nor endless excuses.
The Divine Kingdom will not be realized on Earth through extremist attitudes.
The Master Himself assured us that the sublime realization is in our midst.
The edification of the Divine Kingdom is a work of refinement, order, effort, and application to the Master's designs, based on methodical work and necessary harmony.
Do not bind yourself excessively to the difficulties of yesterday, nor worry too much about tomorrow's probable obstacles. Live and act well today, balance yourself, and you will conquer.

messages.title: Individual Work
paragraphs: “Know that whoever turns a sinner from the error of their way will save them from death and cover a multitude of sins.” — (JAMES, 5:20)
When a man commits an evil deed, its reflections persist for a long time in the spiritual atmosphere in which he lives.
The ignorant creature who observes it becomes worse.
The less benevolent eyes that see it become harder.
The almost rectified man who identifies it comes to a standstill and is discouraged.
The missionary of good who witnesses it finds greater difficulty in helping others.
Around a charityless gesture, indisposition, spite, revolt, and vengeance gather, associating in evil and destructive mental operations.
A good deed, however, always builds and illuminates.
The ignorant creature who observes it learns to elevate themselves.
The less benevolent eyes that see it receive a new clarity for their inner life.
The almost rectified man who identifies it acquires greater strength to restore himself.
The missionary of good who witnesses it is exalted by it, for the benefit of his apostolate of light.
Around the Christian manifestation, gratitude, joy, hope, and optimism intertwine, organizing illuminating and sanctifying mental creations.
If you wish, therefore, to propagate the sublime spirit of Christianity, attend to individual work with Jesus.
Lead beloved hearts away from the dark field of error through your acts, which constitute living lessons of edifying love.
Remember that through the true and substantial conversion of a single Spirit to the Infinite Good, dark multitudes of evils may vanish forever.

messages.title: Words
paragraphs: “Out of the same mouth proceed blessing and cursing.” — (JAMES, 3:10)
You will never regret:
Having listened to a hundred phrases, simply pronouncing one or another small observation.
Avoiding any allusive comment to evil, whatever it may be.
Silencing the explosion of anger.
Preferring silence in moments of irritation.
Renouncing light opinions in the smallest controversies.
Refraining from giving opinions on problems that do not concern you.
Avoiding promises you could not keep.
Meditating for many hours without opening your lips.
Smiling only upon disillusionments and bitterness.
Fleeing from complaints of any nature.
Stimulating good under all prisms.
Pronouncing words of forgiveness and kindness.
Expounding on optimism, faith, and hope.
Exalting trust in Heaven.
Teaching what is useful, true, and sanctifying.
Providing information that helps others.
Expressing good thoughts.
Formulating appeals for fraternity and concord.
Demonstrating benevolence and understanding.
Strengthening work and education, justice and duty, peace and good, even at the sacrifice of one's own heart.
Examine the meaning, manner, and direction of your words before pronouncing them. Out of the same mouth proceeds the blessing or the curse for the journey.

messages.title: Let Us Listen Attentively
paragraphs: “Seek first the Kingdom of God and His justice.” — JESUS (Matthew, 6:33)
Despite all the clarifications of the Gospel, the disciples find it difficult to properly balance the compass of the heart.

One resorts to faith in the thirst for spiritual peace, in the yearning for light, in the search for solutions to the grave problems of destiny. However, first of all, the learner usually seeks the realization of their own caprices; the predominance of their peculiar opinions; the subordination of others to their points of view; the submission of others to the direct or indirect force they possess; the consideration of others for their way of being; the imposition of their highly personal authority; the most pleasant paths; the easy comforts of the passing day; favorable responses to their intents; and full self-satisfaction in vulgar immediatism.
Few accept the conditions of discipleship. In general, they refuse the title of followers of the Master.

They want to be favorites of God. We know, however, human nature, of which we are still partakers, notwithstanding the position of disembodied Spirits. And we know that life will refine all creatures in the lustral waters of experience.

We will struggle, suffer, and learn in the varied spheres of evolutionary and redeeming struggle. Considering, however, the extent of the blessings that grace our road, we believe it would be useful for our permanent happiness and balance to listen attentively to the words of the Lord: “Seek first the Kingdom of God and His justice”.

messages.title: After…
paragraphs: “Afterward, when tribulation or persecution arises…” — JESUS (Mark, 4:17)
Everyone knows the science of starting good works.

One accepts the arm of a benefactor with exclamations of joy, however, afterward… when the need disappears, unwarranted complaint is cultivated in the direction of declared ingratitude, affirming — “he is not as good as he seems.”
One begins the mission of charity with holy enthusiasm, however, afterward… when the first thorns appear, the bankruptcy of faith is proclaimed, shouting with all strength — “it is not worth it.”

One undertakes the journey of virtue and takes advantage of the stimulus that the Lord grants to the soul through a thousand different resources, meanwhile, afterward… when discipline and sacrifice exact the just tax due to spiritual illumination, one complains with annoyance — “like this, neither.”

One helps a companion of the road with extreme affection, adorning their heart with laudatory flowers, however, afterward… if our sowing does not correspond to the demanding tenderness, we abandon them to the hazards of the path, asserting with emphasis — “I can do no more.”
Everyone knows how to begin the ministry of good, few continue in the saving labor, very few finish the edifying task.
Meanwhile, on the other hand, the dangerous achievements of disturbance and shadow materialize rapidly.
One companion begins to betray their divine commitments and executes, without delay, what they desire.
Another begins the planting of discouragement and swiftly reaches the ends they propose.
Another, still, initiates discord and, without delay, creates general disharmony.
Indeed, it is very difficult to persevere in good and always easy to attain evil.
Nevertheless, afterward…

messages.title: Executing Well
paragraphs: “And he said to them, — 'Exact no more than what is appointed you.'” — JOHN THE BAPTIST (Luke, 3:13)
John the Baptist’s warning to the restless crowd is one of the most precious admonitions of the Gospel.
Anxiety is the enemy of fruitful labor.
Precipitation causes disorders and consequent recapitulations.
Every edifying activity demands understanding.
The Precursor’s word does not aim to annul initiative or diminish responsibility, but recommends a spirit of precision and execution in the commitments assumed.
Premature achievements cause great waste of energy and useless friction.
In current evangelical circles, John the Baptist’s advice should be especially remembered.

How many ask for new spiritual messages without having attended to the sacred recommendations of the old messages? How many learners are anxious to transmit the truth to the people without having yet fulfilled the smallest portion of responsibility toward the home they formed in the world? They demand revelations, emotions, and novelties, forgetting that there are also inalienable duties challenging the eternal spirit.
The soul’s individual work program in self-improvement, whether in the incarnate or disembodied condition, is a sovereign law.

It is useless for a man to deceive himself with beautiful words without intimately adhering to them, or to take refuge in the protection of third parties, in the flesh or in the spiritual circles close to him.
In any case, in the experience of each of us, there will be the Creator's ordinance and the creature's service.
It is not enough to multiply promises or ask for various tasks at the same time. First of all, it is essential to receive the Lord’s ordinance each day and execute it in the best possible way.

messages.title: Strait Gate
paragraphs: “Strive to enter through the narrow door, for many, I say to you, will seek to enter and will not be able.” — JESUS (Luke, 13:24)
Before the reincarnation necessary for progress, the soul esteems the “strait gate” as its glorious opportunity in carnal circles.

It recognizes the need for purifying suffering. It yearns for redeeming sacrifice. It exalts the obstacle that teaches. It understands the difficulty that enriches the mind and asks for nothing other than the lesson, expecting nothing less than the light of understanding that will elevate it on the infinite paths of life.
It obtains the fragile vessel of flesh in which it plunges for the service of rectification and perfection.
Regaining, however, the opportunity of earthly existence, it once again seeks the “wide gates” through which the multitudes pass.
Fleeing from difficulty, it strives for the least effort.
Fearing sacrifice, it demands personal advantage.
Far from serving others, it claims the services of others for itself.
And, in the sickly sleep of the past, it crosses the fields of evolution without accomplishing anything useful, belittling the commitments assumed.
In general, almost all men only wake up when illness demands their body for the transformations of death.
“Ah! If it were possible to return!…” — everyone thinks.

With what affliction they cherish the desire to live again in the world in order to learn humility, patience, and faith!… With what transport of joy they would then devote themselves to the happiness of others!…

But… it is too late. They begged for the “strait gate” and received it; however, they backed down at the moment of righteous service. And because they settled very comfortably in the “wide gates,” they return to integrate the anxious ranks of those who seek to enter again and fail.

messages.title: Prayer and Renewal
paragraphs: “In burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin you had no pleasure.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 10:6)
It is certain that all sincere work of spiritual adoration lifts our soul, elevating our feelings.

Supplication in remorse brings us the blessing of comforting tears. Prayer in affliction makes us know our own deficiency, helping us to discover the value of humility. Petition in pain reveals to us the sacred source of Inexhaustible Mercy.

Prayer refreshes, relieves, exalts, clarifies, elevates, but above all, attunes the heart to divine service. Let us not forget, however, that the intimate and profound acts of faith are necessary and useful to ourselves.
In essence, it is not the Lord who needs our votive manifestations, but rather we ourselves who must take advantage of the sublime possibility of repetition, learning from the wisdom of life.
Jesus awaits our spiritual renewal, above all else.
If you have erred, you must seek the door of rectification.
If you have offended someone, correct yourself through due reconciliation.
If you have strayed from the straight path, return to the right way.
If you have been disturbed, harmonize yourself once more.
If you have harbored revolt, recover self-discipline.

In any position of imbalance, remember that prayer can bring you divine suggestions, expand your spiritual vision, and provide abundant consolation; however, conventional or verbalist positions are not enough for the Lord.
The Master confers the Gift upon us and asks us for the Initiative.

In your days of struggle, therefore, make the vows and promises that are to your liking and profit, but do not forget action and profitable renewal in the divine work of the world, which are supremely pleasing in the eyes of the Lord.

messages.title: Corrections
paragraphs: “For the Lord disciplines the one he loves, and chastises every son whom he receives.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 12:6)
When the disciples of the Gospel begin to understand the value of correction, their minds rise to higher planes of life.
Naturally, the Father loves all children; however, those who seek to understand Him will perceive divine love more closely.
Maximum identification with the Lord represents maximum sentimental capacity.
Having reached this position, the spirit penetrates other zones of service and learning.

At first, corrections hurt, the scourges of experience torment; however, if one knows how to conquer in the first trials, one enters into the knowledge of one's own needs and accepts the struggle as spiritual nourishment and the testimony of daily service as an indispensable expression of self-improvement.
Life is full of lessons in this regard.
The mineral sleeps.
The tree dreams.
The irrational creature responds to impulse.
The savage man obeys instinct.
Childhood plays.
Youth idealizes.
The conscious spirit strives and struggles.

The renewed man converted to Jesus, however, is the child of heaven, placed between the lower and upper zones of the evolutionary path. In him, the work of illumination and perfection is incessant; therefore, he must be the first to receive the Lord's corrections and the scourges of paternal rectification.
If you find yourself, then, closer to the Father, learn to understand the love of divine education.

messages.title: And Watch Yourselves
paragraphs: “And take heed to yourselves, lest your hearts be weighed down with carousing, drunkenness, and cares of this life, and that Day come on you unexpectedly.” — JESUS (Luke, 21:34)

In general, man is interested in everything concerning the immediate well-being of physical existence, neglecting spiritual life, burdening his feelings with vices and worries of all sorts. While he has plenty of time to buy troubles in the vast news of the lower planes of earthly activity, he never finds an opportunity for scarce moments of elevated meditation. He fixes with interest the destructive waves of hatred and darkness that plague nations, but usually does not see the shadows that invade him. He searches out his neighbor's faults and distracts himself from his own.
He cares for nothing except properly feeding the physical vehicle, plunging into a sea of fantasies or imprisoning himself in terrible bonds of pain that he creates along the way.
After shaping dark phantoms and nurturing his own tormentors, he cries out desperately for Jesus and His messengers.
The Master, however, is never negligent at any time, and long ago recommended that each one watch over themselves toward higher spirituality.
The Lord knew how bitter unexpected suffering is and did not fail to give us the roadmap, anticipating our request many centuries ago.
Let everyone withdraw from excesses in egoistic satisfaction, flee from the relaxation of duty, cast off petty worries — and they will be prepared for the sublime transformation.

Indeed, the Earth will not live indefinitely without an accounting; however, every disciple of the Gospel must understand that the moment of the death of the physical body is a judgment day in the world of every man.

messages.title: In the Inner Kingdom
paragraphs: “Therefore let us pursue the things which make for peace and the things by which one may edify another.” — PAUL (Romans, 14:19)

We cannot expect, for the time being, that the Gospel of Jesus will achieve immediate victory in the spirit of peoples. Its influence is manifest in the world, in all collectivities; however, when referring to human masses, we are compelled to verify that every transformation is slow and difficult.

The same does not happen, however, in the private sphere of the disciple. Each spirit possesses its own kingdom of feelings and reasoning, actions and reactions, possibilities and tendencies, thoughts and creations.
On this plane, evangelical teaching can exteriorize into immediate works. It will suffice for the learner to become fond of the Master.

While the worker spies on matters of the external world, the service will be disturbed. Likewise, if the disciple does not attend to the guidelines that serve edifying peace in the place where they remain, and if they do not use the resources at hand to materialize true fraternity, their internal kingdom will be divided and tormented, under the heavy storm.

Let us not surrender, therefore, to the imbalance of forces in tribute to evil through comments alluding to the deficiency of many of our brothers whose boat has not yet docked at the shore of righteous understanding.
The path is infinite and the Father watches over everyone. Let us help and build.
If you are a disciple of the Lord, take advantage of the opportunity in building the good. Sowing peace, you will reap harmony; sanctifying the hours with Christ, you will never know abandonment.

messages.title: Let Us Apply Ourselves
paragraphs: “And let ours also learn to maintain good works, to meet urgent needs, that they may not be unfruitful.” — PAUL (Titus, 3.14)
It is necessary to believe in goodness; however, it is indispensable that we move with it in the service of elevation.
It is necessary to keep the faith; yet, if we do not bear witness to it in our daily work, we will remain on the superficial level of mere talk.
Of course, we must all learn the path of enlightenment; however, if we are not willing to walk it, we will not go beyond a verbalist attitude.

In Christian Spiritism, there are pressing problems for disciples in all situations. Knowledge of good is very important, but let us not forget good works; it is right that our hope should expand toward the future and the sublimity of other worlds in a glorious coming age, but let us not overlook the small duties of the passing hour.
Otherwise, we would be legions of servants incapable of working—pretty figures in the shop window of ideas, without any value in practical life.

Nature usually presents beautiful trees that cover themselves with flowers and never bear fruit; the sky sometimes displays clouds that promise rain and dissolve without bringing any benefit to the thirsty earth.

Religious schools likewise reveal a large number of demonstrations of this sort. These are the promising yet unfruitful believers who deceive everyone with their brilliant appearance. The day will come, however, when they will ascertain that it is always better to do so as to teach later, than to always teach without ever doing.

messages.title: Veils
paragraphs: “Nevertheless when one turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.” — PAUL (2 Corinthians, 3.16)
It is not easy to tear away the veils that shadow the human mind.
Whoever merely analyzes may be confronted by countless difficulties, lingering for a long time on the interpretations of others.
Whoever only convinces themselves may tend toward fierce dogmatism.

Many scientists and philosophers, writers and preachers resemble birds of beautiful plumage condemned to low flight among extensive thickets. Vigorous intelligences, temporarily frustrated by thick veils, are always threatened by painful surprises because they do not truly embrace the truths they themselves admit and teach.

As exporters of theories, they forget the treasures of practice, and hence the doubts and denials that sometimes assail their understanding. They expect the good they have not yet sown and demand patrimonies they have not built, due to neglecting themselves.

They manage to theorize valorously and counsel successfully, but in the great moments of life, they feel perplexed, confused, disheartened… This is because they lack true transformation for the good with Christ, and in order for them to truly feel eternal life with the Lord, it is indispensable that they convert to the service of redemption. Only when they reach such a spiritual summit do they free themselves from the heavy veils that obscure their heart and understanding, attaining the Higher Spheres in sublime flights toward the Divinity.

messages.title: Peter's Counsel
paragraphs: “Let him turn away from evil and do good; let him seek peace and pursue it.” — PETER (1 Peter, 3.11)
The great apostle's counsel for us to have happy days seems extremely simple due to its reduced number of words, but it reveals an immense field of obligations.

It is not easy to turn away from evil, embodied in the countless deviations of our soul through successive reincarnations, and it is very difficult to practice good within the harmful personal passions that grip our personality. We must also recognize that if we remain wrapped in the heavy tunic of our old whims, it is impossible to seek peace and pursue it.

Numerous evils—to which we have inclined along our evolutionary paths—have blinded us, and accustomed as we are to exclusivism and useless friction, wasting sacred energies, we do not know how to seek comforting tranquility. This is the real situation of the majority of the incarnate and a large part of the desencarnate who accommodate themselves to human circles, because physical death does not solve problems pertaining to the intimate forum of each individual.
Peter's word, therefore, acts as a generous challenge.
Our effort must converge toward the great achievement.

Though our ideal be torn or our soul wounded, let us turn away from evil and practice the good that is possible; let us identify true peace and follow it. And as soon as we attain the first expressions of the sublime service regarding our own edification, let us remember that it is not enough to avoid evil, but rather to distance ourselves from it, always sowing good; and that it is not merely worthwhile to desire peace, but to seek it and pursue it with all the persistence of our faith.

messages.title: On Pilgrimage
paragraphs: “For here we have no continuing city, but we seek the one to come.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 13.14)
Laughable is the instinct of wrongful appropriation that marks the majority of men.
Is the Earth not comparable to a great cosmic carriage where the spirit finds itself on an educational journey?
If a creature remains in material abundance, they are merely journeying in more comfortable quarters.
If they breathe in poverty, they are likewise traveling toward the same destination, despite the transient second-class condition.
If they present a remarkable physical appearance, they are only donning a fleeting garment of a more pleasant aspect for a short time on the journey undertaken.
If they exhibit less beautiful traits or features of evident imperfections, they are using attire as transient as the finest raiment of their neighbor on the ongoing pilgrimage.

No matter how much the impulse of ownership kindles fires of turmoil and discord in the machinery of the world, the reality is that no man possesses a permanent home on the soil of the Planet. All the material assets to which he clings, eager to possess, wear out and transform. In the goods he incorporates into his name, and even in the body he deems exclusively his, modifications occur every day, impelling him to renew and improve himself for eternity.

If you are not blind, therefore, to the laws of life, if you have already awakened to superior understanding, examine in good time where the train of human experience will leave you provisionally during the sudden stops of death.

messages.title: Let Us Guard the Heart
paragraphs: “He is a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.” — (JAMES, 1.8)
It is urgent to recognize that control of life resides within our feelings.
On the earthly journey, the paths leading to perfection are multiple.
Abundance and scarcity, beauty and ugliness, joy and suffering, freedom and restriction can all attract excellent possibilities of human achievement for the higher spirituality.
The double-hearted man, however, is unfaithful to divine blessings in all sectors of constructive struggle.
If he receives the talents of earthly wealth, he commonly surrenders to the hallucinations of vanity.
If he holds the gifts of poverty, he almost always binds himself to the monsters of non-acceptance.
If he possesses a beautiful body, he generally gives himself over to destructive excesses.
If he is endowed with a defective organic vessel, in most cases he wastes time in useless despair.
In pleasure, he is unrestrained. In pain, he is rebellious.
When free, he oppresses his brethren and enslaves them. When subordinate, he disturbs his fellows and instigates indiscipline.
Feeling is the sanctuary of the creature. Without light within, it is impossible to reflect the luminous peace that flows incessantly from Above.

Let us offer the Lord a firm and tender heart so that the Divine Hands may engrave His August Designs upon it. By attending to such a disposition in our intimate life, we will find the blessed place of co-workers of the Divine Will on all paths.

messages.title: With an Awakened Soul
paragraphs: “Therefore I remind you to stir up the gift of God which is in you.” — PAUL (2 Timothy, 1.6)
A great deal of willpower is indispensable so that we do not get lost indefinitely in the shadow of primitive impulses.
Faced with past millennia in our evolutionary field, we are susceptible to lingering for a long time on the slippery slopes of error, crystallizing attitudes out of harmony with the Eternal Laws.
So that we do not linger at the bottom of precipices, we have at our disposal the light of Divine Revelation—a gift from on high that we must never allow to be extinguished within us.

Given the extensive and heavy baggage of our needs for regeneration and perfection, temptations to stray arise with an overwhelming percentage over the suggestions to proceed on the straight path within spiritual ascension.
In the smallest activities of human struggle, the learner is influenced to remain in the dark.

In ordinary conversations, he is surrounded by slanderous and out-of-place insinuations. In habitual thoughts, he receives a thousand and one disorderly invitations from lower zones. In the application of justice, he is compelled to difficult recapitulations due to the excessive individualism of the past that seeks to perpetuate itself. In acts of labor, in obedience to the determinations of life, he is often led to seek undue rest. Even in nourishing the body, he is led to dangerous appeals toward imbalance.
For this reason, Paul advised his companion not to forget the need to awaken the "gift of God" upon the altar of the heart.

That man will suffer temptations, that he will fall many times, that he will be afflicted with disappointments and discouragements on the enlightening road—this admits of no doubt to any of us who are older brethren in greater experience; however, it is imperative that we march with an awakened soul, in the position of raising ourselves up and rebuilding whenever necessary.
May the shadows of the past scourge us, but may we never forget to rekindle our own light.

messages.title: Of Strong Courage
paragraphs: “For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of a sound mind.” — PAUL (2 Timothy, 1.7)
There is no lack of spiritual work resources for every brother who wishes to lift himself up, improve himself, and elevate himself.
Gaps and needs, problems and obstacles challenge the spirit of service among companions of faith everywhere.
Ignorance begs for instructors, pain calls for nurses, despair pleads for guides.
Where, however, are those who seek to embrace work for the love of serving?
With rare exceptions, we observe avoidance, pretexts, and withdrawal most of the time.
Here, there is fear of responsibility; there, dread of criticism; yonder, terror of taking the initiative for the benefit of all.
How can the artist make the beauty of the melody heard if the instrument flees from him?
In this case, we have Jesus as the divine artist and ourselves—incarnate and disincarnate—as His instruments for the eternal melody of good in the world.

If we chain our heart to the fear of working for collective benefit, how can we find finished work that tranquilizes and helps ourselves? How can we reap happiness we have not sown or amass gifts from which we timidly shrink?

Wherever there is the possibility of being useful, let us advance with strong courage, forging ahead and constructing good even when faced with irony, coldness, or ingratitude, because, according to the enlightened word of the apostle to the gentiles, "God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of a sound mind."

messages.title: In Our Struggle
paragraphs: “According to the authority which the Lord has given me for edification, and not for destruction.” — PAUL (2 Corinthians, 13.10)
In our daily struggle, let us exercise sufficient care in the use of the powers lent to us by the Lord.
Does the idea of destruction assail our minds on countless occasions?
Associations of forces less enlightened in goodness and truth?
We are tempted to set processes of annihilation into motion.
Companions less desirable in our daily labors?
We intend to abandon them completely.
Hardened co-workers?
Leaving them destitute.
Passionate outbursts out of step with the imperatives of evangelical prudence?
Our initial impulses sum up to purposes of violent suppression.
Something that contradicts our personal ideas and programs?
Our crystallized intolerance calls for destruction.
However, what is the purpose of the powers resting in our hands in the name of the Divine Giver?
Paul of Tarsus answers us very appropriately, explaining that he received faculties from the Lord to build up and not to destroy.
We are not in the world's work to annihilate what is imperfect, but to complete what is unfinished.
Let us renew for the good, let us transform for the light.
The Supreme Father does not grant us powers to disseminate death. Our mission is one of indefatigable love for Abundant Life.

messages.title: See, Then
paragraphs: “Therefore take heed that the light which is in you is not darkness.” — JESUS (Luke, 11.35)
There is science and there is wisdom, intelligence and knowledge, intellectuality and spiritual light.
Generally, any person of facile reasoning is considered wiser; however, one must make a distinction.
Man does not yet possess the qualities to register true light. Hence the need for prudence and vigilance.
In all places, there are industrious and knowledgeable people, experts and psychologists. Often, however, they are nothing more than opportunists ready for a strike of base self-interest.
How many write abominable books, spreading poison in hearts? How many take advantage of the label of charity itself with the aim of extracting benefits for their ambition?
Ingenuity and skill are not enough. Simple psychological vision is not satisfactory. Divine light is needed.

There are men who, in an instant, grasp the entire extent of a field, know its soil, and identify its value. There are few men, however, who perceive all this and are willing to sweat for it, loving it before exploring it, granting it understanding before demanding anything.
Light does not always reside where common opinion claims to observe it.
Sagacity does not amount to elevation, and expressive power is only respectable and sacred when it becomes constructive action infused with divine light.
Reason, therefore, concerning your own life.
See clearly whether the pretended clarity within you is not the shadow of spiritual blindness.

messages.title: It Is Not Enough to See
paragraphs: “And immediately he received his sight, and followed Him, glorifying God. And all the people, when they saw it, gave praise to God.” — (LUKE, 18.43)
The attitude of the blind man of Jericho represents a high standard for every sincere disciple of the Gospel.

The well-meaning sick person first seeks the Master before the multitude. Following the healing, he accompanies Jesus, glorifying God. And all the people, observing the benefit, gratitude, and fidelity combined, turn toward trust in the Divine Power.

The majority of those in need, however, assume a very different position. Almost all the sick demand the action of Christ, requiring that the gift descend to the pernicious whims peculiar to them, without any effort to elevate themselves to the Master's blessing.
Rare are those who seek Christ in the midday light; and of all those who receive His gifts, extremely rare are those who follow in His footsteps in the world.
Hence stems the absence of legitimate glorification to God and the incomplete healing of the blindness that obscured them prior to their first contact with faith.
Because of this, the Earth is replete with those who believe and disbelieve, study and do not learn, hope and despair, teach and do not know, trust and doubt.
He who receives gifts may be merely a beneficiary.
He who receives the favor and gives thanks for it, however—seeing the light and following it—shall be redeemed.

It is obvious that the entire world cries out for vision with Christ, but it is not enough simply to see; those who restrict themselves to the act of beholding may be good narrators, excellent statisticians, but in order to see and glorify the Lord it is indispensable to walk in Christ's footsteps, climbing with Him the mountain of work and testimony.

messages.title: What Do You Ask For?
paragraphs: “Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee.” — JESUS (Luke, 12.20)
What do you ask of life?
The ambitious demand reserves of millions.
The selfish demand all satisfactions for themselves alone.
The vain demand praise.
The envious demand the compensations that are not rightfully theirs.
The resentful solicit undue consideration.
The idle ask for prosperity without effort.
The foolish demand entertainment without any concern for service.
The rebellious cry out for rights without duties.
The extravagant demand health without care.
The impatient solicit achievements without foundations.
The insatiable ask for all goods, forgetting the needs of others.
Essentially considering, however, all this is true madness, all fantasy of the heart that has thrown itself exclusively upon the ephemeral possession of mutable things.
Watch carefully, therefore, over the plan of your desires.
What do you ask of life? Do not forget that, perhaps this night, the Lord will ask for your soul.
This message was originally published in 1950 by LAKE and is the 25th lesson of Part 1 of the book “Nosso livro”

messages.title: Factionalism
paragraphs: “But if ye have bitter envying and strife in your hearts, glory not, and lie not against the truth.” — (JAMES, 3.14)
Every religious school presents unmistakable values to the person of good will.

Notwithstanding the abuses of the priesthood, the inferior exploitation of the human element, and the fantasies of external worship, the sincere heart will benefit amply at the source of faith, illuminating itself to find the Divine Consciousness within itself.
However, in every strictly human religious institute, one danger must be avoided — the factional sentiment, which indefinitely postpones the most sublime spiritual edifications.
Catholics, Protestants, Spiritists, all of them move about, threatened by the monster of separation, as if religious thought translated the leaven of discord.
Unfortunately, the number of incarnate leaders who let themselves be dominated by its disturbing claws is very great. Thick obstacles impede the vision of the majority.
They all want God to belong to them, but they do not consider belonging to God.

May every apprentice of Christ be prepared to resist evil; it is imperative, however, that they understand the divine paternity as the sacred heritage of all creatures, recognizing that, in the Father's House, the only difference between men is that which is measured by each one's noble effort.

messages.title: Guidance
paragraphs: “And that ye study to be quiet, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands, as we commanded you.” — PAUL (1 Thessalonians, 4.11)
At every step, we find brothers anxious for new guidance within the circles of evangelical learning.

Valuable services and excellent programs of higher spirituality experience severe delays waiting for the untimely and repeated pleas of those who neglect their assumed commitments to end. We speak thus in the presence of all those who propose to serve Jesus sincerely, because, undeniably, the Christian guidelines have long been traced, waiting for industrious hands to firmly materialize them.

May each disciple maintain the portion of relative peace that the Master has conferred upon them, may each one take care of the business that concerns them and work with the hands they were born with in the conquest of higher expressions of life, and they will build a lofty spiritual residence for themselves.

He who preserves harmony at the cost of untiring good attends to the Lord's designs within the circle of individual commitments and the human family; he who attends to his own business properly discharges social obligations without being a burden to the interests of others, and he who works with his own hands finds the luminous path of glorious eternity.
Before seeking any guidance, therefore, from incarnate or desencarnate friends, do not forget to verify whether you have already attended to this.

messages.title: Little Services
paragraphs: “And be ye kind one to another.” — PAUL (Ephesians, 4.32)
A large mass of learners sometimes complains about the absence of great opportunities in the services of the world.
Here is someone disgruntled for not having obtained a highly relevant position; further along is a restless brother because he has not yet managed to place his name in the major press.
The majority go about forgetting the value of small works which usually translate into a gesture of good manners, a fraternal and comforting smile…
A glass of pure water,
silence in the face of evil that does not call for immediate clarification,
a sanctifying book given with love,
a affectionate sentence,
the transport of a small burden,
the suggestion of good,
tolerance in the face of tiresome conversation,
free favors of a few cents,
a spontaneous gift, however humble,
natural kindness, constitute services of great value that rare people take into fair consideration.

What does the blindness of the receiver matter? What can the malevolence of ungrateful creatures signify in the face of the affective impulse of good hearts? How often, in times past, were we equally blind and perverse toward Christ, who has dispensed all courtesies to us, both large and small?
Do not torment yourself to obtain the opportunity to appear on the huge billboards of the world. This can translate into much difficulty and perturbation for your spirit, now or later.
Be benevolent toward those who surround you.
Do not belittle useful little services. In them rests the well-being of the daily path for all those gathered in human experience.

messages.title: In What Do You Persevere?
paragraphs: “And they continued stedfastly in the apostles' doctrine and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers.” — (ACTS, 2.42)
Less observant onlookers pretend to find a complete negation of spirituality in the current events of the Planet.
They believe that the era of sublime revelations is dead, that the heavenly gates remain closed forever.

And they comment with enthusiasm, as if catching a glimpse of a lost paradise, upon the radiances of apostolic times, when a handful of Christians renewed the secular principles of the most powerful empire in the world.
Many assert that Heaven has stanched the source of gifts, forgetting that the general run of believers has dulled the capacity to receive.

Where is the courage that clothed humble hearts in the face of the circus lions? Where is the faith that put immortal statements in the wounded mouths of anonymous martyrs? Where are the public signs of heavenly voices? Where are the cleansed lepers and the cured blind?
The Lord's opportunities continue to flow, incessantly, over the Earth.
The Father's mercy has not changed. Divine Providence is invariable in all times.

The attitude of Christians today, however, is very different. Very few persevere in the apostles' doctrine, in fellowship with the Gospel, in the spirit of fraternity, in the services of living faith. The majority prefer so-called “points of view,” commune with destructive personalism, strengthen the root of selfishness, and reason without spiritual illumination.
The Lord's Goodness is constant and imperishable.
Let us observe, therefore, in which direction we are persevering.
Before applauding the most audacious, let us seek to know whether we are with the fickleness of men or with the immutability of Christ.

messages.title: Faith
paragraphs: “And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.” — JESUS (Mark, 4.19)
The tree of living faith does not grow in the heart miraculously.
As happens in ordinary life, the Creator gives everything, but does not dispense with the creature's effort.
Any useful plant demands special attention during its development.

It is indispensable to consider the work of protection, assistance, and defense. Stakes, fertilizers, vigilance, all preservation factors must be set in motion so that the precious plant reaches the ends for which it is intended.
The conquest of edifying belief is not a task of minor effort.
Most people admit that faith constitutes a miraculous halo bestowed upon certain Spirits privileged by divine favor. This, however, is a misconception with regrettable consequences.
The sublime virtue is a construction of the inner world, in the unfolding of which each learner functions as the guide, engineer, and worker of themselves.
Realization is not possible when excessive earthly anxieties, partnered with deceptions and inferior ambitions, torture the intimate field, like worms and evildoers, attacking the work.
The Gospel lesson is a living seed. The human heart is as receptive as the soil.
It is imperative to treat the divine plant with devoted tenderness and an energetic instinct of defense.
There are many subtle dangers against it, such as the toxins of bad books, idle opinions, exciting discussions, and the habit of analyzing others before self-examination.
No one can, therefore, in good conscience, transfer the vibration of faith in its entirety to another's spirit, because, truly, this is a task that belongs to everyone.

messages.title: Different Creditors
paragraphs: “But I say unto you, Love your enemies.” — JESUS (Matthew, 5.44)
The problem of the enemy always deserves closer study.
Certainly, no one can adhere immediately to complete union with today's adversary, just as Jesus could not laugh with His persecutors during the martyrdom of Calvary.
However, the Lord's warning, calling us to love our enemies, is clothed with profound significance in every facet through which we examine it, mobilizing the instruments of common analysis.

Generally, we are debtors of high benefits to all those who persecute and slander us; they constitute the instruments that work upon our individuality, compelling us to high-reaching renewals that we rarely understand during the gravest moments of experience. They are the ones who point out our weaknesses, deficiencies, and needs to be met in the task we are executing.
Friends are, on many occasions, improvident companions, inasmuch as they temporize with evil; adversaries, however, confront it with vigor.
Through the rudeness of the enemy, a person commonly turns red and indignant only once, but through the complacency of loved ones, they become pale and cast down countless times.
We do not mean by this that a creature should cultivate enmities; however, we are among those who recognize as meritorious creditors all those who proclaim our faults.
They are courageous doctors who provide us with correction.
It is difficult for many people on Earth to accept such a truth; nevertheless, an instant always arrives when we understand the appeal of Christ in its grand extension.

messages.title: Affirmation and Action
paragraphs: “Jesus saith unto them, My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, and to finish his work.” — (JOHN, 4.34)

Here and there, we find believers of the Gospel invariably ready to claim the good intention of satisfying heavenly dictates. Some give themselves over to idleness and discouragement and, with manifest disrespect for the sacred notions of faith, assure friend or neighbor that they live by attending to the determinations of the Almighty.
There are not a few who neither foresee nor provide in time, and when everything collapses, when inferior forces triumph, behold, in tears, they declare that the orders of the Most High were obeyed.
Regarding the Father's action, however, it must be recognized that if there is a manifestation of His will, there is simultaneously an objective and purpose consequent to it.
A lofty program without materialization is a dead project.
God would not express purposes at random. Because of this, Jesus stated that He came into the world to do the Father's will and accomplish His work.
As we observe, He was referring not only to the paternal desire, but equally to the execution that pertained to Him.
It is not reasonable for a person to remain in endless references to the designs from on High when they do not consider materializing their own task.

The Father naturally keeps impenetrable plans concerning each child. It is imperative, however, that the creature cooperate in the objectification of divine purposes within themselves, understanding that it is a regrettable abuse to make frequent mention of the will of God while living distracted from the work that is incumbent upon us.

messages.title: Ye Therefore…
paragraphs: “Ye therefore, beloved, seeing ye know these things before, beware lest ye also, being led away with the error of the wicked, fall from your own stedfastness.” — PETER (2 Peter, 3.17)
Intimate enlightenment is the inalienable treasure of sincere disciples of Christ.

The world is full of errors by abominable men who have invaded the domains of politics, science, and religion, and have erected shocking creations for less observant spirits; souls numbering in the millions are carried away by them to the surprises of death and are absolutely unbalanced in the circles of spiritual life. From the false summit of their individualistic notions, they plunge into terrifying precipices, where they lose their firmness and light.

A great number of the improvident find rightful help, because they were unaware of their true situation. They were not properly informed. The abominable men concealed the real meaning of life from them.
Such benevolence, however, cannot reach learners who already know the truth beforehand.

The Gospel student will feed upon deplorable errors only if they wish to. They will therefore spin in the whirlwind of shadows if they fall into it voluntarily, in the chapter of individual preference.
The ignorant will attain justification. The victim will be set free. The unprotected sick person will receive nursing and medicine.

But the disciple of Jesus, touched by the benefits of Heaven every day, who surrounds himself with enlightenment and consolation, lights and blessings, must know beforehand how much he is responsible for accomplishing in service and vigilance, and, should he accept the illusions of abominable men, he will act under his own responsibility, entering into the sharing of the distressing realities that await him in the lower Planes.

messages.title: Knowing As One Ought to Know
paragraphs: “And if any man think that he knoweth any thing, he knoweth nothing yet as he ought to know.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 8.2)
Civilization always takes care to know excessively, but at no time has it known as it ought to know.
This is why, even now, the airplane bombs, the radio transmits lies and death, and fuel feeds machinery for aggression.
Thus also, in the individual sphere, man merely considers knowing, forgetting that it is indispensable to know as one ought to know.
In our evangelical activities, all attention is necessary for success in the task entrusted to us.

There are Gospel learners who pretend to keep all the revelation of Heaven in order to impose it on their neighbors; who presume to possess humility in order to tyrannize others; who declare themselves patient while irritating whoever listens to them; who affirm themselves believers while confounding the faith of others; who exhibit titles of beneficence while forgetting ordinary domestic obligations.
These friends, principally, are among those who think they know without actually knowing.

Those who spiritually understand situations help without offending, improve without wounding, clarify without disturbing. They know as they ought to know and have learned to be useful. They use silence and the word, locate good and evil, identify shadow and light, and distribute the gifts of Christ with everyone. They inform themselves regarding the Source of Eternal Wisdom and connect themselves to it like perfect lamps to the center of force. Failures and triumphs, in the Plane of temporary forms, do not modify their energies. These know because they know and use their own knowledge as one ought to know.

messages.title: Essential Need
paragraphs: “But I have prayed for you, that your faith should not fail.” — JESUS (Luke, 22:32)

It is fair to highlight that Jesus, aware that Simon remained in a world where material advantages prevail, did not intercede with the Father so that he would not lack physical resources, such as bodily satisfaction, substantial remuneration, or social standing.
The Master declares that He asked the Supreme Lord that Peter's gift of faith might not weaken.
Thus, Christ emphasized the essential need of the human creature regarding trust in God, within a circle of struggles where all visible benefits are subject to transformation and death.

He testified that, of all the sublime achievements of modern man, living and active faith is among the most difficult to consolidate. He recognized that the spiritual security of earthly companions is not the work of a few days, because tiny events can interrupt it, wound it, postpone it. The ingratitude of a friend, an unthoughtful gesture, someone's misunderstanding, an insignificant difficulty can harm its development.

In the very workshop of human labor, therefore, you must recognize the transience of all transferable goods that surround you. Always mobilize them, heeding the superior designs of fraternity that teach us to love one another with fidelity and devotion. Convince yourself, however, that living faith in the final victory of the eternal spirit is the divine oil that sustains our inner light for divine ascension.

messages.title: Grow
paragraphs: “Instead, grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.” — PETER (2 Peter, 3:18)
A prominent position constantly preoccupies the mind of man.
Even the beggar, ragged and hungry, often remains proud, in expectation of prominence in Heaven.
Usually, however, all anxiety in this regard is a poorly directed purpose aiming at growth in reverse.
It would not strictly be the act of developing, but of swelling.

Along these same lines, many restless learners plead for high financial compensation, favors of easy money, elevation to posts of authority, invoking the need to grow for greater efficiency in Christ's service.
This, however, is almost always pure illusion.
Once the demands materialize, they turn into servants surrounded by impediments.

The Divine Master, who organized planetary life under the influx of the Eternal Father, possesses sufficient power and, to execute His work, would not delay waiting for this or that learner to become a specialist in certain worldly business.
The growth to which the Gospel refers must be guided by Christian virtue and knowledge of the divine will.

Let each one learn their part within the sphere of our duties with Jesus. Attend to the edifying program that is incumbent upon you, even if you find yourself alone or persecuted by the misunderstanding of men, and then you will be growing in grace and discernment for immortal life.

messages.title: The People and the Gospel
paragraphs: “And they could not find what they might do, for all the people hung upon Him, listening to Him.” — (LUKE, 19:48)
Persecution of the postulates of Christianity is of all times.
Even in the days of the Divine Master, in carnal circles, hostilities of every shade were already externalizing against the movements of Christian enlightenment.

On all occasions, however, it has been possible to observe the gravitation of the people toward Jesus. Between Him and the multitude, the powerful magnetism of virtue and love has never been extinguished.

In vain do draconian measures of ignorance and cruelty arise, in vain do the ecclesiastical prejudices of the priesthood appear when without light in their sublime mission of guiding; presumptuous scientists, demagogues bribed by petty interests, clamor in the squares for the consecration of brilliant fantasies.
The people, however, lean toward Christ with the same fascination as on the first day. Undoubtedly, considered as a whole, we are still far from union with Jesus in an integral sense.
From time to time, the mob experiences horrifying disasters. Storms of blood and tears sweep across its paths.
The Master's clarity, however, beckons from a distance. The old and children identify His sanctified glow.
The politicians of the world formulate a thousand promises to the spirit of the masses; rare people, however, take an interest in such platforms.
The Lord's statements, nonetheless, are renewed in every century, ever higher to the popular mind, translating consolations and immortal appeals.

messages.title: Let Us Cooperate Faithfully
paragraphs: “For we are God's fellow workers.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 3:9)
The Father is the Supreme Creator of Life, but man can be His faithful co-worker.
God visits the creature through the creature itself.
Souls closed in upon themselves will declare themselves incapable of noble services; they will affirm themselves impoverished or incompetent.

There are companions who reach the absurdity of proclaiming themselves so sinful and so bad that they feel unable to offer any kind of healthy contribution to the Christian work, as if debtors and the ignorant did not need to work on their own improvement.
The doors of collaboration with divine love, however, remain constantly open, and any person of median reason can identify the call to divine service.
Let us cultivate good, eliminating evil.
Let us make light where darkness reigns.
Let us bring harmony to zones of discord.
Let us help ignorance with fraternal enlightenment.
May love for our neighbor be our essential basis in every construction on the evolutionary path.

Until now, we have been a burden to the economy of life. Prodigal children before the Divine Budget, we have spent precious energies in numerous existences, diverting them to the dark terrain of difficult rectifications or the expiatory prison.
It seems to us, therefore, according to the knowledge we possess, by "excess of mercy," that it is time to cooperate faithfully with God in the performance of our humble task.

messages.title: Exhorted to Battle
paragraphs: “Beloved, while I was very diligent to write to you concerning our common salvation, I found it necessary to write to you exhorting you to contend earnestly for the faith which was once for all delivered to the saints.” — (JUDE, 3)
Christianity is an immense field of spiritual life, to which the worker is called for sublime renewal.

The thirsty find within it the sources of "living water," the hungry, the barns of the "eternal bread." The blind in understanding receive within it the vision of the path; the lepers of the soul, relief and healing.

All travelers of life, however, are blessed with the resources indispensable to the earthly journey, with the purpose of truly rising in Him who is the Light of the Ages. From then on, restored in their spiritual energies, they are exhorted to battle in the great cause of good.
Let no one be deceived, therefore, in the generous and active workshop of faith.
In Christian service, let every learner remember that they were not called to rest, but to the arduous struggle in which the demonstration of individual effort is a divine imperative.
Jesus initiated, within the circle of incarnate intelligences, the greatest movement of liberation of the human spirit on the first day of the Manger.

Let not those who seek the Master of Masters be mistaken... They will certainly receive the expected illumination, edifying consolation, and effective teaching, but they will enter the battle line where permanent combat for the victory of love and truth on Earth constitutes an obligation, through harsh testimonies, because all of us, incarnate and discarnate, still oscillating between animality and spirituality, between the valley of man and the summit of Christ, are constrained to battle until definitive triumph over ourselves for the possession of Immortal Life.

messages.title: Toward the Goal
paragraphs: “I press toward the goal.” — PAUL (Philippians, 3:14)
When Paul wrote to the Philippians, he already possessed vast apostolate experience.
A Doctor of the Law in Jerusalem, he had abandoned the vanities of race and family, surrendering to the Master in sanctifying humility.

After dominating through physical power, intellectual culture, and noble intelligence, he turned to the obscure loom, earning his own sustenance with daily sweat. Entering thorny testimonies to serve his neighbor out of love for Jesus, he received the irony and abandonment of relatives, the distrust and insult of old friends, the lashes of malice and the stones of misunderstanding.
The convert of Damascus, however, never wavered, proceeding invariably toward the goal, which is still and always the divine union of the disciple with the Master.
How many learners are currently disposed to the great example?

In vain do invitations to the sublime banquet spread; in vain does Jesus send messengers to new students, revealing the excellence of superior life. Most of them, however, comprise fugitive workers, fully distracted from accomplishment... They lose sight of the work to be done, disinterest themselves in necessary lessons, and forget the purposes of remaining on Earth. Commonly, at the first stronger obstacles of the march, at the initial corrections of service, they burst into tears of despair, overwhelmed and sad. They declare themselves, incomprehensibly, discouraged, defeated, hopeless...

The explanation is simple, however. They lost their course toward Christ, seduced by fleeting spectacles at the numerous stations of the spiritual journey, and, by forgetting the sublime goal, the moment inevitably arrives when, the motives of transitory fascination having ceased, they feel anguished, like thirsty travelers in the arid deserts of human life.

messages.title: Not Being Ashamed
paragraphs: “For whoever is ashamed of Me and My words, of him the Son of Man will be ashamed.” — JESUS (Luke, 9:26)

There are many learners who are satisfied with themselves solely because of a few quixotic assertions. They gather in grand discussions, quarrelsome and irascible, trying to convince everyone regarding religious faith, and when questioned about the fury in which they delight in imposing their own points of view, they usually retort that it is imperative not to be ashamed of the Master nor of His teachings before the multitude.
Sometimes, however, the concern to preserve Christianity is nothing more than a merely verbal position.
