Such defenders of Christ forget that, above all, it is essential not to forget His sublime principles before the tasks of each day.
A man's life is his own public confession.
The conduct of each believer is their true profession of faith.

The thunder of the voice and verbalistic mimicry, children of individual vanity, alongside incomprehending and complacent listeners, are very childish, accompanied by full forgetfulness of the necessary testimonies with the Master in the workshop of common labor and the purifying home.

It becomes indispensable for the learner of Jesus not to be ashamed, not in heated disputes from which each contender returns more exasperated, but rather before situations, seemingly insignificant or eminently expressive, in which the believer is asked for the example of love, renunciation, and personal sacrifice that the Lord demonstrated in His sublime trajectory.

messages.title: Avarice
paragraphs: “And He said to them, ‘Take heed and beware of covetousness, for one's life does not consist in the abundance of the things he possesses.’” — (LUKE, 12:15)
Let us flee from retaining any possibility without the spirit of service.
Avarice does not consist merely in hoarding money in the coffers of pettiness.

Nature's very beneficent waters, when imprisoned without the concern of being beneficial, tend to form infectious zones. Whoever lives in search of compensations, gathering them around themselves, is likewise no more than an unhappy miser.
All avarice is unhealthy centralization, preparing goals of suffering.

It is not enough to know how to ask, nor is skill and efficiency in conquering enough. It is necessary to acquire in the climate of Christ, spreading the benefits of temporary possession so that existence itself does not constitute an obstacle to the peace and joy of others.

Countless men, attacked by the virus of avarice, gained much in fortune, authority, and intelligence, but only achieved, at the end of the experience, the perversion of those they loved most and the hatred of those who were their neighbors.
They piled up advantages for their own ruin. They ruined themselves, poisoning as well those who shared their tasks in the world.
Let us remember the word of the Divine Master, engraving it upon the spirit.
Man's life does not consist in the abundance of what he possesses, but in the abundance of benefits he scatters and sows, attending to the designs of the Supreme Lord.

messages.title: Sowings and Harvests
paragraphs: “For he who sows to his flesh will of the flesh reap corruption.” — PAUL (Galatians, 6:8)
We will plant every day. It is the law.
Even the inactive and idle are cultivating the tares of improvidence.
It is necessary to recognize, however, that we will harvest daily.
There are vegetables that produce within the course of a brief few weeks; others, however, only reveal fruits in the laborious passage of much time.
In all eras, the mob creates complications of a material nature, accentuating the labyrinth of painful reincarnations, lingering in the difficulties of decadence.

Even today, there are those who intend to honor with someone else's blood and wash away injustice with the reprisals of crime. Hence, yesterday's hatred generating today's wars, personal ambition forming the misery that is to come, easy pleasures demanding tomorrow's rectifications.

To this day, after more than nineteen centuries of Christianity, only a few disciples, from time to time, understand the need for sowing spiritual light within themselves—different from all those known in the world—and advance toward the Master of Masters.
If you wish, therefore, my friend, to plant in the Divine Crop, flee from the old system of sowing in corruption and reaping in decadence. Cultivate good for eternal life.
Observe the multitudes, imprisoned in the old process of rising for error and falling for correction, and follow the path toward the Lord, organizing your own acquisitions of immortal gifts.

messages.title: Pharisees
paragraphs: “Beware first of the leaven of the Pharisees.” — JESUS (Luke, 12:1)
A Pharisee is still any presumptuous, dogmatic, exclusive man, a supposed privileged one of the Divine Forces.

The proud descendant of the doctors of Jerusalem still lives. He crosses all human organizations. He breathes in all earthly temples. He believes himself the sole heir of Divine Goodness. He appreciates nothing except through the prism of personal pride. He draws up capricious programs and attempts to twist universal laws themselves, submitting them to the point of view he espoused in his school or sectarian argument.

He never appears before the Lord's blessing as someone who has become an instrument of His loving designs, but as a proud believer, full of individualistic purposes, declaring himself the holder of special considerations.
Faithful learners need to guard against the leaven of such sick souls. Every idea operates mental fermentations.
Certainly the Master did not order the death of the Pharisees, but He recommended caution when dealing with their influence.

Pharisaic demands constitute dangerous illnesses of the soul. It is urgent to help the sick person and extinguish the disease. However, we will not achieve this by provoking tumults, but by using caution in the ancient recommendation of vigilance.

messages.title: Free Church
paragraphs: “But the Jerusalem which is above is free, which is the mother of us all.” — PAUL (Galatians, 4:26)
The isolated examination of this verse suggests a theme of infinite greatness for the religious disciples of Christianity.
The apostle's word to the Gentiles reminds us of the liberated church of Christ, not within the narrow sphere of men, but in the unlimited divine thought.
The proud and sectarian spirit, for so long dominant in the activities of faith, finds in the assertion of Paul of Tarsus an antidote to its poisonous concerns.
In all eras, noble excommunicated ones, valued misunderstood ones, and sublime slandered ones have lived on Earth.
They have passed through the circles of creatures, just as happens today, persecuted and despised, amid sarcasm and indifference.

At times, they suffer social banishment for not debasing themselves before the criminal exploitations of fanaticism; on other occasions, they are categorized as atheists because of their misunderstood ideas.
This is because, from time to time, gusts of hatred and doubt blow through the unsuspecting churches of Earth. Believers forget "judge not" and entrust themselves to distressing struggles.

Such clashes, however, do not alter the tranquil conscience of the anathematized who feel under the tutelage of Divine Power. Instinctively, they recognize that beyond the obscure sphere of physical action shines the sovereign and invisible temple in which Jesus gathers faithful servants, without lingering over the color or style of their garments.

Benefactors and excommunicated servants of human paths, if you have a spotless conscience, do not be hurt by the stone-throwing of men who distance themselves from one another through unhappy separatism! There is an august and free Church in spiritual life, which is the welcoming mother of all of us!...

messages.title: The Greatest
paragraphs: “And He sat down, called the twelve and said to them: If anyone wants to be first, he shall be last of all and servant of all.” — (MARK, 9:35)
Being among the first on Earth is not a problem with a complicated solution. There are those who consider themselves the greatest in the world in every situation.
Science, philosophy, the priesthood, as well as politics, commerce, and finance can easily exhibit them.

The leading men of science, with legitimate exceptions, tend to be greatly presumptuous; those of philosophy, astute sophists of thought; those of priesthood, fanatics without understanding of true faith. In politics, many of the greatest are tyrants; in commerce, countless are exploiters, and in finance, many of them are nothing more than associates of the shadows against collective interests.
Being first, however, in the spheres of Jesus on Earth, is not a matter of easy access for the vulgar creature.
In the departments of the materialized world, the principal ones must be the first to be served and count on the compulsory obedience of all.
In pure Christianity, dominant spirits are the last in the reception of benefits, for they are true servants of all those who seek their fraternal collaboration.

This is why in all Christian schools there are numerous preachers, many stewards, crowds of workers, co-workers of the cult, valuable polemicists, doctors of the letter, competent interpreters, passionate reformers, but very rare apostles.

Generally speaking, almost all believers set themselves up for teaching and counseling, ready for spectacular combat and humiliating or vain admonition, with few appearing with the desire to serve, in silence, convinced that all glory belongs to God.

messages.title: Do Not Withdraw
paragraphs: “But deliver us from evil.” — JESUS (Matthew, 6:13)
The surface of the world is, undeniably, the great school of incarnate Spirits.
It is impossible to gather the teaching while fleeing from the lesson. No one knows without learning.

A large number of disciples of the Gospel, upon glimpsing a few rays of spiritual light, declare themselves open enemies of earthly experience. From then on, they shy away from the noblest testimonies. They defend themselves against men, as if these were not their brothers on the evolutionary path. They see thorns where the flower blooms, and venomous wounds where there is innocent laughter. And, condemning the landscape to which they were led by the Lord for methodical service in goodness, they withdraw with lowered eyes, shrinking from the effort of sanctification.

They declare themselves, however, desirous of union with Christ, forgetting that the Master does not forsake Humanity. They especially cherish prayer, but, repeating the sublime words of the Lord's Prayer, they forget that Jesus prayed to the Supreme Lord to free us from evil, but did not ask for withdrawal from the struggle.

Moreover, the wisdom of Christianity does not consist in insulating the learner in artificial holiness, but rather in casting them into the open sea of the active contribution of transforming evil into good, darkness into light, and pain into blessing.

The Master did not flee from the disciples; rather, they fled from Him in the ultimate testimony. The Divine Servant did not distance Himself from men; rather, they expelled Him through painful crucifixion.
Fidelity to the end does not mean perpetual adoration in a literal sense; it also translates to a spirit of service until the last day of usable strength in the physiological mechanism.

If you wish, therefore, to serve with the Lord Jesus, ask Him to free you from evil, but not to remove you from the places of struggle, so that you may learn, in His company, to cooperate in the execution of the Heavenly Will, when, how, and wherever necessary.

messages.title: Crises
paragraphs: “Father, save me from this hour; but for this purpose I came to this hour.” — JESUS (John, 12:27)
The lesson of Jesus, in this passage of the Gospel, is one of the most expressive.

The Master was about to experience the abandonment of loved ones, the ingratitude of yesterday's beneficiaries, the irony of the crowd, public mockery, torture, and the cross, but He knew He was there for this very purpose, according to the designs of the Eternal.
He asks for the Father's protection and submits in the condition of a faithful son.
He examines the gravity of the current hour, yet recognizes the necessity of the testimony.
And all lives on Earth will experience the same steps on the infinite scale of necessary experiences.
All beings and things prepare themselves, considering the crises to come. It is the crisis that decides the future.
The earth awaits the plow.
The ore will be sent to the crucible.
The tree will suffer pruning.
The worm will be subjected to sunlight.
The bird will face the storm.
The sheep will await the shearing.
Man will be led into the struggle.
The Christian will know successive testimonies.
This is why we see, in the divine service of the Master, the crisis of the cross accompanied by the eternal blessing of the Resurrection.

When you find yourself in immense struggle, therefore, remember that the Lord has led you to such a position of sacrifice, considering the probability of your exaltation, and do not forget that every crisis is a sublime source of renewing spirit for those who know how to have hope.

messages.title: Divine Politics
paragraphs: “Yet I am among you as one who serves.” — JESUS (Luke, 22:27)
The sincere disciple of the Gospel does not need to breathe the climate of the world's administrative politics to fulfill the ministry entrusted to them.

The Governor of the Earth, among us, to fulfill the objectives of the politics of love, represented, above all, the interests of God close to the human heart, without the need for ordinances and decrees, however respectable.
He administered by serving, He elevated others by humbling Himself.
He wore neither the priest's robe nor the magistrate's toga.
He deeply loved his fellow men and, in that sublime task, bore witness to His celestial greatness.
What would become of Christian organizations if the apostolate pertaining to them were subordinated to kings and ministers, chambers and transitory parliaments?
If you wish to effectively enter the temple of truth and living faith, of peace and love, with Jesus, do not forget the platforms of the Redeeming Gospel.
Love God above all things, with all your heart and understanding.
Love your neighbor as yourself.
Cease the selfishness of primitive animality.
Do good to those who do you evil.
Bless those who persecute and slander you.
Pray for the peace of those who hurt you.
Praise those who thwart your heart inclined to the inferior past.
Share the joys of your spirit and the gifts of your life with the less fortunate and poorest along the way.
Dissipate the darkness by making your light shine.
Reveal the love that calms the storms of hatred.
Keep the flame of hope alive where the cold of discouragement blows.
Raise the fallen.
Be the benevolent crutch of those dragging themselves under moral disabilities.
Fight ignorance by lighting lamps of fraternal aid, without blows of criticism and without shouts of condemnation.
Love, understand, and forgive always.
Will you perhaps depend on human decrees to set your hand to the work?

Remember, my friend, that the administrators of the world are, most of the time, venerable agents of Immortal Wisdom, supporting the economic potentials, temporary and perishable, of the world; however, do not forget the recommendations outlined in the Code of Eternal Life, in the execution of which we must build the Divine Kingdom within ourselves.

messages.title: What Do You Do That is Special?
paragraphs: “What do you do more than others?” — JESUS (Matthew, 5:47)
Initiated into the light of the New Revelation, Christian Spiritualists possess assets of understanding far above the normal comprehension of incarnate men.
Indeed, they know that life continues victoriously beyond death;
that they are in the temporary school of Earth, for the sake of the spiritual illumination they need;
that the fleshly body is a simple garment wearing out each day;
that the labors and sorrows of the world are educational resources;
that pain is the stimulus to the highest achievements;
that our future harvest will take place according to our sowing now;
that the Lord's light will clear our paths whenever we are in the service of good;
that every opportunity for work in the present is a blessing from the Divine Powers;
that no one is on the Planet's Crust on an easy pleasure excursion, but rather on a mission of self-improvement;
that justice is not an illusion and that truth will surprise everyone;
and that existence in the physical Sphere is a blessed workshop of labor, redemption, and ransom;
and that the acts, words, and thoughts of the creature will always produce the fruits corresponding to them, in the infinite field of life.
Indeed, we know all of this.

In view, therefore, of so much knowledge and information from the higher Planes, benefiting our happy circles of spiritual work, is it just that we hear the interrogation of the Divine Master: — What do you do more than others?

messages.title: You Too
paragraphs: “But the chief priests resolved to put Lazarus to death as well.” — (JOHN, 12:10)
It is interesting to observe the musings of Pharisaism regarding Lazarus during the supreme hours of Jesus.
The Master's crucifixion was not enough. They also intended the death of the friend of Bethany.

Lazarus had been a corpse and had revived, had been buried in the darkness of the tomb and had returned to the light of life. He was, therefore, a permanent glorification of the Savior, an undeniable healing by the Divine Physician. He constituted a living charter of Christ's power in Jerusalem, he did not fit in with his compatriots, he had become different.
His destruction was therefore considered indispensable.

The Pharisaism of old times is still the same in passing days, with the only difference being that Jerusalem is entire civilization. For it, the Master must remain crucified, and all Lazaruses will rise sentenced to death.
Any man renewed in Christ disturbs it.
There are participants of the Gospel who feel truly resurrected, brought to the clarity of faith after crossing the sepulcher of hatred, crime, and indifference...

Pharisaism, however, does not tolerate their condition as revived ones, demonstrating the greatness of the Master. It instites persecutions, declasses them according to purely human convention, and tries to nullify their action in all sectors of experience.
Only those Lazaruses who unite with the love of Jesus manage to overcome the terrible siege of ignorance.

Take heed, therefore, of yourself. If you feel brought from shadow to light, from evil to good, under the sublime influx of the Lord, remember that Pharisaism, visible and invisible, obeying impulses of an inferior order, is still working against the value of your faith and against the strength of your ideal.
The Master's crucifixion was not enough. You too shall know the testimony.

messages.title: Resistance to Evil
paragraphs: “But I tell you not to resist evil.” — JESUS (Matthew, 5:39)
Exponents of bad faith often falsely interpret the Master's words regarding resistance to evil.
Jesus did not determine that disciples should surrender defenselessly to destructive currents.
He advised that no disciple should return violence for violence.
Facing cruelty with similar weapons would mean perpetuating hatred and unrestrained ambition in the world.
Good is the only dissolvent of evil, in all sectors, revealing different forces.
Because of this, the attitude required in the face of crime is never indifference, but rather that of active, energetic, renewing, vigilant, and industrious good.

In all eras, men have perpetrated grave errors, trying to repress wickedness, the daughter of ignorance, with wickedness, the daughter of calculation. And these unhappy measures, a great number of times, were carried out in the very name of Christ.

Wars, revolutions, assassinations, persecutions were set in motion by man, who thus presumes to cooperate with Heaven. However, the dark undertakings did nothing more than accentuate the catastrophe of separation and discord. Such retaliations always constitute cravings for undue hegemony of pernicious sectarianism in political parties, philosophical schools, and religious sects, but never a determination of Jesus.
Recognizing in advance that the spiritual myopia of creatures would disfigure His words, the Master reinforced the concept, asserting: "But I say unto you..."
The lower Plane adopts standards of resistance, demanding "an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth"...
Jesus, however, advises us to defend forgiveness seventy times seven for each offense, with diligent, transforming, and endless goodness.

messages.title: Physical Clashes
paragraphs: “But whoever strikes you on your right cheek, turn the other to him also.” — JESUS (Matthew, 5:39)
Some humorists pretend to discover in the Master's warning an exhortation to cowardice, devoid of a sense of self-respect.
Jesus' view, however, does not obey only the dictates of love, the fundamental essence of His Gospel. It is also a piece of common sense and rigorous logic.
When a man attacks another using physical force, spiritual resources of any kind have already been momentarily obliterated in the attacker.
The punch of anger only arises when reason has been cast aside. And when such a problem arises, only the calm of the adversary can mitigate the imbalances resulting from the lack of control.
The countryman knows that the enraged animal does not return to normality if treated with the anger that possesses it.
The bee does not sting the beekeeper who is a friend of gentleness and serenity.

The only resource to restrain a deranged man, compelling him to readjust himself with dignity, is for the opponent or bystanders to maintain a normal position, without falling to the same level of inferiority.

Jesus' recommendation opens up a blessed advance for us... To offer the left cheek after the right one has already been lacerated by the aggressor is to call him back to ennobled reason, immediately reintegrating him into the recognition of his own perversity.
In any physical conflict, the word plays a reduced role in the circles of good. Gesture is the force that will express itself conveniently.
As we recognize, therefore, in Christ's counsel there is no invitation to weakness, but an appeal to the superiority that vulgar people still do not know.

messages.title: Old Leaven
paragraphs: “Therefore purge out the old leaven, that you may be a new lump.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 5:7)
There are old fermentations of a mental nature that represent dangerous toxins to the balance of the soul.
It is very common to observe companions anxious for intimate identification with the past, in the web of past reincarnations.
It happens, however, that the majority of the incarnate on Earth do not possess a respectable and dignified past life from which they can gather seeds of Christian example.

Almost all of us were intoxicated with the mendacious liquor of vanity when administering the assets of the world, if not getting drunk on the destructive wine of crime when called to obey in the works of the Lord.

Whoever possesses strength and light to understand failed experiences, comprehending their own inferiority, may perhaps take advantage of something useful by rereading living pages of the past. Disciples of this sort, however, are still rare in the labors of recapitulation in the flesh, close to which Divine Compassion grants the failing servant the blessing of forgetfulness for the appreciation of new initiatives.
Do not keep the old leaven in your heart, therefore. Each day calls us to a nobler and higher life.
Let us reform ourselves in the clarity of Infinite Good, so that we may be a new spiritual dough in the hands of Our Lord Jesus.

messages.title: Cultivate Peace
paragraphs: “And if a son of peace is there, your peace will rest on him; if not, it will return to you.” — JESUS (Luke, 10.6)

Indeed, there are many desperate people in human life. But how many cling, voluptuously, to their own despair? How many rebels flee from the light of patience? How many criminals weep with sorrow because it is impossible for them to consummate new crimes? How many sad souls voluntarily escape the blessings of hope?

For a man to be a son of peace, it is imperative that he work intensely within his inner world, silencing the voices of non-adaptation to the Divine Will and avoiding manifestations of disharmony before the eternal laws.
Everyone begs for peace on a planet tormented by horrible discords, but few make themselves worthy of it.

They demand that tranquility reside in the same apartment where ungrounded hatred for neighbors dwells, they claim that hope should take a seat with non-acceptance, and they ask faith to approve their idleness in the field of necessary spiritual preparation.
For the overwhelming majority of these comfort-seeking creatures, legitimate peace is a very distant achievement.
In all sectors of life, preparation and merit must precede the benefit.

No one attains well-being in Christ without effort in doing good, without elevated discipline of feelings, without illumination of reasoning. Before the sublime edification, they may register the most beautiful speeches, glimpse the highest perspectives of the higher plane, and live with the great apostles of the Cause of Redemption; but they may equally live far from the inner harmony, which constitutes the divine and inexhaustible source of true happiness, because if man hears the lesson of Christian peace without the firm purpose of attaching himself to it, it is the Lord's own recommendation that this celestial good return to its source, as an untransferable conquest of each one.

messages.title: Winter
paragraphs: “Do your best to come before winter.” — PAUL (2 Timothy, 4.21)
Of course, the common analysis of this verse will reveal the prudent recommendation of Paul of Tarsus so that Timothy would not risk traveling in the season of severe cold.
In the distant times of the epistle, winter did not offer facilities for navigation.
It is possible, however, to go further, beyond the letter and above the circumstantial problem of place and time. Let us mobilize our spiritual interpretation.

How many souls only remember the need for an encounter with the emissaries of the Divine Master on the occasion of the rigorous winter of suffering? How many remember the Savior only in hours of thick fog, threatening storm, and heavy, compact ice over the heart?
In moments like this, the boat of hope tends to sail aimlessly, at the mercy of stormy waves.
The fogs conceal the destination, and everything around the traveler of life tends toward disorder or disorientation.

It is indispensable to seek the Heavenly Friend or those who have already linked themselves definitively to His love, before the anguished periods, so that we may install ourselves in refuges of peace and security.
Discipline, in times of abundance and freedom, is a distinction in the creatures who follow it; but the restraint imposed upon us in scarcity or difficulty turns into martyrdom.
The loyal apprentice of Christ must not march in the world at the whim of satisfied caprices, but rather on the path of temperance and understanding.
Winter is indispensable and useful, as a period of beneficial testing and necessary renewal. Seek, however, the encounter of your experience with Jesus before it comes.

messages.title: Ahead of You
paragraphs: “But go, tell his disciples and Peter that he is going before you to Galilee.” — (MARK, 16.7)
It is rare to find disciples decided on unalloyed fidelity in moments when struggle exceeds the normal scope.
Commonly, as experience rises to greater demonstrations of courage, valor, and faith, their spirits change immediately. Security turns into indecision, and joy into discouragement.
Let obstacles multiply, and painful uncertainty will arise.
The apprentices, however, must not forget the sublime promise from the beginning, when the shepherd reassembled the dispersed flock.

When the companions, after the Resurrection, reflected on the future, oscillating between doubt and perplexity, behold, the Master's Messenger addresses a salutary warning to them, assuring them that the Lord would march ahead of His friends to Galilee, where He would await the beloved collaborators in order to lay the deep foundations of future evangelical work.
It is not up to us to forget that, in the first provisions of the divine apostolate, Jesus always went ahead of His companions in sanctifying testimonies.
And so it happens, invariably, throughout the centuries.
The Master is always doing the utmost in the redemptive work, counting on the effort of co-workers only in the minute particulars of the celestial service...

Do not surrender yourselves to the shadows of indecision when you remain alone or when work worsens on the common road. Go, confident and optimistic, to the salutary trials or lacerating tasks that await our contribution and action. Certainly, we will not be granted delicious facilities in a world where ignorance still establishes lamentable prisons, but let us follow happily in pursuit of the obligations that compete to us, conscious that Jesus, loving and provident, has already gone ahead of us...

messages.title: In the Field
paragraphs: “The field is the world.” — JESUS (Matthew, 13.38)
Jesus has His field of service throughout the entire world.
In it, naturally, as in every farming field, there is an infinite potential for realizations, with strips of excellent land and zones in need of support, correction, and protection.
Sometimes, after bountiful forests, giant swamps emerge, requiring drainage and immediate aid.
Alongside mountains haloed with light, valleys enveloped in indefinite shadow appear.
Straight trunks rise next to twisted trees; dead branches contrast with green foliage full of nests.
The immense glebe of Christ calls for devoted workers who do not show personal preferences for zones of service or kinds of tasks.
Many laborers present themselves to the Lord of Work daily, but true servants are rare.

Most of the laborers who apply for the Master's work do not go beyond the cultivation of certain flowers, recoil before despised swamps, fear deserted places, or are startled by the magnitude of the service, withdrawing into long and ruinous hesitations or fleeing from infectious regions.
On some occasions, they tend to be skillful horticulturists or gardeners; however, almost always they rest upon these titles and become frightened before aggressive and multiform terrains.
Jesus, nevertheless, does not rest and continues waiting for companions for infinite achievements in favor of the Heavenly Kingdom on Earth.
Reflect on this truth and enrich your qualities of collaboration, perfecting them and intensifying them in the works of indiscriminate and uninterrupted good...
It is certain that a co-worker for Jesus cannot be improvised; nevertheless, do not forget to work, day by day, toward the glorious end...

messages.title: In Christian Service
paragraphs: “Not lording it over those entrusted to your care, but being examples to the flock.” — (1 PETER, 5.3)
To the companions of Christian Spiritism fall tasks of enormous proportions regarding souls.
We are concerned with profound problems of faith and transcendent questions of pain.

Because they give freely what they have received by grace, they count on the animosity of those who sell divine gifts; because they seek spiritual wisdom, they receive the gratuitous aversion of those who crystallize themselves in petty science; because they prepare themselves in the face of eternal life, detaching themselves from destructive selfishness, they are categorized as fools by those who find satisfaction in transitory fantasy.
The greater the incomprehension of the world, however, the more their notions of responsibility should intensify.

We do not speak here of scholars, investigators, or mere observers. We refer to those who have already understood the greatness of fraternal aid and have surrendered themselves to it, with their hearts turned toward Christ. They find themselves in circles of an experience too noble to be commented upon, but the responsibility that competes to them is likewise too great to be defined.

To you, therefore, my brother, who guard within yourself the interests of many souls, I repeat the words of the great apostle, so that you may never become vain, nor act “lording it over those entrusted to your care, but being examples to the flock”.

messages.title: Let Us Keep the Teaching
paragraphs: “Let these words sink into your ears.” — JESUS (Luke, 9.44)
Many listen to the word of Christ; however, very few are those who put the lesson into their ears.
It is not a matter of registering mere words, but rather of fixing notes that must palpitate in the book of the heart.
Jesus was not referring to the dead letter, but to the creative verb.

The doctrinal circles of Christianity are full of apprentices who do not know how to heed this appeal. They attend spiritual activities, tuning their minds to all inferior anxieties rather than to the Spirit of Christ. They bend their knees, repeat verbal formulas, concentrate on themselves, yet, deep down, they operate in a sphere distant from righteous service.
Most do not intend to listen to the Lord, but rather to speak to the Lord, as if Jesus performed the simple function of a pageboy subordinate to everyone's whims.
They are students who seek to subvert school order.
They pronounce long prayers, shout protests, and string together promises they cannot keep.
They do not esteem teachings. They formulate impositions.
And, like madmen, they seek to act in the name of Christ.
The results are not long in coming. Failure and disillusionment, sterility and pain arrive slowly, awakening the dormant soul to eternal realities.
Not a few revolt, disenchanted... Let them not complain, however, except of themselves.
“Let my words sink into your ears,” said Jesus.
Even the wind has a direction. Would the Divine Master, then, have transmitted any lesson by chance?

messages.title: In Our Work
paragraphs: “For every house is built by someone, but God is the builder of everything.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 3.4)
The Supreme Lord created the Universe, yet each creature organizes its particular world.
The Divine Architect is the owner of all buildings, yet each Spirit builds its own dwelling.
The Giver of Infinite Goods scatters unlimited values in Creation, yet each one of us must create values inherent to our own personality.

Nature, maternal and rich in blessings, everywhere constitutes the representation of the immeasurable patrimony of Divine Power, and everywhere someone exists, there pulsates the equally creative will of man, who is the heir of God.
The Father lays foundations and establishes laws. The children contribute to the construction of works and operate interferences.
It is understandable, therefore, that we devote all care to our individualistic effort in the buildings of the world, convinced that we will answer for our personal actions in all spheres of life.

Let us collaborate in the good with the enthusiasm of one who recognizes the usefulness of their own action in the circles of service, but without destructive passions that tie us to the islands of isolationism.
Let us present our work to the Lord daily and ask Him to destroy particulars in disagreement with His sovereign and righteous purposes, begging Him for vision and understanding.
We will be compelled to form our own mental field, to erect the house of our elevation, and to build our own sanctuary.
In the unfolding of this service, however, let us never forget that all the patrimonies of life belong to God.

messages.title: Not the Words
paragraphs: “But I will come to you very soon, if the Lord is willing, and then I will find out not only how these arrogant people are talking, but what power they have.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 4.19)

Christ and His co-workers will not come to meet apprentices to find out the words of those who live in a false conception of destiny, but rather of those who have identified themselves with the imperishable spirit of evangelical construction.

It is indubitable that the Lord will be interested in works; however, whenever we refer to works, listeners generally remember only material institutions visible in the world, rich or humble, simple or sumptuous.
Often, creatures less favored with organic faculties, such as the blind or the crippled, believe themselves annihilated or useless before a conception of this nature.
This is because man commonly forgets the works of sanctification he is bound to effect within his own spirit.

Few understand that it is necessary to maneuver heavy instruments of the will in order to conquer ground from selfishness; to use the hoe of personal effort for the definitive establishment of harmony in the heart. Few remember that they possess fragile and small ideas about the good and that it is imperative to maintain inner resources of protection for these germs so that they may bear fruit later.

It is logical that the words of those who do not live puffed up with personalism will be the object of the Master's attention at all times, not least because the verb is also a sacred force that clarifies and edifies. It is urgent, however, to flee from the abuses of unproductive verbosity that squanders time in the “vanity of vanities.”

Do not forget, therefore, that before external works of any nature, always easy and transitory, you have to make the intimate construction of wisdom and love—very difficult to accomplish, indeed, but precisely for that reason, sublimated and eternal.

messages.title: Idle Talk
paragraphs: “Avoid godless chatter, because those who indulge in it will become more and more ungodly.” — PAUL (2 Timothy, 2.16)
Few expressions of social or domestic life are as dangerous as wild idle talk, which offers a vast breeding ground for the monsters of crime.
Religious and scientific activity have discovered numerous factors of imbalance in the world, effectively collaborating to extinguish their essential foci.
How much has been laudably worked in the fight against alcohol and syphilis?
No one disputes their destructive influence. They ruin communities, destroy health, and depress character.

Let us not forget, however, malignant idle talk, which always forms around itself an immense family of sickly or debasing elements, like lethal worms that proliferate in silence and operate in shadows. Few reflect on this.
Is uncontrolled speech not, perhaps, the father of slander, backbiting, gossip, levity, and perturbation?
God created the word; man engendered idle talk.
Dignified speech instills consolation and life. Pernicious murmuring propitiates death.
How many enemies of human peace take advantage of senseless chatter to fulfill criminal desires?

If alcohol intoxicates the vicious, annihilating their energies, what can be said of the tongue strayed from the good, which destroys vigorous seedbeds of happiness and wisdom, love and peace? If there are educators concerned with the intrusion of syphilis, why the indifference regarding the derangements of conversation?
Everywhere, speech is an index of our evolutionary position. It is indispensable to refine, illuminate, and ennoble it.
To despise the sacred possibilities of the verb when the message of Jesus is already shining around us constitutes a ruinous relaxation of our life before God and our own conscience.
Every phrase of the disciple of the Gospel must have a dignified and appropriate place.
Idle talk is waste. And when it is not that, it is nothing less than a dark current of psychic poisons, threatening valuable spirits and entire communities.

messages.title: Evil Workers
paragraphs: “Watch out for those dogs, those evildoers.” — PAUL (Philippians, 3.2)
Paul of Tarsus does not recommend without reason the care to be observed in the face of the harassment of evil workers.
In all activities of the good, the sincere worker needs to protect himself against the poison that proceeds from the unfaithful servant.

While loyal servants toil devotedly in the obligations entrusted to them, evil workers seek undue rest, calling companions to desertion and revolt. Instead of cooperating and attending to the commitments assumed, they give themselves over to jocular or harsh criticism, belittling their fellow laborers.
They esteem discouraging appraisals.
They fixate on the still insecure angles of the work in execution, unconcerned with achievements already made.
They handle legal texts in order to observe how they can enforce rights while forgetting duties.
They listen to the words of others with religious attention to extract less-than-happy verbal concepts, so as to create disturbances.
They call humble co-workers cowards and efficient or understanding ones sycophants.
They highlight everyone's defects except their own.
They line up brilliant and complacent phrases, soaking them in the oil of hidden perversities.
They sow doubt, distrust, and dissension when they perceive that success is near.
They spread suspicions and calumnies among those who organize and those who execute.
They turn themselves into lawyers in order to be accusers.
They dress like sheep while disguising the features of wolves.
They tend to lament as victims in order to be more thorough executioners.
“Watch out for those evildoers.” The apostle's counsel to the Gentiles remains full of opportunity and significance.

messages.title: Hope
paragraphs: “For everything that was written in the past was written to teach us, so that through the endurance taught in the Scriptures and the encouragement they provide we might have hope.” — PAUL (Romans, 15.4)
Hope is the Christian's light.
Not everyone is yet capable of the sublime flight of faith, but the strength of hope is a common treasure.
Not everyone can offer, whenever they wish, the bread of the body and the spiritual lesson, but no one on Earth is prevented from spreading the benefits of hope.

Pain usually agitates those who find themselves in the “valley of the shadow of death,” where fear establishes friction and where affliction perceives the “gnashing of teeth” in the “outer darkness,” but there is an inner light, which is hope.

Human negation declares bankruptcies, issues certificates of impossibility, and traces inextricable labyrinths; however, hope comes from above, like the Sun that illuminates from on high and nourishes new seedbeds, awakens different purposes, creates redemptive modifications, and unlocks higher visions.

The night awaits the day, the flower the fruit, the worm the future… Man, even if he plunges into disbelief or doubt, into tears or laceration, will be succored by God with the indication of the future.

Jesus, as the Divine Master, knows that learners will not always be able to get everything right, that errors are proper to the evolutionary school, and for this very reason, hope is one of the sublime hymns of His Gospel of Love.
Immense have been our falls until now, but Christ's trust is always greater.
Let us not lose ourselves in lamentations. Every moment is an instant to hear Him who uttered the “Come to me…”
Let us rise and press on, convinced that the Lord has offered us the light of hope, so that we may kindle within ourselves the light of spiritual sanctification.

messages.title: In Effective Propaganda
paragraphs: “He must become greater; I must become less.” — JOHN THE BAPTIST (John, 3.30)
There is always a strong desire for constructive propaganda in the hearts of sincere believers.

Comforted by the spiritual bread of Jesus, new disciples strive to extend it to others. But they do not always succeed in the task. Often, moved by strong impulses, they become demanding or precipitate, claiming premature harvests.
The Gospel, however, is replete with teachings in this regard.
John the Baptist's assertion in this passage is significant. It outlines a program for all who intend to act as precursors of the Master in human hearts.
It is not worthwhile to impose the principles of faith.

Demands, even if indirect, merely reveal their authors. Polemics highlight the polemicists… Untimely discussions accentuate the personal collaboration of the discussants. Pure word-preaching makes fine orators, with precious phraseology and dazzling ornaments of form.

Of course, guidance, clarification, and teaching are indispensable tasks in the spread of Christianity; however, it is of fundamental importance for disciples that the Spirit of Jesus grow in their lives. Revealing the Lord in one's own daily experience is the highest and most efficient propaganda of faithful learners.

If you truly desire to extend the clarity of your faith, remember that the Master needs to grow in your acts, words, and thoughts, in fellowship with all those who surround your heart. Only in this direction is it possible to attend to the Divine Administrator and serve one's fellows, healing the congenital hypertrophy of the “self”.

messages.title: Will Suffer Persecutions
paragraphs: “In fact, everyone who wants to live a godly life in Christ Jesus will be persecuted.” — PAUL (2 Timothy, 3.12)

Incontestably, the world's codes of good manners are always respectable, but we must agree that above them prevail the codes of Jesus, whose principles were engraved by Him through His own exemplification.
The world, however, rarely tolerates the code of good manners of the Divine Master.
If you feel wounded and seek earthly justice, you will be considered a sensible man; however, if you prefer the silence of the Great Wronged One of the Cross, ironies will be hurled at your face.

If you demand compensation for your services, there are human laws that support you, considering you prudent; but if you produce something useful without demanding a reward, remembering the Divine Benefactor, you will be interpreted as a fool.

If you defend yourself against the wicked, asserting your reasons, you will be categorized as a dignified man; however, if you apply the Lord's humility and forgiveness, you will be openly accused of being a coward and despicable.

If you practice individual exploitation in disguise, mobilizing your neighbor for the service of your passing interests, you will be attributed admirable gifts of intelligence and skill; however, if you set yourself to general service for the benefit of all, out of love for Jesus, you will be considered an idiot and servile.

As long as you listen to the dictates of social laws, giving to receive, doing something to seek the admiration of others, praising to be praised, you will receive infinite praise from creatures, but the moment you, out of fidelity to the Gospel, are compelled to take stances with the Master, often with heavy suffering for your heart, you will be classified as a fool.
Attend, therefore, to your ministry wherever you are, without any doubt in this regard, certain that for a long time yet, the faithful disciple of Jesus on Earth will suffer persecutions.

messages.title: Let Us Purify Ourselves
paragraphs: “Those who cleanse themselves from the latter will be instruments for special purposes, made holy, useful to the Master and prepared to do any good work.” — PAUL (2 Timothy, 2.21)
In each day of struggle, it is indispensable to pay attention to the use of the vessel of our individual possibilities.
On Earth, where the majority of incarnate souls still sleep the sleep of indifference, the vigilance of the worker of Jesus in this regard is more than necessary.

Whoever does not guard their ears can be used by injustice. Whoever does not watch over their tongue can easily become a vessel of slander, through levity or the preoccupation with sensationalism. Whoever does not illuminate their eyes can become a vessel of false judgments. Whoever is not guided by the Christian spirit will naturally be led to many follies and disturbances, even when good faith inspires praiseworthy purposes.

Men and women of all conditions are being used by the forces of life daily. For now, the majority constitutes material used by malice and vice. Fragile and imperfect vessels, they melt and remelt every day amid unsettling and harsh experiences.

Very rare are those who, with purified interiors, can serve the Lord, qualified for good works. Many aspire to this high position, but do not care for themselves. They claim the status of great missionaries, demand divine light, cry out for advanced revelations, yet in nothing do they strive to free themselves from low passions.

Observe, then, friend, what principles you serve in your daily toil. Remember that the vessel of your possibilities is sacred. What forces of life use it? Do not forget, above all, that we need legitimate purification so that we may be vessels for honor, fit for the Master's use.

messages.title: In Combat
paragraphs: “In your struggle against sin, you have not yet resisted to the point of shedding your blood.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 12.4)
The sincere disciple of the Gospel lives in a silent battle in the field of the heart.

At first, the combat unfolds in a serene climate, in the sweet warmth of a tranquil home. The trees of domestic affections soften the harshest experiences. Hopes of every shade populate the soul, not always attentive to reality.
Ideals speak aloud regarding future victories.
The fighter dominates material elements and not infrequently assumes that true triumph is complete.

The work, however, continues. The victory of the spirit demands the fighter's integral effort. And later, the Christian laborer is invited to harsher testimonies, compelled into solitary battle, without the resources of earlier times. The law of renewal modifies their routes, strips away their illusions, selects their ideals. Death devastates their intimate circle, subjects them to isolation, impels them to meditation. Time imposes withdrawals, changes, and rectifications…
Many become discouraged in the great enterprise and return, fearful, to the lower shadows.

Those who persevere, however, will experience resistance unto blood. This does not refer to the blood of carnage, but rather to the blood ties that not only unite the spirit to the corporeal vessel, but also bind it to companions of the family entourage. When the learner receives pain within themselves, understanding its sanctifying purpose, and exercises justice or accepts it above all concern for blood ties, they will be reaching the sublime position of triumph in the combat against evil.

messages.title: How Do You Suffer?
paragraphs: “However, if you suffer as a Christian, do not be ashamed, but praise God that you bear that name.” — PETER (1 Peter, 4.16)
It is not enough simply to suffer in order to ascend to spiritual glory. It is indispensable to know how to suffer, extracting the blessings of light that pain offers to the heart thirsty for peace.
Many people suffer, but how many creatures complicate themselves in anguish because they do not know how to make use of rectifying and sanctifying trials?

We see those who receive slander and pass it on to their neighbors; those who are tormented by accusations, dragging companions into the disturbances that assail them; and those who try to eliminate reparative illnesses with despair.

How many hearts turn into poisoned wells of hatred and bitterness because small sufferings have invaded their personal circle? There are not a few who knock at the door of unjustified disillusionment, disbelief, distrust, or rebellion, because of a few unattended whims.
Would it be useful to suffer with the voluptuousness of spreading suffering to others? Is it not aggravating the debt to assault the creditor just because they decided to call us to account?

Rare men learn to find the profit in tribulations. The majority belittles the opportunity for edification and, above all, aggravates their own debts, confusing their neighbor and precipitating companions into troubled zones of the evolutionary path.
All creatures suffer in the crucible of necessary experiences, but very few spirits know how to suffer as Christians, glorifying God.

messages.title: Let Us Be Certain
paragraphs: “I will put my laws into their hearts, and in their minds I will write them.” — PAUL (Hebrews, 10:16)
Human institutions live full of codes and scriptures.
Temples remain replete with preachings.
Centers of a religious nature line up countless doctrinal compendiums.
The Gospel, however, does not hide the purposes of the Lord.

All the movement of tearable pages, carriers of restricted vocabulary, represents a phase of spiritual preparation, because Jesus' objective is to inscribe His teachings in our hearts and intelligences.

We may adhere intellectually to the most varied religious programs, navigating the open sea of purely verbalist philosophy and culture, with a certain profit to our individual position before our neighbor; but before the Lord, the fundamental problem of our spirit is transformation for good, with the elevation of all our feelings and thoughts.
The Master will write His divine statutes on the living pages of our soul.

Let us be certain of this. And let us be no less convinced that, sometimes, out of added mercy, He will grant us the precise resources so that we may wash our intimate book with the water of tears, eliminating the residues of this work with the purifying fire of suffering.

messages.title: Without Faltering
paragraphs: “Let us not become weary in doing good, for at the proper time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up.” — PAUL (Galatians, 6.9)
There are people with singular dispositions regarding spiritual service. Today they believe, tomorrow they disbelieve.
Yesterday they surrendered to the manifestations of faith; however, because someone was not cured of a migraine, today they lose confidence, entering the broad path of denial.
They begin the practice of good, but if a thorn of ingratitude from their fellows appears, they proclaim the bankruptcy of the purpose of doing good.
They are children rehearsing learning in the school of life, still far from the position of disciples of the Master.
The exercise of true love cannot tire the heart.
Whoever loves in Christ Jesus keeps trust in God, is happy in renunciation, and knows how to feed on hope.
Evil exhausts the spirit, but good always reinvigorates.
The sincere learner of the Gospel, therefore, neither gets irritated nor knows defeat in edifying struggles, because they understand discouragement as a loss of opportunity.
Problems of the soul are not circumscribed to questions of earthly days and weeks, nor can they live conditioned to physical deficiencies. They are problems of life, renewal, and eternity.
Do not grow tired, then, of doing good, convinced, however, that the harvest, by your own hands, depends on your continuing in the priesthood of love, without faltering.

messages.title: Examine
paragraphs: “If anyone comes to you and does not bring this teaching, do not take them into your house or welcome them.” — JOHN (2 John, 10)

It is reasonable that no one prevents their neighbor from speaking what seems best to them; it is fair, however, that the listener only retains what they recognize as useful and better. In all sectors of earthly activity and in the course of all daily tasks, brothers approach who come to you, bringing their personal messages.
This one is a bearer of an invitation to insubordination; that other is a vessel of sickly complaints.
It is indispensable that the earthly house does not open to ghosts.
Are they knocking at the door? Prudence advises vigilance.
The heart is a sacred enclosure where useless residues should not be piled up.
It is imperative to examine the solicitations that advance.

If the messenger does not bear the characteristics of Jesus, it is wise to deny them shelter, of an absolute character, within the intimate house, while still providing them with some of the precious blessings we have managed to gather for our own benefit in the sector of essential utilities.

Innumerable curious people who approach sincere disciples possess nothing beyond the presumption of good talkers. They are almost always greatly needy under the fallacious guise of theory. Without wounding them or scandalizing them, it is fair that the devoted learner of Jesus lavish upon them some motive for serious reflection. In this way, those who think they carry a banner of supposed redemption come to carry with them the message of good, which is truly salvific.
The problem is not to inform ourselves whether someone is speaking in the name of the Lord; above all, it matters to know whether the bearer has something of Christ to give.

messages.title: We Are of God
paragraphs: “We are from God.” — JOHN (1 John, 4.6)
It is not easy for us to untangle ourselves from the ties that magnetize us to the less elevated circles of life, to which we still belong.
Despite our divine origin, a thousand obstacles bind us to the idea of separation from Heavenly Paternity.
Pride blinds us to the universality of life.
Egoism imprisons our heart.
Vanity erects a false throne of undue favoritism for us, seeking to distance us from reality.
Inferior ambition plunges us into abysses of destructive fantasy.
Rebellion forms storms of hatred over our heads.
Anxiety wounds our being.

And we judge, in these old conflicts of feeling, that we belong to the physical body, to multisecular prejudice, and to human convention, when all the material patrimony that surrounds us represents a loan of forces and possibilities for us to discover ourselves, enriching our own value.
Most of the time, we linger in the gloomy prison of separation, distracted, deceived, blind…
Life, however, continues, secure and strong, sowing light and opportunity so that the fruits of experience do not fail us.

Little by little, work and pain, illness and death compel us to reconsider the paths traversed, impelling our minds to higher zones. Do not despise, then, these admirable companions of the human journey, because almost always in their company we come to understand that we are of God.

messages.title: Substitutes
paragraphs: “To give light to them that sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.” — (LUKE, 1.79)
It is reasonable that the administrator distributes work and answers for the stewardship entrusted to him.
Holding management responsibilities, man is obliged to move a large number of people.
He will guide those under his direction, educate subordinates, and give them tasks that refine their qualities in service.
Even so, the leader does not exempt himself from the fundamental obligations that compete to him.
If there was anyone who could mobilize millions of substitutes for the testimony on the Crust of the Earth, that someone was Jesus.

The Lord had at His disposal legions of enlightened emissaries, and maintained incalculable reserves at His command. He could send to the world enlightened philosophers to renew the understanding of creatures, wise physicians who would cure the blind and the mad, faithful conductors dedicated to teaching the way of good.

In truth, since the earliest days of human organization, the Lord has mobilized a multitude of His direct cooperators in our favor, if only because His divine hands hold the administrative power of the Earth. Yet it must be recognized that, at the moment deemed essential for the launching of the Kingdom of God among men, He came Himself into our sphere of shadows and conflicts.
He did not send substitutes or representatives. He assumed the responsibility for His teachings and, alone, bore incomprehension and the cross.
Let us inspire ourselves in Christ and personally attend to the duty that life grants us.
Before the Supreme Lord, we all have non-transferable service.

messages.title: Let Us Know How to Trust
paragraphs: “Therefore, do not be anxious.” — JESUS (Matthew, 6.31)
Jesus does not recommend indifference or irresponsibility.
The Master, who advocated prayer and vigilance, would not advise the disciple's lack of concern before the collection of service to be done.
He only asks for the fight against chronic pessimism.
Of course, we find ourselves in full work, in the Lord's crop, within the natural order that governs our very ascent.
We will still face, countless times, swamps and deserts, briars and harmful animals.
It is urgent, however, to renew mental attitudes in the work to which we were called, learning to trust in the Divine Power that guides us.
In all places, there are intransigent defeatists.
They feel in darkness, even when the Sun is at its zenith.
They see baseness in the most dignified creatures.
They march tormented by atrocious mistrusts. And, by suspecting everyone, they end up disabled for productive collaboration in any noble service.

Afflicted and distressed, they become disoriented regarding minimal obstacles, worry about frivolities of all sorts, and, if they could, they would paint the firmament in black so that their neighbor's mind would share their inner shadow.

On Earth, Jesus is the Lord who made Himself the servant of all, out of love, and has awaited our contribution in the workshop of the centuries. His trust encompasses the ages, His experience spans civilizations, His devotion has enveloped us for millennia…
Because of this, how can we adopt affliction and despair, if we are just beginning to be useful?

messages.title: Look
paragraphs: “Take ye heed, watch and pray: for ye know not when the time is.” — JESUS (Mark, 13.33)
Mark records a certain formula of vigilance that reveals our need to mobilize all resources of reflection and analysis.
Often, we refer to “pray and watch,” without meditating on its complexity and extent.
It is indispensable to guard the paths, imperative to move possibilities in the sphere of good; however, this attitude does not dispense with vision with understanding.
The imperative placed by Mark at the beginning of Jesus' recommendation is of inestimable value to the perfect interpretation of the text.
It is necessary to look, that is, to examine, ponder, reflect, so that vigilance is not incomplete.
Discernment is the sentinel's first concern.

The disciple cannot guard himself, simultaneously defending the heritage entrusted to him, without extending his psychological vision, seeking to penetrate the essential intimacy of situations and events.
Look at the work of each day. Common service remains full of profitable messages.
Fix your affective relationships. They bear necessary counsels for your balance.
Monitor the circumstances by observing the suggestions they cast into the center of your soul.
In the sentimental house, invisible intelligences gather to exchange impressions with you in silence.
Pause in the appreciation of the day; its fields constituted of hours and minutes are repositories of deep teachings and valuable opportunities.
Look, reflect, ponder!… After that, naturally, you will be ready to watch and pray profitably.

messages.title: You and Your House
paragraphs: “And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house.” — (ACTS, 16.31)
Generally, we find new disciples of the Gospel who feel profoundly isolated within the domestic center regarding the chapter of religious belief.

They claim to be absolutely alone from the point of view of faith. And some, devoid of serious examination, proceed to highlight the hardening or indifference of the hearts surrounding them. This one refers to the mockery of which he is a victim, that other accuses absent relatives.
Such incomprehension, however, demonstrates that the evangelical principles adorn their intellectual zone without penetrating the core of their heart.
Why highlight the faults of others, while forgetting, in turn, the good work of rectification that is incumbent upon us in the plane of hidden goodness?
The apostolic counsel is profoundly expressive.

In the home where there is even a single person who sincerely believes in Jesus and adapts to His redeeming teachings, paving the way according to the Master's standards, there the supreme light for elevation will remain.
It does not matter that parents are unbelievers, that brothers and sisters remain hardened, nor does irony, harsh discussion, or ungrateful observation matter.
The Christian, wherever he may be, finds himself in the domicile of his regenerative convictions, to serve Jesus, perfecting and enlightening himself.
A single stake is enough to support many branches. A cornerstone balances an entire building.
Do not forget, therefore, that if you truly accept Christ and become attached to Him, you will be led to God, you and your house.

messages.title: In the Intimacy of the Being
paragraphs: “Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, long-suffering.” — PAUL (Colossians, 3.12)
Undoubtedly, it is not enough to appreciate the sublime sentiments that Christianity inspires. It is indispensable to clothe ourselves in them.
The apostle does not refer to reasonings. He speaks of depths.
The problem is not one of pure cerebration. It is one of the intimacy of the being.
Someone who possesses a sure roadmap of the path to follow, among crowds that do not know it, is naturally elected to manage guidance.

Holding such a copious baggage of knowledge regarding eternity, the legitimate Christian is the indicated person to protect the spiritual interests of his brothers on the evolutionary journey; however, it is necessary to emphasize the testimony, which is not limited to brilliant phraseology.
It is imperative that we be clothed with “bowels of mercies” to face, with success, the growing dangers of the path.

Evil, to cede ground, understands only the language of true good; pride, in order to renounce its unhappy purposes, understands nothing but humanity. Without a fraternal spirit, it is impossible to break the dark stiletto of selfishness. It is necessary to always expand the reserves of superior feeling, so that we may advance victoriously on the path of ascent.

Sincere Spiritualists will find luminous stimulus in Paul's words. Some companions will certainly observe in our memory a mere problem of religious faith, according to their way of understanding; however, between doing psychism for a few days and solving issues for eternal life, there is always a considerable difference.

messages.title: With a Pure Heart
paragraphs: “See that ye love one another with a pure heart fervently.” — (1 Peter, 1.22)
Frivolous spirits, on all occasions, have given preference to malicious interpretations of sacred texts.
The “love one another” did not escape the depreciative system. The higher Sphere, however, always regards irony as ignorance or spiritual childishness of human creatures.
The sublime exhortation constitutes a powerful synthesis of the theories of fraternity.

The understanding and application of “love one another” is the luminous goal of struggles on Earth. And to those who experience difficulty in interpreting the divine recommendation, we have Peter's providential note when he refers to the pure heart.

Men know some rays of love that are nothing more than fleeting rays shining through the walls of selfish interests, because most approaches of creatures on the Crust of the Earth are inspired by obscure and petty motives, in the terrain of easy pleasures or associations directed towards immediate profit.
The love referred to in the Gospel is rather the divine disposition to serve with joy, in the execution of the Father's Will, in any region where we may remain.
Many people claim they love, yet as soon as circumstances arise against their whims, they begin to detest. Gestures that appeared dedicated are converted into attitudes of inferior interest.
Regarding the subject, however, the apostle provides the dominant note of the lesson. Let us love one another fervently, but let us keep our hearts elevated and pure.

messages.title: Crumb and Multitude
paragraphs: “And he commanded the multitude to sit down on the grass, and took the five loaves, and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven, he blessed, and brake, and gave the loaves to his disciples, and the disciples to the multitude.” — (MATTHEW, 14.19)
Before the picture of the legion of the hungry, any man would experience invincible discouragement, considering the crumb of five loaves and two fishes.
But Jesus employs the immense power of goodness and manages to feed everyone abundantly.
Let us observe, however, that to do this He takes the disciples as intermediaries.
The Master's teaching in this passage of the Gospel is highly symbolic.

Whoever identifies the alluvium of evils created by ourselves, through the deviations of the will in the succession of our existences on Earth, finds it hard to believe in the crumb of good that we possess within ourselves.
Here, illness corrodes; further on, failure appears; over there, multiple expressions of crime manifest themselves.
How to attend to complex needs? Many learners recoil before the extent of the task.

However, if the faithful servant walks toward the Lord, the crumb of his lights is immediately supplied by the miracle of multiplication, since Jesus, considering the spontaneous offer, will bless his tiny patrimony, allowing him to nourish true multitudes of the needy.
The mass of our imperfections is still immeasurable. Everywhere, there are diseases, deficiencies, ruins…

It is imperative, nevertheless, not to doubt our minimal possibilities in the good. Our crumbs of goodwill in the disposition to serve saintly, when led to Christ, are worth more than all the multitude of evils in the world.

messages.title: Objective of Faith
paragraphs: “Receiving the end of your faith, even the salvation of your souls.” — PETER (1 Peter, 1.9)
“What is the purpose of religious effort in my life?” This is the question that all believers should frequently formulate to themselves.
The work of self-clarification would open new paths to spiritual vision.
Rarely does man surrender to the exercises of faith without a spirit of inferior commercialism. Commonly, one seeks the religious temple with the concern of gaining something for the passing day.
Elementary reasonings, however, would lead thought to vaster inferences.

Would belief be merely a resource to facilitate certain mechanical or rudimentary operations of human life? Do irrational animals not perform them without greater effort? Nourishing oneself, resting, propagating the species are characteristics of even embryonic beings.

The objective of faith constitutes a deeper realization. It is the “salvation” to which the Good News refers, par excellence. And since God did not create us for perdition, to save, according to the Gospel, means to elevate, purify, and sublimate, intensifying the illumination of the spirit for Eternal Life.
There is no victory of light without the expulsion of shadows, nor elevation without the sweat of the ascent.

Faith represents the compass, the lit lamp guiding our steps through obstacles; locating it in inferior angles of the path is a mistake of disastrous consequences because, far from being an upward propulsion lever, it is a liberating wing leading upwards.

messages.title: Dogs and Holy Things
paragraphs: “Give not that which is holy unto the dogs.” — JESUS (Matthew, 7.6)
Certainly, the sincere Christian will never remember to make a dog a participant in evangelical service, but in no way was Jesus referring to the literal feature of the sentence.
The Master, in launching the appeal, sought to preserve friends and future companions against the dangers of imprudence.
The Gospel is not only a celestial casket of sublime words. It is also the treasure of gifts of Eternal Life.
If the waste of material resources is reprehensible, what can we say about irresponsibility in the application of sacred riches?

The restless learner in communicating the gifts of faith to socially prominent creatures may be generous, but he remains imprudent. Just because a man is well-dressed or possesses large amounts of money, because he shows himself clothed in temporary authority or stands out in the representative positions of earthly struggle, this does not demonstrate his qualification for Christ's banquet.

The Lord recommended that the Gospel be preached to all creatures; however, with such a warning He does not expect followers to turn into habitual demagogues, but rather into active springs of good to all beings, through actions and teachings, each in their proper position.

Let no one trust in affliction to impose evangelical principles in this or that sector of experience concerning them. Often, what seems love is nothing more than simple caprice, and, as a consequence of this thoughtlessness, we find true packs of dogs advancing on holy things.

messages.title: Individual Scripture
paragraphs: “But all this was done, that the scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled. Then all the disciples forsook him, and fled.” — (MATTHEW, 26.56)
The design to be fulfilled did not constitute an exclusive characteristic for Jesus' mission.
Every man has the map of the divine order in his existence, to be executed with the collaboration of free will, in the grand plan of eternal life.
Above all, in this sense, every thinking creature knows that he will be compelled to return the body of flesh to the earth.

Less educated companions know, intuitively, that they will appear for an accounting exam, that new landscapes will face them beyond the tomb, and that they will reap, just like that, the fruit of the actions they sowed in the bosom of the earthly collectivity.
In general, however, to the ordinary man this contract between the incarnate servant and the Supreme Lord seems extremely vague, and he proceeds through experience from rebellion to rebellion.

Not for this reason, nevertheless, will the scripture, especially in the paragraphs of death, fail to be fulfilled. The moment, in this particular, always arises with multiple pretexts so that divine determinations are realized. At the exact minute, family members and friends tour different worlds of ideas through the spheres of perplexity, fear, sadness, doubt, and painful questioning, and, despite the tangible presence of loved ones in the framework of testimonies concerning him, man alone attends, in the chapter of death, to the items of the scripture written by himself before the Laws of the Eternal Father, with his daily acts, words, and thoughts.

messages.title: Let Us Seek
paragraphs: “And when he came to Rome, he sought me out very diligently, and found me.” — PAUL (II Timothy, 1.17)
All evangelical statements remain marked with hidden beauty and wisdom. It is essential to meditate, make comparisons in silence, and examine daily experiences in order to discover them.
That gesture of Onesiphorus, diligently seeking the apostle of the Gentiles in the cosmopolitan life of Rome, represents an exceedingly expressive teaching.
Paul's note designates a common occurrence, yet the diligent learner goes beyond the letter to glean the lesson.

How many friends of Jesus and His direct followers await their visit, anxious and impatient? How many remain fixed, motionless, in inferior attitudes, demanding provisions they have done nothing to deserve? There are presumptuous believers who try to impose themselves upon the Divine Designs, making demands upon Heaven on the thorny grounds of ingratitude and audacity. Others lament, embittered, like wayward little children, because the Master did not satisfy their absurd and inconvenient desires.
Rare are the learners who reflect upon the immense services of Christ.
Would Jesus be wandering and unoccupied in the Higher Life? Would His direct collaborators be resting in a state of beatific idleness?
It is imperative to meditate upon the magnitude of the work and the responsibility of the divine laborers.

Let us remember that if Paul was a prisoner in the eyes of the world, he was already, in himself, a living and brilliant light, in the condition of an apostle whom Jesus Himself had glorified. Before the vision of the spirit, he was not an incarcerated man, but a triumphant one. Despite this, Onesiphorus, in order to see him, was constrained to seek him out very diligently.
This same imperative remains the same in passing days. To find Jesus and those who serve Him, we must seek them zealously.

messages.title: Diversity
paragraphs: “And there are diversities of operations, but it is the same God which worketh all in all.” — PAUL (1 Corinthians, 12.6)
Without spiritual light along the way, human experience is reduced to a complicated collection of meaningless events.
Far from legitimate understanding, weak hearts interpret life as mere expiatory penance, while strong brains view planetary struggle as a disordered adventure.
Earthly pilgrimage, however, is a preparatory course for a more complete life. Each Spirit exercises itself in its own proper field, expanding the celestial heritage of which it is the bearer.
Divine Power is operating in all intelligences and superintending all labors.
It is essential, therefore, to maintain a strong sense of the evolutionary work that presides over the phenomena of the Universe.
There are no miracles of sudden construction in the plane of the spirit, just as it is impossible to improvise, from one moment to the next, any valuable edifice in the zone of matter.

The service of illuminating the mind, with the elevation of feelings and reasonings, demands time, effort, patience, and perseverance. Hence the multiplicity of characters refining themselves in the workshop of human life, and, for this very reason, the organization of classes, standards, and spheres in infinite number, obeying the superior designs of the Father.

It is necessary, then, that the disciples of the New Revelation, with revived Christianity, learn to value the opportunity of each day's service, without anxieties, without afflictions. All terrestrial activities, framed within the good, proceed from the divine guidance that makes use of each one of us, according to the position in which we place ourselves in spiritual ascent.

Every respectable and edifying task is of celestial origin. Each man and woman may function in different fields; however, under no circumstances should we forget Paul's indisputable assertion when he affirms that “there are diversities of operations, but it is the same God which worketh all in all”.

messages.title: The Word is Creator
paragraphs: “But those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart; and they defile the man.” — JESUS (Matthew, 15.18)
The Master's teaching, beneath the veil of the letter, embodies a profound warning.
It is indispensable to care for the heart as the emitting source of the word, so that we may not lose the harmony necessary for our own happiness.
That which comes from the heart and mind, through the mouth, is a living and pulsating force, enveloping the creature for good or for ill, according to the nature of the emission.
From the depths of tyrants, through this process, originates the initial movement of war, a destructive movement that returns to the source from which it was born, bringing ruin and annihilation.
From the souls of slanderers come the poisons that torment generous spirits, but which return to the slanderers themselves, darkening their mental horizons.

From the hearts of the wicked, the perverse, and the unconscious arise, through verbalist power, the beginnings of downfalls, crimes, and injustices; yet such disturbing elements do not articulate in vain for their very authors, because a day will come when they will reap the bitter fruits of the unhappy activity they set in motion.
Likewise, joy sown through wholesome and constructive words grows and yields its results.
Fraternal help spreads infinite benefits, and the fragrance of the good, even when poured upon the ungrateful, returns in invisible waves to comfort the brow that emits it.
